Sources normalised (2026-11-06): entries cited as the book spells them (يقن → يقين); أمن read and added to `verified` (consistent with the texts; no attributed point rests on it).

nuance.bs: Vjerovati i potvrditi istinu srcem, s povjerenjem; iz istog korijena kao sigurnost (أَمْن). Najčešći od tri glagola.
nuance.en: To believe and affirm the truth in the heart, with trust; from the same root as safety (أَمْن). The most frequent of the three.

why.bs: „Nego recite: ‚Predali smo se‘, a vjerovanje još nije ušlo u vaša srca“ – iman je u srcu.
why.en: “Rather say ‘We submit,’ for the faith hath not yet entered into your hearts” — īmān lives in the heart.

why.bs: Poslanik i vjernici vjeruju u Allaha, meleke, knjige i poslanike – predmet imana.
why.en: The Messenger and the believers believe in Allah, His angels, books and messengers — the objects of faith.

why.bs: „O vi koji vjerujete, vjerujte…“ – vjernicima se naređuje da vjeruju: iman se obnavlja i jača.
why.en: “O ye who believe! Believe…” — believers bidden to believe: faith renewed and strengthened.

nuance.bs: Predati se Allahu i prihvatiti Njegovu vjeru. Prema ar-Rāġibu, islam je dvojak: ispod imana – samo izgovor jezikom (49:14), i iznad imana – kad se jeziku pridruže srce, djelo i potpuna predanost (Ibrahim).
nuance.en: To submit to Allah and accept His religion. According to ar-Rāġib, islām is of two kinds: below īmān — the tongue's acknowledgement alone (49:14) — and above it, when heart, deed and complete submission join the tongue (Ibrāhīm).

why.bs: Beduinima je rečeno da kažu „Predali smo se“, a ne „Vjerujemo“ – islam ispod imana.
why.en: The Bedouins are told to say “We submit”, not “We believe” — islām below īmān.

why.bs: „Predaj se!“ – „Predao sam se Gospodaru svjetova“ – Ibrahimova potpuna predanost, islam iznad imana.
why.en: “Surrender!” — “I have surrendered to the Lord of the Worlds” — Ibrāhīm's complete submission, islām above īmān.

why.bs: Najbolji u vjeri je onaj ko lice svoje preda Allahu čineći dobro.
why.en: Best in religion is the one who submits his face to Allah while doing good.

nuance.bs: Biti čvrsto uvjeren, bez ikakve sumnje. Prema ar-Rāġibu, yaqīn je stepen znanja iznad spoznaje (maʿrifa): smirenost razumijevanja uz čvrst sud. Najčešće se kaže za uvjerenje u ahiret i u ajete.
nuance.en: To be firmly convinced, without any doubt. According to ar-Rāġib, yaqīn is a degree of knowledge above maʿrifa: stillness of understanding with firm judgement. Most often said of conviction in the hereafter and in the signs.

why.bs: „I u ahiret su oni čvrsto uvjereni“ – uvjerenje u ahiret.
why.en: “And are certain of the Hereafter” — conviction in the hereafter.

why.bs: U stvaranju živih bića su znakovi za ljude koji su čvrsto uvjereni.
why.en: “In your creation, and all the beasts that He scattereth in the earth, are portents for a folk whose faith is sure.”

why.bs: Predvodnici koji su bili strpljivi i u Naše ajete čvrsto vjerovali.
why.en: Leaders who were patient and were certain of Our signs.

title.en: To call and to call out

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače ‚zvati‘; razlikuju se po tome je li u prvom planu povišen glas ili molba i obraćanje.
shared.en: Both verbs mean ‘to call’; they differ in whether a raised voice or a request and an address is in view.

tellApart.bs: Zvati, moliti, prizivati – i Allaha u dovi → دَعَا; dozivati povišenim glasom da se čuje, često iz daljine → نَادَى.
tellApart.en: To call, to pray, to invoke — Allah too, in supplication → دَعَا; to call out aloud so as to be heard, often from afar → نَادَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries دعا, ندا
notes: ar-Rāġib: nidāʾ is raising the voice and making it heard; duʿāʾ is like nidāʾ, except that nidāʾ may be just “yā” or “ayā” without a name, while duʿāʾ is hardly said without the name; he cites 2:171 (duʿāʾan wa-nidāʾan, nouns, so not a member ayah here) — attributed to him.
19:3 'a secret call' (nidāʾan khafiyyan): that this joins a word for calling aloud with secrecy is commented on in tafsir; given as tafsir, not a named mufassir.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries دعا, ندا (2026-11-06): 6 attributed points confirmed
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): entries cited as the book spells them (ندى → ندا).

nuance.bs: Zvati nekoga po imenu, pozivati, moliti; odatle دُعَاء – dova. Kaže se za molitvu Allahu, ali i za prizivanje lažnih božanstava i za pozivanje ljudi nečemu.
nuance.en: To call someone by name, to invite, to pray; hence دُعَاء, supplication. It is said of praying to Allah, but also of invoking false gods and of inviting people to something.

why.bs: „Zovite Mene, Ja ću vam se odazvati“ – dova Allahu.
why.en: “Pray unto Me and I will hear your prayer” — supplication to Allah.

why.bs: „Zovite svoga Gospodara ponizno i potajno“ – dova ne traži povišen glas.
why.en: “Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret” — duʿāʾ needs no raised voice.

why.bs: „Zovite Allaha, ili Svemilosnog zovite“ – دَعَا s imenom onoga koga se zove, kako ar-Rāġib i opisuje.
why.en: “Cry unto Allah, or cry unto the Beneficent” — دَعَا with the name of the one called, as ar-Rāġib describes it.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, nidāʾ je podizanje glasa da se čuje. Zato نَادَى često stoji tamo gdje se doziva iz daljine ili glasno – stanovnici Dženneta dozivaju stanovnike vatre.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, nidāʾ is raising the voice so it is heard. Hence نَادَى often stands where someone calls from afar or aloud — the people of Paradise call out to the people of the Fire.

why.bs: Stanovnici Dženneta doviknu stanovnicima vatre – dozivanje preko onoga što dvije skupine razdvaja.
why.en: The companions of Paradise call out to the companions of the Fire — calling across what separates the two groups.

why.bs: Junus je iz tmina zazvao: „Nema boga osim Tebe“ – nidāʾ za usrdnu dovu iz nevolje, ne nužno za daljinu.
why.en: Jonah cried out in the darkness: “There is no Allah save Thee” — nidāʾ for an urgent supplication in distress, not necessarily distance.

why.bs: Zekerijja je Gospodara zazvao „potajnim zovom“ – riječ za glasno dozivanje uz tišinu; tefsir kaže da je dovu sakrio od ljudi.
why.en: Zechariah cried unto his Lord “a cry in secret” — a word for calling aloud joined to secrecy; tafsir says he hid his prayer from people.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o pravom putu; razlikuju se po tome je li u prvom planu pokazivanje puta ili zrelost i ispravnost onoga ko njime ide.
shared.en: Both words speak of the right way; they differ in whether showing the way or the soundness and maturity of the one who walks it is in view.

tellApart.bs: Uputa koju Allah daje, Knjiga kao uputa → هُدًى; ispravnost, zrelost i razboritost, suprotnost zabludi (غَيّ) → رُشْد.
tellApart.en: Guidance Allah gives, the Book as guidance → هُدًى; rightness, maturity and good sense, the opposite of error (غَيّ) → رُشْد.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries هدى, رشد
notes: ar-Rāġib: hidāya is guiding with gentleness; Allah's guidance is of four kinds — the general guidance given to every creature, the call through the prophets, the help (tawfīq) given to the guided, and the guidance to Paradise in the hereafter — attributed to him.

ar-Rāġib: rashad and rushd are the opposite of ghayy and used like hidāya; he reports that some said rushd is said of worldly and otherworldly matters and rashad of otherworldly matters only — given as the view of 'some' he reports.
رُشْد (6) and رَشَد (5) are two vocalisations of one word, filed by the corpus as two lemmas; counted together (11).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries هدى, رشد (2026-11-06): 14 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (improved): He adds that the Quran reserves the word hudā (unlike hidāya) for guidance Allah Himself grants, citing ﴿ هدى للمتقين ﴾

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, upućivanje s blagošću. Allahova uputa je četverostruka: opća uputa svakom stvorenju, poziv po poslanicima, pomoć (tevfik) upućenima i uvođenje u Džennet. On ističe da je riječ هُدًى rezervisana za uputu koju daje sam Allah – zato se i Knjiga zove هُدًى.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, guiding with gentleness. Allah's guidance is fourfold: general guidance to every creature, the call through the prophets, help (tawfīq) to the guided, and leading into Paradise. He notes that the word هُدًى is reserved for guidance Allah Himself grants — so the Book itself is called هُدًى.

why.bs: „Uputa bogobojaznima“ – Knjiga kao uputa.
why.en: “A guidance unto those who ward off (evil)” — the Book as guidance.

why.bs: Onima koji su na pravom putu On uputu povećava – uputa kao pomoć upućenima.
why.en: Those who are guided — He increases them in guidance: guidance as help to the guided.

why.bs: Ko bude slijedio Moju uputu, ni straha ni tuge za njih – uputa poslana ljudima.
why.en: Whoever follows My guidance — no fear for them, nor will they grieve: guidance sent to people.

nuance.bs: Ispravnost razuma i postupanja, suprotno zabludi (غَيّ). Kaže se i za zrelost siročeta koje može upravljati imetkom. Ar-Rāġib prenosi mišljenje da se رُشْد kaže za dunjalučke i ahiretske stvari, a رَشَد samo za ahiretske.
nuance.en: Soundness of mind and conduct, the opposite of error (غَيّ). It is said even of an orphan's maturity to manage property. ar-Rāġib reports the view that رُشْد is said of worldly and otherworldly matters, and رَشَد of otherworldly matters only.

why.bs: „Pravi put se jasno razlučio od stranputice“ – رُشْد nasuprot غَيّ.
why.en: “The right direction is henceforth distinct from error” — رُشْد against غَيّ.

why.bs: Kad kod siročadi primijetite zrelost (رُشْد), predajte im imetak – dunjalučka razboritost.
why.en: When you perceive in the orphans sound judgement (رُشْد), release their property to them — worldly good sense.

why.bs: Oni koji su primili islam, pravi put (رَشَد) su izabrali – ispravnost u vjeri, koju mišljenje što ga ar-Rāġib prenosi veže za ahiret.
why.en: Whoever has accepted Islam — those have sought out the right course (رَشَد) — rightness in religion, which the view ar-Rāġib reports ties to the hereafter.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače skretanje s pravog puta; razlikuju se po uzroku: svako skretanje, ili zabluda koja izvire iz pogrešnog uvjerenja.
shared.en: Both words mean leaving the right way; they differ in the cause: any straying, or error that springs from a corrupt belief.

tellApart.bs: Svako skretanje s pravog puta, namjerno ili ne, malo ili veliko → ضَلَال; zabluda iz pogrešnog uvjerenja, suprotnost رُشْد → غَيّ.
tellApart.en: Any straying from the straight path, intended or not, small or great → ضَلَال; error rooted in a corrupt belief, the opposite of رُشْد → غَيّ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ضل, غوى
notes: ar-Rāġib: ḍalāl is turning aside from the straight path, the opposite of guidance, said of every deviation, intended or unintended, small or great — attributed to him.
ar-Rāġib: ghayy is ignorance that comes from a corrupt belief, as distinct from ignorance with no belief at all — attributed to him.
53:2 (mā ḍalla … wa-mā ghawā) shows both roots side by side, but uses verbs, not these nouns; mentioned here only.
The corpus files ضَلَالَة (9) as a separate lemma; it is not added to ضَلَال.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries ضل, غوى, رشد (2026-11-06): 7 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): His examples of the light end are oversight and forgetting (﴿ أن تضل إحداهما ﴾ = forgets), set against 'far error' which is kufr; 'being at a loss' is not his

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, skretanje s pravog puta – svako, namjerno ili nenamjerno, malo ili veliko. Zato se, kaže on, odnosi i na običan previd ili zaborav i na daleku zabludu nevjerstva (ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, turning aside from the straight path — any such turning, intended or not, small or great. Hence, he notes, it is said both of a mere oversight or forgetting and of the far error of disbelief (ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا).

why.bs: Ko Allahu pripisuje druga, daleko je zalutao – ضَلَال بَعِيد, najveća zabluda.
why.en: Whoever associates others with Allah has gone far astray — ضَلَال بَعِيد, the greatest error.

why.bs: Braća kažu da je njihov otac „u očitoj zabludi“ – za njih je pogriješio u ljubavi prema Jusufu, ne u vjeri.
why.en: The brothers say their father is “in plain aberration” — to them he erred in his love for Joseph, not in faith.

why.bs: „Pa šta ima nakon istine osim zablude?“ – ضَلَال kao sve što nije istina.
why.en: “After the Truth what is there saving error?” — ضَلَال as all that is not the truth.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, neznanje koje izvire iz pogrešnog uvjerenja. Stoji nasuprot رُشْد, a Kur'an ga kaže za one koji biraju krivi put (7:146) i slijede strasti.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ignorance that springs from a corrupt belief. It stands against رُشْد, and the Quran uses it of those who choose the wrong way (7:146) and follow their desires.

why.bs: Pravi put se jasno razlikuje od zablude (غَيّ) – zato nema prisile u vjeri.
why.en: The right course is distinct from the wrong (غَيّ) — so there is no compulsion in religion.

why.bs: Ako vide put zablude, uzimaju ga za put – svjesno biranje krivog puta.
why.en: If they see the way of error, they will adopt it as a way — knowingly choosing the wrong road.

why.bs: Pokoljenja koja su zapustila namaz i povela se za strastima – susrest će غَيّ (tefsir ga tumači kao propast ili kao dolinu u Džehennemu).
why.en: Generations that neglected prayer and followed desires will meet غَيّ (tafsir explains it as ruin, or as a valley in Hell).

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače činiti nepravdu; razlikuju se po tome je li u prvom planu stavljanje stvari na krivo mjesto, oholo prekoračenje ili napad preko granice.
shared.en: All three words mean doing wrong; they differ in whether putting a thing in the wrong place, overbearing excess, or crossing a limit in attack is in view.

tellApart.bs: Nepravda u najširem smislu – i prema sebi, i prema Allahu → ظُلْم; oholo prekoračenje mjere, nasilje nad drugima → بَغْي; prelaženje granice, neprijateljski napad → عُدْوَان.
tellApart.en: Wrong in the widest sense — towards oneself and towards Allah too → ظُلْم; overbearing excess, oppressing others → بَغْي; overstepping a limit, hostile attack → عُدْوَان.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ظلم, بغى, عدا
notes: ar-Rāġib: ẓulm is putting a thing in other than its proper place, by falling short, by excess, or by deviating in time or place; he cites some sages that it is of three kinds — between man and Allah (the greatest: kufr, shirk and nifāq), between man and people, and between man and himself — attributed to him.

ar-Rāġib: baghy is seeking to go beyond the right measure, whether or not one goes beyond it; the blameworthy baghy is passing beyond the truth to falsehood or to the doubtful, and in most places in the Quran it is blameworthy — attributed to him.
ʿudwān is explained by its root ʿ-d-w (going beyond, overstepping); said as the root's sense.

2:193 (no ʿudwān except against the wrongdoers): many mufassirun explain that the just response is called ʿudwān by correspondence (mušākala) with the wrong it answers; given as their explanation (blind review).
6:82: the Prophet's explanation of ẓulm there as shirk (citing 31:13) is reported in the Ṣaḥīḥ collections; the ayah is not cited as a member ayah, the hadith is mentioned in 31:13's note only.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries ظلم, بغى (2026-11-06): 6 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): He gives the definition as that of lexicographers and many scholars, and reports the three-fold division from 'some sages', naming kufr, shirk and nifāq as the gravest; notes/1 (reworded): He defines blameworthy baghy as passing from truth to falsehood or the doubtful, and says it is blameworthy in most Quranic places; 'against others' is not his definition; members/0/nuance (reworded): The three-fold division is reported by him from 'some sages', not stated as his own
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): عدا read and added to `verified` (consistent with the texts; no attributed point rests on it).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, stavljanje stvari na mjesto koje joj ne pripada. Najšira riječ; on navodi mudrace koji je dijele na nepravdu prema Allahu (širk), prema ljudima i prema samome sebi.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, putting a thing where it does not belong. The widest word; he cites sages who divide it into wrong against Allah (shirk), against people, and against oneself.

why.bs: „Zaista, širk je golema nepravda“ – ẓulm prema Allahu; Poslanik je tim ajetom objasnio ẓulm u 6:82.
why.en: “To ascribe partners (unto Him) is a tremendous wrong” — ẓulm against Allah; with this ayah the Prophet explained the ẓulm of 6:82.

why.bs: Ko to učini „iz neprijateljstva i nepravde“ – عُدْوَان i ظُلْم jedno uz drugo.
why.en: Whoever does that “through aggression and injustice” — عُدْوَان and ظُلْم side by side.

why.bs: Allah ne želi nepravdu robovima – ẓulm koji Allah od Sebe odbija.
why.en: Allah wants no injustice for His servants — ẓulm, which Allah disowns for His servants.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, težnja da se pređe prava mjera. Ar-Rāġib razlikuje i pohvalni بَغْي (prelaženje pravde u dobročinstvo); u Kur'anu je imenica najčešće oholo nasilje nad drugima, i suparništvo iz zavisti zbog kojeg su se razišli oni kojima je data Knjiga.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, seeking to go beyond the right measure. ar-Rāġib also names a laudable baghy (going beyond justice to kindness); in the Quran the noun is mostly overbearing wrong against others, and the rivalry out of envy through which those given the Scripture fell into dispute.

why.bs: Allah zabranjuje razvrat, odvratnost i nasilje (بَغْي) – nepravda prema drugima.
why.en: Allah forbids immorality, bad conduct and oppression (بَغْي) — wrong done to others.

why.bs: Razišli su se tek kad im je došlo znanje, „iz međusobnog nasilja“ (بَغْيًا) – suparništvo, ne neznanje.
why.en: They differed only after knowledge came to them, “through transgression among themselves” (بَغْيًا) — rivalry, not ignorance.

why.bs: „O ljudi, vaše nasilje je samo protiv vas samih“ – بَغْي se vraća onome ko ga čini.
why.en: “O mankind! Your rebellion is only against yourselves” — بَغْي recoils on its doer.

nuance.bs: Iz korijena koji znači prelaziti granicu: nepravda kao prekoračenje, neprijateljski napad. Često stoji u paru s grijehom (إِثْم).
nuance.en: From a root meaning to go beyond: wrong as overstepping, hostile attack. Often paired with sin (إِثْم).

why.bs: „A u grijehu i neprijateljstvu ne sarađujte jedni s drugima“ – عُدْوَان uz إِثْم.
why.en: “Help not one another unto sin and transgression” — عُدْوَان beside إِثْم.

why.bs: „Neka nema neprijateljstva osim prema nepravednicima“ – mnogi mufessiri tumače da se pravedan odgovor zove عُدْوَان po paralelizmu s nasiljem na koje odgovara.
why.en: “Let there be no hostility except against wrong-doers” — many mufassirun explain the just response as called عُدْوَان by parallel with the aggression it answers.

why.bs: Musa: „pa neka nema prekoračenja prema meni“ – prelaženje dogovorene granice.
why.en: Moses: “there will be no injustice to me” — overstepping an agreed limit.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače pravdu; razlikuju se po tome je li u prvom planu jednakost i ravnoteža ili pravedan udio koji svakome pripada.
shared.en: Both words mean justice; they differ in whether equality and balance or the fair share due to each is in view.

tellApart.bs: Pravda kao jednakost, pravedan sud, pa i ‚protuvrijednost‘ → عَدْل; pravedan udio, ispravna mjera i vaga → قِسْط.
tellApart.en: Justice as equality, a fair judgement, even an ‘equivalent’ → عَدْل; the fair share, right measure and weight → قِسْط.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عدل, قسط
notes: ar-Rāġib: ʿadl is equality; ʿadl is used of what is grasped by insight (judgements), ʿidl of what is perceived by the senses (weights, numbers) — attributed to him.
ar-Rāġib: qisṭ is the share given justly; qasaṭa is taking another's share (injustice, 72:15 al-qāsiṭūn) while aqsaṭa is giving another his share (justice) — attributed to him.
That قِسْط often stands with weighing and measure (6:152, 55:9, 21:47) is our observation of its 15 places.
In 2:48 and 5:95 the Quran's word is read ʿadl (with fatḥa) in the sense of an equivalent, and ar-Rāġib himself cites 5:95 under ʿadl, as an equivalence grasped by insight rather than by the senses.
49:9 joins both (fa-aṣliḥū baynahumā bi-l-ʿadl wa-aqsiṭū): cited under عَدْل.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries عدل, قسط (2026-11-06): 10 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/3 (reworded): He cites ﴿ أو عدل ذلك صياما ﴾ (5:95) as the example of ʿadl, the equivalence grasped by insight, and glosses it as fasting equal to the food; members/0/nuance (reworded): He explains 5:95 as fasting equal to the food of the expiation; he does not discuss the ransom sense of 2:48
Blind review of the verification-pass texts (2026-11-06): 'ransom' in 2:48 given to the mufassirun, not ar-Rāġib (his gloss there is farīḍa).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, jednakost: podjela na jednake dijelove, a kaže se za ono što se shvata uvidom, poput presuda. Odatle i ‚protuvrijednost‘: post jednak hrani iskupa (5:95, kako ga on tumači); u 2:48 mufesiri to razumiju kao otkupninu jednake vrijednosti.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, equality: dividing into equal shares, said of what is grasped by insight, such as rulings. Hence also an ‘equivalent’: fasting equal to the food of an expiation (5:95, as he explains it); in 2:48 mufassirun take it as a ransom of equal value.

why.bs: „Allah naređuje pravdu i dobročinstvo“ – عَدْل kao temelj.
why.en: “Allah enjoineth justice and kindness” — عَدْل as the foundation.

why.bs: Kad sudite među ljudima, sudite pravedno – pravda u sudu.
why.en: “If ye judge between mankind, that ye judge justly” — justice in judgement.

why.bs: Na Sudnjem danu „niti će se od nje (duše) uzeti otkup“ (عَدْل) – عَدْل kao protuvrijednost.
why.en: On that Day “nor will compensation be received from it” (عَدْل) — عَدْل as an equivalent.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, udio koji se daje pravedno. Zato قِسْط često stoji uz mjeru i vagu (naše zapažanje), a od istog korijena قَاسِط je nepravednik koji otima tuđi udio, a مُقْسِط pravednik koji ga daje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the share given justly. So قِسْط often stands with measure and weighing (our observation), and from the same root a قَاسِط is the unjust who takes another's share, a مُقْسِط the just who gives it.

why.bs: „I vagajte pravedno, i ne zakidajte na vagi“ – qisṭ kao ispravna mjera.
why.en: “Observe the measure strictly, nor fall short thereof” — qisṭ as right measure.

why.bs: Postavit ćemo vage pravedne za Sudnji dan – qisṭ i vaga.
why.en: We place the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection — qisṭ and the scale.

why.bs: „Ustrajno se držite pravde, kao svjedoci Allaha radi, makar i protiv sebe samih“ – pravo svakoga da dobije svoje.
why.en: “Be ye staunch in justice, witnesses for Allah, even though it be against yourselves” — each given his due.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače ono što čovjek dobije za svoje djelo; razlikuju se po tome je li riječ o naplati i za dobro i za zlo, o plaći za trud ili o onome što se vraća čovjeku.
shared.en: All three words mean what one receives for one's deed; they differ in whether it is requital for good and evil alike, a wage for work, or what returns to the doer.

tellApart.bs: Uzvraćanje za djelo – i dobro i zlo → جَزَاء; plaća, nagrada za trud, samo za dobro → أَجْر; ono što se čovjeku vraća za djelo, kao imenica u Kur'anu uvijek dobra nagrada → ثَوَاب.
tellApart.en: Requital for a deed, good or evil → جَزَاء; a wage, reward for effort, only for good → أَجْر; what returns to a person for his deed, as a noun in the Quran always a good reward → ثَوَاب.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries جزاء, أجر, ثوب
notes: ar-Rāġib: jazāʾ is what suffices, requital good for good and evil for evil; ajr is what returns from a deed, worldly or otherworldly, said of what comes under a contract or what is like one, and only of benefit, never harm, while jazāʾ is said with or without a contract and of benefit and harm — attributed to him.

ar-Rāġib: thawāb is from thawb, a thing's return to its first state — what returns to a person for his deeds; the word is used of good and evil but is mostly known for good (he cites the verb in 3:153) — attributed to him.
That the noun ثَوَاب in the Quran is always a reward (all 9 places read) is our observation; the verb أَثَابَ is used of grief in 3:153.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries جزاء, أجر, ثوب (2026-11-06): 16 attributed points confirmed
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): entries cited as the book spells them (جزى → جزاء).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, uzvraćanje: dobro za dobro, zlo za zlo. Zato se kaže i za nagradu i za kaznu, i stoji tamo gdje je djelo mjera uzvrata.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, requital: good for good, evil for evil. So it is said of reward and of punishment alike, and stands where the deed is the measure of what is returned.

why.bs: „Zar je naknada za dobročinstvo išta drugo osim dobročinstva?“ – جَزَاء za dobro.
why.en: “Is the reward of goodness aught save goodness?” — جَزَاء for good.

why.bs: „A naknada za loše djelo je loše djelo poput njega“ – جَزَاء za zlo, po mjeri djela.
why.en: “The guerdon of an ill-deed is an ill the like thereof” — جَزَاء for evil, by the deed's measure.

why.bs: „Naknada primjerena“ (جَزَاءً وِفَاقًا) – uzvrat koji odgovara djelima.
why.en: “Reward proportioned” (جَزَاءً وِفَاقًا) — requital fitting the deeds.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ono što se dobije za djelo, na dunjaluku ili ahiretu, kao po ugovoru, i to samo korist, nikad šteta. Otuda i obična plaća, i mehr.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, what one receives for a deed, in this world or the next, as under a contract — and only benefit, never harm. Hence also an ordinary wage, and the bridal due.

why.bs: Poslanici kažu: „Ne tražim od vas za to nikakvu plaću“ – أَجْر kao plaća.
why.en: The prophets say: “I ask of you no wage therefor” — أَجْر as a wage.

why.bs: „Moj otac te zove da ti uzvrati plaćom za to što si nam napojio (stado)“ – جَزَى i أَجْر u istoj rečenici, plaća za učinjen posao.
why.en: “My father biddeth thee, that he may reward thee with a payment for that thou didst water (the flock) for us” — جَزَى and أَجْر in one sentence, payment for work done.

why.bs: „Kako je lijepa nagrada onih što rade!“ – أَجْر kao Allahova nagrada za trud.
why.en: “A bountiful reward for workers!” — أَجْر as Allah's reward for effort.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ono što se čovjeku ‚vraća‘ za njegova djela (korijen znači povratak). Kaže on da se kaže i za dobro i za zlo, a najčešće za dobro; u Kur'anu je imenica uvijek nagrada (naše zapažanje).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, what ‘returns’ to a person for his deeds (the root means return). He says it is used of good and evil but mostly of good; in the Quran the noun is always a reward (our observation).

why.bs: „Nagrada od Allaha – a kod Allaha je najbolja nagrada.“
why.en: “A reward from Allah. And with Allah is the fairest of rewards.”

why.bs: Allah im je dao nagradu na dunjaluku i lijepu nagradu na ahiretu – ثَوَاب na oba svijeta.
why.en: Allah gave them the reward of this world and the good reward of the Hereafter — ثَوَاب in both worlds.

why.bs: Allahova nagrada je najbolja – ثَوَاب kao ono što se vraća vjerniku.
why.en: He is best in reward — ثَوَاب as what returns to the believer.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi označavaju vatru i u Kur'anu najčešće kaznu na ahiretu; razlikuju se po tome je li to vatra uopće ili njena žestina i rasplamsalost.
shared.en: All three words denote fire and in the Quran most often the punishment of the hereafter; they differ in whether fire in general or its fierceness and blaze is in view.

tellApart.bs: Vatra uopće – i ova, dunjalučka, i ahiretska → نَار; žestoka, razbuktala vatra → جَحِيم; raspaljen plamen, oganj → سَعِير.
tellApart.en: Fire in general — of this world and of the hereafter → نَار; a fierce, blazing fire → جَحِيم; a kindled flame, a blaze → سَعِير.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نور, جحم, سعر
notes: ar-Rāġib: nār is said of the flame that is seen, of heat alone, and of the Fire of the hereafter; jaḥīm is from jaḥma, the fierce blazing of fire; saʿīr is from saʿara, to kindle a fire — attributed to him.
That جَحِيم is said once of the fire prepared for Ibrāhīm (37:97) and otherwise of Hell, and that all 16 places of سَعِير speak of the hereafter, is our observation (all places read).
جَهَنَّم is not a member: the corpus treats it as a proper name outside the noun catalogue.
Content: the ayat are quoted as warnings, with no description beyond the Quran's own words.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries نور, جحم, سعر (2026-11-06): 8 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Opća riječ za vatru: i za vatru koju je Musa ugledao, i za vatru u koju je bačen Ibrahim, i za vatru na ahiretu, kada se kaže ‚vatra‘ bez ikakvog dodatka.
nuance.en: The general word for fire: the fire Moses saw, the fire Ibrāhīm was thrown into, and the Fire of the hereafter, when ‘the Fire’ stands alone.

why.bs: Musa je ugledao vatru – vatra na dunjaluku (u tefsiru se raspravlja je li bila obična vatra ili svjetlo).
why.en: Moses saw a fire — a fire in this world (tafsir discusses whether it was ordinary fire or a light).

why.bs: „O vatro, budi hladnoća i spas Ibrahimu!“
why.en: “O fire, be coolness and peace for Abraham.”

why.bs: „Čuvajte se vatre čije su gorivo ljudi i kamenje“ – vatra na ahiretu.
why.en: “Guard yourselves against the Fire … whose fuel is of men and stones” — the Fire of the hereafter.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od riječi koja znači žestoko razbuktavanje vatre. U Kur'anu je ime za vatru na ahiretu, a jednom za vatru koju su pripremili Ibrahimu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from a word for the fierce blazing of fire. In the Quran a name for the Fire of the hereafter, and once for the fire prepared for Ibrāhīm.

why.bs: „Pa ga bacite u oganj!“ – Ibrahimovi neprijatelji o vatri koju su zapalili: jedino dunjalučko جَحِيم.
why.en: Ibrāhīm's enemies order him flung into the blazing fire they lit: the one worldly use of جَحِيم.

why.bs: „I kad se oganj razbukta“ – جَحِيم uz glagol iz korijena سعر.
why.en: “And when hell is lighted” — جَحِيم with a verb from the root of سَعِير.

why.bs: Onome ko je bio obijestan, prebivalište će biti oganj – opomena.
why.en: For the one who transgressed, Hellfire will be the refuge — a warning.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od glagola koji znači raspaliti vatru: plamen koji se raspiruje. U Kur'anu uvijek o ahiretu (naše zapažanje), često u spoju ‚patnja razbuktalog ognja‘.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from a verb meaning to kindle a fire: a flame that is stoked. In the Quran always of the hereafter (our observation), often in ‘the punishment of the Blaze’.

why.bs: Oni koji nepravedno jedu imetke siročadi gorjet će u ognju – opomena za nepravdu prema siročadi.
why.en: Those who devour orphans' property unjustly will be burned in a Blaze — a warning against wronging orphans.

why.bs: Šejtanima je pripremljena patnja u ognju – عَذَاب السَّعِير.
why.en: For the devils is prepared the punishment of the Blaze — عَذَاب السَّعِير.

why.bs: „Jedna skupina u Džennetu, a druga skupina u razbuktalom ognju“ – سَعِير nasuprot Džennetu.
why.en: “A host will be in the Garden, and a host of them in the Flame” — سَعِير set against Paradise.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače naselje u kojem žive ljudi; Kur'an ponekad isto mjesto zove i jednim i drugim imenom.
shared.en: Both words mean a settlement where people live; the Quran sometimes calls the same place by both names.

tellApart.bs: Svako naselje, mjesto okupljanja ljudi – i njegovi stanovnici → قَرْيَة; grad, često određeni grad (Medina, faraonov grad) → مَدِينَة.
tellApart.en: Any settlement, a place where people gather — and its people → قَرْيَة; a city, often a particular city (Medina, Pharaoh's city) → مَدِينَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries قرى
notes: ar-Rāġib: qarya is a name for the place where people gather and for the people together, used of either — attributed to him.

That the Quran calls one place (as tafsir identifies it) both قَرْيَة and مَدِينَة (18:77 and 18:82; 36:13 and 36:20), and that Mecca is called قَرْيَة (47:13, umm al-qurā 6:92), is our observation; 'qarya = village' is therefore not the Quranic sense.
مَدِينَة: the corpus files the broken plural مَدَائِن (3, Pharaoh's cities) separately; counted together (17).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries قرى (2026-11-06): 3 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reattributed): He cites 47:13 ('your qarya') and calls qarya a name for a city, but never names Mecca, so the Mecca point is now a Quranic observation
Blind review of the verification-pass texts (2026-11-06): 'most often destroyed' softened to 'often'; قَرْيَة rendered town / naselje throughout, keeping city / grad for مَدِينَة.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, mjesto gdje se ljudi okupljaju – i sami ljudi. Ne znači samo selo: u Kur'anu se i Meka zove قَرْيَة (47:13). Često se govori o narodima i njihovim naseljima koja su uništena (naše zapažanje).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the place where people gather — and the people themselves. It does not mean only a village: in the Quran Mecca too is called قَرْيَة (47:13). Often said of peoples and their towns that were destroyed (our observation).

why.bs: „Upitaj naselje gdje smo boravili“ – قَرْيَة za stanovnike.
why.en: “Ask the township where we were” — قَرْيَة for its people.

why.bs: „Tvoje naselje koje te je istjeralo“ – Meka nazvana قَرْيَة.
why.en: “Thy township (O Muhammad) which hath cast thee out” — Mecca called قَرْيَة.

why.bs: Došli su stanovnicima jednog naselja (قَرْيَة)… – isto mjesto (tako ga razumije većina mufesira) u 18:82 zove se مَدِينَة (grad).
why.en: They came to the people of a town (قَرْيَة)… — the same place (as most mufassirun take it) is called مَدِينَة (city) in 18:82.

nuance.bs: Grad; u Kur'anu često određeni grad: Poslanikova Medina, faraonov grad, grad u kojem je Musa zatekao dvojicu kako se tuku.
nuance.en: A city; in the Quran often a particular city: the Prophet's Medina, Pharaoh's city, the city where Moses found two men fighting.

why.bs: „Ako se vratimo u Medinu…“ – مَدِينَة kao ime Poslanikovog grada.
why.en: “If we return to Al-Madinah…” — مَدِينَة as the name of the Prophet's city.

why.bs: Zid je pripadao dvojici dječaka siročadi „u gradu” – isto mjesto koje je u 18:77 قَرْيَة.
why.en: The wall belonged to two orphan boys “in the city” — the place that is قَرْيَة in 18:77.

why.bs: S kraja grada dotrča jedan čovjek – mjesto koje tefsir uzima kao قَرْيَة iz 36:13.
why.en: “There came from the uttermost part of the city a man running” — the place tafsir takes as the قَرْيَة of 36:13.

title.en: To die and to take the soul

shared.bs: Oba glagola govore o smrti; razlikuju se po tome ko je u središtu: onaj ko umire, ili Onaj (i meleki) koji dušu uzima.
shared.en: Both verbs speak of death; they differ in who is at the centre: the one who dies, or the One (and the angels) who takes the soul.

tellApart.bs: Umrijeti – subjekt je onaj ko umire → مَاتَ; uzeti dušu u potpunosti – subjekt je Allah, meleki ili smrt, a čovjek je trpni → تَوَفَّى.
tellApart.en: To die — the subject is the one who dies → مَاتَ; to take the soul in full — the subject is Allah, the angels or death, and the person is acted upon → تَوَفَّى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries موت, وفى
notes: ar-Rāġib: istīfāʾ (same root) is taking a thing in full; death and sleep are both expressed by tawaffī (6:60, 39:42) — attributed to him.
That the subject of تَوَفَّى in all 24 places is Allah, the angels or death, or the verb is passive, is our observation (all places read).
3:55 (mutawaffīka) and 5:117 (tawaffaytanī), about ʿĪsā, are not cited: tafsir differs on their meaning (sleep, being taken up, or death), and the participle in 3:55 is not filed under the verb.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries وفى, موت (2026-11-06): 3 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): He defines istīfāʾ, not tawaffī, as taking a thing in full; that death and sleep are both called tawaffī (6:60, 39:42) is his; members/1/nuance (reworded): 'Taking in full' is his gloss of istīfāʾ in the same root, not a definition of tawaffī; death and sleep being called tawaffī is his

nuance.bs: Umrijeti: subjekt je onaj ko umire. Opća riječ za smrt, i za ljude i za Poslanika – svako će umrijeti.
nuance.en: To die: the subject is the one who dies. The general word for death, of people and of the Prophet alike — everyone will die.

why.bs: „Zar ako umre ili bude ubijen…“ – smrt Poslanika iskazana sa مَاتَ.
why.en: “When he dieth or is slain…” — the Prophet's death expressed with مَاتَ.

why.bs: Merjem: „Da sam barem umrla prije ovoga!“ – čovjek o svojoj smrti.
why.en: Mary: “Oh, would that I had died ere this” — a person speaking of her own death.

why.bs: Allah uzima duše kad umru (مَوْت), i one koje ne umru (لَمْ تَمُتْ) – u snu: oba glagola u jednom ajetu.
why.en: Allah takes the souls at death, and those that do not die (لَمْ تَمُتْ) during sleep — both verbs in one ayah.

meaning.bs: uzeti dušu (u smrti i u snu)
meaning.en: to take the soul (in death and in sleep)

nuance.bs: Iz korijena ‚uzeti nešto u potpunosti‘; prema ar-Rāġibu, njime se izražavaju i smrt i san. Subjekt je Allah, meleki ili smrt; čovjek je onaj čija se duša uzima.
nuance.en: From the root of ‘taking a thing in full’; according to ar-Rāġib, death and sleep alike are expressed by it. The subject is Allah, the angels or death; the person is the one whose soul is taken.

why.bs: On vam noću uzima duše (يَتَوَفَّاكُم), u snu – تَوَفَّى i za san.
why.en: He takes your souls by night (in sleep) — تَوَفَّى said of sleep too.

why.bs: „Uzet će vam duše melek smrti“ – melek kao subjekt.
why.en: “The angel of death … will gather you” — an angel as subject.

why.bs: „I uzmi nam duše s dobrima“ – molba Allahu da On uzme dušu.
why.en: “And make us die the death of the righteous” — asking Allah to take the soul.

title.en: To ask and to seek a ruling

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače ‚pitati‘; razlikuju se po tome šta se traži: odgovor ili stvar uopće, ili rješenje nejasnog pitanja.
shared.en: Both verbs mean ‘to ask’; they differ in what is sought: an answer or a thing in general, or the resolution of an unclear question.

tellApart.bs: Pitati za bilo šta, ili tražiti nešto (i imetak) → سَأَلَ; pitati za rješenje nejasnog pitanja, tražiti fetvu, tumačenje → اِسْتَفْتَى.
tellApart.en: To ask about anything, or to ask for something (property too) → سَأَلَ; to ask for the answer to an unclear question, a ruling or an interpretation → اِسْتَفْتَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries سأل, فتى
notes: ar-Rāġib: suʾāl is a request for knowledge (answered by tongue, or by writing) or for property (answered by hand) — attributed to him.
ar-Rāġib: futyā and fatwā are the answer to what is unclear in rulings; istaftā is asking for it — attributed to him.
اِسْتَفْتَى is used of a dream's interpretation (12:41) and of asking someone's opinion in argument (37:11, 18:22): our reading of all 6 places.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, tražiti znanje ili tražiti imetak. Najopćija riječ za pitanje: od pitanja o mladom mjesecu do pitanja o samom Allahu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to ask for knowledge or to ask for wealth. The most general word for asking: from questions about the new moons to asking about Allah Himself.

why.bs: „Pitaju te o mlađacima“ – pitanje radi znanja.
why.en: “They ask thee … of new moons” — a question for knowledge.

why.bs: „A kad te robovi Moji pitaju za Mene – pa Ja sam blizu.“
why.en: “And when My servants question thee concerning Me, then surely I am nigh.”

why.bs: Ne prose od ljudi navaljujući – سَأَلَ kao traženje imetka.
why.en: They do not ask people persistently — سَأَلَ as asking for property.

meaning.en: to seek a ruling, to consult

nuance.bs: Tražiti odgovor na nejasno pitanje – fetvu u propisu, tumačenje sna ili mišljenje. Prema ar-Rāġibu, fetva je odgovor na ono što je nejasno u propisima.
nuance.en: To ask for the answer to an unclear question — a ruling, a dream's interpretation, or an opinion. According to ar-Rāġib, a fatwā is the answer to what is unclear in rulings.

why.bs: „Pitaju te za fetvu. Reci: ‚O kelali vam fetvu daje Allah‘“ – pitanje o nasljedstvu.
why.en: “They ask thee for a pronouncement. Say: Allah hath pronounced for you concerning distant kindred” — a question of inheritance.

why.bs: „I pitaju te za fetvu o ženama. Reci: ‚Allah vam daje fetvu o njima‘“ – propis koji odgovara na pitanje.
why.en: “They consult thee concerning women. Say: Allah giveth you decree concerning them” — a ruling that answers the question.

why.bs: Jusuf zatvorenicima: „Odlučena je stvar o kojoj tražite mišljenje“ – tumačenje sna.
why.en: Joseph to the prisoners: “Thus is the case judged concerning which ye did inquire” — a dream's interpretation.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače tražiti od nekoga da nešto čini; razlikuju se po tonu: zapovijed, ili brižna preporuka praćena savjetom.
shared.en: Both verbs mean asking someone to do something; they differ in tone: a command, or a caring charge joined with counsel.

tellApart.bs: Narediti, zapovjediti – i dobro i zlo → أَمَرَ; oporučiti, preporučiti uz savjet i brigu, nešto što treba trajno čuvati → وَصَّى.
tellApart.en: To command, to order — good or evil → أَمَرَ; to enjoin, to charge with counsel and care, something to be kept for good → وَصَّى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries أمر, وصى
notes: ar-Rāġib: waṣiyya is directing another to something to be acted on, joined with admonition — attributed to him.
That وَصَّى in the Quran is said of what is to be kept across generations (2:132, 42:13) and of the core commandments (6:151–153) is our reading of its 10 places.
Form IV أَوْصَى (يُوصِيكُمُ اللَّهُ, 4:11) is a separate verb in the catalogue and not a member.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Narediti, tražiti da se nešto učini. Kaže se za Allahove naredbe, ali i za ljude i šejtana koji naređuju zlo.
nuance.en: To command, to require something to be done. Said of Allah's commands, but also of people and of Satan commanding evil.

why.bs: „Allah naređuje pravdu i dobročinstvo“ – Allahova naredba.
why.en: “Allah enjoineth justice and kindness” — Allah's command.

why.bs: „Allah vam zaista naređuje da zakoljete jednu kravu“ – jasna, određena naredba.
why.en: “Allah commandeth you that ye sacrifice a cow” — a plain, specific command.

why.bs: „Allah, zaista, ne naređuje razvrat“ – أَمَرَ o onome što ljudi pogrešno pripisuju Allahu.
why.en: “Allah, verily, enjoineth not lewdness” — أَمَرَ of what people wrongly ascribe to Allah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, uputiti nekoga na ono što treba činiti, uz opomenu i savjet. Zato وَصَّى stoji uz ono što se predaje u amanet: vjeru koju otac ostavlja sinovima, dobročinstvo prema roditeljima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, directing someone to what is to be done, joined with admonition. So وَصَّى stands with what is handed on in trust: the faith a father leaves his sons, kindness to parents.

why.bs: Ibrahim je to oporučio sinovima svojim, i Jakub – vjera predana u amanet.
why.en: Abraham instructed his sons with it, and so did Jacob — faith handed on in trust.

why.bs: „Oporučili smo čovjeku dobročinstvo prema roditeljima“ – trajna preporuka.
why.en: “We have enjoined on man kindness to parents” — a lasting charge.

why.bs: Nakon niza zapovijedi i zabrana: „Eto, to vam On nalaže“ – sažetak uz brigu i savjet.
why.en: After a series of commands and prohibitions: “This He hath command[ed] you” — a summary given with care and counsel.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače ‚zabraniti‘; razlikuju se po tome je li u prvom planu čin odvraćanja ili proglašavanje nečega nedozvoljenim.
shared.en: Both verbs mean ‘to forbid’; they differ in whether the act of restraining or the declaring of a thing unlawful is in view.

tellApart.bs: Zabraniti, odvratiti nekoga od djela – reći mu ‚nemoj‘ → نَهَى; učiniti nešto haram, nedozvoljenim, ili uskratiti → حَرَّمَ.
tellApart.en: To forbid, to hold someone back from a deed — to tell him ‘do not’ → نَهَى; to make a thing ḥarām, unlawful, or to withhold it → حَرَّمَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نهى, حرم
notes: ar-Rāġib: nahy is restraining from a thing; ḥarām is what is withheld, and taḥrīm may be by Allah's decree in creation (taskhīr, 28:12), by a human, or by the sharīʿa — attributed to him.
That people are reproached in the Quran for ḥarrama without authority (6:140, 7:32) is read from the ayat.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, odvratiti od nečega. نَهَى je obraćanje osobi: ‚ne čini‘. Zabranjuje Allah, Poslanik, ali i ljudi – i dobro i zlo.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, restraining from a thing. نَهَى is addressed to a person: ‘do not’. Allah forbids, the Messenger forbids, and people forbid too — good and evil alike.

why.bs: „A od onoga što vam on zabrani – suzdržite se“ – zabrana Poslanika.
why.en: “Whatsoever he forbiddeth, abstain (from it)” — the Messenger's prohibition.

why.bs: Šejtan: „Gospodar vaš nije vam ovo drvo zabranio ni zbog čega drugog nego da ne postanete meleki…“ – zabrana upućena Ademu i njegovoj ženi.
why.en: Satan: “Your Lord forbade you from this tree only lest ye should become angels…” — a prohibition addressed to Adam and his wife.

why.bs: Onaj ko zabranjuje – čak i robu dok klanja (96:10) – نَهَى i za zlu zabranu.
why.en: The one who forbids — even a servant at prayer (96:10) — نَهَى for a wicked prohibition too.

nuance.bs: Proglasiti nešto haramom, nedozvoljenim – propis koji važi, a ne samo zabrana upućena osobi. Prema ar-Rāġibu, uskraćivanje može biti i Allahovom odredbom u stvaranju: Musa nije htio uzeti prsa nijedne dojilje.
nuance.en: To declare a thing ḥarām, unlawful — a standing ruling, not only a prohibition addressed to a person. According to ar-Rāġib, withholding may also be by Allah's decree in creation: the infant Moses would take no wet-nurse.

why.bs: „Reci: Ko je zabranio Allahov ukras…?“ – ukor onima koji haramom proglašavaju bez prava.
why.en: “Say: Who hath forbidden the adornment of Allah…?” — reproach for declaring things unlawful without right.

why.bs: „I Mi smo mu ranije uskratili dojilje“ – taḥrīm kao Allahova odredba, ne propis.
why.en: “We had before forbidden foster-mothers for him” — taḥrīm as Allah's decree, not a law.

why.bs: „Dođite da vam proučim šta vam je vaš Gospodar zabranio“ – haram kao propis.
why.en: The call to come and hear what your Lord has made unlawful for you (حَرَّمَ) — ḥarām as a ruling.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače ‚ostaviti‘; razlikuju se po obliku i tonu: ostavljanje uopće, ili ostavljanje onoga čemu se ne pridaje vrijednost.
shared.en: Both verbs mean ‘to leave’; they differ in form and tone: leaving in general, or leaving what one sets no store by.

tellApart.bs: Ostaviti, napustiti – svojevoljno ili prisilno; ostaviti iza sebe nasljedstvo → تَرَكَ; pustiti, okaniti se, ‚ostavi ih‘ – samo u sadašnjem vremenu i imperativu → وَذَرَ.
tellApart.en: To leave, abandon — by choice or by force; to leave an inheritance behind → تَرَكَ; to let be, give up, ‘leave them’ — only in present and imperative → وَذَرَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ترك, وذر
notes: ar-Rāġib: tark is rejecting a thing, intentionally and by choice, or by force and necessity — attributed to him.
ar-Rāġib: one says yadharu ash-shayʾ, 'he leaves the thing', i.e. casts it off for setting little store by it, and its past tense is not used — attributed to him.
That وَذَرَ appears in the Quran only in the present and the imperative (all 45 uses) is our observation; the headword وَذَرَ is the dictionary form.
74:11 (dharnī, 'leave Me with him') is not cited: it is an ayah of threat whose tafsir needs more room than a line.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, odbaciti nešto namjerno i svojevoljno, ili prisilno. Kaže se i za ono što umrli ostavi iza sebe.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to reject a thing intentionally and by choice, or by force and necessity. Said too of what the dead leave behind.

why.bs: Jusuf: „Ja sam ostavio vjeroispovijest ljudi koji u Allaha ne vjeruju“ – svojevoljno napuštanje.
why.en: Joseph: “Lo! I have forsaken the religion of folk who believe not in Allah” — leaving by choice.

why.bs: Koliko su samo vrtova i izvora ostavili! – ostavljanje prisilno, propašću.
why.en: How much they left behind of gardens and springs — leaving by force, in ruin.

why.bs: Muškarcima pripada dio onoga što ostave roditelji – تَرَكَ za nasljedstvo.
why.en: For men is a share of what the parents leave — تَرَكَ for inheritance.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ostaviti nešto kao da ga odbacuješ jer mu ne pridaješ vrijednost; prošlo vrijeme se, kaže, ne koristi – u Kur'anu se javlja samo u sadašnjem vremenu i imperativu (ذَرْ, ذَرُوا).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to leave a thing as if casting it off, setting little store by it; its past tense, he says, is not used — in the Quran it occurs only in present and imperative (ذَرْ, ذَرُوا).

why.bs: Kad se pozove na džumu, „ostavite trgovanje“ – ostavite ono što je inače dozvoljeno.
why.en: When the call is made for Jumuʿah, “leave your trading” — set aside what is otherwise permitted.

why.bs: „Okanite se onoga što je preostalo od kamate“ – odreknite se potraživanja, jer je tako naređeno.
why.en: “Give up what remaineth (due to you) from usury” — give up a claim, set aside at Allah's command.

why.bs: „Zatim ih pusti da se igraju u svom praznom razgovoru“ – pusti ih.
why.en: “Then leave them to their play of cavilling” — let them be.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače ‚sakupiti‘; razlikuju se po tome je li u prvom planu samo spajanje ili izvođenje i tjeranje mnoštva na jedno mjesto.
shared.en: Both verbs mean ‘to gather’; they differ in whether mere bringing together or driving a multitude out to one place is in view.

tellApart.bs: Sakupiti, spojiti – stvari, imetak, ljude → جَمَعَ; okupiti mnoštvo izvodeći ga i goneći na jedno mjesto – i na Sudnji dan → حَشَرَ.
tellApart.en: To gather, bring together — things, wealth, people → جَمَعَ; to assemble a multitude by bringing it out and driving it to one place — the Day of Judgement too → حَشَرَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries جمع, حشر
notes: ar-Rāġib: jamʿ is bringing a thing together by drawing its parts close; ḥashr is bringing a group out of where they settled and driving them to war and the like, and is said only of a group — attributed to him.
20:124–125 (wa-naḥshuruhu … ḥashartanī aʿmā) use حَشَرَ of one person (both ayat) on the Day of Judgement: shown beside ar-Rāġib's rule as a counter-example.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, sakupiti stvar približavajući njene dijelove jedan drugom. Kaže se za kosti, za imetak, za spletke – i za sakupljanje ljudi na Sudnjem danu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, bringing a thing together by drawing its parts close. Said of bones, of wealth, of schemes — and of gathering people on the Day of Judgement.

why.bs: „Zar čovjek misli da Mi njegove kosti nećemo sakupiti?“ – spajanje dijelova.
why.en: “Thinketh man that We shall not assemble his bones?” — bringing parts together.

why.bs: Onaj ko gomila imetak i prebrojava ga – جَمَعَ za imetak.
why.en: Who collects wealth and counts it — جَمَعَ for wealth.

why.bs: „Dan kada vas On sakupi za Dan sakupljanja“ – i جَمَعَ se kaže za Sudnji dan.
why.en: “The day when He shall gather you unto the Day of Assembling” — جَمَعَ is said of the Last Day too.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, izvesti skupinu ljudi s njihovog mjesta i potjerati ih (u boj i sl.), i kaže se samo za skupinu. U Kur'anu je najčešće sabiranje na Sudnjem danu; kaže se i za pojedinca (20:124–125).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to bring a group out of their place and drive them on (to battle and the like), said only of a group. In the Quran most often the mustering on the Day of Judgement; it is also said of a single person (20:124–125).

why.bs: Musa: „i neka ljudi budu okupljeni u prijepodne“ – okupljanje mnoštva na jedno mjesto.
why.en: Moses: “let the people assemble when the sun hath risen high” — a multitude brought to one place.

why.bs: „I kad divlje zvijeri budu okupljene“ – mnoštvo dovedeno na jedno mjesto.
why.en: “And when the wild beasts are herded together” — a multitude brought to one place.

why.bs: „Gospodaru moj, zašto si me slijepog doveo (حَشَرْتَنِي)…?“ – حَشَرَ za pojedinca, protivprimjer pravilu.
why.en: “My Lord! Wherefor hast Thou gathered me (hither) blind” (حَشَرْتَنِي) — حَشَرَ of one person, a counter-example to the rule.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače ‚uništiti‘; razlikuju se po širini: propast u svakom obliku, ili potpuno zatiranje.
shared.en: Both verbs mean ‘to destroy’; they differ in breadth: perishing in any form, or utter destruction.

tellApart.bs: Uništiti, upropastiti – narode, ali i usjeve, imetak → أَهْلَكَ; zatrti, razoriti do temelja → دَمَّرَ.
tellApart.en: To destroy, cause to perish — peoples, but also crops and wealth → أَهْلَكَ; to wipe out, raze to the ground → دَمَّرَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries هلك, دمر
notes: ar-Rāġib: halāk is used in several senses — loss of a thing, its corruption, death, and passing away altogether — attributed to him.

That دَمَّرَ is said in 7 of its 8 places of Allah's destruction of peoples and their works, and once of the wind 'by the command of its Lord' (46:25), and that its doubled form and the cognate accusative (17:16 tadmīran) stress completeness, is our observation, not a lexicographer's wording.
17:16 has both verbs: nuhlika then dammarnāhā.

meaning.en: to destroy, to cause to perish

nuance.bs: Uništiti, dovesti do propasti. Najčešće o narodima koje je Allah uništio zbog njihovih grijeha, ali i o čovjeku koji upropaštava usjeve ili imetak.
nuance.en: To destroy, bring to ruin. Most often of peoples Allah destroyed for their sins, but also of a man who ruins crops or squanders wealth.

why.bs: „Zar ne vide koliko smo pokoljenja prije njih uništili?“
why.en: “See they not how many a generation We destroyed before them?”

why.bs: Kad se okrene (ili: kad dođe na vlast – tefsir se razilazi), nastoji da uništi usjeve i porod – čovjek kao uzrok propasti.
why.en: When he turns away (or: gains authority — tafsir differs), he strives to destroy crops and offspring — a man as the cause of ruin.

why.bs: „Uništio sam silan imetak“ – أَهْلَكَ i za rasipanje imetka.
why.en: “I have destroyed vast wealth” — أَهْلَكَ also of squandering wealth.

nuance.bs: Uništiti potpuno, ne ostaviti ništa. U Kur'anu (naše zapažanje) gotovo uvijek o Allahovom kažnjavanju naroda i njihovih djela; jednom o vjetru koji razara „po naredbi svoga Gospodara“ (46:25).
nuance.en: To destroy completely, leaving nothing. In the Quran (our observation) almost always of Allah's punishment of peoples and their works; once of the wind that destroys “by commandment of its Lord” (46:25).

why.bs: Kad hoćemo da uništimo (نُهْلِكَ) neki grad… pa ga potpuno zatremo (دَمَّرْنَاهَا تَدْمِيرًا) – oba glagola, drugi kao vrhunac.
why.en: When We intend to destroy (نُهْلِكَ) a city… and We destroy it with complete destruction (دَمَّرْنَاهَا تَدْمِيرًا) — both verbs, the second as the climax.

why.bs: „I razorili smo sve što su gradili faraon i njegov narod“ – zatiranje djela.
why.en: “We annihilated (all) that Pharaoh and his folk had done” — wiping out works.

why.bs: Vjetar „koji sve razara po naredbi svoga Gospodara“ – jedini subjekt koji nije Allah, a i on po Njegovoj naredbi.
why.en: A wind “destroying all things by commandment of its Lord” — the one subject other than Allah, and that by His command.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače ‚steći, zaraditi‘ – i dobra i loša djela; razlikuju se po uloženom naporu i po tome za koga se stiče.
shared.en: Both verbs mean ‘to earn, to gain’ — good deeds and bad; they differ in the effort involved and in for whom the gain is made.

tellApart.bs: Steći, zaraditi uopće – imetak, dobro ili zlo → كَسَبَ; steći za sebe (tefsir: s naporom) → اِكْتَسَبَ.
tellApart.en: To earn, gain in general — wealth, good or evil → كَسَبَ; to acquire for oneself (tafsir: with effort) → اِكْتَسَبَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries كسب
notes: ar-Rāġib: kasb is what a person seeks to gain benefit and a share by; iktisāb is said only of what one gains for oneself, so every iktisāb is kasb but not every kasb is iktisāb; he cites 2:286 — attributed to him.

On 2:286 tafsir often explains why good is with kasabat and evil with iktasabat: the Form VIII stresses effort, and the soul strives harder after evil it desires. Given as the explanation of many mufassirun, not pinned to one; some treat the variation as stylistic only. 'Form VIII stresses effort' is theirs, not ar-Rāġib's (blind review).
4:32 (iktasabū / iktasabna, of men's and women's earnings) shows اِكْتَسَبَ used for what is not evil; so the 2:286 contrast is not a rule of the word.
اِكْتَسَبَ: 5 uses in 4 ayat.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ono čime čovjek nastoji steći korist i udio. Opća riječ: zarađeni imetak, dobra djela i grijesi – sve što čovjek ‚zaradi‘.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, what a person seeks to gain benefit and a share by. The general word: earned wealth, good deeds and sins — all that a person ‘earns’.

why.bs: „Njoj u korist je ono što je zaradila (كَسَبَتْ), a na njenu štetu ono što je stekla (اكْتَسَبَتْ)“ – oba glagola.
why.en: “For it (is only) that which it hath earned (كَسَبَتْ), and against it (only) that which it hath deserved (اكْتَسَبَتْ)” — both verbs.

why.bs: „Neće mu pomoći ni imetak njegov ni ono što je zaradio“ – zarada, imetak.
why.en: “His wealth and gains will not exempt him” — earnings, wealth.

why.bs: „Ko zaradi zlo djelo…“ – كَسَبَ i za zlo.
why.en: Whoever earns an evil deed (كَسَبَ سَيِّئَةً) — كَسَبَ for evil too.

meaning.en: to acquire, to earn for oneself

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, kaže se samo za ono što čovjek stiče za sebe. Mnogi mufessiri dodaju da oblik VIII podrazumijeva napor i time tumače 2:286, mada to ne prihvataju svi, a u 4:32 riječ je o dozvoljenoj zaradi muškaraca i žena.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, said only of what a person gains for himself. Many mufassirun add that Form VIII implies effort and explain 2:286 by it, though not all accept this, and 4:32 uses it for the lawful earnings of men and women.

why.bs: اكْتَسَبَتْ uz ono čime je duša opterećena – prema mnogim mufessirima: napor koji duša ulaže u ono što je privlači.
why.en: اكْتَسَبَتْ with what the soul bears — according to many mufassirun: the effort a soul spends on what draws it.

why.bs: Muškarcima pripada udio od onoga što zarade, i ženama od onoga što zarade – اِكْتَسَبَ bez ikakvog prizvuka zla.
why.en: For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women a share of what they have earned — اِكْتَسَبَ with no shade of evil.

why.bs: Svakom od njih – grijeh koji je stekao – اِكْتَسَبَ za lično stečen grijeh.
why.en: For every person among them is what he has earned of the sin — اِكْتَسَبَ for a sin acquired in person.

shared.bs: Obje riječi označavaju čovjeka u oskudici i obje su među primaocima zekata (9:60); učenjaci se razilaze ko je od njih u većoj nevolji.
shared.en: Both words denote a person in want and both are among the recipients of zakat (9:60); scholars differ over which of the two is in greater need.

tellApart.bs: Siromah, onaj ko je u potrebi – i čovjek u potrebi prema Allahu → فَقِير; nevoljnik, potrebit, najčešće uz siroče i putnika kao onaj koga treba nahraniti → مِسْكِين; ko je od njih u većoj nevolji, učenjaci se razilaze.
tellApart.en: The poor, one in need — and man in his need of Allah → فَقِير; the needy, most often named with the orphan and traveller as one to be fed → مِسْكِين; which is worse off, scholars differ.

sources: Tafsir and fiqh on 9:60 (e.g. al-Qurṭubī, al-Jāmiʿ li-aḥkām al-Qurʾān) — the views on faqīr and miskīn
notes: Scholars differ: in the Shāfiʿī view the faqīr is worse off (cf. 18:79, masākīn who own a boat); in the Ḥanafī view the miskīn is (cf. 90:16, miskīnan ḏā matraba, 'in the dust'). Both views and their proof ayat are given; neither is chosen.
That فَقِير is also said of man's need before Allah (35:15) and of Musa's prayer (28:24), while مِسْكِين is not used that way, is our observation of all places.
فَقِير includes the plural فُقَرَاء and مِسْكِين the plural مَسَاكِين: one lemma each in the corpus.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Onaj ko je u potrebi, kome nešto nedostaje. Kaže se i za čovjekovu potrebu prema Allahu: svi su ljudi ‚siromasi‘ pred Allahom, a Musa je za sebe rekao da je فَقِير dobra koje mu Allah spusti.
nuance.en: One in need, who lacks something. Said too of man's need of Allah: all people are ‘poor’ before Allah, and Moses called himself فَقِير of whatever good Allah sends down.

why.bs: Zekat pripada siromasima (فُقَرَاء) i nevoljnicima (مَسَاكِين) – obje riječi, kao dvije skupine.
why.en: Zakat is for the poor (فُقَرَاء) and the needy (مَسَاكِين) — both words, as two groups.

why.bs: „O ljudi, vi ste siromasi kojima je Allah potreban, a Allah je Neovisni, Hvaljeni“ – potreba svakog stvorenja.
why.en: “O mankind! Ye are the poor in your relation to Allah. And Allah! He is the Absolute” — the need of every creature.

why.bs: Siromasi koji ne dosađuju ljudima traženjem; zbog njihove suzdržanosti neupućeni ih smatraju bogatima.
why.en: The poor who do not ask people persistently; because of their restraint the ignorant think them self-sufficient.

nuance.bs: Potrebit, u oskudici; često se spominje uz siroče i putnika kao onaj kome treba dati hranu. Učenjaci se razilaze je li u većoj nevolji od فَقِير.
nuance.en: One in want; often named with the orphan and the traveller as one to be fed. Scholars differ on whether he is in greater need than the فَقِير.

why.bs: Lađa je pripadala nekim siromasima (مَسَاكِين) – imaju lađu, a ipak su مِسْكِين: dokaz onih koji kažu da je فَقِير u većoj nevolji.
why.en: The ship belonged to poor people (مَسَاكِين) — they own a ship yet are مِسْكِين: the proof of those who hold the faqīr worse off.

why.bs: „ili nevoljnika koji u prašini leži“ (ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ) – dokaz onih koji kažu da je مِسْكِين u većoj nevolji.
why.en: “Or some poor wretch in misery” (ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ) — the proof of those who hold the miskīn worse off.

why.bs: Onaj ko ne podstiče da se nahrani siromah – مِسْكِين kao onaj kome treba hrana.
why.en: Who does not encourage the feeding of the poor — the مِسْكِين as one who must be fed.

shared.bs: Obje riječi označavaju onoga ko je uz tebe i stoji za tebe; u Kur'anu često stoje jedna uz drugu, a razlikuju se po vrsti podrške.
shared.en: Both words denote one who is on your side and stands up for you; in the Quran they often stand together, and they differ in the kind of support.

tellApart.bs: Bliski zaštitnik, onaj ko se brine o tvojim poslovima, prijatelj, srodnik → وَلِيّ; pomagač koji pomaže protiv neprijatelja i daje pobjedu → نَصِير.
tellApart.en: A close protector, one who takes charge of your affairs, a friend, a kinsman → وَلِيّ; a helper who aids against an enemy and gives victory → نَصِير.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ولى, نصر
notes: ar-Rāġib: walāʾ is two or more things being so close that nothing comes between them, used of nearness in place, kinship, religion, friendship, help and belief — attributed to him.
That walī is the one who takes care of one's affairs and naṣīr the one who aids against an enemy is how tafsir often explains the pair; stated as such, not pinned to one mufassir.
That the two often stand together (2:107, 4:45, 9:116) is read from the ayat.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries ولى (2026-11-06): 4 attributed points confirmed
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): نصر read and added to `verified` (consistent with the texts; no attributed point rests on it).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od bliskosti u kojoj ništa ne stoji između dvoje. Zato وَلِيّ znači zaštitnika, prijatelja, saveznika i najbližeg srodnika – onoga ko preuzima brigu o tebi.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from a nearness with nothing between the two. So وَلِيّ means protector, friend, ally and nearest kinsman — one who takes charge of you.

why.bs: „Allah je zaštitnik onih koji vjeruju, On ih izvodi iz tmina na svjetlost“ – Allahova briga o vjernicima.
why.en: “Allah is the Protecting Guardian of those who believe. He bringeth them out of darkness into light” — Allah's care for the believers.

why.bs: Ako neko bude ubijen nepravedno, njegovom bliskom srodniku (وَلِيّ), staratelju njegovog prava, dali smo vlast.
why.en: “Whoso is slain wrongfully, We have given power unto his heir” — the heir is the وَلِيّ, the guardian of his right.

why.bs: „I nemate mimo Allaha ni zaštitnika ni pomagača“ – وَلِيّ i نَصِير zajedno.
why.en: “Ye have not, beside Allah, any guardian or helper” — وَلِيّ and نَصِير together.

nuance.bs: Onaj ko pomaže i daje pobjedu (نَصْر) protiv neprijatelja ili nevolje. Često stoji odmah iza وَلِيّ ili مَوْلَى.
nuance.en: One who helps and gives victory (نَصْر) against an enemy or a hardship. It often comes right after وَلِيّ or مَوْلَى.

why.bs: „Allah je dovoljan kao zaštitnik i Allah je dovoljan kao pomagač.“
why.en: “Allah is sufficient as a Guardian, and Allah is sufficient as a Supporter.”

why.bs: „Divan li je On Zaštitnik i divan li je Pomagač!“ – مَوْلَى i نَصِير.
why.en: “A blessed Patron and a blessed Helper!” — مَوْلَى and نَصِير.

why.bs: Isti ajet: zaštitnik koji se brine, pomagač koji brani.
why.en: The same ayah: a protector who takes care, a helper who defends.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače sumnju; obično se razlikuju po tome je li to puko kolebanje između dvije mogućnosti ili sumnja praćena nemirom i nepovjerenjem.
shared.en: Both words mean doubt; they tend to differ in whether it is a bare wavering between two possibilities or doubt that brings unease and suspicion.

tellApart.bs: Kolebanje između dvije mogućnosti, bez prevage → شَكّ; sumnja s nemirom i nepovjerenjem – ‚nema sumnje u nju‘ → رَيْب.
tellApart.en: Wavering between two possibilities with no preponderance → شَكّ; doubt with unease and suspicion — ‘no doubt about it’ → رَيْب.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries شكك
Tafsir on 2:2 — the sense of rayb
notes: ar-Rāġib: shakk is two opposites being equal in a person's mind, with no sign tipping towards either — attributed to him.

That rayb is doubt joined with unease and suspicion is how tafsir often explains it on 2:2; stated as such. ar-Rāġib's own definition differs: rayb is imagining something about a thing that is then uncovered (entry ريب).
The two meet in 11:62 and 34:54 (shakk … murīb), where murīb is from the root of rayb; cited under شَكّ.
52:30 rayb al-manūn: tafsir explains it as the accidents of time, or death; given as tafsir.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries شكك, ريب (2026-11-06): 3 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/1 (improved): He does not speak of unease: he defines rayb as suspecting something in a thing that is then uncovered, and rība as a sign of rancour and little certainty
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): entries cited as the book spells them (شك → شكك).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, stanje kada su dvije suprotne mogućnosti u čovjekovom umu jednake i nijedna ne preteže. Često se opisuje kao ‚sumnja koja uznemiruje‘ (مُرِيب).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the state in which two opposites are equal in the mind and neither tips the scale. Often described as a doubt ‘that disquiets’ (مُرِيب).

why.bs: „Zar ima sumnje u Allaha, Stvoritelja nebesa i Zemlje?“
why.en: “Can there be doubt concerning Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth?”

why.bs: „Mi smo, doista, u sumnji koja uznemiruje“ (شَكّ مُرِيب) – obje riječi: شَكّ i pridjev iz korijena رَيْب.
why.en: “We verily are in grave doubt” (شَكّ مُرِيب) — both: شَكّ and an adjective from the root of رَيْب.

why.bs: „Pa ako si u sumnji o onome što smo ti objavili…“ – uvjetna rečenica; prema većini mufessira ne podrazumijeva stvarnu sumnju kod Poslanika.
why.en: “If thou (Muhammad) art in doubt concerning that which We reveal unto thee…” — a conditional; most mufassirun hold it implies no actual doubt in the Prophet.

nuance.bs: Sumnja praćena nemirom i nepovjerenjem; tako je često tumači tefsir na početku sure el-Bekara. Kur'an njome kaže da u Knjigu i u Sudnji dan ‚nema sumnje‘.
nuance.en: Doubt joined with unease and suspicion; so tafsir often explains it at the opening of al-Baqarah. The Quran uses it to say there is ‘no doubt’ about the Book and the Last Day.

why.bs: „To je Knjiga u kojoj nema sumnje“ – prvo što Kur'an kaže o sebi.
why.en: “This is the Scripture whereof there is no doubt” — the first thing the Quran says of itself.

why.bs: „Ako ste u sumnji u proživljenje…“ – رَيْب o ahiretu, a odmah zatim dokaz.
why.en: “If ye are in doubt concerning the Resurrection…” — رَيْب about the hereafter, followed at once by proof.

why.bs: „Čekamo da ga zadesi udarac sudbine“ (رَيْب الْمَنُون) – ovdje رَيْب znači nedaću, ne sumnju; tefsir: nedaće vremena ili smrt.
why.en: “(One) for whom we may expect the accident of time” (رَيْب الْمَنُون) — here رَيْب means a calamity, not doubt; tafsir: the accidents of time, or death.

shared.bs: Sva tri glagola govore o opraštanju grijeha; razlikuju se po slici: prekrivanje i zaštita, brisanje i odustajanje od kazne, ili pokrivanje grijeha kao da nije učinjen.
shared.en: All three verbs speak of forgiving sins; they differ in the image: covering and shielding, erasing and forgoing the penalty, or covering the sin as though it were not done.

tellApart.bs: Oprostiti i zaštititi od kazne → غَفَرَ; preći preko, ne kazniti – Allahov oprost, a često i oprost među ljudima (u odmazdi, mehru, uvredi) → عَفَا; izbrisati, pokriti loša djela → كَفَّرَ.
tellApart.en: To forgive and shield from punishment → غَفَرَ; to pardon, let pass unpunished — Allah's pardon, and often pardon between people (in retaliation, bridal due, offence) → عَفَا; to remove, cover over bad deeds → كَفَّرَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries غفر, عفا, كفر
notes: ar-Rāġib: ghafr is clothing a thing with what shields it from dirt (hence mighfar, the helmet); maghfira from Allah is His shielding the servant from punishment — attributed to him.
ar-Rāġib: takfīr of a sin is covering it until it is as if it had not been done — attributed to him.
That ʿafw is from ʿafā, 'to efface' (as wind effaces a trace) is a common explanation in tafsir; given as such. Which of maghfira and ʿafw is the greater is not decided here: tafsir differs.
The ordering in 2:286 (wa-ʿfu ʿannā wa-ghfir lanā) is cited as it stands, without a claim about why.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
