nuance.bs: Propisani post: ramazanski post i post kao iskup (kefaret) u propisima. U Kur'anu (naše zapažanje) uvijek u tom pravnom značenju.
nuance.en: The prescribed fast: the fast of Ramadan and the fast of expiation in the rulings. In the Quran (our observation) always in this legal sense.

why.bs: „Propisan vam je post (الصِّيَام) kao što je bio propisan onima prije vas“ – temeljni ajet o postu.
why.en: “Fasting (الصِّيَام) is prescribed for you, even as it was prescribed for those before you” — the founding ayah of the fast.

why.bs: „Dozvoljeno vam je da u noći posta prilazite svojim ženama…“ – propisi o postu i noći.
why.en: “It is made lawful for you to go in unto your wives on the night of the fast…” — the rulings of the fast and its nights.

why.bs: „…onda post dva uzastopna mjeseca“ – post kao iskup.
why.en: “Let him fast for two successive months” — fasting as expiation.

nuance.bs: Samo jednom u Kur'anu: Merjemin zavjet. Odmah iza njega stoji „pa danas neću razgovarati ni s jednim čovjekom“ (19:26), pa ga tefsir uglavnom tumači kao šutnju; neki dodaju da je post u njihovom zakonu uključivao i šutnju.
nuance.en: Only once in the Quran: Mary's vow. It is followed at once by “and may not speak this day to any mortal” (19:26), so tafsir mostly explains it as silence; some add that fasting in their law included silence.

why.bs: „Ja sam Milostivom zavjetovala suzdržavanje (صَوْمًا), pa danas ni sa kim od ljudi neću razgovarati“ – suzdržavanje od govora.
why.en: “Lo! I have vowed a fast (صَوْمًا) unto the Beneficent, and may not speak this day to any mortal” — holding back from speech.

nuance.bs: Glagol od kojeg su obje imenice. U Kur'anu samo dva puta, oba puta u ajetima o postu (2:184–185).
nuance.en: The verb both nouns come from. Only twice in the Quran, both times in the ayat on fasting (2:184–185).

why.bs: „A bolje vam je da postite (تَصُومُوا)“ – glagol u propisima o postu.
why.en: “And that ye fast (تَصُومُوا) is better for you” — the verb within the rulings of the fast.

why.bs: „Pa ko od vas bude prisutan u tom mjesecu, neka ga posti“ – zapovijed ramazanskog posta.
why.en: “Whosoever of you is present, let him fast the month” — the command of the Ramadan fast.

shared.bs: Obje riječi označavaju putovanje Allahovoj Kući radi obreda. Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḥajj u osnovi znači namjeru (polazak) u posjetu, a ʿumra posjetu koja održava naklonost; šerijat je obje vezao za Kabu.
shared.en: Both words name the journey to Allah's House for its rites. According to ar-Rāġib, ḥajj at root means setting out to visit, and ʿumra a visit that keeps affection alive; the Sharia tied both to the Kaaba.

tellApart.bs: Hadž, u poznatim mjesecima, obaveza onome ko može → حَجّ; umra, posjeta Kabi, koja nije vezana za te mjesece → عُمْرَة.
tellApart.en: Hajj, in the well-known months, a duty on whoever is able → حَجّ; umrah, a visit to the Kaaba not tied to those months → عُمْرَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حج, عمر
Fiqh on 2:196 and 3:97 (whether umrah is obligatory)
notes: ar-Rāġib: the root of ḥajj is setting out to visit, in the Sharia setting out for the House of Allah to perform the rites; ʿumra is a visit, in the Sharia the particular visit — paraphrased and attributed to him.

That hajj is bound to its months (2:197) while umrah may be made at any time is the common ground of fiqh. Whether umrah is obligatory is disputed (Shāfiʿī and Ḥanbalī: yes, with 2:196; Ḥanafī and Mālikī: a sunna); both views are named, neither chosen.
حَجّ sums the corpus's lemmas حَجّ and حِجّ (3:97 is read ḥijju in Ḥafṣ).
Blind review: 'only in 2:196' restricted to the noun (the verb iʿtamara is in 2:158).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries حج, عمر (2026-11-06): 6 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (improved): Confirmed, and he glosses ʿumra more precisely as a visit in which affection is kept alive (ʿimārat al-wudd), tying it to its root

nuance.bs: Hodočašće Kabi u određeno vrijeme, s Arefatom i ostalim obredima. Kur'an ga propisuje svakome ko može do Kuće doći.
nuance.en: The pilgrimage to the Kaaba at its set time, with ʿArafa and its other rites. The Quran makes it a duty on whoever is able to reach the House.

why.bs: „Hadž ima svoje poznate mjesece“ – hadž vezan za vrijeme.
why.en: “The pilgrimage is (in) the well-known months” — hajj bound to its time.

why.bs: „Allahovo je pravo nad ljudima hodočašće Kuće (حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ) – za onoga ko može do nje doći“ – hadž kao obaveza.
why.en: “Pilgrimage to the House is a duty unto Allah for mankind, for him who can find a way thither” — hajj as a duty.

why.bs: „I oglasi među ljudima hadž“ – Ibrahimov poziv na hodočašće.
why.en: “And proclaim unto mankind the pilgrimage” — Abraham's call to the pilgrimage.

nuance.bs: Posjeta Kabi s obredima ihrama, tavafa i sa'ja, koja nije vezana za mjesece hadža. Imenica ʿumra spomenuta je samo u 2:196 (glagol iʿtamara i u 2:158), uz hadž; je li obavezna, učenjaci se razilaze.
nuance.en: A visit to the Kaaba with the rites of iḥrām, ṭawāf and saʿy, not bound to the months of hajj. The noun ʿumra occurs only in 2:196 (the verb iʿtamara also in 2:158), beside hajj; whether it is obligatory, scholars differ.

why.bs: „I radi Allaha hadž i umru obavite potpuno“ – obje riječi zajedno; neki učenjaci odatle zaključuju da je i umra obavezna, drugi ne.
why.en: “Perform the pilgrimage and the visit (العُمْرَة) for Allah” — both words together; some scholars infer from it that umrah is obligatory too, others do not.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače zakleti se. Razlikuje ih (naše zapažanje) to ko se u Kur'anu zaklinje i čemu zakletva služi.
shared.en: Both verbs mean to swear an oath. What tells them apart (our observation) is who swears in the Quran and what the oath is for.

tellApart.bs: Zakletva uopće – i neke Allahove zakletve (لَا أُقْسِمُ…) i zakletve ljudi → أَقْسَمَ; zakletva koja u Kur'anu gotovo uvijek prati laž ili izgovor licemjera → حَلَفَ.
tellApart.en: Oath in general — some of Allah's oaths (لَا أُقْسِمُ…) and people's → أَقْسَمَ; an oath that in the Quran almost always goes with the hypocrites' lie or excuse → حَلَفَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries قسم, حلف
Tafsir on لَا أُقْسِمُ (75:1, 90:1)
notes: That حَلَفَ describes, in 10 of its 11 ayat, the oaths of hypocrites or of people swearing to a lie (4:62, ch. 9, 58:14, 58:18), and is neutral only in the expiation ruling of 5:89, is our own observation of all places — not put in ar-Rāġib's mouth; some later writers draw a rule from it, which we do not.
That أَقْسَمَ is Allah's oath in 8 ayat (لَا أُقْسِمُ / فَلَا أُقْسِمُ) and otherwise people's oaths, often 'their strongest oaths' that are then belied, is our observation of all 19 ayat.
Tafsir differs on the لَا in لَا أُقْسِمُ: an emphasis ('Nay, I swear') or a rejection of what the deniers said before the oath; both are named.
Blind review: أَقْسَمَ carries only some of Allah's oaths — most use the particle wa-.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries قسم, حلف (2026-11-06): 2 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Opća riječ za zakletvu. Njime su izrečene neke Allahove zakletve u Kur'anu (većina ide česticom wa-, npr. وَالْفَجْرِ), a i zakletve ljudi – vjernika, svjedoka u propisima, ali i nevjernika ‚najtežim zakletvama‘.
nuance.en: The general word for an oath. Some of Allah's oaths in the Quran are spoken with it (most use the particle wa-, e.g. وَالْفَجْرِ), and so are people's — believers', witnesses' in the rulings, and disbelievers' ‘strongest oaths’.

why.bs: „Ne! Kunem se Danom kijameta“ – Allahova zakletva; tefsir se razilazi je li لَا pojačanje ili odbijanje tvrdnje poricatelja.
why.en: “Nay, I swear by the Day of Resurrection” — Allah's oath; tafsir differs on whether لَا is emphasis or a rejection of the deniers' claim.

why.bs: „I kunu se Allahom svojim najtežim zakletvama da će, ako im dođe znak, sigurno u njega vjerovati“ – zakletva nevjernika.
why.en: “And they swear a solemn oath by Allah that if there come unto them a portent they will believe therein” — the disbelievers' oath.

why.bs: Vlasnici vrta, „kad se zakleše da će ga sigurno obrati u svitanje“ – zakletva ljudi o vlastitoj namjeri.
why.en: The owners of the garden, “when they vowed that they would pluck its fruit next morning” — people's oath about their own plan.

nuance.bs: Također ‚zakleti se‘, ali u Kur'anu (naše zapažanje) gotovo uvijek o licemjerima i onima koji se kunu da bi prikrili laž ili se opravdali; neutralno je samo u propisu o iskupu za zakletvu.
nuance.en: Also ‘to swear’, but in the Quran (our observation) almost always of hypocrites and those who swear to cover a lie or excuse themselves; it is neutral only in the ruling on expiating an oath.

why.bs: „I kunu se Allahom da su oni doista od vas, a nisu od vas“ – zakletva licemjera.
why.en: “They swear by Allah that they are in truth of you, when they are not of you” — the hypocrites' oath.

why.bs: „…i kunu se na laž, a to znaju (يَحْلِفُونَ عَلَى الْكَذِبِ)“ – zakletva uz laž.
why.en: “…and they swear a false oath knowingly” (يَحْلِفُونَ عَلَى الْكَذِبِ) — an oath bound to a lie.

why.bs: „…to je iskup za vaše zakletve kad se zakunete“ – jedino neutralno mjesto: propis o zakletvi.
why.en: “…This is the expiation of your oaths when ye have sworn” — the one neutral place: the ruling on oaths.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače vijest, obavijest o nečemu. Prema ar-Rāġibu, نَبَأ je vijest od velike koristi koja donosi znanje ili jaku vjerovatnoću.
shared.en: Both words mean news, a report of something. According to ar-Rāġib, نَبَأ is news of great benefit that brings knowledge or a strong probability.

tellApart.bs: Važna vijest od velike koristi – kazivanja o vjerovjesnicima, nevidljivom svijetu i Sudnjem danu → نَبَأ; vijest, obavijest uopće, i ono što se o nekome zna → خَبَر.
tellApart.en: Weighty news of great benefit — accounts of prophets, the unseen and the Last Day → نَبَأ; news, information in general, and what is known about someone → خَبَر.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نبأ, خبر
notes: ar-Rāġib: nabaʾ is news of great benefit from which knowledge or strong probability arises, and news is not properly called nabaʾ until it has these three things — paraphrased and attributed to him.

That نَبَأ (with its plural أَنْبَاء) is mostly said of the stories of earlier prophets and peoples, of the unseen and of the Last Day, is our observation of all 29 places; 49:6 (news brought by a fāsiq, to be verified) shows that a nabaʾ can still need checking.
خَبَر sums the corpus's lemmas خَبَر and its plural أَخْبَار (2 + 3).
Blind review: ġalabat aẓ-ẓann rendered 'strong probability'; the derivation of نَبِيّ from nabaʾ given as many's view (others: from nabwa).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries نبأ, خبر (2026-11-06): 5 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Vijest od težine i koristi. U Kur'anu najčešće o vjerovjesnicima i narodima prije, o nevidljivom svijetu i o Sudnjem danu. Mnogi iz istog korijena izvode i نَبِيّ – vjerovjesnik (drugi iz nabwa, uzvišenost).
nuance.en: News of weight and benefit. In the Quran most often of the prophets and peoples of old, of the unseen and of the Last Day. Many derive نَبِيّ, prophet, from the same root (others from nabwa, elevation).

why.bs: „…o onoj velikoj vijesti (النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيمِ)“ – vijest o proživljenju.
why.en: “(It is) of the awful tidings” — the tidings of the Resurrection.

why.bs: Pupavac: „i došao sam ti iz Sebe s pouzdanom vijesti (بِنَبَإٍ يَقِينٍ)“ – vijest koja donosi sigurno znanje.
why.en: The hoopoe: “I come unto thee from Sheba with sure tidings” (بِنَبَإٍ يَقِينٍ) — news that brings sure knowledge.

why.bs: „Ako vam grešnik donese vijest, provjerite je“ – i važnu vijest treba provjeriti.
why.en: “If an evil-liver bring you tidings, verify it” — even weighty news must be checked.

nuance.bs: Vijest, obavijest uopće; u množini i ono što se o nekome zna (njegova djela i stanje).
nuance.en: News, information in general; in the plural also what is known about someone (their deeds and state).

why.bs: Musa porodici: „donijet ću vam odande kakvu vijest (بِخَبَرٍ)“ – obična vijest o putu.
why.en: Moses to his family: “I will bring you tidings thence” (بِخَبَرٍ) — ordinary news about the way.

why.bs: „Tog dana ona će kazivati svoje vijesti“ – zemlja govori o onome što se na njoj činilo.
why.en: “That day she will relate her chronicles” — the earth tells what was done upon it.

why.bs: „…i iskušat ćemo vijesti o vama“ – أَخْبَار kao ono što se o ljudima zna.
why.en: “…and till We test your record” — أَخْبَار as what is known of people.

title.en: To walk, to travel, to hasten

shared.bs: Sva tri glagola govore o kretanju. Razlikuju se po načinu, dužini puta i po tome je li u kretanju trud.
shared.en: All three verbs speak of motion. They differ in manner, in the length of the way and in whether the motion carries effort.

tellApart.bs: Hodati, ići – kretanje i način hoda → مَشَى; putovati, ići kroz zemlju, najčešće s pozivom da se gleda i pouka uzme → سَارَ; žuriti, i trud u nekom poslu, dobrom ili lošem → سَعَى.
tellApart.en: To walk — motion and the manner of walking → مَشَى; to travel, to go through the land, most often with a call to look and take heed → سَارَ; to hasten, and effort in a matter, good or bad → سَعَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries مشى, سار, سعى
Tafsir on 62:9 (fa-sʿaw)
notes: ar-Rāġib: mashy is moving from place to place by will; sayr is going on through the land; saʿy is a quick walk short of running, and is used for earnest effort in a matter, good or evil — paraphrased and attributed to him.
That سَارَ occurs 13 times in 'travel through the land and see the end of…' is our observation of all 16 places; that مَشَى is often qualified by the manner of walking (17:37, 25:63, 28:25) likewise.
62:9 fa-sʿaw: tafsir mostly explains it as going with care and readiness, not running (the Prophet forbade running to prayer); both senses of saʿy are named.
Blind review: 62:9 fa-sʿaw given as most mufassirun's reading.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries مشى, سار, سعى (2026-11-06): 6 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/2/nuance (improved): Confirmed; he adds that saʿy is most often used of praiseworthy deeds, which we had not said
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): entries cited as the book spells them (سير → سار).

nuance.bs: Obično hodanje s mjesta na mjesto. Kur'an uz njega često kaže kako se hoda – oholo, smjerno, stidljivo.
nuance.en: Ordinary walking from place to place. The Quran often says with it how one walks — proudly, humbly, shyly.

why.bs: Robovi Milostivog su oni „koji po zemlji hodaju smjerno“ – način hoda kao vrlina.
why.en: The servants of the Beneficent are they “who walk upon the earth modestly” — the manner of walking as a virtue.

why.bs: „I ne hodaj po zemlji obijesno“ – način hoda kao porok.
why.en: “And walk not in the earth exultant” — the manner of walking as a vice.

why.bs: „Pa mu dođe jedna od njih dvije, hodajući stidljivo“ – hod koji pokazuje ćud.
why.en: “Then there came unto him one of the two women, walking shyly” — a gait that shows character.

nuance.bs: Putovati, ići dalje kroz zemlju. U Kur'anu najčešće u pozivu „Putujte po zemlji, zatim pogledajte kakav je bio kraj…“ (6:11) – putovanje radi pouke.
nuance.en: To travel, to go on through the land. In the Quran most often in the call “Travel in the land, and see the nature of the consequence…” (6:11) — travel for the lesson it teaches.

why.bs: „Putujte zemljom, pa onda pogledajte kako su završili oni što su poricali“ – putovanje radi pouke.
why.en: “Travel in the land, and see the nature of the consequence for the rejecters!” — travel for a lesson.

why.bs: Musa je, nakon isteka roka, „putovao sa svojom porodicom“ – dugo putovanje.
why.en: Moses, after the term ended, “was travelling with his housefolk” — a long journey.

why.bs: „I planine će se silno pokrenuti“ – سَارَ i za kretanje planina na Sudnjem danu.
why.en: “And the mountains move away with (awful) movement” — سَارَ also for the moving of mountains on the Last Day.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, brz hod, ali ne trčanje; prenosi se na zalaganje u nekom poslu – u dobru (za ahiret) ili u zlu (smutnja po zemlji), mada najčešće za pohvalna djela.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a quick walk short of running; it is carried over to earnest effort in a matter — in good (for the hereafter) or in evil (spreading corruption), though most often of praiseworthy deeds.

why.bs: „I s najudaljenijeg kraja grada dođe jedan čovjek žureći (يَسْعَى)“ – brzi hod.
why.en: “And there came from the uttermost part of the city a man running (يَسْعَى)” — the quick walk.

why.bs: „I da čovjeku pripada samo ono za šta se trudio (مَا سَعَى)“ – trud, zalaganje.
why.en: “And that man hath only that for which he maketh effort” — effort, striving.

why.bs: „…požurite ka spominjanju Allaha“ – većina mufesira: idite odmah i smireno, ne trčite.
why.en: “…haste unto remembrance of Allah” — most mufassirun: go promptly and calmly, not at a run.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o srdžbi. Razlikuju se po jačini, po tome da li se kaže za Allaha i čemu su suprotne.
shared.en: All three words speak of anger. They differ in strength, in whether they are said of Allah, and in what they stand against.

tellApart.bs: Srdžba, i ljudska i Allahova → غَضَب; najjači, uzavreli bijes, u Kur'anu nikada za Allaha → غَيْظ; nezadovoljstvo, suprotno zadovoljstvu (رِضْوَان) → سَخَط.
tellApart.en: Anger, both human and Allah's → غَضَب; the strongest, seething rage, never said of Allah in the Quran → غَيْظ; displeasure, the opposite of good pleasure (رِضْوَان) → سَخَط.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries غضب, غيظ, سخط
notes: ar-Rāġib: ġaḍab is the boiling of the heart's blood in wishing for revenge; when Allah is described by it, he says, punishment alone is meant. Many scholars of Ahl as-Sunna instead affirm anger as an attribute of Allah as befits Him, unlike creatures' anger. Both views are named in the member text; the ayat about Allah's anger carry no likening.
ar-Rāġib: ġayẓ is the most intense anger, the heat a person feels from the boiling of his heart's blood — paraphrased and attributed.

That غَيْظ is never said of Allah (all 6 places read), and that سَخَط and its verb stand against رِضْوَان / رَضِيَ (3:162, 47:28, 9:58), is our own observation. ar-Rāġib: saḵaṭ is intense anger that calls for punishment, and from Allah it is the sending down of punishment.
Blind review: 3:162 سَخَط rendered 'displeasure', not 'anger', with 'as befits Him'.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries غضب, غيظ, سخط (2026-11-06): 5 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/2 (improved): His saḵaṭ entry exists: intense anger calling for punishment, from Allah the sending down of punishment

nuance.bs: Srdžba čovjeka (Musa na svoj narod) i Allahova srdžba na one koji je zasluže. Ar-Rāġib je, kad se kaže za Allaha, tumači kao kaznu; mnogi učenjaci ehli-sunneta potvrđuju je kao Allahovo svojstvo kakvo Njemu dolikuje, ne nalik ljudskom.
nuance.en: The anger of a man (Moses at his people) and Allah's anger at those who earn it. ar-Rāġib explains it, when said of Allah, as punishment; many scholars of Ahl as-Sunna affirm it as an attribute of Allah as befits Him, unlike human anger.

why.bs: „A kad Musaova srdžba utihnu, on uze ploče“ – ljudska srdžba koja prođe.
why.en: “When the anger of Moses abated, he took up the tablets” — human anger that passes.

why.bs: „…pa da vas ne stigne Moja srdžba“ – Allahova srdžba kao posljedica obijesti.
why.en: “…lest My wrath come upon you” — Allah's anger as the outcome of transgression.

why.bs: O onima koji se od vjere odmetnu: „na njima je srdžba od Allaha“ – srdžba kao presuda.
why.en: Upon those who disbelieve after belief: “On them is wrath from Allah” — anger as a verdict.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, najjača srdžba, vrelina koja ključa u srcu. U Kur'anu se kaže za ljude – nevjernike, ali i vjernike koji ga savladavaju – i za vatru; nikada za Allaha (naše zapažanje).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the most intense anger, a heat that boils in the heart. In the Quran it is said of people — disbelievers, and believers who restrain it — and of the Fire; never of Allah (our observation).

why.bs: „…i koji svoj bijes obuzdavaju (الْكَاظِمِينَ الْغَيْظَ)“ – vrlina je obuzdati najjači bijes.
why.en: “…those who control their wrath (الْكَاظِمِينَ الْغَيْظَ)” — the virtue of holding back the fiercest rage.

why.bs: „Umrite u svom bijesu!“ – bijes licemjera prema vjernicima.
why.en: “Perish in your rage!” — the hypocrites' fury at the believers.

why.bs: Vatra, „samo što se od bijesa ne rasprsne“ – غَيْظ i za Džehennem.
why.en: The Fire, “as it would burst with rage” — غَيْظ said even of Hell.

nuance.bs: Nezadovoljstvo, suprotno zadovoljstvu. U Kur'anu (naše zapažanje) ova riječ i njen glagol stoje nasuprot Allahovom zadovoljstvu (رِضْوَان) ili ljudskom zadovoljstvu (رَضُوا).
nuance.en: Displeasure, the opposite of being pleased. In the Quran (our observation) this word and its verb stand against Allah's good pleasure (رِضْوَان) or human contentment (رَضُوا).

why.bs: „Zar je onaj ko slijedi Allahovo zadovoljstvo kao onaj ko je navukao Allahovo nezadovoljstvo (بِسَخَطٍ)?“ – سَخَط nasuprot رِضْوَان, kako Njemu dolikuje.
why.en: “Is one who followeth the pleasure of Allah as one who hath earned condemnation (بِسَخَطٍ) from Allah?” — سَخَط against رِضْوَان, as befits Him.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o ljubavi i privrženosti. Prema ar-Rāġibu, wudd je voljeti nešto i željeti da bude, pa se riječ koristi u oba značenja.
shared.en: All three words speak of love and attachment. According to ar-Rāġib, wudd is loving a thing and wishing it to be, so the word is used in both senses.

tellApart.bs: Voljeti – i ljudi Allaha, i Allah one koji to zaslužuju → أَحَبَّ; željeti, poželjeti (osnovni glagol وَدَّ u Kur'anu uvijek znači to) → وَدَّ; naklonost, prisnost među ljudima → مَوَدَّة.
tellApart.en: To love — people loving Allah, and Allah loving those who earn it → أَحَبَّ; to wish (the basic verb وَدَّ always means this in the Quran) → وَدَّ; affection, warmth between people → مَوَدَّة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حب, ودد
notes: ar-Rāġib: wudd is loving a thing and wishing it to be, and is used in each of the two senses, wishing containing the sense of love — paraphrased and attributed.
That the verb وَدَّ means 'to wish' (mostly وَدَّ لَوْ / أَنْ) in all 16 places, and that مَوَدَّة is in every place affection between people, is our observation of all places.
42:23 (al-mawaddata fī l-qurbā) is not cited: tafsir gives several readings of it.
Blind review: 'always means wish' restricted to the basic verb (Form III yuwāddūna, 58:22, is affection); Allah's love glossed 'as befits Him'.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries حب, ودد (2026-11-06): 4 attributed points confirmed
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): entries cited as the book spells them (ود → ودد).

nuance.bs: Opća riječ za ljubav: prema Allahu, prema imetku, prema ljudima. Kaže se i za Allahovu ljubav prema dobročiniteljima i bogobojaznima, kako Njemu dolikuje.
nuance.en: The general word for love: of Allah, of wealth, of people. It is said too of Allah's love for those who do good and fear Him, as befits Him.

why.bs: „Ako volite Allaha, slijedite mene, pa će vas Allah voljeti“ – ljubav vjernika prema Allahu i Allahova ljubav prema njemu, kako Njemu dolikuje.
why.en: “If ye love Allah, follow me; Allah will love you” — the believer's love for Allah, and Allah's love for him as befits Him.

why.bs: „…sve dok ne potrošite od onoga što volite“ – ljubav prema imetku.
why.en: “…until ye spend of that which ye love” — love of wealth.

why.bs: „Ti ne upućuješ na pravi put onoga koga voliš“ – ljubav prema bližnjem.
why.en: “Thou (O Muhammad) guidest not whom thou lovest” — love for one dear to you.

nuance.bs: Iako je iz korijena naklonosti, glagol u Kur'anu (naše zapažanje) uvijek znači ‚željeti‘, najčešće ono što se neće ostvariti ili što bi drugima naudilo.
nuance.en: Though from the root of affection, the verb in the Quran (our observation) always means ‘to wish’, most often for what will not come true or would harm others.

why.bs: „Mnogi od sljedbenika Knjige žele da vas, nakon što ste vjerovali, vrate u nevjernike“ – želja da drugi zastrane.
why.en: “Many of the people of the Scripture long to make you disbelievers after your belief” — a wish that others go astray.

why.bs: „Možda će oni koji ne vjeruju poželjeti da su bili muslimani“ – kasna želja.
why.en: “It may be that those who disbelieve wish ardently that they were Muslims” — a wish that comes too late.

why.bs: „Oni bi voljeli da ti popustiš, pa da onda i oni popuste“ – želja za kompromisom u vjeri.
why.en: “Who would have had thee compromise, that they may compromise” — a wish for compromise in faith.

nuance.bs: Prisnost i naklonost među ljudima – među supružnicima, prijateljima, pa i prema neprijatelju. Allah je spominje kao Svoj znak i dar.
nuance.en: Warmth and affection between people — between spouses, friends, even towards an enemy. Allah names it as His sign and gift.

why.bs: „…i stavio je među vas naklonost i milost“ – مَوَدَّة među supružnicima kao Allahov znak.
why.en: “…and He ordained between you love and mercy” — مَوَدَّة between spouses as a sign of Allah.

why.bs: „Možda Allah uspostavi naklonost između vas i onih među njima s kojima ste neprijatelji“ – naklonost koja može zamijeniti neprijateljstvo.
why.en: “It may be that Allah will ordain love between you and those of them with whom ye are at enmity” — affection that can replace enmity.

why.bs: „…i naći ćeš da su vjernicima naklonošću najbliži…“ – naklonost jednog naroda prema drugom.
why.en: “…And thou wilt find the nearest of them in affection to those who believe…” — one people's affection for another.

title.en: To hope and to long for

shared.bs: Oba glagola govore o iščekivanju nečeg dobrog. Prema ar-Rāġibu, rajāʾ je pretpostavka koja očekuje ono što raduje, a ṭamaʿ je težnja duše prema nečemu iz želje za njim.
shared.en: Both verbs speak of expecting some good. According to ar-Rāġib, rajāʾ is an expectation of what brings joy, while ṭamaʿ is the soul's inclination towards a thing out of desire for it.

tellApart.bs: Nadati se, s razlogom, najčešće susretu s Allahom i ahiretu → رَجَا; žudjeti, priželjkivati – hvalevrijedno kad se žudi za Allahovim oprostom, a pokudno kad je bez osnova ili iz bolesti srca → طَمِعَ.
tellApart.en: To hope, with grounds, most often for the meeting with Allah and the hereafter → رَجَا; to long for, to covet — praiseworthy when it is longing for Allah's forgiveness, blameworthy when groundless or from a sick heart → طَمِعَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رجا, طمع
Tafsir on 71:13 (lā tarjūna li-llāhi waqāran)
notes: ar-Rāġib: rajāʾ is an expectation that calls for the coming of what brings joy; ṭamaʿ is the soul's inclination to a thing out of desire for it — paraphrased and attributed.
71:13 is explained in much of tafsir as 'why do you not fear Allah's majesty'; we give that reading as tafsir's and do not cite the ayah as a member example.

That رَجَا has as object the meeting with Allah, the Last Day or Allah's mercy in most of its 22 places, and that طَمِعَ is praised (26:82, 26:51, 5:84) and blamed (70:38, 74:15, 33:32), is our observation of all places.
Blind review: the reading 'do not fear' for lā yarjūna (10:7) is named beside 'do not hope'.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries رجا, طمع (2026-11-06): 5 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Nada koja ima osnova i očekuje radost. U Kur'anu najčešće nada u susret s Allahom, u Sudnji dan i u Allahovu milost; „oni koji se ne nadaju da će Nas sresti“ (10:7) su oni koji ga poriču.
nuance.en: Hope that has grounds and expects joy. In the Quran most often hope for the meeting with Allah, for the Last Day and Allah's mercy; “those who expect not the meeting with Us” (10:7) are those who deny it.

why.bs: „Pa onaj ko očekuje da će sresti svoga Gospodara, neka radi dobro djelo“ – nada koja vodi djelu.
why.en: “Whoever hopeth for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work” — hope that leads to deeds.

why.bs: „…takvi se nadaju milosti Allahovoj“ – nada vjernika nakon truda.
why.en: “…these have hope of Allah's mercy” — the believers' hope after effort.

why.bs: „Oni koji se ne nadaju da će Nas sresti i koji su zadovoljni životom na ovom svijetu…“ – odsustvo nade kao poricanje (neki mufesiri: ‚ne boje se‘).
why.en: “Those who expect not the meeting with Us but desire the life of the world…” — no hope, as denial (some mufassirun: ‘do not fear’).

nuance.bs: Težnja duše za nečim. Kad je usmjerena na Allahov oprost, Kur'an je hvali; kad je bez osnova ili iz bolesti srca, kudi je.
nuance.en: The soul's reaching for something. Turned to Allah's forgiveness, the Quran praises it; when groundless or from a sick heart, it blames it.

why.bs: Ibrahim: „i od Koga žudim da mi na Dan suda oprosti moju grešku“ – hvalevrijedna žudnja.
why.en: Abraham: “And Who, I ardently hope, will forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment” — praiseworthy longing.

why.bs: „Zar svaki čovjek među njima žudi da ga uvedu u Džennet pun blagodati?“ – žudnja bez osnova.
why.en: “Doth every man among them hope to enter the Garden of Delight?” — groundless longing.

why.bs: „…pa da ne zažudi onaj u čijem je srcu bolest“ – žudnja iz bolesti srca.
why.en: “…lest he in whose heart is a disease aspire (to you)” — longing from a sick heart.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi su iz korijena veličine (k-b-r) i govore o uzdizanju sebe. Razlikuju se po tome da li je veličina stvarna ili umišljena i kome se pripisuje.
shared.en: All three words are of the root of greatness (k-b-r) and speak of raising oneself up. They differ in whether the greatness is real or assumed, and to whom it is ascribed.

tellApart.bs: Oholo odbiti, uzoholiti se pred istinom i ibadetom → اسْتَكْبَرَ; oholiti se, izdizati se nad drugima po zemlji → تَكَبَّرَ; ohol – o ljudima pokudno, a kao Allahovo ime: Veličanstveni → مُتَكَبِّر.
tellApart.en: To disdain, to grow arrogant before the truth and worship → اسْتَكْبَرَ; to behave arrogantly, to set oneself above others in the land → تَكَبَّرَ; arrogant — blame for people, and as Allah's name: the Supreme → مُتَكَبِّر.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries كبر
notes: ar-Rāġib: istikbār is seeking to become great; it is praiseworthy when rightly placed, and blameworthy when one shows of himself what he does not have — and the Quran's uses are of the second kind. Takabbur is either real excellence beyond others, in which sense Allah is al-Mutakabbir, or a pretended one, which is that of people. Paraphrased and attributed to him.

That اسْتَكْبَرَ is most often refusal of worship, of the messengers or of the truth (Iblis 2:34, 40:60, 71:7), and that مُتَكَبِّر is Allah's name once (59:23) and otherwise always arrogant people (Hell's dwellers; 40:27, 40:35), is our observation of all places.
Blind review: الْمُتَكَبِّر rendered Veličanstveni / the Supreme (not Uzvišeni, which belongs to al-ʿAlī).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries كبر (2026-11-06): 5 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Uzoholiti se tako da se odbije istina, poslanik ili ibadet. Prva oholost u Kur'anu je Iblisova.
nuance.en: To grow so arrogant as to refuse the truth, a messenger or worship. The first arrogance in the Quran is Iblis's.

why.bs: Iblis „odbi i uzoholi se“ – oholost kao odbijanje naredbe.
why.en: Iblis “demurred through pride” — arrogance as refusing a command.

why.bs: „Oni koji se ohole da Mi ibadet čine…“ – oholost pred ibadetom.
why.en: “Those who scorn My service…” — arrogance before worship.

why.bs: Nuhov narod „ustrajaše i silno se uzoholiše“ – oholost pred poslanikom.
why.en: Noah's people “persist (in their refusal) and magnify themselves in pride” — arrogance before a messenger.

nuance.bs: Uzdizati se nad drugima, pokazivati veličinu koja čovjeku ne pripada. U Kur'anu samo dva puta, oba puta pokudno.
nuance.en: To set oneself above others, to show a greatness one does not have. Only twice in the Quran, both times in blame.

why.bs: Iblisu: „Nije tebi da se tu oholiš“ – oholost tamo gdje joj nije mjesto.
why.en: To Iblis: “It is not for thee to show pride here” — arrogance where it has no place.

why.bs: „…one koji se na Zemlji bez prava ohole“ – oholost nad drugima.
why.en: “…those who magnify themselves wrongfully in the earth” — arrogance over others.

nuance.bs: O ljudima: ohol, onaj koji se pravi velikim. Kao Allahovo ime (59:23): Onaj kome jedinome istinska veličina pripada – prema ar-Rāġibu, veličina koja je stvarna, a ne umišljena.
nuance.en: Of people: arrogant, one who makes himself great. As Allah's name (59:23): the One to whom alone true greatness belongs — according to ar-Rāġib, a greatness that is real, not assumed.

why.bs: „…Onaj Koji sve podčinjava, Uzvišeni (الْمُتَكَبِّرُ)“ – Allahovo ime; istinska veličina pripada samo Njemu.
why.en: “…the Compeller, the Superb (الْمُتَكَبِّرُ)” — a name of Allah; true greatness is His alone.

why.bs: Musa: „Ja se utječem svome i vašem Gospodaru od svakog oholog (مُتَكَبِّرٍ) koji u Dan obračuna ne vjeruje“ – ista riječ o čovjeku, pokudno.
why.en: Moses: “I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every scorner (مُتَكَبِّرٍ) who believeth not in a Day of Reckoning” — the same word of a man, in blame.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o poniznosti. Ar-Rāġib ističe da se khušūʿ najčešće kaže za ono što se vidi na tijelu, a ḍarāʿa za ono što je u srcu: ‚kad je srce ponizno, i udovi se skruše‘.
shared.en: All three words speak of lowliness. ar-Rāġib notes that ḫušūʿ is mostly said of what shows in the body and ḍarāʿa of what is in the heart: ‘when the heart is humbled, the limbs become humble’.

tellApart.bs: Skrušen – poniznost koja se vidi na licu, pogledu, glasu → خَاشِع; ponizna molba, preklinjanje iz srca → تَضَرُّع; pokoren, onaj koji se savija pred većim → خَاضِع.
tellApart.en: Humble — lowliness that shows in the face, the gaze, the voice → خَاشِع; humble entreaty, pleading from the heart → تَضَرُّع; submissive, bowing before one greater → خَاضِع.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries خشع, ضرع
notes: ar-Rāġib: ḫušūʿ is ḍarāʿa, mostly used of what is found in the limbs, while ḍarāʿa is mostly used of what is in the heart; hence the saying 'when the heart is humbled the limbs become humble' — he gives it as 'it has been related', and so do we.
Counter-example shown: 57:16 'that their hearts should be humbled (taḫšaʿa qulūbuhum)', so ḫušūʿ of the heart is also Quranic; the distinction is a tendency.
That خَاشِع is said of eyes, faces, voices, the earth and a mountain (54:7, 88:2, 41:39, 59:21), and that خَاضِع occurs once (26:4), is our observation; ar-Rāġib simply glosses ḫuḍūʿ as ḫušūʿ.
Blind review: 6:63 'aloud' corrected to 'humbly and secretly'; 26:4 aʿnāquhum given as necks or (for some mufassirun) leaders.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries خشع, ضرع, خضع (2026-11-06): 7 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/2 (improved): His ḫuḍūʿ entry exists and simply equates ḫuḍūʿ with ḫušūʿ; members/1/nuance (reworded): He says ḍarāʿa is mostly used of what is in the heart (not exclusively), and that taḍarruʿ is showing ḍarāʿa

nuance.bs: Skrušen; poniznost koja se vidi – u namazu, na licima i pogledima na Sudnjem danu, pa i na zemlji i planini. Može biti iz bogobojaznosti, ali i iz poniženja.
nuance.en: Humble; a lowliness that is seen — in prayer, on faces and in eyes on the Last Day, even on the earth and a mountain. It may come from awe, or from abasement.

why.bs: „…koji su u svojim namazima skrušeni“ – skrušenost u ibadetu.
why.en: “Who are humble in their prayers” — humility in worship.

why.bs: „…vidio bi je skrušenu, kako puca od straha pred Allahom“ – planina, kad bi joj bio objavljen Kur'an.
why.en: “Thou (O Muhammad) verily hadst seen it humbled, rent asunder by the fear of Allah” — a mountain, were the Quran sent down upon it.

why.bs: „Neka lica će toga dana biti oborena (خَاشِعَة)“ – skrušenost iz poniženja.
why.en: “On that day (many) faces will be downcast” (خَاشِعَة) — lowliness from abasement.

nuance.bs: Ponizno, usrdno preklinjanje, najčešće u dovi. Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḍarāʿa se najčešće kaže za poniznost u srcu, a taḍarruʿ je njeno pokazivanje.
nuance.en: Humble, earnest entreaty, most often in supplication. According to ar-Rāġib, ḍarāʿa is mostly said of lowliness in the heart, and taḍarruʿ is showing it.

why.bs: „Prizivajte svoga Gospodara ponizno (تَضَرُّعًا) i skriveno“ – kako se upućuje dova.
why.en: “Call upon your Lord humbly (تَضَرُّعًا) and in secret” — how supplication is made.

why.bs: „…prizivate Ga ponizno i skriveno“ – preklinjanje u nevolji na kopnu i moru.
why.en: “Ye call upon Him humbly and in secret” — entreaty in distress on land and sea.

why.bs: „I sjećaj se svoga Gospodara u duši svojoj, ponizno moleći i u strahu“ – تَضَرُّع i u zikru.
why.en: “Remember thy Lord within thyself humbly and with awe” — تَضَرُّع in remembrance too.

nuance.bs: Pokoren, onaj koji se savija pred većim. U Kur'anu jednom (naše zapažanje), o šijama (ili, prema nekim mufesirima, prvacima) koje bi se pognule pred znakom s neba.
nuance.en: Submissive, bending before what is greater. Once in the Quran (our observation), of necks (or, for some mufassirun, leaders) that would bow before a sign from heaven.

why.bs: „…pa bi njihovi vratovi (ili: prvaci njihovi) pred njim ostali pokorno pognuti“ – pokornost na koju bi bili prisiljeni.
why.en: “…so that their necks (or: their leaders) would remain bowed before it” — a submission they would be forced into.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače more, veliku vodu. Razlikuje ih (naše zapažanje) to gdje ih Kur'an koristi.
shared.en: Both words mean the sea, a great body of water. What tells them apart (our observation) is where the Quran uses them.

tellApart.bs: More uopće – slano i slatko, more kojim plove lađe, more kao slika neizmjernosti → بَحْر; more (ili rijeka) u kazivanju o Musau i faraonu – u Kur'anu samo tamo → يَمّ.
tellApart.en: The sea in general — salt and fresh, the sea ships sail, the sea as an image of the boundless → بَحْر; the sea (or river) in the story of Moses and Pharaoh — in the Quran only there → يَمّ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries بحر, يم
Tafsir on 20:39 and 28:7 (al-yamm as the Nile)
notes: ar-Rāġib: the root of baḥr is every wide place gathering much water; yamm he glosses as the sea — paraphrased and attributed.

That all 7 ayat with يَمّ belong to the story of Moses and Pharaoh (the infant set afloat, Pharaoh's drowning, the calf's ashes scattered), while بَحْر is used in that story too (2:50, 20:77, 26:63), is our observation of all places.
Tafsir mostly takes the yamm of 20:39 and 28:7 to be the Nile; for Pharaoh's drowning it is the sea. A claim that yamm is a loanword is not made: it could not be verified here.
Blind review: 28:7 'the same water' corrected — the Nile in 20:39 / 28:7, the sea in 28:40.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries بحر, يم (2026-11-06): 3 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Opća riječ za more i veliku vodu: kojim plove lađe, slatko i slano ‚dva mora‘, more koje se razdvojilo pred Musaom, more kao mjera neizmjernosti Allahovih riječi.
nuance.en: The general word for the sea and great waters: the sea ships sail, the sweet and salt ‘two seas’, the sea parted before Moses, the sea as a measure of the boundlessness of Allah's words.

why.bs: „On je pustio dva mora: ovo je slatko, pitko, a ono slano, gorko“ – بَحْر i za slatku vodu.
why.en: “He it is Who hath given independence to the two seas (though they meet); one palatable, sweet, and the other saltish, bitter” — بَحْر also of fresh water.

why.bs: „I kad smo zbog vas more razdvojili…“ – بَحْر i u kazivanju o Musau.
why.en: “And when We brought you through the sea…” — بَحْر in the story of Moses too.

why.bs: „Kad bi more bilo tinta za riječi Gospodara moga…“ – more kao slika neizmjernosti.
why.en: “Though the sea became ink for the Words of my Lord…” — the sea as an image of the boundless.

nuance.bs: More ili velika voda – u Kur'anu (naše zapažanje) samo u kazivanju o Musau: u nju je majka spustila dojenče, u njoj su potopljeni faraon i njegova vojska (u 20:39 i 28:7 tefsir je tumači kao Nil, u 28:40 kao more).
nuance.en: The sea or a great water — in the Quran (our observation) only in the story of Moses: his mother set the infant upon it, and Pharaoh and his soldiers were drowned in it (tafsir: the Nile in 20:39 and 28:7, the sea in 28:40).

why.bs: „Stavi ga u sanduk, pa ga baci u rijeku (الْيَمّ)“ – tefsir: u Nil.
why.en: “Throw him into the ark, and throw it into the river (الْيَمّ)” — tafsir: the Nile.

why.bs: „…pa kad se pobojiš za njega, baci ga u rijeku i ne boj se“ – ista riječ, isto kazivanje (tefsir: Nil).
why.en: “When thou fearest for him, then cast him into the river and fear not” — the same word, the same story (tafsir: the Nile).

why.bs: „Pa smo njega i njegovu vojsku uhvatili i bacili ih u more“ – faraonov kraj.
why.en: “Therefor We seized him and his hosts, and abandoned them unto the sea” — Pharaoh's end.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače oblak. Razlikuju se po onome što ime ističe i po ulozi oblaka u ajetima.
shared.en: All three words mean cloud. They differ in what the name brings out and in the part the cloud plays in the ayat.

tellApart.bs: Oblak koji vjetrovi vuku i gone, najčešće kišni → سَحَاب; oblak koji zaklanja i daje hlad (od korijena ‚pokriti‘) → غَمَام; kišni oblak – jednom, kao izvor slatke vode → مُزْن.
tellApart.en: The cloud drawn and driven by the winds, usually rain-bearing → سَحَاب; the cloud that covers and shades (from the root ‘to cover’) → غَمَام; the rain cloud — once, as the source of sweet water → مُزْن.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries سحب, غم, مزن
Tafsir on 56:69 (al-muzn as clouds)
notes: ar-Rāġib: saḥāb is so named because the wind drags it, or it drags the water, or it is itself dragged along in its passage; ġamām is the cloud, named for covering (ġamma) the light of the sun — paraphrased and attributed. muzn he glosses as bright (luminous) clouds, a single piece being muzna, and tafsir on 56:69 explains it as the clouds.

That سَحَاب is often tied to the winds and to rain (7:57, 24:43, 30:48, 35:9), though also an image of passing and darkness (27:88, 24:40), and that غَمَام is never the bearer of rain but a shade (2:57, 7:160) or a sign of the Last Day (25:25, 2:210), is our observation of all places. 2:210 (Allah's coming in shades of cloud) is not cited: its meaning is left to tafsir.
Blind review: سَحَاب 'almost always with rain' softened to 'often' (27:88, 24:40, 52:44); Korkut's 'sinovi Israilovi' and 2:57 wording.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries سحب, غم, مزن (2026-11-06): 2 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (improved): He gives three derivations for saḥāb (we had two) and does define muzn: bright, luminous clouds

nuance.bs: Oblak koji vjetrovi tjeraju, skupljaju i iz kojeg pada kiša. U Kur'anu (naše zapažanje) često uz vjetrove i kišu, kao znak Allahove moći i milosti, ali i kao slika prolaznosti (27:88) i tame (24:40).
nuance.en: Clouds driven and gathered by the winds, from which rain falls. In the Quran (our observation) often with winds and rain, as a sign of Allah's power and mercy, but also as an image of passing (27:88) and of darkness (24:40).

why.bs: „Allah goni oblake, zatim ih spaja, zatim ih nagomila, pa vidiš kišu kako izlazi između njih“ – oblak koji nosi kišu.
why.en: “Allah wafteth the clouds, then gathereth them, then maketh them layers, and thou seest the rain come forth from between them” — the rain-bearing cloud.

why.bs: „…kad ponesu teške oblake, Mi ih potjeramo u mrtav kraj“ – vjetrovi i oblaci.
why.en: “…when they bear a cloud heavy (with rain), We lead it to a dead land” — winds and clouds.

nuance.bs: Oblak koji pokriva i zaklanja. U Kur'anu (naše zapažanje) nikad kao kišni oblak: hlad koji je Allah dao sinovima Israilovim i oblaci Sudnjeg dana.
nuance.en: The cloud that covers and screens. In the Quran (our observation) never as a rain cloud: the shade Allah gave the Children of Israel, and the clouds of the Last Day.

why.bs: „I nad vama smo oblake nadvili kao sjenu“ – oblak kao hlad u pustinji.
why.en: “And We caused the white cloud to overshadow you” — the cloud as shade in the desert.

why.bs: „A na Dan kad se nebo s oblacima raspukne…“ – oblaci Sudnjeg dana.
why.en: “A day when the heaven with the clouds will be rent asunder…” — the clouds of the Last Day.

nuance.bs: Kišni oblaci; jednom u Kur'anu, u pitanju: ko spušta vodu za piće iz njih?
nuance.en: Rain clouds; once in the Quran, in a question: who sends down the drinking water from them?

why.bs: „Spuštate li je vi iz kišnih oblaka ili Mi je spuštamo?“ – مُزْن kao izvor pitke vode.
why.en: “Is it ye who shed it from the raincloud, or are We the Shedder?” — مُزْن as the source of drinking water.

shared.bs: Obje riječi označavaju čovjekove bližnje i one koji mu pripadaju. Prema ar-Rāġibu, آل je izveden od أَهْل, ali se koristi uže.
shared.en: Both words name a person's own, those who belong to him. According to ar-Rāġib, آل comes from أَهْل but is used more narrowly.

tellApart.bs: Porodica, ukućani, ali i stanovnici, sljedbenici, oni koji nečemu pripadaju (ehli-kitab, stanovnici sela) → أَهْل; porodica, rod ili pristalice – u Kur'anu (naše zapažanje) uvijek uz ime osobe (Ibrahimova, Lutova, faraonova) → آل.
tellApart.en: Family, household, but also inhabitants, followers, those who belong to something (People of the Book, people of the towns) → أَهْل; family, house or followers — in the Quran (our observation) always with a person's name (of Abraham, of Lot, of Pharaoh) → آل.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries أهل, آل
notes: ar-Rāġib: āl is a transposed form of ahl, but is restricted to being joined to names of rational persons — one does not say āl of a place or a time — and is used of those bound to a person by close kinship or allegiance; ahl is joined to anything. Paraphrased and attributed to him.
That آل is joined to a proper name in all 23 ayat (Ibrahim, ʿImran, Yaʿqub, Musa, Harun, Dawud, Lut, Firʿawn) is our observation; آل فِرْعَوْن (his people and followers) shows it is not only kinship.
Blind review: 'always with a name' marked as our observation; أَهْلُ النَّارِ rendered 'stanovnici Vatre'. 'faraon' is kept, as in Korkut's translation.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries أهل, آل (2026-11-06): 5 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Najšira riječ: ukućani i porodica, ali i stanovnici mjesta, ljudi jedne knjige ili jednog stanja (‚stanovnici Vatre‘, أَهْلُ النَّارِ).
nuance.en: The widest word: household and family, but also the inhabitants of a place, the people of a scripture or of a state (‘the people of the Fire’, أَهْلُ النَّارِ).

why.bs: „I naređuj svojoj porodici (أَهْلَكَ) da klanja namaz“ – ukućani.
why.en: “And enjoin upon thy people [thy household] worship” — the household.

why.bs: „Reci: O sljedbenici Knjige (أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ), dođite…“ – ljudi jedne knjige.
why.en: “Say: O People of the Scripture! Come…” — the people of a scripture.

why.bs: „A da su stanovnici naselja (أَهْلَ الْقُرَى) vjerovali…“ – stanovnici mjesta.
why.en: “And if the people of the townships had believed…” — the inhabitants of a place.

nuance.bs: Porodica ili rod jedne poznate osobe, ali i njeni sljedbenici i pristalice. U Kur'anu uvijek uz vlastito ime: Ibrahimova i Imranova porodica, ali i faraonovi ljudi.
nuance.en: The family or house of a known person, but also his followers and partisans. In the Quran always with a proper name: the family of Abraham and of Imran, but also Pharaoh's people.

why.bs: „Allah je odabrao Adema, Nuha, porodicu Ibrahimovu i porodicu Imranovu“ – آل plemenitih.
why.en: “Lo! Allah preferred Adam and Noah and the Family of Abraham and the Family of 'Imran” — the house of the noble.

why.bs: „…osim Lutove porodice; njih ćemo, doista, sve spasiti“ – porodica poslanika.
why.en: “(All) save the family of Lot. Them we shall deliver every one” — a prophet's household.

why.bs: „Uvedite faraonov narod (آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ) u najžešću kaznu!“ – آل kao pristalice, ne samo rod.
why.en: “Cause Pharaoh's folk to enter the most awful doom” — آل as followers, not only kin.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o bliskom čovjeku. Razlikuju se po dubini veze: od pratioca do prisnog prijatelja.
shared.en: All three words speak of someone close. They differ in the depth of the bond: from a companion to an intimate friend.

tellApart.bs: Drug, pratilac, onaj s kim je čovjek često – i bez ljubavi → صَاحِب; prisni prijatelj, ljubav koja prožima dušu → خَلِيل; iskren prijatelj, onaj čija je ljubav istinita → صَدِيق.
tellApart.en: Companion, one a person is often with — even without love → صَاحِب; intimate friend, a love that pervades the soul → خَلِيل; true friend, one whose affection is sincere → صَدِيق.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries صحب, خل, صدق
notes: ar-Rāġib: ṣāḥib is one who keeps company, be it a person, an animal, a place or a time, and in usage only one whose company is frequent; ḫulla is love, either because it pervades (taḫallala) the soul, or pierces it, or from great need of it — paraphrased and attributed to him.
That صَدِيق is linked with ṣidq (truth) is said of the word's root; ar-Rāġib defines ṣadāqa (friendship) as truthfulness of conviction in affection, something proper to humans.
9:40 (lā taḥzan … li-ṣāḥibihi): the companion in the cave is Abu Bakr by the agreement of tafsir.
خَلِيل includes its plural أَخِلَّاء (43:67) in one corpus lemma.

Blind review: 'your companion' reworded so it cannot read as diminishing the Prophet; khalīl's other derivation (need) named and Allah's ḫulla glossed as unlike human friendship; 43:67 keeps 'except the righteous'.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries صحب, خل, صدق (2026-11-06): 7 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/1 (improved): He defines ṣadāqa as sincerity of conviction in affection, proper to humans, citing 26:101

nuance.bs: Pratilac, drug s kojim se čovjek često nalazi – na putu, u zatvoru, u pećini. Govori o druženju, ne nužno o ljubavi; poricatelje Kur'an podsjeća da Poslanika, ‚svog druga‘, dobro poznaju.
nuance.en: A companion one is often with — on the road, in prison, in a cave. It speaks of keeping company, not necessarily of love; the Quran reminds the deniers that the Prophet, ‘your companion’, is one they know well.

why.bs: „…kad je govorio svome drugu (لِصَاحِبِهِ): Ne tuguj“ – drug u pećini, prema tefsiru Ebu Bekr.
why.en: “…when he said unto his comrade: Grieve not” — the companion in the cave, Abu Bakr according to tafsir.

why.bs: „Nije zalutao vaš drug (صَاحِبُكُمْ)“ – Poslanik kao onaj koga dobro poznaju.
why.en: “Your comrade erreth not” — the Prophet as one they know well.

why.bs: „O moja dva druga iz tamnice!“ – drugovi po okolnosti.
why.en: “O my fellow-prisoners!” — companions by circumstance.

nuance.bs: Prijatelj najprisnije ljubavi – prema ar-Rāġibu, ljubav koja prožima dušu (on bilježi i druga izvođenja, među njima ‚potrebu‘). Najviše: Allah je uzeo Ibrahima za halila – počast najveće bliskosti, bez ikakve sličnosti s ljudskim prijateljstvom; a u kajanju: grešnik žali za lošim prijateljem.
nuance.en: A friend of the closest love — according to ar-Rāġib, a love that pervades the soul (he records other derivations too, among them ‘need’). At the highest: Allah took Abraham as khalīl — an honour of the highest nearness, nothing like a human friendship; in regret: the sinner rues his bad friend.

why.bs: „…a Allah je Ibrahima uzeo za prisnog prijatelja (خَلِيلًا)“ – najviši stupanj bliskosti.
why.en: “Allah (Himself) chose Abraham for friend” — the highest degree of closeness.

why.bs: „Teško meni! Kamo sreće da onoga nisam uzeo za prisnog prijatelja!“ – kajanje zbog lošeg prijatelja.
why.en: “Alas for me! Ah, would that I had never taken such an one for friend!” — regret over a bad friend.

why.bs: „Prijatelji (الْأَخِلَّاءُ) će toga dana biti neprijatelji jedni drugima, osim bogobojaznih“ – prijateljstvo koje nije na bogobojaznosti ne izdrži.
why.en: “Friends on that day will be foes one to another, save those who kept their duty (to Allah)” — friendship not built on taqwa does not endure.

nuance.bs: Prijatelj čija je naklonost iskrena (riječ je iz korijena istine). U Kur'anu dva puta: među onima u čijim kućama je dozvoljeno jesti, i kao prijatelj kojeg grešnik na Sudnjem danu neće imati.
nuance.en: A friend whose affection is true (the word is of the root of truth). Twice in the Quran: among those in whose houses one may eat, and as the friend the sinner will not have on the Last Day.

why.bs: „…ni odana prijatelja (صَدِيقٍ حَمِيمٍ)“ – prijatelj koji tog dana nedostaje.
why.en: “Nor any loving friend” — the friend missed on that Day.

why.bs: „…ili kod vašeg prijatelja (صَدِيقِكُمْ)“ – prijatelj s pravom bliskosti u kući.
why.en: “…or (from the house) of a friend” — a friend with the right of closeness in one's home.

shared.bs: Sva četiri glagola govore o radu uma. Kur'an ih koristi kad poziva na promišljanje i kad kudi one koji to ne čine.
shared.en: All four verbs speak of the work of the mind. The Quran uses them when it calls to reflection and when it blames those who do not reflect.

tellApart.bs: Razmišljati, pustiti misao kroz znakove stvaranja → تَفَكَّرَ; razmišljati o krajnjem smislu, o posljedicama – u Kur'anu (naše zapažanje) o Kur'anu i njegovim riječima → تَدَبَّرَ; shvatiti, razumom pojmiti i po tome se ravnati → عَقَلَ; prodrijeti u smisao, razumjeti ono skriveno iz onog vidljivog → فَقِهَ.
tellApart.en: To reflect, to let thought run through the signs of creation → تَفَكَّرَ; to ponder the outcome, where a thing leads — in the Quran (our observation) of the Quran and its words → تَدَبَّرَ; to grasp, to comprehend by reason and be guided by it → عَقَلَ; to penetrate the meaning, to understand the hidden from the seen → فَقِهَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries فكر, دبر, عقل, فقه
notes: ar-Rāġib: fikr is a faculty that leads knowledge to the known, and tafakkur its running according to the mind's view, said only of what can take form in the heart; he gives no definition of tadabbur, but defines tadbīr as thinking on the ends (dubur) of matters; ʿaql is the faculty ready to receive knowledge, and the knowledge gained by it; fiqh is reaching knowledge of the absent through knowledge of the present, so it is narrower than ʿilm. Paraphrased and attributed to him.

Our observations of all places: تَدَبَّرَ (4 times) has the Quran, its ayat or 'the word' as object; عَقَلَ occurs only as a verb (49 times) — the noun ʿaql is not in the Quran; فَقِهَ is negated or denied in most of its 19 ayat.

Blind review: tadabbur 'always the Quran' marked as our observation (23:68 al-qawl); tafakkur also of stories (7:176) and of the Prophet (34:46); 2:44 is about saying one thing and doing another, not 'hypocrisy'; 22:46 phrased as the Quran ascribing understanding to the heart.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries فكر, دبر, عقل, فقه (2026-11-06): 6 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): The 'thinking on the ends of matters' definition is his for tadbīr; he defines no tadabbur (checked with --mentions)

nuance.bs: Razmišljati, pustiti misao da kruži oko nečega. U Kur'anu najčešće o stvaranju nebesa i Zemlje i o Allahovim znakovima u čovjeku i prirodi, ali i o kazivanjima (7:176) i o Poslaniku (34:46).
nuance.en: To reflect, to let thought turn about a thing. In the Quran most often about the creation of the heavens and earth and Allah's signs in man and nature, but also about stories (7:176) and about the Prophet (34:46).

why.bs: „…i razmišljaju o tome kako su stvorena nebesa i Zemlja“ – razmišljanje o stvaranju.
why.en: “…and consider the creation of the heavens and the earth” — reflection on creation.

why.bs: „…u tome su, zaista, znakovi za ljude koji razmišljaju“ – razmišljanje o znaku u braku.
why.en: “Lo! herein indeed are portents for folk who reflect” — reflection on a sign in marriage.

nuance.bs: Razmišljati o krajnjem smislu i posljedicama (od dubur – ‚kraj, zadnja strana‘). U Kur'anu (naše zapažanje) uvijek s Kur'anom, njegovim ajetima ili „Riječju“ (23:68) kao predmetom.
nuance.en: To ponder the outcome and the end of a thing (from dubur, ‘the back, the end’). In the Quran (our observation) always with the Quran, its ayat or “the Word” (23:68) as object.

why.bs: „Zar oni ne razmišljaju o Kur'anu?“ – poziv na dubinsko promišljanje Objave.
why.en: “Will they not then ponder on the Qur'an?” — a call to ponder the Revelation deeply.

why.bs: „Knjiga blagoslovljena koju smo ti objavili da bi o njenim ajetima razmislili“ – svrha objave.
why.en: “(This is) a Scripture that We have revealed unto thee, full of blessing, that they may ponder its revelations” — the purpose of revelation.

nuance.bs: Shvatiti razumom i po tome se ravnati. Kur'an ne koristi imenicu ‚razum‘, nego samo glagol: razum je ono što se čini (naše zapažanje), često u pitanju „Pa zar ne shvatate?“ (2:44).
nuance.en: To grasp by reason and act by it. The Quran never uses the noun ‘reason’, only the verb: reasoning is something done (our observation), often in the question “Have ye then no sense?” (2:44).

why.bs: „…pa da imaju srca kojima bi shvatali (يَعْقِلُونَ)“ – Kur'an razumijevanje pripisuje srcu.
why.en: “…and have they hearts wherewith to feel [yaʿqilūna: to understand]” — the Quran ascribes understanding to the heart.

why.bs: „…a vi Knjigu učite? Pa zar ne shvatate?“ – razum koji bi trebao spriječiti da se jedno govori, a drugo čini.
why.en: “And ye are readers of the Scripture! Have ye then no sense?” — reason that should prevent saying one thing and doing another.

nuance.bs: Prodrijeti u smisao, razumjeti skriveno iz vidljivog; prema ar-Rāġibu uže od znanja (ʿilm). U Kur'anu (naše zapažanje) najčešće u odricanju: ‚oni ne razumiju‘.
nuance.en: To penetrate the meaning, to understand the hidden from the seen; according to ar-Rāġib narrower than knowledge (ʿilm). In the Quran (our observation) most often negated: ‘they do not understand’.

why.bs: „Srca imaju, a njima ne shvataju (لَا يَفْقَهُونَ)“ – srce koje ne pronikne.
why.en: “…having hearts wherewith they understand not” — a heart that does not penetrate.

why.bs: Musa: „…da razumiju moj govor“ – dova za razumijevanje.
why.en: Moses: “That they may understand my saying” — a prayer to be understood.

shared.bs: Sva tri glagola znače odabrati. Ar-Rāġib ih razlikuje po onome što se uzima: iṣṭifāʾ je uzeti čisti dio (ṣafw), iḫtiyār uzeti najbolje (ḫayr), a iǧtibāʾ uzeti i sabrati (kao vodu u bazenu).
shared.en: All three verbs mean to choose. ar-Rāġib tells them apart by what is taken: iṣṭifāʾ is taking the pure part (ṣafw), iḫtiyār taking the best (ḫayr), and iǧtibāʾ gathering in (like water into a basin).

tellApart.bs: Odabrati ono najčistije – vjerovjesnike, Merjem, poslanike → اصْطَفَى; odabrati i obasuti milošću koju čovjek nije zaslužio, i uputiti → اجْتَبَى; izabrati između više mogućnosti – i Allah, i čovjek → اخْتَارَ.
tellApart.en: To choose the purest — prophets, Mary, messengers → اصْطَفَى; to single out and shower with unearned favour, and guide → اجْتَبَى; to choose among options — Allah, and also a man → اخْتَارَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries صفو, جبى, خير
notes: ar-Rāġib: iṣṭifāʾ is taking the ṣafw (purest part) of a thing, as iḫtiyār is taking its best and iǧtibāʾ taking its gathering-in; Allah's iǧtibāʾ of a servant is His singling him out with a divine bounty bringing kinds of favour without the servant's striving, which is for the prophets and some near them. Paraphrased and attributed.

That اخْتَارَ is once said of a human chooser (Moses, 7:155) while اصْطَفَى and اجْتَبَى are Allah's choice in every place except where idolaters' claims are quoted or rejected (37:153, 39:4, 7:203), is our observation of all places.
7:203 (lawlā jtabaytahā) is explained in tafsir as 'why have you not devised it (yourself)'; it is not cited.
Blind review: 'draw near' removed from اجْتَبَى (not ar-Rāġib's) and pardon kept for Adam only; 3:42 'očistio'; 28:68 mā as negation given as most tafsir's reading.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

Blind review of the verification-pass texts (2026-11-06): 'often with hudā' restricted to Adam and Abraham; Jonah and Joseph given as the ayat say.

nuance.bs: Odabrati najčistiji, najodabraniji dio. Allah odabire vjerovjesnike, njihove porodice, Merjem, poslanike među melekima i ljudima.
nuance.en: To choose the purest, most excellent part. Allah chooses the prophets, their families, Mary, and messengers from angels and from people.

why.bs: „Allah je, zaista, odabrao Adema i Nuha…“ – odabir vjerovjesnika i porodica.
why.en: “Lo! Allah preferred [chose] Adam and Noah…” — the choosing of prophets and families.

why.bs: „O Merjema, tebe je Allah odabrao i očistio te, i nad ženama svih svjetova te odabrao“ – dvostruki odabir.
why.en: “O Mary! Lo! Allah hath chosen thee and made thee pure, and hath preferred [chosen] thee above (all) the women of creation” — a twofold choosing.

why.bs: „Allah odabire poslanike iz reda meleka, i iz reda ljudi“ – odabir za poslanstvo.
why.en: “Allah chooseth from the angels messengers, and (also) from mankind” — choosing for the message.

nuance.bs: Odabrati i obasuti milošću – prema ar-Rāġibu, obilje blagodati koje čovjek nije zaslužio trudom, data vjerovjesnicima i nekima koji su im blizu po stepenu. Uz uputu (هَدَى) kod Adema (20:122, uz oprost) i Ibrahima (16:121); Junus je učinjen jednim od dobrih (68:50), a Jusuf poučen tumačenju događaja (12:6).
nuance.en: To single out and shower with favour — according to ar-Rāġib, an abundance of blessing the servant did not earn by striving, given to prophets and some close to them in rank. With guidance (هَدَى) for Adam (20:122, with pardon) and Abraham (16:121); Jonah is made one of the righteous (68:50), and Joseph is taught the interpretation of events (12:6).

why.bs: „Zatim ga je Gospodar njegov odabrao, primio mu pokajanje i uputio ga“ – Adem nakon posrnuća.
why.en: “Then his Lord chose him, and relented toward him, and guided him” — Adam after his slip.

why.bs: „Pa ga je Gospodar njegov odabrao i učinio ga jednim od dobrih“ – Junus.
why.en: “But his Lord chose him and placed him among the righteous” — Jonah.

why.bs: „…odabrao ga je i uputio na pravi put“ – Ibrahim.
why.en: “He chose him and He guided him unto a straight path” — Abraham.

nuance.bs: Izabrati ono što je bolje između više mogućnosti. Kaže se za Allaha, ali i za čovjeka: Musa je izabrao sedamdesetoricu.
nuance.en: To pick what is better among options. Said of Allah, and also of a man: Moses chose seventy men.

why.bs: „A Ja sam te izabrao, pa slušaj ono što se objavljuje“ – Allah bira Musu.
why.en: “And I have chosen thee, so hearken unto that which is inspired” — Allah chooses Moses.

why.bs: „I Musa je iz svog naroda izabrao sedamdeset ljudi“ – čovjek koji bira.
why.en: “And Moses chose of his people seventy men” — a man who chooses.

why.bs: „Tvoj Gospodar stvara šta hoće i izabire; oni nemaju izbora“ – Allahov izbor nasuprot ljudskom (većina tefsira مَا čita kao odricanje).
why.en: “Thy Lord bringeth to pass what He willeth and chooseth. They have never any choice” — Allah's choice over man's (most tafsir read مَا as negation).

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o miru srca. Prema ar-Rāġibu, iṭmiʾnān je smirenost nakon uznemirenosti.
shared.en: Both words speak of the heart's peace. According to ar-Rāġib, iṭmiʾnān is stillness after agitation.

tellApart.bs: Smiriti se, srce se smiri nakon nemira – ali i zadovoljiti se dunjalukom → اطْمَأَنَّ; smirenost koju Allah spušta u srca u času straha → سَكِينَة.
tellApart.en: To be at ease, the heart settling after unrest — but also to settle for this world → اطْمَأَنَّ; the tranquillity Allah sends down into hearts in a moment of fear → سَكِينَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries طمن, سكن
Tafsir on 2:248 (the sakīna in the Ark)
notes: ar-Rāġib: ṭumaʾnīna and iṭmiʾnān are stillness after disturbance — paraphrased and attributed.

That سَكِينَة is, in 5 of its 6 places, sent down (أَنْزَلَ) by Allah on the Prophet and the believers, and in 2:248 is 'in the Ark … from your Lord', is our observation; tafsir differs on what the sakīna of 2:248 was, and we do not choose.
That اطْمَأَنَّ is also blamed — being content with this world (10:7) or with worship only while it goes well (22:11) — is our observation of all places.
Blind review: 2:260 glossed 'not from doubt — he said Yes'; 9:40 'upon him' given as the Prophet (most) or Abu Bakr (some).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

Sources normalised (2026-11-06): سكن read and added to `verified` (consistent with the texts; no attributed point rests on it).

meaning.en: to be at ease, to be reassured

nuance.bs: Smiriti se nakon nemira; srce se smiruje spominjanjem Allaha i uvjerenjem. Ali čovjek se može smiriti i uz dunjaluk – tada je to pokudno.
nuance.en: To come to rest after unrest; the heart is reassured by the remembrance of Allah and by certainty. But a man may also settle in this world — then it is blamed.

why.bs: „Zaista, spominjanjem Allaha smiruju se srca!“ – mir srca kroz spominjanje Allaha.
why.en: “Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest!” — the heart's peace through remembrance.

why.bs: Ibrahim: „Dakako, ali da mi se srce smiri“ – ne iz sumnje (odgovor mu je bio potvrdan), nego radi uvjerenosti viđenjem.
why.en: Abraham: “Yea, but (I ask) in order that my heart may be at ease” — not from doubt (his answer was yes), but for the certainty of seeing.

why.bs: „…i zadovoljni su ovosvjetskim životom i u njemu se smiruju“ – pokudno smirenje.
why.en: “…desire the life of the world and feel secure therein” — a blameworthy ease.

nuance.bs: Smirenost i spokoj koje Allah spušta u srca, najčešće u trenucima straha i iskušenja – na Hunejnu, u pećini, na Hudejbiji.
nuance.en: Calm and peace that Allah sends down into hearts, most often in moments of fear and trial — at Ḥunayn, in the cave, at al-Ḥudaybiya.

why.bs: „On je Onaj Koji je spustio smirenost u srca vjernika da bi svom vjerovanju još vjerovanja dodali“ – سَكِينَة kao dar.
why.en: “He it is Who sent down peace of reassurance into the hearts of the believers that they might add faith unto their faith” — سَكِينَة as a gift.

why.bs: „…pa Allah spusti na njega Svoju smirenost“ – u pećini, u času najvećeg straha (većina: na Poslanika; neki: na Ebu Bekra).
why.en: “Then Allah caused His peace of reassurance to descend upon him” — in the cave, at the hour of greatest fear (most: upon the Prophet; some: upon Abu Bakr).

why.bs: „…kovčeg u kojem je smirenost od vašeg Gospodara“ – tefsir se razilazi šta je ta سَكِينَة bila.
why.en: “…the ark wherein is peace of reassurance from your Lord” — tafsir differs on what this سَكِينَة was.

shared.bs: Sva tri glagola govore o sporu između dvije strane. Razlikuju se po onome čime se spori i gdje se spor vodi.
shared.en: All three verbs speak of a dispute between two sides. They differ in what the dispute is waged with and where it is held.

tellApart.bs: Raspravljati se, nadmudrivati – pokudno kad je radi pobjede, a naređeno kad je „na način koji je najljepši“ (16:125) → جَادَلَ; raspravljati se dokazima, iznositi argumente, najčešće o Allahu i vjeri → حَاجَّ; sporiti se kao zavađene strane, često pred Allahom na Sudnjem danu → اخْتَصَمَ.
tellApart.en: To argue, to contend — blamed when it is for winning, commanded when it is “in the better way” (16:125) → جَادَلَ; to argue with proofs, to bring arguments, most often about Allah and religion → حَاجَّ; to quarrel as opposing parties, often before Allah on the Last Day → اخْتَصَمَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries جدل, حج, خصم
notes: ar-Rāġib: ǧidāl is negotiation by way of contention and trying to overcome, from ǧadaltu l-ḥabla, 'I twisted the rope tight'; ḥuǧǧa is the evidence that makes the right path (maḥaǧǧa) clear, and muḥāǧǧa is each side seeking to turn the other from his proof; ḫuṣūma is contention, at root each side holding the other's side (ḫuṣm). Paraphrased and attributed to him.

That جَادَلَ is praised or commanded in 16:125, 11:74 and 58:1 and blamed elsewhere, that حَاجَّ is about Allah, His messengers or Ibrahim in most places, and that اخْتَصَمَ is a quarrel in the hereafter in 3 of 8 places (26:96, 39:31, 50:28), are our observations of all places.
Blind review: حَاجَّ is arguing with (or claiming) proofs, often without knowledge (3:66); 50:28 and 22:19 glossed with their context.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Raspravljati se, nastojati nadvladati drugoga u govoru. Najčešće pokudno – raspra bez znanja i dokaza; ali Kur'an naređuje raspravu „na način koji je najljepši“ (16:125).
nuance.en: To argue, to try to get the better of another in speech. Most often blamed — argument without knowledge or proof; but the Quran commands argument “in the better way” (16:125).

why.bs: „…i raspravljaj s njima na način koji je najljepši“ – naređena, lijepa rasprava.
why.en: “…and reason with them in the better way” — commanded, gracious argument.

why.bs: „Allah je čuo riječ žene koja se s tobom raspravlja o svom mužu“ – rasprava žene koja traži pravdu.
why.en: “Allah hath heard the saying of her that disputeth with thee (Muhammad) concerning her husband” — a woman arguing for justice.

why.bs: „…oni koji se raspravljaju o Allahovim ajetima bez ikakvog dokaza koji im je došao“ – pokudna rasprava.
why.en: “Those who wrangle concerning the revelations of Allah without any warrant that hath come unto them” — blameworthy argument.

nuance.bs: Raspravljati se navodeći (ili tvrdeći da navodi) dokaze (ḥuǧǧa); u Kur'anu najčešće o Allahu, o vjeri i o Ibrahimu – često i bez znanja.
nuance.en: To argue by bringing (or claiming to bring) proofs (ḥuǧǧa); in the Quran most often about Allah, the religion and Abraham — often without knowledge.

why.bs: „Zar nisi vidio onoga što se s Ibrahimom raspravljao o njegovom Gospodaru?“ – spor dokazima o Allahu.
why.en: “Bethink thee of him who had an argument with Abraham about his Lord” — a dispute of proofs about Allah.

why.bs: „I narod njegov se s njim raspravljao. Rekao je: Zar se sa mnom o Allahu raspravljate…“ – Ibrahim pred svojim narodom.
why.en: “His people argued with him. He said: Dispute ye with me concerning Allah…” — Abraham before his people.

why.bs: „…pa zašto se raspravljate o onome o čemu nemate znanja?“ – raspravljanje bez znanja.
why.en: “Why then argue ye concerning that whereof ye have no knowledge?” — argument without knowledge.

nuance.bs: Sporiti se kao dvije zavađene strane; u Kur'anu često spor pred Allahom na Sudnjem danu.
nuance.en: To quarrel as two opposing parties; in the Quran often a quarrel before Allah on the Last Day.

why.bs: „Zatim ćete se, zaista, na Sudnjem danu pred svojim Gospodarom sporiti“ – spor pred Allahom.
why.en: “Then lo! on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord ye will dispute” — a quarrel before Allah.

why.bs: „Ovo su dvije suprotstavljene strane koje su se sporile o svom Gospodaru“ – dvije zavađene strane (tefsir: vjernici i nevjernici, ili dvoboj na Bedru).
why.en: “These twain are two opponents who contend concerning their Lord” — two opposing parties (tafsir: believers and disbelievers, or the duel at Badr).

why.bs: „Ne sporite se preda Mnom“ – Allah prekida spor: upozorenje je već bilo dato.
why.en: “Contend not in My presence” — Allah closes the dispute: the warning had already been given.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi označavaju početak dana, ali svaka drugi trenutak u njemu.
shared.en: All three words name the beginning of the day, but each a different moment in it.

tellApart.bs: Zora – svjetlost koja ‚probija‘ noć → فَجْر; jutro, kad se razdani i svane → صُبْح; prijepodne, kad se sunce podigne i svjetlost raširi → ضُحًى.
tellApart.en: Dawn — the light that ‘breaks through’ the night → فَجْر; morning, when day has broken and grown light → صُبْح; forenoon, when the sun has risen and its light spreads → ضُحًى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries فجر, صبح, ضحى
notes: ar-Rāġib: faǧr is splitting a thing widely, and dawn is so named for splitting the night; ṣubḥ is the start of the day, when the horizon reddens with the sun's edge; ḍuḥā is the spreading of the sunlight and the lengthening of the day, and the time is named after it. Paraphrased and attributed to him.
The order dawn → morning → forenoon is shown with the Quran's own pictures (2:187 the white thread, 81:18 'when it breathes', 93:1); ṣubḥ, dawn and morning prayer times are not legislated here.
صُبْح is kept apart from the corpus's separate lemma صَبَاح (37:177).
Blind review: Bosnian ṣubḥ rendered 'jutro' (not 'zora', kept for فَجْر) and 74:34 asfara 'razdani'; 93:1 'prijepodnevna svjetlost'; 20:59 'all can see' marked as tafsir.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Zora, prva svjetlost koja probija tamu noći (od korijena ‚rascijepiti, provaliti‘). Njome počinje post i sabahski namaz.
nuance.en: Dawn, the first light that breaks the dark of night (from the root ‘to split, to burst forth’). The fast and the dawn prayer begin with it.

why.bs: „…dok vam se bijela nit ne razluči od crne niti – od zore (الْفَجْرِ)“ – zora kao granica posta.
why.en: “…until the white thread becometh distinct to you from the black thread of the dawn” — dawn as the limit of the fast.

why.bs: „Mir je ona, sve do pojave zore (مَطْلَعِ الْفَجْرِ)“ – kraj Noći Kadr.
why.en: “(The night is) Peace until the rising of the dawn” — the end of the Night of Decree.

why.bs: „…i učenje Kur'ana u zoru – zaista, učenje Kur'ana u zoru je posvjedočeno“ – učenje na sabahskom namazu.
why.en: “…and (the recital of) the Qur'an at dawn. Lo! (the recital of) the Qur'an at dawn is ever witnessed” — the recitation of the dawn prayer.

nuance.bs: Jutro, kad se razdani. Kur'an mu daje slike: kad ‚zablista‘, kad ‚počne disati‘; i jutro kao čas kazne.
nuance.en: Morning, when day has broken. The Quran gives it pictures: when it ‘brightens’, when it ‘breathes’; and morning as the hour of punishment.

why.bs: „I jutra kad zadiše!“ – jutro koje oživljava.
why.en: “And the breath of morning” — morning coming to life.

why.bs: „I jutra kad se rasvijetli!“ – jutro koje se razvidjelo.
why.en: “And the dawn when it shineth forth” — morning grown light.

why.bs: „Zaista, njihov rok je jutro. Zar jutro nije blizu?“ – jutro kao čas kazne Lutovog naroda.
why.en: “Lo! their tryst is (for) the morning. Is not the morning nigh?” — morning as the hour of Lot's people's punishment.

nuance.bs: Doba kad se sunce podigne i njegova svjetlost raširi; Kur'an se njime zaklinje.
nuance.en: The time when the sun has risen and its light spreads; the Quran swears by it.

why.bs: „Tako mi prijepodneva (وَالضُّحَى)!“ – zakletva prijepodnevnom svjetlošću.
why.en: “By the morning hours” — an oath by the forenoon light.

why.bs: „Tako mi Sunca i njegova sjaja (وَضُحَاهَا)!“ – ضُحًى kao sjaj Sunca.
why.en: “By the sun and his brightness” — ضُحًى as the sun's radiance.

why.bs: Musa traži da se ljudi skupe „kad se sunce podigne (ضُحًى)“ – tefsir: vrijeme kad svi mogu vidjeti.
why.en: Moses asks that the people be gathered “when the sun hath risen high” — tafsir: the time when all can see.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o vremenu koje je za nešto određeno. Razlikuju se po tome je li to trajanje, sastanak ili trenutak.
shared.en: All three words speak of time set for something. They differ in whether it is a span, an appointment or a moment.

tellApart.bs: Rok, određeno trajanje – život, narod, dug, iddet → أَجَل; određeno vrijeme sastanka (i mjesto) – Musaov sastanak, Dan odluke → مِيقَات; vrijeme, čas – u Kur'anu (naše zapažanje) samo o Času i poznatom danu → وَقْت.
tellApart.en: A term, a set span — of a life, a nation, a debt, a waiting period → أَجَل; an appointed time of meeting (and place) — Moses' appointment, the Day of Decision → مِيقَات; time, the hour — in the Quran (our observation) only of the Hour and the known day → وَقْت.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries أجل, وقت
notes: ar-Rāġib: aǧal is the span set for a thing; waqt is the end of the time set for an act, so it is hardly said except of what is determined; mīqāt is the time set for a thing and a promise for which a time is fixed (and, by extension, a place) — paraphrased and attributed to him.

That وَقْت occurs 3 times, all of the Hour or 'the day of the known time' (7:187, 15:38, 38:81), and that أَجَل covers life-spans, nations, debts and waiting periods, is our observation of all places. مِيقَات includes its plural مَوَاقِيت (2:189) in one corpus lemma.
أَجَل is the corpus lemma أَجَل only; the different word أَجْل (min aǧli, 'because of', 5:32) is left out.
Blind review: miqāt in 7:142 'appointed time' (not 'term', kept for ajal); the place sense attributed to ar-Rāġib; 15:38 marked as disputed.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
