Blind review (2026-11-06): 3:110 bs 'ummet' (narod kept for قَوْم); 16:120 en follows ar-Rāġib; 49:11 with his reason (women named next); 13:11 bs 'ono što je u njima'.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, svaka skupina koju spaja jedna stvar – vjera, vrijeme ili mjesto – svojevoljno ili po Allahovom određenju; zato su i životinje „zajednice poput vas“ (6:38). Za Ibrahima Kur'an kaže da je bio أُمَّة: sam je, kaže ar-Rāġib, stajao umjesto cijele zajednice u ibadetu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, any group joined by one thing — a religion, a time or a place — by choice or by Allah's ordering; so even animals are “peoples like unto you” (6:38). Of Abraham the Quran says he was an أُمَّة: alone, ar-Rāġib says, he stood in place of a whole community in worship.

why.bs: „Nema nijednog stvora na zemlji … a da nisu zajednice poput vas“ – zajednice po vrsti i načinu života.
why.en: “There is not an animal in the earth … but they are peoples like unto you” — communities by kind and way of life.

why.bs: „Vi ste najbolja zajednica (خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ) koja je izvedena ljudima“ – zajednica spojena vjerom.
why.en: “Ye are the best community (خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ) that hath been raised up for mankind” — a community joined by faith.

why.bs: „Ibrahim je zaista bio أُمَّة, ponizno pokoran Allahu“ – ar-Rāġib: sam kao cijela zajednica u ibadetu.
why.en: “Lo! Abraham was a nation (أُمَّة) obedient to Allah” — ar-Rāġib: alone like a whole community in worship.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, u osnovi skupina muškaraca bez žena (zato 49:11 spominje i jedne i druge), ali u većini Kur'ana obuhvata i muškarce i žene. Najčešća riječ za narod kojem je poslan vjerovjesnik.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, at root a group of men without women (so 49:11 names both), but in most of the Quran it means men and women alike. The usual word for the people a prophet was sent to.

why.bs: „Neka se ljudi (قَوْم) ne izruguju drugim ljudima … niti žene drugim ženama“ – ar-Rāġib: pošto se zatim spominju žene, ovdje قَوْم znači muškarce.
why.en: “Let not a folk (قَوْم) deride a folk … let women (deride) women” — ar-Rāġib: since women are named next, here قَوْم means men.

why.bs: Nuh: „Narode moj, obožavajte Allaha“ – vjerovjesnikov narod.
why.en: Noah: “O my people! Serve Allah” — a prophet's people.

why.bs: „Allah zaista ne mijenja stanje jednog naroda sve dok oni ne izmijene ono što je u njima samima.“
why.en: “Lo! Allah changeth not the condition of a folk until they (first) change that which is in their hearts.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o onima koje Allah šalje ljudima. Kur'an neke vjerovjesnike naziva i jednim i drugim imenom (19:51), a u 22:52 ih spominje odvojeno – dakle se razlikuju.
shared.en: Both words speak of those Allah sends to people. The Quran calls some prophets by both names (19:51), and in 22:52 names the two apart — so they differ.

tellApart.bs: Poslani, onaj koji nosi poruku – vjerovjesnik ili melek → رَسُول; vjerovjesnik, onaj koji donosi vijest od Allaha (a, po nekima, onaj koji je uzdignut) → نَبِيّ.
tellApart.en: One sent, the bearer of a message — a prophet or an angel → رَسُول; a prophet, one who brings news from Allah (and, for some, one raised high) → نَبِيّ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رسل, نبأ, نبى, ختم
notes: ar-Rāġib (رسل): the root is going forth gently; rasūl is said of the message and of its bearer; Allah's rusul are sometimes angels (innahu la-qawlu rasūlin karīm; 11:81, 11:77, 11:69), sometimes prophets (3:144, 5:67). (نبأ): nabaʾ is news of great benefit; nubuwwa is an embassy between Allah and the rational among His servants; the nabī is so called as one who informs, and may be agent or patient (informing / informed). (نبى): some scholars derive nabī from nubuwwa, height — his rank raised above others (19:57).

The common distinction 'a rasūl brings a new law, a nabī follows an earlier one' is not ar-Rāġib's and scholars differ on it: left out. That نَبِيّ is never said of an angel in the Quran, while رُسُل is (11:81, 22:75), is our observation.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries رسل, نبأ, نبى, ختم (2026-11-06): 15 attributed points confirmed
Blind review (2026-11-06): 19:51 bs 'odabran' (muḫlaṣ).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, onaj koji je poslan; riječ se kaže i za samu poruku i za onoga ko je nosi. Allahovi poslanici su ponekad meleki, a ponekad vjerovjesnici.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, one who is sent; the word is said both of the message and of the one who bears it. Allah's messengers are sometimes angels and sometimes prophets.

why.bs: „Muhammed nije ništa drugo nego poslanik“ – vjerovjesnik kao poslanik.
why.en: “Muhammad is but a messenger” — a prophet as messenger.

why.bs: Meleki Lutu: „Lute, mi smo izaslanici (رُسُل) tvoga Gospodara“ – meleki kao poslanici.
why.en: The angels to Lot: “O Lot! Lo! we are messengers (رُسُل) of thy Lord” — angels as messengers.

why.bs: „Nismo prije tebe poslali nijednog poslanika ni vjerovjesnika…“ – dvije riječi navedene odvojeno.
why.en: “Never sent We a messenger or a prophet before thee…” — the two words named apart.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od نَبَأ – važne vijesti: vjerovjesnik obavještava od Allaha, a i sam je obaviješten; neki učenjaci, kako on navodi, riječ izvode od ‚uzvišenosti‘ (19:57). Kur'an tu riječ kaže samo za ljude, nikad za meleke.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from نَبَأ — weighty news: the prophet informs from Allah and is himself informed; some scholars, he reports, derive it from ‘height’ (19:57). The Quran says it only of humans, never of angels.

why.bs: „On je doista bio izabran, i bio je poslanik, vjerovjesnik“ – Musa nazvan i jednim i drugim imenom.
why.en: “Lo! he was chosen, and he was a messenger (of Allah), a prophet” — Moses called by both names.

why.bs: „…nego Allahov Poslanik i pečat vjerovjesnika“ – ar-Rāġib: njime je vjerovjesništvo dovršeno.
why.en: “…but he is the messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets” — ar-Rāġib: with him prophethood was completed.

why.bs: „Ibrahimu su od ljudi najpreči oni koji su ga slijedili, i ovaj Vjerovjesnik, i oni koji vjeruju.“
why.en: “Lo! those of mankind who have the best claim to Abraham are those who followed him, and this Prophet and those who believe.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o ružnim djelima. Prema ar-Rāġibu, فَاحِشَة je ono čija je ružnoća velika, a مُنكَر sve što zdrav razum smatra ružnim, ili šerijat kad razum zastane.
shared.en: Both words speak of foul deeds. According to ar-Rāġib, فَاحِشَة is what is grave in its ugliness, while مُنكَر is anything sound reason judges ugly, or the Sharia where reason hesitates.

tellApart.bs: Djelo ili riječ velike ružnoće, često blud i razvrat → فَاحِشَة; sve što razum ili šerijat odbacuje, suprotnost dobru (مَعْرُوف) → مُنكَر.
tellApart.en: A deed or word of grave ugliness, often fornication and lewdness → فَاحِشَة; whatever reason or the Sharia rejects, the opposite of the right (مَعْرُوف) → مُنكَر.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries فحش, نكر
notes: ar-Rāġib (فحش): fuḥš, faḥšāʾ and fāḥiša are what is grave in ugliness among deeds and words (16:90, 7:28); fāḥiša mubayyina is an allusion to zinā (4:19, 65:1; likewise 4:15). (نكر): munkar is every deed sound minds judge ugly, or on which minds hesitate and the Sharia judges it ugly (3:104, 9:112, 29:29).
فَحْشَاء (7×) is another lemma of the same root and sense; it is named in the texts, not counted.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries فحش, نكر (2026-11-06): 7 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): He gives the Sharia the verdict only where reason hesitates; members/1 already says this correctly; notes/0 (reworded): The fāḥiša mubayyina he glosses is ﴿إلا أن يأتين بفاحشة مبينة﴾ (4:19 / 65:1); 4:15 (no mubayyina) is added 'likewise'. The verse he cites is الآمرون بالمعروف والناهون عن المنكر = 9:112, not 9:71 (he also cites 5:79)
Blind review (2026-11-06): 'mostly fornication' dropped: 'clear fāḥiša' is his euphemism for zinā, the word also any grave foul deed.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, djelo ili riječ čija je ružnoća velika; ‚očitu فَاحِشَة‘ on naziva ublaženim izrazom za blud. U Kur'anu se kaže za blud, za djelo Lutova naroda, ali i za svako veliko ružno djelo.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a deed or word whose ugliness is grave; a ‘clear فَاحِشَة’ he calls a euphemism for fornication. In the Quran it is used of fornication, of the deed of Lot's people, and of any grave foul deed.

why.bs: „I ne približavajte se bludu, jer to je doista razvrat (فَاحِشَة)“ – blud kao velika ružnoća.
why.en: “And come not near unto adultery. Lo! it is an abomination (فَاحِشَة)” — fornication as grave ugliness.

why.bs: Lut: „Zar činite razvrat koji prije vas niko na svijetu nije činio?“
why.en: Lot: “Will ye commit abomination such as no creature ever did before you?”

why.bs: Kad učine razvrat, kažu da su tako zatekli svoje očeve – „Allah zaista ne naređuje razvrat (الْفَحْشَاء)“.
why.en: When they do some lewdness, they say they found their fathers doing it — “Allah, verily, enjoineth not lewdness (الْفَحْشَاء)”.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, svako djelo koje zdrav razum smatra ružnim, ili o kojem razum zastane, pa ga šerijat proglasi ružnim. Najčešće uz مَعْرُوف: naređivati dobro i odvraćati od zla.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, every deed sound reason judges ugly, or about which reason hesitates and the Sharia then judges ugly. Most often beside مَعْرُوف: enjoining the right and forbidding the wrong.

why.bs: „…koji pozivaju na dobro, naređuju ono što je ispravno, a odvraćaju od zla“ – مُنكَر nasuprot مَعْرُوف.
why.en: “…who invite to goodness, and enjoin right conduct and forbid indecency” — مُنكَر against مَعْرُوف.

why.bs: „…i zabranjuje razvrat (الْفَحْشَاء), zlo (الْمُنكَر) i nasilje“ – obje riječi u jednom ajetu.
why.en: “…and forbiddeth lewdness (الْفَحْشَاء) and abomination (الْمُنكَر) and wickedness” — both words in one ayah.

why.bs: Oni koji izgovore zihar „zaista izgovaraju ružnu riječ (مُنكَرًا) i laž“ – i riječ može biti مُنكَر.
why.en: Those who pronounce ẓihār “indeed utter an ill word (مُنكَرًا) and a lie” — a word too can be مُنكَر.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o dobru koje čovjek čini. Prema ar-Rāġibu, بِرّ je širina u činjenju dobra, a إِحْسَان je davanje više nego što se duguje – iznad pravde.
shared.en: Both words speak of the good a person does. According to ar-Rāġib, بِرّ is breadth in doing good, while إِحْسَان is giving more than one owes — above justice.

tellApart.bs: Čestitost, širina u dobru – u vjerovanju i djelima (2:177) → بِرّ; činiti dobro drugome, i činiti lijepo – više od dužnog (uz pravdu u 16:90) → إِحْسَان.
tellApart.en: Righteousness, breadth in goodness — in belief and in deeds (2:177) → بِرّ; doing good to others and doing things well — more than what is due (beside justice in 16:90) → إِحْسَان.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries بر, حسن
notes: ar-Rāġib (بر): from barr, land as against sea, came the sense of breadth: birr is breadth in doing good; ascribed to Allah (52:28) and to the servant; two kinds, in belief and in deeds, both in 2:177; birr to parents is breadth in iḥsān to them. (حسن): iḥsān is of two kinds — doing good to another, and doing one's own work well; it is wider than inʿām; it is above justice (16:90): justice is giving what one owes and taking what one is owed, iḥsān giving more and taking less; justice is obligatory, iḥsān recommended.
That إِحْسَان is the word for treatment of parents in 2:83, 4:36, 6:151, 17:23, 46:15 is our observation of its places.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries بر, حسن (2026-11-06): 13 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): He glosses birr from Allah as الثواب (reward) and from the servant as الطاعة (obedience); 'beneficence, as befits Him' is not his wording
Blind review (2026-11-06): بِرّ in bs 'čestitost' (Korkut 2:177), dobročinstvo kept for إِحْسَان; 3:92 al-birr also as the reward (many mufassirun).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od بَرّ (kopno, širina): širina u činjenju dobra – i u vjerovanju i u djelima, kako ih nabraja 2:177. Kad se kaže za Allaha (الْبَرّ, 52:28), znači Njegovu nagradu, kao što od roba znači pokornost.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from بَرّ (land, wide space): breadth in doing good — in belief and in deeds, as 2:177 lists them. Said of Allah (الْبَرّ, 52:28) it means His reward, as from the servant it means obedience.

why.bs: „Čestitost nije u tome da lica okrećete prema istoku i zapadu, nego…“ – vjerovanje i djela zajedno.
why.en: “It is not righteousness that ye turn your faces to the East and the West; but…” — belief and deeds together.

why.bs: „Nećete doseći čestitost dok ne budete udjeljivali od onoga što volite“ – mnogi mufesiri الْبِرّ ovdje shvataju i kao nagradu u Džennetu.
why.en: “Ye will not attain unto piety (البِرّ) until ye spend of that which ye love” — many mufassirun also understand البِرّ here as the reward of Paradise.

why.bs: „I pomažite se međusobno u čestitosti i bogobojaznosti“ – بِرّ uz takvu.
why.en: “Help ye one another unto righteousness and pious duty” — بِرّ beside taqwā.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, na dva načina: činiti dobro drugome, i lijepo obaviti svoj posao. Iznad je pravde: pravda je dati koliko se duguje i uzeti koliko pripada, a إِحْسَان dati više i uzeti manje. Kur'an njime opisuje odnos prema roditeljima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, in two ways: doing good to another, and doing one's own work well. It is above justice: justice is giving what one owes and taking what one is owed, إِحْسَان giving more and taking less. The Quran uses it for how one treats parents.

why.bs: „Allah zaista naređuje pravednost i dobročinstvo“ – ar-Rāġib: إِحْسَان je iznad pravde.
why.en: “Lo! Allah enjoineth justice and kindness” — ar-Rāġib: إِحْسَان is above justice.

why.bs: „…i da roditeljima činite dobročinstvo“ – إِحْسَان prema roditeljima.
why.en: “…and (that ye show) kindness to parents” — إِحْسَان towards parents.

why.bs: „Zar je nagrada za dobročinstvo išta drugo nego dobročinstvo?“
why.en: “Is the reward of goodness aught save goodness?”

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o šteti. Prema ar-Rāġibu, ضُرّ je loše stanje čovjeka – u duši, tijelu ili imetku – a أَذًى je ono što živo biće pogodi od štete; u 3:111 أَذًى je ono malo što će ih pogoditi, a ne prava šteta.
shared.en: Both words speak of harm. According to ar-Rāġib, ضُرّ is a bad state of a person — in soul, body or means — while أَذًى is harm that reaches a living being; in 3:111 أَذًى is the little that will reach them, not real harm.

tellApart.bs: Nevolja, teško stanje – bolest, siromaštvo, gubitak (ono što Allah otklanja) → ضُرّ; uznemiravanje, uvreda, povreda – često riječima ili postupcima drugih → أَذًى.
tellApart.en: Adversity, a bad state — illness, poverty, loss (what Allah removes) → ضُرّ; hurt, annoyance, injury — often from others' words or deeds → أَذًى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ضر, أذى
notes: ar-Rāġib (ضر): ḍurr is a bad state — in the soul (little knowledge, virtue, chastity), in the body (a lost or defective limb), or in outward circumstances (little wealth or standing); 21:84 may hold all three; 3:111 lan yaḍurrūkum illā aḏā tells them how little will reach them and assures them against real harm. (أذى): aḏā is harm reaching a living being, in soul, body or what follows from it, worldly or otherworldly (2:264, 9:61, 33:69, 2:222).
3:111 holds the verb ضَرَّ, not the noun ضُرّ; it is cited for أَذًى. Ayyub's plea (21:83) is cited through 21:84 (Allah's removing it).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

The 'touches … Allah removes' sentence is unattributed (he does cite مس and كشف verses)
Blind review (2026-11-06): 'mostly' softened to 'often' (ḍurr is also the harm idols cannot do).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, loše stanje – u duši (malo znanja i vrline), u tijelu (gubitak uda, nedostatak) ili u prilikama (siromaštvo, nizak položaj). U Kur'anu je to često nevolja koja ‚dotakne‘ čovjeka, i koju Allah otklanja.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a bad state — in the soul (little knowledge and virtue), in the body (a lost limb, a defect) or in one's circumstances (poverty, low standing). In the Quran it is often adversity that ‘touches’ a person, and which Allah removes.

why.bs: „A kad čovjeka dotakne nevolja, on Nas zaziva … a kad mu otklonimo nevolju, on prođe kao da Nas nije ni zazivao“ – nevolja i zaborav nakon nje.
why.en: “And if misfortune touch a man he crieth unto Us … but when We have relieved him of the misfortune he goeth his way as though he had not cried unto Us” — adversity, and forgetting after it.

why.bs: „Pa smo mu uslišali molbu i uklonili nevolju koja ga je bila snašla“ – ar-Rāġib: Ejjubova nevolja može obuhvatiti sve tri vrste.
why.en: “Then We heard his prayer and removed that adversity from which he suffered” — ar-Rāġib: Job's adversity may cover all three kinds.

why.bs: „Ako te Allah dotakne nevoljom, nema nikoga ko bi je otklonio osim Njega.“
why.en: “If Allah touch thee with affliction, there is none that can relieve therefrom save Him.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, šteta koja pogodi živo biće – u duši, tijelu ili posljedicama, na ovom ili budućem svijetu. Često dolazi od drugih: prigovaranje uz sadaku, uvrede upućene vjerovjesnicima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, harm that reaches a living being — in soul, body or consequences, in this world or the next. Often it comes from others: reproach that follows charity, insults aimed at the prophets.

why.bs: „Neće vam naškoditi, osim što će vas malo uznemiriti (أَذًى)“ – ar-Rāġib: malo će vas od njih pogoditi.
why.en: “They will not harm you save a trifling hurt (أَذًى)” — ar-Rāġib: little will reach you from them.

why.bs: „Ne poništavajte svoje sadake prigovaranjem i vrijeđanjem (الْأَذَى)“ – povreda riječima.
why.en: “Render not vain your almsgiving by reproach and injury (الْأَذَى)” — hurt by words.

why.bs: „Pitaju te o mjesečnici. Reci: To je tegoba (أَذًى)“ – ar-Rāġib: po šerijatu i po medicini.
why.en: “They question thee (O Muhammad) concerning menstruation. Say: It is an illness (أَذًى)” — ar-Rāġib: by the Sharia and by medicine.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o tome da je čovjek oboren. Prema ar-Rāġibu, i poniznost (ذُلّ) i sramota (خِزْي) mogu doći od samog čovjeka ili od drugoga: za poniznost: od sebe je pohvalna, nametnuta od drugog pokuđena.
shared.en: All three words speak of a person brought low. According to ar-Rāġib, both lowliness (ذُلّ) and shame (خِزْي) may come from the person himself or from another: for lowliness, from oneself it is praised, imposed by another it is blamed.

tellApart.bs: Poniženje koje je nametnuto, kazna → ذِلَّة; poniznost – pohvalna kad je od sebe (prema roditeljima), pokuđena kad je nametnuta (42:45) → ذُلّ; sramota, osramoćenost pred drugima → خِزْي.
tellApart.en: Abasement imposed, a punishment → ذِلَّة; lowliness — praised when one's own (towards parents), blamed when imposed (42:45) → ذُلّ; disgrace, being shamed before others → خِزْي.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ذل, خزى, جنح, ولى
notes: ar-Rāġib (ذل): ḏull (with ḍamma) is from subjugation, ḏill (with kasra) is after unruliness, without subjugation (tameness); 17:24 janāḥa ḏ-ḏull: be as one subdued before them; ḏilla in 2:61, 7:152, 10:27; lowliness a person takes on himself is praised (5:54, 3:123). (خزى): ḫizy is a brokenness that comes over a man, either from himself — excessive shame (ḫazāya) — or from another — a kind of disgrace (ḫizy) (2:114, 16:27, 39:26); likewise ḏull and hūn: from oneself praised, from another blamed.

20:134 (an naḏilla wa naḫzā) holds both roots as verbs, not the members' nouns; named in the text only. 17:111 (Allah has no protector out of weakness) is cited with 'as befits Him' implicit in the negation.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries ذل, خزى, جنح, ولى (2026-11-06): 15 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): Praise/blame is stated for ḏull and hūn (by analogy with ḫizy), not for ḫizy itself; ḫizy from oneself is 'excessive shame', never called praised; members/2/nuance (reworded): He defines the other-inflicted kind as 'a kind of being slighted / held in contempt' (istiḫfāf); 'disgraced' is close but looser. The Quranic-usage sentence is not attributed

Blind review (2026-11-06): praise/blame tied to the source, not to ذُلّ (42:45 is imposed); 10:27 'humiliation will overtake them' (the faces are covered by night); 'far from Allah' limited to weakness and need (17:111); 42:45 bs 'nepravednici'.

nuance.bs: Poniženje koje je nametnuto – u Kur'anu kazna: „na njih je udareno poniženje i bijeda“ (2:61), „prekrit će ih poniženje“ (10:27).
nuance.en: Abasement that is imposed — in the Quran a punishment: “humiliation and wretchedness were stamped upon them” (2:61), “ignominy overtaketh them” (10:27).

why.bs: „I na njih je udareno poniženje i bijeda“ – poniženje kao kazna.
why.en: “And humiliation and wretchedness were stamped upon them” — abasement as punishment.

why.bs: „…i prekrit će ih poniženje“ – poniženje kao kazna za one koji su činili zlo.
why.en: “…and ignominy overtaketh them” — abasement as the punishment of those who did evil.

why.bs: „One koji su uzeli tele zaista će stići srdžba njihovog Gospodara i poniženje u ovosvjetskom životu.“
why.en: “Lo! Those who chose the calf (for worship), terror from their Lord and humiliation will come upon them in the life of the world.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, poniznost je pohvalna kada je čovjek sam uzme na sebe – kao prema roditeljima: „spusti prema njima krilo poniznosti“ (17:24), budi pred njima kao savladan, kaže on. Allah je daleko od svake slabosti: ne treba Mu zaštitnik zbog nemoći (17:111).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, lowliness is praised when a person takes it on himself — as towards parents: “lower unto them the wing of submission” (17:24), be before them as one subdued, he says. Allah is far above any weakness: He needs no protector out of lowliness (17:111).

why.bs: „I spusti prema njima krilo poniznosti (جَنَاحَ الذُّلِّ) iz milosti“ – pohvalna poniznost.
why.en: “And lower unto them the wing of submission (جَنَاحَ الذُّلِّ) through mercy” — praised lowliness.

why.bs: Nepravednici izvedeni pred Vatru, „skrušeni od poniženja“ – nametnuta poniznost.
why.en: The wrongdoers brought before the Fire, “made humble by disgrace” — imposed lowliness.

why.bs: „…niti ima zaštitnika zbog nemoći (مِنَ الذُّلِّ)“ – Allah je slobodan od svake slabosti.
why.en: “…nor hath He any protecting friend through dependence (مِنَ الذُّلِّ)” — Allah is free of all weakness.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, slomljenost koja čovjeka obuzme – od sebe (pretjeran stid) ili od drugoga (prezir drugih). U Kur'anu najčešće sramota kao kazna, na ovom svijetu i na onom.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a brokenness that comes over a person — from himself (excessive shame) or from another (being treated with contempt). In the Quran it is mostly disgrace as punishment, in this world and the next.

why.bs: „Za njih je na ovom svijetu sramota, a na onom svijetu velika kazna.“
why.en: “Theirs in the world is ignominy and theirs in the Hereafter is an awful doom.”

why.bs: „Pa im je Allah dao da okuse sramotu u životu na ovom svijetu.“
why.en: “Thus Allah made them taste humiliation in the life of the world.”

why.bs: „Danas su sramota i zlo zaista na nevjernicima“ – sramota na Sudnjem danu.
why.en: “Disgrace this day and evil are upon the disbelievers” — disgrace on the Day.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o onome što se vidi u snu. U Kur'anu je رُؤْيَا uvijek istinit san koji se ostvari, a kao ‚snovi‘ أَحْلَام dolazi samo u izrazu أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ – ‚zbrkani snovi‘ (12:44, 21:5).
shared.en: Both words speak of what is seen in sleep. In the Quran رُؤْيَا is always a true dream that comes to pass, while as ‘dreams’ أَحْلَام comes only in the phrase أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ, ‘confused dreams’ (12:44, 21:5).

tellApart.bs: San koji se vidi i ima značenje – u Kur'anu uvijek istinit → رُؤْيَا; snovi (samo u izrazu ‚zbrkani snovi‘), a ista riječ znači i punoljetnost i, preneseno, razum → حُلُم.
tellApart.en: What is seen in sleep and has a meaning — in the Quran always true → رُؤْيَا; dreams (only in ‘confused dreams’), and the same word also means maturity and, by extension, minds → حُلُم.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رأى, حلم
notes: ar-Rāġib (رأى): ruʾyā is what is seen in sleep; he quotes the report that nothing of the heralds of prophethood remains but the ruʾyā, and cites 48:27, 17:60. (حلم): ḥilm is restraint of the soul from rage; aḥlāmuhum (52:32) was explained as their minds — ḥilm is not reason itself but one of its fruits; al-ḥulum (24:59) is maturity; ḥalama is to see in a dream (12:44).

That رُؤْيَا is in all its places a true dream (12:5, 12:43, 12:100, 17:60, 37:105, 48:27) and أَحْلَام only the deniers' or courtiers' 'confused dreams' is our observation of all places. The lemma حُلُم (6×) holds dream (12:44 ×2, 21:5), maturity (24:58, 24:59) and minds (52:32).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries رأى, حلم (2026-11-06): 11 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): The report as he quotes it says only 'al-ruʾyā'; 'true' is added. The Quranic-usage sentence is not attributed to him; members/1/nuance (improved): He derives 'minds' and 'maturity' from ḥilm with stated reasons, but lists 'to dream' without deriving it from self-restraint; he also stresses ḥilm is not reason itself. The 'confused dreams' sentence is Quranic usage, unattributed; members/1/ayat/2/why (improved): He reports the gloss ('qīla') and qualifies it: ḥilm is not reason itself but an effect of it

Blind review (2026-11-06): 'only in confused dreams' limited to the dream sense (52:32 is minds); 'reason' as ḥilm's source, not ḥilm itself; 'meaning not recognised' replaced by who says the phrase (12:44, 21:5).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ono što se vidi u snu; navodi predanje da od nagovještaja vjerovjesništva nije ostalo ništa osim sna (ruʾyā). U Kur'anu je رُؤْيَا svaki put san koji se ostvari: Jusufov, vladarev, Ibrahimov, Poslanikov.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, what is seen in sleep; he cites the report that nothing of the heralds of prophethood remains but the dream (ruʾyā). In the Quran every رُؤْيَا comes to pass: Joseph's, the king's, Abraham's, the Prophet's.

why.bs: „Sine moj, ne kazuj svoj san svojoj braći“ – Jusufov san, koji se ostvario (12:100).
why.en: “O my dear son! Tell not thy brethren of thy vision” — Joseph's dream, fulfilled in 12:100.

why.bs: Vladar: „Recite mi šta znači moj san, ako umijete tumačiti snove“ – san sa značenjem.
why.en: The king: “Expound for me my vision, if ye can interpret dreams” — a dream with a meaning.

why.bs: „San si već obistinio“ – Ibrahimov san.
why.en: “Thou hast already fulfilled the vision” — Abraham's dream.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, iz korijena koji znači savladavanje sebe od srdžbe: ‚razum‘ (52:32), jer blagost proizlazi iz razuma, i ‚punoljetnost‘ (24:59), kad čovjek postane dostojan blagosti; isti korijen daje i ‚sanjati‘. Kao snovi, u Kur'anu dolazi samo u izrazu ‚zbrkani snovi‘, koji govore oni što odbacuju viđenje (12:44) ili objavu (21:5).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from a root meaning self-restraint from anger: ‘minds’ (52:32), since forbearance springs from reason, and ‘maturity’ (24:59), when one becomes worthy of forbearance; the same root gives ‘to dream’. As dreams it comes in the Quran only in ‘confused dreams’, said by those who dismiss a vision (12:44) or the revelation (21:5).

why.bs: „Zbrkani snovi (أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ)! A mi tumačenje snova ne znamo“ – dvorjani o vladarevom istinitom snu.
why.en: “Jumbled dreams (أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ)! And we are not knowing in the interpretation of dreams” — the courtiers on the king's true dream.

why.bs: „A kad djeca među vama dosegnu punoljetnost (الْحُلُم)…“ – ista riječ za punoljetnost.
why.en: “And when the children among you come to puberty (الْحُلُم)…” — the same word for maturity.

why.bs: „Zar im njihov razum (أَحْلَامُهُم) to naređuje?“ – ar-Rāġib: tumači se kao razum, jer blagost proizlazi iz razuma.
why.en: “Do their minds (أَحْلَامُهُم) command them to do this?” — ar-Rāġib: explained as their minds, since forbearance springs from reason.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o oduzimanju života. Prema ar-Rāġibu, قَتْل je najopćenitija riječ za to, a ذَبْح je presijecanje grla.
shared.en: Both words speak of taking life. According to ar-Rāġib, قَتْل is the most general word for it, while ذَبْح is cutting the throat.

tellApart.bs: Ubiti – na bilo koji način, kao nečije djelo → قَتَلَ; zaklati, presjeći grlo (najčešće životinju) → ذَبَحَ.
tellApart.en: To kill — in any way, as someone's act → قَتَلَ; to slaughter, to cut the throat (most often of an animal) → ذَبَحَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries قتل, ذبح
notes: ar-Rāġib (قتل): qatl is removing the spirit from the body, like death; called qatl when seen as someone's act, mawt when seen as the loss of life (3:144); in 5:95 He said qatl, not ḏabḥ or ḏakāh, because qatl is the most general of these words — taking a game animal's life in any way is forbidden. (ذبح, headed without any mark in OpenITI; the parser lists it by its opening words): ḏabḥ is cutting animals' throats (2:67, 37:107); yuḏabbiḥūna (2:49) is intensive — slaughtering one after another.
ذَبَحَ (Form I, 5×) is counted; the intensive ذَبَّحَ (2:49, 14:6, 28:4, Pharaoh's killing of the sons) is another verb, named in the text only.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries قتل, ذبح (2026-11-06): 13 attributed points confirmed
Blind review (2026-11-06): ذَبَحَ also names Pharaoh's slaughter of the sons (2:49), which ar-Rāġib cites.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, oduzeti dušu tijelu, kao smrt; kaže se قَتْل kad se gleda kao nečije djelo, a ‚smrt‘ kad se gleda kao gubitak života. To je najopćenitija riječ za ubijanje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, removing the soul from the body, like death; it is called قَتْل when seen as someone's act, and death when seen as the loss of life. It is the most general word for killing.

why.bs: „Pa ako on umre ili bude ubijen…“ – ar-Rāġib: smrt kao gubitak života, ubistvo kao nečije djelo.
why.en: “Will it be that, when he dieth or is slain…” — ar-Rāġib: death as loss of life, killing as someone's act.

why.bs: „Ne ubijajte lovinu dok ste u ihramu“ – ar-Rāġib: rečeno je قَتْل, a ne ‚klanje‘, jer je opće – zabranjen je svaki način.
why.en: “Kill no wild game while ye are on the pilgrimage” — ar-Rāġib: قَتْل, not slaughter, because it is general — every way is forbidden.

why.bs: „Ko ubije dušu, a ne zbog ubijene duše … kao da je ubio sve ljude.“
why.en: “Whosoever killeth a human being for other than manslaughter … it shall be as if he had killed all mankind.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, presjeći grlo životinji. U Kur'anu: krava koju je Allah naredio da se zakolje; Ibrahimov san da kolje sina – a Allah ga je otkupio velikom žrtvom (37:107); i faraonovi ljudi koji „kolju vaše sinove“ (2:49), što ar-Rāġib shvata kao klanje koje se ponavlja, jedno za drugim.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, cutting an animal's throat. In the Quran: the cow Allah ordered slaughtered; Abraham's dream of sacrificing his son — whom Allah ransomed with a great sacrifice (37:107); and Pharaoh's men “slaying your sons” (2:49) — يُذَبِّحُونَ, which ar-Rāġib takes as slaughter repeated, one after another.

why.bs: „Allah vam doista naređuje da zakoljete jednu kravu“ – klanje životinje.
why.en: “Lo! Allah commandeth you that ye sacrifice a cow” — slaughtering an animal.

why.bs: „Sine moj, ja u snu vidim da te koljem“ – Ibrahimov san; sin je otkupljen (37:107).
why.en: “O my dear son, I have seen in a dream that I must sacrifice thee” — Abraham's dream; the son was ransomed (37:107).

why.bs: Sulejman o pupavcu: „…ili ću ga sigurno zaklati, osim ako mi ne donese jasan dokaz“ – klanje kao kazna.
why.en: Solomon of the hoopoe: “…or I verily will slay him, or he verily shall bring me a plain excuse” — slaughter as a penalty.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o obavezi koja se mora ispuniti. Prema ar-Rāġibu, عَهْد je čuvanje i paženje nečega iznova i iznova, a مِيثَاق je ugovor učvršćen zakletvom i zavjetom.
shared.en: Both words speak of a bond that must be kept. According to ar-Rāġib, عَهْد is guarding and attending to a thing again and again, while مِيثَاق is a pact made firm by oath and pledge.

tellApart.bs: Zavjet, obaveza koju treba čuvati – Allahova i ljudska → عَهْد; čvrsti ugovor, učvršćen zakletvom (s vjerovjesnicima, sa sinovima Israilovim, u braku) → مِيثَاق.
tellApart.en: A pledge, a bond to be kept — Allah's and people's → عَهْد; a firm covenant, sealed by oath (with the prophets, the Children of Israel, in marriage) → مِيثَاق.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عهد, وثق
notes: ar-Rāġib (عهد): ʿahd is keeping and attending to a thing time after time; the binding pledge is called ʿahd (17:34); Allah's ʿahd is sometimes what He set in our minds, sometimes what He commanded in the Book and through His messengers, sometimes what we take upon ourselves, like vows (9:75). (وثق, headed without any mark in OpenITI; the parser lists it by its opening words): mīṯāq is a pact confirmed by oath and pledge (3:81, 33:7, 4:154).
2:27 and 13:20 hold both words. 2:124 (lā yanālu ʿahdī) is not cited: tafsir differs on what the ʿahd is there.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries عهد, وثق (2026-11-06): 10 attributed points confirmed
Blind review (2026-11-06): مِيثَاق in bs 'čvrst ugovor' (zavjet kept for عَهْد).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, čuvanje i paženje nečega iznova i iznova; zato se zavjet koji se mora paziti zove عَهْد. Allahov zavjet je ono što je usadio u razum, ono što je naredio Knjigom i poslanicima, i ono što ljudi sami preuzmu, kao zavjet.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, keeping and attending to a thing time after time; so a pledge that must be watched over is called عَهْد. Allah's pledge is what He set in the mind, what He commanded by the Book and the messengers, and what people take upon themselves, like a vow.

why.bs: „I ispunjavajte zavjet (الْعَهْد), jer će se za zavjet zaista pitati.“
why.en: “And keep the covenant (الْعَهْد). Lo! of the covenant it will be asked.”

why.bs: „Oni koji krše Allahov zavjet (عَهْد) pošto su ga čvrsto potvrdili (مِيثَاق)“ – obje riječi zajedno.
why.en: “Those who break the covenant (عَهْد) of Allah after ratifying it (مِيثَاق)” — both words together.

why.bs: „A ko svoj zavjet ispunjava bolje od Allaha?“
why.en: “Who fulfilleth His covenant better than Allah?”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ugovor učvršćen zakletvom i zavjetom. Kur'an ga koristi za Allahov ugovor s vjerovjesnicima, sa sinovima Israilovim, i za brak – „čvrst ugovor“ (4:21).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a pact confirmed by oath and pledge. The Quran uses it for Allah's covenant with the prophets, with the Children of Israel, and for marriage — “a strong pledge” (4:21).

why.bs: „I kad je Allah uzeo ugovor (مِيثَاق) od vjerovjesnika…“ – ugovor s vjerovjesnicima.
why.en: “When Allah made (His) covenant (مِيثَاق) with the prophets…” — the pact with the prophets.

why.bs: „…a uzele su od vas čvrst ugovor (مِيثَاقًا غَلِيظًا)“ – brak kao čvrst ugovor.
why.en: “…and they have taken a strong pledge (مِيثَاقًا غَلِيظًا) from you” — marriage as a firm pact.

why.bs: „Oni koji ispunjavaju zavjet dat Allahu i ne raskidaju ugovor“ – عَهْد i مِيثَاق jedno uz drugo.
why.en: “Such as keep the pact (عَهْد) of Allah, and break not the covenant (مِيثَاق)” — عَهْد and مِيثَاق side by side.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi su optužbe kojima su poricatelji nazivali Poslanika, a Kur'an ih odbacuje: vrača i pjesnika (52:29, 69:41–42), dok čarobnjak „neće uspjeti“ (20:69).
shared.en: All three words are charges the deniers laid against the Prophet, and the Quran rejects them: the soothsayer and the poet (52:29, 69:41–42), while “a wizard shall not be successful” (20:69).

tellApart.bs: Onaj ko obmanjuje oči opsjenom ili traži pomoć šejtana → سَاحِر; vrač koji tvrdi da zna skriveno nagađanjem → كَاهِن; pjesnik – a po nekima, u toj optužbi: onaj ko izmišlja → شَاعِر.
tellApart.en: One who deceives the eye with illusion or seeks the devils' help → سَاحِر; a soothsayer who claims hidden knowledge by guessing → كَاهِن; a poet — and for some scholars, in that charge: a teller of fictions → شَاعِر.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries سحر, كهن, شعر
notes: ar-Rāġib (سحر): siḥr is said of deception and illusions without reality (7:116, 20:66) — in this sense Moses was called sāḥir (43:49) — of seeking the devils' help by drawing near to them (2:102), and of what the ignorant believe — changing forms and natures — which has no reality. (كهن): the kāhin tells hidden past matters by a kind of guessing, the ʿarrāf future ones; both rest on guessing that errs and hits. (شعر): shiʿr is at root fine knowledge, then measured rhymed speech; many mufassirun took 'poet' as a charge of bringing verse; some careful scholars say they charged him with lying, as shiʿr stands for falsehood (26:224).
That all three are the deniers' charges against the Prophet (and sāḥir also against Moses, 43:49), each refuted, is the Quran's own word; the texts present them as charges only.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries سحر, كهن, شعر (2026-11-06): 18 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): He attaches 'in this view they called Moses a sāḥir' to the FIRST sense (deception, illusion, sleight of hand), not to the third (the ignorant's belief in transformation). Fix key 'en' applies to this plain-string note; members/0/ayat/2/why (improved): 'This view' refers to the first sense he lists — deception, illusions without reality, like the juggler's sleight of hand
Blind review (2026-11-06): 'the Quran rejects each' made precise: soothsayer and poet (52:29, 69:41–42), the magician 'will not succeed' (20:69).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, sihr je opsjena bez stvarnosti, ili traženje pomoći šejtana; a vjerovanje da sihr mijenja oblike stvari nema stvarnosti. Poricatelji su tako zvali i Musaa i Poslanika; Kur'an kaže da čarobnjak nikad neće uspjeti.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, sorcery is illusion without reality, or seeking the devils' help; the belief that it changes the forms of things has no reality. The deniers called both Moses and the Prophet by this name; the Quran says the magician will never succeed.

why.bs: „A čarobnjak neće uspjeti gdje god došao“ – sihr bez stvarne moći.
why.en: “A wizard shall not be successful to whatever point (of skill) he may attain” — sorcery without real power.

why.bs: Nevjernici o Poslaniku: „Ovo je doista očiti čarobnjak!“ – optužba koju Kur'an odbacuje.
why.en: The disbelievers of the Prophet: “Lo! this is a mere wizard” — a charge the Quran rejects.

why.bs: Faraonovi ljudi Musau: „O čarobnjače, zamoli za nas svoga Gospodara“ – ar-Rāġib: tako su ga zvali u smislu opsjene i vještine ruku.
why.en: Pharaoh's people to Moses: “O wizard! Entreat thy Lord for us” — ar-Rāġib: they called him so in the sense of illusion and sleight of hand.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, onaj ko kazuje skrivene prošle stvari nekom vrstom nagađanja (a عَرَّاف buduće); obje vještine počivaju na nagađanju koje nekad pogodi, a nekad promaši. U Kur'anu dva puta, oba puta odbačena optužba.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, one who tells hidden past matters by a kind of guessing (the عَرَّاف tells future ones); both crafts rest on guessing that sometimes hits and sometimes misses. Twice in the Quran, both times a rejected charge.

why.bs: „Ti, blagodaću svoga Gospodara, nisi ni vrač ni luđak.“
why.en: “By the grace of Allah thou art neither soothsayer nor madman.”

why.bs: „Niti je to govor vrača – kako se malo opominjete!“
why.en: “Nor diviner's speech - little is it that ye remember!”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, شِعْر u osnovi znači tanano znanje, a zatim odmjeren i rimovan govor. Mnogi mufesiri optužbu ‚pjesnik‘ razumiju kao optužbu da je Kur'an stih; neki učenjaci kažu da su ga time nazvali lažovom, jer je poezija mjesto izmišljanja (26:224).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, شِعْر at root means fine knowledge, then measured, rhymed speech. Many mufassirun take the charge ‘poet’ as calling the Quran verse; some scholars say they meant to call him a liar, since poetry is the home of invention (26:224).

why.bs: „I nije to govor pjesnika – kako malo vjerujete!“
why.en: “It is not poet's speech - little is it that ye believe!”

why.bs: „…ne, nego ga je izmislio, ne, nego je on pjesnik“ – optužbe se nižu jedna za drugom.
why.en: “…nay, he hath but invented it; nay, he is but a poet” — the charges follow one another.

why.bs: „A pjesnike slijede oni koji su zalutali“ – ar-Rāġib: odatle veza poezije i izmišljanja.
why.en: “As for poets, the erring follow them” — ar-Rāġib: hence poetry's link to invention.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o nedostatku razboritosti. Prema ar-Rāġibu, جَهْل je neznanje, pogrešno vjerovanje ili postupanje kako ne treba, a سَفَه je lakoća duše zbog manjka razuma.
shared.en: Both words speak of a lack of sound judgement. According to ar-Rāġib, جَهْل is not knowing, wrong belief or acting as one should not, while سَفَه is a lightness of soul from lack of reason.

tellApart.bs: Neznalica – onaj ko ne zna, ili postupa kako ne treba (najčešće kao prijekor) → جَاهِل; lakouman, nerazborit – u imetku ili u vjeri → سَفِيه.
tellApart.en: One who does not know, or behaves as one should not (mostly as blame) → جَاهِل; light-minded, without sound judgement — in wealth or in religion → سَفِيه.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries جهل, سفه
notes: ar-Rāġib (جهل): jahl has three kinds — the soul empty of knowledge; believing a thing other than it is; doing a thing other than it should be done, whatever one believes (2:67: mockery counted as jahl); the jāhil is mostly named in blame, sometimes not (2:273: one who does not know their state). (سفه): safah is lightness in the body, then lightness of soul from lack of reason, in worldly matters (4:5) and in religion (72:4, 2:13, 2:142).
25:63 (the ignorant addressing the servants of the Merciful) is the rude-behaviour sense, glossed as such. 7:199 is cited in aarada-tawalla, not here.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries جهل, سفه (2026-11-06): 14 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/nuance (reworded): He illustrates worldly safah with 4:5 but does not mention squandering
Blind review (2026-11-06): 72:4 bs 'bezumnik' (neznalica kept for جَاهِل) and 'preko svake mjere'; 4:5 bs 'nerazumnima'.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, neznanje je trojako: neznanje, pogrešno vjerovanje, i postupanje kako ne treba – zato Musa podsmijeh naziva neznanjem. Riječ najčešće kudi, ali ne uvijek: u 2:273 ‚neznalica‘ je samo onaj ko ne poznaje stanje siromaha.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ignorance is of three kinds: not knowing, believing wrongly, and acting as one should not — so Moses calls mockery ignorance. The word mostly blames, but not always: in 2:273 the ‘ignorant’ is simply one who does not know the poor's state.

why.bs: Musa: „Tražim utočište kod Allaha od toga da budem od neznalica“ – ar-Rāġib: podsmijeh kao neznanje.
why.en: Moses: “Allah forbid that I should be among the foolish [the ignorant]!” — ar-Rāġib: mockery as ignorance.

why.bs: „Onaj ko ne zna (الْجَاهِل) smatra ih imućnim zbog njihove suzdržanosti“ – neznalica bez prijekora.
why.en: “The unthinking man [الْجَاهِل, the one who does not know] accounteth them wealthy because of their restraint” — the ignorant without blame.

why.bs: „…a kad im se neznalice obrate, odgovore: Mir“ – neznanje kao grubo ponašanje.
why.en: “…and when the foolish ones (الْجَاهِلُونَ) address them answer: Peace” — ignorance as rude behaviour.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, u osnovi lakoća (i tijela), a zatim lakoća duše zbog manjka razuma – u svjetovnim stvarima (kojima se ne predaje imetak, 4:5) i u vjeri. Licemjeri su vjernike zvali سُفَهَاء, a Kur'an kaže da su to oni sami.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, at root lightness (even of the body), then lightness of soul from lack of reason — in worldly matters (those not to be given wealth, 4:5) and in religion. The hypocrites called the believers سُفَهَاء, and the Quran says they themselves are.

why.bs: „I ne dajite nerazboritima (السُّفَهَاء) svoje imetke“ – nerazboritost u imetku.
why.en: “Give not unto the foolish (السُّفَهَاء) your wealth” — unsoundness in handling wealth.

why.bs: „Zar da vjerujemo kao što su povjerovali bezumnici? Zaista, upravo su oni bezumnici“ – optužba vraćena licemjerima.
why.en: “Shall we believe as the foolish believe? are not they indeed the foolish?” — the charge turned back on the hypocrites.

why.bs: Džini: „Naš je bezumnik o Allahu govorio ono što prelazi svaku mjeru“ – lakoumnost u vjeri.
why.en: The jinn: “the foolish one among us used to speak concerning Allah an atrocious lie” — foolishness in religion.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o brzini. Prema ar-Rāġibu, عَجَلَة je tražiti nešto prije njegova vremena – dolazi od strasti, pa je pokuđena u većini Kur'ana – a سُرْعَة je samo suprotnost sporosti.
shared.en: All three words speak of speed. According to ar-Rāġib, عَجَلَة is seeking a thing before its time — it springs from desire, so it is blamed in most of the Quran — while سُرْعَة is simply the opposite of slowness.

tellApart.bs: Požuriti, prije vremena → عَجِلَ; tražiti da nešto dođe brže (poricatelji traže kaznu) → اِسْتَعْجَلَ; hitati, natjecati se u brzini – hvaljeno ili kuđeno po cilju → سَارَعَ.
tellApart.en: To hurry, before the time → عَجِلَ; to ask for a thing to come sooner (the deniers demanding the punishment) → اِسْتَعْجَلَ; to hasten, to vie in speed — praised or blamed by its goal → سَارَعَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عجل, سرع
notes: ar-Rāġib (عجل): ʿaǧala is seeking a thing and pursuing it before its time; it comes from desire, so it is blamed in most of the Quran (21:37, 20:114, 20:83, 16:1, 13:6, 10:11); Moses' haste (20:84), though haste is blamed, was moved by a praised thing — seeking Allah's pleasure; 'man was created of haste' (21:37) means it is one of the traits he is made with. (سرع): surʿa is the opposite of slowness; sāriʿū (3:133), yusāriʿūna fi l-ḫayrāt (3:114).
That سَارَعَ is praised or blamed by its goal — good deeds and forgiveness (3:114, 3:133, 21:90, 23:61) or disbelief and sin (3:176, 5:41, 5:52, 5:62) — is our observation of all nine places.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries عجل, سرع (2026-11-06): 12 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): He grounds the blame in its coming from desire (šahwa), not in its being before its time; members/2/nuance (reworded): He gives a neutral definition but never says the word carries no blame; that is our inference. The following Quranic-usage sentence keeps the contrast without his name
Blind review (2026-11-06): no flag.

meaning.en: to hasten, to be in haste

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, tražiti nešto prije njegova vremena; dolazi od strasti, pa je u većini Kur'ana pokuđeno. Musaova žurba ka Allahu (20:84) je, kaže on, bila žurba, ali ju je pokrenulo nešto hvale vrijedno – traženje Allahova zadovoljstva.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, seeking a thing before its time; it comes from desire, so in most of the Quran it is blamed. Moses' haste to Allah (20:84) was, he says, haste, but what moved it was praiseworthy — seeking Allah's pleasure.

why.bs: Musa: „A ja sam Ti požurio, Gospodaru moj, da bi Ti bio zadovoljan“ – ar-Rāġib: žurba s hvale vrijednim povodom.
why.en: Moses: “I hastened unto Thee, my Lord, that Thou mightest be well pleased” — ar-Rāġib: haste with a praised motive.

why.bs: „I nemoj žuriti s Kur'anom dok ti se njegova objava ne dovrši“ – ne prije vremena.
why.en: “And hasten not (O Muhammad) with the Qur'an ere its revelation hath been perfected unto thee” — not before its time.

why.bs: „Zato ne žuri da ih stigne kazna; Mi im samo brojimo dane“ – sve ima svoj rok.
why.en: “So make no haste against them (O Muhammad). We do but number unto them a sum (of days)” — everything has its term.

meaning.en: to ask to hasten, to be impatient for

nuance.bs: Tražiti da nešto dođe prije vremena. U Kur'anu najčešće poricatelji koji podrugljivo traže da kazna dođe odmah.
nuance.en: To ask for a thing to come before its time. In the Quran most often the deniers mockingly demanding that the punishment come at once.

why.bs: „Allahova odredba je stigla, zato je ne požurujte!“
why.en: “The commandment of Allah will come to pass, so seek not ye to hasten it.”

why.bs: „I požuruju te s kaznom“ – poricatelji požuruju kaznu.
why.en: “And they will bid thee hasten on the Doom” — the deniers hurrying the punishment.

why.bs: Salih: „O narode moj, zašto tražite da zlo dođe brže nego dobro?“
why.en: Ṣāliḥ: “O my people! Why will ye hasten on the evil rather than the good?”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, سُرْعَة je suprotnost sporosti, za tijela i za djela. Kur'an hvali hitanje ka oprostu i dobrim djelima, a kudi hitanje u nevjerovanje i grijeh – vrijednost daje cilj.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, سُرْعَة is the opposite of slowness, said of bodies and of acts. The Quran praises hastening to forgiveness and good deeds and blames hastening into disbelief and sin — the goal gives it its worth.

why.bs: „I hitajte ka oprostu od svoga Gospodara“ – hvaljeno hitanje.
why.en: “And vie one with another for forgiveness from your Lord” — praised hastening.

why.bs: „Takvi hitaju u dobrim djelima i oni u njima prednjače.“
why.en: “These race for the good things, and they shall win them in the race.”

why.bs: „I vidiš mnoge od njih kako hitaju u grijeh i nasilje“ – kuđeno hitanje.
why.en: “And thou seest many of them vying one with another in sin and transgression” — blamed hastening.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o uspjehu. Prema ar-Rāġibu, فَوْز je postići dobro i pri tome ostati siguran, a فَلَاح je postići ono čemu se teži – na ovom ili na budućem svijetu.
shared.en: Both words speak of success. According to ar-Rāġib, فَوْز is attaining good while being kept safe, while فَلَاح is attaining what one strives for — in this world or the next.

tellApart.bs: Postići dobro uz spas (od Vatre) – ‚veliki uspjeh‘ → فَوْز; uspjeti, postići cilj – na dunjaluku ili na ahiretu → أَفْلَحَ.
tellApart.en: To win the good while kept safe (from the Fire) — ‘the great triumph’ → فَوْز; to prosper, to reach one's aim — in this world or the next → أَفْلَحَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries فوز, فلح
notes: ar-Rāġib (فوز): fawz is winning the good together with safety (85:11, 4:13, 33:71); one moved away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has won (3:185); in 4:73 the hypocrites count their booty a great fawz. (فلح): falḥ is splitting (the farmer is fallāḥ); falāḥ is winning and reaching one's aim, worldly — life, wealth, honour — or otherworldly: lasting without end, wealth without poverty, honour without humiliation, knowledge without ignorance; in 20:64 Pharaoh's magicians most likely meant worldly success.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries فوز, فلح (2026-11-06): 17 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): He calls it 'al-fawz al-kabīr' (the great triumph), contrasting death seen from this world vs. the Hereafter; no superlative. The 'most often with great' sentence is Quranic usage, unattributed
Blind review (2026-11-06): فَوْز bs 'pobjeda, dobitak' (uspjeti kept for أَفْلَحَ); 91:9 bs without 'samo'; 23:1 'above all the Hereafter'; Džennet.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, postići dobro i pri tome ostati siguran; veliki je uspjeh biti udaljen od Vatre i uveden u Džennet. Riječ najčešće dolazi s ‚velik‘: الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيم.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, winning the good while being kept safe; the great triumph is to be moved from the Fire and admitted to Paradise. The word most often comes with ‘great’: الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيم.

why.bs: „Njima pripadaju bašče ispod kojih teku rijeke – to je veliki uspjeh.“
why.en: “Theirs will be Gardens underneath which rivers flow. That is the Great Success.”

why.bs: „…a Allahovo zadovoljstvo je veće; to je, zaista, veliki uspjeh.“
why.en: “And - greater (far)! - acceptance from Allah. That is the supreme triumph.”

why.bs: Licemjer: „Kamo sreće da sam bio s njima, pa da postignem veliki uspjeh!“ – ar-Rāġib: plijen koji oni smatraju uspjehom.
why.en: The hypocrite: “Oh, would that I had been with them, then should I have achieved a great success!” — ar-Rāġib: booty they count as triumph.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od ‚cijepati‘ (zemljoradnik je فَلَّاح): postići ono čemu se teži. Uspjeh je dvojak: dunjalučki – život, imetak, ugled – i ahiretski: trajanje bez nestanka, bogatstvo bez siromaštva, ugled bez poniženja, znanje bez neznanja.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from ‘to split’ (the farmer is فَلَّاح): reaching what one strives for. Success is twofold: worldly — life, wealth, honour — and otherworldly: lasting without end, wealth without poverty, honour without humiliation, knowledge without ignorance.

why.bs: „Vjernici su doista uspjeli“ – uspjeh, prije svega ahiretski.
why.en: “Successful indeed are the believers” — success, above all that of the Hereafter.

why.bs: „Uspio je zaista onaj ko je očisti“ – uspjeh kroz čišćenje duše.
why.en: “He is indeed successful who causeth it to grow [purifieth it]” — success through purifying the soul.

why.bs: Faraonovi čarobnjaci: „Danas će uspjeti onaj ko nadvlada“ – ar-Rāġib: najvjerovatnije dunjalučki uspjeh.
why.en: Pharaoh's magicians: “Whoso is uppermost this day will be indeed successful” — ar-Rāġib: most likely worldly success.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače da skriveno postaje vidljivo ili poznato. Razlikuju se po onome što se otkriva i po tome čemu se suprotstavljaju.
shared.en: All three words mean that something hidden becomes seen or known. They differ in what is disclosed and in what each is set against.

tellApart.bs: Pokazati ono što je bilo u duši ili pokriveno → أَبْدَى; izvesti na vidjelo, a u Kur'anu najčešće dati prevlast ili dati da se sazna → أَظْهَرَ; javno činiti, nasuprot tajnom → أَعْلَنَ.
tellApart.en: To show what was in the soul or covered → أَبْدَى; to bring out into view, in the Quran mostly to make prevail or to let be known → أَظْهَرَ; to do openly, as against in secret → أَعْلَنَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries بدا, ظهر, علن
notes: ar-Rāġib (بدا): badā is to appear plainly (ẓahara ẓuhūran bayyinan); he gives no separate remark on the Form IV ibdāʾ. (ظهر): ẓahara is at root a thing being on the back (surface) of the earth so that it is not hidden, as against baṭana, being in its belly; then used of anything prominent, seen by sight or by insight; 9:33 li-yuẓhirahu may be from emergence or from helping and overpowering — 'to make it prevail'; 72:26 lā yuẓhiru = He does not let anyone see (His unseen); 30:18 tuẓhirūna = entering the time of noon. (علن): ʿalāniya is the opposite of sirr, said mostly of meanings rather than of concrete things.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 14 / 7 / 12 places read): أَبْدَى is paired with أَخْفَى or كَتَمَ in most places (2:271, 2:284, 3:29, 4:149, 5:99, 24:29, 33:54) and is also said of the visible (adornment 24:31, the private parts 7:20); أَظْهَرَ means 'to make prevail' in 9:33, 48:28, 61:9, 'to let know' in 66:3 and 72:26, 'make appear' in 40:26, and in 30:18 'at noon'; every one of the 12 أَعْلَنَ places sets it against a secret counterpart (أَسَرَّ, أَخْفَى, أَكَنَّ).

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 of 4 claims flagged, fixed: 'in one's hands' for أَبْدَى dropped (no ayah shows it); 72:26 now his 'lets no one become aware of it', not 'let see'; 40:26 bs keeps 'make appear'.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries بدا, ظهر, علن (2026-11-06): 13 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/2/nuance (reworded): He gives no examples of 'meanings'; the list words/intentions/deeds is ours

nuance.bs: Od badā – pojaviti se jasno, kako ga opisuje ar-Rāġib. U kur'anskoj upotrebi najčešće stoji nasuprot skrivanju (أَخْفَى, كَتَمَ): pokazati ono što je u duši ili što se daje javno, a i ono što je pokriveno, kao ukras ili stidna mjesta.
nuance.en: From badā, to appear plainly, as ar-Rāġib describes it. In Quranic usage it mostly stands against hiding (أَخْفَى, كَتَمَ): to show what is in the soul or what one gives openly, and also what is covered, such as adornment or the private parts.

why.bs: „Pokažete li ono što nosite u sebi ili to skrijete, Allah će vas za to obračunati“ – pokazati nasuprot skriti.
why.en: “Whether ye make known what is in your minds or hide it, Allah will bring you to account for it” — showing set against concealing.

why.bs: „Ako sadake pokažete, to je lijepo, a ako ih sakrijete i date siromasima, to je za vas bolje.“
why.en: “If ye publish your almsgiving, it is well, but if ye hide it and give it to the poor, it will be better for you.”

why.bs: Vjernice „neka ne pokazuju svoje ukrase, izuzev onog što se od njih samo vidi“ – pokazati ono što je pokriveno.
why.en: Believing women are told “to display of their adornment only that which is apparent” — showing what is covered.

meaning.en: to bring to light, to make prevail

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ẓahara je izvorno biti na površini zemlje, pa se ne skriva, nasuprot baṭana – biti u njenoj utrobi; zatim sve što je istaknuto pogledu ili uvidu. U Kur'anu أَظْهَرَ najčešće znači dati prevlast (9:33) ili dati da se sazna (66:3, 72:26).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ẓahara is at root being on the surface of the earth, so not hidden, as against baṭana, being in its belly; then anything prominent to sight or to insight. In the Quran أَظْهَرَ mostly means to make prevail (9:33) or to let be known (66:3, 72:26).

why.bs: „Da je uzdigne iznad svake vjere“ – ar-Rāġib: može biti od pojavljivanja, ili od pomaganja i nadvladavanja, tj. da prevlada.
why.en: “That He may cause it to prevail over all religion” — ar-Rāġib: it may be from appearing, or from helping and overpowering, i.e. to make it prevail.

why.bs: „On zna skriveno i nikome ne otkriva ono što je skriveno kod Njega“ – ar-Rāġib: ne daje nikome da ga dozna.
why.en: “(He is) the Knower of the Unseen, and He revealeth unto none His secret” — ar-Rāġib: He lets no one become aware of it.

why.bs: Faraon se boji da Musa „ne učini da se na zemlji pojavi nered“ – učiniti da se nešto pojavi.
why.en: Pharaoh fears that Moses “will cause confusion [literally: make corruption appear] in the land” — making a thing appear.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, javnost (عَلَانِيَة) je suprotnost tajni (سِرّ), i to se najčešće kaže za značenja, a ne za konkretne stvari. U Kur'anu svih dvanaest puta stoji uz svoju suprotnost: ono što se tajno krije.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, openness (عَلَانِيَة) is the opposite of secrecy (سِرّ), and is said mostly of meanings rather than of concrete things. In the Quran all twelve times it stands beside its opposite: what is kept secret.

why.bs: „A Allah zna ono što krijete i ono što javno iznosite.“
why.en: “And Allah knoweth that which ye keep hidden and that which ye proclaim.”

why.bs: Nuh: „Zatim sam im se obraćao javno, a obraćao sam im se i potajno“ – javno nasuprot tajno; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Noah: “And lo! I have made public proclamation unto them, and I have appealed to them in private” — openly against secretly; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Ibrahim: „Gospodaru naš, Ti zaista znaš šta mi krijemo i šta javno iznosimo.“
why.en: Abraham: “Our Lord! Lo! Thou knowest that which we hide and that which we proclaim.”

shared.bs: Sve četiri riječi znače skupinu ljudi. Prema ar-Rāġibu, svaka je gleda s druge strane: po čvrstini, po odvojenosti, po dijelu cjeline i po onima koji nekoga osnažuju i od njega se šire.
shared.en: All four words mean a group of people. According to ar-Rāġib, each sees it from another side: its toughness, its separation, its being a part of a whole, and those who strengthen someone and spread out from him.

tellApart.bs: Skupina sa čvrstinom, tabor (Allahova stranka, šejtanova stranka, saveznici) → حِزْب; skupina odvojena od drugih → فَرِيق; dio neke cjeline, i od ljudi i od stvari → طَائِفَة; pristaše koji nekoga osnažuju i slijede njegov put → شِيعَة.
tellApart.en: A group with toughness, a camp (the party of Allah, of Satan, the confederates) → حِزْب; a group set apart from others → فَرِيق; a portion of a whole, of people or of things → طَائِفَة; followers who strengthen someone and keep to his way → شِيعَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حزب, فرق, طوف, شيع
notes: ar-Rāġib (حزب): ḥizb is a group with toughness (ġilaẓ); al-aḥzāb in 33:20–22 are those gathered to fight the Prophet; ḥizb Allāh (5:56) = Allah's helpers. (فرق): farīq is a group separated from others (al-jamāʿa al-mutafarriqa ʿan āḫarīn), with 42:7, 3:78, 2:85, 2:146. (طوف): ṭāʾifa of people is a group of them, and of a thing a piece of it; on 9:122 'some said' it can apply to one and more (49:9, 3:122). (شيع): the root is spreading and strengthening; šīʿa are those by whom a man is strengthened and who spread out from him (37:83, 28:15, 28:4, 15:10, 54:51).
The corpus files the plurals with their singulars (أَحْزَاب under حِزْب; شِيَع, أَشْيَاع under شِيعَة); the duals الْحِزْبَيْن, الْفَرِيقَيْن, طَائِفَتَان are counted too.
37:83: 'his' šīʿa is Nūḥ's by most mufassirun (the previous ayat speak of him); a minority refer it to the Prophet Muhammad — so the why says 'Nuh's, by most mufassirun'.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): all claims OK.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

'Each sees it from another side' is our synthesis of four separate definitions, acceptable

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, skupina u kojoj ima čvrstine (غِلَظ). Množina الْأَحْزَاب su saveznici okupljeni protiv Poslanika (33:22); „Allahova stranka“ (5:56) su, kaže on, Allahovi pomagači, a Kur'an spominje i „šejtanovu stranku“ (58:19).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a group with toughness (غِلَظ) in it. The plural الْأَحْزَاب are the confederates gathered against the Prophet (33:22); “the party of Allah” (5:56) are, he says, Allah's helpers, and the Quran also speaks of “the devil's party” (58:19).

why.bs: „Allahova stranka – oni su doista pobjednici“ – ar-Rāġib: Allahovi pomagači.
why.en: “Lo! the party of Allah, they are the victorious” — ar-Rāġib: Allah's helpers.

why.bs: „Oni su šejtanova stranka. Zaista, šejtanova stranka je ta koja gubi.“
why.en: “They are the devil's party. Lo! is it not the devil's party who will be the losers?”

why.bs: „A kad su vjernici ugledali saveznike (الْأَحْزَاب)…“ – skupine okupljene za borbu protiv Poslanika.
why.en: “And when the true believers saw the clans (الْأَحْزَاب)…” — the groups gathered to fight the Prophet.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, skupina koja se odvojila od drugih – od korijena f-r-q, rastaviti. Zato se često kaže u parovima i podjelama: jedni ovako, drugi onako.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a group separated from others — from the root of parting. So it often comes in pairs and divisions: some this way, others that.

why.bs: „Jedna skupina bit će u Džennetu, a druga skupina u plamenu“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “A host will be in the Garden, and a host of them in the Flame” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Među njima je zaista skupina (فَرِيقًا) koja uvija jezike čitajući Knjigu“ – jedna skupina izdvojena od ostalih.
why.en: “And lo! there is a party (فَرِيقًا) of them who distort the Scripture with their tongues” — one group singled out from the rest.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od ljudi – skupina od njih, a od stvari – njen komad; dakle dio neke cjeline. On navodi da neki kažu da se riječ može odnositi i na jednog čovjeka i više.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, of people a group of them, and of a thing a piece of it — a portion of a whole. He reports that some say the word can apply to one person and more.

why.bs: „Zašto iz svake njihove zajednice (فِرْقَة) ne bi krenuo po jedan dio (طَائِفَة), da bi stekli razumijevanje u vjeri?“ – dio od cjeline; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Of every troop (فِرْقَة) of them, a party (طَائِفَة) only should go forth, that they (who are left behind) may gain sound knowledge in religion” — a part of a whole; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Ako se dvije skupine vjernika međusobno zarate, uspostavite mir među njima“ – dva dijela iste zajednice.
why.en: “And if two parties of believers fall to fighting, then make peace between them” — two parts of one community.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, korijen znači širenje i jačanje; شِيعَة su oni kojima se čovjek osnaži i koji se od njega šire. Otuda i pristaše nekog puta, a u množini (شِيَع) – zajednice podijeljene na sljedbe.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root means spreading and strengthening; شِيعَة are those by whom a man is strengthened and who spread out from him. Hence the adherents of a way, and in the plural (شِيَع) communities split into sects.

why.bs: „A od njegovih sljedbenika bio je, zaista, Ibrahim“ – po većini mufesira, Nuhovih: istog puta i vjere.
why.en: “And lo! of his persuasion verily was Abraham” — by most mufassirun, Noah's: of the same way and faith.

why.bs: Musa zateče dvojicu kako se tuku: „ovaj od njegovih sljedbenika, a onaj od njegovih neprijatelja“ – pristaša nasuprot neprijatelju.
why.en: Moses found two men fighting, “one of his own caste, and the other of his enemies” — a follower as against a foe.

why.bs: „Od onih koji su svoju vjeru rascijepili i postali sljedbe (شِيَعًا) – svaka stranka (حِزْب) raduje se onim što ima.“
why.en: “Of those who split up their religion and became schismatics (شِيَعًا), each sect (حِزْب) exulting in its tenets.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače dobro koje Allah daje. Prema ar-Rāġibu, نِعْمَة je dobro stanje u kojem se čovjek nađe, a فَضْل je ono što je preko onoga što je dovoljno – dar koji davalac nije dužan dati.
shared.en: Both words mean the good Allah gives. According to ar-Rāġib, نِعْمَة is the good state a person finds himself in, while فَضْل is what goes beyond what suffices — a gift the giver is not bound to give.

tellApart.bs: Dobro stanje, blagodat koja se uživa i koja se ne može izbrojati → نِعْمَة; višak, dar iz dobrote preko dužnog, i ono što se trudom stječe → فَضْل.
tellApart.en: The good state, a favour enjoyed and beyond counting → نِعْمَة; the surplus, a gift of bounty beyond what is due, and what is sought by effort → فَضْل.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نعم, فضل
notes: ar-Rāġib (نعم): niʿma is the good state (al-ḥāla al-ḥasana), its pattern that of a state like jilsa; as a genus it is said of little and much (14:34, 2:40, 5:3); inʿām is bringing good to another, said only when the receiver is a rational being. (فضل): faḍl is excess over what suffices, praised or blamed, mostly of the praised; every gift that is not binding on the giver is faḍl (4:32, 57:21, 10:58); 'that you may seek faḍl from your Lord' means wealth and what is earned.
The corpus files the plurals نِعَم / أَنْعُم under نِعْمَة. That فَضْل is often 'sought' (اِبْتَغَى فَضْلًا) of trade and earning — 2:198, 62:10, 73:20 — is our observation of its places.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 of 3 flagged, fixed: 5:3 and 10:58 now say what they show; 62:10 'earning and trade' given to the mufassirun.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries نعم, فضل (2026-11-06): 14 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/nuance (reworded): He glosses one phrase (li-tabtaġū faḍlan min rabbikum), not every 'seeking of faḍl'; 4:32 'ask Allah of His faḍl' he files under the non-binding gift

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, dobro stanje u kojem se čovjek nalazi; kao rod kaže se i za malo i za mnogo. Glagol أَنْعَمَ je, kaže on, ukazati dobro drugome, a kaže se samo kad je primalac razumno biće.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the good state a person is in; as a genus it is said of little and of much. The verb أَنْعَمَ is, he says, to bring good to another, and is said only when the receiver is a rational being.

why.bs: „Ako biste nabrajali Allahovu blagodat, ne biste je mogli izbrojati“ – jednina kao rod: sva dobra stanja.
why.en: “If ye would count the bounty (نِعْمَة) of Allah ye cannot reckon it” — the singular as a genus: every good state.

why.bs: „Danas sam vam usavršio vašu vjeru i upotpunio Svoju blagodat prema vama“ – blagodat kao dobro stanje koje Allah upotpunjuje; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “This day have I perfected your religion for you and completed My favour unto you” — favour as the good state Allah brings to completion; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, višak preko onoga što je dovoljno; svaki dar koji davalac nije dužan dati zove se فَضْل. U „kako biste tražili فَضْل od svoga Gospodara“ (17:12) to je, kaže on, imetak i ono što se stječe.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the surplus over what suffices; every gift the giver is not bound to give is called فَضْل. In “that ye may seek bounty (فَضْل) from your Lord” (17:12) it is, he says, wealth and what is earned.

why.bs: „I molite Allaha da vam da od Svoje dobrote“ – dar koji On nije dužan dati; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “But ask Allah of His bounty” — a gift He is not bound to give; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „…razidite se po zemlji i tražite od Allahove dobrote“ – mufesiri to tumače kao traženje opskrbe zaradom i trgovinom.
why.en: “…then disperse in the land and seek of Allah's bounty” — the mufassirun explain this as seeking provision, by earning and trade.

why.bs: „Reci: Zbog Allahove dobrote i zbog Njegove milosti – eto, zbog toga neka se raduju!“ – dobrota kao dar od Allaha preko dužnog; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Say: In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy: therein let them rejoice” — bounty as a gift from Allah beyond what is due; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače vlast nad nečim. Prema ar-Rāġibu, مُلْك je raspolaganje stvarju po svom sudu, a pravi i trajni pripada Allahu; سُلْطَان je moć da se nadvlada – a i dokaz, jer navaljuje na srca.
shared.en: Both words mean power over something. According to ar-Rāġib, مُلْك is controlling a thing by one's rule, and the true, lasting one belongs to Allah; سُلْطَان is the power to overpower — and also proof, since it storms the hearts.

tellApart.bs: Vladavina, carstvo: raspolagati onim čime se vlada; pravo i trajno samo Allahovo → مُلْك; moć da se nadvlada, ovlast nad nekim; i dokaz koji nadvladava → سُلْطَان.
tellApart.en: Dominion, kingship: control of what one rules; the true and lasting one only Allah's → مُلْك; the power to overpower, authority over someone; and proof that prevails → سُلْطَان.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ملك, سلط
notes: ar-Rāġib (ملك): mulk is the controlling (ḍabṭ) of a thing one disposes of by rule; milk (ownership) is like the genus of mulk — every mulk is milk, not every milk is mulk; the true and lasting mulk is Allah's (64:1, 3:26); he also cites 4:54 'a great kingdom' for Abraham's family. (سلط): salāṭa is the power to overpower; sulṭān is said of that power (17:33, 16:99–100, 55:33), more often of the one who holds it; proof is called sulṭān for how it assails hearts (40:35, 14:10, 4:144); 69:29 may bear both senses.
69:29 (sulṭāniyah) is left out: ar-Rāġib himself says it may mean either power or proof.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 of 3 flagged, fixed: his limit restored (proof's hold is mostly on believers of knowledge and wisdom); 4:54 states its point; 16:99 en and bs both name Satan.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries ملك, سلط (2026-11-06): 15 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): His word is al-hujūm ʿalā l-qulūb, 'assailing / storming the hearts'; 'overpowers' slightly strengthens it. He also limits it: its hold is mostly over believers of knowledge and wisdom (dropped); members/1/nuance (reworded): Same as shared: hujūm = assailing/storming

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, raspolaganje stvarju po svom sudu i vlasti; svako مُلْك je posjedovanje, ali svako posjedovanje nije مُلْك. Pravo i trajno مُلْك pripada Allahu, a On ga daje kome hoće.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the controlling of a thing by one's rule; every مُلْك is ownership, but not every ownership is مُلْك. The true and lasting مُلْك belongs to Allah, and He gives it to whom He wills.

why.bs: „Reci: Allahu, Gospodaru carstva, Ti daješ carstvo kome želiš i oduzimaš carstvo od koga želiš“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Say: O Allah! Owner of Sovereignty! Thou givest sovereignty unto whom Thou wilt, and Thou withdrawest sovereignty from whom Thou wilt” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Njemu pripada carstvo i Njemu pripada hvala“ – pravo i trajno carstvo.
why.en: “Unto Him belongeth Sovereignty and unto Him belongeth praise” — the true and lasting dominion.

why.bs: „…i dali smo im ogromno carstvo“ – carstvo koje Allah daje ljudima; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “…and We bestowed on them a mighty kingdom” — dominion that Allah gives to people; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od سَلَاطَة – moći da se nadvlada: سُلْطَان je ta moć, a češće onaj ko je ima. Dokaz se, kaže on, zove سُلْطَان jer navaljuje na srca – mada najviše djeluje na ljude znanja i mudrosti među vjernicima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from سَلَاطَة, the power to overpower: سُلْطَان is that power, and more often the one who holds it. Proof, he says, is called سُلْطَان because it storms the hearts — though its force falls mostly on the people of knowledge and wisdom among the believers.

why.bs: „On (šejtan) zaista nema vlasti nad vjernicima i nad onima koji se na svoga Gospodara oslanjaju.“
why.en: “Lo! he [Satan] hath no power over those who believe and put trust in their Lord.”

why.bs: „A ko bude nepravedno ubijen, njegovom nasljedniku smo dali ovlast“ – ovlast kao moć; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Whoso is slain wrongfully, We have given power unto his heir” — authority as power; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Pa donesite nam jasan dokaz!“ – سُلْطَان kao dokaz.
why.en: “Then bring some clear warrant” — سُلْطَان as proof.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o predanosti drugome. Prema ar-Rāġibu, ibadet je krajnja poniznost i zaslužuje ga samo Allah, dok je pokornost (طَاعَة) najčešće slijeđenje naredbe; u Kur'anu se pokornost duguje i Poslaniku.
shared.en: Both words speak of yielding to another. According to ar-Rāġib, worship is the utmost humbling, which only Allah deserves, while obedience (طَاعَة) is mostly said of following a command; in the Quran obedience is owed to the Messenger too.

tellApart.bs: Krajnja poniznost – ibadet, koji pripada samo Allahu → عَبَدَ; pokoriti se, poslušati naredbu (Allahovu, Poslanikovu, ali i drugih) → أَطَاعَ.
tellApart.en: The utmost humbling — worship, which belongs only to Allah → عَبَدَ; to comply, to obey a command (Allah's, the Messenger's, but also others') → أَطَاعَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عبد, طوع
notes: ar-Rāġib (عبد): ʿubūdiyya is showing humbleness; ʿibāda is more intense, the utmost humbling, deserved only by the One of utmost favour, Allah (17:23 'that you worship none but Him'); ʿibāda is of two kinds: by subjection (taṣḫīr) and by choice, the latter of rational beings, the one commanded (2:21). (طوع): ṭawʿ is compliance, its opposite compulsion (41:11, 3:83); ṭāʿa is like it but said mostly of carrying out what is commanded and keeping to what is prescribed (4:80).
That أَطَاعَ also takes the Messenger and 'those in authority among you' (4:59), and that obeying parents is limited where they call to shirk (29:8, 31:15), is our observation of Quranic usage.

al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
