nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ibadet je krajnja poniznost, jača od pukog robovanja, i zaslužuje ga samo Onaj čija je dobrota najveća – Allah. Ibadet je, kaže on, dvojak: onaj iz potčinjenosti, kojim Allahu služi sve, i onaj po izboru, koji je naređen razumnim bićima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, worship is the utmost humbling, stronger than mere servitude, and only the One whose favour is greatest deserves it — Allah. Worship, he says, is of two kinds: by subjection, by which all things serve Allah, and by choice, which is commanded to rational beings.

why.bs: „Samo Tebi ibadet činimo i samo Tebe za pomoć molimo“ – ibadet pripada samo Allahu.
why.en: “Thee (alone) we worship; Thee (alone) we ask for help” — worship belongs to Allah alone.

why.bs: „Ljudi, činite ibadet svome Gospodaru“ – ibadet po izboru, koji je naređen.
why.en: “O mankind! worship your Lord” — worship by choice, the kind that is commanded.

why.bs: „Tvoj Gospodar je odredio da ne činite ibadet nikome osim Njemu“ – ar-Rāġib: zato što ga zaslužuje samo Allah.
why.en: “Thy Lord hath decreed, that ye worship none save Him” — ar-Rāġib: because only Allah deserves it.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ṭawʿ je pristajanje, a suprotno mu je prisila; طَاعَة je isto, ali se najčešće kaže za izvršavanje naredbe i držanje propisanog. U Kur'anu se pokornost duguje Allahu i Poslaniku, i onima koji su nadležni, a roditeljima ne kad pozivaju na širk.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ṭawʿ is compliance, its opposite compulsion; طَاعَة is the same but said mostly of carrying out a command and keeping to what is prescribed. In the Quran obedience is owed to Allah and the Messenger, and to those in authority, but not to parents when they call to shirk.

why.bs: „Pokoravajte se Allahu, i Poslaniku se pokoravajte, i onima među vama koji imaju vlast“ – pokornost i ljudima, za razliku od ibadeta.
why.en: “Obey Allah, and obey the messenger and those of you who are in authority” — obedience to people too, unlike worship.

why.bs: „Ko se pokori Poslaniku, pokorio se Allahu“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Whoso obeyeth the messenger hath obeyed Allah” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A ako se budu trudili da Meni pripišeš druga o kome nemaš znanja, ti im se ne pokoravaj“ – granica pokornosti roditeljima.
why.en: “But if they strive to make thee join with Me that of which thou hast no knowledge, then obey them not” — the limit of obedience to parents.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače ustezanje imetka. Prema ar-Rāġibu, بُخْل je zadržavanje onoga što se ne smije zadržati, a شُحّ je škrtost spojena s pohlepom, kao trajna narav.
shared.en: Both words mean holding back one's goods. According to ar-Rāġib, بُخْل is withholding what should not be withheld, while شُحّ is stinginess joined with greed, as a settled habit.

tellApart.bs: Škrtariti: zadržati ono što treba dati (glagol) → بَخِلَ; čin škrtosti, u Kur'anu i kad se drugima naređuje → بُخْل; škrtost s pohlepom, koja je postala navika duše → شُحّ.
tellApart.en: To be stingy: to withhold what should be given (the verb) → بَخِلَ; the act of stinginess, in the Quran also when urged on others → بُخْل; stinginess with greed, grown into the soul's habit → شُحّ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries بخل, شح
notes: ar-Rāġib (بخل): buḵl is withholding possessions from where they should not be withheld, its opposite jūd (generosity); baḵīl is one who does it much; buḵl is of two kinds, with one's own possessions and with others', the latter more blameworthy — his proof 4:37 / 57:24 'who are stingy and enjoin stinginess on people'. (شح): šuḥḥ is buḵl with greed (ḥirṣ), in what has become habit (4:128, 59:9 / 64:16, 33:19).

The noun بُخْل (2×) is a member of its own beside the verb, since its two places carry ar-Rāġib's point about enjoining stinginess. The corpus files أَشِحَّة (33:19) under شُحّ. That the noun شُحّ is the soul's in all three of its places (4:128, 59:9, 64:16) is our observation.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, zadržati imetak ondje gdje ga ne treba zadržati; suprotno mu je darežljivost. U Kur'anu se najčešće kaže za uskraćivanje onoga što je Allah dao iz Svoje dobrote.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to withhold possessions where they should not be withheld; its opposite is generosity. In the Quran it is mostly said of holding back what Allah has given of His bounty.

why.bs: „Neka ne misle oni koji su škrti s onim što im je Allah iz Svoje dobrote podario da je to za njih dobro – naprotiv, to je za njih zlo.“
why.en: “And let not those who hoard up that which Allah hath bestowed upon them of His bounty think that it is better for them. Nay, it is worse for them.”

why.bs: „A ko škrtari, škrtari samo protiv sebe“ – uskraćivanje se vraća onome ko uskraćuje.
why.en: “And as for him who hoardeth, he hoardeth only from his soul” — the withholding returns on the one who withholds.

nuance.bs: Imenica, u Kur'anu samo dvaput, oba puta u istom izrazu: oni koji škrtare i ljudima škrtost naređuju. Prema ar-Rāġibu, škrtost s tuđim imetkom je teža od škrtosti sa svojim, i za to navodi upravo ovaj ajet.
nuance.en: The noun, only twice in the Quran, both times in the same phrase, said of people who are mean themselves and urge others to meanness too. According to ar-Rāġib, stinginess with others' possessions is worse than with one's own, and this is the very ayah he gives for it.

why.bs: „Oni koji škrtare, i ljudima nalažu škrtost, i taje ono čime ih je Allah iz Svoje dobrote obdario.“
why.en: “Who hoard their wealth and enjoin avarice on others, and hide that which Allah hath bestowed upon them of His bounty.”

why.bs: „Oni koji škrtare i ljudima naređuju škrtost“ – isti izraz, drugi put.
why.en: “Who hoard and who enjoin upon the people avarice” — the same phrase, the second time.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, škrtost spojena s pohlepom (حِرْص), u onome što je postalo navika. U kur'anskoj upotrebi imenica je sva tri puta lakomost duše: duše su joj sklone, a uspješan je onaj ko je od nje sačuvan.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, stinginess joined with greed (حِرْص), in what has become habit. In Quranic usage the noun is all three times the soul's avarice: souls are prone to it, and successful is the one kept from it.

why.bs: „A lakomost je dušama stalno prisutna“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “But greed hath been made present in the minds (of men)” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A ko bude sačuvan od lakomosti svoje duše – takvi su ti koji uspijevaju.“
why.en: “And whoso is saved from his own avarice - such are they who are successful.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače ono što je loše. Prema ar-Rāġibu, شَرّ je ono što svi izbjegavaju, kao što je dobro (خَيْر) ono što svi žele; سُوء je sve što čovjeka ožalosti, i ružno djelo.
shared.en: Both words mean what is bad. According to ar-Rāġib, شَرّ is what everyone shuns, as good (خَيْر) is what everyone desires; سُوء is whatever grieves a person, and a foul deed.

tellApart.bs: Zlo, protivnost dobru (خَيْر): ono što svi izbjegavaju → شَرّ; ono što ožalosti – na ovom i na onom svijetu, u duši, tijelu i imetku – i ružno djelo → سُوء.
tellApart.en: Evil, the counterpart of good (خَيْر): what everyone shuns → شَرّ; what grieves — in this world and the next, in soul, body and property — and a foul deed → سُوء.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries شر, سوأ
notes: ar-Rāġib (شر): šarr is what all shun, as ḵayr is what all desire (25:34, 8:22). (سوأ): sūʾ is everything that grieves a person, of worldly and otherworldly matters, of inner and bodily states and of external ones such as loss of wealth, standing or a dear one; 20:22 'without sūʾ' = without blemish, explained (fussira) as leprosy; 4:123 'whoever does sūʾ' = a foul deed; sūʾ al-ḥisāb, sūʾ ad-dār.

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): شَرّ is paired with خَيْر in many places (21:35, 17:11, 99:7–8, 2:216, 3:180, 24:11) and is also what 'touches' man (17:83, 41:49, 70:20); سُوء often qualifies another word — sūʾ al-ʿaḏāb (2:49, 40:45), sūʾ al-ḥisāb (13:21), sūʾ ad-dār (40:52), sūʾ ʿamalihi (35:8).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ono što svi izbjegavaju, kao što je dobro ono što svi žele. U Kur'anu često stoji uz dobro (خَيْر) kao njegov par: kao djelo, kao kušnja i kao ono što čovjeka zadesi.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, what everyone shuns, as good is what everyone desires. In the Quran it often stands with good (خَيْر) as its pair: as a deed, as a trial, and as what befalls a person.

why.bs: „I iskušavamo vas zlom i dobrom, kao kušnjom“ – zlo i dobro kao par.
why.en: “We try you with evil and with good, for ordeal” — evil and good as a pair.

why.bs: „A ko učini zla teškog koliko trun, vidjet će ga“ – zlo kao djelo.
why.en: “And whoso doeth ill an atom's weight will see it then” — evil as a deed.

why.bs: „Od zla onoga što je On stvorio“ – zlo od kojeg se traži utočište.
why.en: “From the evil of that which He created” — evil from which refuge is sought.

meaning.en: ill, what grieves; a foul deed

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, sve što čovjeka ožalosti – od ovosvjetskih i onosvjetskih stvari, stanja duše i tijela, i gubitka imetka, ugleda ili bliske osobe; a i ružno djelo. U Kur'anu često stoji kao odredba: ‚najteža kazna‘ (سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ), ‚zao obračun‘.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, whatever grieves a person — of worldly and otherworldly matters, states of soul and body, and the loss of wealth, standing or someone dear; and also a foul deed. In the Quran it often qualifies another word: ‘the worst torment’ (سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ), ‘the evil reckoning’.

why.bs: „I vratili su se s blagodati od Allaha i dobrotom, a nikakva ih nevolja (سُوء) nije dotakla“ – سُوء kao ono što čovjeka ožalosti, ovdje šteta koja ih nije zadesila.
why.en: “So they returned with grace and favour from Allah, and no harm (سُوء) touched them” — سُوء as what grieves a person, here harm that did not reach them.

why.bs: „Ko učini ružno djelo, bit će mu za njega uzvraćeno“ – ar-Rāġib: سُوء kao ružno djelo.
why.en: “He who doeth wrong will have the recompense thereof” — ar-Rāġib: سُوء as a foul deed.

why.bs: „Izaći će bijela, bez ikakve bolesti“ (bez سُوء) – ar-Rāġib: bez ikakve mane; tumači se kao guba.
why.en: “It will come forth white without hurt” (without سُوء) — ar-Rāġib: without any blemish; explained as leprosy.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače dobro. Prema ar-Rāġibu, خَيْر je ono što svi žele, a suprotno mu je zlo (شَرّ); حَسَنَة je sve što obraduje – blagodat koja čovjeka zadesi – i dobro djelo, a suprotna joj je سَيِّئَة.
shared.en: Both words mean good. According to ar-Rāġib, خَيْر is what everyone desires, its opposite evil (شَرّ); حَسَنَة is whatever gladdens — a blessing that reaches a person — and a good deed, its opposite سَيِّئَة.

tellApart.bs: Dobro koje svi žele, a i imetak, i ‚bolje od‘ → خَيْر; ono što obraduje, blagostanje koje zadesi čovjeka, i dobro djelo nasuprot rđavom → حَسَنَة.
tellApart.en: The good all desire, also wealth, and ‘better than’ → خَيْر; what gladdens, good fortune that reaches a person, and a good deed against an evil one → حَسَنَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries خير, حسن, سوأ
notes: ar-Rāġib (خير): ḵayr is what all desire, such as reason, justice, virtue and what benefits; its opposite šarr. He reports ('qīla') a division into absolute ḵayr and relative ḵayr/šarr (wealth good for one, bad for another); in 2:180 ḵayr = wealth, and some scholars say only much wealth from a good source; ḵayr is also comparative ('better', 2:106; in 2:184 it may be either); it is set against šarr and sometimes against ḍurr (10:107). (حسن): ḥasana is said of every blessing that gladdens, in one's self, body and circumstances, its opposite sayyiʾa; in 4:78 = fertility, plenty, victory. (سوأ): ḥasana and sayyiʾa are of two kinds — by reason and the Law (6:160) and by natural liking (7:131).
ḥasana as a feminine adjective (16:125 al-mawʿiẓa al-ḥasana, 33:21 uswa ḥasana) is filed under the same corpus lemma and counted.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ono što svi žele – razum, pravda, vrlina, ono što koristi; suprotno mu je zlo. Kaže se i za imetak (2:180) i u značenju ‚bolje od‘. On navodi i mišljenje da je nešto dobro u svakom pogledu, a nešto samo za jednog, kao imetak.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, what everyone desires — reason, justice, virtue, what benefits; its opposite is evil. It is said also of wealth (2:180) and in the sense of ‘better than’. He also reports the view that some good is good in every respect, and some only for one person, like wealth.

why.bs: „I neka iz vas bude zajednica koja poziva na dobro“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet za خَيْر kao imenicu.
why.en: “And there may spring from you a nation who invite to goodness” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah for خَيْر as a noun.

why.bs: „Kad smrt dođe nekome od vas, ako ostavlja imetak (خَيْرًا)…“ – ar-Rāġib: ovdje خَيْر znači imetak.
why.en: “When death approacheth one of you, if he leave wealth (خَيْرًا)…” — ar-Rāġib: here خَيْر means wealth.

why.bs: „Pa ko učini dobra teškog koliko trun, vidjet će ga.“
why.en: “And whoso doeth good an atom's weight will see it then.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, sve što obraduje od blagodati koja čovjeka zadesi – u njemu samom, tijelu i prilikama; suprotna joj je سَيِّئَة. On razlikuje dvije vrste: dobro po razumu i Šerijatu – dobro djelo (6:160) – i ono što je ugodno naravi (7:131).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, whatever gladdens of a blessing that reaches a person — in himself, his body and his circumstances; its opposite is سَيِّئَة. He tells two kinds apart: good by reason and the Law — a good deed (6:160) — and what is pleasant to one's nature (7:131).

why.bs: „Ko donese dobro djelo, njemu pripada deset puta toliko“ – حَسَنَة po Šerijatu.
why.en: “Whoso bringeth a good deed will receive tenfold the like thereof” — حَسَنَة by the Law.

why.bs: „A ako ih pogodi nešto dobro, kažu: Ovo je od Allaha“ – ar-Rāġib: plodnost, obilje i pobjeda.
why.en: “Yet if a happy thing befalleth them they say: This is from Allah” — ar-Rāġib: fertility, plenty and victory.

why.bs: „Gospodaru naš, daj nam na ovom svijetu dobro i na onom svijetu dobro“ – riječ je حَسَنَة; mufesiri je tumače na više načina (zdravlje, znanje, ibadet; na ahiretu – Džennet).
why.en: “Our Lord! Give unto us in the world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good” — the word is حَسَنَة; mufassirun explain it in several ways (well-being, knowledge, worship; in the Hereafter, Paradise).

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o onome što je istinito. Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnova riječi حَقّ je podudaranje i sklad – ono što stoji kako treba; صِدْق je, kaže on, kada se riječ podudara i s onim što govornik u sebi misli i sa stvarnošću o kojoj govori.
shared.en: Both words speak of what is true. According to ar-Rāġib, the root of حَقّ is matching and agreement — what stands as it should; صِدْق, he says, is when a statement matches both what the speaker holds within and the reality it reports.

tellApart.bs: Istina sama – ono što postoji i stoji kako treba (i Allahovo ime الْحَقّ) → حَقّ; istinitost onoga ko govori ili radi – kad se riječ slaže s nutrinom i stvarnošću → صِدْق.
tellApart.en: Truth itself — what exists and stands as it should (also Allah's name الْحَقّ) → حَقّ; the truthfulness of one who speaks or acts — word matching heart and reality → صِدْق.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حق, صدق
notes: ar-Rāġib (حق): root is matching and agreement (the door's pivot turning true in its socket); ḥaqq is said (1) of the One who brings things into being by wisdom — so Allah is al-Ḥaqq (10:32); (2) of what is brought into being by wisdom — Allah's every act is ḥaqq (10:5, of the sun and moon), and of the Resurrection (10:53); (3) of a belief that matches the thing as it is; (4) of a deed or word that occurs as, as much as, and when it should. (صدق): ṣidq and kaḏib are at root in speech, and only in reports; ṣidq is the statement matching both the inner conviction (ḍamīr) and what is reported — if a condition fails it is not full ṣidq (a disbeliever saying 'Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah' without belief: true by the fact, a lie by his heart; so Allah calls the hypocrites liars in 63:1); ṣidq is also used of deeds — fulfilling what is due (33:23); 33:8 means the one truthful in tongue is asked about the truth of his deed; 39:33 he realised in deed what he brought in word; every virtuous act outward and inward is called ṣidq and annexed to it (54:55 'seat of ṣidq', 26:84 'tongue of ṣidq' = a praise of him that will not be false).
The corpus files حَقّ as one lemma (247×), including حَقًّا; صِدْق is the noun only (not صَادِق, صِدِّيق or the verb صَدَقَ).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ono što se podudara i stoji kako treba. Kaže se za Allaha, koji je الْحَقّ jer sve stvara mudrošću; za ono što On stvara, jer je svako Njegovo djelo istina; za vjerovanje koje odgovara stvarnosti; i za riječ ili djelo koji dođu onako, onoliko i onda kada treba.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, what matches and stands as it should. It is said of Allah, who is الْحَقّ for He brings all things into being by wisdom; of what He creates, for His every act is truth; of a belief that matches reality; and of a word or deed that comes as, as much as, and when it should.

why.bs: „Eto, to vam je Allah, vaš Gospodar, Istina (رَبُّكُمُ الْحَقُّ). Pa šta ostaje nakon istine osim zablude?“ – ar-Rāġib: الْحَقّ kao Allahovo ime.
why.en: “Such then is Allah, your rightful Lord (رَبُّكُمُ الْحَقُّ). After the Truth what is there saving error?” — ar-Rāġib: الْحَقّ as a name of Allah.

why.bs: Sunce i Mjesec – „Allah to nije stvorio osim s istinom (بِالْحَقِّ)“ – ar-Rāġib: Allahovo djelo je istina jer je po mudrosti.
why.en: The sun and the moon — “Allah created not (all) that save in truth (بِالْحَقِّ)” — ar-Rāġib: Allah's work is truth, for it is by wisdom.

why.bs: „Je li to istina?“ – „Da, tako mi moga Gospodara, to je zaista istina“ – o Sudnjem danu; ar-Rāġib i ovaj ajet navodi.
why.en: “Is it true?” — “Yea, by my Lord, verily it is true” — of the Day of Judgement; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah too.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnova je u govoru: riječ je istinita kad se slaže i s onim što govornik misli i sa stvarnošću. Zato su licemjeri (63:1) lažljivci iako je ono što su rekli istina. Kaže se i za djelo – kad čovjek ispuni ono što je obećao – a svako lijepo djelo, vanjsko i unutrašnje, naziva se صِدْق.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, it is rooted in speech: a word is truthful when it matches both what the speaker holds and the reality. So the hypocrites (63:1) are liars though what they said is true. It is also said of a deed — when one fulfils what he pledged — and every virtuous act, outward and inward, is called صِدْق.

why.bs: „Da upita iskrene o njihovoj iskrenosti“ – ar-Rāġib: onaj ko je iskren jezikom biva pitan za iskrenost svog djela.
why.en: He will ask the truthful (الصَّادِقِينَ) about their truthfulness (عَن صِدْقِهِمْ) — ar-Rāġib: one truthful in tongue is asked about the truth of his deeds.

why.bs: „A onaj ko donese istinu (بِالصِّدْقِ) i potvrdi je“ – ar-Rāġib: potvrdio je djelom ono što je donio riječju.
why.en: “And whoso bringeth the truth (بِالصِّدْقِ) and believeth therein” — ar-Rāġib: he made good in deed what he brought in word.

why.bs: Ibrahimova dova: „I podari mi istinit spomen (لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ) među kasnijim naraštajima“ – ar-Rāġib: da pohvala njemu ne bude laž.
why.en: Abraham's prayer: “And give unto me a good report (لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ) in later generations” — ar-Rāġib: that the praise of him not be false.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o izgovaranju napisanog ili objavljenog teksta. Prema ar-Rāġibu, تِلَاوَة je uža od قِرَاءَة: svaka تِلَاوَة je قِرَاءَة, ali nije svaka قِرَاءَة تِلَاوَة, a تَرْتِيل je način izgovora – lagano i pravilno.
shared.en: All three words concern voicing a written or revealed text. According to ar-Rāġib, تِلَاوَة is narrower than قِرَاءَة: every تِلَاوَة is a قِرَاءَة, but not every قِرَاءَة is a تِلَاوَة, while تَرْتِيل is a manner of voicing — with ease and evenness.

tellApart.bs: Kazivati Allahovu objavu i slijediti je (osnova: ići za nečim) → تَلَا; čitati, izgovarati slova i riječi spojene, bilo koji tekst → قَرَأَ; izgovarati lako i ujednačeno, riječ za riječju po redu → رَتَّلَ.
tellApart.en: To recite Allah's revelation and follow it (root: to follow after) → تَلَا; to read, to voice letters and words joined together, any text → قَرَأَ; to voice with ease and evenness, word after word in order → رَتَّلَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries تلى, قرأ, رتل
notes: ar-Rāġib (تلى): to follow with nothing between, by body, by imitation, or by reading / reflecting on the meaning (masdar tilāwa); 91:2 the moon following the sun in rank; tilāwa is specific to following Allah's revealed books, by reading or by conforming to their commands — it is more specific than qirāʾa: every tilāwa is qirāʾa, not the reverse; one does not say 'talawtu your note'; 2:121 'recite it with its true recital' = following it in knowledge and deed; 2:102 the devils' 'reciting' is so called because they claimed it was from Allah's books. (قرأ): qirāʾa is joining letters and words one to another in tartīl; a single letter uttered is not called qirāʾa; Qurʾān is at root a masdar. (رتل): ratal is a thing's being even and orderly; tartīl is sending the word from the mouth with ease and evenness (73:4, 25:32).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 60 places of تلو_1 read): the object of تَلَا is almost always Allah's ayat, the Book or news revealed by Him; the exceptions are 91:2 and 11:17 (following) and 2:102 (the devils), which ar-Rāġib explains. قَرَأَ is also used of reading one's own record of deeds (17:14, 69:19) and of a book the deniers demand (17:93).

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 4 of 4 flagged, fixed: one Bosnian word per member (kazivati / čitati / izgovarati polagano), English 'intone evenly' for رَتَّلَ; 'distinctly' dropped from his tellApart (his is ease and evenness); his 'fī t-tartīl' limit on qirāʾa restored; 96:1 'Read' in both languages.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnova je slijediti nešto bez ičega između. تِلَاوَة se, kaže on, odnosi na Allahove objavljene knjige – i na njihovo čitanje i na pridržavanje onoga što naređuju – pa se ne kaže za obično pismo. U kur'anskoj upotrebi predmet je gotovo uvijek Allahova objava.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root is to follow a thing with nothing between. تِلَاوَة, he says, belongs to Allah's revealed books — both reading them and keeping to what they command — so it is not said of an ordinary letter. In Quranic usage its object is almost always Allah's revelation.

why.bs: „Oni kojima smo dali Knjigu, koji je kazuju onako kako je treba kazivati“ – ar-Rāġib: slijede je znanjem i djelom.
why.en: “Those unto whom We have given the Scripture, who read it with the right reading” — ar-Rāġib: they follow it in knowledge and deed.

why.bs: „I tako mi Mjeseca kad ga slijedi“ – osnovno značenje: ići za nečim.
why.en: “And the moon when she followeth him” — the root sense: to follow after.

why.bs: „Kazuj ono što ti je od Knjige objavljeno“ – kazivanje objave.
why.en: “Recite that which hath been inspired in thee of the Scripture” — reciting the revelation.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, čitanje je spajanje slova i riječi jednih s drugima uz odmjeren izgovor; jedno izgovoreno slovo nije čitanje. Šira je riječ od تِلَاوَة: kaže se za svaki tekst, a u kur'anskoj upotrebi i za knjigu djela na Sudnjem danu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, reading is joining letters and words one to another in measured delivery; a single uttered letter is not reading. It is wider than تِلَاوَة: it is said of any text, and in Quranic usage even of the record of deeds on the Day of Judgement.

why.bs: „Čitaj svoju knjigu! Danas si sam sebi dovoljan obračunavalac“ – čitanje teksta koji nije objava.
why.en: “Read thy Book. Thy soul sufficeth as reckoner against thee this day” — reading a text that is not revelation.

why.bs: „Čitaj u ime svoga Gospodara, Koji je stvorio“ – naredba اقْرَأْ, od قَرَأَ.
why.en: “Read: In the name of thy Lord Who createth” — the command اقْرَأْ, from قَرَأَ.

why.bs: „Kada čitaš Kur'an, traži zaštitu kod Allaha od protjeranog šejtana“ – قَرَأَ se kaže i za Kur'an, a ne samo za druge tekstove.
why.en: “And when thou recitest (قَرَأْتَ) the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from Satan the outcast” — قَرَأَ is said of the Quran too, not only of other texts.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, korijen znači da je nešto ujednačeno i uredno, a تَرْتِيل je izgovarati riječi lako i pravilno. U Kur'anu samo dva puta, oba puta o Kur'anu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root means that a thing is even and orderly, and تَرْتِيل is sending the words out with ease and evenness. Only twice in the Quran, both times of the Quran.

why.bs: „I izgovaraj Kur'an polagano i razgovijetno (وَرَتِّلِ الْقُرْآنَ تَرْتِيلًا)“ – način izgovora, a ne samo čitanje.
why.en: “And chant the Qur'an in measure (وَرَتِّلِ الْقُرْآنَ تَرْتِيلًا)” — a manner of reciting, not reciting alone.

why.bs: „I Mi smo ga uredno, postupno izložili (وَرَتَّلْنَاهُ تَرْتِيلًا)“ – Allah govori o Kur'anu; mufessiri to tumače kao objavljivanje dio po dio, uredno.
why.en: “And We have arranged it in right order (وَرَتَّلْنَاهُ تَرْتِيلًا)” — Allah speaks of the Quran; mufassirun explain it as revealing it part by part, in order.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače očistiti. Prema ar-Rāġibu, čistoća (طَهَارَة) je dvojaka – čistoća tijela i čistoća duše – dok je osnova riječi زَكَاة rast koji dolazi od Allahova blagoslova: تَزْكِيَة je čišćenje koje čovjeka uvećava u dobru.
shared.en: Both words mean to purify. According to ar-Rāġib, purity (طَهَارَة) is of two kinds — of the body and of the soul — while the root of زَكَاة is growth that comes from Allah's blessing: تَزْكِيَة is a purifying that makes a person grow in good.

tellApart.bs: Očistiti tijelo, mjesto ili dušu od nečistoće → طَهَّرَ; oplemeniti dušu tako da raste u dobru; i hvaliti sebe kao čista (pokuđeno) → زَكَّى.
tellApart.en: To cleanse body, place or soul of impurity → طَهَّرَ; to purify the soul so that it grows in good; also to call oneself pure (blamed) → زَكَّى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries طهر, زكا
notes: ar-Rāġib (طهر): ṭahāra is of two kinds, of the body and of the soul, and most ayat are taken to mean both; 3:55 'purify you from those who disbelieve' = take you out from among them; 3:42 'purified you' among the soul-purification ayat; 2:125 purifying the Kaʿba from the filth of idols (some say: purifying the heart); 74:4 qīla 'your self'. (زكا): root is growth from Allah's blessing, worldly and otherworldly; zakāh named for hoped-for blessing or for growing the soul in good; tazkiya is ascribed to man as its earner (91:9), to Allah as its true doer (4:49), to the Prophet as the means (9:103, 62:2), and to worship as the instrument; man's tazkiya of himself is by deed — praised (91:9, 87:14) — or by word, praising himself — blamed and forbidden (53:32).

Quranic usage (our observation, all places of the two Form II verbs read): طَهَّرَ has Allah, Abraham and Ishmael (the House), and the Prophet (9:103, 74:4) as subjects; زَكَّى has Allah (also negated: 2:174, 3:77), the Prophet (2:129, 2:151, 3:164, 62:2, 9:103) and man himself (91:9 praised; 4:49 and 53:32 blamed). 9:103 has both verbs side by side. 74:4 and 2:125 are not cited (readings differ).

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 of 3 flagged, fixed: bs očistiti / oplemeniti (pročistiti was too close); 3:42 bs 'od grijeha' removed (not in the ayah, and of Mary); 91:9 'samo' removed; Korkut's Ka'ba.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, čistoća je i tjelesna i duševna, i većina ajeta se odnosi na obje. U Kur'anu se čisti tijelo vodom (8:11), Ka'ba (2:125) i duša – Allah je očistio Merjemu (3:42).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, purity is of the body and of the soul, and most ayat are taken to mean both. In the Quran water cleanses the body (8:11), the Kaʿba is cleansed (2:125), and the soul — Allah purified Mary (3:42).

why.bs: „I spušta vam s neba vodu da vas njome očisti“ – čišćenje tijela.
why.en: “And sent down water from the sky upon you, that thereby He might purify you” — cleansing of the body.

why.bs: „O Merjema, Allah te je zaista odabrao i očistio“ – ar-Rāġib ovo ubraja u čišćenje duše.
why.en: “O Mary! Lo! Allah hath chosen thee and made thee pure” — ar-Rāġib counts this as purifying of the soul.

why.bs: „Uzmi od njihovih imetaka sadaku kojom ćeš ih očistiti (تُطَهِّرُهُمْ) i oplemeniti (وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ)“ – obje riječi zajedno.
why.en: “Take alms of their wealth, wherewith thou mayst purify them (تُطَهِّرُهُمْ) and mayst make them grow (وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ)” — both words together.

meaning.en: to purify (cause to grow in good)

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, čišćenje duše koje donosi rast i blagoslov. Pripisuje se čovjeku koji se trudi (91:9), Allahu koji to stvarno čini (4:49) i Poslaniku kao posredniku (62:2). Čovjekovo pročišćavanje sebe djelom je pohvaljeno, a hvaljenje sebe riječima pokuđeno (53:32).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a purifying of the soul that brings growth and blessing. It is ascribed to man who strives for it (91:9), to Allah who truly does it (4:49), and to the Prophet as the means (62:2). Purifying oneself by deeds is praised; praising oneself in words is blamed (53:32).

why.bs: „Uspio je onaj ko je oplemeni (dušu)“ – oplemenjivanje sebe djelom, pohvaljeno.
why.en: “He is indeed successful who causeth it to grow” — purifying oneself by deeds, praised.

why.bs: „Zato ne hvalite sami sebe (فَلَا تُزَكُّوا أَنفُسَكُمْ); On najbolje zna ko je bogobojazan“ – ar-Rāġib: zabranjeno je hvaliti sebe riječima.
why.en: “Therefor ascribe not purity unto yourselves (فَلَا تُزَكُّوا أَنفُسَكُمْ). He is Best Aware of him who wardeth off (evil)” — ar-Rāġib: praising oneself in words is forbidden.

why.bs: Poslanik „koji im kazuje Njegove ajete i oplemenjuje ih (وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ)“ – Poslanik kao posrednik.
why.en: A messenger “to recite unto them His revelations and to make them grow (وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ)” — the Prophet as the means.

shared.bs: Sve četiri riječi su tvar od koje je, prema Kur'anu, stvoren čovjek. Prema ar-Rāġibu, طِين je zemlja (تُرَاب) pomiješana s vodom, صَلْصَال sasušena glina, a حَمَأ crno, ustajalo blato. Mnogi mufessiri ih vide kao faze jedne iste tvari.
shared.en: All four are matter from which, according to the Quran, man was created. According to ar-Rāġib, طِين is earth (تُرَاب) mixed with water, صَلْصَال is dried clay, and حَمَأ is black, foul-smelling mud. Many mufassirun see them as stages of one and the same matter.

tellApart.bs: Suha zemlja, prašina → تُرَاب; zemlja pomiješana s vodom → طِين; sasušena glina koja zveči → صَلْصَال; crno, izmijenjeno blato → حَمَأ.
tellApart.en: Dry earth, dust → تُرَاب; earth mixed with water → طِين; dried clay that rings → صَلْصَال; black, altered mud → حَمَأ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries تراب, طين, صلل, حمى
notes: ar-Rāġib (تراب): quotes 'created you from turāb' and 'would that I were dust' (78:40); turāb is the earth itself; tariba = became poor, as if cleaving to the dust (90:16). (طين): ṭīn is turāb and water mixed, and is still so called when the water's strength has gone (37:11 'sticky clay', 38:76, 28:38 Pharaoh's bricks). (صلل): the root of ṣalṣāl is the echoing sound of a dry thing; dry clay is called ṣalṣāl (55:14, 15:26); qīla: ṣalṣāl is foul-smelling clay, from ṣalla al-laḥm. (حمى): al-ḥamaʾ and al-ḥamʾa are black foul-smelling clay (15:26).

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): تُرَاب 17× — creation from dust (3:59, 18:37, 22:5, 30:20, 35:11, 40:67), and in eight places the deniers' 'when we have become dust' (13:5 … 56:47); طِين 12× — man's creation (6:2, 7:12, 17:61, 23:12, 32:7, 37:11, 38:71, 38:76), Jesus' birds by Allah's permission (3:49, 5:110), Pharaoh's bricks (28:38), stones of clay (51:33); صَلْصَال 4× (15:26, 15:28, 15:33, 55:14) and حَمَأ 3× — always in 15:26/28/33, together with صَلْصَال. حَمِئَة (18:86) is left out: its reading differs. 'Stages of one matter' is the mufassirun's harmonisation, not ar-Rāġib's.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 4 of 5 flagged, fixed: طِين is ilovača / moist clay, صَلْصَال suha zvonka glina / dry ringing clay throughout; 30:20 bs 'šire', 50:3 bs 'dalek' as the ayat say.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries تراب, طين, صلل, حمى (2026-11-06): 17 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/nuance (reworded): He says "قد يسمى" (may be called) and "the strength of the water", not the water itself

nuance.bs: Suha zemlja; prema ar-Rāġibu, تُرَاب je sama zemlja. U Kur'anu je početak čovjekova stvaranja (30:20), a u osam ajeta poricatelji se pitaju zar će biti vraćeni kad postanu prašina, čime izražavaju nevjericu u proživljenje.
nuance.en: Dry earth; according to ar-Rāġib, تُرَاب is the earth itself. In the Quran it is the beginning of man's creation (30:20), and in eight ayat the deniers ask whether they will be brought back once they have become dust, voicing disbelief in the resurrection.

why.bs: „Od Njegovih znakova je to što vas je stvorio od prašine, a vi ste onda ljudi koji se razilaze po zemlji.“
why.en: “And of His signs is this: He created you of dust, and behold you human beings, ranging widely!”

why.bs: „Primjer Ise kod Allaha isti je kao primjer Adema: stvorio ga je od prašine, zatim mu rekao: Budi! – i on bude.“
why.en: “Lo! the likeness of Jesus with Allah is as the likeness of Adam. He created him of dust, then He said unto him: Be! and he is.”

why.bs: Poricatelji: „Zar kad pomremo i postanemo prašina…? To je dalek povratak!“
why.en: The deniers: “When we are dead and have become dust (shall we be brought back again)? That would be a far return!”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, zemlja pomiješana s vodom; tako se može zvati i kad voda u njoj izgubi snagu. U Kur'anu najčešće tvar Ademova stvaranja, ali i ptice koje Isa, Allahovom dozvolom, oblikuje i opeka koju faraon peče (28:38).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, earth mixed with water; it may keep the name even when the water's strength has gone from it. In the Quran mostly the matter of Adam's creation, but also the birds Jesus shapes by Allah's permission and the bricks Pharaoh has fired (28:38).

why.bs: „Ja ću, zaista, stvoriti čovjeka od ilovače.“
why.en: “Lo! I am about to create a mortal out of mire (مِّن طِينٍ).”

why.bs: „Njih smo, zaista, stvorili od ilovače koja se lijepi (مِّن طِينٍ لَّازِبٍ)“ – ilovača s vodom, koja se lijepi.
why.en: “Lo! We created them of plastic clay (مِّن طِينٍ لَّازِبٍ)” — clay with water, which clings.

why.bs: Faraon: „Zapali mi, Hamane, vatru nad ilovačom“ – ista riječ za građu.
why.en: Pharaoh: “Kindle for me (a fire), O Haman, to bake the mud (عَلَى الطِّينِ)” — the same word for building material.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnova je odjek zvuka suhe stvari, pa se sasušena glina zove صَلْصَال. On navodi i mišljenje da je to ustajala, pokvarena glina. U Kur'anu samo četiri puta, uvijek o stvaranju čovjeka.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root is the echoing sound of a dry thing, so dried clay is called صَلْصَال. He also reports a view that it is foul, spoilt clay. Only four times in the Quran, always of man's creation.

why.bs: „Stvorio je čovjeka od suhe zvonke gline, poput grnčarije“ – suha, tvrda glina.
why.en: “He created man of clay (صَلْصَالٍ) like the potter's” — dry, hard clay.

why.bs: „Doista smo čovjeka stvorili od suhe zvonke gline (صَلْصَالٍ), od blata crnog i ustajalog (حَمَإٍ مَّسْنُونٍ)“ – obje riječi zajedno.
why.en: “Verily We created man of potter's clay (صَلْصَالٍ) of black mud altered (حَمَإٍ مَّسْنُونٍ)” — both words together.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, crna glina neugodnog mirisa. U Kur'anu tri puta, uvijek u istom izrazu uz صَلْصَال (15:26, 28, 33).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, black clay with a foul smell. Three times in the Quran, always in the same phrase with صَلْصَال (15:26, 28, 33).

why.bs: „Ja ću od suhe zvonke gline, od blata crnog i ustajalog, stvoriti ljudsko biće“ – riječi upućene melekima.
why.en: “Lo! I am creating a mortal out of potter's clay of black mud altered” — words to the angels.

why.bs: „Od crnog blata ustajalog (مِّنْ حَمَإٍ مَّسْنُونٍ)“ – blato od kojeg je glina.
why.en: “Of black mud altered (مِّنْ حَمَإٍ مَّسْنُونٍ)” — the mud of which the clay is.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače biti prisutan. Prema ar-Rāġibu, شُهُود i شَهَادَة su prisutnost uz gledanje – očima ili uvidom – mada kaže da se može reći i za samu prisutnost: شُهُود više priliči golom prisustvu, a شَهَادَة prisustvu uz gledanje. Riječ حُضُور on objašnjava riječju شَهَادَة, ‚prisutnost na mjestu ili kod nekoga‘. Zato je svjedočenje (شَهَادَة) govor iz znanja stečenog gledanjem.
shared.en: Both words mean being present. According to ar-Rāġib, شُهُود and شَهَادَة are presence together with seeing — by eye or by insight — though he says presence alone can also be so called: شُهُود suits bare presence better, شَهَادَة presence with seeing. He explains حُضُور with the word شَهَادَة, ‘being present at a place or with someone’. So testimony (شَهَادَة) is speech from knowledge gained by seeing.

tellApart.bs: Biti prisutan i vidjeti; posvjedočiti ono što se zna → شَهِدَ; biti prisutan, nastupiti, doći (smrt, ljudi) → حَضَرَ.
tellApart.en: To be present and see; to testify to what one knows → شَهِدَ; to be present, to come upon (death, people) → حَضَرَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries شهد, حضر
notes: ar-Rāġib (شهد): shuhūd and shahāda are presence with seeing, by sight or insight; sometimes said of bare presence, but shuhūd fits bare presence better and shahāda presence with seeing; 27:49 'we did not witness' = we were not present; 25:72 'do not witness falsehood' = are not present at it in person nor in intent; shahāda is speech issuing from knowledge gained by seeing with insight or eye; 12:81 'we testified only to what we knew' = what we reported; the witness must say 'I testify', not 'I know'; shahida may run as an oath. (حضر): ḥaḍar is the opposite of desert life; then made a name for 'being at (šahāda) a place or a person' (2:180, 4:8); 23:98 'that they be present with me' = the jinn, by allusion; muḥtaḍar of one at death.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 7 places of حضر_1 read): in four (2:133, 2:180, 4:18, 5:106) the subject is death; the others are relatives at the division (4:8), the devils (23:98) and the jinn at the Quran (46:29). شهد_1 (38 places) is mostly testifying (3:18, 24:24, 41:20 …); bare presence in 2:185, 22:28, 27:49, 25:72.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 3 of 3 flagged, fixed: his own distinction restored (شُهُود suits bare presence, شَهَادَة presence with seeing); حَضَرَ no longer 'says nothing of seeing' (of مُحْضَر 3:30 he does); 25:72 shows the majority reading (false testimony) beside his.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries شهد, حضر (2026-11-06): 18 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): He defines ḥaḍar as "شهادة مكان أو إنسان" — he uses shahāda itself to define ḥuḍūr. Fix keeps the contrast honest

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, prisutnost uz gledanje – očima ili uvidom; zato i svjedočenje, govor iz znanja stečenog gledanjem. Dodaje da imenica شُهُود više priliči golom prisustvu. Svjedok, kaže on, mora reći ‚svjedočim‘, a ne ‚znam‘. U Kur'anu najčešće svjedočenje, ponekad i sama prisutnost.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, presence together with seeing — by eye or by insight; hence also testimony, speech from knowledge gained by seeing. He adds that the noun شُهُود suits bare presence better. A witness, he says, must say ‘I testify’, not ‘I know’. In the Quran it is mostly testifying, sometimes bare presence.

why.bs: „Nismo posvjedočili osim o onome što znamo“ – ar-Rāġib: ‚svjedočiti‘ ovdje znači ‚obavijestiti‘.
why.en: “We testify only to that which we know” — ar-Rāġib: ‘testify’ here means ‘report’.

why.bs: Zavjerenici protiv Saliha: „Nismo bili prisutni (مَا شَهِدْنَا) pogibiji njegove porodice“ – ar-Rāġib: nismo bili tu.
why.en: The plotters against Ṣāliḥ: “We witnessed not (مَا شَهِدْنَا) the destruction of his household” — ar-Rāġib: we were not present.

why.bs: „I oni koji ne svjedoče laž (لَا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ)“ – mnogi mufesiri: lažno svjedočenje; ar-Rāġib: ne prisustvuju laži ni tijelom ni namjerom.
why.en: “And those who will not witness vanity (لَا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ)” — many mufassirun: false testimony; ar-Rāġib: they are not present at it, in body or in intent.

meaning.en: to be present, to come upon

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnova je život u naselju (suprotno pustinji), a onda bivanje na nekom mjestu ili kod nekoga. Objašnjava je riječju شَهَادَة, u značenju golog prisustva, bez gledanja i znanja u toj odredbi. U kur'anskoj upotrebi, u četiri od sedam mjesta, smrt je ta koja ‚nastupi‘ čovjeku.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root is settled life (the opposite of the desert), then being at a place or with someone. He defines it with the word شَهَادَة itself, meaning bare presence, adding nothing of seeing or knowing in that definition. In Quranic usage, in four of its seven places, it is death that ‘comes upon’ a person.

why.bs: „Propisana vam je, kad nekome od vas nastupi (حَضَرَ) smrt… oporuka“ – smrt koja nastupa.
why.en: “It is prescribed for you, when death approacheth (حَضَرَ) one of you … that he bequeath” — death that comes upon.

why.bs: „A kad diobi budu prisutni rođaci, siročad i siromasi, dajte im nešto od toga“ – prisutnost ljudi.
why.en: “And when kinsfolk and orphans and the needy are present at the division (of the heritage), bestow on them therefrom” — people being present.

why.bs: Džini koji slušaju Kur'an – „a kad su bili prisutni (حَضَرُوهُ), rekoše: Utihnite!“
why.en: The jinn listening to the Quran — “when they were in its presence (حَضَرُوهُ), said: Give ear!”

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače zadržati nekoga od nečega. Prema ar-Rāġibu, صَدّ je ili okretanje sebe od nečega ili odvraćanje drugoga, dok je مَنْع suprotnost davanju (uskraćivanje), a znači i zaštitu.
shared.en: Both words mean keeping someone from something. According to ar-Rāġib, صَدّ is either turning oneself away from a thing or turning another away, while مَنْع is the opposite of giving (withholding), and also means protection.

tellApart.bs: Okrenuti se od, odvraćati druge od (puta, upute) → صَدَّ; spriječiti, uskratiti, zaštititi → مَنَعَ.
tellApart.en: To turn away from, to turn others away from (a way, guidance) → صَدَّ; to prevent, to withhold, to protect → مَنَعَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries صدد, منع
notes: ar-Rāġib (صدد): ṣudūd / ṣadd may be turning away from a thing and refusing (4:61), or turning another away and preventing (27:24 / 29:38 'Satan barred them from the way', 47:1, 2:217, 28:87). (منع): manʿ is said of the opposite of giving — mānīʿ, mannāʿ = miser (107:7, 50:25); and of protection — a manīʿ place; 4:141 'did we not protect you'; 2:114 'who prevents the mosques of Allah'; 7:12 'what prevented you' = what led you, and qīla: what turned you away (ṣaddaka).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 37 places of صدد_1 read): in 22 the object is 'the way of Allah' or 'the way' (عَن سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ / عَنِ السَّبِيلِ); intransitive turning away in 4:55, 4:61, 43:57, 63:5. 28:87 and 20:16 are not cited (addressed to the Prophet).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, dvojako: okrenuti se od nečega i odbiti ga, ili okrenuti drugoga i spriječiti ga. U Kur'anu je najčešće riječ o odvraćanju ljudi od Allahova puta.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, two ways: turning away from a thing and refusing it, or turning another away and preventing him. In the Quran it is most often turning people away from the way of Allah.

why.bs: „Vidiš licemjere kako se od tebe odlučno odvraćaju“ – ar-Rāġib: okretanje sebe, odbijanje.
why.en: “Thou seest the hypocrites turn from thee with aversion” — ar-Rāġib: turning oneself away, refusing.

why.bs: „Šejtan im je uljepšao njihova djela i odvratio ih od puta“ – odvraćanje drugih.
why.en: “Satan maketh their works fairseeming unto them, and debarreth them from the way (of Truth)” — turning others away.

why.bs: Šejtan želi „da vas odvrati od spominjanja Allaha i od namaza“ – odvraćanje od cilja.
why.en: Satan seeketh “to turn you from remembrance of Allah and from (His) worship” — turning away from a goal.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, suprotnost davanju – uskratiti nekome nešto – a znači i zaštititi. Za riječi upućene Iblisu „Šta te je spriječilo“ (7:12) navodi tumačenje ‚šta te je navelo‘, i mišljenje ‚šta te je odvratilo (صَدَّكَ)‘.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the opposite of giving — withholding a thing from someone — and also protecting. For “What hindered thee” said to Iblis (7:12) he gives ‘what led you’, and reports the view ‘what turned you away (صَدَّكَ)’.

why.bs: „I uskraćuju sitnu pomoć (الْمَاعُونَ)“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet za suprotnost davanju.
why.en: “Yet refuse small kindnesses (الْمَاعُونَ)!” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah for the opposite of giving.

why.bs: „A ko je veći nasilnik od onoga ko u Allahovim mesdžidima brani da se spominje Njegovo ime?“
why.en: “And who doth greater wrong than he who forbiddeth the approach to the sanctuaries of Allah lest His name should be mentioned therein”

why.bs: „Šta te je spriječilo da padneš na sedždu kad sam ti naredio?“ – Allahovo pitanje Iblisu.
why.en: “What hindered thee that thou didst not fall prostrate when I bade thee?” — Allah's question to Iblis.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače brojati. Prema ar-Rāġibu, عَدّ je spajanje brojeva jednih s drugima, a إِحْصَاء je dokučiti nešto brojem, obuhvatiti ga u potpunosti; riječ dolazi od حَصًى, kamenčića kojima se nekad brojalo.
shared.en: Both words mean to count. According to ar-Rāġib, عَدّ is joining numbers one to another, while إِحْصَاء is to obtain a thing by number, to encompass it fully; the word comes from حَصًى, the pebbles once used for counting.

tellApart.bs: Brojati; i ubrajati nekoga među → عَدَّ; pobrojati sve, obuhvatiti brojem u potpunosti → أَحْصَى.
tellApart.en: To count, to number; also to reckon someone among → عَدَّ; to enumerate all, to encompass fully by number → أَحْصَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حصا, عد
notes: ar-Rāġib (حصا): iḥṣāʾ is taḥṣīl (obtaining) by number, from ḥaṣā, pebbles counted as we count on fingers; 72:28 'enumerated everything in number' = obtained and encompassed it; 73:20 'you will not be able to iḥṣāʾ it' — he then explains the hadith 'be upright, and you will not iḥṣāʾ' = not obtain it, hard because truth is one and falsehood many; lexicographers: 'not count its reward'. (عد): ʿadad is units composed; ʿadd is joining numbers to one another (19:94 aḥṣāhum wa-ʿaddahum ʿaddā); 'counted' (maʿdūd) is used for few, as against what cannot be counted for its multitude (2:80 'a few days').

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): أَحْصَى (10) — Allah encompassing all things (19:94, 36:12, 58:6, 72:28, 78:29), the record leaving nothing (18:49), people unable (14:34, 16:18, 73:20) and told to keep count of the ʿidda (65:1). عَدَّ (7) — 14:34 and 16:18 put the two side by side: if you count (تَعُدُّوا) Allah's favour you cannot enumerate it (لَا تُحْصُوهَا). 73:20 not cited (readings of 'lan tuḥṣūhu' differ).

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 3 of 3 flagged, fixed: brojati / izbrojati for عَدَّ, pobrojati for أَحْصَى throughout; 'reckon among' (38:62) given to Quranic usage, not to him; 58:6 bs 'pobrojao', not 'zapamtio'.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, dokučiti nešto brojem i obuhvatiti ga. Kad je Allah subjekt, ništa ne izmiče (72:28); kad su ljudi, najčešće je to ono što ne mogu – Allahove blagodati ne mogu se pobrojati (14:34).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to obtain a thing by number and encompass it. With Allah as subject nothing escapes (72:28); with people, it is mostly what they cannot do — Allah's favours cannot be enumerated (14:34).

why.bs: „Ako biste brojali (تَعُدُّوا) Allahove blagodati, ne biste ih mogli pobrojati (لَا تُحْصُوهَا)“ – brojanje je moguće, potpuno obuhvatanje nije.
why.en: “If ye would count (تَعُدُّوا) the bounty of Allah ye cannot reckon it (لَا تُحْصُوهَا)” — counting is possible, encompassing is not.

why.bs: „On obuhvata sve što je kod njih i svaku je stvar pobrojao (وَأَحْصَىٰ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عَدَدًا)“ – ar-Rāġib: dokučio je i obuhvatio.
why.en: “He surroundeth all their doings, and He keepeth count of all things (وَأَحْصَىٰ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عَدَدًا)” — ar-Rāġib: obtained and encompassed it.

why.bs: „Allah je to pobrojao (أَحْصَاهُ اللَّهُ), a oni su to zaboravili.“
why.en: “Allah hath kept account of it (أَحْصَاهُ اللَّهُ) while they forgot it.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, spajanje brojeva jednih s drugima. U Kur'anu može značiti i ‚smatrati, ubrajati među‘ (38:62). Sam broj ne kaže da je nešto obuhvaćeno: ljudi broje, ali ne mogu sve pobrojati (14:34).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, joining numbers one to another. In the Quran it can also mean to reckon someone among (38:62). The count alone does not say a thing is encompassed: people count, but cannot enumerate all (14:34).

why.bs: „On ih je doista sve pobrojao (أَحْصَاهُمْ) i izbrojao ih tačnim brojem (وَعَدَّهُمْ عَدًّا)“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet uz عَدّ, gdje obje riječi stoje jedna uz drugu.
why.en: “Verily He knoweth them (أَحْصَاهُمْ) and numbereth them with (right) numbering (وَعَدَّهُمْ عَدًّا)” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah for عَدّ, where both words stand side by side.

why.bs: „Zaista je dan kod tvoga Gospodara kao hiljadu godina od onih koje vi brojite (مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ)“ – ljudsko brojanje.
why.en: “A Day with Allah is as a thousand years of what ye reckon (مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ)” — human counting.

why.bs: „Šta nam je, pa ne vidimo ljude koje smo ubrajali među zle?“ – brojati kao ubrajati, smatrati.
why.en: “What aileth us that we behold not men whom we were wont to count among the wicked?” — counting as reckoning among.

shared.bs: Obje riječi opisuju ono što nije ozbiljno, i Kur'an ih često spaja kad govori o ovom svijetu. Prema ar-Rāġibu, لَهْو je ono što čovjeka zaokupi i odvrati od onoga što mu je važno, a لَعِب je djelo bez ispravnog cilja.
shared.en: Both words describe what is not earnest, and the Quran often joins them when speaking of this world. According to ar-Rāġib, لَهْو is what occupies a person and distracts him from what concerns him, while لَعِب is an act done without a sound aim.

tellApart.bs: Ono što zaokupi i odvrati od važnog, razonoda → لَهْو; igra, radnja bez ozbiljnog cilja → لَعِب.
tellApart.en: What occupies and distracts from what matters, amusement → لَهْو; play, an act with no earnest aim → لَعِب.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries لهى, لعب
notes: ar-Rāġib (لهى): lahw is what busies a person away from what concerns and matters to him; any enjoyment is called lahw; alhāhu = it busied him from what is more important (102:1, 24:37 — not a prohibition of trade but of being consumed by it to the neglect of prayer); those who take lahw in 21:17 as wife and child are specifying part of the world's adornment. (لعب): root luʿāb, flowing saliva; laʿiba when one's act is not aimed at a sound purpose (29:64, 6:70, 7:98, 21:55, 44:38).

Quranic usage (our observation, all places of both nouns read): لَعِب (8) never stands alone — six times with لَهْو (6:32, 6:70, 7:51, 29:64, 47:36, 57:20) and twice with هُزُو 'mockery' (5:57, 5:58); لَهْو (10 uses in 9 ayat) also alone (21:17, 31:6, 62:11). 21:17 and 31:6 are not cited: tafsir differs on what lahw means there.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 of 3 flagged, fixed: لَعِب is 'play' in every English line ('amusement' belongs to لَهْو). The noun-only scope of 'never alone' was set after verification (the verb stands alone, 12:12).

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries لهى, لعب (2026-11-06): 13 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): The first verse he cites is وما هذه الحياة الدنيا إلا لهو ولعب = 29:64, not 6:32 (6:32 reads وما الحياة الدنيا إلا لعب ولهو)

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ono što zaokupi čovjeka i odvrati ga od onoga što mu je važno; tako se naziva i svaki užitak. U Kur'anu i samostalno – za ono što odvlači od molitve (62:11).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, what occupies a person and distracts him from what matters to him; any enjoyment is also called so. In the Quran it also stands alone — for what draws people away from prayer (62:11).

why.bs: „A kad ugledaju trgovinu ili zabavu, razbježe se prema njoj… Reci: Ono što je kod Allaha bolje je od zabave i od trgovine.“
why.en: “But when they spy some merchandise or pastime they break away to it … Say: That which Allah hath is better than pastime and than merchandise.”

why.bs: „Ovaj dunjalučki život samo je zabava i igra, a ahiretski dom je, zaista, pravi život.“
why.en: “This life of the world is but a pastime and a game. Lo! the home of the Hereafter - that is Life.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnova je pljuvačka koja curi (لُعَاب), a igra je djelo kojim se ne teži ispravnom cilju. U Kur'anu imenica لَعِب nikad ne stoji sama (glagol stoji, npr. 12:12): uz لَهْو ili uz ruganje (هُزُو), kad nevjernici uzimaju vjeru i namaz kao igru.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root is flowing saliva (لُعَاب), and play is an act aimed at no sound purpose. In the Quran the noun لَعِب never stands alone (the verb does, e.g. 12:12): it comes with لَهْو or with mockery (هُزُو), when disbelievers take religion and prayer as play.

why.bs: „Dunjalučki život samo je igra i zabava, a ahiretski dom bolji je za one koji se Allaha boje.“
why.en: “Naught is the life of the world save a pastime and a sport. Better far is the abode of the Hereafter for those who keep their duty (to Allah).”

why.bs: „A kad pozivate na namaz, oni ga uzimaju za ruganje i igru“ – igra uz ruganje.
why.en: “And when ye call to prayer they take it for a jest and sport” — play joined with mockery.

why.bs: „I ostavi one koji svoju vjeru uzimaju kao igru i zabavu.“
why.en: “And forsake those who take their religion for a pastime and a jest.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače ono što nešto čini lijepim za oko. Prema ar-Rāġibu, زُخْرُف je ukras koji je dotjeran i uljepšan – zato se i zlato zove زُخْرُف – dok je زِينَة širi pojam: ukras duše, tijela i imetka.
shared.en: Both words mean what makes a thing pleasing to the eye. According to ar-Rāġib, زُخْرُف is adornment that has been embellished — hence gold too is called زُخْرُف — while زِينَة is the wider word: adornment of the soul, of the body and of possessions.

tellApart.bs: Ukras uopće – znanje i vjera, snaga i stas, imetak i ugled; dozvoljen ili zavodljiv, prema tome kako se koristi → زِينَة; kićenost, dotjerani sjaj – zlato, kićene riječi, Zemlja okićena pred propast → زُخْرُف.
tellApart.en: Adornment in general — knowledge and faith, strength and stature, wealth and standing; lawful or tempting, by how it is used → زِينَة; embellishment, polished glitter — gold, embellished words, the earth decked out before its ruin → زُخْرُف.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries زين, زخرف
notes: ar-Rāġib (زين): true zīna is what does not disgrace a person in any state, in this world or the next; what adorns in one state and not another is in one respect a disgrace. Zīna is of three kinds: of the soul (knowledge, good beliefs), of the body (strength, stature), external (wealth, standing); 49:7 is of the soul, 7:32 was taken as external (a report that some circled the House naked), while some said the zīna there is karam (49:13); 28:79 is worldly zīna. Allah ascribes tazyīn to Himself, to Satan, and leaves the doer unnamed. (زخرف): zuḫruf is ornamented (muzawwaq) zīna, hence gold is called zuḫruf; 17:93 a house of ornamented gold (ḏahab muzawwaq); 6:112 zuḫruf al-qawl = embellished speech.

That زُخْرُف, in its four places (6:112, 10:24, 17:93, 43:35), is never praised — deceptive speech, the earth's finery before it is cut down, a gold house the disbelievers demand, worldly enjoyment — is our observation of Quranic usage.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, pravi ukras je onaj koji čovjeka ne sramoti ni na ovom ni na onom svijetu. Ukras je trojak: duševni (znanje, ispravno vjerovanje), tjelesni (snaga, stas) i vanjski (imetak, ugled). Kur'an ga spominje i kao dozvoljen dar (7:32) i kao ukras ovosvjetskog života koji prolazi (18:46, 28:79).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, true adornment is that which does not disgrace a person in this world or the next. Adornment is of three kinds: of the soul (knowledge, right belief), of the body (strength, stature) and external (wealth, standing). The Quran names it both as a lawful gift (7:32) and as the adornment of worldly life that passes (18:46, 28:79).

why.bs: „Ko je zabranio ukras Allahov, koji je On za Svoje robove izveo?“ – ar-Rāġib: shvaćen je kao vanjski ukras (odjeća), a neki kažu da je to plemenitost (كَرَم).
why.en: “Who hath forbidden the adornment of Allah which He hath brought forth for His bondmen?” — ar-Rāġib: it has been taken as external adornment (clothing); others say it is nobility (كَرَم).

why.bs: „Imetak i sinovi ukras su dunjalučkog života“ – ukras koji prolazi.
why.en: “Wealth and children are an ornament of the life of the world” — adornment that passes.

why.bs: Karun „izađe pred svoj narod u svom ukrasu“ – ar-Rāġib: ovosvjetski ukras, imetak i ugled.
why.en: Qārūn came out “before his people in his pomp” — ar-Rāġib: worldly adornment, wealth and standing.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ukras koji je dotjeran i uljepšan; zato se zlato zove زُخْرُف, a ‚kićene riječi‘ (زُخْرُفَ الْقَوْلِ) su uljepšan govor. U kur'anskoj upotrebi riječ nikad nije pohvalna: varljive riječi, Zemlja okićena prije propasti, zlatna kuća koju traže nevjernici, prolazno uživanje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, adornment that has been embellished; hence gold is called زُخْرُف, and ‘embellished speech’ (زُخْرُفَ الْقَوْلِ) is speech dressed up. In Quranic usage the word is never praised: deceptive words, the earth decked out before its ruin, a house of gold the disbelievers demand, passing enjoyment.

why.bs: Šejtani jedni drugima „ubacuju kićen govor (زُخْرُفَ الْقَوْلِ), radi obmane“ – sjaj bez istine.
why.en: Devils “inspire in one another plausible discourse (زُخْرُفَ الْقَوْلِ) through guile” — glitter without truth.

why.bs: Nevjernici traže od Poslanika „kuću od zlata“ – ar-Rāġib: od ukrašenog zlata.
why.en: The disbelievers demand of the Prophet “a house of gold” — ar-Rāġib: of ornamented gold.

why.bs: „I zlata. A sve to nije ništa drugo do uživanje u dunjalučkom životu.“
why.en: “And ornaments of gold. Yet all that would have been but a provision of the life of the world.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače nečistoću. Prema ar-Rāġibu, رِجْس je prljava stvar, gadna po prirodi, razumu ili šerijatu (ili po svemu troje), a نَجَس je nečistoća koja se opaža čulima ili pronicljivošću – i ovu drugu Allah pripisuje mnogobošcima.
shared.en: Both words mean uncleanness. According to ar-Rāġib, رِجْس is a filthy thing, repugnant by nature, by reason or by the Sharia (or by all three), while نَجَس is filth perceived either by the senses or by insight — and it is the second that Allah ascribes to the polytheists.

tellApart.bs: Gadost – stvar od koje se treba kloniti: vino, kocka, strvina, svinjetina, kipovi, pa i nevjerovanje → رِجْس; nečist – samo jednom u Kur'anu, o mnogobošcima; ar-Rāġib je shvaća kao nečistoću koja se opaža pronicljivošću → نَجَس.
tellApart.en: Defilement — a thing to be shunned: wine, gambling, carrion, pork, idols, and unbelief itself → رِجْس; unclean — only once in the Quran, of the polytheists; ar-Rāġib takes it as an uncleanness perceived by insight → نَجَس.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رجس, نجس
notes: ar-Rāġib (رجس): rijs is the filthy thing; it is so in four ways: by nature, by reason, by the Sharia, or by all of these, like carrion; wine and gambling are rijs by the Sharia — and it has been said (qīla) by reason too, as 2:219 hints; disbelievers are made rijs because shirk is, to reason, the ugliest of things (9:125); on 10:100 it has been said rijs is stench, and it has been said punishment, like 9:28; pork (6:145) is rijs by the Sharia. (نجس, the text misprints النحاسة): najāsa is filth, of two kinds — perceived by the senses and perceived by insight; Allah described the polytheists with the second (9:28).

نَجَس occurs once in the Quran (9:28); رِجْس 10× in 9 ayat (counted from the corpus). The jurists' question whether polytheists are bodily impure is not taken up; we give only ar-Rāġib's classification.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, prljava, gadna stvar – gadna po prirodi, po razumu, po šerijatu ili po svemu troje (kao strvina). Vino i kocka su gadost po šerijatu, a svinjetina također; nevjernike Kur'an naziva gadošću jer je širk razumu najružnija stvar.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a filthy, repugnant thing — repugnant by nature, by reason, by the Sharia, or by all three (like carrion). Wine and gambling are defilement by the Sharia, and so is pork; the Quran calls the disbelievers defilement because shirk is, to reason, the ugliest of things.

why.bs: „Vino, kocka, kameni kipovi i strelice za gatanje samo su gadost od šejtanova djela; zato se toga klonite.“ – ar-Rāġib: gadost po šerijatu.
why.en: “Strong drink and games of chance and idols and divining arrows are only an infamy (رِجْسٌ) of Satan's handiwork. Leave it aside” — ar-Rāġib: defilement by the Sharia.

why.bs: „…ili svinjsko meso – jer je ono zaista gadost“ – ar-Rāġib: po šerijatu.
why.en: “…or swineflesh - for that verily is foul (رِجْسٌ)” — ar-Rāġib: by the Sharia.

why.bs: „A one čija su srca bolesna – njima ona samo dodaje gadost na gadost njihovu“ – ar-Rāġib: nevjerovanje kao gadost razumu.
why.en: “But as for those in whose hearts is disease, it only addeth wickedness (رِجْسًا) to their wickedness” — ar-Rāġib: unbelief as defilement to reason.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, nečistoća je dvojaka: ona koja se opaža čulima i ona koja se opaža pronicljivošću; ovom drugom Allah opisuje mnogobošce. U Kur'anu samo jednom (9:28).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, uncleanness is of two kinds: one perceived by the senses and one perceived by insight; it is with the second that Allah describes the polytheists. In the Quran only once (9:28).

why.bs: „O vi koji vjerujete, mnogobošci su samo nečisti, pa neka se ne približavaju Svetom mesdžidu“ – ar-Rāġib to shvaća kao nečistoću koja se opaža pronicljivošću; učenjaci se razilaze koliko ona seže.
why.en: “O ye who believe! The idolaters only are unclean. So let them not come near the Inviolable Place of Worship” — ar-Rāġib takes it as an uncleanness perceived by insight; scholars differ on how far it reaches.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače skriveni naum protiv nekoga. Prema ar-Rāġibu, كَيْد je vrsta smicalice, a مَكْر odvraćanje drugoga od onoga što namjerava, putem smicalice; i jedno i drugo može biti pokuđeno ili pohvalno, iako se كَيْد češće kaže za pokuđeno.
shared.en: Both words mean a hidden design against someone. According to ar-Rāġib, كَيْد is a kind of stratagem, and مَكْر is turning another away from what he intends, by a stratagem; either can be blameworthy or praiseworthy, though كَيْد is used more often of the blameworthy.

tellApart.bs: Lukavstvo, smicalica – ženâ, sihirbaza, nevjernika; kod Allaha, kako Njemu priliči, ostavljanje vremena koje vodi kazni (7:183) → كَيْد; spletka kojom se drugi odvraća od svog cilja; kod Allaha, kako Njemu priliči, što mufessiri objašnjavaju kao uzvraćanje na njihovu spletku (27:50) → مَكْر.
tellApart.en: Stratagem, ploy — of women, of a magician, of disbelievers; of Allah, as befits Him, the respite that leads to punishment (7:183) → كَيْد; scheming that turns another from his aim; of Allah, as befits Him, which mufassirun explain as requital of their scheme (27:50) → مَكْر.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries كيد, مكر
notes: ar-Rāġib (كيد): kayd is a kind of iḥtiyāl (stratagem); it may be blameworthy or praiseworthy, though used more of the blameworthy — likewise istidrāǧ and makr; 12:76 (kidnā li-Yūsuf); on 7:183 some said kayd is punishment, but the correct view is that it is the respite (imlāʾ, imhāl) leading to punishment; 12:52 'Allah does not guide the kayd of the treacherous' — specifying the treacherous shows He may guide the kayd of one who intends no treachery, like Joseph's with his brother; 20:69 kayd of a magician. (مكر): makr is turning another from what he intends by a stratagem; two kinds: praiseworthy, seeking a fine deed (3:54 'Allah is the best of planners'), and blameworthy (35:43); 27:50 has both; some said that of Allah's makr is giving the servant respite and worldly ease.

Content policy: Allah's kayd and makr are given only with a gloss — ar-Rāġib's (kayd: respite leading to punishment) or the mufassirun's (makr: requital of their plotting), never as human deceit. 86:15–16 and 7:99 are not cited.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 3 of 3 flagged, fixed: no fixed split between Allah's كَيْد and مَكْر — respite (7:183) is his, requital (27:50) the mufassirun's, each 'as befits Him'; bs 'plan Moj' for Allah, not 'lukavstvo'; 71:22 'against a messenger' removed.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries كيد, مكر (2026-11-06): 21 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/1 (reworded): Makes explicit that 'requital' is the mufassirun's, not ar-Rāġib's; members/1/nuance (reworded): He cites 27:50 'for both matters' (blameworthy and praiseworthy) but never calls Allah's makr requital; that gloss is the mufassirun's; members/1/ayat/1/why (reworded): 'Requital' is not in the entry

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, vrsta smicalice; može biti pokuđeno i pohvalno, ali se češće kaže za pokuđeno. Kada se pripisuje Allahu (7:183), on kaže da je ispravno tumačenje – Allahovo ostavljanje vremena koje vodi kazni, a neki su rekli da je to sama kazna.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a kind of stratagem; it can be blameworthy or praiseworthy, but is said more often of the blameworthy. When ascribed to Allah (7:183), he says the correct reading is Allah's granting of respite that leads to punishment; some said it is the punishment itself.

why.bs: „Ovo je od vašeg ženskog lukavstva; vaše je lukavstvo zaista veliko“ – pokuđena smicalica.
why.en: “Lo! this is of the guile of you women. Lo! the guile of you is very great” — a blameworthy ploy.

why.bs: „Ono što su napravili samo je lukavstvo sihirbaza“ – smicalica obmane.
why.en: “That which they have made is but a wizard's artifice” — a ploy of illusion.

why.bs: „I dajem im vremena; Moj je plan (كَيْدِي), zaista, čvrst“ – kako Njemu priliči; ar-Rāġib: ostavljanje vremena koje vodi kazni.
why.en: “I give them rein (for) lo! My scheme (كَيْدِي) is strong” — as befits Him; ar-Rāġib: the respite that leads to punishment.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, odvraćanje drugoga od onoga što namjerava, putem smicalice; pohvalno je kad se njime traži dobro djelo, pokuđeno kad se traži ružno. On navodi 27:50 za obje vrste: njihova spletka (pokuđena vrsta) i Allahovo, kako Njemu priliči (pohvalna vrsta); mufessiri često objašnjavaju ovo drugo kao uzvraćanje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, turning another away from what he intends, by a stratagem; praiseworthy when it seeks a fine deed, blameworthy when it seeks an ugly one. He cites 27:50 for both kinds: their scheme (the blameworthy kind) and Allah's, as befits Him (the praiseworthy kind); mufassirun often explain the latter as requital.

why.bs: „A ružna spletka stiže samo one koji je kuju“ – pokuđena spletka se vraća svom vlasniku.
why.en: “The evil plot encloseth but the men who make it” — the blameworthy scheme returns on its maker.

why.bs: „I oni su skovali spletku, a i Mi smo skovali (Svoju), a oni to nisu ni slutili“ – ar-Rāġib: obje vrste u jednom ajetu; Allahova, kako Njemu priliči, je pohvalna vrsta; mufessiri je objašnjavaju kao uzvraćanje.
why.en: “So they plotted a plot: and We plotted a plot, while they perceived not” — ar-Rāġib: both kinds in one ayah; Allah's, as befits Him, is the praiseworthy kind; mufassirun explain it as requital.

why.bs: Nuhov narod: „I skovali su veliku spletku“ – spletkarenje.
why.en: Noah's people: “And they have plotted a mighty plot” — scheming.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o tijesnom. Prema ar-Rāġibu, ضِيق je suprotnost prostranosti i izražava tugu, siromaštvo ili škrtost, a حَرَج dolazi od gustog, zbijenog skupa stvari, pa znači i tjeskobu i grijeh.
shared.en: Both words speak of tightness. According to ar-Rāġib, ضِيق is the opposite of spaciousness and expresses grief, poverty or stinginess, while حَرَج comes from a thick, close-packed cluster of things, and so means both constriction and sin.

tellApart.bs: Biti stiješnjen – grudi, duša, Zemlja; nemoć i tuga pred nečim → ضَاقَ; teškoća koja se nameće, a i grijeh (‚nema ḥaraja na…‘) → حَرَج.
tellApart.en: To be straitened — the breast, the soul, the earth; helplessness and grief before a thing → ضَاقَ; a hardship laid on someone, and also sin (‘there is no ḥaraj upon…’) → حَرَج.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ضيق, حرج
notes: ar-Rāġib (ضيق): ḍīq is the opposite of saʿa; ḍayq/ḍīqa is used for poverty, stinginess, grief and the like; 11:77 'ḍāqa bihim ḏarʿan' = he was unable to deal with them; 11:12, 26:13, 6:125, 9:25, 9:118, 16:127 — 'all of that expresses grief'. (حرج): the root of ḥaraǧ is a close gathering of a thing, from which the narrowness between is imagined, so narrowness is called ḥaraǧ and sin is called ḥaraǧ; 4:65, 22:78; 6:125 'constricted by his unbelief', and it has been said 'constricted towards Islam'; on 7:2 he lists three readings (prohibition, prayer, ruling).

That the verb ضَاقَ in its seven uses (9:25, 9:118 ×2, 11:77, 15:97, 26:13, 29:33) is said of the breast, the soul, the earth and of Lot 'with them', never of a rule or of sin, is our observation. 7:2 and 6:125 are not cited (readings differ).

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries ضيق, حرج (2026-11-06): 16 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): Verse reference correction only; members/0/ayat/1/why (reworded): bs added 'how to protect them'; he only says عجز عنهم

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, suprotnost prostranosti; o grudima, duši i Zemlji izražava tugu, a ‚ضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًا‘ znači da je bio nemoćan pred njima. U kur'anskoj upotrebi glagol se kaže samo za grudi, dušu, Zemlju i za Luta pred gostima – nikad za propis ili grijeh.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the opposite of spaciousness; said of the breast, the soul and the earth it expresses grief, and ‘ضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًا’ means he was at a loss with them. In Quranic usage the verb is said only of the breast, the soul, the earth and of Lot before his guests — never of a rule or of sin.

why.bs: „…kad im je zemlja, uza svu svoju prostranost, postala tijesna, a tijesne im postale i same duše“ – tijesnoća i tuga.
why.en: “…when the earth, vast as it is, was straitened for them, and their own souls were straitened for them” — the constriction of soul and earth, of grief.

why.bs: Lut se „zbog njih ražalosti i osjeti se nemoćnim pred njima“ – ar-Rāġib: bio je nemoćan pred njima.
why.en: Lot “was distressed and knew not how to protect them (وَضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًا)” — ar-Rāġib: he was at a loss with them.

why.bs: Musa: „I stegnut će mi se grudi, a jezik mi se neće razvezati“ – tjeskoba pred velikim zadatkom.
why.en: Moses: “And I shall be embarrassed (وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي), and my tongue will not speak plainly” — distress before a great task.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, korijen je gust, zbijen skup stvari, pa se tjeskoba među njima zove حَرَج, a tako i grijeh. Zato Kur'an kaže da u vjeri nema teškoće (22:78) i da „nema smetnje“ bolesnom i slijepom (24:61).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root is a thick, close-packed cluster of things, so the tightness among them is called حَرَج, and so is sin. Hence the Quran says there is no hardship in the religion (22:78) and “no blame” upon the sick and the blind (24:61).

why.bs: „…i nije vam u vjeri nametnuo nikakvu teškoću“ – teškoća koja se nameće.
why.en: “…hath not laid upon you in religion any hardship” — a hardship laid upon people.

why.bs: „Nema smetnje slijepom…“ – skidanje teškoće; mnogi mufesiri to shvaćaju i kao krivicu.
why.en: “No blame is there upon the blind…” — a lifting of hardship; many mufassirun take it as blame too, as rendered here.

why.bs: „…a potom u dušama svojim ne nađu nikakve tegobe od onoga što si ti presudio“ – tjeskoba u duši.
why.en: “…and find within themselves no dislike (حَرَجًا) of that which thou decidest” — tightness within the soul.

title.en: Making clear and setting out in detail

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače učiniti nešto razumljivim. Prema ar-Rāġibu, بَيَان je otkrivanje stvari, a فَصْل razdvajanje jedne stvari od druge tako da među njima ostane razmak – a تَفْصِيل Knjige povezuje s time da je ona objašnjenje svega.
shared.en: Both verbs mean making a thing understood. According to ar-Rāġib, بَيَان is uncovering a thing, and فَصْل is separating one thing from another so that a gap stays between them — and he ties the Book's تَفْصِيل to its being an explanation of all things.

tellApart.bs: Pojasniti, otkriti ono što je skriveno ili nejasno – Allah, poslanik, i učeni ljudi → بَيَّنَ; potanko izložiti, razdvojiti dio od dijela – u Kur'anu uvijek Allahovi ajeti, Knjiga, zabranjeno → فَصَّلَ.
tellApart.en: To make clear, to uncover what was hidden or unclear — Allah, a messenger, and people of learning → بَيَّنَ; to set out in detail, separating part from part — in the Quran always Allah's verses, the Book, what is forbidden → فَصَّلَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries بان, فصل
notes: ar-Rāġib (بان): bayān is uncovering (kašf) a thing, more general than speech; bayyantuhu / abantuhu = I gave it a bayān that discloses it (16:44); what explains the summary and the obscure is called bayān (75:19); clear signs bayyināt. (فصل): faṣl is separating one of two things from the other until there is a gap between them; used of acts and words; 17:12 'everything We set out in detail', 11:1 'perfected, then set out in detail', pointing to 16:89 'an explanation of all things'.

Our observation of the corpus: the active فَصَّلَ (17 uses) has Allah as subject every time, and its passive forms are said of the Book's verses (11:1, 41:3, 41:44); بَيَّنَ is also said of messengers (16:44, 14:4, 43:63) and of people (2:160, 3:187).

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 of 3 flagged, fixed: bs 'potanko izložiti' for فَصَّلَ (objasniti stays with بَيَّنَ); 11:1 bs 'učvršćeni' for uḥkimat; 'item by item' (6:119) removed; 2:242 bs 'ajete'.
