ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries بان, فصل (2026-11-06): 16 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): 'part by part' is our inference from the root, not his gloss; members/1/nuance (reworded): Same as shared

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, dati stvari objašnjenje koje je otkriva; بَيَان je otkrivanje, šire od govora. U Kur'anu pojašnjava Allah (ajete), poslanik (Objavu ljudima), ali i ljudi od Knjige, kojima je naređeno da je pojasne a ne skrivaju.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, giving a thing an explanation that uncovers it; بَيَان is disclosure, wider than speech. In the Quran Allah makes clear (the verses), a messenger makes clear (the revelation to people), and so must the People of the Book, who were told to make it clear and not conceal it.

why.bs: „Tako vam Allah pojašnjava Svoje ajete da biste razumjeli.“
why.en: “Thus Allah expoundeth unto you His revelations so that ye may understand.”

why.bs: „…da ljudima pojasniš ono što im je objavljeno“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet za بَيَّنَ.
why.en: “…that thou mayst explain to mankind that which hath been revealed for them” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah for بَيَّنَ.

why.bs: „Zaista ćete je ljudima pojašnjavati i nećete je skrivati“ – pojasniti je suprotno od skriti.
why.en: “Ye are to expound it to mankind and not to hide it” — to make clear is the opposite of to conceal.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, فَصْل je razdvajanje dviju stvari tako da među njima ostane razmak; تَفْصِيل Knjige povezuje s time da je ona objašnjenje svega. U kur'anskoj upotrebi onaj ko potanko izlaže uvijek je Allah, a izloženo su ajeti, Knjiga, zabranjeno, ‚sve‘.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, فَصْل is separating two things so that a gap stays between them; the Book's تَفْصِيل he ties to its being an explanation of all things. In Quranic usage the one who sets out in detail is always Allah, and what is set out is the verses, the Book, what is forbidden, ‘everything’.

why.bs: „Knjiga čiji su ajeti učvršćeni, pa onda potanko izloženi, od Onoga Koji je Mudar i o svemu obaviješten“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “A Scripture the revelations whereof are perfected and then expounded. (It cometh) from One Wise, Informed” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „…a On vam je već razložio šta vam je zabranio“ – zabranjeno, potanko izloženo.
why.en: “…when He hath explained unto you that which is forbidden unto you” — what is forbidden, set out in detail.

why.bs: „…i svaku smo stvar razložili potanko“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And everything have We expounded with a clear expounding” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi imenuju kaznu koja je zadesila ranije narode. Prema ar-Rāġibu, رَجْفَة je snažno potresanje, صَيْحَة podizanje glasa, a صَاعِقَة silan zvuk s neba od kojeg dolazi vatra, kazna ili smrt. Isti narod, Semud, opisan je svakom od tri riječi. Mufesiri često objašnjavaju da je to jedna kazna opisana s različitih strana: strašni glas odozgo i potres tla.
shared.en: All three words name the punishment that seized earlier peoples. According to ar-Rāġib, رَجْفَة is violent shaking, صَيْحَة is raising the voice, and صَاعِقَة is a mighty sound from the sky that brings fire, punishment or death. One people, Thamud, is described with each of the three. Mufassirun often explain that this is one punishment described from different sides: the dreadful sound from above and the quaking of the ground.

tellApart.bs: Potres – tlo se snažno trese (Semud, Medjen) → رَجْفَة; krik – glas koji obuzme strahom; i puhanje u rog → صَيْحَة; munja – silan prasak s neba, i grom koji pogađa → صَاعِقَة.
tellApart.en: Quake — the ground shakes violently (Thamud, Midian) → رَجْفَة; shriek — a sound that seizes with terror; also the blast of the Horn → صَيْحَة; thunderbolt — a mighty crash from the sky, the bolt that strikes → صَاعِقَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رجف, صاح, صعق
notes: ar-Rāġib (رجف): rajf is violent agitation, of the earth and the sea; 79:6, 73:14, 'fa-aḫaḏathumu r-rajfa'; irǧāf is causing rajfa by act or word (33:60). (صاح): ṣayḥa is raising the voice (36:29; 50:42 = the blowing of the Horn); its root is the splitting of sound; because a shout terrifies, it expresses terror in 15:73. (صعق): ṣāʿiqa and ṣāqiʿa are close — a great crash; ṣaqʿ for earthly bodies, ṣaʿq for heavenly ones; some linguists say ṣāʿiqa is of three kinds (death 39:68, punishment 41:13, fire 13:13); he answers that these are effects of it: the ṣāʿiqa is the violent sound from the sky, from which come fire alone, or punishment, or death.

Thamud: الرَّجْفَة 7:78, الصَّيْحَة 11:67, صَاعِقَة 41:17 and 51:44; Midian: الرَّجْفَة 7:91 and 29:37, الصَّيْحَة 11:94 — our listing. That mufassirun reconcile these as one punishment described from different sides is given as 'mufassirun often explain', not as ar-Rāġib's.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, snažno potresanje, kaže se za zemlju i more. U Kur'anu (4 puta) kazna koja je zadesila Semud i Medjen, i potres koji je obuzeo sedamdesetoricu odabranih od Musaovog naroda.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, violent shaking, said of the earth and the sea. In the Quran (4 times) the punishment that seized Thamud and Midian, and the quake that seized the seventy chosen from Moses' people.

why.bs: Semud: „I zahvati ih potres…“ – što 11:67 naziva krikom; mnogi mufessiri to shvaćaju kao jednu kaznu viđenu s dvije strane.
why.en: Thamud: “So the earthquake seized them…” — which 11:67 calls the shriek; many mufassirun take it as one punishment seen from two sides.

why.bs: Medjen, Šuajbov narod: „I zahvati ih potres…“ – što 11:94 naziva krikom; mnogi mufessiri to shvaćaju kao jednu kaznu viđenu s dvije strane.
why.en: Midian, the people of Shuʿayb: “So the earthquake seized them…” — which 11:94 calls the shriek; many mufassirun take it as one punishment seen from two sides.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, podizanje glasa; korijen je pucanje zvuka, a pošto krik plaši, kaže se i za sam strah (15:73). U Kur'anu kazna Semudu, Medjenu i Lutovom narodu, ali i puhanje u rog kod proživljenja (50:42).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, raising the voice; the root is the cracking of sound, and since a shout terrifies, it is said of terror itself (15:73). In the Quran the punishment of Thamud, Midian and Lot's people, and also the blast of the Horn at the resurrection (50:42).

why.bs: Semud: „A one koji su činili nepravdu zahvati krik, pa osvanuše u svojim kućama mrtvi, nepomični.“
why.en: Thamud: “And the (awful) Cry overtook those who did wrong, so that morning found them prostrate in their dwellings.”

why.bs: Lutov narod: „I zahvati ih krik pri izlasku sunca“ – ar-Rāġib: ovdje krik u značenju straha.
why.en: Lot's people: “Then the (Awful) Cry overtook them at the sunrise” — ar-Rāġib: here the shriek in the sense of terror.

why.bs: „Na Dan kada će uistinu čuti krik“ – ar-Rāġib: puhanje u rog.
why.en: “The day when they will hear the (Awful) Cry in truth” — ar-Rāġib: the blowing of the Horn.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, silan zvuk s neba; od njega dolazi vatra, kazna ili smrt – to su njegovi učinci, a sam je jedna stvar. Neki jezikoslovci su, prenosi on, razlikovali tri značenja: smrt, kaznu i vatru. U Kur'anu kazna Semudu i Adu, ali i munje u oluji (13:13).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a mighty sound from the sky; from it come fire, punishment or death — these are its effects, while it is itself one thing. Some linguists, he reports, distinguished three senses: death, punishment and fire. In the Quran the punishment of Thamud and ʿĀd, and also the bolts in a storm (13:13).

why.bs: Semud: „…pa ih je zahvatila munja ponižavajuće kazne“ – treća riječ za istu propast.
why.en: Thamud: “…so the bolt of the doom of humiliation overtook them” — a third word for the same ruin.

why.bs: „Upozoravam vas na munju kakva je bila munja Ada i Semuda“ – ar-Rāġib (prenoseći neke jezikoslovce): munja kao kazna.
why.en: “I warn you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt (which fell of old upon the tribes) of A'ad and Thamud” — ar-Rāġib (reporting some linguists): the thunderbolt as punishment.

why.bs: „…i šalje munje te njima pogađa koga hoće“ – šalje ih Allah i usmjerava.
why.en: “…He launcheth the thunderbolts and smiteth with them whom He will” — sent and aimed by Allah.

shared.bs: Oba glagola su položaji poniznosti i dijelovi namaza. Prema ar-Rāġibu, سُجُود je u osnovi spuštanje i poniznost, i kaže se za ljude, životinje i neživo, dok je رُكُوع pregibanje – položaj u namazu, ili poniznost u ibadetu i izvan njega.
shared.en: Both verbs are postures of humility and parts of the prayer. According to ar-Rāġib, سُجُود is at root lowering and humbling oneself, and is said of people, animals and lifeless things, while رُكُوع is bending — the posture in prayer, or humility in worship and outside it.

tellApart.bs: Sedždu činiti – čelom na zemlju; i pokornost svega stvorenog Allahu, htjelo ili ne htjelo → سَجَدَ; ruku' činiti, pregnuti se – položaj u namazu; u Kur'anu glagol samo o ljudima → رَكَعَ.
tellApart.en: To prostrate — the forehead to the ground; also the submission of all creation to Allah, willingly or not → سَجَدَ; to bow — the posture in prayer; in the Quran the verb is used only of people → رَكَعَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries سجد, ركع
notes: ar-Rāġib (سجد): the root of sujūd is lowering oneself and humility; it was made an expression of humility to Allah and worship; it is general to people, animals and lifeless things; two kinds: by choice — only of man, rewarded (53:62) — and of subjection (tasḫīr) — of man, animals and plants (13:15, 16:48), the silent testimony that they are created; 16:49 holds both kinds; in the Sharia it is specified for the known pillar of the prayer, and the Quran and thanks prostrations; on 2:34 he reports two views (Adam as qibla, or humility and service to him). (ركع): rukūʿ is bending; used sometimes for the specific posture in the prayer, sometimes for humility and lowering oneself, in worship or otherwise (22:77, 2:43, 2:125, 9:112).

That the verb رَكَعَ (5 uses in 4 ayat: 2:43, 3:43, 22:77, 77:48) is used only of people, while سَجَدَ is also said of shadows, creatures and the angels (13:15, 16:49, 22:18), is our observation. 2:34 and 55:6 are not cited (readings differ); 38:24 (Dāwūd, rākiʿan) is not cited.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnova je spuštanje i poniznost. Sedžda je dvojaka: svojevoljna – samo kod čovjeka, i za nju je nagrada – i sedžda pokornosti, kojom sve stvoreno, i ljudi, životinje i biljke, svjedoči da je stvoreno. U šerijatu je to poznati rukn namaza.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root is lowering oneself and humility. Prostration is of two kinds: by choice — only of man, and it is rewarded — and the prostration of subjection, by which all creation, people, animals and plants, testifies that it is created. In the Sharia it is the known pillar of the prayer.

why.bs: „Zato činite sedždu Allahu i Njemu ibadet činite!“ – ar-Rāġib: svojevoljna sedžda, za koju je nagrada.
why.en: “Rather prostrate yourselves before Allah and serve Him” — ar-Rāġib: prostration by choice, which is rewarded.

why.bs: „Allahu čini sedždu (pokorava se) svako na nebesima i na Zemlji, htio to ili ne, pa i njihove sjene“ – ar-Rāġib: sedžda pokornosti.
why.en: “And unto Allah falleth prostrate whosoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, as do their shadows” — ar-Rāġib: the prostration of subjection.

why.bs: „Allahu čini sedždu sve na nebesima i sve na Zemlji od bića koja se kreću, pa i meleki, i oni se ne uzoholjuju“ – ar-Rāġib: obje vrste sedžde u jednom ajetu.
why.en: “And unto Allah maketh prostration whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth of living creatures, and the angels (also) and they are not proud” — ar-Rāġib: both kinds in one ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, pregibanje: nekad poseban položaj u namazu, nekad poniznost i pokornost, u ibadetu ili izvan njega. U Kur'anu se glagol kaže samo za ljude, i uglavnom uz namaz i sedždu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, bending: sometimes the special posture in the prayer, sometimes humility and submission, in worship or outside it. In the Quran the verb is said only of people, and mostly together with the prayer and prostration.

why.bs: „…i činite ruku' s onima koji ruku' čine“ – mnogi mufessiri: ruku' u namazu s onima koji klanjaju.
why.en: “…and bow your heads with those who bow (in worship)” — many mufassirun: bowing in prayer with the worshippers.

why.bs: „O vi koji vjerujete, činite ruku' i sedždu i ibadet činite svome Gospodaru“ – oba položaja jedan za drugim.
why.en: “O ye who believe! Bow down and prostrate yourselves, and worship your Lord” — the two postures one after the other.

why.bs: „A kad im se kaže: Činite ruku'! – oni ruku' ne čine“ – odbijaju naredbu da ruku' učine.
why.en: “When it is said unto them: Bow down, they bow not down!” — they refuse the command to bow.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače baciti. Prema ar-Rāġibu, رَمْي se kaže za predmete poput strijele i kamena, a قَذْف je bacanje u daljinu; oba se prenesena značenja kažu i za vrijeđanje.
shared.en: Both verbs mean to throw. According to ar-Rāġib, رَمْي is said of objects such as an arrow or a stone, while قَذْف is throwing far; both are also used figuratively for insult.

tellApart.bs: Gađati, bacati nešto na nekoga – kamen, strijelu; i potvoriti nekoga (24:4) → رَمَى; hitnuti, baciti daleko ili snažno – u rijeku, strah u srca, istinu na laž → قَذَفَ.
tellApart.en: To throw something at someone — a stone, an arrow; also to accuse someone falsely (24:4) → رَمَى; to hurl, to throw far or with force — into the river, terror into hearts, truth upon falsehood → قَذَفَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رمى, قذف
notes: ar-Rāġib (رمى): ramy is said of objects such as an arrow and a stone (8:17); in speech it is a metonymy for abuse, like qaḏf (24:6, 24:4). (قذف): qaḏf is throwing far — hence a far dwelling is qaḏaf; 20:39 = throw him into it; 33:26, 34:48, 21:18, 37:8; qaḏf is borrowed for abuse and reproach as ramy is.

That the Quran uses رَمَى, never قَذَفَ, for the accusation of chaste women (24:4, 24:6, 24:23; 4:112) — the later legal term qaḏf notwithstanding — is our observation. 8:17: the throw of a handful of earth at Badr; tafsir differs little on it, and it is not a reproach.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, kaže se za predmete poput strijele i kamena; u govoru je prenesen izraz za vrijeđanje. U kur'anskoj upotrebi upravo se ovim glagolom, a ne s قَذَفَ, kaže potvaranje čestitih žena (24:4).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, said of objects such as an arrow or a stone; in speech it is a figurative term for insult. In Quranic usage it is this verb, not قَذَفَ, that names the false accusation of chaste women (24:4).

why.bs: „Ti nisi bacio kad si bacio, već je bacio Allah“ (kako Njemu priliči) – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet za bacanje predmeta; mufesiri: šaka prašine na Bedru.
why.en: “And thou (Muhammad) threwest not when thou didst throw, but Allah threw” (as befits Him) — ar-Rāġib cites it for throwing an object; mufassirun: the handful of dust at Badr.

why.bs: „Koje su ih gađale kamenjem od pečene gline“ – gađanje predmetom.
why.en: “Which pelted them with stones of baked clay” — throwing an object at a target.

why.bs: „A oni koji potvaraju čestite žene…“ – ar-Rāġib: رَمْي u govoru, kao vrijeđanje.
why.en: “And those who accuse honourable women…” — ar-Rāġib: رَمْي in speech, as abuse.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, bacanje u daljinu; otuda i daleko mjesto se zove قَذَف. U Kur'anu Musaova majka ga baca u rijeku, Allah ubacuje strah u srca neprijatelja i baca istinu na laž.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, throwing far; hence a distant place is called قَذَف. In the Quran Moses' mother casts him into the river, Allah casts terror into the hearts of the enemy, and hurls the truth against falsehood.

why.bs: „Baci ga u kovčeg, pa ga baci u rijeku“ – ar-Rāġib: baci ga u nju.
why.en: “Throw him into the ark, and throw it into the river” — ar-Rāġib: throw him into it.

why.bs: „…i ubacio je strah u njihova srca“ – bacanje preneseno na ono što obuzme iznutra.
why.en: “…and cast panic into their hearts” — casting said of what seizes from within.

why.bs: „Naprotiv, Mi istinu bacamo na laž, pa joj ona smrska glavu“ – snažan udar.
why.en: “Nay, but We hurl the true against the false, and it doth break its head” — a forceful hurl.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače nešto teško što se nosi. Prema ar-Rāġibu, وِزْر je težina, nazvana po planinskom skloništu (وَزَر), i njime se izražava grijeh, kao što se izražava i težinom (ثِقْل).
shared.en: Both words mean a heavy thing that is carried. According to ar-Rāġib, وِزْر is weight, named after a mountain refuge (وَزَر), and sin is expressed by it, as it is also expressed by heaviness (ثِقْل).

tellApart.bs: Breme – u Kur'anu najčešće grijeh koji čovjek nosi; niko neće nositi tuđe breme → وِزْر; teret – u Kur'anu najčešće tjelesni tovar, a jednom i grijesi (29:13) → ثَقَل / أَثْقَال.
tellApart.en: Burden — in the Quran mostly the sin a person carries; no one bears another's burden → وِزْر; load — in the Quran mostly a physical load, and once sins (29:13) → ثَقَل / أَثْقَال.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries وزر, ثقل
notes: ar-Rāġib (وزر): wazar is the refuge one takes in a mountain (75:11); wizr is heaviness, by comparison with the mountain's wazar, and sin is expressed by it as it is by ṯiql (16:25, like 29:13); bearing another's wizr is as in the hadith of whoever starts a bad practice — the like of their burden; 6:164 'no bearer bears another's burden' in the sense that it is not lifted off the other; awzār of war are its weapons; 20:87 awzār of the people's ornament. (ثقل): ṯiql and ḫiffa are opposites; at root of bodies, then of meanings (a debt or a wizr weighs one down); 16:7 your heavy loads; 29:13 their sins that weigh them down, like 16:25; on 99:2 it has been said her treasures, and it has been said the bodies of men at the resurrection.

Corpus: the lemma ثَقَل includes its broken plural أَثْقَال and the dual الثَّقَلَان (55:31, men and jinn) — summed by the corpus. That وِزْر means sin in most of its places (6:31, 6:164, 16:25, 17:15, 20:100, 35:18, 39:7, 53:38) and something else in 20:87 (loads of ornaments) and 47:4 (war's burdens) is our observation. 94:2 (said to the Prophet; readings differ) is not cited.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, težina – nazvana po planinskom skloništu – kojom se izražava grijeh. U kur'anskoj upotrebi najčešće grijeh koji čovjek nosi na Sudnjem danu; nositi tuđe breme znači, kaže on, nositi isto toliko, a da se drugome ne skida.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, weight — named after a mountain refuge — by which sin is expressed. In Quranic usage mostly the sin a person carries on the Day of Resurrection; bearing another's burden means, he says, bearing as much again, without its being lifted off the other.

why.bs: „…i nijedan nosilac bremena neće nositi tuđe breme“ – grijeh se ne prenosi s jednog na drugog.
why.en: “…nor doth any laden bear another's load (وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ)” — sin does not pass from one to another.

why.bs: „Da bi na Sudnjem danu nosili svoja bremena u potpunosti, i dio bremena onih koje bez znanja zavode“ – ar-Rāġib: kao 29:13.
why.en: “That they may bear their burdens undiminished on the Day of Resurrection, with somewhat of the burdens of those whom they mislead” — ar-Rāġib: like 29:13.

why.bs: „…nego smo bili natovareni bremenima od nakita naroda“ – breme u doslovnom smislu.
why.en: “…but we were laden with burdens of ornaments of the folk” — burdens in the literal sense.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, težina je u osnovi svojstvo tijela, a onda se kaže i za značenja – za dug i grijeh koji pritišću. U Kur'anu أَثْقَال su najčešće tovari koje nose životinje ili Zemlja, a jednom grijesi (29:13).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, heaviness is at root a property of bodies, and is then said of meanings — of a debt or a sin that weighs one down. In the Quran أَثْقَال are mostly loads carried by animals or by the earth, and once sins (29:13).

why.bs: „I nose vaše terete do mjesta…“ – ar-Rāġib: vaši teški tovari.
why.en: “And they bear your loads for you unto a land…” — ar-Rāġib: your heavy loads.

why.bs: „A zaista će nositi svoje terete, i druge terete uz svoje terete“ – ar-Rāġib: grijesi koji ih pritišću.
why.en: “But they verily will bear their own loads and other loads beside their own” — ar-Rāġib: the sins that weigh them down.

why.bs: „I kad zemlja izbaci svoje terete“ – ar-Rāġib prenosi dva tumačenja: njena blaga, ili tijela umrlih pri proživljenju.
why.en: “And Earth yieldeth up her burdens (أَثْقَالَهَا)” — ar-Rāġib reports two readings: its treasures, or the bodies of the dead at the resurrection.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o tome da čovjek drži sebe u vlasti. Razlikuju se po tome šta se drži i kada: duša na onome što traže razum i vjera, narav koja ne da srdžbi da se uzburka, ili srdžba koja se već podigla pa se zadržava.
shared.en: All three words speak of a person holding himself in check. They differ in what is held and when: the soul kept to what reason and the Law require, a nature that does not let anger stir, or anger already risen that is held in.

tellApart.bs: Držati dušu na onome što traže razum i vjera, opća riječ → صَبْر; narav koja obuzdava dušu da se srdžba ne uzburka → حَلِيم; zadržati u sebi srdžbu ili tjeskobu koja se već podigla, kao što se zadržava dah → كَاظِم.
tellApart.en: Keeping the soul to what reason and the Law require, the general word → صَبْر; a nature that restrains the soul so that anger does not stir → حَلِيم; holding in an anger or distress already risen, as breath is held → كَاظِم.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries صبر, حلم, كظم
notes: ar-Rāġib (صبر): ṣabr is holding back in narrowness; restraining the soul to what reason and the Law require, or from what they require it to be kept from; a general word whose names differ by situation (in calamity ṣabr, against jazaʿ; in battle courage; in an irksome affair 'breadth of breast'; in holding speech kitmān), and Allah called all of it ṣabr (2:177). (حلم): ḥilm is controlling the soul and nature against the stirring of anger; 11:75 Ibrāhīm ḥalīm; 37:101 ġulām ḥalīm = one in whom the strength of ḥilm was found; aḥlām in 52:32 'it was said' = minds, which he says is not its real meaning. (كظم): kaẓm is the outlet of breath, kuẓūm the holding of breath; kaẓm al-ġayẓ is holding anger in (3:134); 68:48 makẓūm.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 15 places read): حَلِيم is said of Allah in 11 places (always beside another Name: غَفُور, غَنِيّ, عَلِيم, شَكُور), of Ibrāhīm (9:114, 11:75), of the boy given to him (37:101), and of Šuʿayb by his mocking people (11:87). The gloss 'He does not hasten punishment' for Allah's ḥilm is the mufassirun's, not ar-Rāġib's entry. كَاظِم is 2× (3:134, 40:18); كَظِيم (12:84, 16:58, 43:17) is a different lemma and not counted.

al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, držati dušu na onome što traže razum i vjera, ili je držati podalje od onoga od čega oni traže da se čuva. To je opća riječ: u nesreći je to strpljenje, u borbi hrabrost, u govoru čuvanje tajne – a Allah je sve to nazvao strpljenjem.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, keeping the soul to what reason and the Law require, or away from what they require it to be kept from. It is a general word: in calamity it is patience, in battle courage, in speech keeping a secret — and Allah called all of it patience.

why.bs: „I tražite pomoć strpljenjem i namazom.“
why.en: “Seek help in patience and prayer.”

why.bs: Talutovi vojnici pred Džalutom: „Gospodaru naš, prelij nas strpljenjem i učini čvrstim korake naše“ – strpljenje u borbi, koje ar-Rāġib naziva i hrabrošću.
why.en: Saul's soldiers facing Goliath: “Our Lord! Bestow on us endurance (صَبْرًا), make our foothold sure” — patience in battle, which ar-Rāġib also calls courage.

why.bs: Jakub, kad su mu donijeli košulju s lažnom krvlju: „Lijepo strpljenje!“
why.en: Jacob, when the shirt with false blood was brought to him: “(My course is) comely patience.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḥilm je ovladavanje duše i naravi nad uzburkavanjem srdžbe; za obećanog dječaka kaže da je u njemu bila snaga blagosti. To upućuje na osobinu, a ne na trenutni napor (naše zapažanje). Blagim Kur'an naziva Ibrahima i dječaka koji mu je obećan, a najčešće Allaha, kako Njemu priliči: mufessiri to objašnjavaju time da On ne požuruje s kaznom.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ḥilm is the soul and nature mastering the stirring of anger; of the promised boy he says the strength of ḥilm was found in him. This suggests a trait rather than a moment's effort (our observation). The Quran calls Abraham and the boy promised to him forbearing, and most often Allah, as befits Him: the mufassirun explain it as His not hastening punishment.

why.bs: „Ibrahim je zaista bio blag, skrušen i pokajan“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Lo! Abraham was mild (لَحَلِيمٌ), imploring, penitent” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Pa smo ga obradovali blagim dječakom“ – ar-Rāġib: dječak u kome je bila snaga blagosti.
why.en: “So We gave him tidings of a gentle son (حَلِيمٍ)” — ar-Rāġib: one in whom the strength of forbearance was found.

why.bs: „Lijepa riječ i opraštanje bolji su nego sadaka za kojom slijedi uznemiravanje; a Allah je Neovisan i Blag“ – blagost kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “A kind word with forgiveness is better than almsgiving followed by injury. Allah is Absolute, Clement (حَلِيمٌ)” — forbearance as befits Him.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, kaẓm je izvorno mjesto kuda izlazi dah, a kuẓūm zadržavanje daha; zato kaẓm al-ġayẓ znači zadržati srdžbu u sebi, ne pustiti je van. Srdžba je već tu – suzdržava se njeno izbijanje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, kaẓm is at root the outlet of breath, and kuẓūm the holding of breath; so kaẓm al-ġayẓ is to hold anger in, not letting it out. The anger is already there — what is held back is its breaking out.

why.bs: „I koji suzdržavaju srdžbu i opraštaju ljudima – a Allah voli one koji čine dobro“ (Njegova ljubav kako Njemu priliči) – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Those who control their wrath and are forgiving toward mankind; Allah loveth the good” (His love as befits Him) — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Na Dan koji se približava, „kad srca budu kod grla, a oni se jedva suzdržavaju“ – mnogi mufessiri to shvataju kao zadržanu tugu, poput zadržanog daha.
why.en: On the Day of the approaching (doom), “when the hearts will be choking the throats” — many mufassirun understand it as grief held in, like held breath.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o neuspjehu. Razlikuju se po tome da li se gubi ono što se već imalo ili se promašuje ono čemu se težilo.
shared.en: Both words speak of failure. They differ in whether one loses what one already had or misses what one was seeking.

tellApart.bs: Izgubiti od onoga što se imalo – kapital, a u Kur'anu samoga sebe i nagradu → خَسِرَ; ostati bez onoga čemu se težilo i nadalo → خَابَ.
tellApart.en: To lose from what one had — capital, and in the Quran one's own self and reward → خَسِرَ; to miss what one sought and hoped for → خَابَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries خسر, خاب
notes: ar-Rāġib (خسر): ḫusr / ḫusrān is the diminishing of capital, said of a man (ḫasira fulān) and of his deed (his trade lost); used of outward acquisitions such as wealth and standing in this world, which is most common, and of inner ones such as health, soundness, reason, faith and reward — which Allah made 'the manifest loss' (39:15); every ḫusrān Allah mentions in the Quran is in this latter sense, not worldly trade. (خاب): ḫayba is missing what was sought (fawt aṭ-ṭalab), with 14:15, 20:61, 91:10.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 16 / 4 places read): the object of خَسِرَ is 'themselves' (أَنْفُسَهُم) in 8 places (6:12, 6:20, 7:9, 7:53, 11:21, 23:103, 39:15, 42:45); خَابَ is said of the tyrant (14:15), the one who invents a lie (20:61), the one who carries wrongdoing (20:111) and the one who corrupts his soul (91:10). 22:11 (ḫasira d-dunyā wa-l-āḫira) is not cited: it names this world too, against ar-Rāġib's general remark.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, gubitak je umanjenje glavnice – kao u trgovini. Kaže se za imetak i ugled na ovom svijetu, ali i za zdravlje, razum, vjerovanje i nagradu; on kaže da je svaki gubitak koji Allah spominje u Kur'anu ove druge vrste. U Kur'anu se često gube ‚sami sebe‘.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, loss is the diminishing of capital — as in trade. It is said of wealth and standing in this world, but also of health, reason, faith and reward; he says every loss Allah mentions in the Quran is of this second kind. In the Quran people often lose ‘themselves’.

why.bs: „Gubitnici su, doista, oni koji će na Sudnjem danu izgubiti same sebe i svoje porodice. Eto, to je očit gubitak!“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “The losers will be those who lose themselves and their housefolk on the Day of Resurrection. Ah, that will be the manifest loss!” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A oni čije vage budu lake – to su oni koji su sami sebe izgubili.“
why.en: “And as for those whose scale is light: those are they who lose their souls.”

why.bs: „Na gubitku su, zaista, oni koji poriču susret s Allahom.“
why.en: “They indeed are losers who deny their meeting with Allah.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḫayba je promašiti ono čemu se težilo. Naglasak je na nadi koja se ne ostvari, a ne na glavnici koja se smanjuje (naše zapažanje). U Kur'anu (4×) se kaže za silnika, lažca, nepravednika i onoga ko svoju dušu grijesima zaprlja.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ḫayba is missing what one sought. The stress falls on the hope that does not come, not on a stock that shrinks (our observation). In the Quran (4×) it is said of the tyrant, the liar, the wrongdoer and the one who corrupts his soul.

why.bs: „I tražili su pobjedu, a razočaran ostade svaki tvrdoglavi silnik“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And they sought help (from their Lord) and every froward potentate was bought to naught” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A bez uspjeha ostaje onaj ko je zaprlja (dušu)“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And he is indeed a failure who stunteth it” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Musa vračarima: „Ne izmišljajte laž o Allahu … a bez uspjeha je ostao ko god izmišlja.“
why.en: Moses to the magicians: “Invent not a lie against Allah … He who lieth faileth miserably.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače mjesto gdje leže mrtvi. U Kur'anu se razlikuju po prizoru u kojem stoje.
shared.en: Both words mean the place where the dead lie. In the Quran they differ in the scene in which they stand.

tellApart.bs: Mjesto gdje mrtvi borave – i na ovom svijetu i pri proživljenju → قَبْر; grobišta iz kojih ljudi izlaze na Sudnji dan – sva tri puta → أَجْدَاث.
tellApart.en: The place where the dead stay — in this world and at the raising → قَبْر; the burial places people come out of on the Day of Resurrection — all three times → أَجْدَاث.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries قبر, جدث
notes: ar-Rāġib (قبر): qabr is the resting place of the dead; qabartuhu = I put him in the grave, aqbartuhu = I gave him a place to be buried (80:21, 'it was said': taught how to bury); 102:2 'you visited the graveyards' = death; 82:4 points to the raising, 'and it was said' to the uncovering of secrets; 35:22 'those in the graves' = those who are as the dead. (جدث): only that ajdāṯ is the plural of jadaṯ (also jadaf), with 70:43 and 36:51.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 6 / 3 places read): قَبْر is said of a grave in this world (9:84, 60:13) and of the raising (22:7, 82:4, 100:9), and figuratively in 35:22; أَجْدَاث is in all three places what people come out of at the Resurrection (36:51, 54:7, 70:43). The contrast is our own observation; ar-Rāġib's جدث entry gives no meaning beyond the plural. 9:84 (addressed to the Prophet) is not cited.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: his 'points to the raising' is on 100:9 (bi'ṯira mā fī l-qubūr), not 82:4; 'in haste' only for 36:51 and 70:43, not 54:7.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, mjesto gdje mrtvi borave. U Kur'anu se spominje i grob na ovom svijetu i proživljenje iz grobova; ar-Rāġib kaže da 100:9 ukazuje na proživljenje, a navodi i mišljenje da se misli na otkrivanje tajni.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the resting place of the dead. The Quran speaks both of a grave in this world and of the raising from the graves; ar-Rāġib says 100:9 points to the raising, and also reports the view that it means the uncovering of secrets.

why.bs: „…i da će Allah proživjeti one koji su u grobovima.“
why.en: “…and because Allah will raise those who are in the graves.”

why.bs: „I kad grobovi budu ispreturani“ – proživljenje iz grobova.
why.en: “And the sepulchres (الْقُبُورُ) are overturned” — the raising from the graves.

why.bs: „Zar on ne zna – kad bude izvrnuto ono što je u grobovima…“ – ar-Rāġib: ukazuje na proživljenje.
why.en: “Knoweth he not that, when the contents of the graves are poured forth…” — ar-Rāġib: it points to the raising.

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib kaže samo da je to množina od jadaṯ. U Kur'anu sva tri puta stoji u istom prizoru: na Sudnji dan ljudi izlaze iz grobišta (žurno, u 36:51 i 70:43) – to je naše zapažanje o kur'anskoj upotrebi.
nuance.en: Ar-Rāġib says only that it is the plural of jadaṯ. In the Quran all three times it stands in the same scene: on the Day of Resurrection people come out of the burial places (hastening, in 36:51 and 70:43) — this is our observation of Quranic usage.

why.bs: „I kad se zapuše u rog, oni će, gle, iz grobišta pohrliti ka svome Gospodaru“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And the trumpet is blown and lo! from the graves (مِّنَ الْأَجْدَاثِ) they hie unto their Lord” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Na Dan kada će iz grobišta izlaziti žureći“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “The day when they come forth from the graves (الْأَجْدَاثِ) in haste” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Oborenih pogleda izlazit će iz grobišta kao da su raštrkani skakavci.“
why.en: “With downcast eyes, they come forth from the graves (الْأَجْدَاثِ) as they were locusts spread abroad.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače da nešto više nije manjkavo. Prema ar-Rāġibu, mjerilo je različito: kod prve da stvari ništa izvana ne treba, kod druge da je postignuto ono radi čega stvar postoji.
shared.en: Both words mean that a thing is no longer lacking. According to ar-Rāġib, the measure differs: for the first that the thing needs nothing outside itself, for the second that what it exists for has been attained.

tellApart.bs: Dovesti do granice gdje stvari ništa izvana ne treba – broj, rok, obred, blagodat → أَتَمَّ; dovesti do toga da je postignuta svrha stvari → أَكْمَلَ (2×; u 5:3 oba glagola stoje jedan uz drugi).
tellApart.en: To bring to the point where the thing needs nothing outside itself — a number, a term, a rite, a favour → أَتَمَّ; to bring it to where its purpose is attained → أَكْمَلَ (2×; in 5:3 the two verbs stand side by side).

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries تمام, كمل
notes: ar-Rāġib (تمام): a thing's tamām is its reaching a limit where it needs nothing outside itself, and the lacking (nāqiṣ) is what needs something outside itself; said of the counted and the measured (a complete number, a complete night); with 6:115, 61:8, 7:142. (كمل): kamāl of a thing is the attaining of what is the purpose of it; 2:233 'two full years' — the utmost on which the child's welfare depends; 16:25 'their burdens in full' — the full measure of punishment; 2:196 'ten complete' — two views reported with 'qīla'.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 16 / 2 places read): أَتَمَّ is said of Allah's light (9:32; the participle مُتِمّ in 61:8 is another lemma) and favour (5:3, 12:6, 48:2), of rites (2:196), the fast (2:187), a covenant's term (9:4), nights and years (7:142, 28:27), and Abraham's fulfilling the words he was tested with (2:124, not cited: readings differ); أَكْمَلَ is only 2:185 (the number of days) and 5:3 (the religion). In 5:3 the religion is 'perfected' and the favour 'completed'; we do not put a reason for the choice in ar-Rāġib's mouth.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, stvar je potpuna (tāmm) kad dođe do granice na kojoj joj ništa izvana ne treba, a manjkava je ona kojoj nešto izvana treba; kaže se za ono što se broji i mjeri. U Kur'anu se upotpunjuju broj noći, obredi hadža, post i Allahova blagodat.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a thing is complete (tāmm) when it reaches the limit at which it needs nothing outside itself, and lacking when it needs something outside; it is said of what is counted and measured. In the Quran a number of nights, the rites of Hajj, the fast and Allah's favour are completed.

why.bs: „I Musau smo odredili trideset noći, a upotpunili smo ih s još deset, pa se navršio rok njegova Gospodara – četrdeset noći“ – broj kojem više ništa ne treba; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And when We did appoint for Moses thirty nights (of solitude), and added to them ten (وَأَتْمَمْنَاهَا بِعَشْرٍ), and he completed the whole time appointed by his Lord of forty nights” — a number needing nothing more; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I upotpunite, Allaha radi, hadž i umru.“
why.en: “Perform (وَأَتِمُّوا) the pilgrimage and the visit (to Makka) for Allah.”

why.bs: „… i upotpunio sam vam Svoju blagodat …“ – u istom ajetu vjera je ‚usavršena‘ (أَكْمَلْتُ).
why.en: “… and completed My favour unto you …” — in the same ayah the religion is ‘perfected’ (أَكْمَلْتُ).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, savršenstvo (kamāl) stvari je da se postigne ono što je njena svrha. Tako „dvije pune godine“ dojenja (2:233) znače, kaže on, krajnje do čega ide djetetova dobrobit. Glagol je u Kur'anu samo dva puta.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the perfection (kamāl) of a thing is the attaining of what is its purpose. So the “two whole years” of nursing (2:233) mean, he says, the utmost on which the child's welfare depends. The verb occurs only twice in the Quran.

why.bs: „Danas sam vam usavršio vašu vjeru …“ – a blagodat ‚upotpunio‘ (أَتْمَمْتُ) u istom ajetu.
why.en: “This day have I perfected your religion for you …” — and the favour ‘completed’ (أَتْمَمْتُ) in the same ayah.

why.bs: „… i da biste broj (dana) usavršili i veličali Allaha zato što vas je uputio.“
why.en: “… that ye should complete the period (وَلِتُكْمِلُوا الْعِدَّةَ), and that ye should magnify Allah for having guided you.”

shared.bs: Sve četiri riječi znače ono što ukazuje na istinu. Prema ar-Rāġibu, razlikuju se po načinu ukazivanja: vidljivo koje upućuje na nevidljivo, najčvršći dokaz, jasno ukazivanje razumom ili osjetilima, i dokaz koji pokazuje pravi put i potvrđuje jednu od dvije suprotne tvrdnje.
shared.en: All four words mean what points to the truth. According to ar-Rāġib, they differ in how they point: the seen that leads to the unseen, the firmest proof, a clear indication by reason or the senses, and a proof that shows the straight way and settles which of two contraries is sound.

tellApart.bs: Vidljiv znak koji je nerazdvojno vezan za nešto što se ne vidi (i ajet Kur'ana) → آيَة; najčvršći dokaz, koji uvijek vodi istini → بُرْهَان; jasno ukazivanje, razumsko ili osjetilno (i svjedoci) → بَيِّنَة; argument koji pokazuje ispravan put u sporu – zove se tako i kad je oboren → حُجَّة.
tellApart.en: A visible sign inseparably joined to something unseen (and a verse of the Quran) → آيَة; the firmest proof, one that always leads to truth → بُرْهَان; a clear indication, by reason or by the senses (also witnesses) → بَيِّنَة; an argument showing the right way in a dispute — so called even when refuted → حُجَّة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries أي, بره, بان, حج
notes: ar-Rāġib (أي): āya is the evident sign; in truth anything apparent that is inseparable from something not apparent, so that whoever perceives the one knows the other — in sensibles and intelligibles (a made thing tells of a maker); every passage of the Quran indicating a ruling, or separated by a verbal break, is an āya; 23:50: 'āya', not 'two āyas', because each became a sign through the other; 29:49. (بره): burhān is the making-plain of a proof (bayān li-l-ḥujja); 'some' derive it from bariha, to be white; it is the firmest of proofs (awkad al-adilla), the one that always entails truth, in his scale of five kinds of indication; with 2:111, 21:24, 4:174. (بان): bayyina is the clear indication, rational or sensible; two witnesses are called bayyina (the hadith 'the bayyina is on the claimant'); with 'a-fa-man kāna ʿalā bayyina min rabbihi' and 8:42. (حج): ḥujja is the indication that makes plain the maḥajja, the straight goal, and entails the soundness of one of two contradictories; 6:149; in 2:150 what the wrongdoers argue with is excepted from ḥujja though it is none, or it is so called as in 42:16 'their argument is refuted'.

Counts: آيَة (382) includes every use, the Quranic verse as well as the sign; بَيِّنَة counts the singular and its plural بَيِّنَات as the corpus files them. 12:24 (burhān rabbihi) is not cited: tafsir differs widely on what Joseph saw.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 6 flags, fixed: ḥujja is 'argument', burhān 'proof' (no shared word); 'Produce your proof' is said to those who claim without evidence (Jews and Christians in 2:111, idolaters in 21:24, 27:64); 29:49 'the Quran' as many mufassirun explain; 30:21 bs 'supruge'; 28:32 no longer draws on the staff of 28:31; 42:16 bs keeps the passive.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries أي, بره, بان, حج (2026-11-06): 35 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): His definition of ḥujja is not about dispute; disputing is muḥājja, discussed later in the entry; members/2/nuance (reworded): The she-camel example is not in his entry; it reads as his continuation. 7:73 itself calls her bayyina, so mark it as Quranic usage; members/3/nuance (reworded): Minor: 'in debate' is not part of his definition; he does say what they argue with (mā yaḥtajjūna bihi) is called ḥujja

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, jasan znak: nešto vidljivo što je nerazdvojno vezano za nešto nevidljivo, pa ko spozna prvo, zna i drugo – kao što stvoreno govori o Stvoritelju. Ajetom se zove i svaki odlomak Kur'ana koji ukazuje na propis ili je odvojen stankom.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a clear sign: something seen that is inseparably joined to something unseen, so that whoever grasps the first knows the second — as a made thing tells of its Maker. Every passage of the Quran that indicates a ruling or is set off by a break is also called a verse (āya).

why.bs: „I sina Merjemina i njegovu majku učinili smo znakom“ – ar-Rāġib: rečeno je ‚znakom‘, a ne ‚dvama znakovima‘, jer je svako od njih znak po onom drugom.
why.en: “And We made the son of Mary and his mother a portent (آيَةً)” — ar-Rāġib: ‘a sign’, not ‘two signs’, because each became a sign through the other.

why.bs: „Ne, on je (mnogi mufessiri kažu: Kur'an) niz jasnih ajeta u prsima onih kojima je dano znanje“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “But it [the Quran, as many mufassirun explain] is clear revelations in the hearts of those who have been given knowledge” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Među Njegovim znakovima je i to što vam je od vaše vlastite vrste stvorio parove, da biste kod njih nalazili smiraj.“
why.en: “And of His signs is this: He created for you helpmeets from yourselves that ye might find rest in them.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, burhān je razjašnjenje dokaza i najčvršći od svih dokaza – onaj koji uvijek vodi istini. U Kur'anu se četiri puta onima koji tvrde bez dokaza kaže da donesu svoj dokaz.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, burhān is the making-plain of a proof and the firmest of all proofs — the one that always leads to truth. Four times in the Quran those who make a claim without evidence are told to bring their proof.

why.bs: „Reci: Donesite svoj dokaz ako govorite istinu!“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Say: Bring your proof (of what ye state) if ye are truthful” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „O ljudi, došao vam je dokaz od vašeg Gospodara“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “O mankind! Now hath a proof from your Lord come unto you” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Musau, kad je izvukao ruku bijelu: „To su dva dokaza od tvoga Gospodara faraonu i njegovim glavešinama.“
why.en: To Moses, as he drew out his hand white: “Then these shall be two proofs from your Lord unto Pharaoh and his chiefs.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, jasno ukazivanje, bilo razumsko bilo osjetilno; zato se i dva svjedoka zovu bayyina. U Kur'anu je kamila poslana Semudu takvo svjedočanstvo (7:73) koje se vidi očima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a clear indication, whether by reason or by the senses; so two witnesses are also called bayyina. In the Quran the she-camel sent to Thamūd is such evidence (7:73), seen with the eyes.

why.bs: Salih: „Došlo vam je očigledno svjedočanstvo od vašeg Gospodara: ovo je Allahova deva, vama kao znak“ – svjedočanstvo osjetilima.
why.en: Ṣāliḥ: “A wonder (بَيِّنَةٌ) from your Lord hath come unto you. Lo! this is the camel of Allah, a token unto you” — evidence to the senses.

why.bs: „… da propadne onaj ko propadne nakon očiglednog svjedočanstva, i da živi onaj ko živi nakon očiglednog svjedočanstva“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… that he who perished (on that day) might perish by a clear proof (of His Sovereignty) and he who survived might survive by a clear proof” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, argument koji upućuje na ispravan put i zahtijeva da je od dvije suprotne tvrdnje jedna tačna – a ḥujjom se može zvati i ono čime se ljudi argumentiraju. Kur'an argumentom naziva i oboreni argument nevjernika (42:16).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the argument that points the right way and requires that of two contrary claims one is sound — and what people argue with may also be called ḥujja. The Quran also calls the disbelievers' refuted plea an argument (42:16).

why.bs: „Reci: Allahov je konačni argument“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Say - For Allah's is the final argument” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A oni koji se o Allahu prepiru nakon što Mu je odgovoreno – njihov je argument ništavan kod njihova Gospodara“ – ar-Rāġib: i oboreni se zove argumentom.
why.en: “And those who argue concerning Allah after He hath been acknowledged, their argument hath no weight with their Lord” — ar-Rāġib: even a refuted one is called an argument.

why.bs: „Eto, taj Naš argument dali smo Ibrahimu protiv njegovog naroda.“
why.en: “That is Our argument. We gave it unto Abraham against his folk.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače ono što se jede od biljaka i drveća. Razlikuju se po tome da li se plod gleda kao prinos i opskrba, ili kao voće koje se iznosi, u Kur'anu najčešće u Džennetu.
shared.en: Both words mean what is eaten from plants and trees. They differ in whether it is seen as yield and provision, or as fruit set out to eat, in the Quran mostly in Paradise.

tellApart.bs: Ono što daje drvo, kao prinos i opskrba, a u prenesenom smislu svaka korist koja iz nečega proizlazi → ثَمَرَة; voće – jedinski oblik dolazi jedanaest puta, a u devet njih je u opisu Dženneta → فَاكِهَة.
tellApart.en: What a tree yields, as produce and provision, and figuratively any benefit that comes from a thing → ثَمَرَة; fruit — the singular occurs eleven times, nine of them describing Paradise → فَاكِهَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ثمر, فكه
notes: ar-Rāġib (ثمر): ṯamar is a name for all that is eaten of the yields of trees; one is ṯamara, plurals ṯimār and ṯamarāt ('fa-aḫraǧa bihi mina ṯ-ṯamarāti rizqan lakum', 16:67, 6:99); of ṯamar 'it was said' it is ṯimār, and 'it was said' its plural, and it is used figuratively for acquired wealth — so Ibn ʿAbbās read 18:34 'wa-kāna lahu ṯamar'; any benefit coming from a thing is its ṯamara (the fruit of knowledge is good deeds). (فكه): fākiha 'it was said' is all fruits, and 'it was said' fruits except grapes and pomegranates — whoever said so looked at their being named apart and joined to it (he cites no verse here; cf. 55:68); fukāha is the pleasant talk of companions; 56:65 tafakkahūn read two ways.

The member sums the corpus lemmas ثَمَرَة (17, mostly the plural ثَمَرَات) and ثَمَر (5). Quranic usage (our observation, all 11 places read): فَاكِهَة describes Paradise in 9 places (36:57, 38:51, 43:73, 44:55, 52:22, 55:52, 55:68, 56:20, 56:32) and the earth's produce in 55:11 and 80:31; the plural فَوَاكِه is another lemma and not counted.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 5 flags, fixed: 'nine of eleven' is of the singular فَاكِهَة only (the plural fawākih not counted); ثَمَرَة is 'produce', not 'fruit'; Ibn ʿAbbās 'understood' 18:34 (not a reading); 80:31 no longer borrows 80:32.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries ثمر, فكه (2026-11-06): 15 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): Plain-string note; the fix is given under 'en'. He does not cite 55:68 — the fākiha verses he cites are 56:20, 56:32, 80:31, 37:42, 77:42; members/1/nuance (reworded): The reason is the second view's (he says its holder 'seemingly looked at' the separate mention); he cites no verse, so 55:68 is ours

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ime za sve što se jede od onoga što drveće daje. Prenosi se i na imetak (tako je Ibn Abbas razumio 18:34) i na svaku korist koja iz nečega proizlazi – ‚plod znanja je dobro djelo‘. U Kur'anu plodovi su najčešće opskrba (رِزْق) koju Allah izvodi kišom.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a name for all that is eaten of what trees yield. It is carried over to wealth (so Ibn ʿAbbās understood 18:34) and to any benefit that comes from a thing — ‘the fruit of knowledge is good deeds’. In the Quran produce is mostly provision (رِزْق) that Allah brings forth with rain.

why.bs: „… i spustio je s neba vodu pa njome izveo plodove kao opskrbu za vas“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ove riječi.
why.en: “… and causeth water to pour down from the sky, thereby producing fruits (مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ) as food for you” — ar-Rāġib quotes these words.

why.bs: „Pogledajte njegov plod kad zarodi, i njegovo sazrijevanje!“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Look upon the fruit thereof, when they bear fruit, and upon its ripening” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I imao je plodova (ثَمَر)“ – ar-Rāġib prenosi da je Ibn Abbas to razumio kao imetak.
why.en: “And he had fruit (ثَمَر)” — ar-Rāġib reports that Ibn ʿAbbās understood it as wealth.

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib prenosi dva mišljenja: da su to svi plodovi, ili svi osim grožđa i šipka, drugo jer se ta dva spominju posebno uz voće – u Kur'anu u 55:68. Jedinski oblik ‚voće‘ u Kur'anu dolazi jedanaest puta, a u devet njih je u opisu Dženneta.
nuance.en: Ar-Rāġib reports two views: that it is all fruits, or all except grapes and pomegranates, the second because these two are named apart beside it — in the Quran in 55:68. The singular ‘fruit’ occurs eleven times in the Quran, nine of them in the description of Paradise.

why.bs: „U njima su voće, i palme, i šipci“ – na ovome počiva mišljenje da voće ne obuhvata šipak.
why.en: “Wherein is fruit, the date-palm and pomegranate” — the view that fruit excludes the pomegranate rests on this.

why.bs: „U njemu za vas ima mnogo voća od kojeg ćete jesti“ – voće u Džennetu.
why.en: “Therein for you is fruit in plenty whence to eat” — fruit in Paradise.

why.bs: „I voće i trava“ – mjesto gdje je voće ovoga svijeta, a ne Dženneta.
why.en: “And fruits and grasses” — a place where fruit is of this world, not of Paradise.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o djelu koje više ništa ne vrijedi. Razlikuju se po obliku i po tome šta se poništava: prva kaže da su djela sama propala, druga da se nešto čini ništavnim.
shared.en: Both words speak of a deed that is no longer worth anything. They differ in form and in what is voided: the first says the deeds themselves have come to nothing, the second that something is made void.

tellApart.bs: Djela su propala – postala bezvrijedna zbog onoga što ih kvari (nevjerovanje, rđava namjera, pretegnuta loša djela); u Kur'anu uvijek o djelima → حَبِطَ; poništiti nešto, učiniti ga ništavnim – milostinju, djela, sihr, neistinu → أَبْطَلَ.
tellApart.en: Deeds have become worthless — through what spoils them (disbelief, a wrong intention, outweighing bad deeds); in the Quran always of deeds → حَبِطَ; to invalidate a thing, make it void — charity, deeds, magic, falsehood → أَبْطَلَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حبط, بطل
notes: ar-Rāġib (حبط): ḥabṭ of deeds is of kinds: (1) worldly deeds that avail nothing at the Resurrection (25:23 'scattered dust'); (2) deeds of the Hereafter not done for Allah's face (the report of the man who recited the Quran to be called a reciter); (3) good deeds against which there are bad deeds that outweigh them — the light scales; the root is ḥabaṭ, an animal eating so much that its belly swells (the hadith: some spring pasture kills by ḥabaṭ). (بطل): bāṭil is the opposite of ḥaqq, what has no firmness when examined (ḏālika bi-anna llāha huwa l-ḥaqq …); ibṭāl is said of corrupting and removing a thing, true or false (8:8); mubṭilūn are those who say what has no reality, or who void the truth.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 12 / 4 places read): the subject of حَبِطَ is always deeds (أَعْمَال, عَمَل, مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ, مَا صَنَعُوا); it is intransitive — the transitive أَحْبَطَ (Allah voided their deeds) is another verb. أَبْطَلَ has as object charities (2:264), deeds (47:33), magic (10:81) and falsehood (8:8). 39:65 and 6:88 (conditionals about prophets) are not cited.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: 18:105 bs 'ajete'; 49:2 replaced by 5:5 (the mufassirun differ on how far the 49:2 warning reaches).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries حبط, بطل (2026-11-06): 14 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): 'Looks full' is our embellishment; he only gives the hadith that spring pasture may kill by ḥabaṭ or nearly; members/1/nuance (reworded): He gives only 8:8 (falsehood); charity (2:264) and magic (10:81) are not in his entry

nuance.bs: Izvorno, prema ar-Rāġibu, kad se životinja toliko najede da joj se trbuh nadme – a, kako kaže hadis koji navodi, to može ubiti. On navodi tri vrste: djela ovoga svijeta koja na Sudnjem danu ne koriste, djela ahireta koja nisu činjena radi Allaha, i dobra djela koja loša djela pretegnu. U Kur'anu su subjekt uvijek djela.
nuance.en: At root, according to ar-Rāġib, when an animal eats so much that its belly swells — and, as the hadith he cites says, it can kill. He gives three kinds: worldly deeds that avail nothing at the Resurrection, deeds of the Hereafter not done for Allah, and good deeds outweighed by bad ones. In the Quran the subject is always deeds.

why.bs: „Takvi su oni koji poriču ajete svoga Gospodara i susret s Njim, pa su im djela propala, i na Danu kijameta im nećemo pridati nikakvu težinu.“
why.en: “Those are they who disbelieve in the revelations of their Lord and in the meeting with Him. Therefor their works are vain, and on the Day of Resurrection We assign no weight to them.”

why.bs: „A ko poriče vjerovanje, njegovo je djelo propalo, i on će na ahiretu biti među gubitnicima.“
why.en: “Whoso denieth the faith, his work is vain and he will be among the losers in the Hereafter.”

why.bs: „A oni od vas koji otpadnu od svoje vjere i umru kao nevjernici – njihova su djela propala i na dunjaluku i na ahiretu.“
why.en: “And whoso becometh a renegade and dieth in his disbelief: such are they whose works have fallen both in the world and the Hereafter.”

nuance.bs: Od bāṭil, što je prema ar-Rāġibu suprotnost istini (ḥaqq): ono što nema postojanosti kad se ispita. Ibṭāl je, kaže on, kvarenje i uklanjanje nečega, bilo istinitog ili neistinitog: u Kur'anu se poništava milostinja, ali i sihr i neistina.
nuance.en: From bāṭil, which according to ar-Rāġib is the opposite of truth (ḥaqq): what has no firmness when examined. Ibṭāl, he says, is spoiling and removing a thing, whether true or false: in the Quran charity is invalidated, but so are magic and falsehood.

why.bs: „O vi koji vjerujete, ne poništavajte svoje sadake prigovaranjem i uznemiravanjem.“
why.en: “O ye who believe! Render not vain your almsgiving by reproach and injury.”

why.bs: Musa vračarima: „Ono što ste donijeli je sihr; Allah će ga, zaista, poništiti.“
why.en: Moses to the magicians: “That which ye have brought is magic. Lo! Allah will make it vain.”

why.bs: „Da bi utvrdio istinu i poništio neistinu, makar to bilo mrsko zločincima“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “That He might cause the Truth to triumph and bring vanity to naught, however much the guilty might oppose” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

title.bs: Čuvati se, strepiti s brigom, drhtati

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi su vrste straha. Prema ar-Rāġibu, prva je čuvanje od onoga čega se boji, druga briga pomiješana sa strahom, treća strah koji se osjeti u sebi.
shared.en: All three words are kinds of fear. According to ar-Rāġib, the first is guarding against what is feared, the second care mixed with fear, the third fear felt within.

tellApart.bs: Čuvati se onoga čega se boji, biti na oprezu → حَذِرَ; brižan strah – strah pomiješan s pažnjom prema onome do čega je stalo → مُشْفِق; osjetiti strah u sebi, da srce zadrhti → وَجِلَ.
tellApart.en: To guard against what is feared, to be on one's guard → حَذِرَ; anxious care — fear mixed with concern for what one holds dear → مُشْفِق; to feel fear within, the heart trembling → وَجِلَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حذر, شفق, وجل
notes: ar-Rāġib (حذر): ḥaḏar is guarding against something feared (iḥtirāz ʿan muḫīf); 39:9, 'Allah warns you of Himself', 'take your precaution' (ḫuḏū ḥiḏrakum) = what holds caution, weapons and the like; 63:4, 64:14. (شفق): išfāq is care mixed with fear, because the mušfiq loves the one he is anxious for and fears what may befall him; with min the sense of fear is more apparent, with fī the sense of care; 21:49, 52:26, 42:18, 42:22. (وجل): waǧal is feeling fear inwardly (istišʿār al-ḫawf); 8:2, 15:52–53, 23:60.

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): وَجِلَ (3×) is twice the hearts of believers when Allah is mentioned (8:2, 22:35) and once the angels' word to Ibrāhīm (15:53; his fear of the strangers, 15:52, is a natural one). مُشْفِق is joined to ḫašya in 21:28 and 23:57 — see the خَوْف/خَشْيَة group. 5:41 and 5:49 (حَذِرَ said to the Prophet) are not cited.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: the root's places named in full (8:2, 22:35, 23:60, 15:52, 15:53 — the verb is 3 of them); 15:53 no longer borrows the fear from 15:52.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries حذر, شفق, وجل (2026-11-06): 25 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḥaḏar je čuvanje od onoga čega se boji. Naglasak je na postupku: čovjek se pazi, sklanja i oprema – „Poduzmite mjere opreza“ (4:71), kaže on, znači oružje i slično.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ḥaḏar is guarding against what is feared. The weight is on the action: one takes care, keeps away, prepares — “Take your precautions” (4:71), he says, means weapons and the like.

why.bs: „Zar je onaj koji tokom noćnih sati pokorno ibadet čini … koji se čuva ahireta i nada se milosti svoga Gospodara [isti kao onaj koji to ne čini]?“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Is he who payeth adoration in the watches of the night … bewaring of the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord, (to be accounted equal with a disbeliever)?” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „O vi koji vjerujete, neki od vaših supruga i vaše djece neprijatelji su vam, pa se od njih čuvajte! A ako budete praštali … Allah, zaista, prašta“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “O ye who believe! Lo! among your wives and your children there are enemies for you, therefor beware of them. And if ye efface … then lo! Allah is Forgiving” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Licemjeri se čuvaju da im se ne objavi sura koja će ih obavijestiti o onome što je u njihovim srcima.“
why.en: “The hypocrites fear lest a surah should be revealed concerning them, proclaiming what is in their hearts.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, išfāq je briga pomiješana sa strahom: ko brižno strepi, voli onoga za koga strepi i boji se onoga što bi ga moglo zadesiti. S min (od) jače se čuje strah, a s fī (u) briga.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, išfāq is care mixed with fear: one who is anxious loves the one he is anxious for and fears what may befall him. With min (of) the fear is heard more, with fī (among) the care.

why.bs: „Oni koji se boje svoga Gospodara iako Ga ne vide, i koji od Časa strepe“ – s min: jače se čuje strah; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Those who fear their Lord in secret and who dread the Hour” — with min: the fear is heard more; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Stanovnici Dženneta: „Mi smo, zaista, ranije među svojom porodicom strepili“ – s fī: briga za porodicu; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: The people of Paradise: “Lo! of old, when we were with our families, we were ever anxious” — with fī: care for one's family; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… a oni koji vjeruju strepe od njega [Časa], znajući da je on istina“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… while those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the Truth” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, waǧal je osjetiti strah u sebi. U Kur'anu srca vjernika drhte kad se spomene Allah (8:2, 22:35; i 23:60), a Ibrahim svojim gostima kaže da ih se boji (15:52), pa mu oni odgovore: „Ne drhti!“ (15:53).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, waǧal is feeling fear within. In the Quran the hearts of believers tremble when Allah is mentioned (8:2, 22:35; also 23:60), and Abraham tells his guests that he fears them (15:52) and they answer: “Be not afraid!” (15:53).

why.bs: „Vjernici su samo oni kojima, kad se Allah spomene, srca zadrhte“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “They only are the (true) believers whose hearts feel fear when Allah is mentioned” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… one kojima, kad se Allah spomene, srca zadrhte, i one strpljive u onome što ih pogodi.“
why.en: “Whose hearts fear when Allah is mentioned, and the patient of whatever may befall them.”

why.bs: Meleki, Ibrahimovi gosti, rekoše mu: „Ne drhti, mi te radujemo viješću o dječaku koji će mnogo znati“; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: The angels, Abraham's guests, said to him: “Be not afraid! Lo! we bring thee good tidings of a boy possessing wisdom”; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače riječ upućenu drugome za njegovo dobro. Razlikuju se po tonu i po onome što se u riječi ističe: odvraćanje uz upozorenje, ili iskrena briga za dobro onoga kome se govori.
shared.en: Both words mean speech addressed to another for his good. They differ in tone and in what the word stresses: restraint with a warning, or sincere care for the good of the one addressed.

tellApart.bs: Opomena koja odvraća i upozorava (najčešće je izriče Allah ili poslanik) → وَعَظَ; iskreno nastojanje oko dobra drugoga; glagol u Kur'anu uvijek dolazi sa ‚za‘ nekoga (نَصَحَ لِـ) → نَصَحَ.
tellApart.en: An admonition that restrains and warns (in the Quran mostly from Allah or a prophet) → وَعَظَ; sincere striving for another's good; the verb in the Quran always takes ‘for’ someone (نَصَحَ لِـ) → نَصَحَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries وعظ, نصح
notes: ar-Rāġib (وعظ): waʿẓ is restraint (zajr) joined with causing fear; he quotes al-Ḫalīl: reminding of good in a way the heart softens to; ʿiẓa and mawʿiẓa are the noun; he cites 16:90 (yaʿiẓukum laʿallakum taḏakkarūn), 34:46, 4:63. (نصح): nuṣḥ is seeking out a deed or word in which lies the other's good (taḥarrī fiʿl aw qawl fīhi ṣalāḥ ṣāḥibihi); cites 7:79 and 11:34; from naṣaḥtu lahu l-wudd, I made my love pure for him, or from naṣaḥtu l-jild, I sewed the hide; tawba naṣūḥ (66:8) from one of the two: sincerity or firmness.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 15 / 5 places read): وَعَظَ takes its hearer as direct object (يَعِظُكُمْ); its subject is Allah in 2:231, 2:232, 4:58, 11:46, 16:90, 24:17 and the passive tūʿaẓūn of 58:3, 65:2, a prophet or Luqmān in 4:63, 26:136, 31:13, 34:46, and people in 7:164. نَصَحَ comes all 5 times with li- (لَكُمْ, لِلَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ): four times a prophet to his people (7:62 Nūḥ, 7:79 Ṣāliḥ, 7:93 Šuʿayb, 11:34 Nūḥ), once the believers who cannot go out to fight, 'when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger' (9:91).
Not cited: 4:34 (tafsir and context need more than a line) and 11:46 (said to a prophet in correction).

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: 'always with li-' is of the verb نَصَحَ only (7:68, 66:8 have none); 9:91 names only who the ayah names.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, opomena je odvraćanje povezano s upozorenjem; on navodi i al-Ḫalīlovo objašnjenje: podsjećanje na dobro na način od kojeg srce omekša. U Kur'anu ga najčešće izriče Allah, a onda poslanici i Lukman svome sinu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, admonition is restraint joined with a warning; he also quotes al-Ḫalīl: reminding of good in a way that softens the heart. In the Quran it is mostly Allah who admonishes, then the prophets, and Luqmān to his son.

why.bs: „On vas opominje (يَعِظُكُمْ) da biste se prisjetili“ – nakon naredbe pravde i zabrane razvrata; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “He exhorteth you in order that ye may take heed” — after the command of justice and the forbidding of immorality; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Allah vas opominje da nikada više ne ponovite nešto slično, ako ste vjernici“ – opomena koja odvraća.
why.en: “Allah admonisheth you that ye repeat not the like thereof ever, if ye are (in truth) believers” — an admonition that restrains.

why.bs: Lukman je opominjao sina: „Sinko moj, ne pripisuj Allahu druga!“
why.en: Luqmān, admonishing his son: “O my dear son! Ascribe no partners unto Allah.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, to je tražiti djelo ili riječ u kojoj je dobro onoga kome se savjet daje; korijen je ili u ‚iskrenoj, čistoj ljubavi‘, ili u ‚šivenju‘ – iskrenost ili čvrstina. U Kur'anu je to najčešće riječ poslanika svome narodu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, it is seeking out the deed or word that holds the good of the one advised; the root is either ‘pure, sincere love’ or ‘sewing’ — sincerity or firmness. In the Quran it is mostly a prophet's word to his people.

why.bs: Salih: „Prenio sam vam poslanicu svoga Gospodara i iskreno vas savjetovao, ali vi ne volite one koji iskreno savjetuju“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Ṣāliḥ: “I delivered my Lord's message unto you and gave you good advice, but ye love not good advisers” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Nuh: „Dostavljam vam poslanice svoga Gospodara i iskreno vas savjetujem.“
why.en: Noah: “I convey unto you the messages of my Lord and give good counsel unto you.”

why.bs: Nema grijeha na slabima, bolesnima i onima koji nemaju čime da troše „ako su iskreni prema Allahu i Njegovom Poslaniku“ – ista riječ, iskrenost prema Allahu.
why.en: There is no blame on the weak, the ill and those without means to spend “if they are true to Allah and His messenger” — the same word, sincerity toward Allah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o onome po čemu je čovjek živ. Prema ar-Rāġibu, nafs se ponekad kaže za ruh, a ruh se naziva i imenom nafsa; ipak, Kur'an ih upotrebljava vrlo različito.
shared.en: Both words speak of that by which a person is alive. According to ar-Rāġib, nafs is sometimes said for rūḥ, and rūḥ is also used as a name for the nafs; yet the Quran uses them very differently.

tellApart.bs: Duša, sâmo biće čovjeka – ona umire, žudi, odgovara za djela → نَفْس; duh koji Allah udahnjuje, šalje s objavom, ili meleki koji se tako nazivaju → رُوح.
tellApart.en: The soul, the person's own self — it dies, desires and answers for its deeds → نَفْس; the spirit that Allah breathes in, sends with revelation, or the angels so named → رُوح.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نفس, روح
notes: ar-Rāġib (نفس): nafs is the rūḥ in 6:93 (aḫrijū anfusakum); he also cites 2:235 and 5:116, and gives the nafs of Allah (3:28) as His essence: in meaning there is nothing other than Him, exalted above any duality (not cited on the page). (روح): rūḥ and rawḥ are at root one; rūḥ was made a name for the nafs, the nafs being part of the rūḥ, like naming a species by its genus; and a name for the part by which life, movement, gaining benefit and warding off harm come about — that, he says, is the rūḥ of 17:85 and of 15:29 'I breathed into him of My rūḥ', whose ascription to Allah is one of possession, singled out for honour like 'My House'; the noblest angels are called arwāḥ (78:38, 70:4); Jibrīl is al-rūḥ al-amīn (26:193) and rūḥ al-qudus; ʿĪsā is called rūḥ (4:171) for his raising of the dead (by Allah's leave, as 3:49 says); the Quran is called rūḥ (42:52) as a cause of the life to come.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 21 rūḥ places read): rūḥ is never a person's own self in the Quran — it is breathed in by Allah (15:29, 32:9, 38:72, 21:91, 66:12), sent down with revelation or as an angel (16:2, 16:102, 26:193, 40:15, 70:4, 78:38, 97:4, 19:17), the support of prophets and believers (2:87, 2:253, 5:110, 58:22), ʿĪsā (4:171), revelation (42:52) and 17:85. It is never said to die or desire; nafs is (3:185, 79:40). nafs counts 295 places, including the reflexive 'oneself'.
17:85 is shown only with the ayah's own words ('of the affair of my Lord'): mufassirun differ on what rūḥ there refers to. 4:171 and 42:52 are left out of the ayat for the same reason.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 3 flags, fixed: Allah's nafs (3:28) added — his 'His very Being', as befits Him; 'rūḥ never the self' softened to 'not spoken of as the self that answers for deeds'; 17:85 leaves its reality with Allah and says the mufassirun differ.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries نفس, روح (2026-11-06): 19 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): 'as befits Him' and 'by Allah's leave' are our wording, not his; the fixes keep the theology but stop attributing it to him. He also reports (qāla baʿḍ an-nās) a view that nafs in 3:28 is ascribed by possession — not used, fine; members/1/nuance (reworded): Minor: the honour he names is to the rūḥ (tašrīfan lahu), and 'as befits Him' is ours. Note the last sentence ('never the person's own self') is our Quranic observation; ar-Rāġib himself says rūḥ was made a name for the nafs, so it must not be read as his

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, nafs se kaže i za ruh, kao u 6:93: „Izvadite svoje duše!“ U Kur'anu je nafs najčešće sâmo biće čovjeka: duša koja okusi smrt, koja žudi i koju treba suzdržati, i koja odgovara za ono što je stekla. Kad se kaže za Allaha („Allah vam nalaže da se čuvate Njega Samog“, 3:28), ar-Rāġib kaže da znači Njegovo Biće, kako Njemu priliči.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, nafs is also said for the rūḥ, as in 6:93: “Deliver up your souls.” In the Quran the nafs is mostly the person's own self: the soul that tastes death, that desires and must be held back, and that answers for what it has earned. When it is said of Allah (“Allah biddeth you beware of Himself”, 3:28), ar-Rāġib says it means His very Being, as befits Him.

why.bs: Meleki govore nepravednicima na samrti: „Izvadite svoje duše!“ – ar-Rāġib: ovdje je nafs isto što i ruh.
why.en: The angels say to the wrongdoers at death: “Deliver up your souls.” — ar-Rāġib: here nafs is the rūḥ.

why.bs: „Svaka duša će okusiti smrt“ – nafs umire.
why.en: “Every soul will taste of death” — the nafs dies.

why.bs: „A onaj ko se bojao stajanja pred svojim Gospodarom i dušu od strasti suzdržavao…“ – duša koju treba suzdržati.
why.en: “But as for him who feared to stand before his Lord and restrained his soul from lust…” — the soul that must be held back.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ruh je ono čime nastaje život, kretanje, pribavljanje koristi i odbijanje štete; kad ga Allah naziva „Mojim duhom“ (15:29), to je pripisivanje vlasništva, kojim se ruh izdvaja i počastvuje. Ruhom se nazivaju i najodličniji meleki: Džibril je „Povjerljivi Duh“ (26:193). U Kur'anu se ruh uvijek pripisuje Allahu („od Moga duha“, 15:29; „od stvari moga Gospodara“, 17:85) i ne govori se o njemu kao o biću koje odgovara za djela.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the rūḥ is that by which life, movement, gaining benefit and warding off harm come about; when Allah calls it “My Spirit” (15:29), it is ascription of possession, singling it out for honour. The noblest angels are also called rūḥ: Jibrīl is “the True Spirit” (26:193). In the Quran the rūḥ is always ascribed to Allah (“of My Spirit”, 15:29; “by command of my Lord”, 17:85) and is not spoken of as the self that answers for deeds.

why.bs: „Pa kad ga uobličim i udahnem u njega od Moga duha…“ – ar-Rāġib: pripisivanje Allahu je počast, kao ‚Moja Kuća‘.
why.en: “So, when I have made him and have breathed into him of My Spirit…” — ar-Rāġib: the ascription to Allah is one of honour, like ‘My House’.

why.bs: „S njim je sišao Povjerljivi Duh“ – Džibril, kako ga ar-Rāġib objašnjava.
why.en: “Which the True Spirit hath brought down” — Jibrīl, as ar-Rāġib explains.

why.bs: „Pitaju te o duhu. Odgovori: Duh je stvar koja pripada mome Gospodaru“ – ovdje Kur'an njegovu suštinu prepušta Allahu; mufessiri se razilaze oko toga šta se tačno misli.
why.en: “They are asking thee concerning the Spirit. Say: The Spirit is by command of my Lord” — here the Quran leaves its reality with Allah; mufassirun differ on what exactly is meant.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače razum, i obje dolaze u izrazu ‚oni koji imaju…‘ (أُولُو). Prema ar-Rāġibovim definicijama, razlikuju se po onome što se u razumu ističe: njegova čistota, ili to što odvraća od ružnog.
shared.en: Both words mean the intellect, and both come in the phrase ‘those who have…’ (أُولُو). Going by ar-Rāġib's definitions, they differ in what they stress about the mind: its purity, or its holding back from what is vile.

tellApart.bs: Razum očišćen od primjesa, srž čovjekova uma, kojem se upućuju pouke i opomene → أَلْبَاب; pamet koja odvraća od ružnog, uz znakove u prirodi i povijesti → نُهَى.
tellApart.en: The intellect cleansed of admixture, the kernel of a person's mind, to which lessons and reminders are addressed → أَلْبَاب; the intelligence that restrains from what is vile, beside signs in nature and history → نُهَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries لب, نهى
notes: ar-Rāġib (لب): lubb is the intellect pure of admixture, so called because it is the pure of what is in a person, like the kernel (lubāb) of a thing; 'it has been said' (qīla) it is the intellect that has grown pure, so every lubb is an intellect but not every intellect a lubb; therefore, he says, Allah tied the judgements only purified minds grasp to ulū l-albāb, citing 2:269. (نهى): nuhya is the intellect that restrains from vile things (al-ʿaql al-nāhī ʿan al-qabāʾiḥ), plural nuhā, citing the phrase 'inna fī ḏālika la-āyātin li-ulī n-nuhā' (identical in 20:54 and 20:128) (the OpenITI text misprints the singular as نهبة).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 16 / 2 places read): أَلْبَاب is always in ulū / ulī l-albāb; six times with taḏakkur, taking heed (2:269, 3:7, 13:19, 14:52, 38:29, 39:9), four times with a call to taqwā (2:179, 2:197, 5:100, 65:10). نُهَى is in 20:54 and 20:128, both 'signs for those of intelligence' after the earth's pasture and the ruins of destroyed generations.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): all claims OK.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
