nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, lubb je razum očišćen od primjesa, srž čovjeka; neki kažu: razum koji se pročistio, pa je svaki lubb razum, a nije svaki razum lubb. Zato, kaže on, Allah ono što shvataju samo čisti umovi veže za ‚one koji imaju razuma‘. U Kur'anu im se najčešće kaže da prime pouku ili da se boje Allaha.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, lubb is the intellect pure of admixture, the kernel of a person; some say: the intellect that has grown pure, so every lubb is an intellect but not every intellect a lubb. That is why, he says, Allah ties what only purified minds grasp to ‘those of understanding’. In the Quran they are mostly told to take heed or to fear Allah.

why.bs: „Kome je data mudrost, dato mu je mnogo dobra, a pouku primaju samo razumom obdareni“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “He unto whom wisdom is given, he truly hath received abundant good. But none remember except men of understanding” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „U tome kako su stvorena nebesa i Zemlja, i u izmjenjivanju noći i dana, zaista ima znakova za razumom obdarene.“
why.en: “Lo! In the creation of the heavens and the earth and (in) the difference of night and day are tokens (of His Sovereignty) for men of understanding.”

why.bs: „Zar je isti onaj ko zna da je ono što ti je objavljeno od tvoga Gospodara istina, i onaj ko je slijep? Pouku primaju samo razumom obdareni.“
why.en: “Is he who knoweth that what is revealed unto thee from thy Lord is the truth like him who is blind? But only men of understanding heed.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od korijena ‚zabraniti, odvratiti‘: pamet koja odvraća od ružnih djela. U Kur'anu dolazi dvaput, oba puta kao znakovi „za one koji imaju pameti“ (20:54, 20:128), uz ono što se vidi očima: ispašu na zemlji i ruševine uništenih naroda.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from the root of forbidding and holding back: the intelligence that restrains from vile deeds. It comes twice in the Quran, both times in signs “for men of thought” (20:54, 20:128), beside what the eyes can see: pasture on the earth and the ruins of destroyed peoples.

why.bs: „Jedite i pasite stoku svoju! U tome, doista, ima znakova za one što imaju pameti“ – ar-Rāġib navodi njegove završne riječi.
why.en: “Eat ye and feed your cattle. Lo! herein verily are portents for men of thought” — ar-Rāġib cites its closing words.

why.bs: „Zar ih nije poučilo to koliko smo pokoljenja prije njih uništili, po čijim nastambama oni sada hode? U tome, doista, ima znakova za one što imaju pameti.“
why.en: “Is it not a guidance for them (to know) how many a generation We destroyed before them, amid whose dwellings they walk? Lo! therein verily are signs for men of thought.”

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o putu koji je Allah propisao ljudima. Prema ar-Rāġibovim objašnjenjima, razlikuju se po tome odakle se taj put gleda: od onoga ko ga se pokorno drži, od onoga što je Allah propisao preko poslanika, ili kao jasna staza propisa.
shared.en: All three words speak of the way Allah has prescribed for people. Following ar-Rāġib, they differ in where that way is seen from: from the one who keeps to it in obedience, from what Allah laid down through a prophet, or as the clear track of its laws.

tellApart.bs: Vjera kao pokornost i predanost, i ono za što se plaća (Dan sudnji) → دِين; vjerski put koji se pripisuje poslaniku (Ibrahimov) ili zajednici, nikad ‚Allahov‘ → مِلَّة; zakon, jasna staza propisa koja se razlikuje od zajednice do zajednice → شِرْعَة.
tellApart.en: Religion as obedience and submission, and that for which one is repaid (the Day of Judgement) → دِين; the creed ascribed to a prophet (Abraham's) or to a community, never ‘Allah's’ → مِلَّة; the law, the clear track of rulings that differs from one community to another → شِرْعَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries دين, ملل, شرع
notes: ar-Rāġib (دين): dīn is said for obedience and for requital, and borrowed for the revealed law; dīn is like milla but said with regard to obedience and submission to the law; he cites 3:19 and 4:125 ('aḥsanu dīnan' = obedience), and 56:86 ġayra madīnīn = not requited. (ملل): milla is like dīn, a name for what Allah prescribed for His servants by the tongues of the prophets; the difference is that milla is ascribed only to the prophet on whom it rests (3:95 'fa-ttabiʿū millata Ibrāhīm', 12:38 'millata ābāʾī'), hardly ever to Allah or to single members of a prophet's community — one does not say millat Allāh or millatī as one says dīn Allāh; it is said with regard to what Allah prescribed, dīn with regard to the one who upholds it; its origin is amlaltu l-kitāb, I dictated the writing (2:282). (شرع): šarʿ is the clear beaten track, borrowed for the divine way; 5:48 šir'atan wa-minhājan points to two things, the second being the part of religion in which laws differ and abrogation enters; he reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that šir'a is what the Quran brought and minhāj what the Sunna brought; 42:13 šaraʿa lakum mina d-dīn points to the principles all the millas share and that are not abrogated.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 15 مِلَّة places read): eight are Abraham's (2:130, 2:135, 3:95, 4:125, 6:161, 12:38, 16:123, 22:78); seven are the creed of a people or community (2:120, 7:88, 7:89, 12:37, 14:13, 18:20, 38:7) — a counter-example to 'only a prophet's', so the page says 'a prophet or a community'; never 'Allah's milla', while dīn Allāh occurs (3:83, 24:2, 110:2). The count of دِين (92) includes the dīn of requital (1:4 and 'yawm ad-dīn'); دَيْن 'debt' is a separate lemma. شِرْعَة is only in 5:48; شَرِيعَة (45:18) is a separate lemma.
2:256 (lā ikrāha fī d-dīn) is not cited: ar-Rāġib himself reports two interpretations (both as qīla).

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 4 flags, fixed: his limit restored (milla is hardly ever ascribed to Allah or to an individual); the community's milla (14:13) marked as Quranic usage; bs 'vjerski put' (not 'millet'), 'Allahov put', 3:19 bs 'Vjera je kod Allaha islam'.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries دين, ملل, شرع (2026-11-06): 30 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): His explicit angle for milla is 'with regard to what Allah prescribed'; being ascribed only to the prophet is a usage rule, not the angle. He contrasts only dīn and milla; šarʿa joins the comparison through our framing; notes/0 (reworded): The verse he quotes is 3:95 (fa-ttabiʿū millata Ibrāhīm), not 2:135. He also adds that milla is used only of the whole body of laws, never of a single rule ('one does not say: prayer is millat Allāh') — not in our note, harmless; notes/2 (reworded): These are two interpretations he reports with qīla (obedience cannot be forced; specific to jizya-paying People of the Book), not qirāʾāt. Second: 'وقيل إن ذلك مختص بأهل الكتاب الباذلين للجزية'; members/2/nuance (reworded): He says 'šir'atan wa-minhājan' (the pair) points to two things: (1) the way each person is set on for public welfare, (2) the chosen religion where laws differ and abrogation enters. He does not equate šir'a alone with (2)

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, dīn se kaže za pokornost i za obračun (nagradu i kaznu), a preneseno i za šerijat; sličan je riječi milla, ali se kaže s obzirom na pokornost i predanost propisima. Zato je dīn i Allahov (‚Allahova vjera‘) i čovjekov.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, dīn is said for obedience and for requital, and by extension for the revealed law; it is like milla, but said with regard to obedience and submission to the law. So dīn is both Allah's (‘the religion of Allah’) and a person's.

why.bs: „Vjera je kod Allaha, zaista, islam“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Lo! religion with Allah (is) the Surrender” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A čija je vjera bolja od vjere onoga koji svoje lice preda Allahu…“ – ar-Rāġib: vjera ovdje znači pokornost.
why.en: “Who is better in religion than he who surrendereth his purpose to Allah…” — ar-Rāġib: religion here means obedience.

why.bs: „Vladaru Sudnjeg dana (يَوْمِ الدِّينِ)“ – dīn u značenju obračuna.
why.en: “Master of the Day of Judgment (يَوْمِ الدِّينِ)” — dīn in the sense of requital.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, milla je kao dīn: ono što je Allah propisao preko poslanika; pripisuje se poslaniku na kojem počiva, a gotovo se nikad ne nalazi pripisana Allahu ili pojedincu – ne kaže se ‚Allahova milla‘. U Kur'anu je to najčešće ‚Ibrahimov vjerski put‘; upotrebljava se i za vjerski put neke zajednice (14:13) – nikada za Allahov.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, milla is like dīn: what Allah prescribed through the prophets; it is ascribed to the prophet on whom it rests, and is hardly ever found ascribed to Allah or to an individual — one does not say ‘Allah's milla’. In the Quran it is mostly ‘the milla of Abraham’; it is also used of a community's creed (14:13) — never of Allah's.

why.bs: Jusuf: „I slijedim vjerski put svojih očeva, Ibrahima, Ishaka i Jakuba“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Joseph: “And I have followed the religion [milla] of my fathers, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Reci: Allah je istinu rekao, pa slijedite vjerski put Ibrahima, pravovjernika.“
why.en: “Say: Allah speaketh truth. So follow the religion [milla] of Abraham, the upright.”

why.bs: Nevjernici poslanicima: „… ili ćete se vratiti našem vjerskom putu“ – milla zajednice, ne poslanika.
why.en: The disbelievers to their messengers: “… unless ye return to our religion [milla]” — the creed of a community, not of a prophet.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, šarʿ je jasna, utrta staza, prenesena na Allahov put. U 5:48, kaže on, izraz upućuje, između ostalog, na onaj dio vjere u kojem se zakoni razlikuju i u koji ulazi derogacija, dok su temelji koje svi poslanici dijele isti (42:13). Prenosi i od Ibn Abbasa: šir'a je ono što je donio Kur'an, a minhādž ono što je donio sunnet.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, šarʿ is the clear, beaten track, transferred to the divine way. In 5:48, he says, the phrase points, among other things, to the part of religion in which laws differ and abrogation enters, while the principles all prophets share stay the same (42:13). He also reports from Ibn ʿAbbās: šir'a is what the Quran brought, and minhāj what the Sunna brought.

why.bs: „Svakome od vas odredili smo zakon i jasan put“ – jedini spomen ove riječi; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “For each We have appointed a divine law and a traced-out way” — the only place of this word; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače privlačnost duše prema nečemu. Prema ar-Rāġibu, hawā je naginjanje duše prema požudi, a šahwa je sâmo stremljenje duše prema onome što želi.
shared.en: Both words mean the soul's pull toward something. According to ar-Rāġib, hawā is the soul's leaning toward shahwa, and shahwa is the soul's very yearning for what it wants.

tellApart.bs: Naginjanje duše koje se slijedi umjesto upute, u Kur'anu uvijek pokuđeno → هَوًى; stremljenje duše prema onome što želi, i ono što se želi – istinsko (glad) ili lažno → شَهْوَة.
tellApart.en: The soul's leaning that is followed instead of guidance, in the Quran always blamed → هَوًى; the soul's yearning for what it wants, and the thing wanted — genuine (hunger) or false → شَهْوَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries هوى, شها, نهى
notes: ar-Rāġib (هوى): hawā is the soul's leaning toward shahwa, also said of the soul so inclined; 'it has been said' (qīla) it is so named because it makes its holder fall (yahwī) into every calamity in this world and into the hāwiya in the next; Allah made following hawā a grave matter (45:23, 38:26); the plural ahwāʾ in 'ahwāʾahum' notes that each has a hawā other than the other's, and each one's hawā has no end, so following their ahwāʾ is the utmost of straying. (شها): shahwa is at root the soul's yearning (nuzūʿ) for what it wants; in this world of two kinds, genuine (the body suffers without it, like food in hunger) and false; the thing desired is also called shahwa; 3:14 may bear both kinds; 19:59 'they followed the shahawāt' is of the false kind; of Paradise he cites 41:31 'mā tashtahī anfusukum'. (نهى): in 79:40 'restrained the soul from hawā' he says the meaning is not telling oneself 'don't' but suppressing the soul from its shahwa.

The corpus files the singular هَوَى under the lemma هَوَاء (11 places: 10 × hawā, plus 14:43 hawāʾ 'void'); the member sums هَوَاء and أَهْوَاء and counts that one place too. شَهْوَة sums the corpus's شَهْوَة (2) and شَهَوَة (the plural, 3).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 28 hawā / ahwāʾ places read): hawā is always blamed — followed by those who stray (e.g. 7:176, 18:28, 28:50, 45:23), forbidden to follow (4:135, 38:26), restrained (79:40), or denied of the Prophet's speech (53:3). The noun shahwa is blamed in 4:27, 19:59, 7:81, 27:55 and set out as worldly enjoyment in 3:14; the verb ištahā is said approvingly of Paradise (41:31). 7:81 and 27:55 (Lot's people) are not cited.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: bs meaning 'požuda, žudnja' (not 'užitak'); spelling.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, hawā je naginjanje duše prema požudi; neki kažu da je tako nazvan jer onoga ko ga slijedi obara u svaku nesreću. Množinu ‚njihove strasti‘ Kur'an upotrebljava, kaže on, da ukaže da svako ima svoju strast, i da joj nema kraja. U Kur'anu je strast uvijek pokuđena.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, hawā is the soul's leaning toward shahwa; some say it is so named because it makes its follower fall into every calamity. The Quran uses the plural ‘their desires’, he says, to show that each has his own desire, and that it has no end. In the Quran desire is always blamed.

why.bs: „Zar si vidio onoga koji je svoju strast uzeo za svoga boga?“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Hast thou seen him who maketh his desire his god” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A onaj ko se bojao stajanja pred svojim Gospodarom i dušu od strasti suzdržavao“ – ar-Rāġib: suzdržati dušu od njene požude.
why.en: “But as for him who feared to stand before his Lord and restrained his soul from lust” — ar-Rāġib: to hold the soul back from its shahwa.

why.bs: „Kad bi se istina povodila za njihovim strastima, nebesa i Zemlja bi propali, i svi koji su u njima“ – množina, mnoge strasti.
why.en: “And if the Truth had followed their desires, verily the heavens and the earth and whosoever is therein had been corrupted” — the plural, many desires.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, šahwa je stremljenje duše prema onome što želi; na ovom svijetu je dvojaka: istinska, bez koje tijelo trpi, kao želja za hranom u gladi, i lažna, bez koje može. I ono što se želi naziva se šahwa. Glagol od istog korijena Kur'an kaže i za ono što duše žele u Džennetu (41:31).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, shahwa is the soul's yearning for what it wants; in this world it is of two kinds: genuine, without which the body suffers, like the wish for food in hunger, and false, which it can do without. The thing wanted is also called shahwa. The Quran uses the verb of this root for what souls desire in Paradise too (41:31).

why.bs: „Ljudima je uljepšana ljubav prema požudama: prema ženama, sinovima i hrpama nagomilanog zlata i srebra…“ – ar-Rāġib: može obuhvatiti obje vrste.
why.en: “Beautified for mankind is love of the joys [passions] (that come) from women and offspring; and stored-up heaps of gold and silver…” — ar-Rāġib: it may cover both kinds.

why.bs: „Zatim su poslije njih došli nasljednici koji su namaz upropastili i za požudama se poveli“ – ar-Rāġib: lažne požude.
why.en: “Now there hath succeeded them a later generation whom have ruined worship and have followed lusts” — ar-Rāġib: the false kind.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače strah koji obuzme čovjeka. Prema ar-Rāġibovim definicijama, razlikuju se po slici koju nose: strah koji ispuni i presiječe, grč i uzmicanje pred strašnim, i strah ubačen u nutrinu.
shared.en: All three words mean a fear that seizes a person. Going by ar-Rāġib's definitions, they differ in the image they carry: fear that fills and cuts off, a shrinking back from the frightening, and fear cast into the inner self.

tellApart.bs: Strah koji ispuni srce i presiječe, u Kur'anu najčešće ubačen u srca neprijatelja → رُعْب; grč i uzmicanje pred strašnim, u Kur'anu prepast Sudnjeg dana → فَزَع; strah ubačen u nutrinu, koji prođe (Ibrahim) → رَوْع.
tellApart.en: Fear that fills the heart and cuts off, in the Quran mostly cast into the hearts of enemies → رُعْب; a shrinking and recoiling before the frightening, in the Quran the alarm of the Last Day → فَزَع; fear cast into the inner self, which passes (Abraham) → رَوْع.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رعب, فزع, روع
notes: ar-Rāġib (رعب): ruʿb is being cut off (inqiṭāʿ) from the fullness of fear; from the image of filling, raʿabtu l-ḥawḍ, I filled the basin, and a sayl rāʿib that fills the valley; from the image of cutting, raʿabtu s-sanām, I cut the hump; he cites 33:26/59:2 (qaḏafa fī qulūbihimu r-ruʿb), 3:151 and 18:18 (la-muliʾta minhum ruʿban). (فزع): fazaʿ is a contraction and recoil that befalls a person from a frightening thing, of the genus of jazaʿ; one does not say faziʿtu mina llāh as one says ḫiftu minhu; the 'greatest fazaʿ' of 21:103 is the fazaʿ of entering the Fire; he cites 27:87, 27:89, 34:23. (روع): ar-rūʿ is the mind (al-ḫalad), as in the hadith 'the Holy Spirit breathed into my rūʿ'; ar-rawʿ is what strikes it, used for the fazaʿ cast into it; he cites 11:74. The OpenITI text is unvocalised: rūʿ / rawʿ are read from the sense.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 5 / 2 / 1 places read): رُعْب is cast by Allah into the hearts of those fighting the believers in 3:151, 8:12, 33:26, 59:2, and in 18:18 fills whoever would look on the sleepers of the cave; the noun فَزَع is only in 21:103 and 27:89, both of the Last Day; رَوْع is only in 11:74.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 flag, fixed: 21:103 'the greatest alarm' as the alarm of entering the Fire is his reading, with the mufassirun's others named.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries رعب, فزع, روع (2026-11-06): 22 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): Each definition is his; the comparison is ours

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ruʿb je stanje kad se čovjek presiječe od straha kojim se ispunio; zato se od istog korijena kaže ‚napuniti bazen‘ i ‚odsjeći‘. U Kur'anu ga Allah četiri puta ubacuje u srca onih koji se bore protiv vjernika, a peti put njime bi se ispunio onaj ko bi ugledao stanovnike pećine.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ruʿb is being cut off by a fear one is filled with; so the same root says ‘to fill a basin’ and ‘to cut off’. In the Quran Allah casts it four times into the hearts of those fighting the believers, and the fifth time it would fill whoever looked on the people of the cave.

why.bs: „U srca onih koji ne vjeruju ubacit ćemo užas, zbog toga što Allahu pripisuju druge“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve because they ascribe unto Allah partners” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Da si ih ugledao, sigurno bi od njih pobjegao i užasom bi se ispunio“ – ar-Rāġib: slika ispunjenosti.
why.en: “If thou hadst observed them closely thou hadst assuredly turned away from them in flight, and hadst been filled with awe [terror] of them” — ar-Rāġib: the image of being filled.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, fazaʿ je grč i uzmicanje koje obuzme čovjeka pred nečim strašnim, srodno uznemirenosti (džazaʿ); zato se ne kaže ‚uplašio sam se (faziʿtu) Allaha‘ kao što se kaže ‚bojim se (ḫiftu) Allaha‘. Imenica fazaʿ u Kur'anu dolazi samo za Sudnji dan.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, fazaʿ is the shrinking and recoil that seizes a person before something frightening, akin to agitation (jazaʿ); so one does not say ‘I took alarm (faziʿtu) at Allah’ as one says ‘I fear (ḫiftu) Allah’. The noun fazaʿ in the Quran is said only of the Last Day.

why.bs: „Ta najveća prepast neće ih rastužiti“ – ar-Rāġib to tumači kao prepast od ulaska u vatru; drugi mufessiri navode i druga tumačenja.
why.en: “The Supreme Horror will not grieve them” — ar-Rāġib takes it to be the alarm of entering the Fire; other mufassirun give other readings.

why.bs: „Ko dođe s dobrim djelom, njemu pripada nešto bolje od njega, a takvi će toga Dana biti sigurni od prepasti.“
why.en: “Whoso bringeth a good deed will have better than its worth; and such are safe from fear [alarm] that Day.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, riječ je vezana za rūʿ, nutrinu, um: rawʿ je ono što ga pogodi, strah ubačen u njega. U Kur'anu dolazi samo jednom: za Ibrahima, kad mu je strepnja prošla.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the word is tied to rūʿ, the inner mind: rawʿ is what strikes it, the fear cast into it. It comes only once in the Quran: of Abraham, when his fright had passed.

why.bs: „Pa kad je Ibrahima strepnja napustila i stigla mu radosna vijest…“ – strepnja koju je osjetio kad gosti nisu htjeli jesti (11:70); ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And when the awe [fright] departed from Abraham, and the glad news reached him…” — the fright he felt when his guests would not eat (11:70); ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače bol zbog onoga što je prošlo. Prema ar-Rāġibu, nadam je žaljenje zbog promijenjenog mišljenja o prošloj stvari, a ḥasra je tuga za propuštenim uz kajanje.
shared.en: Both words mean pain over what is past. According to ar-Rāġib, nadam is grief at a changed opinion about a past matter, and ḥasra is sorrow over what was missed together with regret.

tellApart.bs: Tuga za propuštenim i žaljenje zbog toga, često na Sudnjem danu → حَسْرَة; kajanje kad se uvidi da je odluka bila pogrešna, u Kur'anu uvijek ‚osvanuti pokajan‘ → نَادِم.
tellApart.en: Sorrow over what was missed and regret for it, often on the Last Day → حَسْرَة; regret on seeing that a decision was wrong, in the Quran always after the verb aṣbaḥa (‘to become’) → نَادِم.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حسر, ندم
notes: ar-Rāġib (حسر): ḥasr is uncovering; al-ḥasra is grief over what one has missed and regret (nadam) over it, as though the ignorance that drove him to his deed were lifted off him, or his strength were stripped by excess of grief, or weariness overtook him so that he could not make up for what he neglected; he cites 3:156, 69:50, 39:56, 2:167, 36:30. (ندم): nadam and nadāma are grief (taḥassur) from a change of opinion in a past matter; its root is grief keeping one company (munādama); he cites 5:31 and 23:40.
The corpus splits حَسْرَة (7), حَسْرَت (6:31 yā ḥasratanā) and حَسْرَتَى (39:56 yā ḥasratā); the member sums them (9).

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): ḥasra is the disbelievers' grief in the Hereafter (2:167, 6:31, 19:39, 39:56, 69:50), and also in this world (3:156, 8:36); 36:30 is a cry of grief over people who mocked their messengers. نَادِم comes all five times with aṣbaḥa, 'to become, to wake up as' (5:31, 5:52, 23:40, 26:157, 49:6). 35:8 (said to the Prophet) is not cited.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 4 flags, fixed: tellApart without 'exhaustion' and 'too late' (one of his three images, and not his); ḥasra 'grižnja savjesti / remorse' apart from nadim's 'kajanje / regret'; 19:39 and 26:157 say only what the ayah says.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries حسر, ندم (2026-11-06): 15 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): Inability to make up is only the third of three alternative images he gives (ignorance lifted / strength stripped by grief / weariness from making up); we turned it into a defining condition

meaning.en: anguish, sorrow over what is lost

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḥasra je tuga za onim što je čovjeku promaklo, uz grižnju savjesti zbog toga, kao da se s njega skinulo neznanje koje ga je na djelo navelo, ili mu je snaga klonula od tuge, ili je nemoćan da popravi propušteno. Riječ je od korijena ‚otkriti, ogoliti‘.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ḥasra is grief over what one has missed, with remorse for it, as though the ignorance that drove him to the deed were stripped off him, or his strength had failed from grief, or he were powerless to make up what he neglected. The word is from the root of uncovering, laying bare.

why.bs: „Da neka duša ne bi rekla: Jao meni (doslovno: o tugo moja) zbog onoga što sam prema Allahu zanemarila!“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Lest any soul should say: Alas, my grief that I was unmindful of Allah” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Tako će im Allah pokazati njihova djela kao jad za njih“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Thus will Allah show them their own deeds as anguish for them” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I opomeni ih na Dan jada, kada se o stvari presudi“ – Dan kad se stvar odluči.
why.en: “And warn them of the Day of anguish when the case hath been decided” — the Day on which the matter is settled.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, nadam je žaljenje zbog promijenjenog mišljenja o nečemu što je prošlo: čovjek uvidi da je pogrešno odlučio. U Kur'anu dolazi pet puta, i svaki put s glagolom ‚osvanuti, postati‘ (أَصْبَحَ) – kajanje koje dođe nakon djela.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, nadam is grief at a changed opinion about something past: one sees that one decided wrongly. It comes five times in the Quran, each time with the verb ‘to wake up as, to become’ (أَصْبَحَ) — regret that comes after the deed.

why.bs: Ademov sin, kad je vidio gavrana: „…i postade od onih koji se kaju“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Adam's son, on seeing the raven: “And he became repentant” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Ako vam fasik dođe s nekom viješću, dobro je ispitajte, da ne biste iz neznanja nekim ljudima naudili, pa da se zbog učinjenog kajete“ – kajanje zbog prenagljene odluke.
why.en: “If an evil-liver bring you tidings, verify it, lest ye smite some folk in ignorance and afterward repent of what ye did” — regret for a hasty decision.

why.bs: Semud: „Pa su joj presjekli tetive, i ujutro su se kajali (doslovno: osvanuli su kao pokajnici)“ – kajanje koje dođe nakon djela.
why.en: Thamūd: “But they hamstrung her, and then were penitent” — regret that came after the deed.

title.bs: Napojiti i dati vode za piće
title.en: Giving to drink and providing drink

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače dati nekome da pije. Prema ar-Rāġibu, IV vrsta je jača: ne samo dati piće, nego učiniti da onaj drugi ima izvor iz kojeg pije kako hoće.
shared.en: Both verbs mean to give someone to drink. According to ar-Rāġib, Form IV is the stronger: not only to give a drink, but to make for the other a source he drinks from as he wishes.

tellApart.bs: Dati nekome piće, napojiti (čašu, stado, njivu) → سَقَى; učiniti nekome vodu ili mlijeko dostupnim kao izvor – kiša, slatka voda, mlijeko stoke → أَسْقَى.
tellApart.en: To give someone a drink, to water (a cup, a flock, a field) → سَقَى; to make water or milk available to someone as a supply — rain, sweet water, the milk of cattle → أَسْقَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries سقى
notes: ar-Rāġib (سقى): saqy and suqyā are giving someone what he drinks; isqāʾ is making it for him so that he takes it as he wishes, so isqāʾ is more far-reaching (ablaġ) than saqy — 'asqaytuhu nahran', I gave him a river; for saqy he cites 76:21, 47:15, 26:79; for isqāʾ 77:27 and 15:22 ('We made it a supply of drink for you'), and nusqīkum mimmā fī buṭūnihā (the wording of 23:21; 16:66 has buṭūnihī and the same two readings), read with fatḥa and ḍamma.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 12 / 8 places read): أَسْقَى is said of rain and abundant water (15:22, 25:49, 72:16, 77:27), of milk from cattle (16:66, 23:21), and of the drink of Paradise in the passive (76:17, 83:25). سَقَى is said of single acts of giving drink or watering: the cupbearer (12:41), Moses watering the women's flock (28:23-25), Abraham's 'He gives me drink' (26:79), the cow that does not water the tilth (2:71), land watered with one water (13:4), the pure drink of Paradise (76:21), and the drink of Hell (14:16, 47:15, 88:5, not cited). Paradise has both verbs, so no rule is drawn from it.
16:66: Ḥafṣ reads nusqīkum (Form IV); Nāfiʿ and others read nasqīkum (Form I) — ar-Rāġib mentions both readings, quoting the identical phrase of 23:21 (buṭūnihā); the why says so.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 4 flags, fixed: 'rivers' was his example sentence, not Quranic usage; 'single acts' dropped (26:79 is continual); the drink of Paradise left to سَقَى (76:21) — the corpus files the passive yusqawna (76:17, 83:25) under Form IV, where the two forms coincide; 15:22 bs past tense.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries سقى (2026-11-06): 11 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): The quoted wording 'مما في بطونها' is 23:21; 16:66 reads 'بطونه'. Both verses carry the nusqīkum/nasqīkum variance, so the point stands, but the verse reference should not be 16:66 alone; notes/2 (reworded): Reading attribution (Ḥafṣ Form IV; Nāfiʿ and others Form I) not from the Mufradāt; not verified here; members/1/ayat/2/why (reworded): He quotes 23:21 (buṭūnihā), not 16:66 (buṭūnihī). If the member ayah is 23:21, the fix is unnecessary — check the ref

meaning.en: to give to drink, to water

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, dati nekome ono što pije. U Kur'anu je to čin davanja pića: peharnik poji svoga gospodara, Musa napaja stado dviju žena, njiva se zalijeva, Ibrahim kaže da ga Allah poji, a Gospodar daje stanovnicima Dženneta čisto piće.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to give someone what he drinks. In the Quran it is the act of giving a drink: a cupbearer gives his master drink, Moses waters the two women's flock, a field is watered, Abraham says that Allah gives him drink, and the Lord gives the people of Paradise a pure drink.

why.bs: Ibrahim: „I Koji me hrani i poji“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Abraham: “And Who feedeth me and watereth me” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Pa im on napoji stado, a zatim se skloni u hlad“ – Musa, pojedinačno djelo.
why.en: “So he watered (their flock) for them. Then he turned aside into the shade” — Moses, a single act.

why.bs: „I njihov Gospodar napojio ih je čistim pićem“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet za sakā.
why.en: “Their Lord will slake their thirst with a pure drink” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah for saqā.

meaning.bs: dati vode za piće, opskrbiti pićem

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, isqāʾ je jači od saqy: učiniti nekome izvor iz kojeg pije kako hoće, kao kad se kaže ‚dao sam mu rijeku‘. U Kur'anu je to kiša i obilna voda, te mlijeko iz stoke.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, isqāʾ is stronger than saqy: to make for someone a source he drinks from as he wishes, as one says ‘I gave him a river’. In the Quran it is rain and abundant water, and milk from cattle.

why.bs: „…pa smo s neba spustili vodu i dali vam je za piće, a niste vi njeni čuvari“ – ar-Rāġib: učinili smo je izvorom vašeg pića.
why.en: “And cause water to descend from the sky, and give it you to drink. It is not ye who are the holders of the store thereof” — ar-Rāġib: We made it a supply of drink for you.

why.bs: „I na njoj smo postavili visoka, čvrsto usađena brda i slatkom vas vodom opskrbili“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And placed therein high mountains and given you to drink sweet water therein?” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Opskrbljujemo vas pićem od onoga što je u njihovim utrobama“ – mlijeko stoke; ar-Rāġib, navodeći iste riječi iz 23:21, bilježi i čitanje nasqīkum (I vrsta).
why.en: “We give you to drink of that which is in their bellies” — the milk of cattle; ar-Rāġib, quoting the same words from 23:21, notes the reading nasqīkum (Form I).

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o obrađenoj zemlji i onome što na njoj raste. Ar-Rāġib ih razdvaja po tome čije je djelo: čovjekovo je da zemlju pripremi i baci sjeme, a dati da nikne je Allahovo djelo.
shared.en: Both words speak of cultivated land and what grows on it. Ar-Rāġib sets them apart by whose act each is: man's part is to prepare the soil and cast the seed, while making it grow is Allah's act.

tellApart.bs: Bacanje sjemena i pripremljena, obrađena zemlja, pa i plod rada → حَرْث; ono što nikne i raste, usjev → زَرْع.
tellApart.en: Casting seed and the prepared, tilled land, and so the yield of one's labour → حَرْث; what sprouts and grows, the crop → زَرْع.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حرث, زرع
notes: ar-Rāġib (حرث): ḥarṯ is casting seed into the earth and preparing it for zarʿ; the tilled land is also called ḥarṯ (68:22); from it is imagined the flourishing that results (42:20, the ḥarṯ of the Hereafter and of this world); 2:223 is by way of simile; 2:205 'covers both tilths'. (زرع): zarʿ is causing to grow (inbāt), and in reality that belongs to divine, not human, matters; in 56:63–64 Allah attributes ḥarṯ to them, denies them zarʿ and attributes it to Himself; when said of a man it is because he does the causes; zarʿ is at root a verbal noun used for what is sown (32:27, 44:26).

56:63–64 (أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تَحْرُثُونَ ۝ أَأَنتُمْ تَزْرَعُونَهُ) has the verbs, not the nouns, so it is described in the nuance texts and not cited as a member ayah. 2:223 is not cited (a simile ar-Rāġib explains; it needs more context than a card gives).
The corpus files the plural زُرُوع (26:148, 44:26) under زَرْع.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): all claims OK.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries حرث, زرع (2026-11-06): 23 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, bacanje sjemena u zemlju i njeno pripremanje za usjev; zatim i sama obrađena zemlja, pa i ono što rad donese. U 56:63–64 Allah ljudima pripisuje oranje (تَحْرُثُونَ), a nicanje sebi.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, casting seed into the earth and preparing it for the crop; then the tilled land itself, and also what labour yields. In 56:63–64 Allah ascribes the tilling (تَحْرُثُونَ) to people and the growing to Himself.

why.bs: „Poranite ka svojim njivama (حَرْث), ako hoćete ubrati plodove“ – obrađena zemlja; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Run unto your field (حَرْث) if ye would pluck (the fruit)” — the tilled land; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Ko želi njivu (حَرْث) ahireta, Mi ćemo mu njegovu njivu povećati“ – prema ar-Rāġibu, ono što rad donese.
why.en: “Whoso desireth the harvest (حَرْث) of the Hereafter, We give him increase in its harvest” — according to ar-Rāġib, what labour yields.

why.bs: Davud i Sulejman sude o njivi (حَرْث) u koju su noću zalutale tuđe ovce.
why.en: David and Solomon judge concerning the tilth (حَرْث) into which other people's sheep had strayed by night.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, zarʿ je dati da nikne, a to je u svojoj suštini Allahovo, a ne ljudsko djelo; čovjeku se pripisuje samo zato što čini uzroke. Izvorno glagolska imenica, kaže se i za ono što je posijano: usjev.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, zarʿ is making to grow, and that in its reality is Allah's act, not man's; it is said of a man only because he does the causes. At root a verbal noun, it is said of what is sown: the crop.

why.bs: „…kako Mi tjeramo vodu na suhu zemlju i njome izvodimo usjev (زَرْع)“ – nicanje je Allahovo djelo; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “How We lead the water to the barren land and therewith bring forth crops (زَرْع)” — the growing is Allah's act; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Faraonovi ljudi ostavili su „i usjeve (زُرُوع) i plemenita mjesta“ – množina, koju ar-Rāġib također navodi.
why.en: Pharaoh's people left behind “the cornlands (زُرُوع) and the goodly sites” — the plural, which ar-Rāġib also cites.

why.bs: Ibrahim: „Ja sam, zaista, nastanio dio svoga potomstva u dolini bez usjeva (زَرْع)“ – zemlja na kojoj ništa ne raste.
why.en: Abraham: “Lo! I have settled some of my posterity in an uncultivable valley (غَيْرِ ذِي زَرْعٍ)” — land where nothing grows.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače plovilo na vodi. Razlikuju se po porijeklu riječi koje ar-Rāġib navodi (samo za safīnu) i po tome koliko se u Kur'anu javljaju.
shared.en: Both words mean a craft on the water. They differ in the origin ar-Rāġib gives for the word (only for safīna) and in how often the Quran uses them.

tellApart.bs: Lađa, i za jednu i za više njih, opća riječ za plovidbu i za Nuhovu lađu → فُلْك; brod, imenovan po struganju površine, u Kur'anu u kazivanju o Musau i Hidru i o Nuhovim ljudima → سَفِينَة.
tellApart.en: A ship, said of one or many, the general word for sailing and for Noah's ark → فُلْك; a vessel, named after scraping a surface, in the Quran in the story of Moses and al-Khidr and of Noah's people → سَفِينَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries فلك, سفن
notes: ar-Rāġib (فلك): fulk is the ship (as-safīna), used for one and for many, with a different underlying pattern for each (singular like qufl, plural like ḥumr); he cites 10:22, 2:164, 35:12, 43:12; falak, the course of the stars (21:33), is named so for its likeness to it — a different word in the corpus. (سفن): safn is scraping (naḥt) the surface of a thing (wood, skin; the wind scraping dust off the ground); the safīna is named after safn (18:79), and then by extension any easy mount is likened to it.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 23 / 3 places read): سَفِينَة is only in 18:71, 18:79 (twice) and 29:15 (Noah's ark: 'the people of the ship'); فُلْك is the word for ships people sail (2:164, 10:22, 17:66), for Noah's ark (11:37, 23:27) and for the ship Jonah fled to (37:140).
Decision: bs lađa for فُلْك, brod for سَفِينَة (Korkut uses lađa for both); en ship for فُلْك, vessel for سَفِينَة (Sahih International uses ship for both), so each member keeps its own word.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 flag, fixed: he gives an origin only for safīna.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries فلك, سفن (2026-11-06): 12 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): Only the verse number is off: his quotation matches 35:12, not 16:14

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, lađa – riječ ista za jednu i za više njih. U Kur'anu je to opća riječ za plovidbu (2:164, 17:66) i za Nuhovu lađu (11:37). Riječ فَلَك – putanja zvijezda – po njemu je tako nazvana po sličnosti s njom.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the ship — one word for one and for many. In the Quran it is the general word for sailing (2:164, 17:66) and for Noah's ark (11:37). The word فَلَك, the course of the stars, is in his view named after its likeness to it.

why.bs: „…i u lađama (فُلْك) što morem plove noseći ono od čega ljudi imaju koristi“ – mnoge lađe; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “…and the ships (فُلْك) which run upon the sea with that which is of use to men” — many ships; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Nuhu je rečeno: „Gradi lađu (فُلْك) pred Našim očima i prema Našem nadahnuću“ – jedna lađa.
why.en: Noah is told: “Build the ship (فُلْك) under Our eyes and by Our inspiration” — one ship.

why.bs: „…kad ste na lađama (فُلْك), pa one s njima plove nošene blagim vjetrom…“ – plovidba ljudi.
why.en: “… when ye are in the ships (فُلْك) and they sail with them with a fair breeze…” — people's sailing.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, nazvan po riječi safn – struganje, tesanje površine nečega; zatim se brodu prispodobljuje svako lahko jahalo. U Kur'anu samo u kazivanju o Musau i čovjeku od znanja (18:71, 18:79) i o Nuhovim ljudima (29:15).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, named after safn — scraping, planing the surface of a thing; then any easy mount is likened to it. In the Quran only in the story of Moses and the man of knowledge (18:71, 18:79) and of Noah's people (29:15).

why.bs: „A brod (سَفِينَة) – bio je vlasništvo nekih siromaha koji su na moru radili“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “As for the ship (سَفِينَة), it belonged to poor people working on the river” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I njih dvojica krenuše, pa kad su se ukrcali u brod (سَفِينَة), on ga je probušio.“
why.en: “So they twain set out till, when they were in the ship (سَفِينَة), he made a hole therein.”

why.bs: „Pa smo izbavili njega [Nuha] i ljude u brodu (سَفِينَة), i učinili smo ga znakom za svjetove.“
why.en: “And We rescued him [Noah] and those with him in the ship (سَفِينَة), and made of it a portent for the peoples.”

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi su posude za piće, i sve tri u Kur'anu dolaze u opisu Dženneta. Ar-Rāġibove zasebne definicije razlikuju se po obliku posude i po tome je li u njoj piće.
shared.en: All three words are vessels for drink, and all three come in the Quran in the description of Paradise. Ar-Rāġib's separate definitions differ by the vessel's shape and by whether drink is in it.

tellApart.bs: Posuda s pićem u njoj, a i samo piće → كَأْس; čaša bez drške → أَكْوَاب; ibrik, za koji ar-Rāġib kaže samo da je poznat → أَبَارِيق.
tellApart.en: The vessel with drink in it, and also the drink itself → كَأْس; a cup with no handle → أَكْوَاب; a pitcher, of which ar-Rāġib says only that it is well known → أَبَارِيق.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries كأس, كوب, برق
notes: ar-Rāġib (كأس): the ka's is the vessel with the drink in it, and each of the two alone is also called ka's ('I drank a ka's'; 'a good ka's' meaning the drink); he cites 76:17 and 'ka's min maʿīn'. (كوب): the kūb is a cup (qadaḥ) without a handle, plural akwāb; he cites 56:18. (برق): al-ibrīq maʿrūf — he gives no description beyond 'well known' under the root of lightning; we do not give him an etymology for it.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 6 / 4 / 1 places read): كَأْس (37:45, 52:23, 56:18, 76:5, 76:17, 78:34), أَكْوَاب (43:71, 56:18, 76:15, 88:14) and أَبَارِيق (56:18) are all said of Paradise; 56:18 names all three together. The cards say only what the ayat say.
Bosnian follows Korkut's 56:18 (čaše, ibrici, pehari); English: cup, goblets, pitchers (Sahih International has 'vessels' for akwāb in 56:18 — goblets keeps it apart from the general word).
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: spelling (Džennet throughout the batch).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries كأس, كوب, برق (2026-11-06): 15 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): Mild: make clear the contrast is ours, built from his separate definitions

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, posuda zajedno s pićem u njoj; a i jedno i drugo posebno zove se كَأْس, pa se kaže ‚popio sam pehar‘, misleći na piće.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the vessel together with the drink in it; and each of the two alone is also called كَأْس, so one says ‘I drank a cup’, meaning the drink.

why.bs: „Ondje će biti napajani peharom (كَأْس) čija je primjesa đumbir“ – posuda s pićem; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “There are they watered with a cup (كَأْس) whereof the mixture is of Zanjabil [ginger]” — the vessel with its drink; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „U njemu će jedni drugima dodavati pehar (كَأْس) u kojem nema ni besmislice ni grijeha.“
why.en: “There they pass from hand to hand a cup (كَأْس) wherein is neither vanity nor cause of sin.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, كُوب je čaša bez drške; أَكْوَاب je njena množina. U Kur'anu sva četiri puta u opisu Dženneta.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a كُوب is a cup without a handle; أَكْوَاب is its plural. In the Quran all four times in the description of Paradise.

why.bs: „…sa čašama (أَكْوَاب), ibricima i peharom iz tekućeg izvora“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet za čašu bez drške.
why.en: “With bowls (أَكْوَاب) and ewers and a cup from a pure spring” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah for the handleless cup.

why.bs: „I kružit će se među njima sa srebrenim posudama i čašama (أَكْوَاب) koje su kao staklo.“
why.en: “Goblets of silver are brought round for them, and beakers (أَكْوَاب) (as) of glass.”

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib je spominje pod korijenom munje (برق) i kaže samo da je ibrik poznat. U Kur'anu jednom, uz čaše i pehar.
nuance.en: Ar-Rāġib mentions it under the root of lightning (برق) and says only that the pitcher is well known. In the Quran once, beside the goblets and the cup.

why.bs: „…sa čašama, ibricima (أَبَارِيق) i peharom iz tekućeg izvora“ – jedino mjesto u Kur'anu.
why.en: “With bowls and ewers (أَبَارِيق) and a cup from a pure spring” — the only place in the Quran.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o planinama. جَبَل je samo ime planine; رَوَاسِي ih imenuje po jednom svojstvu – po tome što su čvrsto usađene.
shared.en: Both words speak of mountains. جَبَل is the plain name of the mountain; رَوَاسِي names them by one quality — that they are firmly set.

tellApart.bs: Planina kao takva, i u slikama čvrstine i veličine → جَبَل; ono što je čvrsto usađeno, planine kao oslonac Zemlje → رَوَاسِي.
tellApart.en: The mountain as such, also in images of firmness and greatness → جَبَل; what is firmly set, the mountains as the earth's anchors → رَوَاسِي.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries جبل, رسا
notes: ar-Rāġib (جبل): jabal, plural ajbāl and jibāl (78:7, 79:32, 24:43, 35:27, 20:105, 26:149); its meanings are taken over: firmness ('so-and-so is a mountain that does not budge'), one's innate nature (jabalahu Allāh ʿalā…), and greatness — jibill for a great crowd (36:62). (رسا): rasā is to stand firm, arsāhu to make it firm; 34:13 'qudūr rāsiyāt'; 77:27 'rawāsiya šāmiḵāt' = firm mountains; 79:32 points to 78:7 (the mountains as pegs).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 37 / 10 places read): رَوَاسِي is said nine times of what Allah has placed in the earth (جَعَلَ / أَلْقَى), three times with 'lest it shift with you' (16:15, 21:31, 31:10); the tenth place (34:13) is the firm-standing cauldrons of Solomon. The scenes of the Last Day (18:47, 20:105, 52:10, 77:10, 78:20, 81:3, 101:5) all use الْجِبَال, never رَوَاسِي.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 flag, fixed: 34:13 is رَاسِيَات (same root, another word), so رَوَاسِي is nine times, always of the earth.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Opća riječ za planinu. Ar-Rāġib kaže da je iz nje izvedena slika čvrstine (‚planina koja se ne pomjera‘), urođene naravi i veličine. U Kur'anu se ovom riječju opisuje i kako se planine na Sudnjem danu pomjeraju i raspadaju.
nuance.en: The general word for mountain. Ar-Rāġib says images of firmness (‘a mountain that does not budge’), of innate nature and of greatness are drawn from it. In the Quran this word also describes how the mountains move and crumble on the Last Day.

why.bs: „A planine (جِبَال) je učvrstio (أَرْسَاهَا)“ – ime planine s glagolom istog korijena kao رَوَاسِي; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And He made fast (أَرْسَاهَا) the hills (جِبَال)” — the name of the mountain with a verb of the root of رَوَاسِي; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Da ovaj Kur'an spustimo na neku planinu (جَبَل), vidio bi je kako je ponizna i kako puca od straha pred Allahom“ – slika čvrstoga koje se predaje.
why.en: “If We had caused this Qur'an to descend upon a mountain (جَبَل), thou verily hadst seen it humbled, rent asunder by the fear of Allah” — an image of the firm thing yielding.

why.bs: „I planine (جِبَال) će se silno kretati“ – Sudnji dan.
why.en: “And the mountains (جِبَال) move away with (awful) movement” — the Last Day.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od rasā – stajati čvrsto; رَوَاسِي su čvrsto usađene planine. U Kur'anu se riječ javlja devet puta, uvijek uz Zemlju u koju ih je Allah postavio, a tri puta uz „kako se ne bi zanjihala pod vama“ (16:15); isti korijen daje i „nepomične kotlove“ (رَاسِيَات, 34:13).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from rasā, to stand firm; رَوَاسِي are firmly set mountains. In the Quran the word comes nine times, always with the earth in which Allah has placed them, three of them with “that it quake not with you” (16:15); the same root also gives “boilers built into the ground” (رَاسِيَات, 34:13).

why.bs: „I bacio je na Zemlju čvrsto usađena brda (رَوَاسِي) da se s vama ne ljulja.“
why.en: “And He hath cast into the earth firm hills (رَوَاسِي) that it quake not with you.”

why.bs: „I na njoj smo postavili visoka, čvrsto usađena brda (رَوَاسِي)“ – ar-Rāġib: čvrste planine.
why.en: “And placed therein high [firm] mountains (رَوَاسِي)” — ar-Rāġib: firm mountains.

why.bs: Džini su Sulejmanu pravili „i nepomične kotlove (رَاسِيَات)“ – isto svojstvo čvrstine, izvan planina; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: The jinn made for Solomon “boilers built into the ground (رَاسِيَات)” — the same quality of firmness, outside mountains; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače uzeti nešto u ruku ili ne pustiti ga, i oba se kažu za uskraćivanje. Razlikuju se po pokretu: jedan je skupljanje šake, drugi je držanje i čuvanje onoga što se drži.
shared.en: Both verbs mean to take a thing in hand or not let it go, and both are said of withholding. They differ in the movement: one is closing the hand, the other is holding and keeping what is held.

tellApart.bs: Uhvatiti cijelom šakom, skupiti, uskratiti – i za Allaha: uskraćuje i daje, kako Njemu priliči → قَبَضَ; prihvatiti se nečega i čuvati ga, držati da ne padne, zadržati → أَمْسَكَ.
tellApart.en: To grasp with the whole hand, to draw in, to withhold — and of Allah: He withholds and grants, as befits Him → قَبَضَ; to hold on to a thing and keep it, hold it up so it does not fall, keep back → أَمْسَكَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries قبض, مسك, بسط
notes: ar-Rāġib (قبض): qabḍ is taking a thing with the whole palm; closing the hand on a thing after taking it, or closing it before taking it, which is holding back (imsāk) from it — hence holding the hand back from giving is called qabḍ: 9:67 'yaqbiḍūna aydiyahum' = they refrain from spending; on 2:245 'yaqbiḍu wa yabsuṭu' he gives several readings: He takes away at one time and gives at another, or from some and to others, or gathers and scatters, or causes death and gives life; 25:46 is the shade withdrawn by the sun. (مسك): imsāk is holding on to a thing and keeping it (al-taʿalluq bihi wa ḥifẓuhu): 2:229, and 22:65 'yumsiku as-samāʾa' = preserves it; amsaktu ʿanhu = I withheld; imsāk is used as a metonymy for stinginess.
Quranic usage: 67:19 has both verbs — the birds spread and fold (يَقْبِضْنَ) their wings, and none holds them up (يُمْسِكُهُنَّ) but the Most Merciful.
Not cited: 33:37 (said to the Prophet).

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 flag, fixed: 2:245 given as one of the several readings he lists, as befits Him; 'holding back' left to أَمْسَكَ.

meaning.en: to clench, to draw in, to withhold

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, uhvatiti cijelom šakom; skupiti ruku na nečemu kad se uzme, ili prije nego se uzme – a to je ustezanje od toga, pa ‚stisnuti ruke‘ znači ne davati. Kad je Allah subjekt (2:245), on navodi više tumačenja, među njima da On jednom oduzima, a drugi put daje, kako Njemu priliči.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to grasp with the whole palm; to close the hand on a thing after taking it, or before taking it — which is refraining from it, so ‘to clench the hands’ means not to give. With Allah as subject (2:245) he gives several readings, among them that He takes away at one time and gives at another, as befits Him.

why.bs: „Allah uskraćuje (يَقْبِضُ) i proširuje“ – ar-Rāġib navodi više tumačenja: oduzima pa daje, jednima oduzima a drugima daje, ili usmrćuje i oživljava; kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “Allah straiteneth (يَقْبِضُ) and enlargeth” — ar-Rāġib gives several readings: He takes away and gives, takes from some and gives to others, or causes death and gives life; as befits Him.

why.bs: Licemjeri „stežu (يَقْبِضُونَ) svoje ruke“ – prema ar-Rāġibu, ustežu se od trošenja.
why.en: The hypocrites “withhold (يَقْبِضُونَ) their hands” — according to ar-Rāġib, they refrain from spending.

why.bs: Ptice nad njima, „kako šire krila i skupljaju ih (يَقْبِضْنَ)“ – skupljanje; a drži ih samo Milostivi (أَمْسَكَ).
why.en: The birds above them, “spreading out their wings and closing them (يَقْبِضْنَ)” — drawing in; and none holds them up but the Most Merciful (أَمْسَكَ).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, prihvatiti se nečega i čuvati ga; zato Allah ‚drži‘ nebo da ne padne, tj. čuva ga, kako Njemu priliči. Kaže se i za zadržavanje supruge u braku, a ‚zadržati‘ kod njega je i slika škrtosti.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to hold on to a thing and keep it; so Allah ‘holds’ the sky lest it fall, that is, preserves it, as befits Him. It is said of keeping a wife in marriage, and ‘holding back’ is for him also an image of stinginess.

why.bs: „Allah, zaista, drži (يُمْسِكُ) nebesa i Zemlju da ne nestanu“ – drži i čuva, kako Njemu priliči (ar-Rāġib tako tumači 22:65).
why.en: “Lo! Allah graspeth (يُمْسِكُ) the heavens and the earth that they deviate not” — holds and preserves, as befits Him (so ar-Rāġib explains 22:65).

why.bs: „A kad dođu do kraja svoga roka, zadržite ih (أَمْسِكُوهُنَّ) na lijep način ili se od njih na lijep način rastavite“ – zadržati u braku.
why.en: “Then, when they have reached their term, take them back (أَمْسِكُوهُنَّ) in kindness or part from them in kindness” — keeping in marriage.

why.bs: „Kad biste vi posjedovali riznice milosti moga Gospodara, sigurno biste ih zadržali (أَمْسَكْتُمْ) iz straha od trošenja“ – zadržavanje kao škrtost.
why.en: “If ye possessed the treasures of the mercy of my Lord, ye would surely hold them back (أَمْسَكْتُمْ) for fear of spending” — holding back as stinginess.

title.en: To spread out and to draw out

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače da se nešto širi dalje od sebe, i oba se kažu za ruku i za Zemlju. Ar-Rāġib i sam objašnjava pružanje ruke (بَسْط) kao njeno ‚mad‘, pa se značenja dodiruju; po njegovim definicijama (širenje naspram vučenja) razlikuju se po pravcu: jedan je širenje u širinu, drugi izvlačenje u dužinu.
shared.en: Both verbs mean that a thing reaches out beyond itself, and both are said of the hand and of the earth. Ar-Rāġib himself explains reaching out the hand (بَسْط) as its ‘madd’, so the meanings touch; by his definitions (spreading vs. pulling) they differ in direction: one is spreading in breadth, the other drawing out in length.

tellApart.bs: Raširiti i proširiti – prostirku, oblak, ruku, opskrbu → بَسَطَ; vući, izvlačiti u dužinu – sjenu, Zemlju, rok, kaznu → مَدَّ.
tellApart.en: To spread and widen — a carpet, the clouds, the hand, provision → بَسَطَ; to pull, to draw out in length — the shade, the earth, a span of time, punishment → مَدَّ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries بسط, مد
notes: ar-Rāġib (بسط): basṭ of a thing is spreading it out and widening it — sometimes both are meant, sometimes one; bisāṭ is anything spread (71:19); 42:27 law basaṭa = had He widened (provision); basṭ al-yad is madduhā, extending the hand: for asking (13:14), taking (6:93), attacking (60:2) and giving (5:64). (مد): the root of madd is pulling (al-jarr); hence mudda, a stretch of time; 25:45 'madda ẓ-ẓill'; imdād comes mostly in what is liked and madd in what is disliked (19:79, 2:15, 7:202); 31:27 yamudduhu is from 'one river feeds another', not from that.
Not cited: 15:88 and 20:131 (said to the Prophet), 2:15 (Allah's act needs more tafsir than a card gives).

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: 42:27 en without '[excessively]'; his liked/disliked contrast confined to madd as supplying (25:45, 13:3 are neutral stretching).

meaning.en: to spread out, to reach out, to widen

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, raširiti nešto i proširiti ga. Pružiti ruku znači ispružiti je – da se traži, uzme, napadne ili da. Kad Allah proširuje opskrbu, znači da je čini obilnom, kako Njemu priliči.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to spread a thing out and widen it. To reach out the hand is to extend it — to ask, take, attack or give. When Allah widens provision, it means He makes it ample, as befits Him.

why.bs: „A da Allah proširi (بَسَطَ) opskrbu Svojim robovima, oni bi se na Zemlji osilili“ – prema ar-Rāġibu, učinio je obilnom.
why.en: “And if Allah were to enlarge (بَسَطَ) the provision for His slaves they would surely rebel in the earth” — according to ar-Rāġib, made it ample.

why.bs: Ademov sin bratu: „Ako ti pružiš (بَسَطْتَ) prema meni svoju ruku da me ubiješ, ja svoju ruku neću pružiti prema tebi“ – pružiti ruku za napad.
why.en: Adam's son to his brother: “Even if thou stretch out (بَسَطْتَ) thy hand against me to kill me, I shall not stretch out my hand against thee” — the hand reached out to attack.

why.bs: „Allah je Onaj Koji šalje vjetrove, pa oni pokreću oblake, i On ih rasprostire (يَبْسُطُ) po nebu kako hoće“ – širenje u širinu.
why.en: “Allah is He Who sendeth the winds so that they raise clouds, and spreadeth them (يَبْسُطُ) along the sky as pleaseth Him” — spreading in breadth.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, izvorno vući, izvlačiti; odatle i مُدَّة – vrijeme koje se proteže. Kad znači opskrbljivati nekoga, on primjećuje da Form IV (أَمَدَّ) najčešće dolazi o onome što je drago, a مَدَّ o onome što je mrsko – kao produžena kazna.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, at root to pull, to draw out; hence مُدَّة, time that stretches on. When it means supplying someone, he notes that Form IV (أَمَدَّ) comes mostly of what is liked, and مَدَّ of what is disliked — such as punishment drawn out.

why.bs: „Zar ne vidiš kako je tvoj Gospodar protegao (مَدَّ) sjenu“ – izvlačenje u dužinu; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Hast thou not seen how thy Lord hath spread [drawn out] (مَدَّ) the shade” — drawing out in length; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „On je Taj Koji je protegao (مَدَّ) Zemlju i na njoj postavio čvrsto usađena brda i rijeke.“
why.en: “And He it is Who spread out [stretched out] (مَدَّ) the earth and placed therein firm hills and flowing streams.”

why.bs: „…i produžit ćemo (نَمُدُّ) mu kaznu“ – prema ar-Rāġibu, مَدَّ o onome što je mrsko.
why.en: “… and prolong (نَمُدُّ) for him a span of torment” — according to ar-Rāġib, مَدَّ of what is disliked.

shared.bs: Obje riječi se kažu za bračnog druga. زَوْج je svaki od dvoje koji čine par – i muž i žena, i više od braka; بَعْل je muž, jer se na njega gledalo kao na onoga ko stoji nad ženom, a otuda i sve što stoji nad drugim.
shared.en: Both words are said of a marriage partner. زَوْج is each of the two who make a pair — husband or wife, and more than marriage; بَعْل is the husband, since he was seen as standing over the woman, and from that anything that stands over another.

tellApart.bs: Jedan od dvoje u paru – supružnik, muž ili žena, a i par, vrsta → زَوْج; muž, muški od dvoje supružnika → بَعْل.
tellApart.en: One of a pair — a spouse, husband or wife, and also a pair, a kind → زَوْج; the husband, the male of the two spouses → بَعْل.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries زوج, بعل
notes: ar-Rāġib (زوج): zawj is each of the pair, male and female, among animals that pair, and each of any two that go together, like or opposite; 2:35 'anta wa zawjuka'; zawja (with tāʾ) is 'a poor usage' (luġa radīʾa); 51:49 shows that everything in the world is a zawj, having an opposite, a like, or composition, so that Allah alone is the One (al-fard); 20:53 azwāj = kinds; 6:143 = sorts. (بعل): baʿl is the male of the two spouses (11:72), plural buʿūla (2:228); since the man was seen as standing over the woman, her manager (4:34), anything standing over another was called baʿl, and so the Arabs called the god they worshipped Baʿl (37:125).

Count: the corpus files بُعُولَة (2:228, 24:31) under بَعْل, and the 7 include 37:125, the idol Baʿl — so the card counts every place of the word, not only 'husband'. The corpus has no زَوْجَة: the Quran says زَوْج for a wife too, as ar-Rāġib's remark implies.
Not cited: 33:37 (said to the Prophet); the later observation that the Quran says زَوْج where there is harmony and بَعْل where there is not is not ar-Rāġib's and is left out.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: بَعْل extended, as he says, to anything that stands over another (37:125 the idol Baʿl); the verifier's wording kept ('since the husband was seen as standing over the woman'), not 'named for'.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries زوج, بعل (2026-11-06): 21 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/nuance (reworded): Direction of the derivation is reversed in our text: the husband sense is primary; 'standing over' explains the extension to others

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, svaki od dvoje koji čine par, muški ili ženski, i svako od dvoje što idu zajedno – slični ili suprotni. Riječ je ista za muža i za ženu (oblik زَوْجَة on smatra slabim jezikom), a znači i vrstu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, each of the two who make a pair, male or female, and each of any two that go together — alike or opposite. The word is the same for husband and wife (the form زَوْجَة he calls poor usage), and it also means a kind.

why.bs: „O Ademe, nastani se ti i tvoja supruga (زَوْج) u Džennetu“ – ista riječ za ženu; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “O Adam! Dwell thou and thy wife (زَوْج) in the Garden” — the same word for a wife; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I od svake stvari stvorili smo par (زَوْجَيْنِ)“ – prema ar-Rāġibu, sve ima suprotnost, sličnost ili sastav, a samo je Allah Jedan.
why.en: “And all things We have created by pairs (زَوْجَيْنِ)” — according to ar-Rāġib, everything has an opposite, a like or a composition, and Allah alone is the One.

why.bs: „…i njome smo izveli razne vrste (أَزْوَاج) bilja“ – prema ar-Rāġibu, vrste.
why.en: “… and thereby We have brought forth divers kinds (أَزْوَاج) of vegetation” — according to ar-Rāġib, kinds.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, muški od dvoje supružnika; budući da je muž viđen kao onaj koji je nad ženom, kao onaj koji se o njoj stara i odgovoran je za nju (4:34). Zato se بَعْل zvalo i ono što je iznad drugog, pa i idol Baal (37:125), koji se također broji u ovoj riječi.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the male of the two spouses; since the husband was seen as standing over the woman, as the one who looks after her and is in charge of her (4:34). So whatever stood over another was called بَعْل, and so the idol Baʿl (37:125), which is also counted under this word.

why.bs: Ibrahimova žena: „Zar ću ja roditi, a starica sam, i ovaj moj muž (بَعْل) je starac?“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Abraham's wife: “Shall I bear a child when I am an old woman, and this my husband (بَعْل) is an old man?” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A njihovi muževi (بُعُولَة) imaju više prava da ih u tom razdoblju vrate“ – množina; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And their husbands (بُعُولَة) would do better to take them back in that case” — the plural; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Ilijas svom narodu: „Zar Baala (بَعْل) prizivate, a ostavljate najboljeg Stvoritelja?“ – prema ar-Rāġibu, ime za ono što se smatralo nadređenim.
why.en: Elias to his people: “Will ye cry unto Baal (بَعْل) and forsake the Best of creators” — according to ar-Rāġib, a name for what was held to stand above.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače izlazak iz onoga što Allah traži. Ar-Rāġib svaku izvodi iz druge slike: izlazak iz okvira, raskidanje zastora, odupiranje štapom.
shared.en: All three words mean going out of what Allah requires. Ar-Rāġib derives each from another image: leaving a bound, tearing a veil, resisting with a staff.

tellApart.bs: Izaći iz okvira šerijata, kao datula iz kore – i manjim i većim grijesima, a obično kad ih je mnogo → فَاسِق; raskinuti zastor vjere, otvoreni grijeh → فَاجِر; ne poslušati, izaći iz poslušnosti → عَصَى.
tellApart.en: To go out of the bounds of the Sharia, as a ripe date out of its skin — by small or great sins, though customarily of many → فَاسِق; to tear the veil of religion, open sin → فَاجِر; to disobey, to leave obedience → عَصَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries فسق, فجر, عصا
notes: ar-Rāġib (فسق): fasaqa = went out of the bounds (ḥijr) of the Sharia, from fasaqa ar-ruṭab, the ripe date coming out of its skin; it is more general than kufr; it happens with few or many sins but is customarily said of many; fāsiq is mostly said of one who accepted the Sharia's ruling and then broke all or some of it, and when an original unbeliever is called fāsiq it is because he broke what reason and the fiṭra required of him; 32:18 sets it against faith; 'the fāsiq is more general than the kāfir, and the ẓālim more general than the fāsiq'; he cites 24:4; Ibn al-Aʿrābī: fāsiq as a description of a person was not heard in Arab speech before. (فجر): fajr is splitting widely; fujūr is tearing the veil of religion (šaqq sitr ad-diyāna); fājir, plural fujjār and fajara (82:14, 83:7, 80:42); the liar is called fājir because lying is part of fujūr. (عصا): ʿaṣā ʿiṣyānan = went out of obedience, at root 'to resist with one's staff'; he cites 4:14, 10:91.

The corpus files فَجَرَة (80:42) under فُجّار; the member sums فُجّار (4) and the singular فَاجِر (71:27), one word. Quranic usage (our observation, all 5 places read): the fujjār are set against the abrār (82:13–14; 83:7 with 83:18) and against the muttaqūn (38:28).
عَصَى of Adam (20:121) is not cited (a prophet; the Quran itself adds his repentance and choosing, 20:122); 71:27 is not cited.

meaning.bs: fasik, onaj koji izlazi iz granica vjere

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, onaj ko izađe iz okvira šerijata, kao datula iz svoje kore; šire od nevjerstva. Može biti i s malo grijeha, ali se obično kaže kad ih je mnogo, i najčešće za onoga ko je prihvatio vjerske propise pa ih krši.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, one who goes out of the bounds of the Sharia, as a ripe date out of its skin; wider than unbelief. It can be by few sins, but is customarily said when they are many, and mostly of one who accepted the religious rulings and then breaks them.

why.bs: „Pa zar je vjernik isti kao onaj ko je fasik (فَاسِق)? Ne izjednačuju se!“ – ar-Rāġib: suprotstavljen vjeri.
why.en: “Is he who is a believer like unto him who is an evil-liver (فَاسِق)? They are not alike” — ar-Rāġib: set against faith.

why.bs: Oni koji potvore čestite žene, a ne dovedu četiri svjedoka, „upravo su oni fasici (فَاسِقُون)“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Those who accuse chaste women and do not produce four witnesses — “They indeed are evil-doers (فَاسِقُون)”; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Ako vam fasik (فَاسِق) donese kakvu vijest, provjerite je.“
why.en: “If an evil-liver (فَاسِق) bring you tidings, verify it.”

meaning.bs: razvratnik, onaj koji razdire zastor vjere

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od fajr – široko rascijepiti; fudžur je raskidanje zastora vjere. Lažov se zove فَاجِر jer je laž dio toga. U Kur'anu su فُجَّار suprotstavljeni dobrima (أَبْرَار) i bogobojaznima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from fajr, to split widely; fujūr is tearing the veil of religion. The liar is called فَاجِر because lying is part of it. In the Quran the فُجَّار are set against the righteous (أَبْرَار) and the God-fearing.

why.bs: „A razvratnici (فُجَّار) će, zaista, u ognju biti“ – iza 82:13, gdje su dobri (أَبْرَار) u blagodatima; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And lo! the wicked (فُجَّار) verily will be in hell” — after 82:13, where the righteous (أَبْرَار) are in delight; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Ili zar ćemo bogobojazne učiniti kao razvratnike (فُجَّار)?“
why.en: “Or shall We treat the pious as the wicked (فُجَّار)?”

why.bs: „Oni su ti nevjernici, ti razvratnici (فَجَرَة)“ – nevjerstvo i razvrat zajedno; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Those are the disbelievers, the wicked (فَجَرَة)” — unbelief and wickedness together; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, izaći iz poslušnosti; izvorno – oduprijeti se svojim štapom (عَصًا).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to go out of obedience; at root, to resist with one's staff (عَصًا).

why.bs: „A ko se protivi (يَعْصِ) Allahu i Njegovom Poslaniku i prelazi Njegove granice…“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And whoso disobeyeth (يَعْصِ) Allah and His messenger and transgresseth His limits…” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: O melekima nad vatrom: „koji se ne protive (لَا يَعْصُونَ) Allahu u onome što im naredi“ – poslušnost suprotno neposlušnosti.
why.en: Of the angels over the Fire: “who resist not (لَا يَعْصُونَ) Allah in that which He commandeth them” — obedience as the opposite.

why.bs: Faraonu u času utapanja: „Zar tek sada, a ranije si bio neposlušan (عَصَيْتَ)?“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: To Pharaoh as he drowned: “What! Now! When hitherto thou hast rebelled (عَصَيْتَ)” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o onome od čega čovjek ima koristi u životu. Razlikuju se po tome šta naglašavaju: jedna ono što se daje, druga korištenje koje traje neko vrijeme.
shared.en: Both words speak of what a person benefits from in life. They differ in what they stress: one what is given, the other a use that lasts a while.

tellApart.bs: Ono što se daje i dodjeljuje – na ovom i na onom svijetu, udio, hrana, pa i znanje → رِزْق; korist koja traje neko vrijeme, prolazno uživanje, pa i stvari koje se koriste → مَتَاع.
tellApart.en: What is given and allotted — in this world and the next, a share, food, and knowledge too → رِزْق; benefit that lasts for a time, passing enjoyment, and also the goods one uses → مَتَاع.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رزق, متع
notes: ar-Rāġib (رزق): rizq is said of a continuing gift, of this world or the next; of a share (naṣīb); and of what reaches the stomach and nourishes; 63:10 'spend from what We have provided you' covers wealth, standing and knowledge; 18:19 'bi-rizqin minhu' = food; on 51:22 'it was said' (qīla) the rain is meant; 3:169 and 19:62 are the rizq of the Hereafter; ar-razzāq is said only of Allah. (متع): mutūʿ is extending and rising; matāʿ is benefit extended over time (intifāʿ mumtadd al-waqt); 2:36/7:24 'mustaqarrun wa matāʿun ilā ḥīn' tells that each person has an enjoyment in this world for a known span; 'matāʿ of this world is little' (4:77) — of no account beside the Hereafter (13:26); what is used in a house is matāʿ; 12:65 matāʿahum = their food, or it was said their containers; the gift to a divorced woman is matāʿ (2:241).
Not cited: 56:82 (ar-Rāġib reads rizq there as 'share'; tafsir differs).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, dar koji neprestano pristiže – ovosvjetski ili onosvjetski; zatim udio, i ono što se pojede i od čega se hrani. U „udjeljujte od opskrbe koju smo vam dali“ (2:254) obuhvata, kaže on, imetak, ugled i znanje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a gift that keeps coming — of this world or of the next; then a share, and what is eaten and nourishes. In “spend of that wherewith We have provided you” (2:254) it covers, he says, wealth, standing and knowledge.

why.bs: Stanovnici pećine: „neka razmotri koje je ondje jelo najčistije, pa neka vam od toga donese opskrbu (رِزْق)“ – prema ar-Rāġibu, hrana.
why.en: The people of the cave: “let him see what food is purest there and bring you a supply (رِزْق) thereof” — according to ar-Rāġib, food.

why.bs: „I u njemu će imati svoju opskrbu (رِزْق) ujutro i navečer“ – prema ar-Rāġibu, onosvjetski dar.
why.en: “And therein they have food (رِزْق) for morn and evening” — according to ar-Rāġib, the gift of the Hereafter.

why.bs: „A na nebu je vaša opskrba (رِزْق)“ – kod ar-Rāġiba: ‚kaže se‘ da je to kiša.
why.en: “And in the heaven is your providence (رِزْق)” — in ar-Rāġib: ‘it was said’ that the rain is meant.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, korist koja se proteže kroz vrijeme. Zato je ovaj svijet مَتَاع – uživanje za određeni rok, malo prema budućem svijetu; a مَتَاع su i stvari koje se koriste, kao prtljag i hrana.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a benefit that stretches over time. So this world is مَتَاع — enjoyment for a set span, little beside the Hereafter; and مَتَاع is also the goods one uses, such as baggage and food.

why.bs: „Na Zemlji ćete imati boravište i uživanje (مَتَاع) do jednog vremena“ – prema ar-Rāġibu, svako ima uživanje u ovom svijetu za poznati rok.
why.en: “There will be for you on earth a habitation and provision [enjoyment] (مَتَاع) for a while” — according to ar-Rāġib, each person has an enjoyment in this world for a known span.

why.bs: „A život na ovom svijetu prema ahiretu tek je prolazno uživanje (مَتَاع)“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Whereas the life of the world is but brief comfort (مَتَاع) as compared with the Hereafter” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I kad otvoriše svoj prtljag (مَتَاع), nađoše da im je roba vraćena“ – prema ar-Rāġibu, njihova hrana, a kaže se i njihove vreće.
why.en: “And when they opened their belongings (مَتَاع) they discovered that their merchandise had been returned to them” — according to ar-Rāġib, their food, or, it was said, their containers.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače kretanje odozgo prema dolje. Razlikuju se po tome kako se to kretanje vidi: kao pad i silazak koji se nameće, ili kao spuštanje s visine.
shared.en: Both words mean moving from above to below. They differ in how that movement is seen: as a fall and a descent that is imposed, or as coming down from a height.

tellApart.bs: Spuštanje s visine, opća riječ; u Kur'anu za Kur'an, istinu i ono što s neba dolazi → نَزَلَ; silazak kao pad kamena, koji ar-Rāġib vidi kao spuštanje ‚silom‘ → هَبَطَ.
tellApart.en: Coming down from a height, the general word; in the Quran for the Quran, the truth and what comes down from the sky → نَزَلَ; a descent like a stone's fall, which ar-Rāġib sees as a going down ‘by compulsion’ → هَبَطَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries هبط, نزل
notes: ar-Rāġib (هبط): hubūṭ is descent by way of compulsion (ʿalā sabīl al-qahr), like the falling of a stone; the verb is intransitive and transitive in one form; cites 2:74; when said of man it is by way of belittlement (istiḫfāf), unlike inzāl, which Allah mentions for things whose honour He points out (the angels, the Quran, rain); hubūṭ is mentioned where lowering is meant: 2:36, 7:13, 2:61 (he adds that 'you will have what you asked' in 2:61 holds no honour, citing the ḏilla that follows). (نزل): nuzūl is at root a coming down from a height (inḥiṭāṭ min ʿuluww); inzāl of His favours and punishments is either sending the thing itself (the Quran) or its means (iron, clothing); tanazzul is said of the angel bringing something, not of Allah; 26:193 nazala bihi r-rūḥu l-amīn.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 8 / 6 places read): هَبَطَ is an imperative in 7 of its 8 places — to Adam and his wife and Iblīs (2:36, 2:38, 7:24, 20:123), to Iblīs alone (7:13), to the Children of Israel (2:61), and to Nūḥ, who goes down 'with peace and blessings' (11:48), a counter-example to the 'belittlement' reading; 2:74 is the stones that fall for fear of Allah. نَزَلَ (Form I) is said of the Quran and the truth (17:105, 26:193, 57:16), of what comes down from the sky (34:2, 57:4) and of the punishment descending on a people's yard (37:177). The Adam ayat are not cited: ar-Rāġib's 'belittlement' reading of them is not put on a prophet here. The inzāl/tanzīl contrast (Forms IV/II) is in anzala-nazzala.
