meaning.en: to go down, to descend (as a fall)

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, hubūṭ je spuštanje ‚silom‘, kao kad kamen pada. Kad se kaže za čovjeka, on u tome vidi umanjivanje, za razliku od inzāla (iz korijena نَزَلَ), kojim Allah spominje ono čiju čast ističe – meleke, Kur'an, kišu. U Kur'anu je to gotovo uvijek zapovijed ‚Siđi(te)!‘; ipak, Nuh silazi „s mirom od Nas i blagoslovima“ (11:48), pa ovo nije pravilo bez izuzetka.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, hubūṭ is a descent ‘by compulsion’, as a stone falls. When said of a person, he sees belittlement in it, unlike inzāl (from the root of نَزَلَ), which Allah uses for what He honours — the angels, the Quran, rain. In the Quran it is almost always the command ‘Go down!’; yet Noah goes down “with peace from Us and blessings” (11:48), so this is no rule without exception.

why.bs: „A ima, zaista, i kamenja što od straha pred Allahom pada dolje“ – kamenje koje silazi padajući; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And indeed there are rocks which fall down for the fear of Allah” — stones going down as they fall; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Iblisu: „Pa siđi odavde, tebi ne priliči da se ovdje oholiš!“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: To Iblīs: “Then go down hence! It is not for thee to show pride here” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „O Nuhu, siđi u miru od Nas, i neka su blagoslovi na tebi“ – silazak s počašću, protuprimjer.
why.en: “O Noah! Go thou down with peace from Us and blessings upon thee” — a descent with honour, a counter-example.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, nuzūl je izvorno spuštanje s visine. U Kur'anu (Form I) tako dolaze Kur'an i istina, ono što se s neba spušta i kazna koja se spusti na neki narod.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, nuzūl is at root a coming down from a height. In the Quran (Form I) the Quran and the truth come down so, as does what comes down from the sky and the punishment that comes down upon a people.

why.bs: „S njim je sišao Povjerljivi Duh (Džibril)“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet pod tanzīlom (čitanje nazzala) i bilježi čitanje nazala, koje je ovdje prikazano.
why.en: “Which the True Spirit hath brought down” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah under tanzīl (the reading nazzala) and notes the reading nazala, the one shown here.

why.bs: „S istinom smo ga spustili i s istinom je on sišao.“
why.en: “With truth have We sent it down, and with truth hath it descended.”

why.bs: „On zna … šta silazi s neba i šta se u nj uspinje“ – spuštanje s visine.
why.en: “He knoweth … that descendeth from the heaven and that which ascendeth into it” — coming down from a height.

title.bs: Uspinjati se, uzdizati se, popeti se

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače kretanje prema gore. Razlikuju se po putu i po onome što se diže: uspon po uspinjalištima, odlazak na visoko mjesto, ili penjanje kao po stepenicama i ljestvama.
shared.en: All three words mean moving upwards. They differ in the way and in what rises: going up by ascents, going to a high place, or climbing as on steps and a ladder.

tellApart.bs: Ići u usponu, kao po stepenicama (مَعَارِج) – meleki, Duh, ‚stvar‘ k Allahu → عَرَجَ; otići na visoko mjesto, a preneseno ono što od roba stiže k Allahu → صَعِدَ; popeti se stepenicama i ljestvama → رَقِيَ.
tellApart.en: Going in ascent, as by stairways (مَعَارِج) — the angels, the Spirit, ‘the matter’ to Allah → عَرَجَ; going to a high place, and figuratively what reaches Allah from the servant → صَعِدَ; climbing steps and a ladder → رَقِيَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عرج, صعد, رقى
notes: ar-Rāġib (عرج): ʿurūǧ is going in ascent (ḏahāb fī ṣuʿūd); cites 70:4 and 15:14; al-maʿāriǧ are al-maṣāʿid, ascents (70:3); the Night of the Miʿrāǧ named for the ascent of supplication in it, pointing to 35:10. (صعد): ṣuʿūd is going into a high place; ṣaʿad and ṣaʿūd are said of a steep slope and borrowed for anything hard (72:17, 74:17); ṣuʿūd is borrowed for what reaches Allah from the servant, as nuzūl is borrowed for what reaches the servant from Allah (35:10). (رقى): raqiya is climbing on steps and a ladder; cites 38:10 (fa-l-yartaqū fī l-asbāb) and 17:93 'wa-lan nuʾmina li-ruqiyyika'.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 5 / 1 / 1 places read): عَرَجَ is said of the angels and the Spirit (70:4), of 'the matter' (32:5), of what rises into the sky (34:2, 57:4), and of the deniers in a hypothetical (15:14). صَعِدَ (Form I) is only 35:10; the Form V يَصَّعَّدُ (6:125) is a different verb and is not cited (6:125 was left out in batch 6). رَقِيَ is only 17:93, in the deniers' demand; the noun رُقِيّ in the same ayah is not counted.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ʿurūǧ je ići u usponu; مَعَارِج su uspinjališta, putevi gore. U Kur'anu se uspinju meleki i Duh, ‚stvar‘ k Allahu i ono što se na nebo diže – kako Njemu priliči.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ʿurūǧ is going in ascent; مَعَارِج are the ascents, the ways up. In the Quran the angels and the Spirit ascend, ‘the matter’ ascends to Allah, and whatever rises into the sky — as befits Him.

why.bs: „K Njemu se uspinju meleki i Duh“ – kako Njemu priliči; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “The angels and the Spirit ascend unto Him” — as befits Him; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… i ono što se uspinje u nj“ – ono što se diže prema nebu.
why.en: “… and that which ascendeth into it” — whatever rises towards the sky.

why.bs: „Pa i da im otvorimo jedna vrata na nebu, i da se oni kroz njih stalno uspinju …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And even if We opened unto them a gate of heaven and they kept mounting through it …” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ṣuʿūd je odlazak na visoko mjesto. On kaže da je preneseno upotrijebljen za ono što od roba stiže k Allahu, kao što je nuzūl upotrijebljen za ono što od Allaha stiže robu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ṣuʿūd is going into a high place. He says it is used figuratively for what reaches Allah from the servant, just as nuzūl is used for what reaches the servant from Allah.

why.bs: „Lijepe riječi uzdižu se do Njega“ – riječi roba koje stižu k Allahu, kako Njemu priliči; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Unto Him good words ascend” — the servant's words reaching Allah, as befits Him; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, penjati se po stepenicama i ljestvama. U Kur'anu se glagol u ovom obliku javlja jednom, u 17:93, gdje nevjernici traže od Poslanika da se popne na nebo (u 38:10 dolazi srodni oblik irtaqā, „neka se popnu“).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, climbing on steps and a ladder. In the Quran the verb in this form occurs once, in 17:93, where the deniers demand that the Prophet climb into the sky (38:10 has the related irtaqā, “let them ascend”).

why.bs: „… ili da se na nebo popneš – a ni penjanju tvome nećemo vjerovati dok nam s neba ne spustiš knjigu da je čitamo“ – zahtjev nevjernika.
why.en: “… or thou ascend up into heaven, and even then we will put no faith in thine ascension till thou bring down for us a book that we can read” — the deniers' demand.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače napustiti ono u čemu se bilo. Ar-Rāġib čak ḫaraǧa objašnjava s baraza; razlika je više u upotrebi: napuštanje mjesta ili stanja, ili izlazak na otvoreno, gdje se postaje vidljiv.
shared.en: Both words mean leaving what one was in. Ar-Rāġib even explains kharaja by baraza; the difference lies more in usage: leaving a place or state, or coming out into the open, where one becomes visible.

tellApart.bs: Napustiti mjesto ili stanje – kuću, grad, odjeću, opća riječ → خَرَجَ; izaći na otvoreno, istupiti pred druge, postati vidljiv → بَرَزَ.
tellApart.en: To leave a place or a state — a house, a town, a garment, the general word → خَرَجَ; to come out into the open, step forth before others, become visible → بَرَزَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries خرج, برز
notes: ar-Rāġib (خرج): ḫaraǧa ḫurūǧan is to come forth (baraza) from one's place or state, whether the place is a house, a town or a garment, and whether the state is in oneself or in its outward causes; cites 28:21, 41:47 (fruits from their sheaths), 40:11 and 5:37 (they want to get out of the Fire and will not). (برز): al-barāz is open ground; baraza is to come into the open, either appearing by itself (18:47 the earth bāriza; mubāraza, coming out of the ranks to fight: 3:154, 2:250), or standing out by merit, or being uncovered of what was hidden (14:21, 14:48, 40:16 yawma hum bārizūn; 26:91 Hell brought forth for the deviators, i.e. they are brought before it).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 53 / 5 places read): خَرَجَ is said of people leaving a house, town or land (28:21, 4:100, 60:1), of the dead rising from graves (30:25, 54:7), of vegetation, drink and pearls coming out (7:58, 16:69, 55:22), and of words from mouths (18:5). بَرَزَ is said of soldiers going forth to battle (2:250, 3:154), of people leaving the Prophet's presence (4:81) and of all creatures coming forth before Allah (14:21, 14:48).

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib definira ḫurūǧ kao napuštanje mjesta ili stanja – kuće, grada ili odjeće, bilo da je stanje u samom čovjeku ili u njegovim vanjskim prilikama. Opća riječ: izlaze ljudi iz kuće i grada, mrtvi iz grobova, bilje iz zemlje, piće iz pčelinjih trbuha.
nuance.en: Ar-Rāġib defines ḫurūǧ as leaving one's place or state — a house, a town or a garment, whether the state is within a person or in his outward circumstances. The general word: people go out of houses and towns, the dead out of graves, plants out of the earth, drink out of the bees' bellies.

why.bs: Musa „izađe iz njega u strahu, iščekujući“ – napušta grad; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Moses “escaped from thence, fearing, vigilant” — he leaves the city; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Iz njihovih utroba izlazi piće različitih boja.“
why.en: “There cometh forth from their bellies a drink divers of hues.”

why.bs: „Poželjet će da izađu iz Vatre, no nikako iz nje neće izaći“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “They will wish to come forth from the Fire, but they will not come forth from it” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, barāz je otvoren prostor, a baraza je izaći na otvoreno: pojaviti se sam po sebi – kao borac koji istupi iz reda – istaknuti se vrlinom ili ostati otkriven kad se skine ono što je skrivalo. Tako na Sudnjem danu svi izlaze pred Allaha.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, barāz is open ground, and baraza is to come out into the open: to appear by oneself — as a fighter steps out of the ranks — to stand out by merit, or to be left uncovered when what hid one is removed. So on the Day of Judgement all come forth before Allah.

why.bs: Talutovi vojnici „kad izađoše na otvoreno pred Džaluta i vojsku njegovu“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Saul's soldiers “when they went into the field against Goliath and his hosts” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Oni kojima je bilo propisano da poginu istupili bi prema mjestima gdje će pasti“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Those appointed to be slain would have gone forth to the places where they were to lie” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… i istupit će pred Allaha, Jedinog, Svemoćnog“ – otkriveni pred Njim; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… and they will come forth unto Allah, the One, the Almighty” — uncovered before Him; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o odlasku. Ar-Rāġib čak jednu objašnjava drugom; razlika je više u upotrebi: odlazak od nečega i nestanak, ili prolazak i nastavljanje puta do kraja.
shared.en: Both words speak of going. Ar-Rāġib even explains one by the other; the difference lies more in usage: going away from something and vanishing, or passing through and carrying on to the end.

tellApart.bs: Otići od nekoga ili nečega, nestati; s بِـ ‚odnijeti‘ → ذَهَبَ; proći kroz nešto i ići dalje, a za ljude i običaje – biti prošlost → مَضَى.
tellApart.en: To go away from someone or something, to vanish; with بِـ ‘to take away’ → ذَهَبَ; to pass through and go on, and of peoples and customs — to be past → مَضَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ذهب, مضى
notes: ar-Rāġib (ذهب): after gold, aḏ-ḏahāb is al-muḍiyy, going; ḏahaba š-šayʾ and aḏhabahu; used of concrete things and of meanings (maʿānī); cites 37:99, 11:74, 35:8 (as a figure for death), 35:16 (= 14:19), 35:34, 33:33, 4:19, 8:46, 2:17, 2:20, 11:10. (مضى): al-muḍiyy and al-maḍāʾ are nafāḏ, passing through / carrying through; said of concrete things and of events; cites 43:8 and 8:38.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 35 / 4 places read): ذَهَبَ is often 'go!' to a prophet (20:24, 20:42–43, 79:17), often a fear, light, hearing or evil going away (11:74, 2:17, 2:20, 11:10), and with بِـ is 'take away' (2:17). مَضَى is the example or way of the ancients that has passed (43:8, 8:38), Lūṭ told to 'go on where you are commanded' (15:65), and Mūsā resolved to go on for ages (18:60). 35:8 (said to the Prophet) is not cited.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries ذهب, مضى (2026-11-06): 14 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): Plain-string claim: fix keyed under 'en'. The verse he quotes reads ويأت بخلق جديد, which is 14:19 / 35:16; 4:133 reads ويأت بآخرين; members/1/nuance (reworded): He glosses it only as النفاذ; 'to the end' is our addition. The same phrase in 'shared' is not attributed to him

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib objašnjava ḏahāb riječju muḍiyy (prolazak) i kaže da se upotrebljava i za stvari i za značenja. U Kur'anu poslanik odlazi faraonu, a odlaze i strah, svjetlo i zlo; s بِـ (ذَهَبَ بِـ) znači ‚odnijeti‘.
nuance.en: Ar-Rāġib explains ḏahāb by the word muḍiyy (passing) and says it is used both of things and of meanings. In the Quran a prophet goes to Pharaoh, and fear, light and evil go away; with بِـ (ذَهَبَ بِـ) it means ‘to take away’.

why.bs: Musau i Harunu: „Otiđite vas dvojica faraonu, on se, zaista, osilio.“
why.en: To Moses and Aaron: “Go, both of you, unto Pharaoh. Lo! he hath transgressed (the bounds).”

why.bs: „Pa kad je strepnja otišla od Ibrahima …“ – nestaje nešto što nije tijelo; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And when the awe departed from Abraham …” — what goes away is no body; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… Allah im odnese svjetlo“ – ذَهَبَ بِـ: odnijeti; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… Allah taketh away their light” — ذَهَبَ بِـ: to take away; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

meaning.en: to pass on, to go on

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, muḍiyy je nafāḏ – prolazak kroz nešto i nastavljanje dalje; kaže se i za stvari i za događaje. U Kur'anu prošli su primjer i običaj ranijih naroda, a Lutu i njegovima se kaže da idu dalje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, muḍiyy is nafāḏ — passing through and going on; it is said of things and of events. In the Quran the example and the way of earlier peoples have passed, and Lot and his family are told to go on.

why.bs: „… a primjer onih prijašnjih već je prošao“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… and the example of the men of old hath gone (before them)” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… a ako se vrate – već je prošao postupak s ranijim narodima“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… but if they return (thereto) then the example of the men of old hath already gone” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Lutu: „… i niko od vas neka se ne okreće, a vi idite dalje onamo kamo vam se zapovijeda.“
why.en: To Lot: “… Let none of you turn round, but go whither ye are commanded.”

shared.bs: Sve četiri riječi pripadaju razmjeni. Razlikuju se po strani u razmjeni i po obimu: ko daje cijenu, a ko robu, jedan čin prodaje ili cijelo bavljenje kapitalom radi dobiti.
shared.en: All four words belong to exchange. They differ in the side of the exchange and in scope: who gives the price and who the goods, a single act of sale or the whole business of using capital for profit.

tellApart.bs: Dati cijenu i uzeti robu, i preneseno: zamijeniti jedno za drugo → اشْتَرَى; u Kur'anu prodati → شَرَى; prodaja kao čin – dati robu, uzeti cijenu → بَيْع; bavljenje kapitalom radi dobiti → تِجَارَة.
tellApart.en: Giving the price and taking the goods, and figuratively: exchanging one thing for another → اشْتَرَى; in the Quran to sell → شَرَى; sale as an act — giving the goods, taking the price → بَيْع; using capital to seek profit → تِجَارَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries شرى, بيع, تجارة
notes: ar-Rāġib (شرى): širāʾ and bayʿ go together: the buyer pays the price and takes the priced thing, the seller the reverse; when goods are bartered for goods each can be seen as buyer and seller, so each word is used in the other's place; šaraytu more often means 'I sold' and ibtaʿtu 'I bought'; 12:20 wa-šarawhu = they sold him; 4:74 yašrūna = sell; širāʾ and ištirāʾ are allowed for anything by which a thing is obtained (3:77, 2:16, 2:86); 9:111 names what was bought with; 2:207 yašrī = sells. (بيع): bayʿ is giving the priced thing and taking the price; cites 2:275, 62:9, 2:254, 14:31; bāyaʿa is pledging obedience; 9:111 and 48:18. (تجارة): tiǧāra is dealing with capital to seek profit (at-taṣarruf fī raʾs al-māl ṭalaban li-r-ribḥ); 61:10 is explained by the next ayah, faith in Allah; cites 2:16, 4:29, 2:282.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 21 / 4 / 6 / 8 places read): اشْتَرَى is literal buying only in 12:21 (the Egyptian who bought Yūsuf); elsewhere it is exchanging error for guidance, a small price for Allah's verses or covenant, or the life of this world for the Hereafter (2:16, 2:86, 3:77), and Allah's purchase of the believers' lives (9:111). شَرَى means 'sell' in all 4 places (2:102, 2:207, 4:74, 12:20). The bayʿ member counts the noun only; the verbs بَايَعَ / تَبَايَعَ are not counted. The 2:275 English renders al-bayʿ as 'sale' (Sahih: 'trade') to keep each member its own word. 62:11 is not cited.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries شرى, بيع, تجارة (2026-11-06): 28 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/2/nuance (reworded): 'A single act' is our contrast with tiǧāra, not in his entry; drop it from the attributed sentence; members/3/nuance (reworded): The contrast with a single sale is an inference from taṣarruf, not his words

meaning.en: to buy, to purchase; to exchange for

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, kupac daje cijenu i uzima robu; ali širāʾ i ištirāʾ se kažu i za sve čime se nešto stekne. Zato u Kur'anu ljudi ‚kupuju‘ zabludu za uputu, a Allah ‚kupuje‘ od vjernika njihove živote – kako Njemu priliči. Doslovna kupovina je samo u 12:21.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the buyer gives the price and takes the goods; but širāʾ and ištirāʾ are also said of anything by which something is obtained. So in the Quran people ‘buy’ error for guidance, and Allah ‘purchases’ the believers' lives — as befits Him. Literal buying is only in 12:21.

why.bs: „A onaj koji ga je kupio u Egiptu reče svojoj ženi …“ – doslovna kupovina.
why.en: “And he of Egypt who purchased him said unto his wife …” — literal buying.

why.bs: „Eto, to su oni koji su zabludu kupili po cijenu upute“ – zamjena; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “These are they who purchase error at the price of guidance” — an exchange; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Allah je, zaista, od vjernika kupio njihove živote i njihove imetke time što će njima pripasti Džennet“ – kako Njemu priliči; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Lo! Allah hath bought from the believers their lives and their wealth because the Garden will be theirs” — as befits Him; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, šaraytu češće znači ‚prodao sam‘ nego ‚kupio sam‘. U Kur'anu je značenje ‚prodati‘ na sva četiri mjesta: Jusuf biva prodan, a vjernik prodaje sebe tražeći Allahovo zadovoljstvo.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, šaraytu more often means ‘I sold’ than ‘I bought’. In the Quran the sense is ‘sell’ in all four places: Joseph is sold, and a believer sells himself seeking Allah's pleasure.

why.bs: „I prodali su ga za bijednu cijenu, za nekoliko dirhema“ – ar-Rāġib: prodali su ga.
why.en: “And they sold him for a low price, a number of silver coins” — ar-Rāġib: they sold him.

why.bs: „A među ljudima ima i onaj koji prodaje sebe, tražeći Allahovo zadovoljstvo“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And of mankind is he who would sell himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Neka se, dakle, bore na Allahovom putu oni koji ovosvjetski život prodaju za ahiret“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Let those fight in the way of Allah who sell the life of this world for the other” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, bayʿ je dati robu i uzeti cijenu (ali napominje da se bayʿ i širāʾ mogu reći jedno za drugo). U Kur'anu je prodaja dozvoljena, ostavlja se kad se pozove na džumu, a na Sudnjem danu je nema.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, bayʿ is giving the goods and taking the price (though he notes that bayʿ and širāʾ can each be said for the other). In the Quran sale is permitted, is left when the call to the Friday prayer is made, and on the Day of Judgement there is none.

why.bs: „A Allah je prodaju učinio dozvoljenom, a kamatu zabranjenom“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Whereas Allah permitteth trading [sale] and forbiddeth usury” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Kad se u petak pozove na namaz, požurite ka spominjanju Allaha, a prodaju ostavite“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “When the call is heard for the prayer of the day of congregation, haste unto remembrance of Allah and leave your trading [sale]” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… prije nego što nastupi Dan u kojem nema ni prodaje, ni prijateljstva, ni posredovanja.“
why.en: “… ere a day come when there will be no trafficking [sale], nor friendship, nor intercession.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, tiǧāra je raspolaganje kapitalom radi dobiti – dakle, po našem čitanju, ne jedan čin prodaje, nego cijelo bavljenje. Kur'an njome opisuje i ono što donosi dobit na ahiretu: ar-Rāġib kaže da je „trgovina“ u 61:10 objašnjena sljedećim ajetom, vjerovanjem u Allaha.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, tiǧāra is using capital to seek profit — so, in our reading, not a single act of sale but the whole business. The Quran also uses it for what profits in the Hereafter: ar-Rāġib says the “commerce” of 61:10 is explained by the next ayah, faith in Allah.

why.bs: „Ljudi koje od sjećanja na Allaha ne odvlače ni trgovina ni prodaja“ – obje riječi zajedno: cijelo bavljenje i pojedini čin.
why.en: “Men whom neither merchandise nor sale beguileth from remembrance of Allah” — both words together: the whole business and the single act.

why.bs: „… osim ako to bude trgovina s obostranim pristankom među vama“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… except it be a trade by mutual consent” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „O vjernici, da vas uputim na trgovinu koja će vas izbaviti od bolne kazne?“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “O ye who believe! Shall I show you a commerce that will save you from a painful doom?” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o volji koja se okreće prema djelu. Razlikuju se po tome koliko je volja čvrsta: namjera u duši, koja može ostati neostvarena, ili srce vezano za izvršenje.
shared.en: Both words speak of the will turning towards a deed. They differ in how firm the will is: an intention in the soul, which may remain unrealised, or a heart bound to carrying the deed out.

tellApart.bs: Ono što čovjek u sebi naumi, često neostvareno → هَمَّ; srce čvrsto vezano za to da se stvar izvrši → عَزَمَ.
tellApart.en: What a person intends within himself, often unrealised → هَمَّ; a heart firmly bound to carrying the matter through → عَزَمَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries همم, عزم
notes: ar-Rāġib (همم): al-hamm is grief that melts a person away; and al-hamm is what you intend in yourself (mā hamamta bihi fī nafsika), which he calls the root sense; he quotes a poet: 'your hamm is what you have not carried out'; cites 5:11, 12:24, 3:122, 4:113, 9:74, 9:13, 40:5. (عزم): ʿazm and ʿazīma are tying the heart to carrying out the matter (ʿaqd al-qalb ʿalā imḍāʾ al-amr); cites 3:159, 2:235, 2:227, 42:43 (ʿazm al-umūr) and 20:115.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 8 / 4 places read): in 5:11 and 9:74 the intention was not attained, in 3:122 Allah was the ally of the two parties who were about to lose heart; 9:13 and 40:5 are intentions against messengers. عَزَمَ is said of resolving on divorce (2:227), on the marriage contract (2:235), of the Prophet's decision after consultation (3:159), and of 'the matter' being resolved (47:21). Left out on purpose: 12:24 (tafsir differs widely on Yūsuf's hamm), 4:113 (said to the Prophet), 20:115 (read two ways). The poet's line is his quotation, not his definition.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries همم, عزم (2026-11-06): 16 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): Plain-string claim: fix keyed under 'en'. His wording has لَمِنْ, which is 42:43; 31:17 and 3:186 read مِنْ عزم الأمور. The poet's line literally ends 'is a toil for you' (لك منصب); the paraphrase is acceptable

meaning.en: to intend, to be about to

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, hamm je ono što čovjek naumi u sebi – i to je osnovno značenje riječi. U Kur'anu su takve namjere često ostale neostvarene: Allah je zadržao ruke onih koji su naumili napasti, a drugi su naumili ono što nisu postigli.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, hamm is what a person intends within himself — and this is the root sense of the word. In the Quran such intentions often remain unrealised: Allah withheld the hands of those who intended to attack, and others intended what they did not attain.

why.bs: „… kad su neki ljudi naumili da prema vama pruže ruke svoje, pa je On ruke njihove od vas zaustavio“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… how a people were minded to stretch out their hands against you but He withheld their hands from you” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… i naumiše ono što nisu postigli“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… And they purposed that which they could not attain” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Kad su dvije skupine među vama naumile da posustanu, a Allah im je bio Zaštitnik“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “When two parties of you almost fell away, and Allah was their Protecting Friend” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ʿazm je vezivanje srca za izvršenje stvari. Nije to samo pomisao, nego odluka nakon koje dolazi djelo: zato Kur'an nakon odluke kaže „onda se osloni na Allaha“ (3:159).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ʿazm is tying the heart to carrying the matter through. It is no mere thought but a decision followed by the deed: so after the decision the Quran says “then put thy trust in Allah” (3:159).

why.bs: „… i savjetuj se s njima o stvari. A kad se odlučiš, onda se osloni na Allaha“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… consult with them upon the conduct of affairs. And when thou art resolved, then put thy trust in Allah” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A ako čvrsto odluče da se razvedu – Allah, doista, sve čuje i zna“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And if they decide upon divorce (let them remember that) Allah is Hearer, Knower” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I nemojte se odlučiti na bračnu vezu dok propisani rok ne istekne“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Do not resolve on the knot of marriage “until (the term) prescribed is run” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o brizi da nešto ostane sačuvano. Razlikuju se po slici koju nose: čuvati da se ne izgubi i ne zaboravi, ili paziti kao pastir – hraniti, braniti i pratiti kuda stvar ide.
shared.en: Both words speak of care that something stays safe. They differ in the image they carry: keeping so that it is not lost or forgotten, or tending as a shepherd does — feeding, defending and watching where the thing is going.

tellApart.bs: Čuvati, zadržati, sačuvati od gubitka i zaborava, opća riječ → حَفِظَ; paziti kao pastir stado – hraniti i braniti, i preneseno: paziti na nešto kako treba → رَعَى.
tellApart.en: To keep, retain, guard from loss and forgetting, the general word → حَفِظَ; to tend as a shepherd tends a flock — feeding and defending, and figuratively: to observe something as it deserves → رَعَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حفظ, رعى
notes: ar-Rāġib (حفظ): ḥifẓ is said of the state of the soul by which what understanding yields is fixed, of retention in the soul (its opposite is forgetting), and of using that power; then it is used of every kind of attending, looking after and riʿāya; cites 15:9, 2:238, 23:5, 33:35, 4:34, 12:64. (رعى): riʿy is at root guarding an animal, either by feeding that keeps it alive or by driving the enemy from it; riʿy and riʿāʾ are then used for guarding and governing (as-siyāsa); 20:54 kulū wa-rʿaw anʿāmakum; 57:27 mā raʿawhā ḥaqqa riʿāyatihā = they did not keep it as it should be kept; murāʿāt of a matter is watching what it will come to.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 7 / 2 places read): حَفِظَ (Form I) is said of Allah guarding the heaven from every devil (15:17), of guarding one's private parts (24:30, 24:31), of oaths (5:89), of the brothers promising to guard Binyāmīn (12:65), and of the angels who guard a person (13:11). رَعَى is only 20:54 (pasturing livestock) and 57:27 (monasticism not observed as it deserved). 4:34 and 13:11 are not cited (left out in batch 7 / readings of muʿaqqibāt differ).
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): all claims OK.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries حفظ, رعى (2026-11-06): 15 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): He lists three uses (disposition of the soul, retention, exercising that power) without saying 'at root'; 'opposite of forgetting' belongs to the second (ḍabṭ fī n-nafs). Small conflation

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḥifẓ je najprije snaga duše kojom se učvrsti ono što se razumjelo, i pamćenje u duši – suprotno zaboravu – a zatim svaka briga i čuvanje. U Kur'anu Allah čuva nebo od šejtana, kako Njemu priliči, a vjernici čuvaju svoja stidna mjesta.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ḥifẓ is first the power of the soul that holds fast what is understood, and retention in the soul — the opposite of forgetting — and then every kind of care and guarding. In the Quran Allah guards the heaven from the devils, as befits Him, and believers guard their private parts.

why.bs: „I sačuvali smo ga od svakog prokletog šejtana“ – Allah čuva nebo, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “And We have guarded it from every outcast devil” — Allah guards the heaven, as befits Him.

why.bs: „Reci vjernicima da obore poglede svoje i da čuvaju stidna mjesta svoja.“
why.en: “Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and be modest [literally: guard their private parts].”

why.bs: Jusufova braća ocu: „… a brata ćemo svoga čuvati.“
why.en: Joseph's brothers to their father: “… and guard our brother.”

meaning.en: to tend, to pasture; to observe

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, riʿy je izvorno čuvanje životinje – hranom koja je drži u životu ili odbijanjem neprijatelja od nje; zatim se kaže za svako čuvanje i upravljanje. Zato „nisu je pazili onako kako je treba paziti“ (57:27) znači nisu je čuvali kako je zaslužila.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, riʿy is at root guarding an animal — by the food that keeps it alive or by driving the enemy from it; then it is said of all guarding and governing. So “they observed it not with right observance” (57:27) means they did not keep it as it should be kept.

why.bs: „Jedite i napasajte svoja stada“ – izvorno značenje; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Eat ye and feed your cattle [literally: pasture them]” — the root sense; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… pa je nisu pazili onako kako je treba paziti“ – ar-Rāġib: nisu je čuvali kako dolikuje.
why.en: “… and they observed it not with right observance” — ar-Rāġib: they did not keep it as it should be kept.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o sili. Razlikuju se po tome da li je to moć koju neko ima, žestina koja nanosi štetu, ili silovit zahvat kojim se nešto ščepa.
shared.en: All three words speak of force. They differ in whether it is a power one has, a severity that inflicts harm, or a violent grip by which something is seized.

tellApart.bs: Moć, sposobnost – u tijelu, u srcu, u pomagačima, a i Allahova moć → قُوَّة; žestina i nedaća, najčešće u nanošenju štete i u boju → بَأْس; zahvatiti nešto silovito, napasti → بَطْش.
tellApart.en: Power, capacity — in the body, in the heart, in helpers, and Allah's power too → قُوَّة; severity and hardship, mostly in inflicting harm and in battle → بَأْس; seizing something with violence, an assault → بَطْش.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries قوى, بؤس, بطش
notes: ar-Rāġib (قوى): quwwa is used for qudra, power (2:63), and for the readiness latent in a thing (the date-stone is 'potentially' a palm); in the body (41:15, 18:95), in the heart (19:12 'with strength of heart'), in outside helpers (11:80, 'it was said': troops and wealth; 27:33), and in divine power (33:25, 51:58); 81:20 and 53:5 of Jibrīl. (بؤس): buʾs, baʾs and baʾsāʾ are hardship and what is hateful (aš-šidda wa-l-makrūh), but buʾs is more in poverty and war, baʾs and baʾsāʾ in nikāya, inflicting harm; cites 4:84, 6:42, 2:177, 59:14. (بطش): baṭš is seizing a thing with assault (tanāwul aš-šayʾ bi-ṣawla); cites 26:130, 44:16, 54:36, 85:12.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 30 / 25 / 5 places read): the baṭš member sums the nouns بَطْش (43:8, 50:36, 85:12) and بَطْشَة (44:16, 54:36); the verb بَطَشَ (5×) is not counted. بَأْس is very often Allah's punishment that comes upon a people (6:43, 7:4, 7:97, 40:84–85) and also war (2:177, 33:18); baʾs and quwwa stand together in 27:33. Allah's quwwa, baʾs and baṭš are given with 'as befits Him'.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries قوى, بؤس, بطش (2026-11-06): 24 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/nuance (improved): He assigns war (الحرب) to buʾs, not to baʾs; 'in battle and in punishment' is our gloss. The fix states his actual buʾs/baʾs contrast

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, quwwa je moć, sposobnost: u tijelu, u srcu, u pomagačima izvana, a i Allahova moć. Jahji je rečeno da Knjigu prihvati snažno (19:12) – ar-Rāġib: snagom srca.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, quwwa is power, capacity: in the body, in the heart, in helpers from outside, and also Allah's power. John was told to take the Scripture with strength (19:12) — ar-Rāġib: with strength of heart.

why.bs: „O Jahja, uzmi Knjigu svom snagom!“ – ar-Rāġib: snagom srca.
why.en: “O John! Hold fast [literally: take with strength] the Scripture” — ar-Rāġib: with strength of heart.

why.bs: Velikaši kraljici: „Mi smo ljudi snage i ljudi velike žestine“ – snaga i žestina jedna do druge; ar-Rāġib to navodi kao snagu pomagača izvana (vojske).
why.en: The chiefs to the queen: “We are lords of might and lords of great prowess” — strength and might side by side; ar-Rāġib cites it as strength in helpers from outside (an army).

why.bs: „Allah je, zaista, Onaj Koji daje opskrbu, Vlasnik snage, Čvrsti“ – Allahova moć, kako Njemu priliči; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Lo! Allah! He it is that giveth livelihood, the Lord of unbreakable might” — Allah's power, as befits Him; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, baʾs je teškoća i ono što je mrsko, ali se, za razliku od buʾs (više za siromaštvo i rat), više kaže za nanošenje štete (nikāya). U Kur'anu je to često Allahova kazna koja stiže neki narod, a i sama borba.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, baʾs is hardship and what is hateful, but unlike buʾs (said more of poverty and war) it is said more of inflicting harm (nikāya). In the Quran it is often Allah's punishment that comes upon a people, and battle itself.

why.bs: „… a Allah je veće žestine i strožije kazne“ – kako Njemu priliči; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… Allah is stronger in might and stronger in inflicting punishment” — as befits Him; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… i ljudi velike žestine“ – baʾs pored quwwa.
why.en: “… and lords of great prowess” — baʾs beside quwwa.

why.bs: „Žestina koju imaju jedni prema drugima ljuta je“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Their adversity among themselves is very great” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, baṭš je zahvatiti nešto uz nasrtaj (ṣawla), kao u izrazu ‚ruka koja udara‘. Po našem čitanju, to je čin zahvaćanja, a ne samo snaga koju neko ima. Kad se kaže za Allaha, to je Njegov zahvat, kako Njemu priliči.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, baṭš is seizing something with an assault (ṣawla), as in ‘a striking hand’. In our reading it is the act of seizing, not a power one merely has. Said of Allah, it is His seizing, as befits Him.

why.bs: „Na Dan kad ćemo zahvatiti najvećim zahvatom – Mi ćemo se, zaista, osvetiti“ – kako Njemu priliči; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “On the day when We shall seize them with the greater seizure, (then) in truth We shall punish” — as befits Him; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Zahvat Gospodara tvoga je, zaista, žestok“ – kako Njemu priliči; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Lo! the punishment [baṭš: the seizing] of thy Lord is stern” — as befits Him; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Pa smo uništili one koji su od njih bili jači u zahvatu …“
why.en: “Then We destroyed men mightier than these in prowess …”

shared.bs: Obje riječi imenuju drugi dio dana, kada dan ide prema noći. U Kur'anu skoro uvijek stoje u paru s riječju za jutro: tako se kaže ‚i ujutro i navečer‘, tj. stalno.
shared.en: Both words name the latter part of the day, as it goes towards night. In the Quran they almost always stand in a pair with a word for morning: so one says ‘morning and evening’, that is, constantly.

tellApart.bs: Večer kao širi dio dana, i za ibadet i za druge događaje (dovođenje konja, izlaganje Vatri, opskrba u Džennetu) → عَشِيّ; riječ koja se u Kur'anu javlja samo u paru ‚rano jutro i predvečerje‘ ili ‚jutra i predvečerja‘ → أَصِيل.
tellApart.en: The evening as a wider part of the day, for worship and for other events too (horses presented, people exposed to the Fire, provision in Paradise) → عَشِيّ; a word the Quran uses only in the pair ‘early morning and late day’ or ‘mornings and late days’ → أَصِيل.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عشا, أصل
notes: ar-Rāġib (عشا): al-ʿašiyy is from the sun's decline past noon (zawāl) onwards (his text: 'to the morning'), citing 79:46 (ʿašiyyatan aw ḍuḥāhā); ʿišāʾ is the time from the maġrib prayer to the ʿatama; the rest of the entry is other senses of the root (night-blindness, 43:36 ya'šu). (أصل): he opens with 'bi-l-ġuduwwi wa-l-āṣāl, i.e. the evenings (al-ʿašāyā)', and says ʿašiyya is also called aṣīl and aṣīla; he cites 'bukratan wa-aṣīlā'. He does not set aṣīl apart from ʿašiyy in time.

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): عَشِيّ 10× + عَشِيَّة 1× (79:46, the same word, summed). عَشِيّ pairs with الإِبْكَار (3:41, 40:55), الغَدَاة (6:52, 18:28), بُكْرَة (19:11, 19:62), الإِشْرَاق (38:18), غُدُوّ (40:46), stands alone in 38:31, and in 30:18 beside 'when you are at noon'. أَصِيل 7×: with بُكْرَة 4× (25:5, 33:42, 48:9, 76:25), as الآصَال with الغُدُوّ 3× (7:205, 13:15, 24:36) — never alone. 6:52 and 18:28 (said to the Prophet about not driving away the poor) are not cited.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): all claims OK.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries عشا, أصل (2026-11-06): 11 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): His limit is 'to the morning' (ilā ṣ-ṣabāḥ), i.e. it runs through the night; 'a wide part of the day' drops that limit. The Quranic examples (38:31, 40:46) are not attributed to him and are fine

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ʿašiyy je vrijeme od kada sunce prijeđe podne pa dalje – po njegovim riječima sve do jutra: širok raspon vremena. U Kur'anu se veže za veličanje Allaha, ali i za druge događaje: navečer su Sulejmanu dovedeni konji, navečer se faraonovi ljudi izlažu Vatri.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ʿašiyy is the time from the sun's passing noon onwards — in his wording, on until the morning: a wide span of time. In the Quran it goes with glorifying Allah, but also with other events: in the evening horses were presented to Solomon, in the evening Pharaoh's people are exposed to the Fire.

why.bs: Zekerijja svom narodu daje znak: „Slavite Ga ujutro i navečer!“
why.en: Zechariah signals to his people: “Glorify your Lord at break of day and fall of night.”

why.bs: „Kad su mu navečer bili pokazani plemeniti, brzi konji“ – večer kao vrijeme događaja, ne samo ibadeta.
why.en: “When there were shown to him at eventide lightfooted coursers” — the evening as the time of an event, not only of worship.

why.bs: „Na Dan kad ga vide, bit će im kao da nisu ostali osim jedne večeri ili njenog jutra“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “On the day when they behold it, it will be as if they had but tarried for an evening or the morn thereof” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib objašnjava الآصَال kao večeri i kaže da se ʿašiyya zove i aṣīl – ne odvaja ga od večeri po vremenu. Razlika je u kur'anskoj upotrebi: aṣīl se nikad ne javlja sam, nego uvijek u paru s ranim jutrom (بُكْرَة) ili s jutrima (الغُدُوّ).
nuance.en: Ar-Rāġib explains الآصَال as evenings and says that ʿašiyya is also called aṣīl — he does not set it apart from the evening in time. The difference is in Quranic usage: aṣīl never stands alone, but always in a pair with the early morning (بُكْرَة) or with the mornings (الغُدُوّ).

why.bs: „I slavite Ga izjutra rano i u predvečerje“ – ar-Rāġib navodi riječi ‚bukratan wa aṣīlā‘.
why.en: “And glorify Him early and late” — ar-Rāġib cites the words ‘bukratan wa aṣīlā’.

why.bs: „Pred Allahom padaju na sedždu svi na nebesima i na Zemlji, milom ili silom, a i njihove sjene, u jutra i u predvečerja.“
why.en: “And unto Allah falleth prostrate whosoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, as do their shadows in the morning and the evening hours.”

why.bs: Nevjernici o Kur'anu: „… pa mu se diktiraju u rano jutro i u predvečerje“ – isti par i u riječima onih koji poriču.
why.en: The disbelievers about the Quran: “… so that they are dictated to him morn and evening” — the same pair, even in the words of those who deny.

shared.bs: Obje riječi imenuju početak dana i u Kur'anu najčešće stoje u paru s riječju za večer.
shared.en: Both words name the beginning of the day and in the Quran most often stand in a pair with a word for evening.

tellApart.bs: Prvi dio dana, iz kojeg je izvedeno i značenje žurbe i ranog polaska → بُكْرَة; jutro i jutarnji pohod – riječ istog korijena kao ‚poći rano‘ i ‚sutra‘ → غُدُوّ.
tellApart.en: The first part of the day, from which the sense of hurrying and setting out early is derived → بُكْرَة; the morning and the morning's going-out — a word of the same root as ‘to set out early’ and ‘tomorrow’ → غُدُوّ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries بكر, غدا
notes: ar-Rāġib (بكر): the root word is bukra, the first part of the day; from it the verb bakara 'went out at bukra', and since it comes before the rest of the day, the sense of hastening was taken from it — anyone hurrying in a matter is said to bakara; the rest of the entry is bikr (first-born, virgin; 2:68, 56:36). (غدا): al-ġudwa and al-ġadāt are from the beginning of the day; the Quran sets al-ġuduww against al-āṣāl (bi-l-ġuduwwi wa-l-āṣāl) and al-ġadāt against al-ʿašiyy; 34:12 ġuduwwuhā šahr; ġadawtu 'I went out early' (68:22); ġad is the day after today (54:26).

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): بُكْرَة 7× — with أَصِيل 4× (25:5, 33:42, 48:9, 76:25), with عَشِيّ 2× (19:11, 19:62), alone in 54:38 (the punishment that came upon Lot's people early in the morning). غُدُوّ 5× — with الآصَال 3× (7:205, 13:15, 24:36), with عَشِيّ in 40:46, and in 34:12 for the wind's morning course for Solomon. غَدَاة (6:52, 18:28) is another lemma and is not counted.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, bukra je prvi dio dana; kako dolazi prije ostalog dijela dana, od nje je izvedeno i značenje žurbe – za svakoga ko se u nečemu požuri kaže se bakara. U Kur'anu je najčešće u paru s predvečerjem ili večeri, a jednom stoji sama: kazna je stigla „rano ujutro“ (54:38).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, bukra is the first part of the day; since it comes before the rest of the day, the sense of hurrying was derived from it — anyone who hastens in a matter is said to bakara. In the Quran it is mostly paired with the late day or the evening, and once it stands alone: the punishment came “early in the morning” (54:38).

why.bs: „I rano ujutro ih je, doista, zadesila kazna trajna“ – riječ stoji sama, bez para za večer.
why.en: “And in truth the punishment decreed befell them early in the morning” — the word stands alone, without an evening pair.

why.bs: „I spominji ime Gospodara svoga u rano jutro i u predvečerje.“
why.en: “Remember the name of thy Lord at morn and evening.”

why.bs: Stanovnici Dženneta: „… i u njemu će imati opskrbu svoju ujutro i navečer.“
why.en: The people of Paradise: “… and therein they have food for morn and evening.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ġudwa i ġadāt su od početka dana; Kur'an ġuduww suprotstavlja predvečerjima (الآصَال). Isti korijen daje i glagol ‚poći rano‘ i riječ ‚sutra‘. U Kur'anu ġuduww imenuje i jutarnji pohod: vjetar je Sulejmanu prelazio mjesec dana puta za jedno jutro.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ġudwa and ġadāt are from the beginning of the day; the Quran sets ġuduww against the late days (الآصَال). The same root gives the verb ‘to set out early’ and the word ‘tomorrow’. In the Quran ġuduww also names the morning's journey: the wind covered a month's travel for Solomon in one morning.

why.bs: „I u sebi spominji Gospodara svoga, skrušeno i sa strepnjom, bez glasnih riječi, u jutra i u predvečerja“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj par.
why.en: “And do thou (O Muhammad) remember thy Lord within thyself humbly and with awe, below thy breath, at morn and evening” — ar-Rāġib cites this pair.

why.bs: „A Sulejmanu – vjetar: jutarnji mu je pohod trajao mjesec dana, i večernji mjesec dana“ – jutarnji pohod; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And unto Solomon (We gave) the wind, whereof the morning course was a month's journey and the evening course a month's journey” — the morning's journey; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Faraonovi ljudi: „Vatra – pred nju bivaju izvedeni jutrom i predvečer.“
why.en: Pharaoh's people: “The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening.”

title.en: To form, to proportion, to determine

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi u Kur'anu najčešće opisuju Allahovo djelo nad onim što je stvorio, kako Njemu priliči: šta stvorenje dobija nakon što je stvoreno. Razlikuju se po onome što se daje: lik, sklad ili mjeru.
shared.en: All three words in the Quran most often describe Allah's work on what He has created, as befits Him: what a creature receives once created. They differ in what is given: a form, balance, or a measure.

tellApart.bs: Dati lik po kojem se stvar raspoznaje → صَوَّرَ; učiniti skladnim, bez pretjerivanja i manjka → سَوَّى; dati mjeru i način po kojima stvar biva ono što treba biti → قَدَّرَ.
tellApart.en: To give the form by which a thing is told apart → صَوَّرَ; to make balanced, free of excess and lack → سَوَّى; to give the measure and manner by which a thing becomes what it is meant to be → قَدَّرَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries صور, سوا, قدر
notes: ar-Rāġib (صور): ṣūra is that by which things are marked and distinguished from others; it is of two kinds — sensed (seen by everyone, e.g. the shape of a man or a horse) and intelligible (known to the learned, e.g. reason and deliberation proper to man); 7:11 (ṣawwarnākum) and 64:3 (ṣawwarakum fa-aḥsana ṣuwarakum) point to both; he also cites 3:6 (in the wombs). (سوا): taswiyat aš-šayʾ is making a thing sawāʾ (level), in height or in lowness; 82:7 'made your creation as wisdom required'; 87:2 the act is Allah's; sawiyy is what is kept from excess and deficiency in measure and manner. (قدر): Allah's taqdīr is of two kinds: giving power (qudra), and making things on a particular measure and manner as wisdom required (a date-stone yields palms, not apples or olives); 87:3 'gave each thing what is good for it and guided it'; 80:19 what He placed in man in potential appears stage by stage; human taqdīr is twofold — reflecting by reason (praised) and by wish and desire (blamed, 74:18–19).

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): صَوَّرَ 4×, always Allah forming people (3:6, 7:11, 40:64, 64:3); سَوَّى 13×, 12× Allah (creation, man, the heaven) and once the idolaters in Hell 'equating' their idols with the Lord (26:98); قَدَّرَ 16×, mostly Allah, but also Dāwūd commanded (34:11), the denier who 'measured out' (74:18–20) and the servers of Paradise who measure the cups (76:16). 91:7 (sawwāhā) is not cited: ar-Rāġib himself argues against one reading of it; 15:29 and 32:9 are not cited (they go on to the rūḥ).
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): all claims OK.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

He quotes only 'fakkara wa-qaddara fa-qutila kayfa qaddar' = 74:18–19, not 74:20. Everything else in the note checks; members/0/nuance (reworded): His only theological caveat is about the hadith 'khalaqa Ādam ʿalā ṣūratihi' (ownership/honour, not likeness), not about the verses; 'as befits Him' is our addition placed after 'ar-Rāġib says'. Drop it (or move it outside the attribution)

meaning.en: to form, to give a form

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ṣūra je ono po čemu se stvar raspoznaje i razlikuje od drugih: vidljiv lik (izgled čovjeka) i lik koji se razumom spoznaje (razum i promišljanje svojstveni čovjeku). Kad Allah kaže da je ljude oblikovao, ar-Rāġib kaže da se misli na oboje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ṣūra is that by which a thing is recognised and set apart from others: a visible form (a man's shape) and a form grasped by the mind (reason and deliberation proper to man). When Allah says He formed people, ar-Rāġib says both are meant.

why.bs: „… i oblikovao vas je, pa je likove vaše lijepim učinio“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… and He shaped you and made good your shapes” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „On je Taj Koji vas oblikuje u maternicama kako hoće“ – lik se daje još prije rođenja; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “He it is Who fashioneth you in the wombs as pleaseth Him” — the form is given before birth; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I Mi smo vas, zaista, stvorili, zatim vas oblikovali“ – oblikovanje dolazi nakon stvaranja.
why.en: “And We created you, then fashioned you” — forming follows creating.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, taswiya je učiniti stvar jednakom, ujednačenom; a sawiyy je ono što je sačuvano od pretjerivanja i manjka u mjeri i načinu. Kad Allah kaže da je čovjeka učinio skladnim, ar-Rāġib to tumači: dao mu je građu onakvu kakvu mudrost traži.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, taswiya is making a thing even, uniform; and sawiyy is what is kept from excess and lack in measure and manner. When Allah says He proportioned man, ar-Rāġib explains: He gave him a make such as wisdom requires.

why.bs: „Koji stvara, pa skladnim čini“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet; odmah zatim dolazi „i Koji određuje mjeru“ (87:3) (قَدَّرَ).
why.en: “Who createth, then disposeth [i.e. proportioneth]” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah; right after it comes “Who measureth” (87:3) (قَدَّرَ).

why.bs: „Koji te je stvorio, pa te skladnim učinio, pa te uravnotežio“ – ar-Rāġib: učinio je tvoju građu kakvu mudrost traži.
why.en: “Who created thee, then fashioned, then proportioned thee?” — ar-Rāġib: He made your creation as wisdom requires.

why.bs: Vjernik svome drugu: „Zar ti poričeš Onoga Koji te je stvorio od zemlje, potom od kapi sjemena, a onda te skladno uobličio u čovjeka?“
why.en: The believer to his companion: “Disbelievest thou in Him Who created thee of dust, then of a drop (of seed), and then fashioned thee a man?”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, Allahovo određivanje mjere ima dva vida: davanje moći i davanje posebne mjere i načina kako mudrost traži – kao što je u košticu hurme stavljeno da iz nje izraste palma, a ne jabuka. I čovjek ‚odmjerava‘: razumom, što je pohvalno, ili po želji i strasti, što je pokuđeno.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, Allah's determining has two aspects: giving power, and giving a particular measure and manner as wisdom requires — as a date-stone is set to grow a palm, not an apple. Man too ‘measures out’: by reason, which is praised, or by wish and desire, which is blamed.

why.bs: „I Koji određuje mjeru, pa upućuje“ – ar-Rāġib: svakoj stvari dade ono što joj je na dobro i uputi je.
why.en: “Who measureth, then guideth” — ar-Rāġib: He gave each thing what is good for it and guided it.

why.bs: „Od kapi sjemena ga je stvorio, pa mu mjeru odredio“ – ar-Rāġib: ono što je u njega položeno pojavljuje se korak po korak.
why.en: “From a drop of seed. He createth him and proportioneth [qaddarahu: determineth] him” — ar-Rāġib: what was placed in him appears stage by stage.

why.bs: „On je, doista, razmišljao i odmjeravao“ – ljudsko odmjeravanje, koje ar-Rāġib ovdje navodi kao pokuđeno, po želji.
why.en: “For lo! he did consider; then he planned” — human measuring, which ar-Rāġib cites here as the blamed kind, by wish.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o onome što ljude razdvaja. U Kur'anu četiri puta stoje zajedno: neprijateljstvo i mržnja.
shared.en: Both words speak of what divides people. In the Quran they stand together four times: enmity and hatred.

tellApart.bs: Raskid i prelaženje granice, kada se srca ne slažu – stanje između ljudi → عَدَاوَة; odbojnost duše prema nečemu, suprotno ljubavi → بَغْضَاء.
tellApart.en: A breach and overstepping, when hearts do not fit together — a state between people → عَدَاوَة; the soul's turning away from something, the opposite of love → بَغْضَاء.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عدا, بغض
notes: ar-Rāġib (عدا): al-ʿadw is overstepping and the absence of fitting together (munāfāt al-iltiʾām); considered in the heart it is called al-ʿadāwa and al-muʿādāt, in walking al-ʿadw (running), in dealings al-ʿudwān; from al-muʿādāt comes ʿaduww; an enemy is either by his own intent or by a state that harms one as an enemy would. (بغض): buġḍ is the soul's aversion from what it shuns, the opposite of ḥubb, which is the soul's attraction to what it desires; buġḍāʾ is the verbal noun in 'baġaḍtuhu buġḍāʾ' (buġḍ goes with baġuḍa); he cites 5:64 and 5:91 (al-ʿadāwata wa-l-baġḍāʾ).

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): عَدَاوَة 6×, of which 4× together with بَغْضَاء (5:14, 5:64, 5:91, 60:4), alone in 5:82 and 41:34; بَغْضَاء 5×, alone only in 3:118. The ordering 'enmity and hatred' is the same in all four pairs. 5:64 and 5:82 are not cited (statements about whole communities that need their context).
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): all claims OK.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries عدا, بغض (2026-11-06): 8 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): Plain-string note (fix under 'en'). The verse he quotes, 'wa-alqaynā baynahumu l-ʿadāwata wa-l-baġḍāʾ', is 5:64; 5:14 reads 'fa-aġraynā'. He pairs buġḍ with baġuḍa and buġḍāʾ with the transitive baġaḍtuhu

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, korijen znači prelaženje granice i neslaganje; kada se to odnosi na srce, zove se ʿadāwa. U kur'anskoj upotrebi to je stanje između dvije strane („između tebe i njega“, 41:34), koje se lijepim postupkom može pretvoriti u prijateljstvo.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root means overstepping and not fitting together; when it concerns the heart it is called ʿadāwa. In Quranic usage it is a state between two sides (“between whom and thee”, 41:34), which a good deed can turn into friendship.

why.bs: „Uzvrati onim što je ljepše, i eto – onaj između koga i tebe je neprijateljstvo bit će kao prisan prijatelj.“
why.en: “Repel the evil deed with one which is better, then lo! he, between whom and thee there was enmity (will become) as though he was a bosom friend.”

why.bs: „Šejtan samo želi da pomoću vina i kocke posije među vama neprijateljstvo i mržnju“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Satan seeketh only to cast among you enmity and hatred by means of strong drink and games of chance” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, buġḍ je odbojnost duše od onoga od čega se odvraća – suprotnost ljubavi, koja je privlačenje duše prema onome što želi. To je osjećaj u duši; u jednom ajetu Kur'an kaže da se mržnja već pokazala u riječima, a da je ono što grudi kriju još veće.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, buġḍ is the soul's aversion from what it turns away from — the opposite of love, which is the soul's attraction to what it desires. It is a feeling in the soul; in one ayah the Quran says hatred has already shown in speech, and what the breasts conceal is greater.

why.bs: „Iz njihovih usta već je izbila mržnja, a ono što skrivaju u grudima još je veće.“
why.en: “Hatred is revealed by (the utterance of) their mouths, but that which their breasts hide is greater.”

why.bs: Ibrahim i oni s njim svom narodu: „Među nama i vama ukazalo se neprijateljstvo i mržnja za vječna vremena – sve dok ne povjerujete u Allaha Jedinog.“
why.en: Abraham and those with him to their people: “And there hath arisen between us and you hostility and hate for ever until ye believe in Allah only.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o lošem osjećaju prema drugome koji se nosi u sebi. Razlikuju se po predmetu: zavist je vezana za blagodat koju drugi ima, zloba je prikrivena netrpeljivost.
shared.en: Both words speak of an ill feeling towards another that one carries within. They differ in their object: envy is tied to a blessing someone else has; resentment is a hidden rancour.

tellApart.bs: Željeti da drugi izgubi blagodat, a ponekad i raditi na tome → حَسَدَ; neprijateljstvo i prikrivena netrpeljivost koja se uvukla u grudi → غِلّ.
tellApart.en: To wish that another lose a blessing, and sometimes to work towards it → حَسَدَ; enmity and hidden rancour that has entered the breast → غِلّ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حسد, غل
notes: ar-Rāġib (حسد): ḥasad is wishing the removal of a blessing from one who deserves it, and perhaps with that an effort to remove it; he quotes a report 'the believer emulates (yaġbiṭu) and the hypocrite envies' and cites 2:109 and 113:5. (غل): the root is tadarruʿ (taking a thing on like a coat of mail) and being in its midst; most of the entry is ġull (fetter, aġlāl) and ġulūl (treachery); al-ġill is al-ʿadāwa (enmity), with 7:43 and 59:10; ġalla yaġillu 'became one with ġill, i.e. ḍiġn (rancour)'; al-ġulla and al-ġalīl are what a man carries inside of thirst, strong feeling and anger.

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): the verb حَسَدَ 3× (4:54, 48:15, 113:5); the noun حَسَد (2:109) and حَاسِد (113:5) are other lemmas, not counted. The catalogue lemma غِلّ (9×) includes the plural أَغْلَال 'fetters' (7:157, 13:5, 34:33, 36:8, 40:71, 76:4) — the corpus files both under one lemma; ġill as rancour is 3× (7:43, 15:47, 59:10), always in the breasts or hearts. 48:15 is not cited.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): all claims OK.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries حسد, غل (2026-11-06): 13 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/nuance (reworded): Minor: tadarruʿ is 'putting a thing on like a coat of mail'; 'getting into' matches only his side example (inġalla bayna š-šaǧar = entered among the trees). Our notes/0 already gloss it correctly

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, zavist je željeti da drugi, koji je zaslužuje, izgubi blagodat – a ponekad uz to i nastojati da je izgubi. Zato se u Kur'anu zavidi „na onome čime ih je Allah obdario iz Svoje dobrote“ (4:54).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, envy is wishing that another, who deserves it, lose a blessing — and sometimes with that striving to make him lose it. So in the Quran people are envied “because of that which Allah of His bounty hath bestowed upon them” (4:54).

why.bs: „Ili ljudima zavide zbog onoga što im je Allah iz Svoje blagodati podario?“
why.en: “Or are they jealous of mankind because of that which Allah of His bounty hath bestowed upon them?”

why.bs: „I od zla zavidljivca kada zavist pokaže“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And from the evil of the envier when he envieth” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib kaže da je ġill neprijateljstvo, i da se za onoga u kome je kaže da je postao čovjek ḍiġna, prikrivene netrpeljivosti; korijen znači obaviti se nečim (kao oklopom) i biti u njegovoj sredini. U Kur'anu je ġill (kao zloba) uvijek u grudima ili srcima, i to je ono što se uklanja iz stanovnika Dženneta.
nuance.en: Ar-Rāġib says ġill is enmity, and that one who has it is said to have become a man of ḍiġn, hidden rancour; the root means wrapping oneself in a thing (as in armour) and being in its midst. In the Quran ġill (as resentment) is always in breasts or hearts, and it is what is removed from the people of Paradise.

why.bs: „I Mi smo iz grudi njihovih odstranili svaku zlobu; ispod njih rijeke teku“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And We remove whatever rancour may be in their hearts. Rivers flow beneath them” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Gospodaru naš, oprosti i nama i našoj braći koja su nas u vjerovanju prestigla, i ne daj da u našim srcima bude zlobe prema onima koji vjeruju“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Our Lord! Forgive us and our brethren who were before us in the faith, and place not in our hearts any rancour toward those who believe” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I Mi smo iz grudi njihovih odstranili svaku zlobu; kao braća su na divanima, jedni prema drugima.“
why.en: “And We remove whatever rancour may be in their breasts. As brethren, face to face, (they rest) on couches raised.”

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače glad. Razlikuju se po onome što glad sa sobom donosi: samu bol praznog stomaka, tijelo koje se od gladi isušuje, ili glad praćenu umorom.
shared.en: All three words mean hunger. They differ in what the hunger brings with it: the bare pain of an empty stomach, a body that wastes from hunger, or hunger joined to fatigue.

tellApart.bs: Bol koja zahvati živo biće kad mu je stomak bez hrane, opća riječ → جُوع; glad od koje se trbuh uvuče → مَخْمَصَة; glad praćena umorom → مَسْغَبَة.
tellApart.en: The pain that seizes a living being when its stomach is empty of food, the general word → جُوع; hunger that makes the belly shrink → مَخْمَصَة; hunger joined to fatigue → مَسْغَبَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries جوع, خمص, سغب
notes: ar-Rāġib (جوع): al-ǧūʿ is the pain that comes to a living being from the stomach being empty of food; al-maǧāʿa is a time of drought. (خمص): maḫmaṣa (5:3) is a famine (maǧāʿa) that brings about ḫamṣ of the belly, i.e. its shrinking (ḍumūr); a ḫāmiṣ man is lean; the aḫmaṣ of the foot is its hollow. (سغب): masġaba (90:14) is from saġab, hunger with fatigue — 'it has been said' also thirst with fatigue.

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): جُوع 4× — a trial (2:155), the 'garment of hunger and fear' of the ungrateful town (16:112), the food of the people of the Fire that 'avails not against hunger' (88:7), and Quraysh fed against hunger (106:4); مَخْمَصَة 2× — the one forced by it may eat what is otherwise forbidden (5:3), and what befalls those who go out in Allah's way (9:120); مَسْغَبَة 1× (90:14). The verb جَاعَ (20:118) is not a member.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries جوع, خمص, سغب (2026-11-06): 11 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): He does not call ǧūʿ the general term; the classification is ours and should sit visibly under Quranic usage rather than right after 'According to ar-Rāġib'

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, glad je bol koja pogodi živo biće kada mu je stomak prazan. U kur'anskoj upotrebi to je opća riječ: glad je iskušenje, kazna nezahvalnom gradu, i ono od čega je Allah nahranio Kurejšije.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, hunger is the pain that strikes a living being when its stomach is empty. In Quranic usage it is the general word: hunger is a trial, a punishment of an ungrateful town, and what Allah fed Quraysh against.

why.bs: „I Mi ćemo vas sigurno iskušati ponečim od straha i gladi, i gubitkom imetka, života i plodova.“
why.en: “And surely We shall try you with something of fear and hunger, and loss of wealth and lives and crops.”

why.bs: „Koji ih je nahranio u gladi i od straha ih osigurao.“
why.en: “Who hath fed them against hunger and hath made them safe from fear.”

why.bs: Grad koji je bio nezahvalan na Allahovim blagodatima: „… pa mu je Allah dao da okusi odjeću gladi i straha – za ono što su radili.“
why.en: The town that was ungrateful for Allah's favours: “… so Allah made it experience the garb of dearth [literally: hunger] and fear because of what they used to do.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, maḫmaṣa je glad od koje se trbuh uvuče. U Kur'anu dolazi dva puta: kao teška nužda zbog koje je dopušteno jesti ono što je inače zabranjeno (5:3) i kao jedna od teškoća podnesenih na Allahovom putu (9:120).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, maḫmaṣa is a hunger that makes the belly shrink. It comes twice in the Quran: as the hard necessity that permits eating what is otherwise forbidden (5:3), and among the hardships endured in Allah's cause (9:120).

why.bs: „A ko bude primoran gladovanjem, ne naginjući grijehu – pa Allah, zaista, prašta i milostiv je“ – ar-Rāġib navodi riječi ‚fī maḫmaṣa‘.
why.en: “Whoso is forced by hunger [fī maḫmaṣa: in emaciating hunger], not by will, to sin: (for him) lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful” — ar-Rāġib cites the words ‘fī maḫmaṣa’.

why.bs: Onima koji izađu na Allahovom putu „ne pogađa ih ni žeđ, ni umor, ni gladovanje“, a da im se to ne upiše kao dobro djelo.
why.en: Those who go out in the cause of Allah: “neither thirst nor toil nor hunger [maḫmaṣa: emaciating hunger] afflicteth them”, but that a good deed is recorded for them by it.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, saġab je glad uz umor (a neki kažu: žeđ uz umor). Riječ dolazi samo jednom u Kur'anu, u opisu dana u kojem je nahraniti siročad i siromahe teški uspon dobra.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, saġab is hunger together with fatigue (and some say: thirst together with fatigue). The word comes only once in the Quran, describing a day on which feeding orphans and the poor is the steep ascent of good.

why.bs: „Ili dati hrane u dan gladi koja iscrpljuje“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And to feed in the day of hunger [masġaba: exhausting hunger]” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače skupinu čovjekovih bližnjih na koje se oslanja. Razlikuju se po veličini i po tome šta riječ ističe.
shared.en: All three words mean a group of a man's own people on whom he relies. They differ in size and in what the word brings out.

tellApart.bs: Čovjekovi srodnici kojima postaje brojniji, kao da je s njima ‚potpun broj‘ (od riječi deset) → عَشِيرَة; manja skupina, ispod deset ljudi (neki kažu do četrdeset) → رَهْط; rod koji se od njega ‚odvojio‘, od riječi za odvajanje → فَصِيلَة.
tellApart.en: A man's relatives by whom he grows in number, as if with them he were a ‘complete number’ (from the word for ten) → عَشِيرَة; a smaller band, under ten men (some say up to forty) → رَهْط; the kin ‘separated off’ from him, from the word for separating → فَصِيلَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عشر, رهط, فصل
notes: ar-Rāġib (عشر): al-ʿašīra are a man's people by whom he grows numerous, i.e. they are to him like the complete number, since ten is the complete number; 9:24; so ʿašīra became a name for every group of a man's relatives by whom he grows numerous; ʿašīr is a companion, near or acquainted. (رهط): ar-rahṭ is a band (ʿiṣāba) of fewer than ten, 'and it has been said' up to forty; 27:48, 11:91, 11:92. (فصل): faṣīlat ar-raǧul is his ʿašīra separated off from him (al-munfaṣila ʿanhu), 70:13; faṣl is separating one thing from another so that there is a gap between them.

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): عَشِيرَة 3× (9:24, 26:214, 58:22) — each time beside fathers, sons, brothers or wives, as something a believer might put before Allah, or be told to warn; عَشِير (22:13 'companion') is a different sense and not summed; رَهْط 3× (11:91, 11:92 Šuʿayb's kin that protects him; 27:48 nine men who spread corruption — many mufassirun: nine men, not cited); فَصِيلَة 1× (70:13).
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): all claims OK.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ʿašīra su čovjekovi srodnici kojima postaje brojniji, kao da mu daju ‚potpun broj‘ – jer je deset potpun broj. U Kur'anu rodbina stoji uz očeve, sinove, braću i žene, kao ono što vjernik ne smije pretpostaviti Allahu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ʿašīra are a man's relatives by whom he grows in number, as if they gave him the ‘complete number’ — since ten is the complete number. In the Quran kindred stands beside fathers, sons, brothers and wives, as what a believer must not put before Allah.

why.bs: „Ako vaši očevi, sinovi, braća, supruge i vaša rodbina … budu vam draži od Allaha i Njegova Poslanika …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “If your fathers, and your sons, and your brethren, and your wives, and your tribe … are dearer to you than Allah and His messenger …” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Vjernici ne vole one koji se protive Allahu, „pa makar to bili njihovi očevi ili sinovi, njihova braća ili njihova rodbina“.
why.en: Believers do not love those who oppose Allah, “even though they be their fathers or their sons or their brethren or their clan”.

why.bs: „I upozori svoju najbližu rodbinu.“
why.en: “And warn thy tribe of near kindred.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, rahṭ je skupina manja od deset ljudi (neki kažu: do četrdeset). U Kur'anu Šuajbov narod kaže da ga ne kamenuje samo zbog njegove porodice – mala skupina koja ga štiti.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, rahṭ is a band of fewer than ten men (some say: up to forty). In the Quran Shuʿayb's people say they do not stone him only because of his family — a small band that protects him.

why.bs: „Da nije tvoje porodice, mi bismo te kamenovali, a ti kod nas nisi cijenjen“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “But for thy family, we should have stoned thee, for thou art not strong against us” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Šuajb: „Narode moj, zar vam je do moje porodice više stalo nego do Allaha?“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Shuʿayb: “O my people! Is my family more to be honoured by you than Allah?” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, čovjekova faṣīla je njegova rodbina ‚koja se od njega odvojila‘ – riječ je od faṣl, odvajanja. Dolazi samo jednom u Kur'anu, u opisu Sudnjeg dana (70:11–14): grešnik bi se rado otkupio i svojim najužim rodom koji ga je štitio.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a man's faṣīla is his kindred ‘separated off from him’ — the word is from faṣl, separating. It comes only once in the Quran, describing the Day of Judgement (70:11–14): the wrongdoer would gladly ransom himself even with his nearest kin who used to shelter him.

why.bs: „i najuži rod svoj, koji mu je pružao zaklon“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And his kin that harboured him” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače umor. U Kur'anu se obje spominju u opisu Dženneta, gdje ih nema, a jedna od njih i u ajetu o stvaranju nebesa i Zemlje.
shared.en: Both words mean tiredness. In the Quran both are named in describing Paradise, where they are absent, and one of them also in the ayah about creating the heavens and the earth.

tellApart.bs: Umor od napora, koji ljude pogađa na putu i u borbi → نَصَب; malaksalost, iz korijena koji znači i slabost – u Kur'anu uvijek zanijekana → لُغُوب.
tellApart.en: Fatigue from exertion, which strikes people on a journey and in striving → نَصَب; weariness, from a root that also means weakness — in the Quran always denied → لُغُوب.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نصب, لغب
notes: ar-Rāġib (نصب): naṣab and nuṣb are taʿab (fatigue) — read both ways in 38:41; anṣabanī 'it tired and troubled me'; he cites 35:35 and 18:62. (لغب): al-luġūb is at-taʿab wa-n-naṣab, 'saġiban laġiban' = hungry and tired; he cites 50:38; sahm luġb is an arrow with weak feathers, raǧul luġb a weak man. He defines luġūb by naṣab itself: the distinction 'naṣab is bodily toil, luġūb the exhaustion that follows' is the mufassirun's reading of 35:35, not his.

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): نَصَب 4× — met on a journey (18:62), suffered in Allah's way (9:120), and absent in Paradise (15:48, 35:35); لُغُوب 2× — absent in Paradise (35:35) and in Allah's creating the heavens and earth (50:38): never affirmed of anyone. نُصُب / نُصْب (idols, 'a set-up stone') are other lemmas.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 flag, fixed: he glosses luġūb as 'fatigue and naṣab' (close to naṣab); the 35:35 split is given to many mufassirun.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, naṣab je umor, ono što čovjeka zamara i uznemirava. U Kur'anu ga ljudi doživljavaju – Musa na putovanju, borci na Allahovom putu – a u Džennetu ga nema.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, naṣab is fatigue, what tires and troubles a person. In the Quran people meet it — Moses on a journey, those who strive in Allah's way — and in Paradise there is none.

why.bs: Musa svom momku: „Donesi nam naš jutarnji obrok, zaista smo na ovom našem putovanju umor iskusili“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Moses to his boy: “Bring us our breakfast. Verily we have found fatigue in this our journey” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Onima koji izađu na Allahovom putu „ne pogađa ih ni žeđ, ni umor, ni gladovanje“, a da im se to ne upiše kao dobro djelo.
why.en: Those who go out in the cause of Allah: “neither thirst nor toil nor hunger afflicteth them”, but that a good deed is recorded for them by it.

why.bs: Stanovnici Dženneta: „Umor ih ondje neće dotaći, niti će odande biti istjerani.“
why.en: The people of Paradise: “Toil cometh not unto them there, nor will they be expelled from thence.”

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib luġūb objašnjava riječima ‚umor i naṣab‘, dakle ih drži bliskima, a navodi da isti korijen znači i slabost (slaba strijela, slab čovjek). U Kur'anu je malaksalost uvijek zanijekana: u Džennetu, i kod Allaha u stvaranju nebesa i Zemlje, kako Njemu priliči. Mnogi mufessiri u 35:35 objašnjavaju: umor je od napora, a malaksalost ono što poslije njega slijedi.
nuance.en: Ar-Rāġib explains luġūb as ‘fatigue and naṣab’, so he treats the two as close, and notes that the same root also means weakness (a weak arrow, a weak man). In the Quran weariness is always denied: in Paradise, and of Allah in creating the heavens and the earth, as befits Him. Many mufassirun explain 35:35: fatigue is from exertion, and weariness what follows it.

why.bs: „… gdje nas ne dotiče umor i gdje nas ne dotiče malaksalost“ – obje riječi zajedno.
why.en: “… where toil toucheth us not nor can weariness affect us” — both words together.

why.bs: „I doista smo nebesa i Zemlju, i sve što je među njima, stvorili u šest dana, i nije Nas dotakla nikakva malaksalost“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet; kako Allahu priliči.
why.en: “And verily We created the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them, in six Days, and naught of weariness touched Us” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah; as befits Allah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače one koji se od čovjeka rađaju. Razlikuju se po tome šta riječ ističe: potomstvo kao loza i djeca, ili porod kao ono što se od roditelja odvaja.
shared.en: Both words mean those born of a person. They differ in what the word brings out: offspring as a line and children, or progeny as what separates off from the parent.

tellApart.bs: Potomci, izvorno mala djeca, a u upotrebi i mladi i stari, jedan ili više – riječ loze vjerovjesnika i dova za djecu → ذُرِّيَّة; porod kao ono što ‚izlazi‘ iz oca, riječ istog korijena kao ‚odvojiti se‘ → نَسْل.
tellApart.en: Descendants, originally the young children, though in use both young and old, one or many — the word of the prophets' lines and of prayers for children → ذُرِّيَّة; progeny as what ‘issues’ from the father, a word of the same root as ‘to come away’ → نَسْل.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ذرو, ذر, نسل
notes: ar-Rāġib (ذرو): aḏ-ḏurriyya was originally the young among offspring, though in common usage it covers young and old together; it is used for one and for many, its origin being plural; he cites 3:34, 17:3, 36:41, 2:124; he reports three derivations, all with 'qīla' (from ḏaraʾa, Allah's bringing forth creation, with the hamza dropped; from ḏarw; from ḏarr). (ذر): a short entry citing ḏurriyya verses and pointing to ذرأ. (نسل): nasl is separating from a thing (fur from a camel, a shirt from a man); nasala 'ran fast' (21:96); an-nasl is the child, since it issues (nāsil) from its father; 2:205; tanāsalū 'they begot one another'.

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): ذُرِّيَّة 32× (the catalogue counts 32; 30 ayat) — the lines of Adam, Noah and Abraham (3:34, 17:3, 19:58, 57:26), prayers for offspring (3:38, 14:40, 25:74), weak children left behind (4:9), and the believers' offspring joined to them in Paradise (52:21, 13:23); نَسْل 2× (2:205, 32:8). In 2:205 many mufassirun take an-nasl as the young of people and animals; Sahih International renders it 'animals'. 2:124 is not cited (tafsir differs on Abraham's request).
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): all claims OK.
