nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḏurriyya su izvorno mala djeca među potomcima, ali se u upotrebi kaže i za male i za velike, za jednog i za više. U Kur'anu je to riječ loze vjerovjesnika i dove za djecu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ḏurriyya are originally the young among descendants, but in use it is said of young and old alike, of one and of many. In the Quran it is the word of the prophets' lines and of prayers for children.

why.bs: Zekerijja: „Gospodaru moj, daruj mi od Sebe dobro potomstvo; Ti, doista, čuješ dovu.“
why.en: Zechariah: “My Lord! Bestow upon me of Thy bounty goodly offspring. Lo! Thou art the Hearer of Prayer.”

why.bs: „Neka se boje oni koji bi strahovali za svoje nejako potomstvo kad bi ga iza sebe ostavili.“
why.en: “And let those fear (in their behaviour toward orphans) who if they left behind them weak offspring would be afraid for them.”

why.bs: „A one koji vjeruju i čije ih potomstvo u vjerovanju slijedi – njima ćemo pridružiti potomstvo njihovo.“
why.en: “And they who believe and whose seed follow them in faith, We cause their seed to join them.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, korijen znači odvajanje od nečega (kao što dlaka spada s deve), a nasl je dijete jer ‚izlazi‘ iz oca. U Kur'anu dolazi dva puta: porod koji smutljivac uništava, i porod čovjekov stvoren od bezvrijedne tekućine.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root means separating from a thing (as fur comes off a camel), and nasl is the child because it ‘issues’ from its father. In the Quran it comes twice: the progeny a corrupter destroys, and man's progeny made from a worthless fluid.

why.bs: „A kad se okrene, trudi se po Zemlji da u njoj nered čini i da upropaštava usjeve i porod – a Allah nered ne voli“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet; mnogi mufessiri: porod ljudi i životinja.
why.en: “And when he turneth away (from thee) his effort in the land is to make mischief therein and to destroy the crops and the cattle [an-nasl: the progeny]; and Allah loveth not mischief” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah; many mufassirun: the young of people and of animals.

why.bs: „Zatim je porod njegov učinio od izvatka bezvrijedne tekućine.“
why.en: “Then He made his seed from a draught of despised fluid.”

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o mladom čovjeku prije zrelosti. Razlikuju se po onome što ističu: nježnost malog djeteta, dob prije punoljetnosti, ili dječaka kome su izbili brkovi.
shared.en: All three words speak of a young person before maturity. They differ in what they stress: the tenderness of a small child, the age before puberty, or a boy whose moustache has begun to show.

tellApart.bs: Dijete dok je još nježno, i za jedno i za više njih → طِفْل; onaj ko još nije dostigao punoljetnost → صَبِيّ; dječak kome su izbili brkovi, u Kur'anu najčešće sin o kome se donosi radosna vijest → غُلَام.
tellApart.en: A child while still tender, for one or many → طِفْل; one who has not yet reached puberty → صَبِيّ; a boy whose moustache has sprouted, in the Quran most often a son whose coming is announced → غُلَام.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries طفل, صبا, غلم
notes: ar-Rāġib (طفل): the ṭifl is the child as long as it is soft (nāʿim); it may fall on the plural; plural aṭfāl; cites 40:67 (yuḫriǧukum ṭiflan), 24:31 (aṭ-ṭifl allaḏīna lam yaẓharū) and 24:59 (al-aṭfāl). (صبا): the ṣabiyy is one who has not reached puberty (al-ḥulum); cites 19:29. (غلم): the ġulām is ṭārr aš-šārib, one whose moustache has sprouted; cites 'annā yakūnu lī ġulām' (3:40 / 19:8 / 19:20), 18:80, 18:82 and 12:19.

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): طِفْل 4× (22:5, 24:31, 24:59, 40:67), twice of man brought out of the womb as a child (22:5, 40:67); صَبِيّ 2× (19:12 Yaḥyā, 19:29 ʿĪsā in the cradle); غُلَام 13× with the plural ġilmān (52:24): in 8 places the son announced or asked about (3:40, 15:53, 19:7, 19:8, 19:19, 19:20, 37:101, 51:28), also Yūsuf drawn from the well (12:19), the boy and the two orphans in the story of Mūsā and al-Ḫiḍr (18:74, 18:80, 18:82) and the youths serving in Paradise (52:24). Not cited: 24:31 (a ruling on adornment that needs its fiqh context) and 18:74 / 18:80 (the story needs tafsir context). For 19:12 the bs keeps Korkut's 'mudrost' with ḥukm beside it, the en Sahih's 'judgement'.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 3 flags, fixed: ṭifl 'while still tender', not 'newborn'; 24:59 described as the ruling once children reach puberty; 19:12 'wisdom / mudrost' in both languages.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ṭifl je dijete dok je još nježno; riječ može značiti i više djece. U Kur'anu dolazi tamo gdje se opisuje kako Allah izvodi čovjeka iz utrobe majke kao dijete, i u propisu o tome šta djeca čine kad dostignu punoljetnost.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ṭifl is a child while it is still tender; the word can also stand for several children. In the Quran it comes where Allah describes bringing man out of the womb as a child, and in the ruling on what children must do once they reach puberty.

why.bs: „On je Onaj Koji vas je stvorio od zemlje, potom od kapi sjemena, potom od ugruška, a zatim vas izvodi kao dijete“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “He it is Who created you from dust, then from a drop (of seed) then from a clot, then bringeth you forth as a child” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… onda vas kao dijete izvodimo, a potom da biste dosegli punu snagu svoju“ – ista slika rođenja.
why.en: “… afterward We bring you forth as infants, then (give you growth) that ye attain your full strength” — the same picture of birth.

why.bs: „A kad djeca među vama dostignu spolnu zrelost, neka traže dozvolu“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet za množinu.
why.en: “And when the children among you come to puberty then let them ask leave” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah for the plural.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ṣabiyy je onaj ko još nije dostigao punoljetnost. Riječ ističe dob, a ne nježnost. U Kur'anu dolazi dva puta, oba puta o nedoraslom kome je Allah dao ono što se u toj dobi ne očekuje: Jahji ḥukm, a Isa je govorio iz bešike.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ṣabiyy is one who has not yet reached puberty. The word stresses age, not tenderness. In the Quran it comes twice, both times of a youngster given by Allah what is not expected at that age: ḥukm to John, and Jesus spoke from the cradle.

why.bs: „O Jahja, uzmi Knjigu svom snagom!“ – i dadosmo mu mudrost (ḥukm) još kao nedoraslom.
why.en: “O John! Hold fast the Scripture. And we gave him wisdom [ḥukm] when a child [ṣabiyyan: while yet a youngster].”

why.bs: Merjem pokaza na njega, a oni rekoše: „Kako da govorimo onome ko je u bešici, nedorastao?“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Mary pointed to him; they said: “How can we talk to one who is in the cradle, a young boy?” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ġulām je dječak kome su izbili brkovi. U Kur'anu se ipak najčešće kaže za sina o kome se donosi radosna vijest – Ibrahimu, Zekerijji i Merjemi – dakle i prije rođenja.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ġulām is a boy whose moustache has sprouted. In the Quran, though, it is most often said of a son whose coming is announced as good news — to Abraham, Zechariah and Mary — so even before birth.

why.bs: „O Zekerijja, Mi te radujemo viješću o dječaku čije je ime Jahja.“
why.en: “O Zachariah! Lo! We bring thee tidings of a son [ġulām: a boy] whose name is John.”

why.bs: „Pa smo ga obradovali blagim dječakom“ – Ibrahima.
why.en: “So We gave him tidings of a gentle son [ġulām: a boy]” — Abraham.

why.bs: Kad je onaj koji je zahvatao vodu spustio vedro: „O radosti, evo dječaka!“ – Jusuf; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: When their water-drawer let down his pail: “Good luck! Here is a youth” — Joseph; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Sve četiri riječi znače devu. Razlikuju se po spolu, dobi i broju.
shared.en: All four words mean the camel. They differ by sex, age and number.

tellApart.bs: Ženka; u Kur'anu uvijek Salihova kamila, Allahov znak → نَاقَة; deva kad dostigne punu dob → جَمَل; deve kao skupina, bez jednine od iste riječi → إِبِل; jedna deva, mužjak ili ženka, kao što se insān kaže za oba spola → بَعِير.
tellApart.en: The female; in the Quran always Ṣāliḥ's she-camel, Allah's sign → نَاقَة; a camel once it has reached full age → جَمَل; camels as a group, with no singular from the same word → إِبِل; one camel, male or female, as insān is said of both sexes → بَعِير.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries إبل, جمل, بعر
notes: ar-Rāġib (إبل): ibil falls on many camels and has no singular from its own word; cites 6:144; on 88:17 'qīla clouds were meant' — if so, he says, by likening clouds to camels. (بعر): the baʿīr is known and falls on male and female, as insān does; plurals abʿira, abāʿir, buʿrān; cites 12:72. (جمل): jamal is said of the baʿīr when it has reached full age (iḏā bazala); cites 7:40; jimālat in 77:33 he discusses separately ('qīla' young she-camels). He has no entry for نَاقَة (root نوق); the word only appears in passing in other entries (e.g. بصر on 17:59), so the نَاقَة member rests on Quranic usage alone.

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): نَاقَة 7× (7:73, 7:77, 11:64, 17:59, 26:155, 54:27, 91:13), every time the she-camel sent to Ṯamūd through Ṣāliḥ, called 'Allah's she-camel' in 7:73, 11:64 and 91:13; جَمَل 1× (7:40 — the reading of the Ḥafṣ text, al-jamal, is given; some read al-jummal 'thick rope'); جِمَالَت (77:33) is a different lemma, not counted, and its sense is read two ways; إِبِل 2× (6:144, 88:17); بَعِير 2× (12:65, 12:72), both in the story of Yūsuf's brothers, as the measure of a load. Bosnian has one word for the animal (deva): the members are told apart by kamila (nāqa), stado deva (ibil) and the glosses.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 flag, fixed: 7:77 bs 'uzoholiše se' for ʿatawā.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries إبل, جمل, بعر, بصر (2026-11-06): 16 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/2/ayat/0/why (reworded): He makes it conditional ('if that is correct') and does not belittle it with 'only'

nuance.bs: Ženka deve. U Kur'anu (7×) uvijek je to ista kamila – ona koja je Semudu poslana kao znak po Salihu; Kur'an je naziva „Allahovom kamilom“ (11:64).
nuance.en: The female camel. In the Quran (7×) it is always the same one — the she-camel sent to Thamūd as a sign through Ṣāliḥ; the Quran calls her “the camel of Allah” (11:64).

why.bs: „Narode moj, ova Allahova kamila vama je znak, pa je pustite da jede po Allahovoj zemlji.“
why.en: “O my people! This is the camel of Allah, a token unto you, so suffer her to feed in Allah's earth.”

why.bs: „Ovo je kamila; ona ima svoje pojenje, a vi svoje, u određeni dan.“
why.en: “(Behold) this she-camel. She hath the right to drink (at the well), and ye have the right to drink, (each) on an appointed day.”

why.bs: „Pa su osakatili (ʿaqarū) kamilu i oholo se usprotivili naredbi Gospodara svoga.“
why.en: “So they hamstrung (ʿaqarū) the she-camel, and they flouted the commandment of their Lord.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, jamal je deva kad dostigne punu dob. U Kur'anu dolazi samo jednom, u slici onoga što je nemoguće: velika životinja i iglene uši.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, jamal is a camel once it has reached full age. In the Quran it comes only once, in an image of the impossible: a large animal and the eye of a needle.

why.bs: „… niti će u Džennet ući sve dok deva kroz ušicu igle ne prođe“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: They will not enter the Garden “until the camel goeth through the needle's eye” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ibil znači mnoštvo deva i nema jednine od iste riječi. Kur'an je spominje među stokom koju je Allah stvorio i kao znak koji treba pogledati.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ibil means many camels and has no singular from the same word. The Quran names it among the livestock Allah created and as a sign to look at.

why.bs: „Zar ne gledaju u deve, kako su stvorene?“ – ar-Rāġib bilježi i mišljenje da su to oblaci, a to bi, ako je tačno, kaže, bilo poređenje oblaka s devama.
why.en: “Will they not regard the camels, how they are created?” — ar-Rāġib also records a view that clouds are meant, which, if correct, he says would be by likening clouds to camels.

why.bs: „Te dvoje od deva, i dvoje od goveda“ – deve kao vrsta stoke; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And of the camels twain and of the oxen twain” — camels as a kind of livestock; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, baʿīr je deva i kaže se i za mužjaka i za ženku, kao što se insān kaže i za muškarca i za ženu. U Kur'anu (2×) dolazi u priči o Jusufovoj braći, kao mjera tovara.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, baʿīr is a camel, said of male and female alike, just as insān is said of man and woman. In the Quran (2×) it comes in the story of Joseph's brothers, as the measure of a load.

why.bs: „… a ko ga donese – njemu tovar deve“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… he who bringeth it shall have a camel-load” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… i dobit ćemo još jednu devinu mjeru.“
why.en: “… and we shall have the extra measure of a camel (load).”

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o životinjama. Razlikuju se po tome koliko je skupina široka: sve što se kreće po zemlji, domaća stoka, ili životinja bez govora.
shared.en: All three words speak of animals. They differ in how wide the group is: everything that moves on the earth, domestic livestock, or the animal without speech.

tellApart.bs: Svako živo biće koje se kreće po zemlji, najšira riječ → دَابَّة; deve, goveda, ovce i koze – stoka koja služi čovjeku → أَنْعَام; životinja bez govora, u Kur'anu uvijek u spoju ‚živinče od stoke‘ → بَهِيمَة.
tellApart.en: Every creature that moves on the earth, the widest word → دَابَّة; camels, cattle, sheep and goats — livestock that serves man → أَنْعَام; the animal without speech, in the Quran always in ‘the beasts of livestock’ → بَهِيمَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries دب, نعم, بهم
notes: ar-Rāġib (دب): dabb / dabīb is light walking, used of animals and more of crawling creatures; used of every animal, though custom narrows it to the horse; cites 24:45, 31:10, 11:6, 6:38; on 35:45 Abū ʿUbayda said man alone is meant, he prefers the general sense; 27:82 'qīla' a creature unlike those we know, 'qīla' the wicked. (نعم): naʿam is specific to camels, so called because camels were their greatest blessing (niʿma); anʿām is said of camels, cattle and sheep, and not called anʿām unless camels are among them. (بهم): bahīma is whatever has no speech (nuṭq), for the vagueness (ibhām) of its voice, but custom restricts it to what is not a beast of prey or a bird; cites 5:1.

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): أَنْعَام / نَعَم 33× in 31 ayat — the singular naʿam only in 5:95; three of them in bahīmat al-anʿām (5:1, 22:28, 22:34); livestock for food, milk, warmth, riding (16:5, 16:66, 23:21, 40:79); 25:44 likens the heedless to livestock. بَهِيمَة 3×, always in that construct. دَابَّة 18× with dawābb (e.g. 11:6, 24:45, 29:60). 27:82 (the dābba brought out of the earth) is not cited: tafsir differs on what it is, and ar-Rāġib reports two views.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 flag, fixed: 5:1 bs grammar.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries دب, نعم, بهم (2026-11-06): 20 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/nuance (reworded): He says naʿam is restricted (muḫtaṣṣ) to camels — a present usage limit, not an original sense that later widened

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, riječ dolazi od dabīb – laganog hoda – i kaže se za svaku životinju, iako je u običnom govoru sužena na konja. U Kur'anu je to najšira riječ: svako biće koje Allah opskrbljuje i koje je stvorio od vode.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the word comes from dabīb, light walking, and is said of every animal, though everyday speech narrows it to the horse. In the Quran it is the widest word: every creature Allah provides for and has created from water.

why.bs: „Allah je od vode stvorio svako živo biće: neka se od njih kreću na trbuhu, neka na dvije noge, a neka na četiri“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Allah hath created every animal of water. Of them is (a kind) that goeth upon its belly and (a kind) that goeth upon two legs and (a kind) that goeth upon four” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Nema nijednog živog bića na Zemlji, a da njegova opskrba nije na Allahu“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And there is not a beast in the earth but the sustenance thereof dependeth on Allah” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Nema živog bića na Zemlji, niti ptice što na dva krila leti, a da nisu zajednice kao i vi“ – ptica se navodi pored dābbe; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “There is not an animal in the earth, nor a flying creature flying on two wings, but they are peoples like unto you” — the bird is named beside the dābba; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, naʿam se kaže posebno za deve – nazvana tako jer su deve Arapima bile najveća blagodat (niʿma) – a anʿām se kaže za deve, goveda i sitnu stoku, ali tek kad su deve među njima. U Kur'anu je to stoka koju je Allah stvorio čovjeku: za hranu, mlijeko, toplinu i jahanje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, naʿam is said specifically of camels — so called because camels were the Arabs' greatest blessing (niʿma) — and anʿām is said of camels, cattle, sheep and goats, but only when camels are among them. In the Quran it is the livestock Allah created for man: for food, milk, warmth and riding.

why.bs: „I stoku je On stvorio za vas; u njoj imate toplinu i koristi, i od nje jedete.“
why.en: “And the cattle hath He created, whence ye have warm clothing and uses, and whereof ye eat.”

why.bs: „Allah je Onaj Koji je za vas učinio stoku – da na nekima od nje jašete, a nekima se hranite.“
why.en: “Allah it is Who hath appointed for you cattle, that ye may ride on some of them, and eat of some.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, bahīma je svaka životinja koja nema govora – nazvana tako zbog nejasnoće (ibhām) njenog glasa – a u običnom govoru se kaže za sve osim zvijeri i ptica. U Kur'anu (3×) dolazi samo u spoju bahīmat al-anʿām: stoka kao dozvoljena hrana i kurban.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, bahīma is any animal without speech — so named for the vagueness (ibhām) of its voice — and in everyday speech it is said of all but beasts of prey and birds. In the Quran (3×) it comes only in bahīmat al-anʿām: livestock as lawful food and sacrifice.

why.bs: „Dopušteno vam je živinče od stoke, izuzev onoga što vam se kazuje“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “The beast of cattle is made lawful unto you (for food) except that which is announced unto you” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Svakoj zajednici dali smo obred, kako bi spominjali Allahovo ime nad živinčetom od stoke koje im je On dao za opskrbu.“
why.en: “And for every nation have We appointed a ritual, that they may mention the name of Allah over the beast of cattle that He hath given them for food.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače izvor svjetla koji se pali. Ar-Rāġib kaže da se sirāj naziva i misbāḥ; Kur'an ih ipak koristi za različite stvari.
shared.en: Both words mean a kindled source of light. ar-Rāġib says the sirāj is also called a misbāḥ; the Quran still uses them for different things.

tellApart.bs: Svjetiljka koja gori fitiljem i uljem, pa se kaže za sve što sija; u Kur'anu sunce i Poslanik → سِرَاج; lampa u niši iz poređenja o svjetlu, i zvijezde kao ukras najbližeg neba → مِصْبَاح.
tellApart.en: A lamp burning with wick and oil, then anything that shines; in the Quran the sun and the Prophet → سِرَاج; the lantern in the niche of the parable of light, and the stars adorning the nearest heaven → مِصْبَاح.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries سرج, صبح
notes: ar-Rāġib (سرج): the sirāj is what shines (az-zāhir) by wick and oil, and is used of everything that gives light; cites 71:16 and 78:13 'meaning the sun'. (صبح): under ṣubḥ he lists the miṣbāḥ, cites 24:35, says 'the sirāj is called miṣbāḥ', and that al-maṣābīḥ are the prominent stars (aʿlām al-kawākib), citing 67:5.

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): سِرَاج 4× — the sun (71:16, 78:13, and 25:61, where most read it as the sun) and the Prophet (33:46); مِصْبَاح 4× counting maṣābīḥ — the lantern of 24:35 (twice in the ayah) and the stars (41:12, 67:5). 25:61 is not cited (sirāǧan / suruǧan are read differently). The 24:35 note gives the parable with the mufassirun's usual reading beside it.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): all claims OK.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries سرج, صبح (2026-11-06): 12 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): 71:16 names the sun itself; his gloss 'yaʿnī aš-šams' only interprets 78:13. Minor

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, sirāj je ono što sija pomoću fitilja i ulja, a kaže se i za sve što daje svjetlo; navodi ajete 71:16 i 78:13 o suncu. U Kur'anu se tako naziva sunce, a i Poslanik, kao svjetiljka koja sija – svjetlo koje dopire do drugih.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, sirāj is what shines by wick and oil, and it is said of anything that gives light; he cites 71:16 and 78:13 of the sun. In the Quran the sun is so called, and the Prophet too, as an illuminating lamp — a light that reaches others.

why.bs: „I učinio je mjesec na njima svjetlom, a sunce svjetiljkom“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And hath made the moon a light therein, and made the sun a lamp” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I postavili smo svjetiljku žarku“ – ar-Rāġib: sunce.
why.en: “And have appointed a dazzling lamp” — ar-Rāġib: the sun.

why.bs: „… i kao pozivača k Allahu, s Njegovim dopuštenjem, i kao svjetiljku koja obasjava“ – o Poslaniku.
why.en: “And as a summoner unto Allah by His permission, and as a lamp that giveth light” — of the Prophet.

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib riječ navodi pod ṣubḥ (jutro), kaže da se sirāj naziva i misbāḥ, a da su maṣābīḥ istaknute zvijezde. U Kur'anu je to lampa u niši iz poređenja o Allahovom svjetlu, kako Njemu priliči, i zvijezde kojima je ukrašeno najbliže nebo.
nuance.en: ar-Rāġib lists the word under ṣubḥ (morning), says the sirāj is also called misbāḥ, and that maṣābīḥ are the prominent stars. In the Quran it is the lantern in the niche of the parable of Allah's light, as befits Him, and the stars that adorn the nearest heaven.

why.bs: „… Svjetlo Njegovo nalik je niši, a u njoj lampa; lampa je u staklu …“ – poređenje; mnogi mufessiri ga tumače kao svjetlo upute u srcu vjernika; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… The similitude of His light is as a niche wherein is a lamp [miṣbāḥ: a lantern]. The lamp is in a glass …” — a parable; many mufassirun explain it as the light of guidance in the believer's heart; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I Mi smo, zaista, najbliže nebo ukrasili lampama“ – zvijezde; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And verily We have beautified the world's heaven with lamps [maṣābīḥ: lanterns]” — the stars; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o tome šta je čovjek u stanju učiniti. Razlikuju se po onome što ističu: imati sve što djelo traži, imati moć nad nečim, ili snagu za ono što je teško.
shared.en: All three words speak of what a person is able to do. They differ in what they stress: having all that the act requires, having power over something, or the strength for what is hard.

tellApart.bs: Moći, jer čovjek ima sve što mu za djelo treba, i sredstva → اِسْتَطَاعَ; imati moć nad nečim, opća riječ → قَدَرَ; mjera onoga što se može podnijeti s mukom → طَاقَة.
tellApart.en: To be able because one has all the act requires, the means too → اِسْتَطَاعَ; to have power over something, the general word → قَدَرَ; the measure of what can be borne with hardship → طَاقَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries طوع, قدر, طوق
notes: ar-Rāġib (طوع): istiṭāʿa is an istifʿāl of ṭawʿ — the presence of what makes the act feasible; for 'the verifiers' (al-muḥaqqiqūn) the things by which a man is enabled to do what he wants: four — a specific constitution of the agent, a conception of the act, a material receptive to it, and an instrument if the act needs one; its opposite is ʿaǧz; istiṭāʿa is more specific (aḫaṣṣ) than qudra; cites 3:97 with the hadith 'provision and mount'; 'lā yastaṭīʿu' is also said of what is hard for lack of practice (riyāḍa), with 18:67; 18:97 for isṭāʿa = istaṭāʿa. (قدر): qudra of man is a state (hayʾa) by which he is able to do something; of Allah it is the negation of incapacity; absolute qudra belongs to Allah alone, a man is rightly 'qādir ʿalā kaḏā'; cites 'lā yaqdirūna ʿalā šayʾin mimmā kasabū' (2:264); qadara ʿalayhi also means 'to straiten' (13:26, 65:7, 21:87). (طوق): ṭāqa is the amount a man can do with hardship, likened to the ṭawq that encircles a thing; 2:286 = what is hard for us to undergo, not what we have no qudra for; 2:249; negating ṭāqa may express negating qudra.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 25 places of قدر_1 read): 'to have power / be able' is in 8 ayat (2:264, 5:34, 14:18, 16:75, 16:76, 48:21, 57:29, 90:5), all negated or 'before you gain power'; the count also holds 'to straiten' provision (12 places incl. 21:87, e.g. 13:26, 65:7, 89:16), 'to esteem' Allah as He deserves (6:91, 22:74, 39:67) and 'to measure, determine' (54:12, 77:23) — only ability ayat are cited. اِسْتَطَاعَ 42× (incl. isṭāʿa in 18:97); طَاقَة 2× (2:249, 2:286). 9:42 (an excuse sworn about going out with the Prophet) is not cited.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 3 flags, fixed: al-muḥaqqiqūn rendered 'the careful scholars' in both languages, his limit restored (lack of practice: the obligation may still hold, no excuse); 3:97 bs; قَدَرَ 'almost always negated' softened to 'often' (5:34 is affirmative).

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries طوع, قدر, طوق (2026-11-06): 28 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): Dropped limit: the instrument is needed only 'if the act is instrumental, like writing'. 'scholars he follows' for 'inda l-muḥaqqiqīn' is acceptable; members/0/ayat/2/why (reworded): He does not say 'not impossible'; he says hard for lack of practice, and that obligation can still hold and it is no excuse

meaning.en: to be able (to have the means)

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, istiṭāʿa je uža od qudre: to je postojanje svega što djelo čini izvodljivim – po pomnim učenjacima (al-muḥaqqiqūn), četiri stvari: odgovarajuća građa onoga ko radi, predodžba djela, ono na čemu se djeluje i sredstvo ako ga djelo traži. Zato se hadž veže za onoga „ko može naći put do nje“ (3:97). Kaže se i za ono što je teško zbog nenaviknutosti; tada, kaže on, obaveza može ostati i to nije opravdanje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, istiṭāʿa is narrower than qudra: it is having all that makes an act feasible — for the careful scholars (al-muḥaqqiqūn), four things: a fitting constitution of the doer, a conception of the act, the material it acts on, and a tool if the act needs one. Hence the Hajj is tied to one “who can find a way thither” (3:97). It is also said of what is hard for lack of practice; then, he says, the obligation may still hold and this is no excuse.

why.bs: „Ljudi su Allahu dužni hodočastiti Kuću – onaj ko može naći put do nje“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And pilgrimage to the House is a duty unto Allah for mankind, for him who can find a way thither” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I nisu ga mogli preći, niti su ga mogli probiti“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet za dva oblika glagola (isṭāʿa i istaṭāʿa).
why.en: “And (Gog and Magog) were not able to surmount, nor could they pierce (it)” — ar-Rāġib cites it for two forms of the verb (isṭāʿa and istaṭāʿa).

why.bs: „Ti, zaista, nećeš moći sa mnom strpljivo izdržati“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet za ono što je čovjeku teško zbog nenaviknutosti.
why.en: “Lo! thou canst not bear with me” — ar-Rāġib cites it for what is hard for a person for lack of practice.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, qudra kod čovjeka je stanje kojim može učiniti nešto određeno, a kod Allaha znači da Mu nikakva nemoć nije svojstvena, kako Njemu priliči; zato se za čovjeka kaže ‚moćan je za to i to‘, a apsolutna moć pripada samo Allahu. U Kur'anu se glagol, kad je riječ o ljudima, često javlja u niječnom obliku: nemaju moći ni nad čim što su stekli (2:264); a 5:34 govori o sticanju moći nad prekršiocima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, qudra in man is a state by which he can do a certain thing, while of Allah it means no incapacity belongs to Him, as befits Him; so a man is called ‘able to do such and such’, and absolute power is Allah's alone. In the Quran, said of people, the verb often comes in denial: “They have no control of aught of that which they have gained” (2:264); yet 5:34 speaks of gaining power over wrongdoers.

why.bs: „… nad onim što su stekli nemaju nikakve moći“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… They have no control of aught of that which they have gained” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Allah daje primjer: rob, u tuđem posjedu, koji ni nad čim nema moći …“
why.en: “Allah coineth a similitude: (on the one hand) a (mere) chattel slave, who hath control of nothing …”

why.bs: „Izuzev onih koji se pokaju dok još nad njima nemate moći.“
why.en: “Save those who repent before ye overpower them.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ṭāqa je mjera onoga što čovjek može učiniti s mukom – po slici obruča (ṭawq) koji nešto obuhvata. Zato dova u 2:286 ne znači ‚ne opterećuj nas onim za šta uopće nemamo moći‘, nego ono što bi nam bilo teško podnijeti; ponekad se, kaže on, nijekanjem ṭāqe niječe i sama moć.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ṭāqa is the measure of what one can do with hardship — from the image of a ring (ṭawq) encircling a thing. So the prayer in 2:286 (لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ) does not ask to be spared only what lies wholly beyond our ability, but what would be hard for us to bear; at times, he says, denying ṭāqa denies power itself.

why.bs: „Gospodaru naš, ne opterećuj nas onim za šta nam nema snage!“ – ar-Rāġib: ono što nam je teško podnijeti.
why.en: “Our Lord! Impose not on us that which we have not the strength to bear!” — ar-Rāġib: what is hard for us to undergo.

why.bs: „Nemamo mi danas snage za Džaluta i njegove vojnike“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet u istom značenju.
why.en: “We have no power [ṭāqa: strength] this day against Goliath and his hosts” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah in the same sense.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače naći. Ar-Rāġib alfā objašnjava upravo sa wajada; razlika je u tome koliko je riječ široka.
shared.en: Both words mean to find. ar-Rāġib explains alfā simply by wajada; the difference is in how wide the word is.

tellApart.bs: Naći – osjetilima, razumom ili osjećajem, pa i imati nešto na dohvat; najšira riječ → وَجَدَ; zateći nekoga u stanju u kojem je već bio – u Kur'anu očeve na njihovom putu i muža kod vrata → أَلْفَى.
tellApart.en: To find — by the senses, the mind or a feeling, even to have something within reach; the widest word → وَجَدَ; to come upon someone in the state they were already in — in the Quran fathers on their way and a husband at the door → أَلْفَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries وجد, لفى
notes: ar-Rāġib (وجد): wuǧūd is of kinds: by one of the five senses; by the faculty of appetite (finding satiety) and of anger (grief, displeasure); by the mind or through it (knowing Allah, prophethood); what is ascribed to Allah means pure knowledge, since He is above organs and instruments (7:102); finding also expresses being able to get hold of (9:5, 28:15); 27:23 is finding by sight and insight; 'fa-lam taǧidū māʾan' = you could not obtain water. (لفى): alfaytu = waǧadtu, with 2:170 and 12:25.

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): أَلْفَى 3× (2:170, 12:25, 37:69), always with someone found in a state (fathers on their way, fathers astray, a husband at the door); the saying of 2:170 comes with وَجَدْنَا in 5:104 and 31:21 (and 43:22). وَجَدَ is 106×. 'Coming upon unexpectedly' as the sense of alfā is a later linguists' distinction, not ar-Rāġib's: our nuance rests only on these three places. The en quote of 2:170 is Pickthall's, with [alfaynā] beside it.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): all claims OK.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries وجد, لفى (2026-11-06): 17 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): His pair is al-ǧawāriḥ wa-l-ālāt (limbs/organs and instruments), not senses

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, nalaženje ima više vrsta: jednim od pet osjetila, prohtjevom (naći sitost) i srdžbom (tuga, ljutnja), te razumom, kao spoznaja Allaha. Kad se pripiše Allahu, znači čisto znanje, kako Njemu priliči, jer je On iznad udova i oruđa. Riječ znači i imati nešto na dohvat.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, finding is of several kinds: by one of the five senses; by appetite (finding satiety) and by anger (grief, displeasure); and by the mind, as knowing Allah. When ascribed to Allah it means pure knowledge, as befits Him, for He is above limbs and instruments. The word also means having something within reach.

why.bs: „Nismo našli da većina njih drži do zavjeta, nego smo našli da su većinom nepokorni“ – Allahovo nalaženje je znanje; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “We found no (loyalty to any) covenant in most of them. Nay, most of them We found wrong-doers” — Allah's finding is knowledge; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Pupavac Sulejmanu: „Našao sam, zaista, ženu koja njima vlada“ – ar-Rāġib: nalaženje i okom i razumom, jer je pupavac o njima i prosudio.
why.en: The hoopoe to Solomon: “Lo! I found a woman ruling over them” — ar-Rāġib: finding by sight and by insight, for the hoopoe went on to judge their state.

why.bs: „Nama je dovoljno ono na čemu smo našli svoje očeve“ – ista rečenica kao u 2:170, ali s wajada.
why.en: “Enough for us is that wherein we found our fathers” — the same saying as in 2:170, but with wajada.

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib alfā objašnjava jednom riječju: ‚našao sam‘. U Kur'anu (3×) riječ uvijek znači zateći nekoga u stanju u kojem je već bio: dvaput je riječ o očevima, jednom Jusuf i žena zatiču njenog muža kod vrata. Ista rečenica o očevima dolazi i s wajada (5:104, 31:21), pa je razlika mala.
nuance.en: ar-Rāġib explains alfā with one word: ‘I found’. In the Quran (3×) it always means coming upon someone in the state they were already in: twice it is about fathers, once Joseph and the woman meet her husband standing by the door. The same saying about the fathers also comes with wajada (5:104, 31:21), so the difference is small.

why.bs: „Ne, nego ćemo se držati onoga na čemu smo zatekli svoje očeve“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “We follow that wherein we found [alfaynā] our fathers” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… i kod vrata zatekoše gospodara njenog“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… and they met her lord and master at the door” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Oni su, zaista, zatekli očeve svoje u zabludi.“
why.en: “They indeed found their fathers astray.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi izražavaju ‚ne‘ prema nečemu. Razlikuju se po tome da li je to osjećaj u duši ili odlučno odbijanje.
shared.en: Both words express a ‘no’ to something. They differ in whether it is a feeling within or a firm refusal.

tellApart.bs: Osjećati odbojnost prema nečemu – po naravi, ili po razumu i vjeri; unutrašnje stanje → كَرِهَ; žestoko odbiti, ne pristati – svako ibāʾ je odbijanje, ali nije svako odbijanje ibāʾ → أَبَى.
tellApart.en: To feel aversion to something — by nature, or by reason and the Law; an inner state → كَرِهَ; to refuse vehemently, not to consent — every ibāʾ is a refusal, but not every refusal is ibāʾ → أَبَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries كره, أبى
notes: ar-Rāġib (كره): 'qīla' karh and kurh are one; 'qīla' karh is hardship that reaches a man from outside, by compulsion, and kurh what he feels from himself and loathes — of two kinds: loathed by nature, or by reason / the Law; so a man may say of one thing 'I want it and dislike it'; 2:216 'you dislike it by nature'; 49:12 the soul is made to loathe it; 'karihtu' is used of both, though more often of one of them (the OpenITI text is unvowelled, so we do not say which). (أبى): ibāʾ is intense refusal (šiddat al-imtināʿ): every ibāʾ is imtināʿ, not every imtināʿ ibāʾ; cites 9:32, 9:8, 2:34 'abā wa-stakbara', 'illā Iblīsa abā'.

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): كَرِهَ 17× in 16 ayat, 7 of them in 'even if the disbelievers / polytheists / criminals dislike it' (8:8, 9:32, 9:33, 10:82, 40:14, 61:8, 61:9). أَبَى 13× in 12 ayat (twice in 2:282): its subject is Iblīs (2:34, 15:31, 20:116), Pharaoh (20:56), most people (17:89, 17:99, 25:50), the people of a town (18:77), hearts (9:8), the heavens, earth and mountains (33:72), a scribe and witnesses (2:282), and Allah (9:32). Not cited: the Iblīs ayat (the prostration to Adam was left out in batch 6; it needs tafsir context) and 33:72 (the amāna is read many ways; ar-Rāġib lists four).

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 flag, fixed: the karh/kurh distinction is a view he reports (qīla), beside the view that they are one; 'karihtu' is used of both (which more often is not said: the OpenITI text is unvowelled).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries كره, أبى, أمن (2026-11-06): 14 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): Our text lacks harakat, so which of karh/kurh is 'more frequent' is not visible here; please confirm the vowelling in a printed edition before relying on it; members/0/nuance (reworded): his limit restored: karihtu is said of both kinds (which one is more frequent is not stated, the text being unvowelled)

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib navodi jedno mišljenje da su karh i kurh isto, i drugo koje razlikuje teškoću nametnutu izvana (karh) od odbojnosti koju čovjek osjeća u sebi (kurh); ovu drugu dijeli na dvije vrste: po naravi, i po razumu ili vjeri. Zato, kaže on, čovjek za istu stvar može reći da je želi i da mu je mrska. Glagol karihtu se, kaže on, koristi za oboje.
nuance.en: ar-Rāġib reports one view that karh and kurh are the same, and another that distinguishes hardship imposed from outside (karh) from the aversion a person feels within (kurh); this second he divides in two: by nature, and by reason or the Law. So, he says, one may say of the same thing that he wants it and dislikes it. The verb karihtu, he says, is used of both.

why.bs: „Propisana vam je borba, iako vam je mrska. A može biti da vam je mrsko nešto, a ono je dobro za vas“ – mrsko po naravi, kaže ar-Rāġib; on navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Warfare is ordained for you, though it is hateful unto you; but it may happen that ye hate a thing which is good for you” — hateful by nature, ar-Rāġib says; he cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Zar bi ijedan od vas volio da jede meso mrtvog brata svoga? Pa vama je to mrsko!“ – ar-Rāġib: duša je stvorena da se od toga gnuša.
why.en: “Would one of you love to eat the flesh of his dead brother? Ye abhor that” — ar-Rāġib: the soul is made to loathe it.

why.bs: „To je stoga što im je mrsko ono što je Allah objavio, pa je On njihova djela poništio.“
why.en: “That is because they are averse to that which Allah hath revealed, therefor maketh He their actions fruitless.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ibāʾ je žestoko uzdržavanje: svako ibāʾ je odbijanje, ali nije svako odbijanje ibāʾ. U Kur'anu tako odbijaju ljudi koji ne pristaju ni na šta osim nevjerovanja, a i Allah, kako Njemu priliči, ‚odbija‘ sve osim da upotpuni Svoje svjetlo.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ibāʾ is intense holding back: every ibāʾ is a refusal, but not every refusal is ibāʾ. In the Quran people so refuse, consenting to nothing but disbelief, and Allah, as befits Him, ‘refuses’ all but to perfect His light.

why.bs: „Hoće da Allahovo svjetlo ustima svojim ugase, a Allah odbija sve drugo osim da Svoje svjetlo upotpuni, makar to nevjernicima bilo mrsko“ – obje riječi u istom ajetu; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Fain would they put out the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah disdaineth [yaʾbā: refuseth] (aught) save that He shall perfect His light, however much the disbelievers are averse” — both words in one ayah; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Mi smo, zaista, ljudima u ovom Kur'anu na razne načine iznijeli svakojake primjere, ali većina ljudi odbi sve osim nevjerovanja.“
why.en: “And verily We have displayed for mankind in this Qur'an all kind of similitudes, but most of mankind refuse aught save disbelief.”

why.bs: „… zamoliše njene stanovnike da ih nahrane, ali su ovi odbili da im budu domaćini“ – Musa i njegov pratilac.
why.en: “… they asked its folk for food, but they refused to make them guests” — Moses and his companion.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače uzeti nešto s mjesta gdje je bilo. Razlikuju se po načinu: izvući, ugrabiti u brzini, ili oteti silom od drugoga.
shared.en: All three words mean taking a thing from where it was. They differ in manner: drawing out, snatching in haste, or taking by force from another.

tellApart.bs: Izvući nešto s njegova mjesta – i ruku i ono što je u srcu; opća riječ → نَزَعَ; ugrabiti brzo, u trenu → خَطِفَ; oteti od drugoga silom → سَلَبَ.
tellApart.en: To pull a thing from its place — a hand, or what is in the heart; the general word → نَزَعَ; to snatch quickly, in an instant → خَطِفَ; to take from another by force → سَلَبَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نزع, خطف, سلب
notes: ar-Rāġib (نزع): nazʿ is pulling a thing from its place (ǧaḏbuhu min maqarrihi); used of non-bodily things too, as drawing enmity and love from the heart ('wa-nazaʿnā mā fī ṣudūrihim min ġill', 7:43 / 15:47); 'nazaʿa fulān kaḏā' = salaba, with 3:26; on 79:1 and 54:20 he gives 'qīla' readings. (خطف): ḫaṭf / iḫtiṭāf is iḫtilās bi-s-surʿa, snatching with speed; 37:10 of the eavesdropping devils, 22:31, 2:20; yataḫaṭṭafu (29:67) = they are killed and robbed. (سلب): salb is taking a thing from another by force (ʿalā l-qahr), 22:73.

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): نَزَعَ 10× — Moses drawing out his hand (7:108, 26:33), malice drawn from hearts in Paradise (7:43, 15:47), mercy withdrawn (11:9), kingship (3:26), one drawn out of every nation (19:69, 28:75), garments (7:27), the wind tearing people out (54:20). خَطِفَ (Form I) 3×: 2:20, 22:31, 37:10; the Form V تَخَطَّفَ (8:26, 28:57, 29:67) is a separate verb, not counted or cited. سَلَبَ 1× (22:73). Not cited: 7:27 (Satan stripping the garments of Adam and his wife; it needs its context).
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 flag, fixed: ḫaṭf is snatching 'with speed' (not 'by stealth'); 22:31 marked as a simile.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, nazʿ je povući nešto s njegova mjesta, a kaže se i za ono što nije tijelo: izvući neprijateljstvo ili ljubav iz srca. Može značiti i oduzeti, kao vlast. U Kur'anu Musa izvlači ruku, a Allah izvlači zlobu iz srca stanovnika Dženneta.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, nazʿ is pulling a thing from its place, and it is said of what is not a body too: drawing enmity or love out of the heart. It can also mean taking away, as kingship. In the Quran Moses draws out his hand, and Allah draws malice out of the hearts of the people of Paradise.

why.bs: „I izvukli smo iz grudi njihovih svaku zlobu; ispod njih rijeke teku“ – o stanovnicima Dženneta; ar-Rāġib navodi ove riječi.
why.en: “And We remove whatever rancour may be in their hearts. Rivers flow beneath them” — of the people of Paradise; ar-Rāġib cites these words.

why.bs: „Zatim izvuče svoju ruku, i gle – ona bijela, svima koji gledaju“ – Musa.
why.en: “And he drew forth his hand (from his bosom), and lo! it was white for the beholders” — Moses.

why.bs: „Reci: O Allahu, Vlasniče vlasti, Ti vlast daješ kome hoćeš i oduzimaš je od koga hoćeš“ – ovdje nazʿ znači oduzeti, kako Allahu priliči; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Say: O Allah! Owner of Sovereignty! Thou givest sovereignty unto whom Thou wilt, and Thou withdrawest sovereignty from whom Thou wilt” — here nazʿ means taking away, as befits Allah; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḫaṭf je ugrabiti u brzini. U Kur'anu tako munja samo što ne ugrabi vid, šejtan ugrabi ono što prisluškuje, a u poređenju ptice grabe onoga ko je pao s neba.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ḫaṭf is snatching away with speed. In the Quran lightning almost snatches sight, a devil snatches what it overhears, and, in a simile, one who has fallen from the sky is snatched by birds.

why.bs: „Munja zamalo da im ugrabi vid“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “The lightning almost snatcheth away their sight from them” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Osim onoga koji nešto ugrabi, pa ga stigne prodorna zublja“ – ar-Rāġib: o šejtanima koji kradom prisluškuju.
why.en: “Save him who snatcheth a fragment, and there pursueth him a piercing flame” — ar-Rāġib: of the devils who eavesdrop by stealth.

why.bs: „… a ko Allahu pripisuje druga – kao da se s neba sručio, a ptice ga ugrabile“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… for whoso ascribeth partners unto Allah, it is as if he had fallen from the sky and the birds had snatched him” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

meaning.en: to rob, to take by force

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, salb je oduzeti nešto drugome silom. U Kur'anu dolazi samo jednom, u poređenju o nemoći onih koji se mimo Allaha prizivaju: ne mogu povratiti ni ono što im muha otme.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, salb is taking a thing from another by force. In the Quran it comes only once, in a parable of the helplessness of those invoked besides Allah: they cannot recover even what a fly robs from them.

why.bs: „A kad bi im muha išta otela, ne bi joj to mogli oduzeti natrag“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And if the fly took [yaslubhum: robbed them of] something from them, they could not rescue it from it” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

title.bs: Poricati: utjerivati u laž, svjesno nijekati, ne priznavati

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače odbiti nešto kao istinu. Razlikuju se po tome šta se odbija i šta je u srcu onoga ko odbija: proglasiti lažnim onoga ko govori, zanijekati ono u što je srce uvjereno, ili ne priznati nešto kao poznato.
shared.en: All three words mean refusing something as true. They differ in what is refused and what is in the heart of the one refusing: calling the speaker a liar, denying what the heart is sure of, or not acknowledging something as known.

tellApart.bs: Proglasiti lažnim onoga ko govori istinu – poslanike, znakove, istinu → كَذَّبَ; svjesno zanijekati ono što srce potvrđuje → جَحَدَ; ne priznati, odbaciti kao nepoznato – srcem ili samo jezikom → أَنْكَرَ.
tellApart.en: Calling the one who speaks the truth a liar — messengers, signs, the truth → كَذَّبَ; knowingly denying what the heart affirms → جَحَدَ; not acknowledging, rejecting as unknown — with the heart or with the tongue alone → أَنْكَرَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries كذب, جحد, نكر
notes: ar-Rāġib (كذب): kaḏḏabtuhu is ascribing a lie to someone, whether he is truthful or lying, but what comes in the Quran is the belying of the truthful (kaḏḏabū bi-āyātinā, rabbi nṣurnī bimā kaḏḏabūn, bal kaḏḏabū bi-l-ḥaqq …); akḏabtuhu is finding him a liar; on 6:33 fa-innahum lā yukaḏḏibūnaka (read with and without shadda): they do not find you a liar and cannot establish a lie against you. (جحد): ǧuḥūd is denying what the heart affirms and affirming what the heart denies; cites 27:14 and 'bi-āyātinā yaǧḥadūn'. (نكر): inkār is the opposite of ʿirfān (recognising); at root something comes to the heart that it cannot picture, a kind of ignorance (11:70, 12:58); it is used of denial with the tongue, whose cause is denial of the heart, but the tongue may deny a thing whose image is present in the heart, and then it lies; so 16:83 yaʿrifūna niʿmata llāhi ṯumma yunkirūnahā, and 40:81.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 12 / 3 places read): جَحَدَ always takes bi-; its object is Allah's signs (āyāt) in every place but 16:71 (His favour). أَنْكَرَ (Form IV) is 3×: 13:36 (some of the clans deny part of it), 16:83, 40:81. كَذَّبَ (Form II) is the common word (its objects: messengers, signs, the truth, the Day). 6:33 is a consolation addressed to the Prophet, not a reproach; ar-Rāġib's reading of it is given as his.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: 'svjesno' removed from the Bosnian quotes of 6:33 and 29:49 (not in the Arabic).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries كذب, جحد, نكر (2026-11-06): 18 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): He states a general rule ('what comes in the Quran is in belying the truthful') without 'always'; dropping 'always' keeps it exactly his. The object list (messengers, signs, the truth) matches his examples (āyātinā, ʿabdanā, bi-l-ḥaqq, rusul); members/0/ayat/1/why (reworded): His comment on 6:33 stops at 'cannot establish your lie'; he does not say it is ǧuḥūd (that word comes from the ayah itself: bi-āyāti llāhi yaǧḥadūn). The current wording puts it after 'ar-Rāġib explains:'

meaning.en: to belie, to call a lie

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, takḏīb je pripisati nekome laž, govorio on istinu ili ne; ali u Kur'anu, kaže on, to je utjerivanje u laž onoga ko govori istinu: poslanika, Allahovih znakova, istine.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, takḏīb is ascribing a lie to someone, whether he speaks the truth or not; but in the Quran, he says, it is the belying of one who speaks the truth: messengers, Allah's signs, the truth.

why.bs: „Nuhov narod utjerao je u laž poslanike“ – utjerani u laž su oni koji su govorili istinu.
why.en: “Noah's folk denied the messengers” — those called liars were the ones who spoke the truth.

why.bs: „… oni tebe ne utjeruju u laž, nego zulumćari niječu Allahove ajete“ – ar-Rāġib objašnjava: ne nalaze te lažovom i ne mogu dokazati tvoju laž; ono što čine, sam ajet naziva ǧuḥūd.
why.en: “… they deny not thee (Muhammad) but evil-doers flout the revelations of Allah” — ar-Rāġib explains: they do not find you a liar and cannot establish a lie against you; what they do, the ayah itself calls ǧuḥūd.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ǧuḥūd je zanijekati ono što srce potvrđuje, ili potvrditi ono što srce niječe. U Kur'anu (svih 12 mjesta) glagol ide s prijedlogom bi-, a predmet su mu Allahovi znakovi, osim u 16:71, gdje je to Njegova blagodat.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ǧuḥūd is denying what the heart affirms, or affirming what the heart denies. In the Quran (all 12 places) the verb takes the preposition bi-, and its object is Allah's signs, except in 16:71, where it is His favour.

why.bs: „I zanijekali su ih, a duše su im u njih bile uvjerene, iz nepravde i oholosti“ – nijekanje uprkos znanju; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And they denied them, though their souls acknowledged them, for spite and arrogance” — denial against knowledge; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… a Naše ajete niječu samo zulumćari“ – ajeti su jasni u prsima onih kojima je dato znanje.
why.en: “… none deny Our revelations save wrong-doers” — the revelations are clear in the hearts of those given knowledge.

meaning.en: to disown, to refuse to acknowledge

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, inkār je suprotnost prepoznavanju (ʿirfān): u srce dođe nešto što ono ne može sebi predočiti. Kaže se i za odricanje jezikom, a jezik ponekad odriče ono čija je slika u srcu prisutna – i tada laže; tako on razumije 16:83.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, inkār is the opposite of recognising (ʿirfān): something comes to the heart that it cannot picture. It is also said of disowning with the tongue, and the tongue sometimes disowns a thing whose image is present in the heart — and then it lies; so he understands 16:83.

why.bs: „Oni poznaju Allahovu blagodat, a zatim je ne priznaju …“ – poznaju je, pa je ipak odriču; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “They know the favour of Allah and then deny it” — they know it, and yet disown it; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… pa koji to od Allahovih znakova ne priznajete?“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Which, then, of the tokens of Allah do ye deny?” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače rugati se i omalovažavati. Razlikuju se po onome čemu se ruga i po slici koju riječ nosi: ismijavanje ljudi, ili sprdnja i šala s onim što zaslužuje ozbiljnost.
shared.en: Both words mean mocking and belittling. They differ in what is mocked and in the image the word carries: ridiculing people, or making a jest of what deserves to be taken seriously.

tellApart.bs: Ismijavati nekoga – s min, a kad je predmet spomenut, to su uvijek ljudi → سَخِرَ; zbijati sprdnju – s bi-, i s ljudima, i s Allahovim ajetima, i s opomenom; ar-Rāġib: traženje šale u potaji → اِسْتَهْزَأَ.
tellApart.en: Ridiculing someone — with min, and when the object is named it is always people → سَخِرَ; making a jest — with bi-, of people, of Allah's signs, of the warning; ar-Rāġib: seeking out a hidden jest → اِسْتَهْزَأَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries سخر, هزؤ
notes: ar-Rāġib (سخر): the entry is mainly taṣḫīr (driving to a purpose by compulsion); within it: saḫirtu minhu and istasḫartuhu 'for mocking him', citing 11:38 and 37:12; on 23:110 / 38:63 siḫriyyan read both as subjection and as mockery, the next words (wa-kuntum minhum taḍḥakūn) pointing to the second. (هزؤ): hazʾ is joking in secret (mazḥ fī ḫufya), also said of what is like joking; istihzāʾ is seeking out hazʾ, though it may express simply doing it; cites 9:65 and other ayat; istihzāʾ cannot truly be from Allah, as play cannot; 2:15 means He requites them with the requital of mockery: He gave them respite, then seized them unawares, or, since they mocked and He knew it, it is as if He mocked them; 'on these ways' he reads 9:79 saḫira llāhu minhum.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 7 / 19 ayat read): سَخِرَ always takes min; where its object is named it is people (Noah 11:38, the believers 2:212 / 9:79, messengers 6:10 / 21:41, a folk 49:11). اِسْتَهْزَأَ takes bi-: messengers (15:11, 36:30, 43:7), signs (4:140, 30:10), 'Allah and His signs and His messenger' (9:65), and 'what they used to scoff at' — the warned punishment (6:5, 16:34, 39:48 …). 6:10 and 21:41 hold both verbs. Allah as the subject (2:15, 9:79) carries ar-Rāġib's 'requital' reading and 'as befits Him'.

al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib ga spominje unutar natuknice o potčinjavanju (taṣḫīr): ‚saḫirtu minhu‘ znači ismijati nekoga. U Kur'anu (7 ajeta) glagol u šest njih ide s min, a kad je spomenuto koga ismijavaju, to su uvijek ljudi: Nuh, vjernici, poslanici; u 37:12 stoji sam (‚ti se čudiš, a oni ismijavaju‘). Kad se kaže za Allaha (9:79), ar-Rāġib to tumači kao i istihzāʾ: On im uzvraća za ismijavanje – kako Njemu priliči.
nuance.en: Ar-Rāġib mentions it within his entry on subjection (taṣḫīr): ‘saḫirtu minhu’ means to ridicule someone. In the Quran (7 ayat) the verb takes min in six of them, and when it is said whom they ridicule, it is always people: Noah, the believers, messengers; in 37:12 it stands alone (‘you marvel, and they ridicule’). When it is said of Allah (9:79), ar-Rāġib reads it as he reads istihzāʾ: He requites them for their ridicule — as befits Him.

why.bs: „O vjernici, neka jedni ljudi ne ismijavaju druge – možda su bolji od njih …“ – ismijavanje ljudi, zabranjeno među vjernicima.
why.en: “O ye who believe! Let not a folk deride a folk who may be better than they (are)” — ridicule of people, forbidden among believers.

why.bs: Glavešine Nuhova naroda ismijavaju ga dok gradi lađu, a on im odgovara da će im se isto vratiti – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: The chiefs of Noah's people ridicule him as he builds the ship, and he answers that the same will come back to them — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… pa ih ismijavaju – Allah njih ismijava …“ – kod Allaha to je uzvrat, kako Njemu priliči, kako ar-Rāġib tumači.
why.en: “… and deride them - Allah (Himself) derideth them” — from Allah it is requital, as befits Him, as ar-Rāġib explains.

meaning.en: to scoff, to make a jest of

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, hazʾ je šala u potaji, a istihzāʾ je traženje takve šale. On kaže da istihzāʾ od Allaha u pravom smislu nije moguć, kao ni igra; 2:15 znači da im On uzvraća za izrugivanje – kako Njemu priliči. U Kur'anu ide s bi-, a predmet su poslanici, Allahovi ajeti, pa i ‚Allah, Njegovi ajeti i Njegov Poslanik‘ (9:65).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, hazʾ is joking in secret, and istihzāʾ is seeking out such a jest. He says istihzāʾ cannot truly come from Allah, as play cannot; 2:15 means that He requites them with the requital of scoffing — as befits Him. In the Quran it takes bi-, and its object is messengers, Allah's signs, even ‘Allah and His signs and His messenger’ (9:65).

why.bs: „… Reci: ‚Zar ste se Allahu, Njegovim ajetima i Njegovom Poslaniku izrugivali?‘“ – oni su to nazvali ‚pričom i igrom‘; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Say: Was it at Allah and His revelations and His messenger that ye did scoff?” — they had called it ‘talk and jest’; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… pa je one koji su ih ismijavali stiglo ono čemu su se izrugivali“ – oba glagola u jednom ajetu: سَخِرُوا za ljude koji su to činili, يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ za ono s čim su zbijali sprdnju.
why.en: “… that whereat they scoffed surrounded such of them as did deride” — both verbs in one ayah: سَخِرُوا of the people who did it, يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ of what they made a jest of.

why.bs: Allah im uzvraća za izrugivanje i ostavlja ih da slijepo lutaju u svojoj obijesti – ar-Rāġib: uzvrat za izrugivanje, kako Njemu priliči; dao im je vremena, pa ih iznenada zahvatio.
why.en: Allah requites their scoffing and leaves them to wander in their transgression — ar-Rāġib: the requital of scoffing, as befits Him; He gave them respite, then seized them unawares.

title.bs: Započeti, podići u postojanje, stvoriti bez uzora

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o nastanku. Razlikuju se po tome šta ističu: početak koji dolazi prije onoga što slijedi, nastanak koji raste i razvija se, ili stvaranje bez ikakva uzora.
shared.en: All three words speak of coming to be. They differ in what they stress: a beginning that comes before what follows, a coming to be that grows and develops, or creation without any model.

tellApart.bs: Učiniti nešto prvim, započeti – Allah započinje stvaranje pa ga ponavlja → بَدَأَ; dati da nastane i podizati, najčešće o živim bićima → أَنْشَأَ; Stvoritelj bez uzora, oruđa, tvari, vremena i mjesta – samo Allah → بَدِيع.
tellApart.en: Making something first, beginning — Allah begins creation, then repeats it → بَدَأَ; bringing into being and raising, mostly of living things → أَنْشَأَ; the Originator, without model, tool, matter, time or place — Allah alone → بَدِيع.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries بدأ, نشأ, بدع
notes: ar-Rāġib (بدأ): badaʾtu bi-kaḏā = I put it first; badʾ and ibdāʾ are putting a thing before another, a kind of putting first; cites 32:7, 29:20 kayfa badaʾa l-ḫalq, 10:34 / 30:11 Allāhu yabdaʾu l-ḫalq, 7:29; mabdaʾ of a thing is what it is made of or comes from (letters for speech, wood for a door, the stone for the palm); Allah is al-mubdiʾ al-muʿīd, the cause of the beginning and the end; a thing badīʾ is one not known before, like al-badīʿ. (نشأ): našʾ and našʾa are bringing a thing about and raising it (iḥdāṯ aš-šayʾ wa-tarbiyatuhu); naša'a s-saḥāb for its forming in the air and growing bit by bit (13:12 wa-yunšiʾu s-saḥāba ṯ-ṯiqāl); inšāʾ is bringing into existence and raising, said mostly of animate beings (67:23, 53:32, 23:31, 23:14, 56:61, 56:62); 'all these are of the bringing into existence proper to Allah'; 56:72 likens bringing out fire to bringing man into being. (بدع): ibdāʿ is making a thing without following or imitating a model; of Allah it is bringing a thing into existence without tool, matter, time or place, and that is Allah's alone; badīʿ is said of the originator (badīʿu s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ) and of the originated (a new-dug well).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 11 / 20 / 2 places read): بَدَأَ (Form I) is Allah's beginning of creation in 9 places, mostly paired with يُعِيدُهُ; 9:13 (they began against you) and 12:76 (Joseph began with their bags) are of people. أَنْشَأَ (Form IV) has Allah as subject in every place but 56:72, the rhetorical 'did you produce its tree?'. بَدِيع is only 2:117 and 6:101, both بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ. 29:20 is quoted for its يُنْشِئُ only (Pickthall renders its بَدَأَ 'originated'). 46:9 (bidʿ, of the Prophet) is not this lemma and is not cited.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 3 flags, fixed: 12:76 no longer says who searched (the mufassirun differ); 'bez uzora' taken out of the Bosnian quotes of 2:117 and 6:101 and the 2:117 quote re-translated; he cites only the opening words of 2:117.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

Other numbers checked: 32:7, 10:34, 30:11, 7:29, 13:12, 67:23, 53:32, 23:31, 23:14, 56:61, 56:62, 56:72 all match

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, badʾ je staviti nešto ispred drugoga, učiniti ga prvim; Allah je al-Mubdiʾ al-Muʿīd, uzrok početka i kraja. U Kur'anu najčešće o Allahovom započinjanju stvaranja, uz ponavljanje (يُعِيدُهُ) – kako Njemu priliči; ali i o ljudima: u 12:76 pretraga je počela od vreća njegove braće, prije vreće Jusufova brata.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, badʾ is putting a thing before another, making it first; Allah is al-Mubdiʾ al-Muʿīd, the cause of the beginning and of the end. In the Quran it is mostly Allah's beginning of creation, paired with repeating it (يُعِيدُهُ) — as befits Him; but also of people: in 12:76 the search began with the brothers' bags, before the bag of Joseph's brother.

why.bs: „… i započeo je stvaranje čovjeka od ilovače“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… and He began the creation of man from clay” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Pa je počeo od njihovih vreća, prije vreće svoga brata …“ – osnovni smisao: jedno staviti ispred drugoga.
why.en: “Then he (Joseph) began the search with their bags before his brother's bag” — the basic sense: putting one thing before another.

meaning.bs: podići u postojanje, dati da nastane i raste
meaning.en: to bring forth, to bring into being and raise

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, inšāʾ je dati da nešto nastane i podizati ga, a najčešće se kaže o živim bićima; Allahovo podizanje ljudi i pokoljenja on vidi kao stvaranje svojstveno samo Allahu – kako Njemu priliči. Tako i oblaci nastaju u zraku i rastu malo-pomalo (13:12).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, inšāʾ is bringing a thing into being and raising it, and it is said mostly of living beings; Allah's bringing forth of people and generations he sees as creation proper to Allah alone — as befits Him. So too clouds form in the air and grow bit by bit (13:12).

why.bs: „… zatim smo ga podigli kao drugo stvorenje …“ – nakon stupnjeva, novi rast; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… and then produced it as another creation” — after the stages, a new growth; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… i podiže teške oblake“ – oblaci koji nastaju i rastu malo-pomalo; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… and raiseth the heavy clouds” — clouds that form and grow bit by bit; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… zatim Allah podiže posljednje nastajanje …“ – drugo stvaranje, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “… then Allah bringeth forth the later growth” — the second coming-to-be, as befits Him.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ibdāʿ je napraviti nešto ne slijedeći nikakav uzor; kad se kaže o Allahu, to je stvaranje bez oruđa, tvari, vremena i mjesta – a to je samo Allahovo. U Kur'anu dolazi samo dvaput, oba puta kao بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ibdāʿ is making a thing without following any model; said of Allah, it is creation without tool, matter, time or place — and that is Allah's alone. In the Quran it comes only twice, both times as بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ.

why.bs: „Stvoritelj nebesa i Zemlje! Kad odredi neku stvar, samo joj kaže: ‚Budi!‘ – i ona biva.“ – stvaranje bez prethodnog uzora i tvari, kako Njemu priliči; ar-Rāġib navodi početne riječi, ‚Stvoritelj nebesa i Zemlje‘.
why.en: “The Originator of the heavens and the earth! When He decreeth a thing, He saith unto it only: Be! and it is.” — creation with no prior model or matter, as befits Him; ar-Rāġib cites the opening words, ‘Originator of the heavens and the earth’.

why.bs: „Stvoritelj nebesa i Zemlje! Kako bi On imao dijete …“
why.en: “The Originator of the heavens and the earth! How can He have a child”

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače izvući nekoga iz opasnosti. نَجَّى i أَنْجَى su dva oblika istog korijena, čiji je osnovni smisao, prema ar-Rāġibu, odvojiti se od nečega; أَنْقَذَ ističe izvlačenje iz škripca.
shared.en: All three words mean bringing someone out of danger. نَجَّى and أَنْجَى are two forms of one root, whose basic sense, according to ar-Rāġib, is separating from something; أَنْقَذَ stresses pulling someone out of a predicament.

tellApart.bs: Izbaviti, odvojiti od opasnosti – ar-Rāġib ih navodi zajedno, a Kur'an oba oblika koristi za iste događaje → نَجَّى, أَنْجَى; osloboditi iz škripca, iz teškog položaja → أَنْقَذَ.
tellApart.en: Delivering, separating from danger — ar-Rāġib lists them together, and the Quran uses both forms of the same events → نَجَّى, أَنْجَى; freeing from a predicament → أَنْقَذَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نجو, نقذ
notes: ar-Rāġib (نجو): the root of naǧāʾ is separating from a thing; naǧā fulān min fulān, wa-anǧaytuhu wa-naǧǧaytuhu — he lists the two forms together, citing 27:53 (wa-anǧaynā llaḏīna āmanū), 29:33, 2:49 (wa-iḏ naǧǧaynākum min āli firʿawn), 10:23, 7:83, 7:72, 37:115, 54:34, 41:18 and others, with no difference of meaning drawn; naǧwa is high ground set apart (10:92 is read as 'We leave you on a height'). (نقذ): inqāḏ is rescuing from a predicament (taḫlīṣ min warṭa); cites 3:103.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 35 / 23 / 4 places read): the same events take both forms — Pharaoh's folk 2:49 (II) / 7:141, 14:6 (IV); Noah 10:73, 21:76 (II) / 7:64, 26:119 (IV); 6:63 and 10:103 hold both. Every prayer 'deliver me / us' is Form II: 10:86, 26:118, 26:169, 28:21, 66:11; Form IV has no imperative. أَنْقَذَ: 3:103 (Allah), 36:23 (the idols cannot), 36:43 (they will not be saved), 39:19 (rhetorical, to the Prophet — not cited). No II/IV distinction is claimed: ar-Rāġib draws none; later grammarians' views on intensive tafʿīl are not put in his mouth. 10:92 (Pharaoh's body), which ar-Rāġib quotes, is not cited here.

'Same meaning' is our inference phrased as his

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, korijen naǧāʾ izvorno znači odvojiti se od nečega; on navodi ‚anǧaytuhu‘ i ‚naǧǧaytuhu‘ zajedno, ne razlikujući ih. Naše zapažanje: sve molbe u zapovjednom načinu ‚izbavi me / nas‘ u Kur'anu su ovim oblikom (10:86, 26:118, 26:169, 28:21, 66:11); uvjetna obećanja ‚ako nas izbaviš / izbavi‘ (10:22, 6:63) imaju أَنْجَى.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root naǧāʾ originally means separating from something; he lists ‘anǧaytuhu’ and ‘naǧǧaytuhu’ together, without telling them apart. Our observation: every imperative prayer ‘deliver me / us’ in the Quran takes this form (10:86, 26:118, 26:169, 28:21, 66:11); the conditional vows ‘if You / He deliver us’ (10:22, 6:63) use أَنْجَى.

why.bs: „I kad smo vas izbavili od faraonovih ljudi …“ – usporedi 7:141, isti događaj s أَنْجَى; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And (remember) when We did deliver you from Pharaoh's folk” — compare 7:141, the same event with أَنْجَى; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I izbavi nas Svojom milošću od naroda koji ne vjeruje.“ – molba; molbe za izbavljenje u zapovjednom načinu u Kur'anu dolaze ovim oblikom.
why.en: “And, of Thy mercy, save us from the folk that disbelieve.” — a prayer; the imperative prayers for deliverance in the Quran take this form.

nuance.bs: Isti korijen; ar-Rāġib ga navodi uz نَجَّى, ne praveći nikakvu razliku. U Kur'anu se oba oblika kažu za isti događaj: izbavljenje od faraonovih ljudi je نَجَّيْنَاكُمْ u 2:49, a أَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ u 7:141; u 6:63 su oba u jednom ajetu.
nuance.en: The same root; ar-Rāġib lists it beside نَجَّى without drawing any difference. In the Quran both forms are said of the same event: the deliverance from Pharaoh's folk is نَجَّيْنَاكُمْ in 2:49 and أَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ in 7:141; 6:63 has both in one ayah.

why.bs: „I kad smo vas izbavili od faraonovih ljudi …“ – isti događaj kao u 2:49, ovdje s أَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ.
why.en: “And (remember) when We did deliver you from Pharaoh's folk” — the same event as 2:49, here with أَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ.

why.bs: „Reci: ‚Ko vas izbavlja iz tmina kopna i mora?‘ … ‚Ako nas izbavi od ovoga …‘“ – oba oblika u jednom ajetu: يُنَجِّيكُمْ, zatim أَنْجَانَا.
why.en: “Say: Who delivereth you from the darkness of the land and the sea? … If we are delivered from this (fear)” — both forms in one ayah: يُنَجِّيكُمْ, then أَنْجَانَا.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, inqāḏ je izbavljenje iz škripca, iz teškog položaja (warṭa). U Kur'anu samo 4 puta: jednom o Allahovom spasu (3:103), a inače u odrečnim i retoričkim rečenicama – niko ne može spasiti onoga koga Allah hoće kazniti.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, inqāḏ is freeing from a predicament (warṭa). In the Quran only 4 times: once of Allah's rescue (3:103), otherwise in negative and rhetorical sentences — no one can rescue the one Allah wills to punish.

why.bs: „… a bili ste na rubu vatrene jame, pa vas je On iz nje izvukao …“ – izvučeni sa samog ruba, kako Njemu priliči; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… and (how) ye were upon the brink of an abyss of fire, and He did save you from it” — pulled back from the very edge, as befits Him; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Ako hoćemo, potopit ćemo ih, i niko im neće pomoći, niti će oni biti izvučeni“ – iz takvog bezizlaza niko drugi ne izvlači.
why.en: “And if We will, We drown them, and there is no help for them, neither can they be saved” — from such a predicament no one else pulls them out.

shared.bs: Obje riječi kažu da je nešto postalo obavezno. Razlikuju se po slici iz koje dolaze: zapisivanje koje utvrđuje, ili usijecanje, rez koji presuđuje.
shared.en: Both words say that something has become binding. They differ in the image they come from: writing that makes a thing fixed, or cutting into, a notch that decides.

tellApart.bs: Zapisati, pa preneseno: utvrditi, odrediti, propisati – pisanje je kraj onoga što se hoće, pa ga potvrđuje → كَتَبَ; usjeći, pa: odlučno odrediti obavezu → فَرَضَ.
tellApart.en: To write, and so figuratively: to fix, to decree, to prescribe — writing is the end of what is willed, so it confirms it → كَتَبَ; to cut into, and so: to settle an obligation decisively → فَرَضَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries كتب, فرض
notes: ar-Rāġib (كتب): kitāba is at root joining leather to leather by sewing, in usage joining letters in writing; establishing, decreeing, obliging, imposing and resolving (al-iṯbāt wa-t-taqdīr wa-l-īǧāb wa-l-farḍ wa-l-ʿazm) are expressed by writing, because a thing is willed, then said, then written: willing is the beginning and writing the end, so what is willed is expressed by writing when it is to be confirmed; cites 58:21, 9:51, 3:154, 5:45 (kataba = 'We revealed and imposed'), 2:180, 2:183, 4:77, 57:27, 59:3; on 9:51 'lanā' and not 'ʿalaynā': whatever befalls us we count a favour for us, not a misfortune against us; mentions 'kataba rabbukum ʿalā nafsihi r-raḥma' (6:54). (فرض): farḍ is cutting into a hard thing and leaving a mark; farḍ is like īǧāb, but īǧāb is said with regard to a thing's occurring and being fixed, farḍ with regard to the cutting (decisiveness) of the ruling in it; 24:1 'We made acting on it binding'; 28:85; 'farada llāhu ʿalayhi' is an obligation He puts on him, 'farada llāhu lahu' is what He did not forbid him; 2:237 'you named a dowry for them'; 2:197 'whoever fixes upon himself the performance of the pilgrimage' — ascribing it to the person shows he sets its time.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 8 places of فَرَضَ read; كَتَبَ's 49 include the literal 'to write' — 2:79, 2:282 …): the count of كَتَبَ is the verb in all its senses. Left out on purpose: 33:38, 33:50, 66:2 (rulings about the Prophet and his household) and 28:85.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 flag, fixed: a stray count sentence dropped from the كَتَبَ nuance.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, pisanjem se izražava utvrđivanje, određivanje, obavezivanje i odluka: stvar se najprije hoće, pa izgovori, pa zapiše – pisanje je kraj, pa se njime izražava ono što se želi potvrditi.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, writing expresses establishing, decreeing, obliging and resolving: a thing is first willed, then said, then written — writing is the end, so it expresses what is to be confirmed.

why.bs: „O vjernici, propisan vam je post, kao što je bio propisan onima prije vas …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet za kataba kao obavezu.
why.en: “O ye who believe! Fasting is prescribed for you, even as it was prescribed for those before you” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah for kataba as obligation.

why.bs: „Reci: ‚Nas neće pogoditi ništa osim onoga što nam je Allah propisao …‘“ – ar-Rāġib: ‚nama‘ (lanā), a ne ‚protiv nas‘, da bismo sve što nas pogodi smatrali blagodati.
why.en: “Say: Naught befalleth us save that which Allah hath decreed for us.” — ar-Rāġib: ‘for us’ (lanā), not ‘against us’, so that whatever befalls us is counted a favour.

why.bs: „… vaš Gospodar je Sebi propisao milost …“ – kako Njemu priliči; ar-Rāġib spominje ove riječi.
why.en: “… Your Lord hath prescribed for Himself mercy” — as befits Him; ar-Rāġib mentions these words.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, farḍ je izvorno usijecanje u nešto tvrdo. Farḍ je kao obavezivanje (īǧāb), ali īǧāb se kaže gledajući na to da je nešto nastalo i ustaljeno, a farḍ gledajući na odlučnost propisa. ‚Farada ʿalayhi‘ je obaveza koju Allah stavlja; ‚farada lahu‘ ono što mu nije zabranio. I ljudi ‚određuju‘ sebi: hadž (2:197), vjenčani dar (2:237).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, farḍ is at root cutting into a hard thing. Farḍ is like obliging (īǧāb), but īǧāb is said with regard to a thing's occurring and being fixed, farḍ with regard to the decisiveness of the ruling. ‘Farada ʿalayhi’ is an obligation Allah lays on him; ‘farada lahu’ is what He did not forbid him. People too ‘settle’ things on themselves: the pilgrimage (2:197), a bridal gift (2:237).

why.bs: „Sura koju smo objavili i učinili obaveznom …“ – ar-Rāġib: obavezali smo da se po njoj radi; on navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “(Here is) a surah which We have revealed and enjoined” — ar-Rāġib: We made acting on it binding; he cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… pa ko u njima sebi odredi hadž …“ – ar-Rāġib: ko sebi utvrdi obavljanje hadža; čin je pripisan čovjeku, jer on određuje vrijeme.
why.en: “… whoever is minded to perform the pilgrimage therein” — ar-Rāġib: whoever fixes upon himself the performance of the pilgrimage; the act is ascribed to the person, for he sets its time.

why.bs: „… a već ste im odredili vjenčani dar …“ – ar-Rāġib: imenovali ste im mehr i time ga sebi obavezali.
why.en: “… and ye have appointed unto them a portion” — ar-Rāġib: you named a dowry for them and so bound yourselves to it.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o neposlušnosti koja ide predaleko. Razlikuju se po slici: prelijevanje preko granice, ili uzmicanje od poslušnosti, odbijanje.
shared.en: Both words speak of disobedience that goes too far. They differ in the image: overflowing a bound, or shying away from obedience, refusing it.

tellApart.bs: Preći mjeru u neposlušnosti – i voda koja nadođe preko granice → طَغَى; odbiti poslušnost, uzmaknuti od nje, najčešće ‚od naredbe svoga Gospodara‘ → عَتَا.
tellApart.en: Going beyond the bound in disobedience — also water that rises past its bound → طَغَى; refusing obedience, shying away from it, mostly ‘from the command of their Lord’ → عَتَا.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries طغى, عتا
notes: ar-Rāġib (طغى): ṭuġyān is exceeding the bound in disobedience (taǧāwuz al-ḥadd fī l-ʿiṣyān); cites innahu ṭaġā (20:24 / 20:43 / 79:17), 96:6, 20:45, 20:81, 18:80 and others; borrowed for water passing its bound in 69:11, and aṭ-ṭāġiya (69:5) points to the flood; ṭāġūt is every transgressor and everything worshipped besides Allah. (عتا): ʿutuww is shying away from obedience (an-nubūw ʿan aṭ-ṭāʿa); cites 25:21, 51:44 (fa-ʿataw ʿan amri rabbihim), 65:8, 67:21; ʿitiyy of old age (19:8) is a state past mending.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 12 / 5 places read): طَغَى is said of Pharaoh (20:24, 20:43, 79:17), of man (96:6), of the waters (69:11), of those 'who transgressed in the lands' (89:11), and forbidden in the balance (55:8) and in food (20:81). عَتَا is said of peoples in all 5 places, with ʿan in 4 (7:77, 7:166, 51:44, 65:8; 25:21 has the absolute ʿutuwwan). Left out on purpose: 11:112 (addressed to the Prophet and those with him), 53:17 (the Prophet's sight; read variously), 18:80 (the boy al-Ḫiḍr killed; batch 8 left 18:74 / 18:80 out). 7:166 not cited: Pickthall renders it 'took pride'.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: peoples such as Thamud (91:11) added to the subjects of طَغَى; bs gloss of عَتَا made natural.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
