meaning.en: to transgress, to exceed the bounds

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ṭuġyān je prekoračenje granice u neposlušnosti; preneseno se kaže i za vodu koja pređe svoju granicu (69:11). U Kur'anu se kaže za faraona, za čovjeka uopće, za narode poput Semuda (91:11) i za vodu potopa, a zabranjuje se i prekoračenje u vagi (55:8) i u hrani (20:81).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ṭuġyān is exceeding the bound in disobedience; figuratively it is also said of water that passes its bound (69:11). In the Quran it is said of Pharaoh, of man in general, of peoples such as Thamud (91:11) and of the waters of the flood, and transgressing is forbidden in the balance (55:8) and in food (20:81).

why.bs: „Idi faraonu, on je zaista prešao granicu.“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ove riječi.
why.en: “Go thou unto Pharaoh! Lo! he hath transgressed (the bounds).” — ar-Rāġib cites these words.

why.bs: „Kad je voda prešla granicu, Mi smo vas ponijeli u lađi koja plovi“ – voda koja pređe svoju mjeru; ar-Rāġib kaže da je riječ ovdje prenesena.
why.en: “Lo! when the waters rose, We carried you upon the ship” — water passing its measure; ar-Rāġib says the word is borrowed here.

why.bs: „Nikako! Čovjek zaista prelazi granicu“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Nay, but verily man is rebellious” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

meaning.en: to defy, to turn away from obedience

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ʿutuww je uzmicanje od poslušnosti. U Kur'anu (svih 5 mjesta) kaže se o narodima, a u četiri od pet slijedi ‚od‘ (ʿan): od naredbe svoga Gospodara, od onoga što im je zabranjeno.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ʿutuww is shying away from obedience. In the Quran (all 5 places) it is said of peoples, and in four of the five ‘from’ (ʿan) follows: from the command of their Lord, from what they were forbidden.

why.bs: „Pa su se oglušili o naredbu svoga Gospodara, i zahvatio ih je grom dok su gledali.“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “But they rebelled against their Lord's decree, and so the thunderbolt overtook them even while they gazed” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Koliko je naselja koja su se oglušila o naredbu svoga Gospodara i Njegovih poslanika …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And how many a community revolted against the ordinance of its Lord and His messengers” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi su od istog korijena i znače najaviti nekome šta ga čeka. Razlikuju se po tome šta se najavljuje.
shared.en: Both words come from one root and mean announcing to someone what awaits him. They differ in what is announced.

tellApart.bs: Najava i dobra i zla → وَعْد; najava samo zla, prijetnja → وَعِيد.
tellApart.en: Announcing good or evil → وَعْد; announcing evil only, a threat → وَعِيد.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries وعد
notes: ar-Rāġib (وعد): waʿd is in good and in evil; waʿīd is in evil only (awʿadtuhu); waʿd of good: 14:22, 28:61, 48:20, 24:55; of evil: 22:47 (they hasten the punishment, 'and Allah will not fail His promise' — that is waʿīd), 22:72, 11:81, 7:70, 10:46 / 13:40 / 40:77, 14:47, 2:268; 'alā inna waʿda llāhi ḥaqq' (10:55) contains both: the Rising and the requital of servants, good for good and evil for evil; of īʿād: 7:86, 14:14, 50:45, 50:28.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 46 / 6 places read): وَعِيد is always Allah's threat — three times 'My threat' (14:14, 50:14, 50:45), and 20:113, 50:20 (the Day of the threat), 50:28. وَعْد is mostly Allah's promise; 10:48 and its parallels are the deniers' 'when is this promise?', and 19:54 praises Ismāʿīl as 'true to the promise'. The verb وَعَدَ (70×) is not a member here.

His 'wa-immā nuriyannaka baʿḍa llaḏī naʿiduhum' matches 10:46 letter for letter; 13:40 is written wa-in mā and 40:77 has fa-immā. Minor

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, waʿd se kaže i za dobro i za zlo. Najčešće je obećanje dobra, ali i kazna koju nevjernici požuruju Allahov je waʿd (22:47); a ‚Allahovo obećanje je istina‘ obuhvata oboje: proživljenje i uzvrat – dobrom za dobro, zlom za zlo.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, waʿd is said of good and of evil. Mostly it is a promise of good, but the punishment the deniers hasten is also Allah's waʿd (22:47); and ‘Allah's promise is true’ holds both: the Rising and the requital — good for good, evil for evil.

why.bs: „Zar je onaj kome smo dali lijepo obećanje, pa će ga i dočekati …“ – obećanje dobra; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Is he whom We have promised a fair promise which he will find (true)” — a promise of good; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I traže od tebe da kazna požuri, a Allah neće iznevjeriti Svoje obećanje …“ – ‚obećanje‘ je ovdje kazna: ar-Rāġibov primjer za waʿd u zlu.
why.en: “And they will bid thee hasten on the Doom, and Allah faileth not His promise” — the ‘promise’ here is the punishment: ar-Rāġib's example of waʿd for evil.

why.bs: „… Allahovo obećanje je zaista istina …“ – ar-Rāġib: proživljenje i uzvrat, i za dobro i za zlo.
why.en: “Lo! verily Allah's promise is true.” — ar-Rāġib: the Rising and the requital, both good and evil.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, waʿīd je samo za zlo. U Kur'anu dolazi 6 puta i uvijek je Allahova prijetnja; tri puta kao ‚Moja prijetnja‘.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, waʿīd is for evil only. In the Quran it comes 6 times and is always Allah's threat; three times as ‘My threat’.

why.bs: „… To je za onoga ko se boji stajanja preda Mnom i boji se Moje prijetnje.“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ove riječi.
why.en: “This is for him who feareth My Majesty and feareth My threats.” — ar-Rāġib cites these words.

why.bs: „… svi su utjerali u laž poslanike, pa se obistinila Moja prijetnja.“
why.en: “… every one denied their messengers, therefor My threat took effect.”

why.bs: „Ne prepirite se preda Mnom, a Ja sam vam prijetnju unaprijed poslao.“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Contend not in My presence, when I had already proffered unto you the warning [al-waʿīd]” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o odnosu stvorenja prema Allahovoj uzvišenosti i čistoti – kako Njemu priliči. U Kur'anu stoje zajedno u riječima meleka (2:30).
shared.en: Both words speak of the creatures' response to Allah's exaltedness and purity — as befits Him. In the Quran they stand together in the angels' words (2:30).

tellApart.bs: Uzvisiti Allaha iznad svega što Mu ne priliči – riječju, djelom i namjerom, a slavi Ga sve stvoreno → سَبَّحَ; božansko čišćenje – ‚nuqaddisu laka‘ ar-Rāġib tumači kao čišćenje stvari u pokornosti Njemu → قَدَّسَ.
tellApart.en: Exalting Allah above all that does not befit Him — by word, deed and intention, and all creation glorifies Him → سَبَّحَ; divine purification — ar-Rāġib reads ‘nuqaddisu laka’ as purifying things in obedience to Him → قَدَّسَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries سبح, قدس
notes: ar-Rāġib (سبح): sabḥ is swift passage in water or air, borrowed for the stars' course (36:40), horses (79:3) and busy work (73:7); tasbīḥ is declaring Allah far above (tanzīh), at root swift passage in His worship; it was made general for acts of worship, in word, deed or intention (37:143 'some said: of those who prayed; better to take it as all three'); cites 2:30, 3:41, 50:40, 68:28; on 17:44 all things glorify Him in reality, in a way we do not understand ('wa-lākin lā tafqahūna tasbīḥahum'), some by subjection, some by choice; subḥān is at root a verbal noun; as-subbūḥ al-quddūs are names of Allah. (قدس): taqdīs is the divine purification mentioned in 'wa-yuṭahhirakum taṭhīran', not the removal of sensible impurity; 2:30 nuqaddisu laka = 'we purify things in obedience to You' (nuṭahhiru l-ašyāʾa rtisāman laka), and 'it has been said' (qīla): we describe You with holiness; rūḥ al-qudus is Gabriel, who brings down from Allah what purifies our souls (16:102); the holy house and the holy land (5:21) are purified of širk.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 40 / 1 places read): سَبَّحَ (Form II) has as subject the angels, the prophets, the believers, the thunder (13:13), the mountains and birds with David (21:79, 38:18), and 'all that is in the heavens and the earth' (57:1, 59:1, 61:1, 62:1, 64:1). قَدَّسَ (Form II) is only 2:30; the root's other words (al-Quddūs, rūḥ al-qudus, al-muqaddasa) are not members. His proof text 'wa-yuṭahhirakum taṭhīran' (33:33) is not cited: its context is debated among mufassirun. The many imperatives 'glorify your Lord' addressed to the Prophet are not cited.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 4 flags, fixed: his 'some by compulsion, some by choice' restored; 'divine purification' as he words it; the verb قَدَّسَ is only in 2:30, the participle muqaddas in 5:21.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries سبح, قدس (2026-11-06): 26 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): His quote is 'wa-kullun fī falakin yasbaḥūn' with wa-: that is 36:40; 21:33 reads 'kullun fī falakin yasbaḥūn' without wa-. Other numbers checked: 79:3, 73:7, 37:143, 2:30, 3:41 (wa-sabbiḥ bi-l-ʿašiyy; 40:55 has bi-ḥamdi rabbika in between), 50:40, 68:28, 17:44, 16:102, 5:21 all match

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, tasbīḥ je uzvisivanje Allaha iznad svega što Mu ne priliči; izvorno je brzo kretanje u ibadetu, a obuhvata ibadet riječju, djelom i namjerom. On kaže da sve stvari slave Allaha, jedne po podređenosti Njegovoj volji, a druge svojim izborom, i da 17:44 znači pravo slavljenje svega na nebesima i na Zemlji, na način koji mi ne razumijemo.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, tasbīḥ is exalting Allah above all that does not befit Him; at root it is swift passage in worship, and it covers worship in word, deed and intention. He says all things glorify Allah, some by compulsion and some by choice, and that 17:44 means a real glorifying of all in the heavens and the earth, in a way we do not understand.

why.bs: „… a mi Te slavimo hvaleći Te i svetost Ti iskazujemo“ – riječi meleka, oba glagola zajedno; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet pod obje natuknice.
why.en: “… while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee” — the angels' words, both verbs together; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah under both entries.

why.bs: „… ali vi ne razumijete njihovo slavljenje“ – sve stvoreno slavi Allaha, na način koji ne poimamo; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… but ye understand not their praise” — all things glorify Allah, in a way we do not grasp; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Allaha slavi sve što je na nebesima i na Zemlji …“ – slavljenje svega stvorenog, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifieth Allah” — the glorifying of all creation, as befits Him.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, taqdīs je božansko čišćenje, a ne uklanjanje vidljive nečistoće. ‚Nuqaddisu laka‘ (2:30) on tumači: čistimo stvari u pokornosti Tebi; navodi i drugo tumačenje (‚rečeno je‘): opisujemo Te svetošću. Sam glagol u Kur'anu dolazi samo ovdje (particip muqaddas stoji u ‚svetoj zemlji‘, 5:21).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, taqdīs is divine purification, not the removal of visible impurity. ‘Nuqaddisu laka’ (2:30) he reads: we purify things in obedience to You; he also gives another reading (‘it has been said’): we describe You with holiness. The verb itself occurs in the Quran only here (the participle muqaddas is in ‘the holy land’, 5:21).

why.bs: „… a mi Te slavimo hvaleći Te i svetost Ti iskazujemo“ – jedino mjesto na kojem dolazi sam glagol; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee” — the only place where the verb itself occurs; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi označavaju zelen komad zemlje uz vodu. Razlikuju se po tome šta je u prvom planu: drveće koje zaklanja tlo, zemlja koja drži vodu, ili mjesto gdje se voda zadržava i zelenilo raste.
shared.en: All three words name a green piece of land with water. They differ in what comes first: trees that cover the ground, land that holds water, or a place where water collects and greenery grows.

tellApart.bs: Zemlja pod drvećem koje je zaklanja – vrt, a u Kur'anu najčešće Džennet → جَنَّة; komad zemlje s vodom, nazvan po zjenici oka → حَدَائِق; mjesto gdje se voda zadržava, sa zelenilom, u Kur'anu samo o Džennetu → رَوْضَة.
tellApart.en: Land under trees that cover it — a garden, in the Quran mostly Paradise → جَنَّة; a piece of land with water, named after the pupil of the eye → حَدَائِق; a place where water collects, with greenery, in the Quran only of Paradise → رَوْضَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries جن, حدق, روض
notes: ar-Rāġib (جن): the root is covering a thing from the senses; al-janna is every orchard (bustān) with trees whose trees cover the ground; cites 34:15, 34:16, 18:39; 'it is said' that the covering trees themselves may be called janna; Paradise is called al-janna either by likening it to a garden on earth, though the gap between them is great, or because its blessings are hidden from us (32:17); he reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that jannāt is plural because the gardens are seven. (حدق): ḥadāʾiq ḏāt bahja (27:60) is the plural of ḥadīqa, a piece of land with water, named by likeness to the pupil of the eye (ḥadaqa) in shape and in holding water. (روض): al-rawḍ is a place where water collects (mustanqaʿ al-māʾ) and greenery; 30:15 'with regard to the water'; 30:15 is an expression for the riyāḍ of Paradise, its beauties and delights; 42:22 rawḍāt al-jannāt points to what is prepared for them in the hereafter in its outward sense, and 'it is said' to the knowledge and character He fitted them for.

Quranic usage (our observation; ḥadāʾiq all 3 and rawḍa both places read, جَنَّة read through the concordance): جَنَّة is mostly Paradise, but also earthly gardens (2:265–266, 6:141, 17:91, 18:32–42, 34:15–16, 68:17) and the garden of Adam (2:35, 7:19, not cited: scholars discuss whether it is the Paradise of the hereafter); the count is the lemma's, all senses together. حَدَائِق is plural only: 27:60 and 80:30 of what rain brings out of the earth, 78:32 of the God-fearing in Paradise. رَوْضَة is only of Paradise (30:15, 42:22 rawḍāt). Paradise is described only as the ayat give it.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): all claims OK.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries جن, حدق, روض (2026-11-06): 23 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, korijen جنن znači zakloniti nešto od osjetila, a جَنَّة je svaki vrt s drvećem koje svojim krošnjama zaklanja tlo. Džennet je, kaže on, tako nazvan ili po sličnosti sa zemaljskim vrtom – iako je razlika među njima golema – ili zato što su njegove blagodati od nas skrivene. U Kur'anu je to najčešće Džennet, ali i zemaljski vrtovi (18:39, 34:16).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root جنن means to cover a thing from the senses, and جَنَّة is any garden whose trees cover the ground. Paradise, he says, is so named either by likeness to a garden on earth — though the gap between them is great — or because its blessings are hidden from us. In the Quran it is mostly Paradise, but earthly gardens too (18:39, 34:16).

why.bs: O narodu Sebe: „… a umjesto njihova dva vrta dali smo im dva vrta s gorkim plodom …“ – zemaljski vrtovi; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Of Sheba: “in exchange for their two gardens gave them two gardens bearing bitter fruit” — earthly gardens; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: U priči o dvojici ljudi: „Zašto, kad si ušao u svoj vrt, nisi rekao: ‚Biva ono što Allah hoće‘ …“ – vrt s drvećem i plodovima; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: In the parable of the two men: “If only, when thou enteredst thy garden, thou hadst said: That which Allah willeth” — a garden of trees and fruit; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I pohitajte ka oprostu od svoga Gospodara i ka Džennetu širokom koliko nebesa i Zemlja …“ – Džennet, onako kako ga ajet opisuje.
why.en: “And vie one with another for forgiveness from your Lord, and for a paradise as wide as are the heavens and the earth” — Paradise, as the ayah describes it.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, حَدِيقَة (mn. حَدَائِق) je komad zemlje koji ima vode, nazvan tako jer oblikom i time što drži vodu podsjeća na zjenicu oka (حَدَقَة). U Kur'anu dolazi samo u množini, tri puta: dvaput o onome što kiša izvodi iz zemlje, jednom o bogobojaznima u Džennetu (78:32).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, حَدِيقَة (plural حَدَائِق) is a piece of land that has water, so named because in shape and in holding water it resembles the pupil of the eye (حَدَقَة). In the Quran it comes only in the plural, three times: twice of what rain brings out of the earth, once of the God-fearing in Paradise (78:32).

why.bs: „… i spušta vam s neba vodu, pa njome dajemo da niknu voćnjaci puni ljepote …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “and sendeth down for you water from the sky wherewith We cause to spring forth joyous orchards” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „i voćnjaci gusti“ – među onim što iz zemlje niče kao opskrba ljudima.
why.en: “And garden-closes of thick foliage” — among what grows from the earth as provision for people.

why.bs: „voćnjaci i vinogradi“ – ono što bogobojazne čeka u Džennetu.
why.en: “Gardens [ḥadāʾiq] enclosed and vineyards” — what awaits the God-fearing in Paradise.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, رَوْض je mjesto gdje se voda zadržava, i zelenilo. Za 30:15 kaže da je to izraz za ljepote i užitke Dženneta. U Kur'anu dolazi samo dvaput, oba puta o Džennetu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, رَوْض is a place where water collects, and greenery. Of 30:15 he says it is an expression for the beauties and delights of Paradise. In the Quran it comes only twice, both times of Paradise.

why.bs: „A oni koji su vjerovali i dobra djela činili bit će na livadi obradovani“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Those who believed and did good works are made glad in a rawḍa, a meadow (Pickthall: ‘a Garden’) — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… a oni koji su vjerovali i dobra djela činili bit će u livadama džennetskih vrtova …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “while those who believe and do good works (will be) in flowering meadows of the Gardens” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o onome što čovjek oblači. Razlikuju se po širini: sve što pokriva i štiti, komadi odjeće koji se nose, ili jedna vrsta odjeće – košulja.
shared.en: All three words speak of what a person wears. They differ in breadth: whatever covers and protects, the pieces of clothing that are worn, or one kind of garment — the shirt.

tellApart.bs: Sve što se oblači i sve što pokriva i štiti, pa i preneseno – noć, bogobojaznost, glad i strah → لِبَاس; komadi odjeće koji se oblače, odlažu i njima se pokriva → ثِيَاب; košulja bilo koje vrste, koja štiti od vrućine ili u boju → سَرَابِيل.
tellApart.en: Whatever is worn and whatever covers and protects, figuratively too — night, God-fearing, hunger and fear → لِبَاس; pieces of clothing that are put on, laid aside and wrapped round → ثِيَاب; a shirt of any kind, guarding against heat or in battle → سَرَابِيل.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries لبس, ثوب, سربل
notes: ar-Rāġib (لبس): labisa ṯ-ṯawb is to be covered by it; libās, labūs and libs are what is worn; cites 18:31 (wa-yalbasūna ṯiyāban ḫuḍran) and 7:26; libās was made a name for whatever covers a person from what is shameful, so a spouse is libās for the other (2:187), as a poet called his wife his izār; taqwā is made libās by way of likeness (7:26); labūs in 21:80 is the coat of mail; in 16:112 hunger and fear are made libās by embodiment and likeness; the root is covering a thing, also in meanings (labs, 6:9, 2:42, 6:82). (ثوب): the root is a thing's return to its first state or to the state intended by thought; the ṯawb is so named because the yarn returns to the state planned for it; plural aṯwāb and ṯiyāb; 74:4 taken as purifying the garment, and 'it is said' the garments stand for the self. (سربل): sirbāl is the shirt (qamīṣ) of whatever kind; cites 14:50 and 16:81, 'i.e. they protect some of you from the violence of others'.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 8 / 8 / 2 places read): لِبَاس is often figurative — spouses (2:187), taqwā (7:26), hunger and fear (16:112), the night (25:47, 78:10) — and concrete in 7:26, 7:27 and the silk of Paradise (22:23, 35:33). ثِيَاب is concrete garments: put on (18:31, 76:21), laid aside (24:58, 24:60), wrapped round (11:5, 71:7), garments of fire (22:19); 74:4 is not cited (addressed to the Prophet, and read literally or figuratively — ar-Rāġib reports both). سَرَابِيل: 16:81 (twice) and 14:50. 2:187 is described, not cited.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 4 flags, fixed: سِرْبَال 'of any kind' (16:81 armour); 74:4 with his two readings; Bosnian quotes of 7:26 and 24:60 re-translated from the Arabic.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries لبس, ثوب, سربل (2026-11-06): 26 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/2/nuance (reworded): He says 'of whatever kind/sort' (من أي جنس كان), not 'cloth' — and his own examples (armour in 16:81, pitch in 14:50) are not cloth

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, لِبَاس je ono što se oblači, a korijen znači pokriti. On kaže da je لِبَاس postalo ime za sve što čovjeka pokriva od ružnoga – zato su supružnici jedno drugom ‚odjeća‘ (2:187) – a bogobojaznost se naziva odjećom po sličnosti, kao što se glad i strah slikovito prikazuju kao odjeća (16:112). U Kur'anu je i noć ‚odjeća‘ (78:10).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, لِبَاس is what is worn, and the root means to cover. He says لِبَاس became a name for whatever covers a person from what is shameful — so spouses are ‘clothing’ for each other (2:187) — and God-fearing is called clothing by likeness, as hunger and fear are pictured as clothing (16:112). In the Quran the night too is ‘clothing’ (78:10).

why.bs: „O sinovi Ademovi, poslali smo vam odjeću koja skriva vašu golotinju, i ukras; a odjeća bogobojaznosti – ona je najbolja“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “O Children of Adam! We have revealed unto you raiment to conceal your shame, and splendid vesture, but the raiment of restraint from evil, that is best” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… pa joj je Allah dao da okusi odjeću gladi i straha …“ – glad i strah koji obuhvate grad kao odjeća; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “so Allah made it experience the garb of dearth and fear” — hunger and fear wrapping the town like clothing; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I noć smo učinili odjećom“ – noć koja pokriva kao odjeća.
why.en: “And have appointed the night as a cloak” — the night that covers like clothing.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, korijen ثوب znači povratak stvari u prvobitno stanje ili u stanje koje joj je namijenjeno, a ثَوْب je tako nazvan jer se pređa vraća u stanje koje joj je određeno; množine su أَثْوَاب i ثِيَاب. U Kur'anu su to komadi odjeće: oblače se (18:31), odlažu (24:60) i njima se umotava (71:7); za 74:4, ‚i svoju odjeću očisti‘, ar-Rāġib navodi dva tumačenja: da se misli na samu odjeću, ili da je ‚odjeća‘ slika za samu osobu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root ثوب means a thing's return to its first state or to the state meant for it, and ثَوْب is so named because the yarn returns to the state planned for it; the plurals are أَثْوَاب and ثِيَاب. In the Quran they are pieces of clothing: put on (18:31), laid aside (24:60) and wrapped round oneself (71:7); for 74:4, ‘and purify your garments’, ar-Rāġib gives two readings: the clothes themselves, or ‘garments’ as a figure for the self.

why.bs: „… i oblačit će zelene haljine od tanke svile i brokata …“ – haljine stanovnika Dženneta; ar-Rāġib navodi ove riječi.
why.en: “and will wear green robes of finest silk and gold embroidery” — the garments of the people of Paradise; ar-Rāġib cites these words.

why.bs: Nuh: „… stavljali su prste u uši i umotavali se u svoje haljine …“ – haljine kojima se pokriva da se ne čuje i ne vidi.
why.en: Noah: “they thrust their fingers in their ears and cover themselves with their garments” — garments drawn over oneself so as not to hear or see.

why.bs: „Starim ženama koje se više ne nadaju udaji nema krivnje ako odlože svoje haljine [gornju odjeću], a ne pokazuju ukras …“ – haljine koje se skidaju i odlažu.
why.en: “it is no sin for them if they discard their (outer) clothing [ṯiyāb] in such a way as not to show adornment” — garments that are taken off and laid aside.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, سِرْبَال je košulja (قَمِيص), bilo koje vrste. U Kur'anu dolazi samo u množini, na dva mjesta: košulje koje štite od vrućine i one koje štite u boju (16:81), i košulje od katrana grješnika (14:50).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, سِرْبَال is a shirt (قَمِيص) of whatever kind. In the Quran it comes only in the plural, in two places: shirts that guard against heat and those that guard in battle (16:81), and the shirts of pitch of the guilty (14:50).

why.bs: „… i dao vam košulje koje vas čuvaju od vrućine i košulje koje vas čuvaju u vašem boju …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet: jedne od drugih, kaže on, štite u boju.
why.en: “and hath given you coats to ward off the heat from you, and coats (of armour) to save you from your own foolhardiness” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah: they guard some of you, he says, from the violence of others.

why.bs: „Košulje su im od katrana, a lica im prekriva Vatra“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Their raiment [sarābīl] of pitch, and the Fire covering their faces” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače tvrdu tvar od koje su tlo i brda. Razlikuju se po stepenu: kamen kao takav, ili posebno tvrd kamen – stijena.
shared.en: Both words mean the hard matter of the ground and the hills. They differ in degree: stone as such, or especially hard stone — rock.

tellApart.bs: Kamen, opća riječ – kamenje koje pada kao kazna, kojim se Vatra loži, s kojim se porede tvrda srca → حَجَر (mn. حِجَارَة); posebno tvrd kamen, stijena koja se kleše → صَخْرَة.
tellApart.en: Stone, the general word — stones that fall as punishment, that fuel the Fire, to which hard hearts are likened → حَجَر (plural حِجَارَة); especially hard stone, rock that is hewn → صَخْرَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حجر, صخر
notes: ar-Rāġib (حجر): al-ḥajar is the well-known hard substance (al-jawhar aṣ-ṣulb); plural aḥjār and ḥijāra; on 2:24 'it is said' they are sulphur stones, and 'it is said' the stones themselves, which points to how great that Fire is, kindled with people and stones unlike the fire of this world, which cannot be kindled with stones; 'it is said' the stones are those as hard as stones against accepting the truth (2:74); the rest of the entry is ḥijr (enclosure, intellect, forbidden). (صخر): aṣ-ṣaḵr is hard stone (al-ḥajar aṣ-ṣulb); cites 31:16 and 89:9.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 9 + 2 / 2 + 1 places read): the member حَجَر sums حِجَارَة (plural, 10) and حَجَر (2: 2:60, 7:160, Moses' staff); حِجَارَة is stones of punishment (8:32, 11:82, 15:74, 51:33, 105:4), the fuel of the Fire (2:24, 66:6), hearts likened to stones (2:74) and 17:50. صَخْرَة sums صَخْرَة (18:63, 31:16) and صَخْر (89:9). Pickthall renders ḥajar 'rock' in 2:60 and 2:74; those ayat are not quoted here so that each member keeps its own English word.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, حَجَر je poznata tvrda tvar; množina je أَحْجَار i حِجَارَة. U Kur'anu je to najčešće množina حِجَارَة: kamenje koje pada na kažnjene narode, kamenje kojim se loži Vatra, i kamenje s kojim se porede tvrda srca (2:74).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, حَجَر is the well-known hard substance; its plurals are أَحْجَار and حِجَارَة. In the Quran it is mostly the plural حِجَارَة: stones that fall on peoples punished, stones that fuel the Fire, and stones to which hard hearts are likened (2:74).

why.bs: „… pa se čuvajte Vatre čije su gorivo ljudi i kamenje …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi tri mišljenja: sumporno kamenje; pravo kamenje, čime se ukazuje na veličinu te Vatre, jer se ovosvjetska vatra kamenjem ne loži; ili ljudi tvrdi poput kamena u odbijanju istine.
why.en: “then guard yourselves against the Fire prepared for disbelievers, whose fuel is of men and stones” — ar-Rāġib reports three views: sulphur stones; the stones themselves, which points to how great that Fire is, for the fire of this world is not kindled with stones; or people as hard as stones in refusing the truth.

why.bs: Meleki Ibrahimu o Lutovu narodu: „da na njih pošaljemo kamenje od gline“ – kamenje kao kazna.
why.en: The angels to Abraham about Lot's people: “That we may send upon them stones of clay” — stones as punishment.

why.bs: „Reci: ‚Budite kamenje ili željezo‘“ – kamen kao slika tvrde, beživotne tvari.
why.en: “Say: Be ye stones or iron” — stone as the image of hard, lifeless matter.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, صَخْر je tvrd kamen. U Kur'anu dolazi tri puta: stijena u kojoj ni zrno gorušice nije skriveno od Allaha (31:16), stijene koje je Semud klesao u dolini (89:9) i stijena kod koje su se Musa i njegov mladić sklonili (18:63).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, صَخْر is hard stone. In the Quran it comes three times: the rock in which not even a mustard seed is hidden from Allah (31:16), the rocks Thamud hewed in the valley (89:9), and the rock where Moses and his young man took shelter (18:63).

why.bs: Lukman sinu: „… pa makar bilo u stijeni, ili na nebesima, ili u zemlji, Allah će ga iznijeti …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Luqman to his son: “and though it be in a rock, or in the heavens, or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „i sa Semudom, koji su klesali stijene u dolini“ – stijena tvrda za klesanje; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And with (the tribe of) Thamud, who clove the rocks in the valley” — rock hard to hew; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Mladić Musau: „Jesi li vidio kad smo se sklonili kod stijene …“
why.en: The young man to Moses: “Didst thou see, when we took refuge on the rock”

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o stanju u kojem čovjeku ništa ne prijeti. Razlikuju se po tome šta je u središtu: smirena duša bez straha, ili biti pošteđen svake nevolje.
shared.en: Both words speak of a state in which nothing threatens a person. They differ in what is at the centre: a soul at rest, without fear, or being spared every harm.

tellApart.bs: Smirenost duše i nestanak straha – suprotno od straha → أَمْن; biti slobodan od nevolja, vanjskih i unutarnjih, i pozdrav kojim se to želi → سَلَام.
tellApart.en: The soul at rest and fear gone — the opposite of fear → أَمْن; being free of harms, outward and inward, and the greeting that wishes it → سَلَام.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries أمن, سلم
notes: ar-Rāġib (أمن): the root of amn is the soul's tranquillity (ṭumaʾnīnat an-nafs) and the removal of fear; amn, amāna and amān are at root verbal nouns; cites 2:125 (maṯābatan li-n-nās wa-amnan) and 29:67; amanatan nuʿāsan (3:154) 'i.e. amnan', and 'it is said' a plural; maʾmanahu (9:6) is the place of his safety. (سلم): as-salm and as-salāma are being free (at-taʿarrī) of outward and inward harms (āfāt); 26:89 inward, 2:71 outward; 15:46 udḫulūhā bi-salāmin āminīn 'i.e. salāma', and 11:48; true salāma is only in Paradise, with lasting without passing away, wealth without want, honour without abasement, health without sickness (6:127, 10:25 dār as-salām 'i.e. as-salāma'); 'it is said' as-Salām is one of Allah's names (59:23), described so as no fault or harm touches Him; salām from people is by word and from Allah by act, the giving of that salāma of Paradise (36:58, 13:24, 37:130); 25:63 qālū salāman 'we seek safety from you' or 'right speech'; the greeting of 51:25 (the wording he quotes; 11:69 is parallel).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 5 + 2 / 39 places read): أَمْن stands against fear in 4:83 and 24:55; the member sums أَمْن and أَمَنَة (3:154, 8:11; ar-Rāġib explains 3:154 as amn). سَلَام is greeting (6:54, 10:10, 13:24, 19:47, 25:63, 28:55, 51:25), Allah's salām on prophets (37:79, 37:109, 37:120, 37:130, 37:181), safety (11:48, 21:69), dār as-salām (6:127, 10:25) and the name as-Salām (59:23, not cited). The adjective آمِن (15:46 āminīn) is another lemma and is not counted.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: 6:82 — the Prophet explained this ẓulm as shirk (Bukhari, Muslim); as-Salām is stated as Allah's Name (59:23), his qīla is only about dār as-salām (6:127).

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries أمن, سلم (2026-11-06): 20 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): His quotation إذ دخلوا عليه فقالوا سلاما قال سلام is 51:25 only; 11:69 lacks إذ دخلوا عليه; notes/1 (reworded): He quotes only 3:154 (أمنة نعاسا); 8:11 is not cited, and he also reports (qīla) that amana there is a plural; members/0/nuance (reworded): He explains only 3:154 (and reports a plural reading); 8:11 is not his, and 'that Allah sends down' fits 3:154 (أنزل) but not 8:11 (يغشيكم), and is our gloss; members/1/nuance (reworded): His definition is headed السلم والسلامة, but he gives سلاما as a verbal noun of سلم alongside سلامة and glosses بسلام / دار السلام as السلامة, so applying it to سلام is fair. 'as befits Him' is not in the text

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnova أَمْن je smirenost duše i nestanak straha. U Kur'anu stoji nasuprot strahu (4:83): sigurnost je kad straha nema. أَمَنَة u 3:154 on tumači kao أَمْن; tu i u 8:11 to je sigurnost od Allaha.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root of أَمْن is the soul at rest and fear removed. In the Quran it stands against fear (4:83): security is the absence of fear. أَمَنَة in 3:154 he explains as أَمْن; there and in 8:11 it is security from Allah.

why.bs: „Oni koji vjeruju i svoje vjerovanje ne miješaju s nepravdom – njima pripada sigurnost, i oni su upućeni“ – sigurnost kao nagrada vjerovanja; Poslanik je ovu ‚nepravdu‘ objasnio kao širk, pripisivanje ortaka Allahu (Buhari, Muslim).
why.en: “Those who believe and obscure not their belief by wrongdoing, theirs is safety; and they are rightly guided” — security as the reward of faith; the Prophet explained this ‘wrongdoing’ as shirk, associating others with Allah (Bukhari, Muslim).

why.bs: „A kad im dođe kakva vijest o sigurnosti ili o strahu, oni je razglase …“ – sigurnost kao suprotnost strahu.
why.en: “And if any tidings, whether of safety or fear, come unto them, they noise it abroad” — security set against fear.

why.bs: „I kad smo Kuću učinili mjestom kojem se ljudi vraćaju i sigurnim mjestom …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And when We made the House (at Makka) a resort for mankind and sanctuary” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, سَلَام i سَلَامَة znače biti slobodan od nevolja, vanjskih i unutarnjih; pravi, potpuni mir je, kaže on, tek u Džennetu, gdje je trajanje bez prolaznosti. Selam je i pozdrav: od ljudi riječima, a od Allaha, kaže on, djelom – darivanjem tog džennetskog mira. As-Salām je i jedno od Allahovih lijepih imena (59:23); ar-Rāġib navodi mišljenje da se i ‚Kuća mira‘ (6:127) po njemu tako zove.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, سَلَام and سَلَامَة mean being free of harms, outward and inward; true, complete peace, he says, is only in Paradise, where there is lasting without passing away. Salām is also the greeting: from people by word, and from Allah, he says, by act — the giving of that peace of Paradise. As-Salām is also one of Allah's Beautiful Names (59:23); ar-Rāġib notes the view that ‘the abode of peace’ (6:127) is named after it.

why.bs: „Uđite u nj u miru, sigurni!“ – ar-Rāġib ovdje سَلَام tumači kao pošteđenost od zla; uz njega stoji آمِنِين, ‚sigurni‘, iz korijena riječi أَمْن.
why.en: “Enter them in peace, secure” — ar-Rāġib reads سَلَام here as soundness, being spared harm; beside it stands آمِنِين, ‘secure’, from the root of أَمْن.

why.bs: „Rekli smo: ‚O vatro, budi hladnoća i mir Ibrahimu!‘“ – mir kao pošteđenost od štete.
why.en: “We said: O fire, be coolness and peace for Abraham” — peace as being spared harm.

why.bs: „Njima pripada Kuća mira kod njihova Gospodara …“ – ar-Rāġib je tumači kao Kuću pošteđenosti od svakog zla; neki ovdje as-Salām čitaju kao Allahovo ime.
why.en: “For them is the abode of peace with their Lord” — ar-Rāġib explains it as the abode of soundness from every harm; some read as-Salām here as Allah's name.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi označavaju predmete koje su ljudi oblikovali ili postavili, a neke od njih obožavali mimo Allaha. Razlikuju se po građi i po tome da li riječ sama govori o obožavanju ili samo o obliku.
shared.en: All three words name objects that people shaped or set up, some of which they worshipped besides Allah. They differ in material and in whether the word itself speaks of worship or only of shape.

tellApart.bs: Izrađen lik – od srebra, bakra ili drveta – koji se obožava → أَصْنَام; kamenje koje se obožavalo → أَوْثَان; ono što je oblikovano po uzoru na nešto, riječ koja sama ne govori o obožavanju → تَمَاثِيل.
tellApart.en: A made figure — of silver, copper or wood — that is worshipped → أَصْنَام; stones that were worshipped → أَوْثَان; what is shaped after the likeness of something, a word that does not itself speak of worship → تَمَاثِيل.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries صنم, وثن, مثل
notes: ar-Rāġib (صنم): aṣ-ṣanam is a body (juṯṯa) made of silver, copper or wood which they worshipped, seeking nearness to Allah by it; plural aṣnām; cites 6:74 and 21:57; 'some sages' say whatever is worshipped besides Allah, indeed whatever distracts from Allah, is called ṣanam, and on that he reads Abraham's prayer in 14:35 (not cited here). (وثن): al-waṯan, plural awṯān, is stones that were worshipped; cites 29:25 (innamā ttaḫaḏtum min dūni llāhi awṯānan). (مثل): the root of muṯūl is standing upright; al-mumaṯṯal is what is shaped after the likeness of another; at-timṯāl is the shaped thing (aš-šayʾ al-muṣawwar).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 5 / 3 / 2 places read): أَصْنَام is Abraham's people (6:74, 14:35, 21:57, 26:71) and the people the Children of Israel passed (7:138); أَوْثَان is Abraham's words (29:17, 29:25) and 22:30. تَمَاثِيل: 21:52 (Abraham's people devoted to them) and 34:13 (made by the jinn for Solomon, not named as objects of worship). What Solomon's tamāṯīl were, and the rulings on images, are discussed by the mufassirun and the jurists; we say only what the ayah says. 14:35 is not cited (ar-Rāġib's reading of Abraham's prayer is a sages' view).

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: 26:71 bs 'Rekli su'; 29:25 quoted only up to 'instead of Allah' (Pickthall follows another reading of مَوَدَّة).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries صنم, وثن, مثل (2026-11-06): 15 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/2/nuance (reworded): 'made after the likeness of another' is his definition of الممثل (a neighbouring derivative), not of التمثال; and 'standing upright' is the root sense of المثول specifically. 'The word itself does not speak of worship' is our inference in a separate sentence — fine

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, صَنَم je tijelo izrađeno od srebra, bakra ili drveta koje su obožavali, misleći da se njime približavaju Allahu. On prenosi i riječi nekih mudraca da se ‚kipom‘ može nazvati sve što se obožava mimo Allaha, pa i sve što od Allaha odvraća.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, صَنَم is a body made of silver, copper or wood which they worshipped, thinking it brought them nearer to Allah. He also reports some sages as saying that anything worshipped besides Allah, even anything that turns one away from Allah, may be called an ‘idol’.

why.bs: Ibrahim ocu Azeru: „Zar kipove uzimaš za božanstva? …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Abraham to his father Azar: “Takest thou idols for gods?” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Ibrahim: „Tako mi Allaha, smislit ću nešto protiv vaših kipova …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Abraham: “And, by Allah, I shall circumvent your idols” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Rekli su: ‚Obožavamo kipove i ostajemo im predani‘“ – Ibrahimov narod.
why.en: “They said: We worship idols, and are ever devoted unto them” — Abraham's people.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, وَثَن je kamenje koje se obožavalo. U Kur'anu dolazi tri puta: dvaput u Ibrahimovim riječima njegovu narodu (29:17, 29:25) i jednom u zapovijedi da se kloni prljavštine idola (22:30).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, وَثَن is stones that were worshipped. In the Quran it comes three times: twice in Abraham's words to his people (29:17, 29:25), and once in the command to shun the filth of idols (22:30).

why.bs: Ibrahim: „Vi mimo Allaha obožavate samo idole i izmišljate laž …“
why.en: Abraham: “Ye serve instead of Allah only idols [awṯān], and ye only invent a lie”

why.bs: „Vi ste mimo Allaha uzeli samo idole …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Ye have chosen only idols [awṯān] instead of Allah.” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… pa klonite se prljavštine idola i klonite se lažnog govora“
why.en: “So shun the filth of idols [awṯān], and shun lying speech”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnovno značenje glagolske imenice مُثُول je uspravno stajanje, a تِمْثَال je oblikovana stvar; srodni oblik korijena, kaže on, označava ono što je načinjeno po uzoru na nešto drugo. Riječ sama ne govori o obožavanju: Ibrahimov narod bio je predan likovima (21:52), a džini su Sulejmanu izrađivali likove (34:13) koji se tu ne spominju kao predmet obožavanja.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the verbal noun مُثُول basically means standing upright, and تِمْثَال is a shaped thing; a related form of the root, he says, denotes what is shaped after the likeness of something else. The word itself does not speak of worship: Abraham's people were devoted to images (21:52), while the jinn made images for Solomon (34:13), which are not named there as objects of worship.

why.bs: Ibrahim ocu i svome narodu: „Kakvi su to likovi kojima ste vi predani?“
why.en: Abraham to his father and his folk: “What are these images unto which ye pay devotion?”

why.bs: „Izrađivali su mu što god je htio: mihrabe i likove, zdjele kao bazene i kotlove nepomične …“ – džini Sulejmanu; ovdje likovi nisu predmet obožavanja.
why.en: “They made for him what he willed: synagogues and statues [tamāṯīl], basins like wells and boilers built into the ground” — the jinn for Solomon; here the images are not objects of worship.

shared.bs: Obje riječi označavaju velelepnu građevinu. Razlikuju se po tome šta se ističe: građevina sklopljena dio uz dio, ili zdanje visoko i ukrašeno.
shared.en: Both words name a grand building. They differ in what stands out: a building joined part to part, or an edifice high and adorned.

tellApart.bs: Dvorac, građevina sklopljena dio uz dio, kakve ljudi grade ili ostave u ruševinama → قَصْر; visoka, ukrašena kuća – Sulejmanova staklena dvorana, zdanje koje faraon traži → صَرْح.
tellApart.en: A palace, a building joined part to part, like those people build or leave in ruins → قَصْر; a high, adorned house — Solomon's hall of glass, the edifice Pharaoh asks for → صَرْح.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries قصر, صرح
notes: ar-Rāġib (قصر): qaṣartu kaḏā also means 'I joined part of it to part' (ḍamamtu baʿḍahu ilā baʿḍ), and from it the qaṣr is named, plural quṣūr; cites 22:45, 25:10, 77:32 ('it is said' qaṣr there is tree-stumps). (صرح): aṣ-ṣarḥ is a high, adorned house (bayt ʿālin muzawwaq), named so as being ṣarḥ of admixture, i.e. pure; cites 27:44 twice.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 4 / 3 places read): قَصْر: 7:74 (Thamud build palaces in the plains), 22:45 (the high-built palaces of destroyed towns), 25:10 (what Allah could give, not cited: said to the Prophet), 77:32 (sparks 'like the qaṣr', read in more than one way — not cited). صَرْح: 27:44 (twice, Solomon's hall), 28:38 and 40:36 (Pharaoh's). Pickthall renders qaṣr 'lofty tower' in 22:45, the same words he uses for ṣarḥ, so 22:45 is paraphrased in English.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 3 flags, fixed: قَصْر 'mostly' worldly palaces, 77:32 a simile for the Fire's sparks; Pharaoh's stated aims in 28:38 and 40:36 as the ayat give them.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, glagol قَصَرَ znači i ‚spojiti dio s dijelom‘, i otuda je قَصْر dobio ime; množina je قُصُور. U Kur'anu su to najčešće dvorci ljudi ovoga svijeta: Semudovi u ravnicama (7:74) i visoko sazidani dvorci uništenih gradova (22:45); jednom je to poredba za iskre koje baca Vatra (77:32).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the verb قَصَرَ also means ‘to join part to part’, and from it قَصْر takes its name; the plural is قُصُور. In the Quran they are mostly the palaces of people of this world: Thamud's in the plains (7:74), and the high-built palaces of destroyed towns (22:45); once it is a simile for the sparks thrown up by the Fire (77:32).

why.bs: Semudu: „… na njenim ravnicama gradite dvorce, a u planinama klešete kuće …“
why.en: To Thamud: “Ye choose castles in the plains and hew the mountains into dwellings”

why.bs: „… i koliko je napuštenih bunara i visoko sazidanih dvoraca!“ – ono što ostaje iza uništenih naroda; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: How many destroyed towns, deserted wells and high-built palaces — what is left behind by peoples destroyed; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, صَرْح je visoka, ukrašena kuća, nazvana tako jer je ‚čista‘, bez primjese. U Kur'anu je to Sulejmanova dvorana uglačana od stakla (27:44) i zdanje koje faraon traži od Hamana, nadajući se da će ugledati Musaova boga (28:38) i dosegnuti puteve (40:36).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, صَرْح is a high, adorned house, so named as being ‘pure’, free of admixture. In the Quran it is Solomon's hall made smooth with glass (27:44), and the edifice Pharaoh asks Haman to build, hoping to look up at the god of Moses (28:38) and to reach the ways (40:36).

why.bs: „Rečeno joj je: ‚Uđi u zdanje!‘ …“ i: „To je zdanje uglačano od stakla“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “It was said unto her: Enter the hall” and: “Lo! it is a hall, made smooth, of glass” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Faraon: „… pa mi, Hamane, peci glinu i podigni mi visoko zdanje, ne bih li pogledao Musaova boga …“ – faraonova oholost.
why.en: Pharaoh: “so kindle for me (a fire), O Haman, to bake the mud; and set up for me a lofty tower in order that I may survey the god of Moses” — Pharaoh's arrogance.

why.bs: „O Hamane, sagradi mi visoko zdanje, ne bih li dosegao puteve“
why.en: “O Haman! Build for me a tower that haply I may reach the roads”

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o nedostatku mekoće. Razlikuju se po tome gdje je ta tvrdoća: u srcu koje ne prima opomenu, u grubosti i težini, ili u neugodnoj naravi u ophođenju.
shared.en: All three words speak of a lack of softness. They differ in where that hardness lies: in a heart that does not take a reminder, in coarseness and weight, or in an unpleasant nature in dealing with people.

tellApart.bs: Srce koje otvrdne kao kamen → قَسَا; grubost, suprotnost nježnosti – izvorno o tijelima, pa o postupanju, kazni i zavjetu → غَلِيظ; neugodna, odbojna narav → فَظّ.
tellApart.en: A heart that hardens like stone → قَسَا; harshness, the opposite of delicacy — at root of bodies, then of conduct, punishment and covenant → غَلِيظ; an unpleasant, repellent nature → فَظّ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries قسو, غلظ, فظ
notes: ar-Rāġib (قسو): qaswa is ġilaẓ al-qalb, thickness of the heart; its origin is from 'a hard stone' (ḥajar qāsin); cites 2:74, 39:22, 22:53, 5:13; the reading qasiyya (5:13) 'not pure', from a debased silver coin. (غلظ): ġilẓa is the opposite of riqqa (delicacy); at root used of bodies, borrowed for meanings, like 'big' and 'many'; 9:123 'i.e. roughness (ḫušūna)'; cites 31:24, 11:58 / 41:50 and 9:73 (uġluẓ ʿalayhim). (فظ): al-faẓẓ is one of disagreeable character (al-karīh al-ḫulq), borrowed from faẓẓ, the water of the rumen, disliked to drink and taken only in the direst need; cites 3:159.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 3 / 9 + 1 / 1 places read): the verb قَسَا is always said of hearts (2:74, 6:43, 57:16); the adjective قَاسِيَة (5:13, 22:53, 39:22) is another lemma. The member غَلِيظ sums غَلِيظ (9) and غِلْظَة (9:123): punishment (11:58, 14:17, 31:24, 41:50), covenant (4:21, 4:154, 33:7), the angels of 66:6 (not cited) and the heart in 3:159. فَظّ is only 3:159, a supposition that praises the Prophet's gentleness, not a reproach.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: Bosnian quotes of 9:123 and 3:159 re-translated from the Arabic.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, قَسْوَة je ‚zadebljalost srca‘, a izvorno dolazi od izraza za tvrd kamen. U Kur'anu glagol stoji samo uz srca – sva tri puta – i to srca koja ne primaju opomenu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, قَسْوَة is ‘thickness of the heart’, from the expression for a hard stone. In the Quran the verb is said only of hearts — all three times — hearts that do not take a reminder.

why.bs: „Zatim su vam nakon toga otvrdnula srca, pa su kao kamenje, ili još tvrđa …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Then, even after that, your hearts were hardened and became as rocks, or worse than rocks, for hardness” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Pa zašto se nisu ponizili kad im je došla Naša kazna? Ali, srca su im otvrdnula …“ – srce koje ni nevolja ne omekša.
why.en: “If only, when Our disaster came on them, they had been humble! But their hearts were hardened” — a heart that even hardship does not soften.

why.bs: „… i da ne budu kao oni kojima je ranije data Knjiga, pa im se vrijeme oduljilo i srca im otvrdnula …“ – opomena vjernicima.
why.en: “that they become not as those who received the scripture of old but the term was prolonged for them and so their hearts were hardened” — a warning to the believers.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, غِلْظَة je suprotnost nježnosti (رِقَّة); izvorno se kaže za tijela, a preneseno za značenja, kao ‚veliko‘ i ‚mnogo‘. Zato u Kur'anu ide uz kaznu (teška kazna), uz zavjet (čvrst zavjet) i uz postupanje prema neprijatelju u boju (9:123), gdje je to, kaže on, grubost.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, غِلْظَة is the opposite of delicacy (رِقَّة); at root it is said of bodies, and figuratively of meanings, like ‘big’ and ‘many’. So in the Quran it goes with punishment (a heavy punishment), with a covenant (a firm covenant) and with conduct towards the enemy in battle (9:123), where, he says, it is harshness.

why.bs: „O vjernici, borite se s onima među nevjernicima koji su vam najbliži, i neka u vama nađu grubost …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “O ye who believe! Fight those of the disbelievers who are near to you, and let them find harshness in you” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Dajemo im da malo uživaju, a zatim ih nagonimo u tešku kaznu“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “We give them comfort for a little, and then We drive them to a heavy doom” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… a one su od vas uzele čvrst zavjet“ – bračni zavjet, ‚čvrst‘ u prenesenom značenju.
why.en: “and they have taken a strong pledge from you” — the marriage pledge, ‘firm’ in a borrowed sense.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, فَظّ je čovjek neugodne naravi; riječ je prenesena od imena za vodu iz buraga, koja se nerado pije, samo u najvećoj nuždi. U Kur'anu samo jednom, u pretpostavci koja hvali Poslanikovu blagost: da je bio osoran, ljudi bi se od njega razišli (3:159).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, فَظّ is a person of disagreeable character; the word is borrowed from the name for the water of the rumen, which is drunk unwillingly, only in the direst need. In the Quran only once, in a supposition that praises the Prophet's gentleness: had he been rude, people would have dispersed from him (3:159).

why.bs: „Po milosti Allahovoj postupao si s njima blago; da si bio osoran i tvrda srca, raspršili bi se oko tebe …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet; osornost se ovdje od Poslanika odriče.
why.en: “It was by the mercy of Allah that thou wast lenient with them (O Muhammad), for if thou hadst been stern and fierce of heart they would have dispersed from round about thee” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah; rudeness is here denied of the Prophet.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o oružanom sukobu. Razlikuju se po tome da li se gleda sama borba dviju strana ili rat kao stanje i događaj koji se rasplamsa i završi.
shared.en: Both words speak of armed conflict. They differ in whether one looks at the fighting itself, between two sides, or at war as a state and an event that flares up and ends.

tellApart.bs: Međusobna borba, djelo dviju strana – ono što se propisuje, od čega se neki ustežu ili što izostane → قِتَال; rat kao stanje i događaj – vatra koja se pali i gasi, rat koji ‚odloži svoje terete‘ → حَرْب.
tellApart.en: Fighting one another, the act of two sides — what is prescribed, what some shrink from or what does not come → قِتَال; war as a state and an event — a fire lit and put out, a war that ‘lays down its burdens’ → حَرْب.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries قتل, حرب
notes: ar-Rāġib (قتل): al-muqātala is al-muḥāraba (warring) and seeking to kill (taḥarrī al-qatl); cites 2:193, 59:12, 9:123, 4:74; iqtitāl is like muqātala (49:9). (حرب): al-ḥarb is 'well known' (maʿrūf); al-ḥarab is plunder in war, then any plunder; taḥrīb is stirring up war; the rest of the entry is ḥarba (spear) and miḥrāb.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 10 / 4 places read): قِتَال (the verbal noun of قَاتَلَ) is prescribed (kutiba: 2:216, 2:246, 4:77), shrunk from (2:246, 4:77, 47:20), urged (8:65) and spared (33:25). حَرْب: 2:279 (war from Allah and His Messenger on those who persist in usury), 5:64 (a fire of war that Allah puts out), 8:57, 47:4. Only the phrase 'till the war lays down its burdens' of 47:4 is quoted; its rulings are discussed by the jurists and are not our subject. ar-Rāġib says little about ḥarb; the contrast rests on Quranic usage.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): all claims OK.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: قِتَال je glagolska imenica od قَاتَلَ, ‚boriti se s nekim‘. Prema ar-Rāġibu, مُقَاتَلَة je ratovanje (مُحَارَبَة) i nastojanje da se ubije. U Kur'anu je borba često ono što se propisuje (2:216, 2:246, 4:77), a pred čim se neki ustežu.
nuance.en: قِتَال is the verbal noun of قَاتَلَ, ‘to fight someone’. According to ar-Rāġib, مُقَاتَلَة is warring (مُحَارَبَة) and seeking to kill. In the Quran fighting is often what is prescribed (2:216, 2:246, 4:77), and what some shrink from.

why.bs: „Propisana vam je borba, iako vam je mrska …“ – borba kao propis.
why.en: Fighting (al-qitāl) “is ordained for you, though it is hateful unto you” — fighting as an ordinance.

why.bs: „… ‚Da se možda nećete boriti ako vam borba bude propisana?‘ …“ i: „A kad im je borba propisana, okrenuše se, osim malo njih“ – sinovi Israilovi nakon Musaa.
why.en: “Would ye then refrain from fighting if fighting were prescribed for you?” and: “Yet, when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, all save a few of them” — the Children of Israel after Moses.

why.bs: „… a Allah je vjernike poštedio borbe …“ – borba koja nije morala biti.
why.en: Allah spared the believers the fighting — a fight that did not have to come.

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib kaže samo da je حَرْب ‚poznata stvar‘ i od istog korijena navodi حَرَب, pljačku u ratu. U Kur'anu (četiri puta) حَرْب je rat kao stanje i događaj: vatra koju ljudi pale, a Allah gasi (5:64), rat koji ‚odloži svoje terete‘ (47:4) i rat kojim se prijeti onima koji ustraju u kamati (2:279).
nuance.en: ar-Rāġib says only that حَرْب is ‘well known’, and from the same root gives حَرَب, plunder in war. In the Quran (four times) حَرْب is war as a state and an event: a fire people light and Allah puts out (5:64), a war that ‘lays down its burdens’ (47:4), and the war threatened against those who persist in usury (2:279).

why.bs: „Kad god potpale vatru za rat, Allah je ugasi …“ – rat kao vatra koja se pali i gasi.
why.en: “As often as they light a fire for war, Allah extinguisheth it” — war as a fire lit and put out.

why.bs: „… sve dok rat ne odloži svoje terete“ – rat kao stanje koje traje dok ne završi.
why.en: “till the war lay down its burdens” — war as a state that lasts until it ends.

why.bs: „A ako to ne učinite, onda znajte da vam je navješten rat od Allaha i Njegova Poslanika …“ – opomena onima koji ustraju u kamati.
why.en: “And if ye do not, then be warned of war (against you) from Allah and His messenger” — a warning to those who persist in usury.

shared.bs: Obje riječi kude nemjeru, najčešće s imetkom. Razlikuju se po tome da li se gleda prelaženje granice u bilo kojem djelu ili razbacivanje imetka koji se tako gubi.
shared.en: Both words blame a lack of measure, most often with wealth. They differ in whether one looks at crossing the limit in any act, or at scattering wealth so that it is lost.

tellApart.bs: Prijeći granicu u bilo čemu – u trošenju, jelu, kažnjavanju, grijehu → أَسْرَفَ; razbacati imetak kao sjeme koje se rasipa, pa propada → بَذَّرَ.
tellApart.en: Crossing the limit in anything — spending, eating, retaliation, sin → أَسْرَفَ; scattering wealth like seed strewn about, so that it is wasted → بَذَّرَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries سرف, بذر
notes: ar-Rāġib (سرف): sarf is exceeding the limit (taǧāwuz al-ḥadd) in every act a person does, though in spending it is better known; cites 25:67 and 4:6; it is said sometimes with regard to quantity and sometimes to manner, hence Sufyān's saying that what is spent in other than obedience to Allah is sarf even if little; cites 7:31 (or 6:141, same wording), 40:28, 40:43; the people of Lūṭ are called musrifīn; 39:53 covers isrāf in wealth and in other things; in retaliation (17:33) the excess is killing someone other than the killer, or more than the killer. (بذر): tabḏīr is scattering (tafrīq); its root is casting seed, borrowed for everyone who wastes his wealth, since strewing seed looks like waste to one who does not know its outcome; cites 17:27 and 17:26.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 6 / 1 places read): أَسْرَفَ (Form IV verb) is said of spending (25:67), eating and drinking (7:31, 6:141), retaliation (17:33), and of a life that goes beyond bounds (20:127, 39:53). بَذَّرَ is only 17:26 (لَا تُبَذِّرْ تَبْذِيرًا); 17:27 has the participle مُبَذِّرِين, cited in the nuance but not counted. 39:53 was not cited: an ayah on forgiveness that would need 4:48 beside it.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): all claims OK.

meaning.en: to exceed the bounds, to be prodigal

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, isrāf je prelaženje granice u svakom djelu koje čovjek čini, iako je najpoznatije u trošenju; može se ticati količine, a može i načina. U Kur'anu se tako pretjeruje u trošenju, jelu i piću, i u odmazdi za ubijenog.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, isrāf is exceeding the limit in any act a person does, though it is best known in spending; it may concern the amount, and it may concern the manner. In the Quran one so exceeds in spending, in eating and drinking, and in retaliation for one slain.

why.bs: „I oni koji, kad troše, ne pretjeruju niti škrtare, nego je između toga sredina“ – mjera između dvije krajnosti; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Those who, when they spend, are neither prodigal nor grudging” — the measure between two extremes; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Jedite i pijte, ali ne pretjerujte“ – pretjerivanje i izvan imetka.
why.en: “Eat and drink, but be not prodigal” — exceeding the bounds beyond wealth too.

why.bs: „… neka ne pretjeruje u ubijanju“ – ar-Rāġib kaže: da ne ubije nekog drugog osim ubice, ili više od njega.
why.en: “But let him not commit excess in slaying” — ar-Rāġib says: by killing someone other than the killer, or more than him.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, tabḏīr je raspršivanje; izvorno je to bacanje sjemena, pa je preneseno na svakoga ko upropaštava svoj imetak. Glagol je u Kur'anu samo jednom, a sljedeći ajet rasipnike (مُبَذِّرِين) naziva braćom šejtana (17:27).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, tabḏīr is scattering; at root it is casting seed, and it is borrowed for anyone who wastes his wealth. The verb is in the Quran only once, and the next ayah calls the squanderers (مُبَذِّرِين) brothers of the devils (17:27).

why.bs: „Daj rođaku njegovo pravo, i siromahu, i putniku, i ne rasipaj rasipanjem“ – nakon davanja onima kojima pripada; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Give the kinsman his due, and the needy, and the wayfarer, and squander not (thy wealth) in wantonness” — after giving to those it belongs to; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače ostati negdje neko vrijeme. Razlikuju se po tome da li se gleda trajanje boravka ili ostajanje na mjestu, često uz čekanje.
shared.en: Both words mean remaining somewhere for a time. They differ in whether one looks at the length of the stay, or at staying put, often while waiting.

tellApart.bs: Boraviti na mjestu, ne odvajajući se od njega – u Kur'anu najčešće uz pitanje ili mjeru ‚koliko‘ → لَبِثَ; ostati na mjestu, često čekajući → مَكَثَ.
tellApart.en: To stay at a place, keeping to it — in the Quran mostly with the question or measure ‘how long’ → لَبِثَ; to stay put, often while waiting → مَكَثَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries لبت, مكث
notes: ar-Rāġib (the OpenITI text prints the لبث entry under the headword لبت): labiṯa bi-l-makān is staying at a place keeping to it (aqāma bihi mulāziman lahu); cites 29:14, 20:40 (fa-labiṯta sinīn; 26:18 has wa-labiṯta fīnā), 18:19, 79:46, 46:35 (or 10:45), 34:14. (مكث): al-makṯ is ṯabāt maʿa ntiẓār, staying put while waiting; cites 27:22 (fa-makaṯa ġayra baʿīd, noting another reading), 43:77 (innakum mākiṯūn) and 'qāla li-ahlihi mkuṯū' — that wording, without fa-, is 28:29 (20:10 has fa-qāla).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 25 / 4 places read): لَبِثَ is mostly a span that is asked (18:19, 23:112), estimated ('a day or part of a day', 'only a little', 'ten', 'an evening or its morning') or counted (18:25, 29:14); also 11:69, Ibrāhīm 'delayed not' to bring the calf. مَكَثَ: 20:10 and 28:29 (Mūsā to his family: stay here), 27:22 (he was not long), 13:17 (what benefits people remains in the earth — staying without waiting, a counter-example). The participle مَاكِث (18:3, 43:77) is not counted.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 5 flags, fixed: مَكَثَ is staying put, 'often' while waiting (18:3, 43:77 are lasting stays); 28:29 bs re-translated; 11:69 bs 'nije odugovlačio' (zadržati se is kept for مَكَثَ).

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries لبت, مكث (2026-11-06): 11 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): Wrong verse number: the quoted 'fa-labiṯta sinīn' is 20:40, not 26:18

meaning.en: to tarry, to remain (for a span)

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, boraviti na mjestu, ne odvajajući se od njega. U Kur'anu se uz ovaj glagol najčešće pita ili mjeri koliko je boravak trajao: dan ili dio dana, godine, hiljadu godina bez pedeset.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, staying at a place, keeping to it. In the Quran this verb mostly comes with asking or measuring how long the stay lasted: a day or part of a day, years, a thousand years less fifty.

why.bs: „Koliko ste boravili?“ Rekoše: „Boravili smo dan ili dio dana“ – mladići pećine pitaju o trajanju; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “How long have ye tarried? They said: We have tarried a day or some part of a day” — the youths of the cave ask about the length; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… pa je među njima boravio hiljadu godina bez pedeset“ – Nuhov boravak izmjeren; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And he continued with them for a thousand years save fifty years” — Noah's stay, measured; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… i nije odugovlačio, nego je donio pečeno tele“ – Ibrahim nije oklijevao da ugosti goste.
why.en: “And delayed not to bring a roasted calf” — Abraham did not linger in honouring his guests.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, makṯ je ostajanje na mjestu uz čekanje. Musa kaže porodici da ostane dok on ode do vatre; ipak, u 13:17 ono što koristi ljudima ‚ostaje u zemlji‘, a u 18:3 vjernici u svojoj nagradi ostaju zauvijek, bez ikakvog čekanja.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, makṯ is staying put while waiting. Moses tells his family to stay while he goes to the fire; yet in 13:17 what benefits people ‘remains in the earth’, and in 18:3 the believers stay in their reward for ever, with no waiting at all.

why.bs: Musa porodici: „Zadržite se tu! Opazio sam vatru …“ – ostaju i čekaju ga; ar-Rāġib navodi ove riječi.
why.en: Moses to his family: “Bide ye (here). Lo! I see in the distance a fire” — they stay and wait for him; ar-Rāġib cites these words.

why.bs: „I nije se dugo zadržao …“ – kratko zadržavanje; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “But he was not long in coming” — a short halt; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… a ono što ljudima koristi ostaje u zemlji“ – ostajanje bez čekanja, protuprimjer.
why.en: “As for that which is of use to mankind, it remaineth in the earth” — staying without waiting, a counter-example.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače čekati ono što još nije došlo. Razlikuju se po tome da li je to samo iščekivanje ili čekanje da se nešto određeno desi, često nekome drugom.
shared.en: Both words mean waiting for what has not yet come. They differ in whether it is plain expectation, or waiting for something specific to happen, often to someone else.

tellApart.bs: Čekati, iščekivati ono što dolazi – opća riječ → اِنْتَظَرَ; čekati da nešto određeno nastupi ili prestane, vrebati da nekoga nešto pogodi → تَرَبَّصَ.
tellApart.en: To wait for, to expect what is coming — the general word → اِنْتَظَرَ; to wait for a definite thing to arrive or pass, to lie in wait for something to strike someone → تَرَبَّصَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نظر, ربص
notes: ar-Rāġib (نظر): naẓar is also intiẓār; naẓartuhu and intaẓartuhu mean I deferred him (aḫḫartuhu); cites 11:122, 10:102 (the 'qul fa-ntaẓirū…' wording is 10:102, not 10:20), 57:13, then the inẓār verses (see anzara-amla-mahhala). (ربص): tarabbuṣ is waiting with regard to a thing — a commodity, by which a rise or fall in price is sought, or a matter whose ending or arrival is awaited; cites 2:228, 9:52 and 'qul tarabbaṣū fa-innī maʿakum mina l-mutarabbiṣīn' (that wording is 52:31).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 7 / 11 places read): اِنْتَظَرَ is mostly the paired command 'wait, we too are waiting' to the deniers (7:71, 10:20, 10:102, 11:122, 32:30); 6:158 asks what they wait for; 33:23 is the believers who 'still are waiting'. تَرَبَّصَ is the waiting period of divorced and widowed women (2:228, 2:234) and, most often, the deniers' and hypocrites' waiting for harm to strike the believers (4:141, 9:52, 9:98, 52:30, 57:14), answered by 'wait, I am waiting with you' (9:52, 20:135, 52:31). Ayat addressed to the Prophet (32:30) were not cited.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: what the believers of 33:23 wait for is given as many mufassirun's reading; 33:23 bs completed ('smrću', 'zamijenili').

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, intiẓār je čekanje, ostavljanje za kasnije. U Kur'anu je to najčešće zapovijed nevjernicima: ‚Čekajte, i mi čekamo‘; vjernici iz 33:23 također čekaju – kako kažu mnogi mufessiri, šehadet na Allahovu putu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, intiẓār is waiting, putting off till later. In the Quran it is most often the command to the deniers: ‘Wait, we too are waiting’; the believers of 33:23 also wait — many mufassirun say, for martyrdom in Allah's way.

why.bs: „Pa čekaju li oni išta osim dana poput dana onih koji su prije njih prošli? Reci: ‚Pa čekajte, i ja sam s vama među onima koji čekaju!‘“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “What expect they save the like of the days of those who passed away before them? Say: Expect then! I am with you among the expectant” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I čekajte, i mi čekamo!“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And wait! Lo! We (too) are waiting” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… neki su od njih svoj zavjet ispunili smrću, a neki još čekaju, i ništa nisu zamijenili“ – čekanje vjernika, bez ikakvog zla.
why.en: “Some of them have paid their vow by death (in battle), and some of them still are waiting” — the believers' waiting, with no ill intent.

meaning.en: to await, to lie in wait

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, tarabbuṣ je čekanje u vezi s nečim: robom, da joj cijena skoči ili padne, ili stvari da nastupi ili prestane. Tako čekaju razvedene žene svoj rok, a nevjernici i licemjeri – da vjernike nešto pogodi.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, tarabbuṣ is waiting with regard to a thing: goods, for their price to rise or fall, or a matter, for it to arrive or pass. So divorced women wait out their term, and the deniers and hypocrites wait for something to strike the believers.

why.bs: „Razvedene žene neka čekaju, sustežući se, tri mjesečna perioda“ – čekanje određenog roka; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Women who are divorced shall wait, keeping themselves apart, three (monthly) courses” — waiting out a set term; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Reci: ‚Čekate li za nas išta drugo osim jednog od dva dobra? A mi čekamo da vas Allah pogodi kaznom …‘“ – čekanje ishoda za drugoga; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Can ye await for us aught save one of two good things … while we await for you that Allah will afflict you with a doom” — waiting for an outcome to befall another; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Reci: ‚Čekajte, i ja sam s vama među onima koji čekaju!‘“ – odgovor onima koji su rekli da čekaju da njega stigne nesreća (52:30); ar-Rāġib navodi ove riječi.
why.en: Await, I am awaiting with you — the answer to those who said they waited for misfortune to strike him (52:30); ar-Rāġib cites these words.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače dati nekome vremena prije onoga što ga čeka. Razlikuju se po tome šta se ističe: odgađanje roka, produžavanje vremena ili polaganost bez žurbe.
shared.en: All three words mean giving someone time before what awaits him. They differ in what is stressed: putting off the term, lengthening the time, or unhurried gentleness.

tellApart.bs: Odgoditi, odložiti rok – u Kur'anu najčešće zanijekano: ‚neće im se odgoditi‘ → أَنْظَرَ; pustiti uzde, dati da vrijeme potraje (Allah nevjernicima, kako Njemu priliči) → أَمْلَى; dati vremena polako, blago, bez žurbe → مَهَّلَ.
tellApart.en: To defer, to put off a term — in the Quran mostly negated: ‘they will not be reprieved’ → أَنْظَرَ; to give rein, to let time run long (Allah with the deniers, as befits Him) → أَمْلَى; to give time slowly, gently, without haste → مَهَّلَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نظر, ملا, مهل
notes: ar-Rāġib (نظر): naẓartuhu / intaẓartuhu, I deferred him (aḫḫartuhu); cites 57:13, 'wa-mā kānū iḏan munẓarīn', 7:14–15, 11:55, 32:29, 44:29; in 44:29 He denied them inẓār, pointing to 7:34 / 16:61 (same wording) (when their term comes they cannot put it off an hour). (ملا): imlāʾ is imdād, extending; hence malāwa / malī for a long stretch of time (19:46 wa-hǧurnī maliyyā); 7:183 / 68:45 wa-umlī lahum means I give them respite (amhiluhum); 47:25 also means respite, and whoever reads it otherwise (this text prints أملأ) takes it from imlāʾ of a book; cites 3:178; amlaytu (dictate) is from amlaltu (25:5, 2:282). (مهل): mahl is tuʾada and calm; mahlan is like rifqan (gently); amhaltuhu, I treated him gently (rafaqtu bihi); cites 86:17.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 12 / 8 / 2 places read): أَنْظَرَ is mostly the passive negated 'nor will they be reprieved' (2:162, 3:88, 6:8, 16:85, 21:40, 32:29); 11:55 and 10:71 are a prophet's challenge 'give me no respite'; 7:195 the same to the idols; 7:14, 15:36, 38:79 are Iblīs's request (not cited, as in earlier batches). أَمْلَى: Allah's respite to the deniers (3:178, 7:183, 13:32, 22:44, 22:48, 68:45); its count includes 25:5 (tumlā, 'dictated') and 47:25, where who gives the respite is read two ways (not cited). مَهَّلَ: 73:11 and 86:17, both commands; 86:17 also has أَمْهِلْهُمْ (Form IV, 1×, not counted).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, inẓār je odgađanje, ostavljanje za kasnije. U Kur'anu je najčešće zanijekan: kad dođe kazna ili određeni rok, nevjernicima se više ne odgađa – kako ar-Rāġib upućuje na 7:34, rok se ne može pomaknuti ni za trenutak.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, inẓār is deferring, putting off till later. In the Quran it is mostly negated: when the punishment or the set term comes, the deniers are not reprieved — as ar-Rāġib points to 7:34, the term cannot be moved by an hour.

why.bs: „A kad oni koji su činili zulum vide kaznu, neće im se ona olakšati niti će im se odgoditi.“
why.en: “And when those who did wrong behold the doom, it will not be made light for them, nor will they be reprieved.”

why.bs: „… na Dan pobjede neće koristiti nevjernicima njihovo vjerovanje, niti će im se odgoditi“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “On the day of the victory the faith of those who disbelieve … will not avail them, neither will they be reprieved” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Hud svom narodu: „… pa svi zajedno smišljajte protiv mene, i ne dajte mi odgode!“ – izazov s pouzdanjem u Allaha; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Hūd to his people: “So (try to) circumvent me, all of you, give me no respite” — a challenge in trust in Allah; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

meaning.en: to give rein, to grant a long respite

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, imlāʾ je produžavanje, davanje vremena da se oduži; on 7:183 objašnjava kao ‚dajem im vremena‘. U Kur'anu Allah tako nevjernicima pušta uzde, kako Njemu priliči – i kaže da to nije dobro za njih (3:178).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, imlāʾ is extending, letting time run long; he explains 7:183 as ‘I give them respite’. In the Quran Allah so gives the deniers rein, as befits Him — and says it is not good for them (3:178).

why.bs: „A Ja im puštam uzde – Moj plan je, zaista, čvrst“ – kako Njemu priliči; ar-Rāġib navodi ove riječi.
why.en: “I give them rein (for) lo! My scheme is strong” — as befits Him; ar-Rāġib cites these words.

why.bs: „Neka ne misle oni koji ne vjeruju da je dobro za njih to što im puštamo uzde …“ – vrijeme koje nije blagodat; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And let not those who disbelieve imagine that the rein We give them bodeth good unto their souls” — time that is no favour; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… pa sam nevjernicima pustio uzde, a zatim ih kaznio“ – dugo vrijeme, pa onda kazna, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “But I indulged the disbelievers a long while, then I seized them” — a long time, then the seizing, as befits Him.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, mahl je polaganost i smirenost, a ‚mahlan‘ znači ‚polako, blago‘. U Kur'anu je dvaput zapovijed: dati nevjernicima malo vremena, bez žurbe.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, mahl is slowness and calm, and ‘mahlan’ means ‘gently, slowly’. In the Quran it is twice a command: to give the deniers a little time, without haste.

why.bs: „Zato daj vremena nevjernicima, pusti ih malo“ – isti korijen dvaput, u dva oblika; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “So give a respite to the disbelievers. Deal thou gently with them for a while” — the same root twice, in two forms; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Ostavi Meni one koji poriču, koji su u blagodatima, i daj im još malo vremena“ – kratko, polagano vrijeme.
why.en: “Leave Me to deal with the deniers … and do thou respite them awhile” — a short, unhurried time.

shared.bs: Obje riječi u Kur'anu opisuju ono što se smije uzeti, najčešće hranu, i često stoje zajedno (‚halal i lijepo‘). Razlikuju se po tome da li se gleda dozvola ili sama dobrota i čistoća stvari.
shared.en: Both words describe in the Quran what may be taken, most often food, and they often stand together (‘lawful and good’). They differ in whether one looks at the permission, or at the goodness and cleanness of the thing itself.

tellApart.bs: Ono što je dozvoljeno, ‚odvezano‘ od zabrane → حَلَال; ono što je lijepo i čisto, ugodno čulima i duši, i u ljudima i riječima → طَيِّب.
tellApart.en: What is permitted, ‘untied’ from prohibition → حَلَال; what is good and clean, pleasing to the senses and the soul, said of people and words too → طَيِّب.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries طيب, حل
notes: ar-Rāġib (حل): the root is untying a knot (20:27); ḥalla also means to alight (from untying loads); from untying a knot is borrowed ḥalla š-šayʾu, it became lawful; cites 5:88 wording ('wa-kulū mimmā razaqakumu llāhu ḥalālan ṭayyiban') and 16:116 'hāḏā ḥalālun wa-hāḏā ḥarām'. (طيب): the root of ṭayyib is what the senses and the soul find pleasant; lawful ṭayyib food in the Law is what is taken as permitted, in the permitted amount and from the permitted place — then it is good now and later; cites 2:57 / 2:172 / 7:160 / 20:81 wording, 16:114 wording, 5:87, 23:51; the ṭayyib person is free of the impurity of ignorance, sin and ugly deeds and adorned with knowledge, faith and good deeds (16:32); cites 8:37, 24:26, 4:2, 14:24, 35:10, 9:72, 7:58 (good, pure land), 4:43 (earth without impurity).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 6 places of حَلَال and the 16 of طَيِّب read; the 30 of طَيِّبَة not all read): حَلَال stands beside طَيِّب in 4 of its 6 places (2:168, 5:88, 8:69, 16:114); the other two (10:59, 16:116) blame people who declare things lawful and unlawful of their own accord. The طَيِّب member sums the adjective طَيِّب (16) and the noun طَيِّبَة / ṭayyibāt (30), which the corpus files apart; طَيِّب is also said of land (7:58), earth (4:43, 5:6), words (35:10, 22:24) and people (16:32, 24:26). The muḥill/aḥalla verbs are not counted.
