nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, korijen je odvezivanje čvora; odatle je preneseno ‚postati dozvoljen‘. U Kur'anu حَلَال u četiri od šest mjesta stoji uz طَيِّب; na druga dva kudi one koji sami proglašavaju šta je dozvoljeno a šta zabranjeno.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root is untying a knot; from it is borrowed ‘to become lawful’. In the Quran حَلَال stands beside طَيِّب in four of its six places; in the other two it blames those who declare of their own accord what is lawful and what forbidden.

why.bs: „O ljudi, jedite od onoga što je na zemlji dozvoljeno i lijepo“ – dozvola i dobrota zajedno.
why.en: “O mankind! Eat of that which is lawful and wholesome in the earth” — permission and goodness together.

why.bs: „I ne govorite o onome što vaši jezici lažno opisuju: ‚Ovo je dozvoljeno, a ovo zabranjeno‘ …“ – dozvola pripada Allahu; ar-Rāġib navodi ove riječi.
why.en: “And speak not, concerning that which your own tongues qualify … the falsehood: This is lawful, and this is forbidden” — permission belongs to Allah; ar-Rāġib cites these words.

why.bs: „… pa ste od njega jedno proglasili zabranjenim, a drugo dozvoljenim. Reci: ‚Je li vam Allah dozvolio …‘“ – dozvola koja nije od Allaha.
why.en: “How ye have made of it lawful and unlawful? Hath Allah permitted you” — a permission that is not Allah's.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, طَيِّب je izvorno ono što je ugodno čulima i duši; hrana je u šerijatu طَيِّب kad je uzeta kako je dozvoljeno, u dozvoljenoj mjeri i s dozvoljenog mjesta. Kaže se i za zemlju, riječi i ljude – čiste od ružnog.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, طَيِّب is at root what pleases the senses and the soul; food is ṭayyib in the Law when it is taken as permitted, in the permitted amount and from the permitted place. It is said of land, words and people too — clean of what is foul.

why.bs: „O vjernici, ne zabranjujte lijepe stvari koje vam je Allah dozvolio“ – طَيِّبَات su ono što je Allah dozvolio; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “O ye who believe! Forbid not the good things which Allah hath made lawful for you” — the ṭayyibāt are what Allah made lawful; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A iz lijepe zemlje izlazi njeno bilje s dopuštenjem njenog Gospodara“ – ar-Rāġib kaže: čista zemlja.
why.en: “As for the good land, its vegetation cometh forth by permission of its Lord” — ar-Rāġib says: pure land.

why.bs: „K Njemu se uzdižu lijepe riječi“ – kako Njemu priliči; طَيِّب i za riječ; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Unto Him good words ascend” — as befits Him; ṭayyib said of speech; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače doći do znanja o nečemu. Razlikuju se po putu: razumom, od vidljivog prema skrivenom, ili tankim zapažanjem, kao čulima.
shared.en: Both words mean coming to know something. They differ in the way: by the mind, from the seen to the hidden, or by fine noticing, as with the senses.

tellApart.bs: Dublje shvatiti, od onoga što se vidi doći do onoga što je skriveno → فَقِهَ; osjetiti, primijetiti tanko, kao dodirom čula – u Kur'anu uvijek zanijekano ili uz ‚kad biste osjetili‘ → شَعَرَ.
tellApart.en: To understand in depth, reaching from what is seen to what is hidden → فَقِهَ; to perceive, to notice finely, as by the touch of the senses — in the Quran always negated or under ‘if only you perceived’ → شَعَرَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries فقه, شعر
notes: ar-Rāġib (فقه): fiqh is reaching knowledge of what is absent through knowledge of what is present (al-tawaṣṣul ilā ʿilm ġāʾib bi-ʿilm šāhid), so it is more specific than ʿilm; cites 4:78 and 'kānū lā yafqahūn'; fiqh is also knowledge of the rulings of the Law; tafaqqaha, to seek it (9:122). (شعر): šaʿartu, I struck the hair; from it is borrowed šaʿartu, I came to know with a fine knowledge, like hitting a hair; al-mašāʿir are the senses; 'wa-antum lā tašʿurūn' means you do not perceive it with the senses; had 'lā yaʿqilūn' been said in many of the places where 'lā yašʿurūn' comes, it would not have been right, since much that is not sensed may be grasped by the mind.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 19 / 25 places read): شَعَرَ (Form I) is negated in 24 of its 25 places (mā / lā yašʿurūn) and the 25th is 'law tašʿurūn', if only you perceived (26:113): the Quran never says someone did perceive. فَقِهَ is mostly negated too, but not always: 6:98 'a people who understand', 20:28 Mūsā's prayer 'that they may understand my saying'. 49:2 was not cited (the scope of its warning differs), nor 8:65 (said to the Prophet).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, fiqh je dolaženje do znanja o skrivenom preko znanja o vidljivom; zato je uže od znanja (عِلْم). U Kur'anu je najčešće zanijekan – ne shvataju govor, ni hvalu svega stvorenog – ali Musa moli da ga shvate (20:28).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, fiqh is reaching knowledge of the hidden through knowledge of the seen; so it is narrower than knowledge (عِلْم). In the Quran it is mostly negated — they do not understand speech, nor the praise of all creation — but Moses prays to be understood (20:28).

why.bs: „Pa šta je tim ljudima, jedva da ijedan govor shvataju!“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “What is amiss with these people that they come not nigh to understand a happening?” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… i nema ničega što Ga ne slavi hvaleći Ga, ali vi ne shvatate njihovo slavljenje“ – ono što se ne vidi, a razumom se ne dosegne.
why.en: “There is not a thing but hymneth His praise; but ye understand not their praise” — what is not seen, and the mind does not reach.

why.bs: Musa: „… da shvate moj govor“ – molba da se razumije poruka; potvrdno, protuprimjer.
why.en: Moses: “That they may understand my saying” — a prayer that the message be grasped; affirmed, a counter-example.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, šuʿūr je tanko saznanje, kao kad se dodirne dlaka; مَشَاعِر su čula. ‚Ne osjećate‘ je: ne opažate čulima. On kaže da se na mnogo mjesta ne bi moglo reći ‚ne razumiju‘ umjesto ‚ne osjećaju‘, jer se razumom zna i ono što se čulima ne opaža.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, šuʿūr is fine knowing, as when one touches a hair; مَشَاعِر are the senses. ‘You do not perceive’ is: you do not sense it. He says that in many places ‘they do not reason’ could not stand for ‘they do not perceive’, since the mind knows much that the senses do not catch.

why.bs: „Naprotiv, živi su, samo što vi to ne primjećujete“ – o onima koji su ubijeni na Allahovu putu: živi su, ali ne za čula.
why.en: “Nay, they are living, only ye perceive not” — of those slain in Allah's way: alive, though not to the senses.

why.bs: „Zaista, oni su ti koji nered čine, ali to ne osjećaju“ – ne primjećuju šta čine.
why.en: “Are not they indeed the mischief-makers? But they perceive not” — they do not notice what they do.

why.bs: „… pa da im dođe iznenada, a da oni ne osjete“ – kazna koju ne primijete dok ne stigne.
why.en: “So that it will come upon them suddenly, when they perceive not” — a punishment unnoticed until it arrives.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače ići za drugim. Razlikuju se po tome da li se izvršava naredba ili se ide nečijim tragom i putem.
shared.en: Both words mean going after another. They differ in whether a command is carried out, or someone's trace and way is followed.

tellApart.bs: Izvršiti ono što je naređeno, pokoriti se naredbi → أَطَاعَ; ići tragom, slijediti put, osobu ili nešto što ne naređuje – strast, običaj očeva → اِتَّبَعَ.
tellApart.en: To carry out what is commanded, to yield to an order → أَطَاعَ; to go along a trace, to follow a way, a person, or what gives no command — desire, the fathers' custom → اِتَّبَعَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries طوع, تبع
notes: ar-Rāġib (طوع): ṭawʿ is compliance (inqiyād), its opposite is karh (41:11, 3:83); ṭāʿa is like it, but is mostly said of carrying out what is commanded and keeping to what is laid down (al-iʾtimār li-mā umira wa-l-irtisām fī-mā rusim); cites 4:81 and 47:21, 'wa-aṭīʿū r-rasūl', 4:80, 33:1 / 33:48 wording, 81:21. (تبع): tabiʿahu and ittabaʿahu are going after his trace (qafā aṯarahu), sometimes by keeping to what is commanded and laid down; cites 2:38, 36:20–21, 20:123, 7:3, 26:111, 12:38, 45:18, 2:102, 2:168 (= 2:208, 6:142), 38:26, 18:66, 31:15; atbaʿahu is catching up with him (26:60, 18:85).

Quranic usage (our observation, the places of اِتَّبَعَ read for their objects, those of أَطَاعَ for their persons): أَطَاعَ takes persons who command — Allah, the Messenger, those in authority, or the leaders and the deniers one is told not to obey. اِتَّبَعَ also takes what gives no order: desires (hawā), the footsteps of Satan, conjecture, what was found with the fathers (2:170), as well as the Messenger and what was sent down. 3:31 (the Prophet told to say 'follow me') was not cited, to keep to ayat that need no commentary; 6:116 (a conditional to the Prophet) was left out.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: Bosnian quotes of 36:21 and 2:170 re-translated from the Arabic.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ṭawʿ je pokornost, suprotno prisili; ṭāʿa je isto, ali se najčešće kaže za izvršavanje onoga što je naređeno. Zato أَطَاعَ u Kur'anu ide uz one koji naređuju: Allaha, Poslanika, one koji imaju vlast – ili one koje ne treba slušati.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ṭawʿ is compliance, the opposite of compulsion; ṭāʿa is the same, but is mostly said of carrying out what is commanded. So أَطَاعَ in the Quran goes with those who command: Allah, the Messenger, those in authority — or those who must not be obeyed.

why.bs: „Ko se pokori Poslaniku, pokorio se Allahu …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Whoso obeyeth the messenger hath obeyed Allah” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… govorit će: ‚Kamo sreće da smo se pokorili Allahu i pokorili se Poslaniku!‘“ – kajanje zbog neizvršene naredbe.
why.en: “They say: Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and had obeyed His messenger!” — regret for commands not carried out.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ittibāʿ je ići nečijim tragom; ponekad je to izvršavanje naredbe, ali ne uvijek. Zato se u Kur'anu slijedi i ono što ne naređuje: strast, šejtanove korake, ono na čemu su zatečeni očevi – ali i poslanike i ono što je objavljeno.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ittibāʿ is going along someone's trace; sometimes this is carrying out a command, but not always. So in the Quran one also follows what gives no command: desire, Satan's footsteps, what the fathers were found upon — but also the messengers and what was sent down.

why.bs: „Slijedite one koji od vas ne traže platu, a upućeni su!“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Follow those who ask of you no fee, and who are rightly guided” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Kad im se kaže: „Slijedite ono što je Allah objavio“, kažu: „Ne, mi slijedimo ono u čemu smo zatekli svoje očeve“ – slijeđenje običaja, bez naredbe.
why.en: “Follow that which Allah hath revealed, they say: We follow that wherein we found our fathers” — following a custom, with no command.

why.bs: „… i ne slijedite šejtanove stope“ – trag koji se ne slijedi; ar-Rāġib navodi ove riječi.
why.en: “And follow not the footsteps of the devil” — a trace not to be followed; ar-Rāġib cites these words.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače učiniti da nešto ne ostane kakvo je bilo. Razlikuju se po tome šta se dešava: stvar se zamijeni drugom, mijenja joj se stanje, ili se riječ izvrne od svog mjesta.
shared.en: All three words mean making something not stay as it was. They differ in what happens: the thing is replaced by another, its state is changed, or a word is bent away from its place.

tellApart.bs: Staviti jedno na mjesto drugog, zamijeniti → بَدَّلَ; izmijeniti stanje ili oblik stvari → غَيَّرَ; iskriviti riječ, nagnuti je s njenog mjesta → حَرَّفَ.
tellApart.en: To put one thing in another's place, to replace → بَدَّلَ; to alter a thing's state or form → غَيَّرَ; to distort a word, to tilt it from its place → حَرَّفَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries بدل, غير, حرف
notes: ar-Rāġib (بدل): ibdāl, tabdīl, tabaddul, istibdāl are putting one thing in another's place, wider than ʿiwaḍ (exchange for something given); tabdīl may be said of change in general, even without a replacement; cites 2:59, 24:55, 25:70 (two qīla views), 2:181, 16:101, 34:16, 7:95, 14:48 ('tubaddalu l-arḍu ġayra l-arḍ', i.e. changed from its state), 40:26, 2:108, 47:38, 50:29, 10:64, 30:30. (غير): taġyīr is said two ways: changing a thing's form without its essence (rebuilding one's house), and replacing it with another (13:11 wording 'inna llāha lā yuġayyiru mā bi-qawmin ḥattā yuġayyirū mā bi-anfusihim'); under ġayr he cites 4:56 (skins replaced: the form denied, not the matter). (حرف): ḥarf is the edge of a thing; taḥrīf of a thing is tilting it, like cutting a pen slantwise; taḥrīf of speech is putting it on an edge of possibility so it can be taken two ways; cites 4:46 / 5:13, 5:41, 2:75.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 21 / 3 / 4 places read): بَدَّلَ is said of a word replaced (2:59, 7:162), of Allah's favour exchanged (2:211, 14:28), of the earth on the Last Day (14:48), of ayah for ayah (16:101), and, praised, of believers who 'did not change' (33:23). غَيَّرَ: 4:119 (Satan's vow, not cited — read many ways), 8:53, 13:11; the participle مُغَيِّر in 8:53 is not counted. حَرَّفَ: 2:75, 4:46, 5:13, 5:41, all of people of the Book; whether taḥrīf was of the wording or of the meaning is discussed by the mufassirun and is not decided here. 5:41 (addressed to the Prophet) and 25:70 (two readings) were not cited.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 3 flags, fixed: he sets 8:53 under taġyīr as replacing; 'often' a change of state; Bosnian quotes of 2:59 and 8:53 re-translated.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries بدل, غير, حرف (2026-11-06): 15 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): 'like cutting a pen slantwise' glosses his bare 'ka-taḥrīf al-qalam'; acceptable lexical gloss; members/0/nuance (improved): Aligns the illustration with his gloss, which is exactly the 'change in general' sense the sentence introduces

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, tabdīl je stavljanje jedne stvari na mjesto druge; ponekad se kaže i za promjenu uopće, i kad zamjene nema. Tako se zamjenjuje rečena riječ drugom, a na Sudnjem danu zemlja se mijenja iz svog stanja.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, tabdīl is putting one thing in another's place; at times it is said of change in general, even with no replacement. So a word that was told is replaced by another, and on the Last Day the earth is changed from its state.

why.bs: „Pa su oni koji su činili zulum umjesto rečene riječi izgovorili neku drugu“ – riječ na mjestu riječi; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “But those who did wrong changed the word which had been told them for another saying” — a word in a word's place; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Na Dan kad zemlja bude zamijenjena drugom zemljom, i nebesa …“ – ar-Rāġib kaže: izmijenjena od svog stanja.
why.en: “On the day when the earth will be changed to other than the earth” — ar-Rāġib says: changed from its state.

why.bs: „… a ništa nisu zamijenili“ – vjernici koji su ostali vjerni zavjetu.
why.en: “And they have not altered in the least” — believers who kept their covenant.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, taġyīr se kaže na dva načina: promjena oblika stvari, a ne njene suštine, i zamjena stvari drugom – a pod ovo drugo on svrstava 8:53. U Kur'anu je to često promjena stanja: Allah ne mijenja blagodat koju je dao narodu dok oni ne promijene ono što je u njima – kako Njemu priliči.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, taġyīr is said two ways: changing a thing's form, not its essence, and replacing it with another — and it is under the second that he sets 8:53. In the Quran it is often a change of state: Allah does not alter the favour He gave a people until they alter what is in themselves — as befits Him.

why.bs: „To je zato što Allah neće izmijeniti blagodat kojom je neki narod obdario, dok oni ne izmijene ono što je u njihovim dušama“ – promjena stanja, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: Allah does not alter a favour He has bestowed on a people until they alter what is in themselves — a change of state, as befits Him.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḥarf je rub stvari, a taḥrīf je naginjanje, kao kad se pero zareže ukoso; iskriviti govor znači staviti ga na rub mogućeg, da se može shvatiti na dva načina. U Kur'anu je to uvijek ono što se kaže o nekima od sljedbenika Knjige; da li je riječ o tekstu ili o značenju, o tome mufessiri raspravljaju.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ḥarf is the edge of a thing, and taḥrīf is tilting, as when a pen is cut slantwise; to distort speech is to set it on an edge of possibility, so that it can be taken two ways. In the Quran it is always said of some of the people of the Book; whether the wording or the meaning is meant, the mufassirun discuss.

why.bs: „… a jedna skupina njih slušala je Allahov govor, a zatim ga, nakon što su ga shvatili, iskrivljavala, znajući“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: A party of them heard Allah's word, then distorted it after they had understood it, knowingly — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Neki od njih ‚izvrću riječi s njihovih mjesta‘ – riječ pomaknuta sa svog mjesta; ar-Rāġib navodi ove riječi.
why.en: Some of them ‘shift words from their places’ — a word moved from where it belongs; ar-Rāġib cites these words.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače da nečega bude više. Razlikuju se po mjeri: bilo kakav dodatak, ili dodavanje istog toliko još jednom i više puta.
shared.en: Both words mean that there comes to be more of something. They differ in the measure: any addition at all, or adding the same amount again, once or many times.

tellApart.bs: Dodati nešto onome što stvar jeste, u dobru ili u zlu → زَادَ; dodati stvari njoj jednako, udvostručiti i umnožiti – u Kur'anu za nagradu i kaznu → ضَاعَفَ.
tellApart.en: To add something to what a thing already is, for good or ill → زَادَ; to add to a thing its equal, to double and multiply — in the Quran of reward and punishment → ضَاعَفَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries زاد, ضعف
notes: ar-Rāġib (زاد): ziyāda is that something else is joined to what the thing is in itself; it may be blameworthy, like excess beyond sufficiency (an extra finger), or praiseworthy (10:26, with the report that this ziyāda is the sight of Allah's Face; 2:247: He gave him of knowledge and body more than He gave the people of his time); cites 19:76; of the disliked kind 35:42 ('mā zādahum illā nufūrā'; 17:41 has mā yazīduhum), 16:88, 11:63, 2:10 — this increase is what human nature is built on: whoever takes up a deed, good or bad, grows stronger in it, state by state. (ضعف): ḍiʿf is a correlative word, like half and pair, the joining of two equal amounts, particular to number; aḍʿaftu, ḍaʿʿaftu, ḍāʿaftu: I joined to it its like or more; 'some said ḍāʿaftu is more emphatic than ḍaʿʿaftu', so most read 33:30 yuḍāʿaf; cites 4:40 and 6:160, and on that view muḍāʿafa of a good deed implies ten of its like.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 9 places of ضَاعَفَ read; زَادَ's 49 sampled for what is increased): ضَاعَفَ is said of Allah's multiplying of a good deed or a goodly loan (2:245, 2:261, 4:40, 57:11, 57:18, 64:17) and of a punishment doubled (11:20, 25:69, 33:30). زَادَ is said of guidance, faith, knowledge and stature, and also of aversion, sickness and loss. 33:30 (to the Prophet's wives) and 2:10 (Allah increasing sickness, which needs commentary beside it) were not cited.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: his 'whoever takes up a thing grows stronger in it' tied to 2:10, where he says it; 57:11 — spending that Allah, free of need, calls a loan.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ziyāda je da se onome što stvar jeste pridruži nešto drugo; može biti hvale vrijedna ili pokuđena. Allah povećava uputu onima koji su na Pravom putu, kako Njemu priliči; a opomene nekima povećaju samo odbojnost, a to je pokuđeno povećanje. Objašnjavajući pokuđeno povećanje (2:10), ar-Rāġib kaže: ko se nečega lati, u dobru ili zlu, u tome jača.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ziyāda is that something else is joined to what a thing already is; it may be praiseworthy or blameworthy. Allah increases in guidance those who are guided, as befits Him; and the reminders increase some only in aversion, a blameworthy increase. Explaining a blameworthy increase (2:10), ar-Rāġib says: whoever takes up a thing, good or bad, grows stronger in it.

why.bs: „A Allah povećava uputu onima koji su na Pravom putu“ – kako Njemu priliči; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Allah increaseth in right guidance those who walk aright” — as befits Him; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… i dao mu je više znanja i tijela“ – ar-Rāġib, koji navodi ovaj ajet, kaže: više nego ljudima njegova vremena.
why.en: “And hath increased him abundantly in wisdom and stature” — ar-Rāġib, who cites this ayah, says: more than the people of his time.

why.bs: „… a kad im je došao opominjač, to im je povećalo samo odbojnost“ – pokuđeno povećanje; ar-Rāġib navodi ove riječi.
why.en: “When a warner came unto them it aroused in them naught save repugnance” — the warner's coming only increased their aversion, a blameworthy increase; ar-Rāġib cites these words.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḍiʿf je spoj dvije jednake mjere, riječ broja; ḍāʿafa je dodati stvari njoj jednako ili više. Neki kažu da je ḍāʿafa jače od ḍaʿʿafa, pa bi umnožavanje dobrog djela značilo deset puta (6:160). U Kur'anu Allah tako umnožava dobro djelo, kako Njemu priliči, a nekima se kazna udvostručuje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ḍiʿf is the joining of two equal amounts, a word of number; ḍāʿafa is adding to a thing its like or more. Some say ḍāʿafa is stronger than ḍaʿʿafa, so that multiplying a good deed would mean ten-fold (6:160). In the Quran Allah so multiplies a good deed, as befits Him, and for some the punishment is doubled.

why.bs: „Allah, zaista, ni koliko trun ne čini nepravdu; a ako je dobro djelo, On ga umnoži“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And if there is a good deed, He will double it” — as befits Him; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Ko je taj koji će Allahu dati lijep zajam, pa da mu ga On umnoži …“ – trošenje na Allahovu putu, koje On, Kojem ništa ne treba, naziva zajmom; vraća se umnoženo.
why.en: “Who is he that will lend unto Allah a goodly loan, that He may double it for him” — spending in Allah's way, which He, free of need, calls a loan; it is returned multiplied.

why.bs: „… udvostručit će mu se kazna na Sudnjem danu“ – udvostručenje i u kazni.
why.en: “The doom will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection” — doubling in punishment too.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o pomoći koja nekome dolazi izvana. Razlikuju se po onome što pomoć donosi: prevlast nad onim ko mu se suprotstavlja, dotok onoga što mu treba, ili ruku koja radi zajedno s njim.
shared.en: All three words speak of help that comes to someone from outside. They differ in what the help brings: the upper hand over whoever stands against him, a supply of what he needs, or a hand that works alongside him.

tellApart.bs: Pomoći protiv protivnika, dati pobjedu – najčešće Allah vjernicima i poslanicima → نَصَرَ; opskrbiti, pojačati dotokom (vojskom, imetkom, sinovima, plodovima) – ar-Rāġib: najčešće u onome što je drago → أَمَدَّ; potpomoći, stati uz nekoga u poslu – oba puta ljudi → أَعَانَ.
tellApart.en: Helping against an opponent, giving victory — mostly Allah to believers and messengers → نَصَرَ; reinforcing with a supply (hosts, wealth, sons, fruit) — ar-Rāġib: mostly of what is welcome → أَمَدَّ; assisting, backing someone in a task — both times people → أَعَانَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نصر, مد, عون
notes: ar-Rāġib (نصر): naṣr and nuṣra are ʿawn (help); cites 61:13, 110:1, 3:160, 2:250, 30:47, 40:51 and others; Allah's naṣr of the servant is evident, and the servant's naṣr of Allah is his helping His servants, keeping His limits, honouring His covenants, holding to His rulings and avoiding what He forbids (57:25, 47:7, 61:14); intiṣār and istinṣār are seeking help (42:39, 8:72, 42:41); on 54:10 fa-ntaṣir. (مد): the root sense of madd is drawing out; amdadtu l-ǧayša bi-madad and a man with food; imdād comes mostly in what is welcome (al-maḥbūb) and madd in what is disliked; cites 52:22, 23:55, 71:12, 3:125, 27:36, and for madd 19:79, 2:15, 7:202. (عون): ʿawn is muʿāwana and muẓāhara (backing); aʿantuhu; cites 18:95 and 25:4; taʿāwun is mutual backing (5:2); istiʿāna is seeking help (2:45).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 10 / 2 places read; نَصَرَ's 59 read for the examples, no 'always' claimed): أَمَدَّ (Form IV) has Allah as subject in every place but 27:36, where the Queen's envoys offer Solomon wealth; what is supplied is angels (3:124–125), wealth and sons (17:6, 23:55, 26:133, 71:12), fruit and meat in the Garden (52:22). 23:55 is a supply that is not a sign of favour (respite), which ar-Rāġib still cites in his one mixed example list after the imdād/madd remark (the unvowelled نمدهم does not show the form). أَعَانَ is only 18:95 (Dhul-Qarnayn asks the people to help him with strength) and 25:4 (the disbelievers' claim that others helped the Prophet compose the Quran). Pickthall renders both نَصَرَ (47:7) and أَعَانَ (18:95) 'help': the أَعَانَ ayat are paraphrased in English. 8:9 (مُمِدُّكُمْ) is a participle, not counted here.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 flag, fixed: bs gloss of أَعَانَ 'stati uz nekoga u poslu' (potpomoći was too close to نَصَرَ's pomoći).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries نصر, مد, عون (2026-11-06): 16 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): The verse he quotes is wa-li-yaʿlama llāhu man yanṣuruhu = 57:25, not 22:40 (wa-la-yanṣuranna llāhu man yanṣuruhu). Plain-string claim: fix given under key 'text'; notes/1 (reworded): His examples follow 'imdād mostly in the welcome, madd in the disliked' as one undivided list (imdād and madd verses mixed); he does not label 23:55, and the unvowelled text cannot show whether it is numidd- (IV) or namudd- (I); members/1/ayat/1/why (reworded): He cites it in an unlabelled list that mixes imdād and madd verses; the classification 'in what is welcome' is our (obvious) reading, not his explicit label; members/1/ayat/2/why (reworded): Cited, but not labelled imdād; unvowelled نمدهم cannot show Form IV

meaning.en: to help to victory, to give victory

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib definira naṣr kao pomoć (ʿawn). Allahova pomoć robu je očita – kako Njemu priliči; a rob ‚pomaže Allaha‘ kad pomaže Njegove robove, čuva Njegove granice i drži se Njegovih propisa. U Kur'anu je to najčešće pomoć protiv protivnika, pobjeda nad onim ko se suprotstavlja.
nuance.en: Ar-Rāġib defines naṣr as help (ʿawn). Allah's help to the servant is evident — as befits Him; and the servant ‘helps Allah’ when he helps His servants, keeps His limits and holds to His rulings. In the Quran it is mostly help against an opponent, victory over whoever stands against.

why.bs: „Allah vam je već dao pobjedu na Bedru, kad ste bili slabi …“ – pomoć protiv neprijatelja, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “Allah had already given you the victory at Badr, when ye were contemptible” — help against an enemy, as befits Him.

why.bs: „O vjernici, ako vi pomognete Allaha, On će pomoći vas i učvrstiti vaše korake“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet: rob ‚pomaže Allaha‘ pokornošću i pomaganjem Njegovih robova.
why.en: “O ye who believe! If ye help Allah, He will help you and will make your foothold firm” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah: the servant ‘helps Allah’ by obedience and by helping His servants.

nuance.bs: Osnova je ‚pružiti, produžiti‘, a amadda je dati dotok onoga što treba: vojsku, hranu, imetak. Prema ar-Rāġibu, imdād se najčešće kaže za ono što je drago, a madd za ono što je mrsko. U Kur'anu je subjekt Allah (kako Njemu priliči) na svim mjestima osim 27:36.
nuance.en: The root is ‘to draw out, to extend’, and amadda is supplying what is needed: troops, food, wealth. According to ar-Rāġib, imdād is said mostly of what is welcome, and madd of what is disliked. In the Quran the subject is Allah (as befits Him) in every place but 27:36.

why.bs: „… zar vam nije dovoljno da vas vaš Gospodar pojača s tri hiljade spuštenih meleka?“ – pojačanje dotokom, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “… Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should support you with three thousand angels sent down (to your help)?” — reinforcement by a supply, as befits Him.

why.bs: „I opskrbit ćemo ih voćem i mesom, kakvo god požele“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet među primjerima, odmah nakon što kaže da je imdād najčešće u onome što je drago.
why.en: “And We provide them with fruit and meat such as they desire” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah among his examples, right after saying imdād is mostly in what is welcome.

why.bs: „Zar misle da im imetkom i sinovima kojima ih opskrbljujemo …“ – ar-Rāġib i ovaj ajet navodi u istom nizu primjera; nastavak (23:56) kaže da to nije žurba u dobru – tako da opskrba nije uvijek znak naklonosti.
why.en: “Think they that in the wealth and sons wherewith We provide them” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah too in the same list; the next ayah (23:56) says it is not a hastening of good — so a supply is not always a sign of favour.

meaning.bs: stati uz nekoga u poslu, biti mu na ruku

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ʿawn je saradnja i podrška (muẓāhara): stati uz nekoga u poslu. Glagol je u Kur'anu samo dva puta, oba puta o ljudima koji pomažu ljude; srodni oblici su taʿāwun ‚međusobno pomaganje‘ (5:2) i istiʿāna ‚traženje pomoći‘ (1:5, 2:45).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ʿawn is working together and backing (muẓāhara): standing by someone in a task. The verb is in the Quran only twice, both times of people assisting people; related forms are taʿāwun ‘aiding one another’ (5:2) and istiʿāna ‘seeking aid’ (1:5, 2:45).

why.bs: „… pa potpomozite me snagom, napravit ću između vas i njih bedem“ – Zul-Karnejn traži od ljudi radnu snagu; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Dhul-Qarnayn asks the people to aid him with strength, so that he may set a barrier between them and Gog and Magog — labour, not victory; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Nevjernici tvrde da je Kur'an izmišljotina i da su mu u tome pomogli drugi ljudi – Kur'an tu tvrdnju odbacuje kao nepravdu i laž; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: The disbelievers claim the Quran is an invention and that other folk aided him in it — the Quran rejects the claim as wrong and falsehood; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o tome da čovjek svoju stvar stavlja u Allahove ruke. Razlikuju se po slici: osloniti se na nekoga kao na zastupnika koji vodi tvoj posao, ili vratiti i predati svoju stvar onome kome pripada.
shared.en: Both words speak of a person putting his affair into Allah's hands. They differ in the image: leaning on someone as on an agent who runs your affair, or handing your affair back to the One it belongs to.

tellApart.bs: Osloniti se na nekoga kao na zastupnika – u Kur'anu uvijek na Allaha, s ʿalā → تَوَكَّلَ; predati, vratiti svoju stvar Allahu – samo 40:44 → فَوَّضَ.
tellApart.en: Relying on someone as on an agent — in the Quran always on Allah, with ʿalā → تَوَكَّلَ; committing, handing one's affair back to Allah — only 40:44 → فَوَّضَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries وكل, فوض
notes: ar-Rāġib (وكل): tawkīl is relying on another and making him your deputy (nāʾib); wakīl is faʿīl in the sense of the passive; 4:81 'wa-kafā bi-llāhi wakīlā': be content with Him to take charge of your affair; tawakkul is said two ways: tawakkaltu li-fulān = I took charge for him, and tawakkaltu ʿalayhi = I relied on him; cites 9:51, 65:3, 60:4, 5:23, 33:3, 11:123, 25:58; at the end: wakīl is sometimes explained as kafīl, but wakīl is more general — every kafīl is a wakīl, not every wakīl a kafīl. (فوض): 40:44 wa-ufawwiḍu amrī ilā llāh = I return it (arudduhu) to Him; the root is from 'fawḍā' (from the saying mā lahum fawḍā baynahum, with a line of poetry), whence šarikat al-mufāwaḍa.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 40 places of تَوَكَّلَ read): it always takes ʿalā, and the one relied on is always Allah (Allah, our Lord, Him, the Living, the Mighty the Merciful). فَوَّضَ is only 40:44, the words of the believer of Pharaoh's people. 3:159 (an instruction to the Prophet) is not used as an illustration.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): all claims OK.

meaning.en: to rely, to put one's trust

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnova je tawkīl: osloniti se na drugoga i učiniti ga svojim zastupnikom; ‚tawakkaltu ʿalayhi‘ znači ‚oslonio sam se na njega‘. U Kur'anu (svih 40 mjesta) glagol ide s ʿalā i uvijek je to oslanjanje na Allaha; tako je Allah ‚al-Wakīl‘ – Onaj kome se prepušta vođenje stvari, kako Njemu priliči.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the base is tawkīl: relying on another and making him your agent; ‘tawakkaltu ʿalayhi’ means ‘I relied on him’. In the Quran (all 40 places) the verb takes ʿalā and it is always reliance on Allah; so Allah is ‘al-Wakīl’ — the One to whom the running of affairs is left, as befits Him.

why.bs: „… a ko se osloni na Allaha, On mu je dovoljan …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… And whosoever putteth his trust in Allah, He will suffice him” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A zašto se ne bismo oslonili na Allaha, kad nas je uputio našim putevima? …“ – riječi poslanika njihovim narodima: oslanjanje uz strpljivo podnošenje uznemiravanja.
why.en: “How should we not put our trust in Allah when He hath shown us our ways?” — the messengers' words to their peoples: reliance together with patient endurance of hurt.

meaning.en: to commit, to hand over (one's affair)

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ‚ufawwiḍu amrī ilā llāh‘ znači ‚vraćam svoju stvar Njemu‘. U Kur'anu je samo jednom, u riječima vjernika iz faraonova naroda, kad je izrekao svoj savjet i ostao sam: predaje stvar Allahu, Koji vidi robove.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ‘ufawwiḍu amrī ilā llāh’ means ‘I return my affair to Him’. It is in the Quran only once, in the words of the believer among Pharaoh's people, when he had given his counsel and stood alone: he hands the affair over to Allah, Who sees the servants.

why.bs: „Pa sjetit ćete se onoga što vam govorim, a ja svoju stvar predajem Allahu – Allah, zaista, vidi robove“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And ye will remember what I say unto you. I confide my cause unto Allah. Lo! Allah is Seer of (His) slaves” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

title.bs: Utočište: utjecati se, čvrsto se držati, pribježište
title.en: Refuge: seeking refuge, holding fast, a haven

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o traženju zaštite. Razlikuju se po slici: bijeg pod nečiju zaštitu od onoga čega se boji, čvrsto držanje za ono što spašava, ili mjesto u koje se bježi.
shared.en: All three words speak of seeking protection. They differ in the image: fleeing under someone's protection from what one fears, holding fast to what saves, or a place one flees into.

tellApart.bs: Utjecati se nekome od nečega – s bi- (kome) i min / an (od čega) → عَاذَ; uhvatiti se i držati se čvrsto – Allaha i Njegova užeta → اِعْتَصَمَ; pribježište, mjesto u koje se bježi – u Kur'anu samo tri puta: osim kod samog Allaha (9:118) nigdje ga nema, ili se ne može naći (9:57, 42:47) → مَلْجَأ.
tellApart.en: Seeking refuge with someone from something — with bi- (with whom) and min / an (from what) → عَاذَ; taking hold and holding fast — to Allah and His rope → اِعْتَصَمَ; a haven, a place one flees into — in the Quran only three times: none except with Allah Himself (9:118), or none to be found (9:57, 42:47) → مَلْجَأ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عوذ, عصم
notes: ar-Rāġib (عوذ): ʿawḏ is taking refuge with another and clinging to him (al-iltiǧāʾ ilā l-ġayr wa-t-taʿalluq bihi); cites 2:67, 44:20, qul aʿūḏu bi-rabbi (truncated: 113:1 or 114:1), 19:18, 3:36 (uʿīḏuhā bika); maʿāḏa llāh: we take refuge in Him and seek His help against doing it, for it is an evil we keep clear of; ʿūḏa is what one takes refuge in (amulets were called so). (عصم): ʿaṣm is holding (imsāk), iʿtiṣām is holding on (istimsāk); 11:43 lā ʿāṣima l-yawma min amri llāh; iʿtiṣām is clinging to a thing: 3:103 wa-ʿtaṣimū bi-ḥabli llāhi ǧamīʿan, 3:101 wa-man yaʿtaṣim bi-llāh; istaʿṣama (12:32): he sought what would hold him back from indecency; the ʿiṣma of the prophets is Allah's guarding of them. No Mufradāt entry for لجأ was found (the لج entry is laǧāǧ, persistence); but ar-Rāġib defines ʿawḏ itself with iltiǧāʾ, the verbal noun of this root.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 10 / 5 / 3 places read): عَاذَ is with Allah (or 'the Lord', 'the Beneficent') in every place but 72:6, where men sought refuge with men of the jinn and it increased them in folly; the feared thing follows with min (19:18, 23:97, 40:27, 113–114) or an 'that' (2:67, 11:47, 23:98, 44:20). اِعْتَصَمَ always takes bi-: Allah (3:101, 4:146, 4:175, 22:78) or the rope of Allah (3:103). مَلْجَأ: 9:57 (the hypocrites would flee to a refuge if they found one), 9:118 (no refuge from Allah but in Him), 42:47 (no refuge on that Day). Pickthall renders both عَاذَ and مَلْجَأ 'refuge'; the مَلْجَأ ayat are paraphrased in English. 11:47 (Noah) is not used as an illustration.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 4 flags, fixed: مَلْجَأ — none except with Allah only in 9:118; 9:57 is hypothetical, 42:47 has none (tellApart and nuance); 19:18 bs 'bogobojazan'; 72:6 bs re-translated from the Arabic.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries عوذ, عصم, لج (2026-11-06): 15 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): He quotes only قل أعوذ برب, which opens both 113:1 and 114:1. --mentions ملجأ confirms no لجأ entry; he does use al-malǧaʾ to gloss wazar (وزر, 75:11), manāṣ (نوص, 38:3) and al-ʿaṣr

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ʿawḏ je pribjeći drugome i prionuti uz njega. Uz glagol stoji kome se utječe (bi-) i od čega (min, ili ‚da ne …‘). U Kur'anu je to gotovo uvijek utjecanje Allahu; jedini izuzetak je 72:6, gdje su ljudi tražili zaštitu kod džina – i to im je samo povećalo obijest.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ʿawḏ is taking refuge with another and clinging to him. With the verb stand the one sought (bi-) and the thing feared (min, or ‘lest …’). In the Quran it is almost always refuge with Allah; the one exception is 72:6, where men sought protection with jinn — and it only increased them in revolt.

why.bs: „Reci: ‚Utječem se Gospodaru svitanja‘“ – ar-Rāġib navodi formulu ‚qul aʿūḏu bi-rabbi‘.
why.en: “Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the Daybreak” — ar-Rāġib cites the formula ‘qul aʿūḏu bi-rabbi’.

why.bs: „Rekla je: ‚Ja se Svemilosnom utječem od tebe, ako si bogobojazan‘“ – Merjem pred melekom koji joj je došao u liku čovjeka; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “She said: Lo! I seek refuge in the Beneficent One from thee, if thou art Allah-fearing” — Mary before the angel who came to her in the form of a man; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A bilo je ljudi koji su zaštitu tražili kod nekih džina, pa su ovi samo uvećali njihovu pobunu“ – jedino mjesto gdje se ne utječe Allahu.
why.en: “… individuals of humankind used to invoke the protection of individuals of the jinn, so that they increased them in revolt against Allah” — the one place where refuge is not sought with Allah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ʿaṣm je držanje (imsāk), a iʿtiṣām držanje za nešto, prianjanje. Nije bijeg od opasnosti nego trajno držanje za ono što čuva. U Kur'anu (svih 5 mjesta) ide s bi-: drži se Allaha ili Allahova užeta.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ʿaṣm is holding (imsāk), and iʿtiṣām is holding on to something, clinging. It is not fleeing from a danger but a lasting hold on what keeps one safe. In the Quran (all 5 places) it takes bi-: holding fast to Allah or to the rope of Allah.

why.bs: „I svi se čvrsto držite Allahova užeta i ne razjedinjujte se …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And hold fast, all of you together, to the cable of Allah, and do not separate” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… a ko se čvrsto drži Allaha, taj je upućen na pravi put“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ‚ko se drži Allaha‘.
why.en: “He who holdeth fast to Allah, he indeed is guided unto a right path” — ar-Rāġib cites ‘who holds fast to Allah’.

meaning.en: a haven, a place to flee to

nuance.bs: Mjesto u koje se bježi i sklanja. Ar-Rāġib nema posebnu natuknicu za ovaj korijen, ali samo ʿawḏ objašnjava njegovom imenicom (iltiǧāʾ – sklanjanje). U Kur'anu je riječ samo tri puta: munafici bi pohrlili u pribježište da ga nađu (9:57); od Allaha nema pribježišta osim kod Njega (9:118); a na onaj Dan ga nema (42:47).
nuance.en: A place one flees into and shelters in. Ar-Rāġib has no entry of its own for this root, but he explains ʿawḏ itself with its verbal noun (iltiǧāʾ — taking shelter). In the Quran the word is only three times: the hypocrites would turn to a refuge if they found one (9:57); there is none from Allah except in Him (9:118); and on that Day there is none (42:47).

why.bs: „… i shvatili su da nema pribježišta od Allaha osim kod Njega …“ – trojica koji su izostali iz pohoda; bijeg od Allaha vodi samo Njemu.
why.en: The three who stayed behind came to see that there is no haven from Allah except in Him — flight from Allah leads only to Him.

why.bs: „… tog Dana nećete imati pribježišta …“ – na Sudnjem danu nema mjesta u koje bi se pobjeglo.
why.en: On that Day there will be no haven to flee to — on the Day of Judgement there is no place of escape.

title.en: Breaking and going back on (a pledge)

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače ne održati preuzetu obavezu, a obje su posuđene iz rada rukama. Razlikuju se po slici: rasplesti ono što je čvrsto svezano ili sagrađeno, ili rašiti ispredeno i otkano.
shared.en: Both words mean failing to keep an obligation one has taken on, and both are borrowed from handiwork. They differ in the image: undoing what was tied or built firm, or unravelling what was spun and woven.

tellApart.bs: Raskinuti, rasplesti čvrsto svezano (uže, čvor, gradnju) – suprotno od ‚učvrstiti‘; u Kur'anu ugovor, zavjet, zakletve i pređa → نَقَضَ; pogaziti, rašiti otkano – blisko prvom; u Kur'anu zakletve, prisega i obećanja data u nevolji → نَكَثَ.
tellApart.en: Breaking, undoing what was tied firm (a rope, a knot, a building) — the opposite of ‘making fast’; in the Quran a covenant, a pact, oaths, and yarn → نَقَضَ; going back on, unravelling what was woven — close to the first; in the Quran oaths, a pledge of allegiance, and promises made in distress → نَكَثَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نقض, نكث
notes: ar-Rāġib (نقض): naqḍ is the coming apart of what was bound, of a building, a rope and a knot, the opposite of ibrām (making fast); naqḍ al-ʿahd is borrowed from undoing the rope and the knot; cites 8:56, 2:27, 16:91; munāqaḍa in speech; 94:3 anqaḍa ẓahrak: broke it so that it creaked. (نكث): nakṯ is the unravelling of garments and yarn, close to naqḍ, and borrowed for breaking a covenant; cites 9:12 and 7:135 / 43:50; nakṯ is like naqḍ, nakīṯa like naqīḍa.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 6 / 5 places read): نَقَضَ — the covenant of Allah (2:27, 13:25), the pact (13:20), their treaty (8:56), oaths after confirming them (16:91), and the woman who undid her yarn (16:92). نَكَثَ — oaths after their treaty (9:12, 9:13), a pledge of allegiance (48:10), and Pharaoh's people going back on their word each time the plague was lifted (7:135, 43:50). 16:92 holds both: نَقَضَتْ غَزْلَهَا … أَنكَاثًا, she undid her yarn into unravelled strands. Pickthall renders both verbs 'break': the نَكَثَ ayat are paraphrased in English. 48:10 mentions 'the Hand of Allah' — not quoted here.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): all claims OK.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, naqḍ je razvezivanje onoga što je bilo svezano – užeta, čvora, gradnje – suprotno od učvršćivanja (ibrām); odatle je posuđeno ‚raskinuti ugovor‘. Kur'an i sam pokazuje tu sliku: žena koja rasplete svoju pređu nakon što ju je čvrsto ispredla (16:92).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, naqḍ is the undoing of what was bound — a rope, a knot, a building — the opposite of making fast (ibrām); from there ‘breaking a covenant’ is borrowed. The Quran itself shows the image: the woman who undoes her yarn after spinning it strong (16:92).

why.bs: „I ne budite kao ona koja je raspredala svoju pređu, nakon što ju je čvrsto ispredla, u niti …“ – osnovna slika glagola, uz zakletve u istom odlomku.
why.en: “And be not like unto her who unravelleth the thread, after she hath made it strong, to thin filaments” — the verb's basic image, beside oaths in the same passage.

why.bs: „Oni koji raskidaju Allahov ugovor nakon što su ga potvrdili …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ‚koji raskidaju Allahov ugovor‘.
why.en: “Those who break the covenant of Allah after ratifying it” — ar-Rāġib cites ‘who break the covenant of Allah’.

meaning.en: to go back on (an oath, a pledge)

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, nakṯ je rašivanje otkanog ruha i pređe, blisko naqḍu, i posuđeno je za kršenje ugovora. U Kur'anu se odnosi na zakletve, na prisegu vjernosti i na riječ datu u nevolji: faraonov narod obećavao je vjerovati čim kazna prestane, pa bi to pogazio.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, nakṯ is the unravelling of woven cloth and yarn, close to naqḍ, and borrowed for breaking a covenant. In the Quran it is used of oaths, of a pledge of allegiance, and of a word given in distress: Pharaoh's people promised to believe as soon as the punishment was lifted, and then went back on it.

why.bs: Kad bi Allah od njih otklonio kaznu do roka do kojeg su imali stići, oni bi odmah pogazili datu riječ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: When Allah lifted the punishment from them for a term they were to reach, they at once went back on their word — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Ako pogaze svoje zakletve nakon ugovora i napadnu vašu vjeru … – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: If they go back on their oaths after their treaty and assail your religion … — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o kvarenju na Zemlji. Razlikuju se po širini: jedna je opća riječ za svako izlaženje iz ravnoteže i ispravnosti, druga uži, oštriji izraz za zlo koje se prepoznaje sudom, a ne čulima.
shared.en: Both words speak of corruption on the earth. They differ in breadth: one is the general word for any departure from balance and soundness, the other a narrower, sharper term for evil recognised by judgement rather than by the senses.

tellApart.bs: Pokvariti, izvesti iz ravnoteže – opća riječ, suprotna popravljanju (iṣlāḥ); u duši, tijelu, stvarima → أَفْسَدَ; bezobzirno zlo činiti – ar-Rāġib: kvarenje koje se prepoznaje sudom; u Kur'anu samo u zabrani ‚ne činite zlo na Zemlji kao smutljivci‘ → عَثَا.
tellApart.en: Corrupting, putting out of balance — the general word, the opposite of setting right (iṣlāḥ); in soul, body, things → أَفْسَدَ; doing wanton evil — ar-Rāġib: corruption recognised by judgement; in the Quran only in the ban ‘do not do evil on the earth, making mischief’ → عَثَا.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries فسد, عثى
notes: ar-Rāġib (فسد): fasād is a thing's departure from balance (iʿtidāl), whether little or much, the opposite of ṣalāḥ; used of the soul, the body and things that leave straightness; afsadahu ġayruhu; cites 23:71, 21:22, 30:41, 2:205, 2:11, 2:12, 27:34, 10:81, 2:220. (عثى): ʿayṯ and ʿuṯiyy are close (like ǧaḏaba / ǧabaḏa), except that ʿayṯ is said mostly of corruption perceived by the senses, ʿuṯiyy of what is perceived by judgement (ḥukman); on this 'wa-lā taʿṯaw fī l-arḍi mufsidīn'; also ʿaṯā yaʿṯū ʿuṯuwwan.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 15 / 5 places read): عَثَا (Form I) is in all five places the same prohibition, لَا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ — to the Israelites given water (2:60), to Thamud (7:74), to Midian (11:85, 26:183, 29:36) — always paired with the participle of أَفْسَدَ. أَفْسَدَ (Form IV) mostly with fī l-arḍ; its object is named in 27:34 (kings ruin a township). The pairing shows the two are not the same word: ʿuṯiyy is said with the state of being mufsid beside it.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, fasād je izlaženje nečega iz ravnoteže, malo ili mnogo, a suprotnost mu je ispravnost (ṣalāḥ); kaže se za dušu, tijelo i stvari. To je opća riječ: u Kur'anu najčešće ‚kvariti na Zemlji‘, uz suprotnost ‚popraviti‘.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, fasād is a thing's departure from balance, a little or much, and its opposite is soundness (ṣalāḥ); it is said of the soul, the body and things. It is the general word: in the Quran mostly ‘to make mischief on the earth’, against its opposite ‘to set right’.

why.bs: „I ne kvarite na Zemlji nakon što je ona uređena …“ – kvarenje kao narušavanje uspostavljenog reda.
why.en: “Work not confusion in the earth after the fair ordering (thereof)” — corruption as the undoing of an order set right.

why.bs: „Rekla je: ‚Kad vladari uđu u neko naselje, unište ga, a ugledne njegove stanovnike učine poniženim …‘“ – riječi kraljice Sabe; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “She said: Lo! kings, when they enter a township, ruin it and make the honour of its people shame” — the words of the Queen of Sheba; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ʿayṯ i ʿuṯiyy su bliski, ali ʿayṯ se najčešće kaže za kvarenje koje se opaža čulima, a ʿuṯiyy za ono što se prepoznaje sudom. U Kur'anu je glagol svih pet puta u istoj zabrani, uvijek uz ‚kao smutljivci‘ (mufsidīn) – zabrana bezobzirnog zla, a ne samo štete.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ʿayṯ and ʿuṯiyy are close, but ʿayṯ is said mostly of corruption perceived by the senses, ʿuṯiyy of what is recognised by judgement. In the Quran the verb is all five times in the same prohibition, always with ‘making mischief’ (mufsidīn) — a ban on wanton evil, not merely on damage.

why.bs: „O narode moj, dajte potpunu mjeru i tačnu vagu, po pravdi, ne oštećujte ljude u onome što im pripada i ne činite zlo na Zemlji kao smutljivci“ – Šuajb: zakidanje na mjeri je zlo koje se prepoznaje sudom.
why.en: “O my people! Give full measure and full weight in justice, and wrong not people in respect of their goods. And do not evil in the earth, causing corruption” — Shuʿayb: short measure is an evil recognised by judgement.

why.bs: „… jedite i pijte od Allahove opskrbe i ne činite zlo na Zemlji kao smutljivci“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovu formulu.
why.en: “Eat and drink of that which Allah hath provided, and do not act corruptly, making mischief in the earth” — ar-Rāġib cites this formula.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o dobru koje jedan daje drugome. Razlikuju se po težini i po onome što se čini: blagodat toliko velika da obavezuje primaoca – djelom ili, kod ljudi, prigovaranjem riječima – ili samo dobro koje se nekome uručuje.
shared.en: Both words speak of good that one gives to another. They differ in weight and in what is done: a favour so great that it lays an obligation on the receiver — by deed or, among people, by reminding in words — or simply good conveyed to someone.

tellApart.bs: Ukazati veliku, ‚tešku‘ milost – djelom (pravo samo Allahovo) ili riječima, kao prebacivanje (ružno među ljudima) → مَنَّ; darovati blagodat, uručiti dobro – kaže se samo za razumna bića kao primaoce → أَنْعَمَ.
tellApart.en: Bestowing a great, ‘weighty’ grace — by deed (truly Allah's alone) or by words, as reproach (ugly among people) → مَنَّ; conferring favour, conveying good — said only when the receiver is a rational being → أَنْعَمَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries منن, نعم
notes: ar-Rāġib (منن): minna is a heavy favour (an-niʿma aṯ-ṯaqīla), in two ways: by deed — manna fulān ʿalā fulān when he loads him with favour (3:164, 4:94, 37:114, 14:11, 28:5), and that in truth is only Allah's; and by word — ugly among people except when the favour is denied, hence 'the reminding of favour destroys the good deed' and 'when a favour is denied, the reminding becomes good'; 49:17: their minna is by word, Allah's minna on them by deed, His guiding them; 47:4 mannan = release without ransom; 38:39 fa-mnun = spend it; 74:6 explained two ways (qīla … wa-qīla); ġayr mamnūn explained (qīla) as 'uncounted' or 'not cut off'. (نعم): niʿma is the good state; inʿām is conveying good (iṣāl al-iḥsān) to another, said only when the receiver is of the rational kind — one does not say anʿama fulān ʿalā farasihi; cites 1:7, 33:37, 43:59.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 14 / 16 places read): مَنَّ has Allah as subject except where it is reminding by word: the Bedouins (49:17), and Moses' words to Pharaoh (26:22, read in tafsir in more than one way and not used here). أَنْعَمَ has Allah as subject everywhere but once (33:37, 'and thou hast favoured him', the Prophet to Zayd — not used as an illustration); always with ʿalā and a human receiver. 74:6 (said to the Prophet, read two ways) and 20:37 are not used as illustrations. Pickthall renders both verbs 'favour' in some places: 49:17 is paraphrased in English.

meaning.en: to bestow grace; to reproach with a favour

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, minna je ‚teška‘ blagodat, i ima dva vida: djelom – kad neko drugoga obaspe dobrom, a to je u pravom smislu samo Allahovo, kako Njemu priliči; i riječju – prebacivanje učinjenim dobrom, što je među ljudima ružno, osim kad se na blagodat uzvrati nezahvalnošću. U 49:17 su oba: njihovo je riječju, Allahovo djelom – uputa u vjeru.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, minna is a ‘weighty’ favour, and has two sides: by deed — when one loads another with good, and that in truth is only Allah's, as befits Him; and by word — reproaching with a favour done, which is ugly among people unless the favour is met with ingratitude. In 49:17 both are present: theirs by word, Allah's by deed — guidance to faith.

why.bs: „Allah je zaista učinio dobro vjernicima time što im je poslao Poslanika iz njihovih redova …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet kao minna djelom, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “Allah verily hath shown grace to the believers by sending unto them a messenger of their own” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah as minna by deed, as befits Him.

why.bs: „Računaju ti kao uslugu to što su prihvatili islam. Reci: ‚Ne računajte mi svoj islam kao uslugu, nego Allah vama čini dobro time što vas je uputio u iman …‘“ – ar-Rāġib: njihova minna je riječima, Allahova djelom.
why.en: They count their becoming Muslim as a favour done to the Prophet; he is told to answer that it is Allah who has shown them grace by guiding them to faith — ar-Rāġib: their minna is by word, Allah's by deed.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, inʿām je uručiti dobro drugome, i kaže se samo kad je primalac razumno biće – ne kaže se da je neko ‚darovao blagodat‘ svome konju. U Kur'anu glagol ide s ʿalā, a darovatelj je Allah (kako Njemu priliči) na svim mjestima osim 33:37.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, inʿām is conveying good to another, and it is said only when the receiver is a rational being — one does not say someone ‘conferred favour’ on his horse. In the Quran the verb takes ʿalā, and the giver is Allah (as befits Him) in every place but 33:37.

why.bs: „Put onih kojima si darovao blagodat, a ne onih na koje se gnjev spustio, niti onih koji su zalutali“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ‚kojima si darovao blagodat‘.
why.en: “The path of those whom Thou hast favoured; Not the (path) of those who earn Thine anger nor of those who go astray” — ar-Rāġib cites ‘whom Thou hast favoured’.

why.bs: „… Gospodaru moj, nadahni me da budem zahvalan na Tvojoj blagodati koju si darovao meni i mojim roditeljima …“ – Sulejman: blagodat koju čovjek prepoznaje i na kojoj zahvaljuje.
why.en: “My Lord, arouse me to be thankful for Thy favour wherewith Thou hast favoured me and my parents” — Solomon: a favour one recognises and gives thanks for.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače da se nešto unaprijed postavlja za nekoga. Razlikuju se po onome što se priprema: stvar spremljena da bude na raspolaganju kad zatreba, ili stanje stvari uređeno tako da bude kako treba.
shared.en: Both words mean setting something up for someone beforehand. They differ in what is prepared: a thing kept ready to be at hand when needed, or a state of affairs arranged to be as it should.

tellApart.bs: Pripremiti, spremiti da bude pri ruci – snagu za odbranu, opremu, a najčešće Džennet ili kaznu koje je Allah pripremio → أَعَدَّ; urediti, dati da se stvar dobro složi – u Kur'anu samo molitva i nada mladića iz pećine → هَيَّأَ.
tellApart.en: Making ready, keeping at hand — strength for defence, equipment, and most often the Garden or the punishment Allah has prepared → أَعَدَّ; setting right, letting an affair turn out well — in the Quran only the prayer and hope of the youths of the Cave → هَيَّأَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عد, هيأ
notes: ar-Rāġib (عد): iʿdād is from ʿadd (counting), as isqāʾ from saqy: aʿdadtu hāḏā laka = I made it such that you can count on it and take it as you need it; cites 8:60, 2:24, 9:100 and aʿtadnā (4:18, 25:11); 12:31 aʿtadat lahunna muttakaʾan 'is said to be from it'; ʿudda is much that is counted of wealth and weapons (9:46). (هيأ): hayʾa is the state a thing is in, sensed or understood, more often sensed (3:49 ka-hayʾati ṭ-ṭayr); muhāyaʾa is what people make ready for and agree on by estimate; cites 18:10 and 18:16.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 20 / 2 places read): أَعَدَّ (Form IV) — Allah prepares the Garden or reward (3:133, 9:89, 9:100, 33:29, 33:35, 33:44, 57:21) or punishment and the Fire (2:24, 3:131, 4:93, 4:102, 33:8, 33:57, 33:64, 48:6, 58:15, 65:10, 76:31); people make ready force (8:60) and equipment (9:46). هَيَّأَ (Form II) is only 18:10 (the youths' prayer) and 18:16 (their hope). Pickthall renders 18:16 'prepare': that ayah is not quoted. أَعْتَدَ (root عتد) is a different verb and not counted here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, iʿdād dolazi od brojanja: ‚pripremio sam ti ovo‘ znači učinio sam da na to možeš računati i uzeti ga kad ti zatreba. U Kur'anu ljudi pripremaju snagu i opremu, a najčešće je Allah Taj Koji priprema – Džennet ili kaznu – kako Njemu priliči.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, iʿdād comes from counting: ‘I made this ready for you’ means I made it so that you can count on it and take it when you need it. In the Quran people make ready strength and equipment, and most often it is Allah Who prepares — the Garden or the punishment — as befits Him.

why.bs: „I pripremite protiv njih koliko god možete snage i konja privezanih …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Make ready for them all thou canst of (armed) force and of horses tethered” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I požurite ka oprostu od vašeg Gospodara i Džennetu širokom kao nebesa i Zemlja, pripremljenom za bogobojazne“ – Džennet je spreman unaprijed, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “And vie one with another for forgiveness from your Lord, and for a paradise as wide as are the heavens and the earth, prepared for those who ward off (evil)” — the Garden is ready beforehand, as befits Him.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, hayʾa je stanje u kojem se stvar nalazi, a muhāyaʾa ono za što se ljudi spremaju i oko čega se dogovore; on navodi oba kur'anska mjesta. Riječ ne govori o spremljenoj stvari nego o uređenom stanju: da se nečija stvar složi kako treba.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, hayʾa is the state a thing is in, and muhāyaʾa what people make ready for and agree on; he cites both Quranic places. The word speaks not of a thing kept ready but of a state set right: that someone's affair comes together as it should.

why.bs: „… Gospodaru naš, daj nam milost od Sebe i uredi nam u našoj stvari pravi put“ – molitva mladića u pećini; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Our Lord! Give us mercy from Thy presence, and shape for us right conduct in our plight” — the prayer of the youths in the Cave; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Mladići se nadaju da će im Gospodar raširiti Svoju milost i urediti im u njihovoj stvari ono što olakšava – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: The youths hope that their Lord will spread His mercy for them and set right for them, in their plight, what eases it — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

title.en: Standing up and being made to stand

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o stajanju. Razlikuju se po tome ko stoji i zašto: ustati i stajati vlastitim kretanjem ili snagom (pa i ustati u nečemu, ostati postojan), ili biti zaustavljen i postavljen pred nekoga.
shared.en: Both words speak of standing. They differ in who stands and why: rising and standing by one's own movement or strength (and so standing to a task, staying steadfast), or being halted and set before someone.

tellApart.bs: Ustati, stajati, uspraviti se – i ljudi i Čas; kod ar-Rāġiba po izboru, po potčinjenosti, i u smislu ‚brinuti se o nečemu‘ → قَامَ; zaustaviti nekoga i postaviti ga – u Kur'anu sva tri puta prijelazno, o nevjernicima na Sudnjem danu → وَقَفَ.
tellApart.en: Rising, standing, standing upright — of people and of the Hour; in ar-Rāġib by choice, by subjection, and in the sense of ‘taking care of something’ → قَامَ; halting someone and setting him in place — in the Quran all three times transitive, of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgement → وَقَفَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries قوم, وقف
notes: ar-Rāġib (قوم): qiyām is of several kinds: standing of a person either by subjection (taṣḫīr, 11:100 qāʾim wa-ḥaṣīd, 59:5) or by choice (39:9, 3:191, 25:64); qiyām li-š-šayʾ is watching over and keeping it (5:8, 3:18, 13:33 'qāʾim ʿalā kulli nafs' = guarding it); and qiyām as resolve (5:6 iḏā qumtum ilā ṣ-ṣalāh); qiyāma is the rising of the Hour (30:12-type yawma taqūmu s-sāʿa, 83:6), said of what happens to a man's rising all at once; 4:142 qāmū kusālā is from qiyām, not iqāma. (وقف): waqaftu l-qawma aqifuhum waqfan, and wuqūf; cites 37:24 wa-qifūhum innahum masʾūlūn; waqf of a house (endowment) is borrowed from it; mawqif is where a man stands; muwāqafa is each one making his matter stand on what the other does.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 30 / 3 places read): وَقَفَ is never intransitive in the Quran: 37:24 'halt them' (an order about the wrongdoers), 6:27 and 6:30 passive, 'when they are made to stand' before the Fire / before their Lord. قَامَ is of people (to prayer 5:6, 4:142; at night 73:2, 73:20), of the Hour (30:12, 30:14, 30:55, 40:46, 45:27), of the Reckoning (14:41), of heaven and earth standing by His command (30:25), of the Spirit and the angels (78:38), and once 'stood still' in the dark (2:20). 83:6 (people stand for the Lord) and 6:30 (they are made to stand before their Lord) show the two words side by side. 9:84, 9:108, 73:2 and 74:2 (said to the Prophet) are not used as illustrations; 18:14 (qāmū, read in tafsir in more than one way) is not used.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: 83:6 says only that the plain verb is used there, not the passive of 6:30 (the rising itself is at Allah's call, 30:25); 2:238 bs re-translated ('Allahu predani').

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries قوم, وقف (2026-11-06): 14 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): Under 'watching over' he quotes كونوا قوامين لله شهداء بالقسط = 5:8; 4:135 (قوامين بالقسط شهداء لله) he quotes later, in the qayyima passage

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, qiyām je više vrsta: stajanje po potčinjenosti (biljka koja stoji) ili po izboru (čovjek u namazu), brižno održavanje nečega (‚qāʾim‘ nad nečim = onaj ko ga čuva) i odlučnost (‚kad ustanete na namaz‘). U Kur'anu ustaju ljudi, ali i ‚ustaje‘ Čas (Kijamet); jednom znači i zastati na mjestu, u mraku (2:20).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, qiyām is of several kinds: standing by subjection (a plant that stands) or by choice (a man in prayer), keeping and caring for something (‘qāʾim’ over a thing = the one who guards it) and resolve (‘when you rise for prayer’). In the Quran people rise, but the Hour also ‘rises’ (the Qiyāma); once it means stopping in one's place, in the dark (2:20).

why.bs: „Dana kad će ljudi stajati pred Gospodarom svjetova“ – ovdje je običan glagol ‚stajati‘ (yaqūmu), a ne pasiv ‚biti postavljen‘ kao u 6:30.
why.en: “The day when (all) mankind stand before the Lord of the Worlds?” — here the plain verb ‘stand’ (yaqūmu) is used, not the passive ‘are made to stand’ of 6:30.

why.bs: „Brižno čuvajte namaze, a osobito srednji, i stanite Allahu predani“ – stajanje po izboru, u ibadetu.
why.en: “Be guardians of your prayers, and of the midmost prayer, and stand up with devotion to Allah” — standing by choice, in worship.

why.bs: „… kad im zasvijetli, idu u njemu, a kad se nad njima smrači, zastanu …“ – ovdje qāma znači stati na mjestu, suprotno hodanju.
why.en: “As often as it flasheth forth for them they walk therein, and when it darkeneth against them they stand still” — here qāma means stopping in place, the opposite of walking.

nuance.bs: Kod ar-Rāġiba ‚waqaftu l-qawma‘ znači ‚zaustavio sam ljude‘, a mawqif je mjesto na kojem čovjek stoji. U Kur'anu je glagol sva tri puta prijelazan: nevjernici ne stoje sami, nego bivaju zaustavljeni i postavljeni – pred Vatru, pred svoga Gospodara – da budu pitani.
nuance.en: In ar-Rāġib ‘waqaftu l-qawma’ means ‘I halted the people’, and mawqif is the place where a man stands. In the Quran the verb is all three times transitive: the disbelievers do not stand by themselves, they are halted and set in place — before the Fire, before their Lord — to be questioned.

why.bs: „I zaustavite ih, oni će, zaista, biti pitani“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And stop them, for they must be questioned” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A kad bi samo vidio kad budu postavljeni pred svoga Gospodara …“ – nisu stali sami, nego su postavljeni; usporedi 83:6, gdje ljudi stoje.
why.en: “If thou couldst see when they are set before their Lord!” — they did not stand of themselves, they were set there; compare 83:6, where people stand.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi označavaju ono što se izgovori ili prenese. Razlikuju se po obimu i po onome šta ističu: jednu riječ ili izreku koja ima težinu, ono što je izrečeno (pa i ono što je samo u duši), ili kazivanje koje do čovjeka dođe sluhom ili objavom.
shared.en: All three words name what is spoken or passed on. They differ in scope and in what they stress: a single word or a pronouncement that carries weight, what is said (even what is only in the soul), or an account that reaches a person by hearing or revelation.

tellApart.bs: Riječ, izreka, pa i Allahova odredba (‚kelima Gospodara tvoga‘) → كَلِمَة; izrečeno uopće, i ono u duši, i ono što se nekome pripisuje → قَوْل; kazivanje, vijest koja dođe sluhom ili objavom – i Kur'an sebe tako naziva → حَدِيث.
tellApart.en: A word, a pronouncement, even Allah's decree (‘the word of your Lord’) → كَلِمَة; what is said in general, also what is in the soul, and what is ascribed to someone → قَوْل; an account, tidings that come by hearing or revelation — and the Quran calls itself so → حَدِيث.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries كلم, قول, حدث
notes: ar-Rāġib (كلم): kalām falls on the composed words and the meanings beneath them; for many theologians it is said only of a composed, meaningful sentence and is more specific than qawl, which they say also of single words, while kalima falls for them on each of the three kinds (noun, verb, particle); 'and the opposite has been said'. Cites 18:5 kaburat kalimatan. On 6:115 wa-tammat kalimatu rabbika: the kalima here is the decree (qaḍiyya), and every decree is called kalima, whether word or deed; other readings he reports with qīla (the Quran, the promise of reward and punishment). Jesus is called a kalima since he was brought into being by 'Be' (3:59), with other qīla readings. 4:46 yuḥarrifūna l-kalim: kalim is the plural of kalima; he prefers the reading that they distorted the meaning, not the words. (قول): qawl and qīl are one; its plainest use is the composed sounds brought out in speech, a single word or a sentence; also what is conceived in the soul before it is uttered (58:8 wa-yaqūlūna fī anfusihim), belief, inspiration (18:86); 'with their mouths' (3:167) shows it was a lie, not sound belief; 36:7 laqad ḥaqqa l-qawlu: Allah's knowledge of them and His word against them, like 'wa-tammat kalimatu rabbika'; 51:8 qawl muḫtalif: the matter of the resurrection, called qawl because what is spoken of is called qawl; 69:40 qawl rasūl: the speech is ascribed to the messenger who conveys it from the one who sent him — both ascriptions are right. (حدث): ḥudūṯ is a thing's coming to be after it was not; every speech that reaches a person by hearing or by revelation, awake or asleep, is called ḥadīṯ (66:3, 88:1, 12:101 taʾwīl al-aḥādīṯ = what one is told in sleep); Allah called His Book ḥadīṯ (52:34, 53:59, 4:87, 45:6, 6:68); 34:19 ǧaʿalnāhum aḥādīṯ = tales told of them.

Quranic usage (our observation): كَلِمَة (42) is summed with the collective plural كَلِم (4: 4:46, 5:13, 5:41, 35:10), which ar-Rāġib calls its plural; كَلَام (4) is left out of the count — in all four places (2:75, 7:144, 9:6, 48:15) it is Allah's speech. حَدِيث (all 28 places read) is the Quran in many places (7:185, 18:6, 39:23, 45:6, 52:34, 53:59, 56:81, 68:44, 77:50), and a story in the formula هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ (20:9, 51:24, 79:15, 85:17, 88:1). 52:34 is paraphrased: Pickthall's 'speech' is also his word for قَوْل in 69:40. Left out: 66:3 (the secret told to a wife — tafsir differs on what it was), 31:6 lahw al-ḥadīṯ (readings differ), 2:37 kalimāt of Adam (he reports several readings).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, kod mnogih teologa ‚kelima‘ se kaže za svaku vrstu riječi – imenicu, glagol, česticu. U kur'anskoj upotrebi to je često jedna izreka koja nosi težinu. ‚Kelima tvoga Gospodara‘ (6:115) on tumači kao Allahovu odredbu: svaka odredba zove se ‚kelima‘, bila riječ ili djelo – kako Njemu priliči.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, for many theologians ‘kalima’ is said of each kind of word — noun, verb, particle. In Quranic usage it is often a single pronouncement that carries weight. ‘The word of your Lord’ (6:115) he reads as Allah's decree: every decree is called ‘kalima’, whether word or deed — as befits Him.

why.bs: „Teška je riječ što im iz usta izlazi …“ – jedna izreka, a velika; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Dreadful is the word that cometh out of their mouths” — a single pronouncement, and a grave one; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I ispunila se riječ tvoga Gospodara, istinom i pravdom …“ – ar-Rāġib: ovdje je ‚kelima‘ Allahova odredba, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “Perfected is the Word of thy Lord in truth and justice” — ar-Rāġib: here ‘kalima’ is Allah's decree, as befits Him.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, qawl je najprije ono što se izgovori, jedna riječ ili rečenica; ali se kaže i za ono što je u duši prije nego se izgovori, za uvjerenje i za nadahnuće. Govor se može pripisati i onome ko ga prenosi: u 69:40 to je govor poslanika koji ga dostavlja od Onoga Koji ga je poslao.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, qawl is first what is uttered, a single word or a sentence; but it is also said of what is in the soul before it is uttered, of a belief and of inspiration. Speech can be ascribed to the one who conveys it: in 69:40 it is the speech of the messenger who delivers it from the One Who sent him.

why.bs: „To je, zaista, govor plemenitog poslanika“ – ar-Rāġib: govor se pripisuje poslaniku jer ga on dostavlja, a i Onome Koji ga je poslao; oboje je ispravno.
why.en: “That it is indeed the speech of an illustrious messenger” — ar-Rāġib: the speech is ascribed to the messenger because he conveys it, and also to the One Who sent him; both are right.

why.bs: „Već se nad većinom njih obistinio govor, pa oni ne vjeruju“ – ar-Rāġib: Allahovo znanje o njima i Njegova riječ protiv njih, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “Already hath the judgment … proved true of most of them, for they believe not” — ar-Rāġib: Allah's knowledge of them and His word against them, as befits Him.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, svaki govor koji do čovjeka dođe sluhom ili objavom, na javi ili u snu, zove se hadis – kazivanje; i Allah je Svoju Knjigu nazvao tako. U Kur'anu je to često Kur'an sam, a u formuli ‚Je li ti došlo kazivanje o …‘ priča o prošlim ili budućim događajima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, every speech that reaches a person by hearing or revelation, awake or asleep, is called ḥadīth — an account; and Allah named His Book so. In the Quran it is often the Quran itself, and in the formula ‘Has the account of … come to you?’ a story of past or coming events.

why.bs: „Je li ti stigla vijest o onome što sve prekriva?“ – kazivanje koje dolazi objavom; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Hath there come unto thee tidings of the Overwhelming?” — an account that comes by revelation; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Neka donesu kazivanje poput njega, ako istinu govore“ – Kur'an je ovdje nazvan hadisom; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: They are told to bring an account like it, if they are truthful — here the Quran is called ḥadīth; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A je li ti došlo kazivanje o Musau?“ – formula kojom počinje priča.
why.en: “Hath there come unto thee the story of Moses?” — the formula that opens a story.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o onome što nema vrijednosti. Razlikuju se po tome šta je u pitanju: govor koji se ne uzima u obzir jer je rečen bez razmišljanja, ili ono što je suprotno istini i ne opstaje kad se ispita – u riječi ili u djelu.
shared.en: Both words speak of what has no worth. They differ in what is meant: speech that is not counted because it was said without thought, or what is the opposite of truth and does not hold up when examined — in word or in deed.

tellApart.bs: Govor bez razmišljanja, koji se ne računa – i prazne zakletve; u Kur'anu uvijek govor → لَغْو; suprotnost istini, ono što nema postojanosti – lažna božanstva, nepravedno uzimanje imetka → بَاطِل.
tellApart.en: Speech without thought, not counted — also idle oaths; in the Quran always speech → لَغْو; the opposite of truth, what has no firmness — false gods, wealth taken wrongly → بَاطِل.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries لغا, بطل
notes: ar-Rāġib (لغا): laġw is speech that is not counted, said without deliberation or thought, like laġā, the chirping of sparrows and such birds; any ugly speech may be called laġw (78:35, 28:55, 56:25, 23:3); on 25:72 'they passed by laġw with dignity': they alluded to the ugly without saying it outright, or (qīla) they did not join those engaged in it; laġw in oaths is what has no binding intent, said from habit to link speech (2:225); 88:11 lāġiya = laġw. (بطل): al-bāṭil is the opposite of al-ḥaqq, what has no firmness when it is examined (31:30); said with regard to words and deeds; baṭala, abṭalahu (7:118 wa-baṭala mā kānū yaʿmalūn); 3:71 talbisūna l-ḥaqqa bi-l-bāṭil; ibṭāl is spoiling and removing a thing, true or false (8:8); mubṭil is one who says what has no reality (30:58), or who annuls the truth (40:78).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 9 / 25 places read): لَغْو is always speech: oaths said without intent (2:225, 5:89), what the believers turn from (23:3, 25:72, 28:55), and what is not heard in Paradise (19:62, 52:23, 56:25, 78:35). بَاطِل is said of what is called on besides Allah (22:62, 31:30, 29:52, 29:67), of falsehood against truth (2:42, 17:81, 21:18), and of deeds: consuming wealth wrongly (2:188, 4:29, 4:161, 9:34). Pickthall's 'vain' (laġw) and 'vanity' (bāṭil, 2:188) are kept apart by naming the member in brackets.
