nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, laġw je govor koji se ne uzima u obzir, rečen bez razmišljanja, kao cvrkut vrabaca; a može se nazvati tako i svaki ružan govor. Takva je i zakletva bez namjere, izrečena iz navike. U Kur'anu (svih 9 mjesta) to je uvijek govor: vjernici ga se klone, a u Džennetu se ne čuje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, laġw is speech that is not counted, said without thought, like the chirping of sparrows; and any ugly speech may also be called so. So too is an oath without intent, said out of habit. In the Quran (all 9 places) it is always speech: the believers shun it, and in Paradise it is not heard.

why.bs: „I koji se prazne priče klone“ – osobina vjernika; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And who shun vain conversation” — a trait of the believers; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Allah vas neće kazniti za ono što je prazno u vašim zakletvama …“ – zakletva bez namjere, rečena iz navike, kako ar-Rāġib objašnjava.
why.en: “Allah will not take you to task for that which is unintentional in your oaths” — an oath without intent, said out of habit, as ar-Rāġib explains.

why.bs: „U njemu neće slušati prazne priče, ni laži“ – o Džennetu; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “There hear they never vain discourse, nor lying” — of Paradise; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, bāṭil je suprotnost istini (ḥaqq): ono što nema postojanosti kad se ispita. Kaže se i za riječi i za djela. U Kur'anu to su lažna božanstva koja se mimo Allaha prizivaju, neistina koja nestaje pred istinom, i imetak uzet na nepravedan način.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, bāṭil is the opposite of truth (ḥaqq): what has no firmness when it is examined. It is said of words and of deeds. In the Quran it is the false gods called on besides Allah, falsehood that vanishes before truth, and wealth taken in a wrongful way.

why.bs: „… Allah je Istina, a ono što mimo Njega prizivaju – to je neistina …“ – ar-Rāġib za značenje riječi navodi gotovo isti ajet 31:30.
why.en: “Allah, He is the True, and that whereon they call instead of Him, it is the false” — ar-Rāġib cites the near-identical 31:30 for the meaning of the word.

why.bs: „… Došla je istina, a neistina je nestala …“ – ono što nema postojanosti ne opstaje.
why.en: “Truth hath come and falsehood hath vanished away” — what has no firmness does not last.

why.bs: „I ne jedite među sobom svoje imetke na ništavan način …“ – bāṭil u djelu, ne samo u riječi.
why.en: “And eat not up your property among yourselves in vanity [bāṭil]” — bāṭil in a deed, not only in a word.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o skrivenom govoru. Razlikuju se po tome gdje je govor: tajna koju čovjek nosi u sebi ili čini skriveno, ili govor koji se vodi nasamo, među nekolicinom, da ga drugi ne čuju.
shared.en: Both words speak of hidden speech. They differ in where the speech is: a secret a person keeps within or does in hiding, or talk held apart, among a few, so that others do not hear it.

tellApart.bs: Ono što je skriveno u duši, suprotno javnom – i dijeljenje imetka tajno → سِرّ; govor nasamo među dvojicom ili više njih → نَجْوَى.
tellApart.en: What is hidden in the soul, the opposite of the open — also giving wealth in secret → سِرّ; talk held apart between two or more → نَجْوَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries سرر, نجو
notes: ar-Rāġib (سرر): isrār is the opposite of iʿlān (2:274 sirran wa-ʿalāniyatan; 16:23 yaʿlamu mā yusirrūna wa-mā yuʿlinūn); it is used of things and of meanings; sirr is speech kept hidden in the soul (الحديث المكتم في النفس), citing 20:7 yaʿlamu s-sirra wa-aḫfā and 9:78 sirrahum wa-naǧwāhum; asrartu ilā fulān: confiding to someone, which is disclosure to him and hiding from others (60:1). (نجو): the root is separation; nāǧaytuhu = I spoke with him in secret, its origin being to be alone with him on a raised ground (naǧwa), or (qīla) from rescue, or that you rescue your secret from being known; naǧwā is in origin a verbal noun (58:10 innamā n-naǧwā mina š-šayṭān, 58:8, 58:12); on 21:3 wa-asarrū n-naǧwā: they did not disclose it in any way, since a naǧwā may come out later; naǧwā is also said of the people (17:47 wa-iḏ hum naǧwā).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 11 / 11 places read): سِرّ is what Allah knows (6:3, 9:78, 20:7, 25:6, 43:80), giving in secret and openly (2:274, 13:22, 14:31, 35:29, 16:75) and a secret promise (2:235). نَجْوَى is talk between people: of three or five (58:7), of conspirators (20:62, 21:3), forbidden whispering (58:8, 58:10), the talk with the Prophet (58:12–13), and 4:114 (no good in much of it). 9:78 and 43:80 hold both words side by side. 58:7 has Pickthall's 'secret conference': the member is named in brackets.

Give the unvowelled Arabic instead. 58:12 is cited under ناجيتم, before the verbal-noun remark

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, sirr je govor sakriven u duši, a isrār je suprotnost javnom (iʿlān). U Kur'anu je to ono što Allah zna i od čega je skrivenije – kako Njemu priliči – i dijeljenje imetka tajno i javno.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, sirr is speech hidden in the soul, and isrār is the opposite of the open (iʿlān). In the Quran it is what Allah knows, and what is more hidden still — as befits Him — and giving wealth in secret and openly.

why.bs: „… On zna tajnu i ono što je još skrivenije“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “He knoweth the secret (thought) and (that which is yet) more hidden” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Oni koji dijele imetke svoje noću i danju, tajno i javno …“ – tajno, kao suprotnost javnom; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj par riječi.
why.en: “Those who spend their wealth by night and day, by stealth and openly” — in secret, as the opposite of openly; ar-Rāġib cites this pair of words.

why.bs: „Zar ne znaju da Allah zna njihovu tajnu i njihovo došaptavanje …“ – obje riječi zajedno: ono u duši i ono nasamo rečeno.
why.en: “Allah knoweth both their secret and the thought that they confide” — both words together: what is in the soul and what is said apart.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, munāǧāt je razgovor nasamo; porijeklo mu je, kaže, osamiti se s nekim na uzvišenom mjestu (naǧwa), a navodi i druga objašnjenja. Naǧwā je prvobitno glagolska imenica, a kaže se i za same ljude koji se došaptavaju (17:47). U Kur'anu to je uvijek govor među ljudima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, munāǧāt is talk held apart; its origin, he says, is to be alone with someone on a raised place (naǧwa), and he also gives other explanations. Naǧwā is in origin a verbal noun, and it is also said of the people who confer (17:47). In the Quran it is always talk among people.

why.bs: „… Nema došaptavanja trojice a da On nije četvrti …“ – Allah zna i ono što se govori nasamo, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “There is no secret conference [najwā] of three but He is their fourth” — Allah knows even what is said apart, as befits Him.

why.bs: „… I nasamo su se došaptavali …“ – ar-Rāġib: nisu to ni na koji način otkrili, jer se došaptavanje ponekad kasnije otkrije.
why.en: “And they confer in secret” — ar-Rāġib: they did not disclose it in any way, since such counsel sometimes comes out later.

why.bs: „Nema dobra u mnogim njihovim došaptavanjima, osim kod onoga ko naređuje sadaku, dobro ili mirenje među ljudima …“
why.en: “There is no good in much of their secret conferences save (in) him who enjoineth almsgiving and kindness and peace-making among the people.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi su Allahova imena koja govore o Njegovom znanju, kako Njemu priliči. Razlikuju se po onome što ističu: znanje o stvari kakva jeste, ili upućenost u ono što se zbiva i u nutrinu stvari.
shared.en: Both words are names of Allah that speak of His knowledge, as befits Him. They differ in what they stress: knowing a thing as it truly is, or being informed of what takes place and of the inner side of things.

tellApart.bs: Onaj Koji zna sve, svaku stvar kakva jeste; često uz ‚Mudri‘ i ‚Onaj Koji čuje‘; kaže se i za ljude (učen sihirbaz, učen dječak) → عَلِيم; Onaj Koji je upućen u vijesti o djelima i u nutrinu stvari; često ‚o onome što radite‘; u Kur'anu gotovo uvijek o Allahu → خَبِير.
tellApart.en: The One Who knows everything, each thing as it is; often beside ‘the Wise’ and ‘the Hearer’; also said of people (a learned sorcerer, a knowing boy) → عَلِيم; the One informed of the reports of deeds and of inner things; often ‘of what you do’; in the Quran almost always of Allah → خَبِير.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries علم, خبر
notes: ar-Rāġib (علم): ʿilm is grasping a thing as it truly is (idrāk aš-šayʾ bi-ḥaqīqatihi), of two kinds: grasping the thing itself, and judging something of it; ʿalīm is the intensive form; on 12:76 wa-fawqa kulli ḏī ʿilmin ʿalīm: ʿalīm may point to a person above another (more knowing relative to him, though not to the one above him), or to Allah, though indefinite, since the One truly described as al-ʿAlīm is He; ʿallām al-ġuyūb (5:109): nothing hidden is hidden from Him. (خبر): ḫubr is knowledge of known things by way of report (ḫabar); qīla ḫibra is knowledge of the inner side of matters; on wa-llāhu ḫabīrun bimā taʿmalūn: knowing the reports of your deeds, or (qīla) knowing the inner side of your affairs, or (qīla) ḫabīr in the sense of the one who informs (cf. 'fa-yunabbiʾukum bimā kuntum taʿmalūn').

Quranic usage (our observation, all 45 places of خَبِير and the 163 of عَلِيم listed): خَبِير is Allah in every place read (25:59 'ask about Him one who is informed' and 35:14 are read by most mufassirun of Allah too; some read 25:59 of a knowing person); 23 of its 45 places carry 'bimā taʿmalūn / yaʿmalūn / taṣnaʿūn' (of what you do), and it stands beside laṭīf in 5 (6:103, 22:63, 31:16, 33:34, 67:14). عَلِيم stands with ḥakīm in about 36 ayat and with samīʿ in about 32; only 7 carry 'of what you do'; it is said of people in 7:109, 7:112, 10:79, 26:34 (a skilled sorcerer), 12:55 (Joseph), 15:53 and 51:28 (the promised son), and 12:76 is read two ways (his two readings). 66:3 (nabbaʾaniya l-ʿalīmu l-ḫabīr, both names) is left out: tafsir differs on the secret it concerns.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, znanje (ʿilm) je spoznati stvar onakvom kakva uistinu jeste, a ʿalīm je pojačani oblik. Uistinu je ‚al-ʿAlīm‘ samo Allah – kako Njemu priliči; ali Kur'an tako naziva i ljude: učene sihirbaze, Jusufa, obećanog dječaka. Često stoji uz ‚Mudri‘ i ‚Onaj Koji čuje‘.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, knowledge (ʿilm) is grasping a thing as it truly is, and ʿalīm is the intensive form. Truly ‘al-ʿAlīm’ is Allah alone — as befits Him; but the Quran also calls people so: learned sorcerers, Joseph, the promised boy. It often stands beside ‘the Wise’ and ‘the Hearer’.

why.bs: „… i On sve zna“ – znanje o svakoj stvari, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “And He is knower of all things” — knowledge of every thing, as befits Him.

why.bs: „… a iznad svakog onog ko ima znanje ima još učeniji“ – ar-Rāġib daje dva čitanja: čovjek učeniji od drugoga, ili Allah, Kojem jedinom uistinu pripada to ime.
why.en: “Over every lord of knowledge there is one more knowing” — ar-Rāġib gives two readings: a person more knowing than another, or Allah, to Whom alone the name truly belongs.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḫubr je znanje o stvarima koje dolazi kao vijest (ḫabar); neki kažu da je to poznavanje nutrine stvari. ‚Allah je upućen u ono što radite‘ znači, kaže on, da zna vijesti o vašim djelima – ili, prema drugima, nutrinu vaših stvari. U Kur'anu je to gotovo uvijek Allah, kako Njemu priliči; u gotovo polovini mjesta uz ‚u ono što radite‘.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ḫubr is knowledge of things that comes as report (ḫabar); some say it is knowing the inner side of things. ‘Allah is aware of what you do’ means, he says, that He knows the reports of your deeds — or, according to others, the inner side of your affairs. In the Quran it is almost always Allah, as befits Him; in nearly half of its places with ‘of what you do’.

why.bs: „… a Allah je upućen u ono što radite“ – ar-Rāġib: zna vijesti o vašim djelima, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “And Allah is Informed of what ye do” — ar-Rāġib: He knows the reports of your deeds, as befits Him.

why.bs: „Zar da ne zna Onaj Koji je stvorio, a On je Blagi, Upućeni?“ – uz ‚Blagi‘ (al-Laṭīf): upućen i u ono što je najsitnije i najskrivenije, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “Should He not know what He created? And He is the Subtile, the Aware.” — beside ‘the Subtle’ (al-Laṭīf): aware even of what is finest and most hidden, as befits Him.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o onome ko je nad nečim i zna šta se zbiva – i o Allahu, kako Njemu priliči, i o ljudima i melecima. Razlikuju se po tome šta ističu: prisutnost i svjedočenje, bdijenje i motrenje, ili čuvanje i staranje.
shared.en: All three words speak of one who is over something and knows what happens — of Allah, as befits Him, and of people and angels. They differ in what they stress: presence and testimony, watching and observing, or keeping and taking care.

tellApart.bs: Prisutan koji vidi, okom ili uvidom, pa svjedoči; i šehid → شَهِيد; onaj koji bdije i motri nad nekim → رَقِيب; čuvar koji pazi i odgovara za nešto – ‚nisam vam ja čuvar‘ → حَفِيظ.
tellApart.en: One present who sees, by eye or insight, and so testifies; also the martyr → شَهِيد; one who keeps watch over someone → رَقِيب; a keeper who guards and is answerable for something — ‘I am not a keeper over you’ → حَفِيظ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries شهد, رقب, حفظ
notes: ar-Rāġib (شهد): šuhūd and šahāda are presence with witnessing, by sight or by insight; šahāda is a statement that comes from knowledge gained by such witnessing; šahīd is said of the witness and of the one who sees a thing; 50:21 sāʾiq wa-šahīd: one who testifies for or against him; 4:41 'from every nation a witness'; 50:37 wa-huwa šahīd: they witness with their hearts what they hear; 'Allah is witness over everything' and 'wa-kafā bi-llāhi šahīdan' point to 'nothing of them is hidden from Allah' (40:16); the martyr is called šahīd because the angels are present with him (41:30), or because he sees what is prepared for him, or because the souls of the martyrs are present with Allah (3:169). (رقب): raqaba is the neck; raqabtuhu = I guarded him; raqīb is the guardian (al-ḥāfiẓ), either because he watches the neck of the one guarded or because he raises his own neck; cites 11:93 'watch, I am watching with you' and 50:18 raqībun ʿatīd; marqab is the high place the watcher looks down from. (حفظ): ḥifẓ is a state of the soul that keeps what understanding brings, then any looking after, tending and care (15:9, 2:238); 4:80 fa-mā arsalnāka ʿalayhim ḥafīẓan = a keeper, like 'you are not a tyrant over them' and 'not a guardian (wakīl) over them'; 50:4 kitāb ḥafīẓ: keeping their deeds, or itself kept, nothing lost.

Quranic usage (our observation): شَهِيد (47 ayat read; the count sums the singular and šuhadāʾ) is Allah witness over all (e.g. 3:98, 5:117, 85:9), the witnesses of the nations and of contracts (2:282, 4:41, 24:4), and the martyrs (3:140, 4:69, 57:19). رَقِيب (all 5 read) is Allah in 4:1, 5:117, 33:52, Shuʿayb in 11:93, and the recording angel in 50:18. حَفِيظ (all 12 read; the count includes ḥafaẓa, the guardian angels, 6:61) is Allah (11:57, 34:21, 42:6), the prophet who is not made a keeper over people (4:80, 6:104, 6:107, 11:86, 42:48), Joseph (12:55), the Book (50:4) and the one who keeps (Allah's command) in 50:32. 5:117 holds šahīd and raqīb side by side. The ayat said to the Prophet (4:80, 6:107, 42:48) are not quoted: 11:86 (Shuʿayb) shows the same formula. 12:55 is paraphrased: Pickthall renders ḥafīẓ ʿalīm as one phrase.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: his third reason for the name šahīd added (their souls are present with Allah); 5:117 bs re-translated.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries شهد, رقب, حفظ (2026-11-06): 19 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/2/nuance (reworded): He discusses 4:80 (fa-mā arsalnāka ʿalayhim ḥafīẓan), not 'I am not a keeper over you' (6:104/11:86), and glosses it only as ḥāfiẓ; 'not answerable for you' is not his

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, šuhūd je biti prisutan uz viđenje, okom ili uvidom, a šahāda je izjava koja proizlazi iz takvog znanja. Kad se kaže da je Allah svjedok svega, to znači, kaže on, da Mu ništa od njih nije skriveno – kako Njemu priliči. Šehid je nazvan tako, kaže on, jer su meleki prisutni uz njega, ili jer vidi šta mu je pripremljeno, ili jer su njihove duše prisutne kod Allaha.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, šuhūd is being present with seeing, by eye or by insight, and šahāda is a statement that comes from such knowledge. When Allah is said to be witness over everything, it means, he says, that nothing of them is hidden from Him — as befits Him. The martyr is called šahīd, he says, because the angels are present with him, or because he sees what is prepared for him, or because their souls are present with Allah.

why.bs: „Pa kako će biti kad od svake zajednice dovedemo svjedoka …“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “When We bring of every people a witness” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… a Allah je svemu svjedok“ – ništa Mu nije skriveno, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “And Allah is of all things the Witness” — nothing is hidden from Him, as befits Him.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, raqīb je čuvar koji motri; riječ je od raqaba, vrat: ili zato što pazi na vrat onoga koga čuva, ili zato što podiže svoj vrat da gleda. U Kur'anu je to Allah, kako Njemu priliči, melek koji bilježi govor, i Šuajb koji sa svojim narodom čeka ishod.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, raqīb is a guardian who keeps watch; the word is from raqaba, the neck: either because he watches over the neck of the one he guards, or because he raises his own neck to look. In the Quran it is Allah, as befits Him, the angel who records speech, and Shuʿayb waiting with his people for the outcome.

why.bs: „Ne izgovori on nijednu riječ, a da uz njega nije nadzornik spreman“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “He uttereth no word but there is with him an observer ready” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… Dok sam bio kod njih, bio sam njihov svjedok; a kad si me preuzeo, Ti si bio Nadzornik nad njima …“ – Isa razlikuje dvije riječi: svjedok je bio dok je bio prisutan, a Allah je nadzornik nad njima, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “I was a witness of them while I dwelt among them, and when Thou tookest me Thou wast the Watcher over them” — Jesus sets the two words apart: he was a witness while present, and Allah is the Watcher over them, as befits Him.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḥifẓ je najprije pamćenje, a zatim svako staranje, paženje i čuvanje. ‚Nismo te poslali da im budeš čuvar‘ (4:80) on poredi s ‚nisi ti nad njima silnik‘ i ‚nisi im nadglednik (wakīl)‘. U Kur'anu je to Allah, kako Njemu priliči, Jusuf nad riznicama zemlje, i Knjiga koja čuva djela.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ḥifẓ is first retaining in memory, then any looking after, tending and keeping. He likens ‘We have not sent you as a keeper over them’ (4:80) to ‘you are not a tyrant over them’ and ‘you are not a guardian (wakīl) over them’. In the Quran it is Allah, as befits Him, Joseph over the storehouses of the land, and the Book that keeps the deeds.

why.bs: „… a ja vam nisam čuvar“ – Šuajbove riječi: on dostavlja poruku, a ne odgovara za njihova djela.
why.en: “And I am not a keeper over you” — Shuʿayb's words: he conveys the message, he is not answerable for their deeds.

why.bs: „Postavi me nad riznicama zemlje, ja sam čuvar, znalac“ – Jusuf traži da bude postavljen nad riznicama: zna ih čuvati i zna njima upravljati.
why.en: Joseph asks to be set over the storehouses of the land, saying that he is a keeper (ḥafīẓ) and knowing (ʿalīm): he can guard them and knows how to manage them.

why.bs: „… a kod Nas je Knjiga koja čuva“ – ar-Rāġib: Knjiga koja čuva njihova djela, ili koja je sama sačuvana, ništa se ne gubi.
why.en: “With Us is a recording Book” — ar-Rāġib: a Book that keeps their deeds, or that is itself kept, nothing lost.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o tome da je nešto jednako nečemu drugom. Razlikuju se po tome u čemu je ta jednakost: u bilo kojem pogledu, u samoj suštini, ili u položaju i mjeri. Kur'an sve tri koristi i da zaniječe da je išta jednako Allahu.
shared.en: All three words speak of one thing being equal to another. They differ in what the equality lies in: in any respect at all, in the very substance, or in rank and measure. The Quran uses all three also to deny that anything is equal to Allah.

tellApart.bs: Sličnost u bilo kojem pogledu – najopćenitija riječ; ‚ništa nije poput Njega‘ → مِثْل; takmac koji dijeli suštinu – ‚ne činite Allahu takmace‘ → أَنْدَاد; ravan po položaju i mjeri → كُفُو.
tellApart.en: Likeness in any respect — the most general word; ‘nothing is like Him’ → مِثْل; a rival sharing the substance — ‘do not set up rivals to Allah’ → أَنْدَاد; equal in rank and measure → كُفُو.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries مثل, ندد, كفؤ
notes: ar-Rāġib (مثل): miṯl is said in two ways: like maṯal (likeness), and as likeness to another in any meaning whatever — the most general of the words set for likeness: nidd is said of sharing in substance only, šibh in quality only, musāwī in quantity only, šakl in measure and extent only, and miṯl covers all of these; so when Allah willed to deny likeness in every respect He named it: 42:11 laysa ka-miṯlihi šayʾ (the kāf with miṯl for emphasis, or miṯl there meaning 'attribute' — both reported with qīla). (ندد): the nadīd of a thing is what shares its substance, a kind of likeness, since miṯl is said of any sharing at all: 'every nidd is a miṯl, but not every miṯl is a nidd'; cites 2:22, 2:165, 41:9. (كفؤ): kufʾ is equality in rank and measure (fī l-manzila wa-l-qadr): one is kufʾ to another in marriage or in fighting; cites 112:4 wa-lam yakun lahu kufuwan aḥad; mukāfaʾa is equality and requital in an act.

Quranic usage (our observation): أَنْدَاد (all 6 places read) is always what people set up as rivals to Allah (2:22, 2:165, 14:30, 34:33, 39:8, 41:9). كُفُو is only 112:4. مِثْل (74 ayat) is of every kind of likeness: the challenge to bring the like of the Quran (2:23, 10:38, 11:13, 17:88, 52:34), a recompense like the deed (6:160, 42:40), and 42:11. The count of مِثْل is the corpus's; ka-miṯlihi in 42:11 is the one ar-Rāġib discusses.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, miṯl je najopćenitija riječ za sličnost: obuhvata sličnost u suštini, u svojstvu, u količini i u mjeri. Zato je Allah, kad je htio zanijekati svaku sličnost s Njim, upotrijebio upravo nju: ‚ništa nije poput Njega‘ (42:11).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, miṯl is the most general word for likeness: it covers likeness in substance, in quality, in quantity and in measure. So when Allah willed to deny every likeness to Him, He used just this word: ‘nothing is as His likeness’ (42:11).

why.bs: „… Ništa nije poput Njega; On je Onaj Koji čuje i vidi“ – ar-Rāġib: zanijekana je sličnost u svakom pogledu.
why.en: “Naught is as His likeness; and He is the Hearer, the Seer” — ar-Rāġib: likeness in every respect is denied.

why.bs: „… kad bi se ljudi i džini okupili da donesu nešto poput ovog Kur'ana, ne bi donijeli nešto poput njega …“
why.en: “Though mankind and the jinn should assemble to produce the like of this Qur'an, they could not produce the like thereof”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, nidd je ono što s nečim dijeli samu suštinu; to je vrsta sličnosti, pa je ‚svaki nidd miṯl, a nije svaki miṯl nidd‘. U Kur'anu (svih 6 mjesta) to su uvijek takmaci koje ljudi postavljaju Allahu – kao da im pripada ono što pripada samo Njemu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a nidd is what shares the very substance of a thing; it is a kind of likeness, so ‘every nidd is a miṯl, but not every miṯl is a nidd’. In the Quran (all 6 places) they are always rivals that people set up to Allah — as if what belongs to Him alone belonged to them.

why.bs: „… zato ne činite Allahu takmace, a vi znate“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And do not set up rivals to Allah when ye know (better)” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Ima ljudi koji pored Allaha uzimaju sebi takmace i ljube ih ljubavlju kakvom se ljubi Allah …“ – takmac kome se daje ljubav koja pripada samo Allahu.
why.en: “Yet of mankind are some who take unto themselves (objects of worship which they set as) rivals to Allah, loving them with a love like (that which is the due) of Allah (only)” — a rival given the love that is due to Allah alone.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, kufʾ je jednakost u položaju i mjeri: kaže se da je neko ravan drugome u braku ili u borbi. U Kur'anu dolazi samo jednom, u suri al-Iḫlāṣ: niko Allahu nije ravan.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, kufʾ is equality in rank and measure: one is said to be another's equal in marriage or in fighting. In the Quran it comes only once, in Sura al-Iḫlāṣ: no one is equal to Allah.

why.bs: „I nema nikoga ko bi Mu bio ravan“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And there is none comparable unto Him” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače da nešto nije teško. Razlikuju se po slici koju nose: lahkoća kao suprotnost tegobi (pa i nešto malo), ili nešto lagano, bez težine – pa i ono što ljudi olahko shvate.
shared.en: Both words mean that something is not hard. They differ in the image they carry: ease as the opposite of hardship (and also something small), or something light, without weight — even what people take lightly.

tellApart.bs: Lahko, suprotno teškom; i malo, neznatno – ‚to je Allahu lahko‘ → يَسِير; lagano, bez težine; i ono što se smatra sitnicom – ‚to je Meni lagano‘ → هَيِّن.
tellApart.en: Easy, the opposite of hard; also little, slight — ‘that is easy for Allah’ → يَسِير; light, without weight; also what is counted a trifle — ‘it is light for Me’ → هَيِّن.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries يسر, هان
notes: ar-Rāġib (يسر): yusr is the opposite of ʿusr (2:185, 65:7); yasīr and maysūr are what is easy (17:28 qawlan maysūran); yasīr is also said of a small thing: in the first sense 33:30 'and that is easy for Allah' and 'inna ḏālika ʿalā llāhi yasīr'; in the second 33:14 'they would have tarried in it but little'. (هان): hawān is of two kinds: a person's humbling himself in a way that brings no disgrace, which is praised (25:63 yamšūna ʿalā l-arḍi hawnan), and humiliation from one who has power and holds him light, which is blamed (46:20 ʿaḏāb al-hūn, 22:18); and 'hāna l-amru ʿalā fulān' = it was easy for him: 19:9 huwa ʿalayya hayyin, 30:27 wa-huwa ahwanu ʿalayh, 24:15 wa-taḥsabūnahu hayyinan.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 15 / 4 places read): يَسِير is mostly 'easy for Allah / for Us' (4:30, 4:169, 22:70, 29:19, 33:30, 35:11, 50:44, 57:22, 64:7), also an easy reckoning (84:8), 'not easy' (74:10), and small or short (12:65, 25:46, 33:14, 33:20). The هَيِّن member sums هَيِّن (3: 19:9, 19:21, 24:15) with the comparative أَهْوَن (30:27), which ar-Rāġib cites beside it. The link between hayyin 'easy' and the 'lowliness' of its root is not his: he only files the sense in the same entry; 'light, of no weight' is our gloss, borne out by 24:15 (thought light, but great with Allah). Pickthall gives both members 'easy': the member is named in brackets.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: 84:8 bs re-translated; bs genitive 'Jahje'.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries يسر, هان (2026-11-06): 12 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/nuance (reworded): He glosses hāna l-amru with سهل 'easy'; notes/1 itself says 'light' is our gloss, so it should not sit inside his gloss. bs 'lagana' covers both and can stay

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, yusr je suprotnost tegobi (ʿusr), a yasīr je ono što je lahko; kaže se i za nešto malo. U Kur'anu najčešće: ‚to je Allahu lahko‘ – kako Njemu priliči; ali i lahko polaganje računa, i kratko vrijeme.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, yusr is the opposite of hardship (ʿusr), and yasīr is what is easy; it is also said of something small. In the Quran mostly: ‘that is easy for Allah’ — as befits Him; but also an easy reckoning, and a short while.

why.bs: „… To je Nama lahko sabiranje“ – o proživljenju; lahko, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “That is a gathering easy [yasīr] for Us (to make)” — of the resurrection; easy, as befits Him.

why.bs: „… taj će biti obračunat lahkim obračunom“ – lahkoća za čovjeka.
why.en: “He truly will receive an easy [yasīr] reckoning” — ease for a human being.

why.bs: „… i ne bi se u tome zadržali osim malo“ – ar-Rāġib: drugo značenje, ‚malo‘.
why.en: “And would have hesitated thereupon but little” — ar-Rāġib: the second sense, ‘little’.

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib ovo značenje (‚stvar mu je bila lagana‘) navodi u natuknici o poniznosti i poniženju (hawān), i za njega citira 19:9, 30:27 i 24:15. U Kur'anu dva puta: ‚to je Meni lagano‘ – Allahove riječi o rođenju Jahje i Isaa, kako Njemu priliči; i jednom ono što su ljudi smatrali sitnicom, a kod Allaha je veliko.
nuance.en: Ar-Rāġib gives this sense (‘the matter was easy for him’) in his entry on humility and humiliation (hawān), and cites 19:9, 30:27 and 24:15 for it. In the Quran twice: ‘it is light for Me’ — Allah's words on the birth of John and of Jesus, as befits Him; and once what people counted a trifle, though with Allah it is great.

why.bs: „… Gospodar tvoj kaže: ‚To je Meni lagano, a i tebe sam prije stvorio, a nisi bio ništa‘“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Thy Lord saith: It is easy [hayyin] for Me, even as I created thee before, when thou wast naught” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… i smatrali ste to sitnicom, a to je kod Allaha veliko“ – lagano u očima ljudi, teško kod Allaha.
why.en: “Ye counted it a trifle. In the sight of Allah it is very great.” — light in people's eyes, weighty with Allah.

why.bs: „On je Taj Koji stvaranje započinje, pa ga ponavlja, i to Mu je još lakše …“ – poredbeni oblik iste riječi (ahwan); ar-Rāġib ga navodi uz nju; kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “He it is Who produceth creation, then reproduceth it, and it is easier for Him” — the comparative of the same word (ahwan); ar-Rāġib cites it beside it; as befits Him.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače nešto lijepo i poželjno. Razlikuju se po mjeri i po onome što opisuju: obilna ljepota, u Kur'anu uvijek ljepota postupka, ili dobro u najširem smislu – ono što razum, duša ili oko smatraju lijepim.
shared.en: Both words mean something fine and desirable. They differ in measure and in what they describe: abundant beauty, in the Quran always the beauty of a way of acting, or good in the widest sense — what reason, the soul or the eye find fine.

tellApart.bs: Obilna ljepota; pridjev u Kur'anu uvijek o postupku: lijepo strpljenje, lijepo praštanje, lijepo rastajanje → جَمِيل; dobro, lijepo u bilo kojem pogledu – dobar zajam, dobra opskrba, dobro obećanje → حَسَن.
tellApart.en: Abundant beauty; the adjective in the Quran always of a way of acting: beautiful patience, beautiful forbearance, a beautiful parting → جَمِيل; good, fine in any respect — a goodly loan, good provision, a good promise → حَسَن.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries جمل, حسن
notes: ar-Rāġib (جمل): ǧamāl is much beauty (al-ḥusn al-kaṯīr), of two kinds: beauty proper to a person in himself, his body or his deed, and beauty that reaches others from him; he cites the hadith 'Allah is beautiful and loves beauty' as pointing to the many goods that flow from Him; cites 16:6 wa-lakum fīhā ǧamāl, 12:18 fa-ṣabrun ǧamīl, 70:5 fa-ṣbir ṣabran ǧamīlan. (حسن): ḥusn is everything delightful and desired, of three kinds: found fine by reason, by desire (hawā), and by the senses; ḥasan is said of things and of events; in common usage ḥasan is mostly what is found fine by the eye, but 'most of what comes in the Quran of ḥasan is what is found fine by insight (baṣīra)'; cites 39:18 aḥsanahu, 2:83 qūlū li-n-nāsi ḥusnan, 29:8.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 7 / 20 places read): جَمِيل is always a way of acting: patience (12:18, 12:83, 70:5), forbearance (15:85), releasing a wife (33:28, 33:49), keeping away (73:10). حَسَن is a goodly loan to Allah (2:245, 5:12, 57:11, 57:18, 64:17, 73:20), good provision (11:88, 16:67, 16:75, 22:58), a good promise (20:86, 28:61), reward (18:2), enjoyment (11:3), a good acceptance and growth (3:37), a good trial (8:17), a good share (48:16); of what is seen only in 55:70 and 55:76 (ḥisān), and in 35:8 an evil deed seen as good. 'In the Quran mostly by insight' is ar-Rāġib's own observation and agrees with these places. ḥusn, ḥasana, ḥusnā and aḥsan are other lemmas, not counted here. 73:10 and 33:28 (said to the Prophet) are not quoted.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ǧamāl je obilna ljepota (al-ḥusn al-kaṯīr), bilo ona koja je u samom čovjeku – u duši, tijelu ili djelu – bilo ona koja od njega dolazi drugima. Pridjev jamīl u Kur'anu dolazi na 7 mjesta i uvijek opisuje postupak: strpljenje, praštanje, rastanak.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ǧamāl is abundant beauty (al-ḥusn al-kaṯīr), whether the beauty in a person himself — in his soul, body or deed — or the beauty that reaches others from him. The adjective jamīl comes in the Quran in 7 places, and always describes a way of acting: patience, forbearance, parting.

why.bs: „… ‚Lijepo strpljenje!‘ …“ – Jakubove riječi kad su mu donijeli Jusufovu košulju; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “(My course is) comely patience” — Jacob's words when they brought him Joseph's shirt; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… pa lijepo praštaj“ – ljepota u načinu na koji se prašta.
why.en: “So forgive, (O Muhammad), with a gracious forgiveness” — beauty in the way one forgives.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḥusn je sve što raduje i za čim se žudi, bilo da je lijepo razumu, želji ili osjetilima. Kaže se i za stvari i za događaje; u govoru ljudi najčešće za ono što je lijepo oku, ali u Kur'anu, kaže on, najčešće za ono što je lijepo uvidu. Tako je i u kur'anskoj upotrebi: dobar zajam, dobra opskrba, dobro obećanje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ḥusn is everything that delights and is desired, whether fine to reason, to desire or to the senses. It is said of things and of events; in people's speech mostly of what is fine to the eye, but in the Quran, he says, mostly of what is fine to insight. So too in Quranic usage: a goodly loan, good provision, a good promise.

why.bs: „Ko je taj koji će Allahu dati dobar zajam, pa da mu ga On višestruko uveća …“ – dobro po uvidu, ne po izgledu.
why.en: “Who is it that will lend unto Allah a goodly loan, so that He may give it increase manifold?” — good to insight, not to the eye.

why.bs: „Pa ju je Gospodar njen primio dobrim prijemom i dao joj da dobro uzraste …“ – o Merjemi; dobro i u prihvatanju i u rastu.
why.en: “And her Lord … vouchsafed to her a goodly growth” — of Mary; good both in being accepted and in growing up.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o svjetlu na nebu ili iz vatre. Razlikuju se po tome šta ističu: zvijezdu koja izlazi i po kojoj se ravna put, nebesko tijelo kad se ukaže i zablista, ili užareni plamen koji sijevne.
shared.en: All three words speak of light in the sky or from a fire. They differ in what they stress: the star that rises and by which a course is set, a heavenly body as it appears and shines, or a blazing flame that flashes.

tellApart.bs: Zvijezda koja izlazi, putokaz → نَجْم; zvijezda kad se ukaže i zablista, ukras neba → كَوْكَب; užareni plamen – iz vatre, ili onaj koji na nebu progoni → شِهَاب.
tellApart.en: The rising star, a guide on the way → نَجْم; a star as it appears and shines, the sky's ornament → كَوْكَب; a blazing flame — from a fire, or the one that pursues in the sky → شِهَاب.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نجم, كب, شهب
notes: ar-Rāġib (نجم): the root of najm is the rising star (al-kawkab aṭ-ṭāliʿ), pl. nujūm; najama 'it rose', so najm is now a noun, now a verbal noun (rising); the rising of plants and of an opinion is likened to it; cites 16:16 and 37:88 ('in the science of the stars'); on 53:1 he gives three 'qīla' readings: the star (hawā named because najm itself implies rising), the Pleiades, or the Quran sent down in portions (and 56:75 is read both ways); in 55:6 najm is the plant without a stem, 'and it was said: the stars'. (كب): al-kawākib are 'the stars that appear (al-bādiya), and they are not called kawākib unless they appear'; cites 6:76, 24:35, 37:6, 82:2. (شهب): shihāb is the bright flame from a kindled fire, and of what appears in the air, as 37:10.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 13 / 5 / 5 places read): نَجْم — a guide (6:97, 16:16), subjected (16:12), prostrating (22:18), its setting (52:49), dimmed and fallen on the Last Day (77:8, 81:2), sworn by (53:1, 56:75, 86:3). كَوْكَب — 6:76, 12:4 (Joseph's dream), 24:35 (the glass 'like a shining star'), 37:6 (the sky's ornament), 82:2 (scattered). شِهَاب — a brand from a fire (27:7) and the flame that pursues the eavesdropper (15:18, 37:10, 72:9); the count sums the plural شُهُب (72:8), filed as its own lemma. Not cited: 53:1 and 55:6 (he gives several readings), 56:75, 86:3, 37:88, 6:76 (tafsir differs on Abraham's words) and 12:4.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnovno značenje riječi نَجْم je zvijezda koja izlazi; ista riječ je i glagolska imenica ‚izlaženja‘, pa se tako kaže i za nicanje bilja i za misao koja se javi. U Kur'anu su zvijezde putokaz (6:97, 16:16), potčinjene Allahovoj naredbi (16:12), a na Sudnjem danu se zamrače (81:2).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root sense of نَجْم is the star that rises; the same word is also the verbal noun ‘rising’, so it is said of plants that sprout and of a thought that occurs. In the Quran the stars are a guide (6:97, 16:16), subjected to Allah's command (16:12), and on the Last Day they are dimmed (81:2).

why.bs: „I putokaze; a po zvijezdi se oni upravljaju.“ – zvijezda kao putokaz; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And landmarks (too), and by the star they find a way.” — the star as a guide; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „On vam je dao zvijezde da se po njima upravljate u tminama kopna i mora …“ – zvijezde koje izlaze i zalaze služe za put.
why.en: “He it is Who hath set for you the stars that ye may guide your course by them amid the darkness of the land and the sea” — the stars that rise and set serve the way.

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib je spominje u natuknici كب: kawākib su zvijezde koje se ukažu, i ne zovu se tako dok se ne pokažu. U Kur'anu je كَوْكَب ono što se vidi i blista: ukras najbližeg neba (37:6), staklo koje sja ‚kao blistava sjajnica‘ (24:35), a na Sudnjem danu sjajnice se raspu (82:2).
nuance.en: Ar-Rāġib treats it under the entry كب: kawākib are the stars that appear, and they are not called so until they show. In the Quran كَوْكَب is what is seen and shines: the ornament of the lowest heaven (37:6), the glass that gleams ‘like a shining star’ (24:35), and on the Last Day the shining stars are scattered (82:2).

why.bs: „Mi smo najbliže nebo ukrasili ukrasom – sjajnicama.“ – vidljive, blistave zvijezde; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Lo! We have adorned the lowest heaven with an ornament, the planets [kawākib]” — the visible, shining stars; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „i kad se sjajnice raspu“ – ono što je krasilo nebo rasuto je na Sudnjem danu; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “When the planets [kawākib] are dispersed” — what adorned the sky is scattered on the Last Day; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, شِهَاب je svijetli plamen iz zapaljene vatre, a i ono što se pojavi u zraku (37:10). U Kur'anu su oba: Musa obećava porodici plamen od vatre koju je ugledao (27:7), a na nebu plamen progoni onoga ko krišom prisluškuje (15:18, 37:10, 72:9).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, شِهَاب is the bright flame from a kindled fire, and also what appears in the air (37:10). The Quran has both: Moses promises his family a flame from the fire he has seen (27:7), and in the sky a flame pursues the one who listens by stealth (15:18, 37:10, 72:9).

why.bs: „… ili ću vam donijeti plamen uzet od nje, da se ugrijete“ – plamen iz vatre, prvo značenje koje ar-Rāġib daje.
why.en: “or bring to you a borrowed flame that ye may warm yourselves” — a flame taken from a fire, the first sense ar-Rāġib gives.

why.bs: „osim onoga ko nešto ugrabi – njega progoni plamen probojni“ – plamen koji se javlja na nebu; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Save him who snatcheth a fragment, and there pursueth him a piercing flame.” — the flame that appears in the sky; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi opisuju zemlju kao nešto na čemu se počiva i hoda – Allahovu blagodat. Razlikuju se po slici: postelja koja je prostrta i pokorna, ležište koje je pripremljeno i poravnato kao dječija kolijevka, ili prostirka rasprostrta u širinu.
shared.en: All three words describe the earth as something to rest and walk on — a favour from Allah. They differ in the image: a bed that is spread and made tractable, a resting-place prepared and smoothed like a child's cradle, or a carpet spread wide.

tellApart.bs: Prostrto da se na njemu počine, zemlja ‚pokorna‘ – i postelje u Džennetu → فِرَاش; pripremljeno, poravnato ležište – zemlja, ali najčešće ‚ružno ležište‘ Džehennema → مِهَاد; nešto rasprostrto u širinu → بِسَاط.
tellApart.en: Spread to rest on, the earth made ‘tractable’ — and the couches of the Garden → فِرَاش; a prepared, smoothed resting-place — the earth, but mostly the ‘evil resting-place’ of Hell → مِهَاد; something spread out wide → بِسَاط.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries فرش, مهد, بسط
notes: ar-Rāġib (فرش): farsh is spreading out cloth; what is spread is called farsh and firāsh; on 2:22 'made the earth a firāsh for you': He made it tractable (ḏallalahā) and did not make it remote, so that settling on it would be impossible; pl. furush (56:34, 55:54); farsh in 6:142 is the animals that are ridden; firāsh is used of each spouse; farāš (101:4) the moth. (مهد): mahd is what is prepared for a child (19:29); mahd and mihād are the place made smooth and trodden; cites 'made the earth mahdan' and 'mihādan', 'and that is like al-arḍ firāšan'; mahhadtu 'I prepared and levelled' (74:14). (بسط): basṭ of a thing is spreading and widening it; bisāṭ is a name for everything spread out (71:19), and al-bisāṭ is also wide land.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 3 / 7 / 1 places read): فِرَاش — the earth (2:22) and, as the plural فُرُش, the couches of the Garden (55:54, 56:34). مِهَاد — the earth only in 78:6; the other six places are Hell, five of them 'an evil resting-place' (2:206, 3:12, 3:197, 13:18, 38:56) and 7:41 'a resting-place of Hell'. بِسَاط — only 71:19, in Noah's words. Left out: مَهْد (5, filed as its own lemma) is mostly the cradle of Jesus (3:46, 5:110, 19:29) and the earth only in 20:53 and 43:10, where some readings have mihādan — not summed. فَرْش (6:142, animals) and فَرَاش (101:4, moths) are other words. 56:34 is not cited (furush there is read as couches or as wives).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, farš je prostiranje odjeće, a ono što je prostrto zove se firāš. Za 2:22 kaže da je Allah zemlju učinio pokornom, a ne tako nepristupačnom da se na njoj ne bi moglo nastaniti. Množina فُرُش su postelje u Džennetu (55:54, 56:34).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, farš is spreading out cloth, and what is spread is called firāš. On 2:22 he says Allah made the earth tractable, not so remote that one could not settle on it. The plural فُرُش is the couches of the Garden (55:54, 56:34).

why.bs: „Onaj koji vam je zemlju učinio posteljom, a nebo zdanjem …“ – ar-Rāġib: učinio ju je pokornom, mjestom na kojem se može nastaniti.
why.en: “Who hath appointed the earth a resting-place [a bed, firāš] for you, and the sky a canopy” — ar-Rāġib: He made it tractable, a place one can settle on.

why.bs: „Naslonjeni na posteljama čija je postava od debele svile …“ – množina فُرُش: prostrte postelje u Džennetu.
why.en: “Reclining upon couches [furush] lined with silk brocade” — the plural فُرُش: spread couches in the Garden.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, mahd je ono što se pripremi za dijete (kolijevka), a mahd i mihād su mjesto poravnato i utabano; ‚zemlju smo učinili ležištem‘ on stavlja uz 2:22 (posteljom). U Kur'anu je zemlja mihād samo u 78:6; na ostalih šest mjesta to je Džehennem, pet puta ‚ružno ležište‘ – naše zapažanje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, mahd is what is prepared for a child (a cradle), and mahd and mihād are a place made smooth and trodden; he sets ‘We made the earth a resting-place’ beside 2:22 (a bed). In the Quran the earth is mihād only in 78:6; in the other six places it is Hell, five times ‘an evil resting-place’ — our observation.

why.bs: „Zar zemlju nismo učinili ležištem?“ – pripremljeno, poravnato mjesto; ar-Rāġib navodi riječ mihādan.
why.en: “Have We not made the earth an expanse [mihād]” — a prepared, smoothed place; ar-Rāġib cites the word mihādan.

why.bs: „… bit ćete pobijeđeni i sakupljeni u Džehennem – a ružno je to ležište!“ – ista riječ za pripremljeno počivalište, ovdje rečena za Džehennem, kao na još pet mjesta.
why.en: “Ye shall be overcome and gathered unto Hell, an evil resting-place.” — the same word for a prepared resting-place, said here of Hell, as in five other places.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, basṭ je rasprostiranje i proširivanje nečega; bisāṭ je ime za sve što je rasprostrto, a tako se zove i široka zemlja. U Kur'anu samo jednom, u Nuhovim riječima njegovom narodu (71:19).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, basṭ is spreading a thing out and widening it; bisāṭ is the name for anything spread out, and wide land is also called so. In the Quran only once, in Noah's words to his people (71:19).

why.bs: „I Allah vam je zemlju učinio prostirkom“ – rasprostrta u širinu; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And Allah hath made the earth a wide expanse [bisāṭ] for you” — spread out wide; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi su sjedišta za odmor, gotovo uvijek u Džennetu. Razlikuju se po onome što označavaju: sam divan na kojem se sjedi i naslanja, ili divan nad kojim je nadstrešnica – baldahin.
shared.en: Both words are seats of rest, almost always in the Garden. They differ in what they name: the couch itself, to sit and recline on, or a couch with a canopy over it.

tellApart.bs: Divan za sjedenje – ar-Rāġib ga veže za radost (surūr); jedni naspram drugih, poredani, uzdignuti → سُرُر; divan pod nadstrešnicom, na kojem se naslanja i s kojeg se gleda → أَرَائِك.
tellApart.en: A couch to sit on — ar-Rāġib links it to gladness (surūr); facing one another, ranged, raised → سُرُر; a couch under a canopy, to recline on and to look from → أَرَائِك.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries سرر, أريك
notes: ar-Rāġib (سرر): sarīr is what one sits on, from surūr (gladness), since it belonged to people of ease (ulī n-niʿma); pl. asirra and surur; cites 52:20, 88:13, 43:34; the bier is called sarīr by likeness of form and in hope of the gladness the dead finds in returning to Allah. (أريك): arīka is a ḥajala (a curtained canopy) on a sarīr, pl. arāʾik; named either because it is made of arāk wood, or as a place of staying (from aruka bi-l-makān).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 6 / 5 places read): سُرُر — the Garden in five places: facing one another (15:47, 37:44), lined (56:15), ranged (52:20), raised (88:13); 43:34 is this world: the couches Allah would have given to the houses of those who disbelieve, were it not that mankind would then become one community (43:33). The singular سَرِير is not in the Quran (the thrones of Joseph and of the Queen of Sheba are عَرْش). أَرَائِك — all 5 in the Garden: with reclining (18:31, 36:56, 76:13) or looking (83:23, 83:35). Pickthall gives 'couches' to both words (and to فُرُش): the member is named in [brackets].

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, sarīr je ono na čemu se sjedi, a ime je od surūr – radosti, jer je to bilo za ljude blagostanja; u množini asirra i surur. U Kur'anu su to divani u Džennetu: jedni naspram drugih (15:47, 37:44), poredani (52:20), uzdignuti (88:13). Jednom su ovosvjetski (43:34).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, sarīr is what one sits on, and the name comes from surūr — gladness, since it belonged to people of ease; its plurals are asirra and surur. In the Quran they are the couches of the Garden: facing one another (15:47, 37:44), ranged (52:20), raised (88:13). Once they belong to this world (43:34).

why.bs: „na divanima, jedni naspram drugih“ – stanovnici Dženneta sjede licem u lice.
why.en: “On couches [surur] facing one another” — the people of the Garden sit face to face.

why.bs: „U njemu su divani uzdignuti“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Wherein are couches [surur] raised” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, arīka je zastrta nadstrešnica (ḥaǧala) nad divanom (sarīr); ime je dobila ili zato što se pravila od drveta arāk, ili kao mjesto boravka (od aruka bi-l-makān). U Kur'anu (svih 5 mjesta) samo u Džennetu: na njima se naslanja (18:31, 36:56, 76:13) i s njih se gleda (83:23, 83:35).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, arīka is a curtained canopy (ḥaǧala) over a couch (sarīr); it was named either because it was made of arāk wood, or as a place of staying (from aruka bi-l-makān). In the Quran (all 5 places) only in the Garden: they recline on them (18:31, 36:56, 76:13) and look from them (83:23, 83:35).

why.bs: „Oni i njihove supruge u hladovinama su, na baldahinima naslonjeni.“ – divan pod nadstrešnicom.
why.en: “They and their wives, in pleasant shade, on thrones [arāʾik] reclining” — a couch under a canopy.

why.bs: „Na baldahinima gledaju.“ – s baldahina se gleda.
why.en: “On couches [arāʾik], gazing” — from the canopied couches they look on.

title.bs: Pad: srušiti se, strmoglaviti se, pasti
title.en: Falling: to fall down, to plunge, to drop

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače pasti s visine. Razlikuju se po tome šta ističu: pad koji se čuje – i padanje ničice, strmoglavljivanje iz visine u dubinu, ili pad s mjesta na kojem je nešto bilo.
shared.en: All three words mean falling from a height. They differ in what they stress: a fall that is heard — and falling prostrate, plunging from a height into the depth, or dropping from where a thing was.

tellApart.bs: Pasti tako da se čuje, i pasti ničice → خَرَّ; strmoglaviti se iz visine nadolje – i propasti → هَوَى; pasti s mjesta – list s drveta, a i ‚pasti u iskušenje‘ → سَقَطَ.
tellApart.en: To fall so that it is heard, and to fall prostrate → خَرَّ; to plunge from a height downward — and to be ruined → هَوَى; to drop from a place — a leaf from a tree, and ‘to fall into temptation’ → سَقَطَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries خر, هوى, سقط
notes: ar-Rāġib (خر): cites 22:31, 34:14, 16:26; kharra is 'he fell a fall from which a kharīr is heard' — the sound of water, wind and whatever falls from a height; in 'and they fell down before him prostrate' (12:100 wording) the word points to two things together, the falling and the sound of their glorification, and 'wa-sabbaḥū bi-ḥamdi rabbihim' (32:15) shows that this sound was glorifying Allah and nothing else. (هوى): besides hawā 'desire', al-huwiyy is falling from height to low; he notes 'it was said' that desire is so named because it plunges its owner into calamity; ahwāhu is lifting it into the air and dropping it (53:53). (سقط): suqūṭ is a thing's being thrown down from a high place to a low one, as a man falls from a roof (9:49 cited), or an upright figure stoops in old age (52:44 sāqiṭan); saqaṭ is what is of little account; on 7:149 'when it was made to fall in their hands' he says it means regret.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 12 / 8 / 3 places read): خَرَّ — 6 of 12 are falling prostrate or weeping (12:100, 17:107, 17:109, 19:58, 32:15, 38:24; 25:73 negates it), the others a body or a thing falling (7:143, 16:26, 19:90, 22:31, 34:14). The corpus files under هوي_1 also hawiya 'to desire' (2:87, 5:70, 53:23) and 14:37 'incline towards'; the falling sense is in 20:81 and 22:31 (53:1 is read in different ways: he gives a star, the Pleiades, or the Quran coming down in parts) and ahwā 'overthrew' (53:53) — the count is the catalogue's for the whole key. سَقَطَ (Form I) is only 6:59, 7:149, 9:49; asqaṭa (Form IV, 'cause to fall', of pieces of the sky) and tasāqaṭa (19:25) are other forms. Not cited: 12:100 and 38:24 (prostration before Joseph; David's), 7:143, 53:1 (readings differ).

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 4 flags, fixed: خَرَّ falling prostrate or weeping is 6 of 12 (25:73 negates it); 53:1 is not given as a plain fall (he reports three readings); Bosnian quotes of 22:31 and 6:59 re-translated.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, خَرَّ je pasti tako da se čuje zvuk (ḫarīr) – kao šum vode, vjetra i svega što pada s visine. Kad ‚padnu ničice‘, kaže on, riječ ukazuje na dvoje zajedno: na padanje i na zvuk njihovog slavljenja – a ‚i hvale svoga Gospodara‘ (32:15) pokazuje da je taj zvuk bio slavljenje Allaha. U Kur'anu je šest od dvanaest mjesta padanje na sedždu ili u plaču.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, خَرَّ is to fall so that a sound (ḫarīr) is heard — like the sound of water, of wind, and of whatever falls from a height. When they ‘fall down prostrate’, he says, the word points to two things together: the falling and the sound of their glorifying — and ‘and hymn the praise of their Lord’ (32:15) shows that this sound was glorifying Allah. In the Quran six of the twelve places are falling in prostration or in tears.

why.bs: „… koji, kad se njima opomenu, padnu ničice i hvale svoga Gospodara …“ – pad i zvuk slavljenja zajedno, kako ar-Rāġib objašnjava.
why.en: “who, when they are reminded of them, fall down prostrate and hymn the praise of their Lord” — the fall and the sound of glorifying together, as ar-Rāġib explains.

why.bs: „… pa kad se srušio, džinima je postalo jasno …“ – Sulejmanovo tijelo pada kad je štap izgrižen; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And when he fell the jinn saw clearly” — Solomon's body falls once the staff is gnawed through; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, huwiyy je pad iz visine nadolje (pored hawā – žudnje, koja je od istog korijena). U Kur'anu se ovaj glagol u značenju pada javlja u 20:81 i 22:31 (53:1 se tumači na različite načine), a ahwā ‚oborio je‘ u 53:53 – ar-Rāġib: podigao ga je u zrak pa ga bacio.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, huwiyy is falling from a height to what is below (beside hawā — desire — from the same root). In the Quran the verb in the sense of falling is in 20:81 and 22:31 (53:1 is read in different ways), and ahwā ‘He overthrew’ in 53:53 — ar-Rāġib: He lifted it into the air and dropped it.

why.bs: „… kao da se srušio s neba, pa ga ptice zgrabe ili ga vjetar odnese i strmoglavi na dalek kraj.“ – oba glagola u jednom ajetu: خَرَّ za pad s neba, تَهْوِي za strmoglavljivanje.
why.en: “it is as if he had fallen from the sky and the birds had snatched him or the wind had blown [tahwī] him to a far-off place” — both verbs in one ayah: خَرَّ for the fall from the sky, تَهْوِي for being swept down.

why.bs: „… a onaj na koga se sruči Moja srdžba – taj je propao.“ – doslovno ‚strmoglavio se‘; mnogi mufessiri: propao je; Allahova srdžba, kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “and he on whom My wrath cometh, he is lost [hawā] indeed.” — literally ‘he has plunged’; many mufassirun: he has perished; Allah's wrath, as befits Him.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, suqūṭ je kad nešto bude bačeno s visokog mjesta na niže, kao kad čovjek padne s krova; saqaṭ je i ono što malo vrijedi. Izraz ‚palo im je u ruke‘ (7:149) on objašnjava kao kajanje. U Kur'anu je osnovni oblik samo tri puta (6:59, 7:149, 9:49).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, suqūṭ is a thing's being thrown down from a high place to a lower one, as a man falls from a roof; saqaṭ is also what is of little worth. The phrase ‘it fell into their hands’ (7:149) he explains as regret. In the Quran the basic form is only three times (6:59, 7:149, 9:49).

why.bs: „… nema lista koji opadne, a da ga On ne zna …“ – Allahovo znanje, kako Njemu priliči, obuhvata i pad jednog lista.
why.en: “Not a leaf falleth [tasquṭu] but He knoweth it” — Allah's knowledge, as befits Him, takes in even the fall of a leaf.

why.bs: „… Eto, u iskušenje su pali! …“ – pad kao s visine; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Surely it is into temptation that they (thus) have fallen.” — a fall as from a height; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače vrat. Razlikuju se po tome šta se njima kaže: vrat kao dio tijela – mjesto okova i onoga što je čovjeku ‚pričvršćeno‘, ili vrat kao cijela osoba, pa i rob kojeg treba osloboditi.
shared.en: Both words mean the neck. They differ in what is said with them: the neck as a part of the body — the place of fetters and of what is ‘fastened’ to a person — or the neck standing for the whole person, even a slave to be set free.

tellApart.bs: Vrat kao dio tijela – okovi, udes pričvršćen za vrat, ruka vezana za vrat → عُنُق; šija za cijelu osobu, najčešće rob: ‚osloboditi šiju‘ → رَقَبَة.
tellApart.en: The neck as a part of the body — fetters, the augury fastened to the neck, the hand chained to the neck → عُنُق; the nape for the whole person, mostly a slave: ‘freeing a nape’ → رَقَبَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عنق, رقب
notes: ar-Rāġib (عنق): ʿunuq is the bodily limb, pl. aʿnāq; cites 17:13, 38:33, 40:71; 'above the necks' (8:12) means their heads; 'it was said' that the nobles of a people are called aʿnāq, and 26:4 is read so. (رقب): raqaba is the name of the known limb, then it expresses the whole person, and by convention became a name for slaves, as 'head' and 'back' are said for mounts; cites 4:92; fī r-riqāb (9:60) he reads as the mukātabūn (slaves who have contracted to buy their freedom), to whom zakāh is paid; raqīb (the guardian) from the same root.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 9 / 7 ayat read): عُنُق — mostly the bodily neck: fetters (13:5, 34:33, 36:8, 40:71), the augury (17:13), the hand (17:29), Solomon's horses (38:33), 8:12, and 26:4 (necks, or nobles). رَقَبَة (9 occurrences in 7 ayat) — a person to be freed in all but 47:4: tahrīr raqaba as expiation (4:92 thrice, 5:89, 58:3), fakk raqaba (90:13), 'for slaves' (2:177, 9:60 — ar-Rāġib: the mukātabūn; Pickthall 'captives'; mufassirun differ). Not cited: 8:12 and 47:4 (battle), 26:4 (read two ways), 38:33 (tafsir differs), 9:60.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 flag, fixed: عُنُق 'mostly' the bodily neck — he reads aʿnāq in 26:4 as the nobles.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, عُنُق je ud tijela, u množini aʿnāq; ‚iznad vratova‘ (8:12) znači glave, a navodi i da se ugledni ljudi zovu aʿnāq, pa tako shvata 26:4. U Kur'anu (svih 9 mjesta) to je najčešće tjelesni vrat: mjesto okova (13:5, 36:8, 40:71), udes pričvršćen za vrat (17:13), ruka vezana za vrat (17:29).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, عُنُق is the bodily limb, plural aʿnāq; ‘above the necks’ (8:12) means the heads, and he reports that the nobles of a people are called aʿnāq, taking 26:4 so. In the Quran (all 9 places) it is mostly the bodily neck: the place of fetters (13:5, 36:8, 40:71), the augury fastened to the neck (17:13), the hand chained to the neck (17:29).

why.bs: „Svakom čovjeku smo njegov udes pričvrstili za vrat …“ – ono što je za vrat pričvršćeno ne može se odbaciti; mnogi mufessiri: njegova djela; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And every man's augury have We fastened to his own neck” — what is fastened to the neck cannot be thrown off; many mufassirun: his deeds; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I ne drži ruku vezanu za vrat, a ni ne pružaj je sasvim …“ – slika škrtosti; vrat kao dio tijela.
why.en: “And let not thy hand be chained to thy neck nor open it with a complete opening” — an image of stinginess; the neck as a part of the body.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, رَقَبَة je ime poznatog uda, zatim se njome izražava cijela osoba, a u govoru je postala ime za robove – kao što se ‚glava‘ i ‚leđa‘ kažu za jahaće životinje. U Kur'anu je na svim mjestima osim 47:4 to osoba koju treba osloboditi: kao iskup (4:92, 5:89, 58:3) ili kao dobro djelo (90:13).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, رَقَبَة is the name of the known limb; then it expresses the whole person, and in usage it became a name for slaves — as ‘head’ and ‘back’ are said for mounts. In the Quran, in every place but 47:4, it is a person to be set free: as expiation (4:92, 5:89, 58:3) or as a good deed (90:13).

why.bs: „… neka oslobodi roba vjernika …“ – رَقَبَة je ovdje cijela osoba; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “must set free a believing slave” — the رَقَبَة here is the whole person; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „osloboditi roba“ – doslovno ‚odriješiti šiju‘ (fakku raqaba).
why.en: “(It is) to free a slave,” — literally ‘to unbind a nape’ (fakku raqaba).

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o ostajanju koje ne prestaje. Razlikuju se po tome šta ističu: ostati u istom stanju, bez promjene i kvarenja; trajnost kao ime onoga što ostaje; ili vrijeme bez granice.
shared.en: All three words speak of a staying that does not cease. They differ in what they stress: remaining in the same state, without change or decay; lastingness as the name of what remains; or time without a bound.

tellApart.bs: Onaj koji trajno ostaje – ‚u njemu će trajno boraviti‘ → خَالِد; trajnost kao imenica – ‚Džennet besmrtnosti‘, a nijednom čovjeku na ovom svijetu nije data → خُلْد; ‚zauvijek / nikad‘ – vrijeme bez granice, koje naglašava da trajanju nema kraja → أَبَدًا.
tellApart.en: The one who abides — ‘they will abide therein’ → خَالِد; lastingness as a noun — ‘the Garden of Immortality’, given to no human in this world → خُلْد; ‘for ever / never’ — time without a bound, stressing that the stay has no end → أَبَدًا.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries خلد, أبد
notes: ar-Rāġib (خلد): ḫulūd is a thing's being free from the onset of corruption and remaining in the state it is in; the Arabs call anything that change and decay are slow to reach ḫālid — the hearth-stones are ḫawālid, for their long stay, not for lasting for ever; ḫuld is the name of the part of a man that stays unchanged while he lives; muḫallad was at root what stays a long time, then was borrowed for what is kept for ever; ḫulūd in the Garden is things remaining in their state with no corruption coming upon them (cites 2:82, 2:39 wording, 4:93); 56:17 wildān muḫalladūn: 'kept in their state' or 'wearing earrings'; 7:176 aḫlada ilā l-arḍ: he leaned to it, thinking he would last in it. (أبد): cites 'ḫālidīna fīhā abadan'; abad expresses an extended span of time that is not divided as time is — one says 'the time of such-and-such' but not 'the abad of such-and-such'; it should have no dual or plural, though ābād is said (some call it post-classical); ta'abbada 'it remained for ever', and it is also said of what remains a long time.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 74 / 6 / 28 places read): خَالِد — almost always 'abiding therein', of the Garden or the Fire; 11 places add أَبَدًا — the Garden 8 (4:57, 4:122, 5:119, 9:22, 9:100, 64:9, 65:11, 98:8), the Fire 3 (4:169, 33:65, 72:23); 18:3 has mākiṯīna fīhi abadan. خُلْد — in a construct naming the hereafter's Garden (25:15), abode (41:28) and punishment (10:52, 32:14), and the lasting life given to no one in this world (21:34; Satan's 'tree of immortality', 20:120). أَبَدًا with a negation is 'never' (2:95, 5:24, 9:83, 24:4 …). Whether ḫālid alone means without end in every place (4:14, 4:93 for a believer who sins) is a question on which the scholars of creed differ; those ayat are not cited, and ar-Rāġib's 'long stay' remark is given only as what he says of the Arabs' usage. 20:120 (Adam) is not cited. خُلُود (50:34) and مُخَلَّد (2) are other lemmas.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: Bosnian quotes of 2:82 and 9:100 re-translated from the Arabic.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries خلد, أبد (2026-11-06): 18 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): The plural he names is آباد (ābād), not āmād (which is the plural of amad)

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḫulūd je kad je nešto pošteđeno kvarenja i ostaje u stanju u kojem jeste; Arapi su ḫālid zvali i ono do čega promjena sporo dolazi – zbog dugog ostanka, ne zbog vječnog trajanja. Ḫulūd u Džennetu je, kaže on, kad stvari ostaju kakve jesu, a kvarenje ih ne dotiče. U Kur'anu je to gotovo uvijek ‚u njemu će trajno boraviti‘.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ḫulūd is a thing's being spared decay and remaining in the state it is in; the Arabs also called ḫālid what change is slow to reach — for its long stay, not for lasting for ever. Ḫulūd in the Garden, he says, is things remaining as they are, untouched by decay. In the Quran it is almost always ‘they will abide therein’.

why.bs: „… takvi pripadaju Džennetu i u njemu će trajno ostati.“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet: u Džennetu stvari ostaju kakve jesu, bez kvarenja.
why.en: “such are rightful owners of the Garden. They will abide therein.” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah: in the Garden things remain as they are, without decay.

nuance.bs: Imenica istog korijena. U Kur'anu (6 mjesta) najčešće u spoju koji imenuje ono što ostaje: ‚Džennet besmrtnosti‘ (25:15), ‚kuća‘ i ‚kazna‘ besmrtnosti na ahiretu (41:28, 10:52, 32:14) – i ostanak koji na ovom svijetu nije dat nijednom čovjeku (21:34). Ar-Rāġibov primjer za ḫuld (dio čovjeka koji se ne mijenja dok je živ) nije kur'anska upotreba, pa se na njega ne oslanjamo.
nuance.en: A noun of the same root. In the Quran (6 places) mostly in a construct naming what lasts: ‘the Garden of Immortality’ (25:15), the ‘abode’ and the ‘punishment’ of immortality in the hereafter (41:28, 10:52, 32:14) — and the lasting life given to no human in this world (21:34). Ar-Rāġib's example for ḫuld (the part of a man that does not change while he lives) is not a Quranic use, so we do not rest on it.

why.bs: „Nijednom čovjeku prije tebe nismo dali besmrtnost …“ – na ovom svijetu niko ne ostaje.
why.en: “We appointed immortality for no mortal before thee.” — in this world no one remains.

why.bs: „… ili Džennet besmrtnosti koji je obećan bogobojaznima …“ – trajnost kao ime Dženneta.
why.en: “or the Garden of Immortality which is promised unto those who ward off (evil)” — lastingness as the Garden's name.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, abad izražava protegnuto vrijeme koje se ne dijeli kao što se dijeli vrijeme: kaže se ‚vrijeme toga i toga‘, ali ne ‚abad toga i toga‘. U Kur'anu na 11 mjesta dolazi iza ‚u njemu će trajno boraviti‘ – 8 puta o Džennetu, 3 puta o Vatri – i tako kaže da boravku nema kraja; uz negaciju znači ‚nikad‘ (5:24, 18:35).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, abad expresses an extended span of time that is not divided as time is divided: one says ‘the time of such-and-such’, but not ‘the abad of such-and-such’. In the Quran it follows ‘abiding therein’ in 11 places — 8 of the Garden, 3 of the Fire — and so says that the stay has no end; with a negation it means ‘never’ (5:24, 18:35).

why.bs: „… i pripremio im je vrtove ispod kojih teku rijeke; u njima će ostajati, i to zauvijek …“ – خَالِد i أَبَدًا zajedno: boravak, i to da mu nema kraja.
why.en: “He hath made ready for them Gardens underneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide for ever.” — خَالِد and أَبَدًا together: the stay, and that it has no end.

why.bs: „… Ne mislim da će ovo ikada propasti.“ – uz negaciju: vlasnik bašče mislio je da je njegovo dobro trajno, a ono je uništeno (18:42).
why.en: “I think not that all this will ever perish.” — with a negation: the owner of the garden thought his wealth would last, and it was destroyed (18:42).

title.bs: Rascijepiti se: raspuknuti se, rasjeći se, razdvojiti se
title.en: Splitting: to split, to be cleft, to part

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače da se nešto rascijepi. Razlikuju se po slici: pukotina koja se otvori u nečemu, rascjep po dužini, ili cijepanje kojim se dijelovi odvoje jedan od drugog.
shared.en: All three words mean that something splits. They differ in the image: a breach that opens in a thing, a cleft along its length, or a splitting by which the parts move apart from one another.

tellApart.bs: Pukotina u nečemu, raspolućivanje – nebo, Mjesec, zemlja → اِنْشَقَّ; rascjep po dužini – nebo na Sudnjem danu (82:1) → اِنْفَطَرَ; rascijepiti se tako da se dijelovi razdvoje – more pred Musaom → اِنْفَلَقَ.
tellApart.en: A breach in a thing, splitting in two — the sky, the moon, the earth → اِنْشَقَّ; a cleft along the length — the sky on the Last Day (82:1) → اِنْفَطَرَ; splitting so that the parts stand apart — the sea before Moses → اِنْفَلَقَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries شق, فطر, فلق
notes: ar-Rāġib (شق): šaqq is the breach (ḫurm) that occurs in a thing — 'I split it in two halves'; cites 80:26, 50:44, 69:16, 84:1, 54:1; on 54:1 three views: it split in the Prophet's time, or it is a splitting that comes near the Hour, or 'the matter became clear'. (فطر): the root of faṭr is splitting lengthwise (aš-šaqq ṭūlan); fuṭūr (67:3) is flaw and weakness, which may be by way of corruption or of soundness (73:18); from it Allah's faṭr of creation — bringing it into being in a form disposed to an act. (فلق): falq is splitting a thing and separating parts of it from one another — falaqtuhu fa-nfalaqa; cites 6:96, 6:95 and 26:63.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 5 / 1 / 1 places read): اِنْشَقَّ (Form VII) — the sky (55:37, 69:16, 84:1), the moon (54:1), the earth (19:90). اِنْفَطَرَ — only 82:1; the same image is in munfaṭir (73:18) and tafaṭṭara (19:90, 42:5), which the verb catalogue does not file as Form VII. اِنْفَلَقَ — only 26:63; Allah as fāliq (6:95, 6:96) is the participle. 19:90 holds tafaṭṭara and inšaqqa together. 54:1: most mufassirun hold the moon split as a sign in the Prophet's time; ar-Rāġib also reports the other views.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: the verb اِنْفَطَرَ is only in 82:1, the participle munfaṭir in 73:18; 26:63 bs re-translated.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries شق, فطر, فلق (2026-11-06): 17 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/ayat/0/why (reworded): He gives the root sense but neither cites 82:1 nor applies 'lengthwise' to it; our wording reads his root sense into this ayah

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, šaqq je pukotina koja nastane u nečemu – ‚raspolovio sam ga‘. U Kur'anu se raspukne nebo (55:37, 69:16, 84:1), Mjesec (54:1) i zemlja (19:90).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, šaqq is the breach that comes about in a thing — ‘I split it in two halves’. In the Quran the sky splits (55:37, 69:16, 84:1), the moon (54:1) and the earth (19:90).

why.bs: „Kad se nebo raspukne“ – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “When the heaven is split asunder” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Približio se Čas i Mjesec se raspuknuo.“ – većina mufessira: znak u Poslanikovo vrijeme; ar-Rāġib navodi i druga mišljenja.
why.en: “The hour drew nigh and the moon was rent in twain.” — most mufassirun: a sign in the Prophet's time; ar-Rāġib also reports other views.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnovno značenje korijena faṭr je cijepanje po dužini; fuṭūr (67:3) je pukotina i slabost. Od istog korijena je i Allahovo stvaranje (faṭara) – ali to nije ovo značenje. U Kur'anu je glagol u ovom obliku samo u 82:1 (particip munfaṭir u 73:18).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root sense of faṭr is splitting lengthwise; fuṭūr (67:3) is a flaw and weakness. Allah's originating of creation (faṭara) is from the same root — but that is not this sense. In the Quran the verb in this form is only in 82:1 (the participle munfaṭir is in 73:18).

why.bs: „Kad se nebo rasiječe“ – rascjep; ar-Rāġib kao osnovno značenje korijena daje cijepanje po dužini.
why.en: “When the heaven is cleft asunder” — a cleaving; ar-Rāġib gives the root sense as splitting along the length.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, falq je rascijepiti nešto i odvojiti mu dijelove jedan od drugog. U Kur'anu je ovaj oblik samo u 26:63 – more se razdvojilo pred Musaom.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, falq is splitting a thing and separating its parts from one another. In the Quran this form is only in 26:63 — the sea parted before Moses.

why.bs: „… Udari more svojim štapom! I ono se razdvojilo, a svaki dio bio je poput ogromnog brda.“ – dijelovi stoje odvojeni; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Smite the sea with thy staff. And it parted, and each part was as a mountain vast.” — the parts stand apart; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Sve četiri riječi znače nešto što zaklanja. Razlikuju se po tome kako zaklanja i šta: pregrada između dvoga, pokrivač stavljen odozgo, omotač u kojem je nešto zatvoreno, ili koprena preko očiju.
shared.en: All four words mean something that screens. They differ in how it screens and what: a barrier between two, a cover laid on top, a sheath in which a thing is enclosed, or an overlay on the eyes.

tellApart.bs: Ono što sprečava da se do nečega dođe, pregrada između dvoga → حِجَاب; pokrivač stavljen preko, kao poklopac – i nemar koji se skida → غِطَاء; omotači u kojima je nešto zatvoreno – uvijek na srcima → أَكِنَّة; koprena na očima i pogledu → غِشَاوَة.
tellApart.en: What keeps one from reaching a thing, a barrier between two → حِجَاب; a cover laid over, like a lid — and the heedlessness that is lifted → غِطَاء; sheaths in which a thing is enclosed — always on hearts → أَكِنَّة; an overlay on the eyes and the sight → غِشَاوَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حجب, غطا, كن, غشى
notes: ar-Rāġib (حجب): ḥaǧb and ḥiǧāb are preventing from reaching; on 7:46 the ḥiǧāb is not what blocks the sight, but what keeps the delight of the people of the Garden from reaching the people of the Fire and their harm from reaching the people of the Garden, like the wall of 57:13; 42:51 'from behind a veil': from where the one spoken to does not see Him; 38:32 the sun hidden in setting; 83:15 maḥǧūbūn: kept from the light. (غطا): ġiṭāʾ is what is put over a thing, a lid (ṭabaq) and the like, as ġišāʾ is what is put over a thing like clothing; it is borrowed for ignorance (al-ǧahāla): 50:22. (كن): kinn is that in which a thing is kept; kinān is the cover in which a thing is kept, pl. akinna, like ġiṭāʾ / aġṭiya; cites 'upon their hearts akinna lest they understand it' (6:25 / 17:46 wording) and 41:5, 'it was said: in a cover against understanding what you bring us', like 11:91. (غشى): ġišāwa is what a thing is covered with; cites 2:7 and 45:23.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 7 / 2 / 4 / 2 places read): حِجَاب — between the Garden and the Fire (7:46), between the Prophet reciting and the deniers (17:45, 'a hidden barrier'), Mary's seclusion (19:17), 33:53, 38:32, 41:5, 42:51. غِطَاء — both of sight: eyes 'in a cover' from Allah's reminder (18:101), and the cover removed (50:22). أَكِنَّة — all 4 on hearts (6:25, 17:46, 18:57, 41:5). غِشَاوَة — both on the eyes / sight, beside the sealing of hearing and heart (2:7, 45:23). 41:5 holds akinna and ḥiǧāb together, in the deniers' own words. Not cited: 38:32 (what was hidden — the sun or the horses — is read two ways), 33:53, 17:45. مَحْجُوب, أَكْنَان, غَاشِيَة are other lemmas.
